cases.title: A fresh single-stage draft activates
cases.why: The happy-path baseline the rest of the section is measured against.
cases.setup: A draft event group with one draft stage that has a bidding-time schedule.
cases.steps: `PATCH` with `status: "active"` and the stage uuid in `draft_trade_request_uuids`.
cases.expected: 200; the event group is active with one live stage.
cases.oracle: Status active; the stage appears in `stages`; a vendor can bid on it.

cases.title: Activation must never answer with an untyped 500
cases.why: The standing regression. From ~16:29 on 2026-09-08 this endpoint returned `{"status":500,"error":"Internal Server Error"}` for **both** `status: "active"` and `status: "draft"`, invariant across stage type (auction / RFQ / RFP), line-item count (1 or 2), invited vendors (0, 1, 154), sheet filled or empty, and schedule default or explicitly saved. Nothing was written — the title never appeared in the events list — so the raise happened before the commit.
cases.setup: Any valid draft event group and stage.
cases.steps: `PATCH` to activate. Capture the full response body and the request payload.
cases.expected: Either 200, or a `render_error_json` failure with a `{code, message}`.
cases.oracle: Fail if the body is `{"status":500,"error":…}` with no code. Attach the payload to the failure — the payload is what makes the report actionable. The three ranked causes are a `lock_transaction` double-render at `event_groups_controller.rb:74`, `set_customized_audiences` (`trade_controller_helper.rb:687-729`), and `TradeSchedule.change_auction_time(nil)` in `publish_auction`; the third cannot explain the draft-status 500, so an exception class from Sentry is what distinguishes them.

cases.title: Activation of a stage with no bidding-time schedule fails cleanly
cases.why: `change_auction_time(nil)` has no nil guard, so this is a real unguarded dereference. The correct behaviour is a refusal naming the schedule.
cases.setup: A draft stage whose bidding-time `TradeSchedule` is absent.
cases.steps: `PATCH` to activate.
cases.expected: A `{code, message}` refusal about the schedule.
cases.oracle: Not a bare 500. This is the regression guard's narrowest form.

cases.title: Activation succeeds identically for auction, rfq and rfp stages
cases.why: Publishing must not be strategy-sensitive; if one mode fails, the cause is in that mode's setup rather than in publish.
cases.steps: Build three single-stage drafts, one per mode. Activate each.
cases.expected: All three activate.
cases.oracle: Three active events; report per-mode outcomes separately so a single failure is attributable.

cases.title: Activation succeeds with a single invited vendor
cases.why: The minimum useful audience, and the fixture every bid case needs.
cases.steps: `PATCH` with one `audience_company_uuids` entry.
cases.expected: Active with that vendor invited.
cases.oracle: One audience row for the stage; the vendor can see the event.

cases.title: An attachment URL from another company is refused
cases.why: Every attachment URL is validated for company ownership before anything else happens; it is a cross-tenant read vector.
cases.steps: `PATCH` with an attachment URL owned by another company.
cases.oracle: Nothing written; the event stays draft.

cases.title: A caller without update permission is refused
cases.why: The policy has two independent branches (Procol employee acting as CSM, or allowed-company plus trade create) and both need proving.
cases.setup: A user in neither branch.
cases.steps: `PATCH` to activate.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: Event unchanged.

cases.title: Publishing RFP + RFQ where the RFP ends later is refused
cases.why: Code 712, "RFP duration exceeds RFQ end time. Please adjust." — a real ordering constraint between stage windows.
cases.setup: A two-stage draft with the RFP ending after the RFQ.
cases.steps: `PATCH` to activate both.
cases.oracle: Neither stage goes live.

cases.title: Re-activating an already-active event is idempotent
cases.why: Clients retry. A retry that duplicates stages or audiences is a data-integrity bug.
cases.steps: `PATCH` to activate twice with identical bodies.
cases.expected: No duplicates.
cases.oracle: Stage count, audience count and bid count identical after the second call.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: An unknown status together with a config change crashes with a 500
cases.why: Unvalidated enum assignment is the classic Rails 500. Any typo'd status from a client takes the endpoint down for that request.
cases.setup: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}} (any state).
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with status "banana" and config {show_under_open_events: true}. 2. Check the response shape.
cases.expected: Must be a 422 {code, message}. Today `config.present?` routes into UpdateService#execute (event_group_controller_helper.rb:33-34), which does `@event_group.status = @status` (update_service.rb:79); assigning 'banana' to the EventGroup enum (in_active/active/draft/withdrawn) raises ArgumentError, which no rescue_from catches, so the answer is an untyped 500.
cases.oracle: Response is 422 with a numeric code, not `{status: 500}`; event status unchanged.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: status "in_active" plus a config change soft-deletes a live event with no withdraw flow
cases.why: It is a second, unguarded exit from a live event that skips everything the withdraw path does (remarks, stage closure, PR release, notifications).
cases.setup: A dedicated active sandbox copy (this case is destructive — run it last or on its own copy).
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with status "in_active" and config {show_under_open_events: true}. 2. Read the event and its stages back.
cases.expected: Should be refused (only 'withdrawn' is a legal way down, with remarks). Today execute() sets status 'in_active' directly (update_service.rb:79) — no withdraw remark, stages left active, PR quantities not released, no vendor notification.
cases.oracle: Event status and every stage's status after the call; if the event is in_active while stages are still active, the defect is confirmed.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: status "draft" on a live event turns it back into a draft
cases.why: A live event silently vanishing from invited vendors mid-bidding is a business-critical failure, reachable with a one-field PATCH.
cases.setup: A dedicated active sandbox copy with vendor {{vendorUuid}} invited (destructive).
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with {status: "draft"}. 2. Read the event back as the buyer and as the vendor.
cases.expected: Should be refused — amendment of a live event goes through /item_versions. Today ['withdrawn','draft'].include?(status) routes into execute (event_group_controller_helper.rb:33), which has no 'is the event a draft?' check and sets status draft (update_service.rb:62-79); get_valid_stages_for_user then hides the event from everyone but the owner (event_group.rb:512-514).
cases.oracle: Read-back status; the vendor's GET of the event.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: A junk stage uuid in the publish list voids every real stage and still goes live
cases.why: One bad id in a client's list silently destroys the event's stages — and the reply is 200.
cases.setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event with its stage attached.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with draft_trade_request_uuids: ["WrongUuid1="]. 2. Read the event and its stages back.
cases.expected: Should be 422 (unknown stage). Today ParamsAuth decodes the junk to nil (params_auth.rb:72-73) giving [nil]; that list is present, so every real stage `exclude?`s and is set to void (update_service.rb:528-530), yet the event itself is saved as active (update_service.rb:251-253). Result: an 'active' event with no live stage.
cases.oracle: Event status vs stage statuses: event active with every stage void confirms the defect.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: A valid uuid of some other record in the stage list voids this event's stages
cases.why: Same failure as the junk-uuid case but with a well-formed id — the kind a buggy client really sends (wrong variable).
cases.setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event with its stage attached; {{lineItemUuid}} is a line item (not a stage).
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with draft_trade_request_uuids: ["{{lineItemUuid}}"]. 2. Read stages back.
cases.expected: Should be 422. uuids are untyped (EncryptDecrypt just encodes an integer), so the line-item uuid decodes to an integer that is not one of this event's stage ids; every real stage is voided (update_service.rb:528-530) and the event still goes active (update_service.rb:251-253).
cases.oracle: Stage statuses after the call.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: draft_trade_request_uuids: null crashes the request before it reaches the controller
cases.why: JSON null for an optional list is a normal client output; a before_action crash on it is a platform-wide 500.
cases.setup: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}}.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with draft_trade_request_uuids: null. 2. Check the response shape.
cases.expected: Must be a 422. Today the global before_action check_for_uuid runs `value.map` on every key containing 'uuids' (params_auth.rb:72-73); nil.map raises NoMethodError → untyped 500. This affects every endpoint, not only publish.
cases.oracle: Response is 422 {code, message}, not a 500.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: A draft with no stages can be published into an empty live event
cases.why: 'Publish without a schedule/without a stage' is the most basic publish precondition and nothing enforces it.
cases.setup: A fresh draft event group (POST /event_groups) with a line item but no stage attached.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with the publish body and draft_trade_request_uuids: []. 2. Read the event back.
cases.expected: Should be 422 (nothing to publish). Today process_trade_requests_for_publish loops over zero stages (update_service.rb:525-537) and the event is saved active (update_service.rb:251-253) — an active event nobody can bid on.
cases.oracle: Read-back: status active with zero stages confirms the defect.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: Publishing an RFP that ends after its RFQ is refused with 712
cases.why: The technical stage must finish before commercial bids close; publishing the wrong order makes evaluation impossible.
cases.setup: A draft event with an RFP stage (technical) and an RFQ stage, where the RFP bid_end_time is later than the RFQ bid_end_time. {{tradeId}} is one of them.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with both stage uuids in draft_trade_request_uuids. 2. Read the event back.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 712 'RFP duration exceeds RFQ end time. Please adjust.' from UpdateService#validate_rfp_rfq_bid_end_time (update_service.rb:303-312), checked before any stage is touched. Event stays draft.
cases.oracle: 422 with code 712; event status still draft; no stage active.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: A vendor cannot publish the buyer's event
cases.why: Wrong actor on the most powerful write in the module.
cases.setup: Signed in as the invited vendor of the sandbox event.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. As the vendor, PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with the publish body.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action' — EventGroupPolicy#update? requires the event's company in Current.allowed_companies and create_record permission (event_group_policy.rb:37-40), raised at event_groups_controller.rb:73 and mapped by pundit_user_not_authorized.
cases.oracle: 422 code 455; event unchanged.

cases.title: A numeric title crashes the update service's type signature
cases.why: Wrong-type scalars are the commonest client bug; every one of them is a 500 on this endpoint today.
cases.setup: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}}.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with title: 12345.
cases.expected: Must be 422. UpdateService#initialize is Sorbet-typed `title: T.nilable(String)` (update_service.rb:16); an Integer violates the sig and sorbet-runtime raises TypeError (no T::Configuration override exists), which is unrescued → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; title unchanged.

cases.title: An attachment URL from another company's S3 folder is refused
cases.why: Attaching another tenant's file path to your event (and so getting a signed URL for it) is a cross-tenant read.
cases.setup: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}}.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with attachments: [{url: "https://procol.s3.amazonaws.com/trade_files/docs/QA_Platform_999999999/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf"}].
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action' — validate_company_urls extracts company id 999999999 from /trade_files/<x>/<name>_<id>/ and it is not in Current.allowed_companies (s3_url_validator.rb:25-33; event_groups_controller.rb:78).
cases.oracle: 422 code 101; attachments unchanged.

cases.title: Publishing with an empty audience goes live with no participants
cases.why: 'Publish without participants' — an event no vendor can see, reported as live.
cases.setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event with its stage attached.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with audience_company_uuids: []. 2. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_audience.
cases.expected: Should be 422 (no participants). Today the key is present, so the stage is marked customised_audience 'restricted' (trade_controller_helper.rb:704-706) with no audience rows — a restricted stage nobody can see. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: Audience count 0 while status active confirms the defect.

cases.title: audience_company_uuids: null crashes with a 500
cases.why: The field the invite screen sends most; null when the user clears the picker.
cases.setup: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}}.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with audience_company_uuids: null.
cases.expected: Must be 422. check_for_uuid runs nil.map for the 'uuids' key (params_auth.rb:73) → NoMethodError → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: 501 audience entries are refused with 511
cases.why: The 500 cap is the only size guard on invitations; the count is taken on the raw list, which is what this case exploits cheaply.
cases.setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event with its stage attached.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH with audience_company_uuids containing 501 entries (here, 501 copies of "WrongUuid1="). 2. Read the event back.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 511 'Participants limit exceeded. Maximum 500 participants are allowed.' — set_customized_audiences counts the NEW audience ids before any validity filter and refuses > 500 (trade_controller_helper.rb:728-729). The whole publish is refused.
cases.oracle: 422 code 511; event still draft.

cases.section: Live audience — add and remove vendors on a running stage
cases.title: An invited vendor can call add-audience on the buyer's live stage
cases.why: A bidder able to change who else is bidding is a direct procurement-integrity breach.
cases.setup: Signed in as the invited vendor of stage {{tradeId}}; the stage's config has no is_user_allowed_to_modify_audience key (the default).
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}}`. 1. As the vendor, PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}} with audience_to_add_uuids: ["{{vendorUuid}}"]. 2. Check the response.
cases.expected: Must be refused (422 code 455). Today the policy is add_audience_live_auction? → allowed_to_view_event? = show? (read_record) && is_allowed_to_view? (trade_request_policy.rb:125-127, 222-224) — both true for an invited vendor — and is_audience_modification_allowed? returns true when the config key is absent (trade_request_model_helper.rb:936-941). A vendor can add (or, via remove_audience, remove) participants.
cases.oracle: A 200 'successfully added' to the vendor confirms the defect.

cases.section: Live audience — add and remove vendors on a running stage
cases.title: An invited vendor can remove a competitor who has not bid yet
cases.why: Same hole as add — used offensively it removes rivals before they quote.
cases.setup: Signed in as the invited vendor; another invited vendor (uuid in place of {{vendorUuid}}) has not bid.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/remove_audience?id={{tradeId}}`. 1. As the vendor, PATCH /v1/trade/remove_audience?id={{tradeId}} with audience_to_remove_uuids: [<competitor uuid>].
cases.expected: Must be refused (455). remove_audience_live_auction authorises with the same add_audience_live_auction? policy (v1/trade_controller.rb:52) and only blocks removal of vendors who already bid (512). The competitor is hidden.
cases.oracle: Competitor's audience row visibility after the call.

cases.section: Live audience — add and remove vendors on a running stage
cases.title: A vendor who has already bid cannot be removed
cases.why: Removing a bidder would orphan a live bid.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} (RFQ) has an active bid from {{vendorUuid}}.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/remove_audience?id={{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /v1/trade/remove_audience?id={{tradeId}} with audience_to_remove_uuids: ["{{vendorUuid}}"].
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 512 'You cannot remove a vendor who has already participated.' (v1/trade_controller.rb:63-66).
cases.oracle: 422 code 512; the vendor is still visible.

cases.title: Self-participating twice creates duplicate audience rows
cases.why: Dead uniqueness validation: any path that forgets to de-dupe produces double participants.
cases.setup: gate: `open_tenders`. Active open-tender event; caller is a mapped vendor.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/participants`. 1. POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/participants as the vendor. 2. POST it again. 3. Count the vendor's active audience rows per stage.
cases.expected: Second call should be a no-op or 422. Today Audience.create! runs again (participate_service.rb:38) and the model's uniqueness validation never fires because its condition compares the enum string to a symbol — `if: -> { self.status == :active }` is always false (audience.rb:36). Two active rows per stage.
cases.oracle: Row count 1 after the second call; 2 confirms the defect.

cases.title: Rejecting a vendor already in a proposal is refused with 750
cases.why: Rejecting an awarded vendor would invalidate an award in flight.
cases.setup: Active event with a proposal (active/selected/requested) that includes {{vendorUuid}}, or a commercial stage with a selected bid.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/reject_participant`. 1. PATCH reject_participant with the vendor and remarks.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 750 'You cannot reject a vendor that is already evaluated or awarded' (event_group_controller_helper.rb:2566-2573).

cases.title: A vendor cannot reject another participant
cases.why: Wrong actor; show? alone would let any viewer reject.
cases.setup: Signed in as an invited vendor.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/reject_participant`. 1. As the vendor, PATCH reject_participant with another company and remarks.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action' — after show? passes, the caller must be a purchaser or auction-team member (event_groups_controller.rb:987).

cases.title: 'Extending' to a past time ends a running stage immediately
cases.why: 'Extend to a past time' is a back door to force-ending an event.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} is live and its window has not ended; trade_force_close may be OFF.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with increase_auction_time: 946684800 (2000-01-01). 2. Read the stage.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 195 'Invalid time.' Today the only time check is the reopen rule, which applies only when the current end has ALREADY passed (trade_controller_helper.rb:5830-5831); a running stage's end is simply overwritten (5833). The stage closes now — a force-close that bypasses the trade_force_close config and its mandatory remarks.
cases.oracle: bid_end_time in the past and stage closed after a 200 confirms the defect.

cases.title: A non-numeric extension time is coerced to 1970
cases.why: Unvalidated numeric coercion on a time field turns garbage into an early close.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} is live.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with increase_auction_time: "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}".
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 195/507. The controller does `Time.at(increase_auction_time.to_i)` (trade_controller.rb:645); a non-numeric string .to_i's to 0, so the end becomes 1970-01-01 and the stage ends.
cases.oracle: bid_end_time unchanged (correct) vs 1970 (defect).

cases.title: Extending an expired stage without reopen permission is refused with 496
cases.why: 'Extend after close' — reopening must be a privileged act.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} (RFQ/auction) whose window has ended but is not yet closed; reopen configs off; caller is a normal buyer (not Procol employee, not super admin).
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with increase_auction_time in the future.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 496 'You are not allowed to reopen an expired event' (trade_controller_helper.rb:5830-5831). RFP stages are always reopenable (trade_controller_helper.rb:2027-2028).
cases.oracle: 422 code 496; end time unchanged.

cases.title: Extending after an award proposal exists is refused with 801
cases.why: Re-opening bidding under an award would let vendors re-price after seeing the outcome.
cases.setup: The event has a proposal in requested/active/selected status (for this stage's lot, if lots are used).
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with increase_auction_time.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 801 'You cannot edit the time as proposals are already submitted.' (trade_controller.rb:438-439; time_extension_blocked? trade_controller_helper.rb:6794-6804).

cases.title: A vendor cannot extend the deadline
cases.why: A bidder extending their own deadline is a fairness breach.
cases.setup: Signed in as the invited vendor of {{tradeId}}.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. As the vendor, PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with increase_auction_time.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 — TradeRequestPolicy#update? requires the stage's company in the user's allowed companies and create_record (trade_request_policy.rb:74-79; trade_controller.rb:404).

cases.title: Force-ending without remarks is refused with 783
cases.why: Force-ending must be justified and audited.
cases.setup: gate: `trade_force_close`. Stage {{tradeId}} is inside its submission window.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with force_end: true and no remarks.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 783 'Missing Remarks' — get_trade_force_close_data (trade_controller_helper.rb:5905), reached only when allow_force_end? is true (trade_controller.rb:423-425).
cases.oracle: 422 code 783; stage still running.

cases.title: status "closed" on a running stage closes it with no force-close gate
cases.why: The force-close feature flag is meaningless if a plain status write does the same thing.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} is running; trade_force_close OFF (use a copy — destructive).
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with status: "closed". 2. Read the stage.
cases.expected: Should be refused. Any present status goes to set_trade_request_in_active (trade_controller.rb:638-641), which assigns it verbatim (trade_controller_helper.rb:201). 'closed' is not a cancel status, so no remarks and no schedule handling — the stage is just closed, bypassing the trade_force_close config and the mandatory remarks (783).
cases.oracle: Stage status `closed` after a 200 confirms the defect.

cases.title: A stage cannot be withdrawn once a proposal is submitted
cases.why: Withdrawing under an award in approval would orphan the approval.
cases.setup: The event has a selected or requested proposal.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with status: "in_active" and withdraw_remark.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 841 'Cannot withdraw the event as proposals are already submitted.' (trade_controller_helper.rb:193-198).

cases.title: Withdrawing an event with remarks closes every stage
cases.why: The legal way down, and the baseline for the refusals below.
cases.setup: A dedicated active sandbox copy with no submitted proposals (destructive — run last).
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with status withdrawn and withdraw_remark {remarks, attachments: []}. 2. Read the event and stages.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. withdraw_event_group sets closed_at/closed_by, writes a withdraw_project_remark, marks each live stage in_active (drafts cancelled) and withdraws open proposals (update_service.rb:316-346).
cases.oracle: Event withdrawn; every stage in_active/cancelled; one remark.

cases.title: Withdrawing an event without withdraw_remark crashes with a 500
cases.why: A missing optional-looking field crashes the most consequential lifecycle action.
cases.setup: An active sandbox copy with at least one live stage.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with {status: "withdrawn"} only.
cases.expected: Must be 422 (remarks required). add_withdraw_remarks returns early for a blank remark, but the stage loop then reads `@withdraw_remark['remarks']` on nil (update_service.rb:327) → NoMethodError → 500 (the transaction rolls back).
cases.oracle: No 5xx; event still active.

cases.title: An event with a submitted proposal cannot be withdrawn
cases.why: Withdraw must never pull the rug from under an award in approval.
cases.setup: The event has a selected or requested proposal.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with the withdraw body.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 841 — each stage's set_trade_request_in_active refuses (trade_controller_helper.rb:193-198) and the error is returned from withdraw_event_group (update_service.rb:329-330). Transaction rolls back.
cases.oracle: 422 code 841; event still active.

cases.title: A buyer who does not own the event can withdraw it through the API
cases.why: The UI hides the button; the API does not enforce the same rule.
cases.setup: Signed in as a second buyer of the same company with create_record permission, who is not the event's owner and not a super admin. Dedicated sandbox copy.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. As that buyer, PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with the withdraw body.
cases.expected: Should be 101 — is_allowed_to_withdraw? (owner or super admin only, event_group_controller_helper.rb:2604-2611) is used only to build the UI config (…:552). The API only checks EventGroupPolicy#update? (company + create_record), so any buyer can withdraw anyone's event.
cases.oracle: A 200 for the non-owner confirms the defect.

cases.title: An uninvited vendor cannot read the event
cases.why: The core confidentiality rule of a restricted event.
cases.setup: Signed in as a vendor mapped to the buyer but NOT on any stage's audience.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. As that vendor, GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 — EventGroupPolicy#show? requires get_valid_stages_for_user to be non-empty (event_group_policy.rb:52-54), so the controller's own 682 check (event_groups_controller.rb:135) is never reached.
cases.oracle: 422 (455); no event payload.

cases.title: With restrict_event_visibility_to_owner, a non-owner buyer is refused
cases.why: The owner-only visibility switch is a customer-requested confidentiality control.
cases.setup: Config-dependent: restrict_event_visibility_to_owner ON. Signed in as a buyer who is not the owner, not an approver, has no assigned chat and no share, and is not in a planning designation.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} as that buyer.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action' — is_valid_owner is false (event_groups_controller.rb:140-143; trade_controller_helper.rb:5932-5946). With the config OFF the same user reads the event (200).
cases.oracle: 101 with config ON; 200 with config OFF.

cases.title: A vendor reading get_audience does not see competitors
cases.why: A competitor list is the single most sensitive thing a vendor could read.
cases.setup: Signed in as the invited vendor.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_audience`. 1. As the vendor, GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_audience. 2. Inspect the companies returned.
cases.expected: Refused, or a response listing only the vendor's own company. The action only authorises show? (event_groups_controller.rb:553), which an invited vendor passes; nothing in get_audience itself checks the caller is the buyer, so the participant list must be confirmed not to leak.
cases.oracle: No company other than the vendor's own in the response.

cases.title: A vendor cannot change the event's owner
cases.why: Wrong actor.
cases.setup: Signed in as the invited vendor.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/change_ownership`. 1. POST change_ownership as the vendor.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 533 or 455 — the lookup is scoped to Current.workspace (event_groups_controller.rb:1090-1091) and change_ownership? needs show? plus owner/super admin/Procol employee (event_group_policy.rb:88-90).
cases.oracle: 422; owner unchanged.

cases.title: When the current owner is deactivated, ownership can go to any active user anywhere
cases.why: Handing a tenant's event to an outsider is a cross-tenant data leak.
cases.setup: An event whose owner's UserCompanyMapping is no longer active; caller is a super admin; target is an active user of ANOTHER company (put their uuid in place of {{userUuid}}).
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/change_ownership`. 1. POST change_ownership with the foreign user.
cases.expected: Must be refused. validate_new_owner returns nil (valid) as soon as the current owner is inactive (trade_controller_helper.rb:5953-5954), and the target is looked up with User.active.find_by(id:) — not scoped to the workspace (event_groups_controller.rb:1093). A user from another tenant can be made owner.
cases.oracle: Owner after the call is not a member of the event's company → defect.

cases.title: Versioning a live event creates an amendment draft
cases.why: Baseline for every amendment case.
cases.setup: A dedicated active sandbox copy (after this, the original is no longer 'latest').
cases.steps: `POST /item_versions`. 1. POST /item_versions with {item_uuid: "{{eventGroupUuid}}", item_type: "EventGroup"}. 2. Read the returned uuid and new_item_data.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 {uuid, new_item_data} — item is active and latest, create_version? passes, create_version builds a replica (item_versions_controller.rb:5-27; versioning/methods.rb:3-18).
cases.oracle: A new draft event exists; the original is still active but not latest.

cases.title: A class name like "User" is refused before constantize
cases.why: constantize on user input is a known Rails RCE/IDOR shape; the allow-list is the only thing in the way.
cases.setup: Authenticated buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /item_versions`. 1. POST /item_versions with item_uuid {{userUuid}} and item_type "User".
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 — the allow-list check runs before `item_type.constantize` (item_versions_controller.rb:9-13), so no arbitrary class is instantiated.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2; no ItemVersion of type User.

cases.title: A raw integer item_id of another tenant's event cannot be versioned
cases.why: The lookup is unscoped, so the policy is the only barrier to amending another tenant's event.
cases.setup: Authenticated buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /item_versions`. 1. POST /item_versions with item_id: 1 (raw, not a uuid) and item_type EventGroup.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 888 (if id 1 is not active/latest) or 455 — the raw item_id is looked up unscoped (item_versions_controller.rb:13), then create_version? → update? requires the event's company in the caller's allowed companies (event_group_policy.rb:37-44).
cases.oracle: Never a 200; no ItemVersion created.

cases.title: A vendor cannot version the buyer's event
cases.why: Wrong actor.
cases.setup: Signed in as the invited vendor.
cases.steps: `POST /item_versions`. 1. POST /item_versions as the vendor.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 — create_version? = update? && create_record (event_group_policy.rb:42-44; item_versions_controller.rb:18).

cases.title: The original event can no longer be edited once an amendment exists
cases.why: Edits must go to the amendment, or the two versions diverge.
cases.setup: The sandbox event has been versioned (an amendment draft exists).
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} (the ORIGINAL) with the publish body.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 — `event_group.latest?` is false (event_groups_controller.rb:79).

cases.title: Publishing an amendment draft without amendment_remarks crashes with a 500
cases.why: The amendment remark is mandatory by design, but the refusal is a crash instead of a validation error.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} is an AMENDMENT draft (the new_item returned by /item_versions), with its stages.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/<amendment draft> with the publish body minus amendment_remarks.
cases.expected: Must be 422 (remarks required). publish calls add_amendment_remarks!(nil) for amendment drafts (update_service.rb:234), which raises StandardError 'Remarks for amendment not found' (versioning/methods.rb:103); nothing rescues it → 500.
cases.oracle: 422 with a message; draft unchanged.

cases.title: A vendor cannot clone the buyer's event
cases.why: A vendor cloning the buyer's event would copy its line items and specs into a new event.
cases.setup: Signed in as the invited vendor.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/create_clone`. 1. POST create_clone as the vendor.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 — create_clone? requires the event's company in Current.allowed_companies and create_record (event_group_policy.rb:46-50).

cases.title: Two publishes at once: the lock answers 516 but the second update still runs and then 500s
cases.why: The lock meant to stop double-publish both fails to stop it and turns it into a 500.
cases.setup: A draft copy with its stage attached.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. Fire two identical publish PATCHes to /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} within the same second. 2. Compare both responses and read the event and audience.
cases.expected: Expected: one 200 and one 422 code 516 'Transaction in Progress' with no second write. Today lock_transaction renders 516 but only `return`s from itself (event_groups_controller.rb:1513-1518), so update carries on, performs the publish/update a second time and then renders again → AbstractController::DoubleRenderError → 500. The after_action also deletes the lock the other request holds (…:1522-1526).
cases.oracle: Exactly one of the two answers is 516 and nothing is written twice (audience rows, remarks, notifications).

cases.title: Activation succeeds with one line item and with several
cases.why: It rules line-item count in or out as a factor — which is exactly what the regression investigation needed.
cases.steps: Activate a 1-item event and a 2-item event.
cases.expected: Both succeed.
cases.oracle: Both active with the expected item counts.

cases.title: Activation succeeds with a large audience below the cap
cases.why: Large audiences are normal on real tenants (154 on one client), and they are where the audience-application code path gets exercised properly.
cases.steps: `PATCH` with ~150 vendor uuids.
cases.expected: Active with all of them invited.
cases.oracle: Audience count equals the request; record the duration.

cases.title: More than 500 new audience companies is refused
cases.why: The explicit cap ("Participants limit exceeded. Maximum 500 participants are allowed.", 511), enforced during publish.
cases.steps: `PATCH` with 501 uuids.
cases.oracle: The event is not activated with 501; the message names the limit.

cases.title: Activation succeeds with the pricing sheet filled and with it empty
cases.why: It separates sheet completeness from activation. The UI enforces "sheet partially filled"; the API's tolerance is the thing to know.
cases.steps: Activate with sheet values present, then with none.
cases.expected: Both succeed at the API layer, or the refusal is a readable one.
cases.oracle: Record both outcomes; a 500 on either is the finding.

cases.title: Activating a non-existent event group is refused
cases.why: The first precondition, and it must not be a 500.
cases.steps: `PATCH /api/event_groups/<fabricated>`.
cases.expected: 422, code 533 "Project does not exist."
cases.oracle: That code and message.

cases.title: Activating a superseded version is refused
cases.why: `latest?` is checked before any write; without it, a stale client could overwrite newer work.
cases.setup: An event group with a newer version.
cases.steps: `PATCH` the older one.
cases.oracle: The newer version is untouched.

cases.title: A Procol-employee CSM can update without the trade permission flag
cases.why: The other policy branch. It is a deliberate back door for support, and it must work for the right people and nobody else.
cases.setup: A Procol employee who is CSM for the company, without `trade: create_record`.
cases.steps: `PATCH` to update.
cases.expected: Allowed.
cases.oracle: The update applies. Then repeat as a Procol employee who is *not* CSM for that company — that must be refused.

cases.title: A `purchase_request_id` must resolve to an active BOQ PR in the workspace
cases.why: An unvalidated link would attach an event to a foreign or inactive requisition.
cases.steps: `PATCH` with an inactive PR id, then with another workspace's PR id.
cases.expected: Refused both times (101).
cases.oracle: No link created.

cases.title: A draft-status PATCH with line items takes the generic branch
cases.why: It is the autosave path, and confusing it with publish is how a draft accidentally goes live.
cases.steps: `PATCH` with `status: "draft"` and `line_items` present.
cases.expected: Line items are updated; the event stays draft.
cases.oracle: Status draft; line items reflect the payload.

cases.title: Line items sent with `status: "active"` are ignored
cases.why: They are only read on the generic branch. Silently ignoring them is the documented behaviour, and a test expecting otherwise chases a phantom.
cases.steps: `PATCH` to activate with a new line item in `line_items`.
cases.expected: Activation succeeds; the new line item is **not** created.
cases.oracle: Line-item count unchanged. Record it as expected behaviour, not a bug — but flag it if the UI ever relies on it.

cases.title: `status: "active"` on an already-active event with no draft stages runs no service
cases.why: Neither branch guard matches, so no service is called and the controller still renders with variables that were never assigned. That is a latent edge case, and this is the case that watches it.
cases.setup: An active event group, no `draft_trade_request_ids`, no `line_items`, no `config`.
cases.steps: `PATCH` with `status: "active"`.
cases.expected: A coherent response — not a 500, not a silent state change.
cases.oracle: Assert no state change **and** no 500. ≈ BE-9.6.

cases.title: A terms attachment missing its `type` key is refused cleanly
cases.why: The structure is rehydrated into a PORO, so a missing key is a prime candidate for an unhandled exception — precisely what PRD §5 forbids.
cases.steps: `PATCH` with `terms_and_conditions.attachments: [{value: []}]`.
cases.expected: A 4xx with a readable message.

cases.title: Absent `terms_and_conditions.clauses` does not crash activation
cases.why: The UI sends an empty-but-present structure; other clients may send neither. Both must work.
cases.steps: `PATCH` with clauses nil, then with the whole key absent.
cases.expected: Activation succeeds both ways.
cases.oracle: No 500; the stored terms are empty rather than null-broken. ≈ BE-2.24.

cases.title: A stage absent from `draft_trade_request_uuids` is voided
cases.why: Any stage on the event group not named in the publish gets voided. A ghost stage that survived would accept bids nobody expects.
cases.setup: A draft event group with three draft stages.
cases.steps: `PATCH` naming two of them.
cases.expected: Two live stages; the third voided.
cases.oracle: The third stage's status is `void`; it is absent from the read payload. ≈ BE-9.3.

cases.title: Adding a draft stage to an already-live event publishes just that stage
cases.why: It is the second publish-branch trigger, and it must not re-publish or disturb the live stage.
cases.setup: A live event plus a new draft stage on the same event group.
cases.steps: `PATCH` with `status: "active"` and only the new stage's uuid.
cases.expected: The new stage goes live; the existing one is untouched, bids intact.
cases.oracle: Stage count +1; the original stage's bid count unchanged. ≈ BE-2.19.

cases.title: Activating an event group with zero stages is a safe no-op
cases.why: The publish loop over stages must tolerate an empty set rather than raising on it.
cases.setup: A draft event group with no stages.
cases.steps: `PATCH` to activate.
cases.expected: A coherent response, no exception.
cases.oracle: No 500; the resulting state is explainable. ≈ BE-9.5.

cases.title: An approval-gated stage becomes `requested`, not `active`
cases.why: On those tenants "published" means "pending approval", so an assertion of active is wrong there and would look like a publish failure.
cases.setup: gate: publish approval configured.
cases.steps: `PATCH` to activate.
cases.expected: Stage status `requested`; an approval record exists.
cases.oracle: Status requested; approval present. ≈ BE-9.7.

cases.title: Auto-routing to the auction team forces the stage to `draft`
cases.why: gate: `routeAuctionsToAuctionTeam`. It looks exactly like a failed publish unless you know.
cases.setup: gate: `routeAuctionsToAuctionTeam`. An auction stage.
cases.steps: `PATCH` to activate.
cases.expected: Stage status draft, assigned to the auction team.
cases.oracle: Status draft plus the assignment. ≈ BE-9.8.

cases.title: Activation fires invitation mails exactly once
cases.why: Three `after_commit` callbacks fire on the draft→active transition, each guarded against scheduled templates and dummy event groups. Two invitation mails per vendor is a support call; zero is a dead event.
cases.steps: Activate, then re-issue the same activation.
cases.expected: One invitation per vendor overall.
cases.oracle: Count the enqueued mail jobs across both calls.

cases.title: The activation response carries the full published shape
cases.why: The response is what the UI renders straight after publish; a missing key there is what makes the screen look broken after a successful publish.
cases.steps: Activate and inspect the response.
cases.expected: `stages`, `stage_vs_participants_data`, `config` (including `should_allow_awarding`) and `is_bid_placed_globally` all present.
cases.oracle: Each key present and internally consistent with the request.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: Re-publishing an already live event changes nothing
cases.why: A client that retries a publish after a timeout sends exactly this. Publish must be idempotent: no duplicate audience rows, no re-sent invites, no re-stamped window.
cases.setup: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}} is already active with stage {{tradeId}} live and vendor {{vendorUuid}} invited.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. Read GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_audience and note the participant count. 2. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with the exact publish body the journey sent. 3. Read the audience and stages again.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. The event is not a draft, so update_event_group_data takes the 'publish a new stage' branch (event_group_controller_helper.rb:29-31); every listed stage is already non-draft and is skipped by `next unless tr.draft?` (update_service.rb:267). Audience count, stage count and stage statuses are unchanged.
cases.oracle: Audience count and stage statuses are identical before and after; no second invite email is queued.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: A publish body with no status publishes nothing but answers 200
cases.why: A 200 that did nothing is the worst possible answer to a publish: the UI shows success while vendors are never invited.
cases.setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event with its stage attached (not yet published).
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with the publish body minus `status`. 2. Read the event back.
cases.expected: No branch of update_event_group_data matches (status is nil, line_items empty, config absent — event_group_controller_helper.rb:29-36), so nothing is written and the controller renders 200 with the unchanged event. Correct behaviour would be a 422 code 2 (Insufficient parameters); today the client is told 'OK' for a publish that did not happen — even the new title is dropped.
cases.oracle: Read-back status is still `draft` and the title is still the old one.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: Publishing a withdrawn event does not bring it back
cases.why: Resurrecting a withdrawn event would re-open bidding vendors were told had ended.
cases.setup: A withdrawn sandbox copy.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with the publish body. 2. Read the event back.
cases.expected: The event is not a draft, so only the new-stage branch runs; its stages are not drafts (`next unless tr.draft?`, update_service.rb:267), so nothing changes and it stays withdrawn. Ideally a 422 saying a withdrawn event cannot be published; today a silent 200.
cases.oracle: Read-back status remains `withdrawn`; no stage becomes active.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: status "draft" on a withdrawn event resurrects it
cases.why: Withdrawn is meant to be terminal (it is what the clone rules treat as a closed event).
cases.setup: A withdrawn sandbox copy.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with {status: "draft"}. 2. Read the event back.
cases.expected: Should be refused. Today execute() has no source-state guard and writes status draft over withdrawn (update_service.rb:62-79), making a closed event editable and re-publishable.
cases.oracle: Read-back status; if it is `draft`, the defect is confirmed.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: An empty draft_trade_request_uuids list publishes every stage
cases.why: Documents that [] means 'all', not 'none' — the opposite of what a reader expects, and the reason the next cases are dangerous.
cases.setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event with two stages attached.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with draft_trade_request_uuids: []. 2. Read every stage's status.
cases.expected: HTTP 200, event active. An empty list is `.present? == false`, so process_trade_requests_for_publish does not exclude anything and publishes every stage (update_service.rb:528-533).
cases.oracle: Every attached stage is active (or requested under approvals); none is void.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: A stage whose window has already started is slid forward to 'now' at publish
cases.why: Documents that 'publish with a stage in the past' is accepted by design and pins the duration-preserving shift.
cases.setup: A draft event whose stage was created with bid_start_time in the past (e.g. 10 minutes ago) and a 30-minute window.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. Note the stage's bid_start_time and bid_end_time. 2. Publish with the working body. 3. Read the stage schedule back.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. publish_auction calls TradeSchedule.change_auction_time (trade_controller_helper.rb:4542), which — when start_time <= now — moves start to now and end to now + original duration (trade_schedule.rb:138-147). The stage is live for its full duration.
cases.oracle: New start ≈ publish time; end − start equals the original duration.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: Under a create-trade approval flow the event reports active while its stage is 'requested'
cases.why: Two statuses that disagree is exactly where visibility leaks: a vendor must not be able to bid on a 'requested' stage.
cases.setup: Config-dependent: a workspace whose approval flow requires approval for create_trade. Draft event with an RFQ stage.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. Publish with the working body. 2. Read the event and the stage status.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. publish_auction sets the non-RFP stage to 'requested' when approval is needed (trade_controller_helper.rb:4536) while the event group is saved 'active'. Vendors must not see the stage until approved.
cases.oracle: Stage status `requested`; the invited vendor cannot place a bid on it.

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: Publishing an event uuid that does not exist answers 533
cases.why: A stale link or truncated uuid must give a clean not-found, not a type error.
cases.setup: Authenticated buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/WrongUuid1=`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/WrongUuid1= with the publish body.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 533 'Project does not exist.' — check_for_uuid decodes the id to nil and find_and_validate_event_group_and_pr returns 533 (event_group_controller_helper.rb:2580-2581).

cases.section: Publish — state and order of actions
cases.title: Publishing with a purchase_request_id that is not this workspace's BOQ PR is refused
cases.why: Linking another tenant's PR to your event would leak or consume their quantities.
cases.setup: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}}.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with the publish body plus purchase_request_id: 1 (a raw id that is not an active BOQ PR of this workspace).
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action' — the PR lookup is scoped to PurchaseRequest.active.boq for Current.workspace (event_group_controller_helper.rb:2583-2587). Note: a junk purchase_request_uuid decodes to nil and is silently ignored instead.
cases.oracle: 422 code 101; no PR mapping written.

cases.title: show_under_open_events: "yes" crashes with a 500
cases.why: Form-encoded clients send booleans as strings; this field is in the working publish body.
cases.setup: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}}.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with show_under_open_events: "yes".
cases.expected: Must be 422. The sig is `show_under_open_events: T.nilable(T::Boolean)` (update_service.rb:19); a String raises TypeError → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: An unknown key inside terms_and_conditions crashes with a 500
cases.why: Extra keys from a newer client version must not take the endpoint down.
cases.setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event with its stage attached.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with terms_and_conditions: {clauses: [], attachments: [], QA_Platform_extra: 1}.
cases.expected: Must be 422. publish builds `TermsAndConditions.new(**@terms_and_conditions.symbolize_keys)` (update_service.rb:242); an unknown keyword raises ArgumentError (terms_and_conditions.rb:34) → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; event still draft.

cases.title: terms_and_conditions.clauses as a string crashes with a 500
cases.why: A single clause sent as a string instead of a one-element array is an obvious client slip.
cases.setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event with its stage attached.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with terms_and_conditions: {clauses: "QA_Platform_tnc_{{stamp}}", attachments: []}.
cases.expected: Must be 422. TermsAndConditions#initialize is typed `clauses: T::Array[String]` (terms_and_conditions.rb:33) → TypeError → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: attachments as a string crashes the URL check with a 500
cases.why: The attachment guard added for tenant isolation itself crashes on the simplest malformed input.
cases.setup: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}}.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with attachments: "QA_Platform_file_{{stamp}}.pdf".
cases.expected: Must be 422. extract_urls_from_attachments calls `attachments.each` (event_groups_controller.rb:1749) — String has no #each → NoMethodError → 500, before the 101 URL check.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: A non-S3 attachment URL (external host or javascript:) is accepted unchecked
cases.why: A stored javascript:/phishing link shown to every invited vendor is a stored-XSS / phishing vector.
cases.setup: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}}.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with attachments: [{url: "javascript:alert('QA_Platform_{{stamp}}')"}]. 2. Read the event back.
cases.expected: Should be refused. url_belongs_to_allowed_companies? returns true for any URL that does not contain 'amazonaws.com/trade_files/' (s3_url_validator.rb:26), so the value is stored and later rendered to vendors as a link.
cases.oracle: Read-back attachments: if the javascript: URL is stored, the defect is confirmed.

cases.title: A title with a script tag is stored with the tag stripped
cases.why: Titles are shown in vendor emails and dashboards; this pins the global sanitiser for this endpoint.
cases.setup: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}}.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH with title "<script>alert(1)</script>QA_Platform_{{stamp}}". 2. Read the event back.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 (or 422), never 500. The global sanitize_input_params strips HTML tags from every string param (params_auth.rb:18-31), so the stored title must contain no <script>.
cases.oracle: Read-back title contains no '<script'.

cases.title: A junk vendor uuid in the audience is dropped silently
cases.why: Silent drops mean the buyer believes a vendor was invited when it was not.
cases.setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event with its stage attached.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH with audience_company_uuids: ["WrongUuid1="]. 2. GET get_audience.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. The uuid decodes to nil; get_valid_audience_ids keeps only ids with a BuyerSellerCompanyMapping in an allowed status (common_controller_helper.rb:110-115), so nil is dropped and no row is written. Should arguably be a 422 naming the bad id.
cases.oracle: Audience count is 0; no 5xx.

cases.title: Exactly 500 audience entries pass the cap
cases.why: Exact-limit boundary for the 511 guard, plus proof that duplicates collapse to one row.
cases.setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event with its stage attached.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH with 500 copies of "{{vendorUuid}}" in audience_company_uuids. 2. GET get_audience.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. 500 is not > 500 (trade_controller_helper.rb:728); create_audience de-duplicates with .uniq (common_controller_helper.rb:97), so exactly one audience row is written for the vendor.
cases.oracle: Status active; audience count 1.

cases.title: The same vendor listed twice gets one audience row
cases.why: Duplicate invites double-count a vendor in participation and awarding.
cases.setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event with its stage attached.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH with audience_company_uuids: ["{{vendorUuid}}", "{{vendorUuid}}"]. 2. GET get_audience.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; exactly one active audience row per stage — create_audience calls .uniq (common_controller_helper.rb:97). This matters because the Audience uniqueness validation is dead code (see the participate-twice case).
cases.oracle: One audience row for the vendor on each stage.

cases.title: A blacklisted vendor in the audience is dropped without telling the buyer
cases.why: Inviting a blacklisted vendor must never succeed, and silently not inviting them surprises the buyer.
cases.setup: A vendor ALREADY blacklisted in this workspace (do not blacklist one for the test); put its uuid in place of {{vendorUuid}}. Draft copy of the sandbox event.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH with audience_company_uuids: [<blacklisted vendor uuid>]. 2. GET get_audience.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 and the vendor is NOT invited: set_customized_audiences subtracts blacklisted vendors (trade_controller_helper.rb:695). Correct outcome for the vendor; the gap is that the buyer gets no error or warning.
cases.oracle: The blacklisted vendor has no audience row.

cases.title: A user uuid passed as a vendor uuid is decoded as a company id
cases.why: Untyped ids mean a wrong-kind id can collide with a real vendor, inviting a company nobody chose.
cases.setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event; {{userUuid}} is a user, not a company.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH with audience_company_uuids: ["{{userUuid}}"]. 2. GET get_audience.
cases.expected: Should be refused as 'not a vendor'. uuids are untyped encodings of integers (params_auth.rb:72-73), so the user's integer id is treated as a company id; it is invited only if it happens to equal a mapped vendor company id (common_controller_helper.rb:113). Usually dropped silently — occasionally invites an unrelated vendor.
cases.oracle: Audience rows after the call match no unexpected company.

cases.section: Live audience — add and remove vendors on a running stage
cases.title: Adding an already-invited vendor to a live stage creates nothing new
cases.why: Idempotency of the invite action — a double click must not re-send invites.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} is live with {{vendorUuid}} already invited.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}} with audience_to_add_uuids: ["{{vendorUuid}}"]. 2. Count audience rows.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 'Selected vendors successfully added'. bucket_audience_by_visibility removes ids that already have an active row (common_controller_helper.rb:24-29), so no row, email or activity log is created.
cases.oracle: Audience row count unchanged; no update_audience email queued.

cases.section: Live audience — add and remove vendors on a running stage
cases.title: Adding an empty list of vendors is refused with code 2
cases.why: Empty-array boundary for the only required field.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} is live.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}} with audience_to_add_uuids: [].
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (v1/trade_controller.rb:40).
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: Live audience — add and remove vendors on a running stage
cases.title: audience_to_add as a plain string crashes with a 500
cases.why: The endpoint accepts two spellings of the field and only one is type-normalised.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} is live.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}} with audience_to_add: "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}" (the non-uuid key, as a string).
cases.expected: Must be 422. The raw key is not uuid-decoded, so set_trade_request_audience runs `audience_to_add -= blacklisted_audience` on a String (common_controller_helper.rb:10) → NoMethodError → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Live audience — add and remove vendors on a running stage
cases.title: Adding vendors to a closed stage is refused with 95
cases.why: Inviting a vendor to a round that has ended would send them a dead invite.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} has closed (window over) or been withdrawn.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}} with a vendor.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 95 — the lookup is TradeRequest.active_or_draft (v1/trade_controller.rb:30), so a closed/withdrawn stage is 'not found'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 95; no audience row.

cases.section: Live audience — add and remove vendors on a running stage
cases.title: With audience modification disabled on the stage, a buyer cannot add vendors
cases.why: Stage-level lock on the audience; the one switch that closes the vendor hole above.
cases.setup: Config-dependent: stage {{tradeId}} has config is_user_allowed_to_modify_audience: false; caller is not a super admin.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}} with a vendor.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 685 'You are not allowed to update the audience' (v1/trade_controller.rb:37; trade_request_model_helper.rb:936-941). Super admins bypass it.

cases.section: Live audience — add and remove vendors on a running stage
cases.title: Live add-audience has no 500-participant cap
cases.why: The cap enforced at publish is trivially bypassed by publishing small and adding later.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} is live.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}} with 501 entries in audience_to_add_uuids.
cases.expected: For parity with publish it should be 422 code 511. set_trade_request_audience → process_audience_addition has no size check (common_controller_helper.rb:7-45); here the junk ids are then filtered, but 501 real vendors would all be invited.
cases.oracle: Response code: 200 (no cap) vs 511.

cases.section: Live audience — add and remove vendors on a running stage
cases.title: A vendor with a technical response cannot be removed from the RFP
cases.why: Technical-stage variant of the same guard.
cases.setup: An RFP stage (its uuid in place of {{tradeId}}) with a latest template response from {{vendorUuid}}.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/remove_audience?id={{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /v1/trade/remove_audience?id=<rfp stage> with that vendor.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 512 (v1/trade_controller.rb:59-61).

cases.section: Live audience — add and remove vendors on a running stage
cases.title: Removing and re-adding a vendor makes them visible again without a duplicate row
cases.why: The re-invite path must reuse the row, not duplicate it.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} is live; {{vendorUuid}} invited with no bid.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH remove_audience with the vendor. 2. PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}} with the vendor. 3. Count audience rows.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. The not-visible row is flipped back to visible by set_audience_visible (common_controller_helper.rb:37, 76-83); no second row.
cases.oracle: Exactly one row, visible: yes.

cases.title: Self-participating in a draft event answers 533
cases.why: A vendor must never join an event that has not been published.
cases.setup: gate: `open_tenders`. A draft event; caller is a vendor.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/participants`. 1. As a vendor, POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/participants.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 533 'Project does not exist.' — the lookup is EventGroup.active (event_groups_controller.rb:277-278).
cases.oracle: 422 code 533; no audience row.

cases.title: Self-participation without the open-tenders feature is refused
cases.why: The only uninvited-join path must be gated on the feature.
cases.setup: Config-dependent: the buyer company does NOT have open_tenders. Event active; caller is an invited vendor.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/participants`. 1. POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/participants as the vendor.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 — EventGroupPolicy#participate? = show? && record.company.open_tenders? (event_group_policy.rb:25-27).

cases.title: Self-participation after a stage has ended answers 33
cases.why: Joining a closed round would let a vendor into a window that has ended.
cases.setup: gate: `open_tenders`. Event active but one open-tender stage's window is over.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/participants`. 1. POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/participants as a vendor.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 33 'Order not active' — ParticipateService raises unless every open-tender stage is upcoming or running (participate_service.rb:27-29).
cases.oracle: 422 code 33; no audience row.

cases.title: Self-participation by a company with no vendor mapping crashes with a 500
cases.why: Unmapped/pending vendors browsing open tenders are exactly who clicks 'participate'.
cases.setup: gate: `open_tenders`. Active open-tender event; caller is a company that can see open tenders but has no BuyerSellerCompanyMapping with the buyer (e.g. the buyer itself).
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/participants`. 1. POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/participants.
cases.expected: Must be 422. BuyerSellerCompanyMapping.find_by(...) returns nil and `.dealing_with_company_id` is called on it (participate_service.rb:30-34) → NoMethodError, which is not a CustomException or RecordInvalid, so the controller's rescues miss it → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: Rejecting a participant without remarks is refused with 752
cases.why: Rejection emails the vendor; it must carry a reason.
cases.setup: Active sandbox event; {{vendorUuid}} has participated.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/reject_participant`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/reject_participant with company_uuid only.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 752 'Please enter remarks to reject the participant.' (event_groups_controller.rb:983).
cases.oracle: 422 code 752; vendor not in rejected_company_ids.

cases.title: Rejecting a vendor who never responded is refused with 751
cases.why: Reject is for responses; a non-participant should be removed from the audience instead.
cases.setup: Active sandbox event; {{vendorUuid}} invited but has no bid and no technical response.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/reject_participant`. 1. PATCH reject_participant with the vendor and remarks.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 751 'You cannot reject a vendor that has not participated in any event.' (event_group_controller_helper.rb:2575).

cases.title: Extending a closed RFQ stage answers 4
cases.why: Closed commercial stages must stay closed.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} is an RFQ with status closed.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with increase_auction_time.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found' — only active/draft/requested (plus closed for BOQ/RFP) are editable (trade_controller.rb:590-594).
cases.oracle: 422 code 4.

cases.title: Extending the RFP beyond the RFQ's end is refused with 712
cases.why: Same ordering rule as publish, on the extend path.
cases.setup: Live event with an RFP stage (its uuid in place of {{tradeId}}) and an RFQ stage.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/<rfp stage> with increase_auction_time later than the RFQ's bid end (no extend_rfq_time).
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 712 'RFP duration exceeds RFQ end time. Please adjust.' — update_trade_schedule → validate_rfp_rfq_bid_end_time (trade_controller_helper.rb:2025, 668-669).

cases.title: Moving the evaluation end to the past is refused with 195
cases.why: The evaluation path has the guard the bidding path lacks — this pins the good one.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} is in its evaluation (extra closing) window, which has not yet ended.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with extra_closing_time: 946684800.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 195 'Invalid time.' — get_extra_closing_trade_schedule refuses a time before now or before the window start (trade_controller_helper.rb:5889-5890). Note the bidding-window path has no such check (see the past-time extension case).

cases.title: force_end with trade_force_close OFF answers 200 and does nothing
cases.why: The buyer is told the event ended when it did not.
cases.setup: Config-dependent: trade_force_close is OFF for the company. Stage {{tradeId}} is running.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with force_end: true and remarks. 2. Read the stage.
cases.expected: Should be 422 (not allowed). allow_force_end? is false (trade_request_model_helper.rb:1621-1624; trade_controller_helper.rb:5928-5930), so the flag is ignored and, with no other field, the request falls through to a 200 success with the stage still open.
cases.oracle: Stage still running after a 200.

cases.title: force_end: "false" (a string) still force-ends
cases.why: Truthiness bug on a destructive flag; form clients send 'false'.
cases.setup: gate: `trade_force_close`. Stage {{tradeId}} is running (use a copy — destructive).
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with force_end: "false" and remarks. 2. Read the stage.
cases.expected: Should NOT end the stage. The gate is `params["force_end"].present?` (trade_controller_helper.rb:5929); the string 'false' is present, so the stage is force-closed.
cases.oracle: Stage still running after the call.

cases.title: An unknown stage status crashes with a 500
cases.why: Unvalidated enum assignment on the stage endpoint.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} is live.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with status: "banana".
cases.expected: Must be 422. `trade_request.status = 'banana'` on the TradeRequest enum raises ArgumentError (trade_controller_helper.rb:201) → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; stage unchanged.

cases.title: Cancelling a live (non-draft) stage is refused with 101
cases.why: Cancel is the draft-only removal; on a live stage it would skip vendor notification.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} is live.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with status: "cancelled".
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 — allowed_to_cancel? is false for any non-draft stage (trade_request_model_helper.rb:1495-1496; trade_controller_helper.rb:187-188). Live stages are withdrawn (in_active), not cancelled.

cases.title: withdraw_remark as a plain string crashes with a 500
cases.why: The event and stage endpoints disagree on this field's type.
cases.setup: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}}.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH with status withdrawn and withdraw_remark: "QA_Platform_withdraw_{{stamp}}".
cases.expected: Must be 422. The UpdateService sig is `withdraw_remark: T.nilable(T.any(Hash, ActionController::Parameters))` (update_service.rb:20); a String raises TypeError → 500. (The stage endpoint takes a string here, so clients confuse the two.)
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: A buyer cannot read another buyer's draft
cases.why: Drafts are private to their creator until published.
cases.setup: A draft owned by buyer A; signed in as buyer B of the same company (not super admin).
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. As buyer B, GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 — get_valid_stages_for_user returns [] for a draft whose owner is someone else (event_group.rb:512-514), so show? fails.

cases.title: A raw integer event id cannot be used to read another tenant's event
cases.why: Enumerable integer ids are the classic IDOR.
cases.setup: Authenticated buyer using the current web client version.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/1`. 1. GET /event_groups/1.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 533 or 455 — for uuid-enabled clients check_for_uuid decodes even an integer id (params_auth.rb:57-61), which yields nil (533); on an old client the raw id is used but EventGroupPolicy#show? blocks another company's event (455).
cases.oracle: Never a 200 with another company's event.

cases.title: During bidding, a non-owner buyer's read of a masked event shows no bid stats
cases.why: Sealed-bid confidentiality inside the buyer's own organisation.
cases.setup: Config-dependent: stage {{tradeId}} has show_bidding_stats (or closed-envelope bidding) enabled and is running; signed in as a buyer of the company who is not the owner/super admin and not on the auction team.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} and the stage details. 2. Inspect bid amounts/ranks.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with bidders/bids masked — event_masking_enabled? is true for a running stage viewed by a non-owner (trade_request_model_helper.rb:258-270); auction-team users are never masked.
cases.oracle: No bid prices or bidder names in the payload.

cases.title: Changing ownership without a new owner is refused with code 2
cases.why: Missing-field baseline.
cases.setup: Signed in as the event's owner.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/change_ownership`. 1. POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/change_ownership with {}.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 — validate_new_owner returns 2 for a blank owner (trade_controller_helper.rb:5950-5952).
cases.oracle: 422 code 2; owner unchanged.

cases.title: Transferring to a user outside the owner's teams is refused with 960
cases.why: Ownership moves within a team only.
cases.setup: Signed in as the owner (active); target user shares no active team with the owner (put their uuid in place of {{userUuid}}).
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/change_ownership`. 1. POST change_ownership with that user.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 960 'New Owner must be in same team as that of current owner' (trade_controller_helper.rb:5955-5957).

cases.title: A buyer who is not the owner cannot change ownership
cases.why: Taking over a colleague's event must need admin rights.
cases.setup: Signed in as another buyer of the company (not owner, not super admin).
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/change_ownership`. 1. POST change_ownership.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 (event_group_policy.rb:88-90).

cases.title: Ownership can be changed on a draft even though the UI forbids it
cases.why: UI-only rules are not rules.
cases.setup: A draft event (no active commercial stage) owned by the caller; a valid same-team user in place of {{userUuid}}.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/change_ownership`. 1. GET the event and note config.is_allowed_to_change_ownership (false). 2. POST change_ownership.
cases.expected: Should be refused to match the UI. is_allowed_to_change_ownership? requires an active commercial stage and restrict_event_visibility_to_owner ON (event_group_controller_helper.rb:604-614) but is only used for the UI config (…:563); the change_ownership action never calls it (event_groups_controller.rb:1089-1103), so the transfer succeeds.
cases.oracle: A 200 'Ownership transferred' while the config said false.

cases.title: Versioning the same event twice is refused with 888
cases.why: Two amendments of one event would fork it.
cases.setup: The sandbox event was just versioned once.
cases.steps: `POST /item_versions`. 1. POST /item_versions again with the same body.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 888 'Invalid Parameters' — the original is no longer latest? once a non-inactive ItemVersion exists (versioning/methods.rb:72-74; item_versions_controller.rb:13-16). The find_or_initialize idempotency in create_version (methods.rb:8) is therefore unreachable.
cases.oracle: 422 code 888; still one draft version.

cases.title: Versioning a TradeRequest (not allow-listed) is refused with code 2
cases.why: Stages must be amended through their event, not directly.
cases.setup: Active sandbox event.
cases.steps: `POST /item_versions`. 1. POST /item_versions with item_uuid {{tradeId}}, item_type "TradeRequest".
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 — ALLOWED_ITEM_TYPES is %w(EventGroup) (item_versions_controller.rb:3, 9).
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: Versioning a draft is refused with 888
cases.why: 'Versioning a draft' is a wrong-state action.
cases.setup: A draft event (its uuid in place of {{eventGroupUuid}}).
cases.steps: `POST /item_versions`. 1. POST /item_versions with the draft's uuid.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 888 — `!item.active?` (item_versions_controller.rb:14). Drafts are edited in place.

cases.title: Vendors cannot be added to the original once an amendment exists
cases.why: Same latest-version rule on the audience path.
cases.setup: The sandbox event has been versioned.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{tradeId}} (a stage of the original).
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 (v1/trade_controller.rb:36).

cases.title: The original's deadline cannot be extended once an amendment exists
cases.why: Same rule on the extend path.
cases.setup: The sandbox event has been versioned.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with increase_auction_time.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 (trade_controller.rb:403).

cases.title: An amendment published with blank remarks is accepted and notifies vendors with no reason
cases.why: Vendors get a 'the event was revised' email that does not say what changed.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} is an amendment draft.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH with the working body (amendment_remarks: {remarks: ""}).
cases.expected: Should be 422. `remarks.blank?` checks the HASH, which is non-empty (versioning/methods.rb:103), so a remark with an empty message is stored and event_revise_notification is sent with remark '' (event_group_controller_helper.rb:2632-2637).
cases.oracle: Remark message after publish.

cases.title: Cloning a live event returns a new draft
cases.why: 'Clone of a live event' baseline.
cases.setup: Active sandbox event not created from a PR.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/create_clone`. 1. POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/create_clone with {}. 2. GET the returned event_group_uuid.
