cases.expected: HTTP 200 {event_group_uuid}. CloneService copies the event and line items and ONLY the technical/RFQ stages (clone_service.rb:13-27); meta_data.source_event_group_id points at the source.
cases.oracle: New event is a draft; source unchanged; no auction stage copied.

cases.title: Listing scheduled events without the feature answers 904 (HTTP 403)
cases.why: Feature gate; also the only 403 (not 422) in this area.
cases.setup: Config-dependent: scheduled_events_enabled is OFF for the workspace.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/scheduled`. 1. GET /event_groups/scheduled.
cases.expected: HTTP 403, code 904 'Scheduled events feature is not enabled for your workspace' (event_groups_controller.rb:375). With the config ON it answers 200 with the templates.
cases.oracle: 403 with code 904.

cases.title: An unknown schedule_type crashes the publish with a 500
cases.why: User-supplied recurrence validated by raising is a guaranteed 500.
cases.setup: gate: `scheduled_events_enabled`. A draft copy with its stage.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH with the publish body plus config {is_scheduled_template: true, schedule: {schedule_type: "hourly", time_of_day: "09:00"}}.
cases.expected: Must be 422. handle_recurring_template → ScheduleBuilder.build raises ArgumentError 'Unknown schedule_type: hourly' (schedule_builder.rb:52; update_service.rb:567), unrescued → 500 after the stages were processed (the transaction rolls back).
cases.oracle: No 5xx; event still draft.

cases.section: Publish the event to the invited vendor — `PATCH /event_groups/:id`
cases.title: Publish the event to the invited vendor answers within 12 seconds
cases.why: A regression that makes a core call several times slower is a defect even when the body is right.
cases.setup: A buyer walking the API journey (RFQ only, Technical / RFP only, Technical + RFQ, Technical + Auction), at the step "Publish the event to the invited vendor".
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, do “Publish the event to the invited vendor” in the API journey (`PATCH /event_groups/:id`). 2. Time the answer.
cases.expected: The app answers within 12 seconds.
cases.oracle: Checked automatically on every API journey run; the report shows what actually came back. Engine check: `max_ms 12000`, learned from 27 real response(s).

cases.title: Read the event back answers within 25 seconds
cases.why: A regression that makes a core call several times slower is a defect even when the body is right.
cases.setup: A buyer walking the API journey (RFQ only, Technical / RFP only, Technical + RFQ, Technical + Auction), at the step "Read the event back".
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, do “Read the event back” in the API journey (`GET /event_groups/:id`). 2. Time the answer.
cases.expected: The app answers within 25 seconds.
cases.oracle: Checked automatically on every API journey run; the report shows what actually came back. Engine check: `max_ms 25000`, learned from 28 real response(s).

cases.title: Transient config keys are stripped from the persisted config
cases.why: `is_scheduled_template`, `schedule`, `ends_at` and `max_occurrences` are deliberately removed; a leak would make an ordinary event behave like a recurring template.
cases.steps: `PATCH` with all four in `config`. Read the event group back.
cases.expected: None of them are persisted.
cases.oracle: All four absent from the stored config.

cases.title: config as a string on publish crashes with a 500
cases.why: Config is T.untyped in the sig, so nothing screens it before it is used.
cases.setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event with its stage attached.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with the publish body plus config: "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}".
cases.expected: Must be 422. publish does `@config.respond_to?(:to_unsafe_h) ? … : @config.to_h` (update_service.rb:246); String#to_h does not exist → NoMethodError → 500 — after the stages were already processed, inside the transaction.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; event still draft (transaction rolled back).

cases.title: audience_except_company_uuids is ignored at publish
cases.why: A documented field that is silently ignored on one path is an invitation leak.
cases.setup: A draft copy of the sandbox event with its stage attached.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH with the publish body plus audience_except_company_uuids: ["{{vendorUuid}}"] and audience_company_uuids: ["{{vendorUuid}}"]. 2. GET get_audience.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 and the vendor IS invited: publish builds options with only audience_company_ids and stage_numbers (update_service.rb:229-238), so the except list never reaches set_customized_audiences. A client relying on 'everyone except' at publish gets the wrong audience.
cases.oracle: The vendor has an audience row despite being in the except list.

cases.title: Rejecting the same vendor twice records it twice and re-notifies
cases.why: Double-submits of a punitive action should not double-notify.
cases.setup: Active event; {{vendorUuid}} participated and is not awarded.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/reject_participant`. 1. PATCH reject_participant with the vendor and remarks. 2. Repeat. 3. Read precomputed rejected_company_ids (via get_audience).
cases.expected: Second call should be a no-op. Today there is no 'already rejected' check: the id is appended again and RejectParticipantWorker is enqueued again (event_groups_controller.rb:998-1000), so the vendor gets a second rejection email.
cases.oracle: rejected_company_ids contains the vendor once.

cases.title: The deadline can be extended to the year 2100
cases.why: An accidental extra digit leaves an event open for decades, blocking awarding.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} is live (RFQ, no proposal yet).
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with increase_auction_time: 4102444800 (2100-01-01) and remarks. 2. Read the stage schedule.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 today — get_auction_trade_schedule assigns the new end time with no upper bound (trade_controller_helper.rb:5833). A sane maximum would refuse it; at minimum it must not 5xx.
cases.oracle: Stage bid_end_time after the call.

cases.title: Extending the RFP with extend_rfq_time moves the RFQ too
cases.why: The escape hatch for the 712 rule must keep the RFP ≤ RFQ invariant.
cases.setup: Live event with RFP + RFQ; {{tradeId}} replaced by the RFP stage uuid.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/<rfp stage> with increase_auction_time past the RFQ end and extend_rfq_time: true. 2. Read both schedules.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. update_rfq_time_with_rfp runs before the RFP schedule is updated (trade_controller.rb:659-662), so the 712 check then passes.
cases.oracle: RFP end ≤ RFQ end after the call.

cases.title: Extending a stage that has not been published does not 500
cases.why: 'Extend before publish' is a wrong-order action the UI never sends.
cases.setup: Stage {{tradeId}} is a draft (event not published).
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}`. 1. PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}} with increase_auction_time.
cases.expected: Drafts are diverted to edit_draft before any schedule logic (trade_controller.rb:603), so the extension field is either ignored or applied as a schedule edit. It must not 5xx and must not mark the draft live.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; stage still draft.

cases.title: Withdrawing an already-withdrawn event again re-stamps it
cases.why: Double submit on a terminal action should not rewrite who closed it and when.
cases.setup: A withdrawn sandbox copy.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with the withdraw body again. 2. Read closed_at and withdraw remarks.
cases.expected: Should be a no-op or 422. There is no 'already withdrawn' guard: closed_at/closed_by are overwritten and a second withdraw_project_remark is written (update_service.rb:318-322); stage loop finds nothing.
cases.oracle: closed_at unchanged and one remark.

cases.title: Withdraw-remark attachments bypass the company URL check
cases.why: Same cross-tenant file leak the top-level guard exists to stop, via a side door.
cases.setup: A dedicated active sandbox copy.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH with the withdraw body whose withdraw_remark.attachments holds another company's trade_files S3 URL.
cases.expected: Should be 101 like top-level attachments. validate_company_urls runs only on params[:attachments] (event_groups_controller.rb:77-78); withdraw_remark.attachments goes straight into the Remark (update_service.rb:348-353) and is later signed for readers (event_group_controller_helper.rb:2620).
cases.oracle: The foreign URL is not stored.

cases.title: get_audience with malformed filters does not 500
cases.why: A rescue that returns nil just moves the crash one call later.
cases.setup: Active sandbox event.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_audience?filters=%7Bbad`. 1. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_audience?filters={bad.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 or 422, never 500. CommonFunctions.parse_filters rescues the JSON error and returns nil (lib/common_functions.rb parse_filters), and that nil is then handed to apply_audience_filters/apply_stage_participation_filters (event_groups_controller.rb:569-580), which must tolerate it.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: Versioning without item_type is refused with code 2
cases.why: Missing-field baseline.
cases.setup: Active sandbox event.
cases.steps: `POST /item_versions`. 1. POST /item_versions with item_uuid only.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 (item_versions_controller.rb:9-11).
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: Cloning a draft is refused by the policy (455), not by the state check
cases.why: Pins which code a client actually gets; the helpful message is dead code for this case.
cases.setup: A draft event.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/create_clone`. 1. POST create_clone on the draft.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 — create_clone? already requires !record.draft? (event_group_policy.rb:49), so the controller's friendlier 1122 'Only active or withdrawn events can be cloned.' (event_groups_controller.rb:111-113) is unreachable for drafts.

cases.title: Cloning a PR-created event is refused by the policy (455), not 1123
cases.why: Cloning a PR event would double-consume PR quantities; the user just gets a generic 'not authorized'.
cases.setup: An active event created from a purchase request.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/create_clone`. 1. POST create_clone.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 — create_clone? requires !record.created_from_pr? (event_group_policy.rb:49), so 1123 'Events with purchase requests cannot be cloned.' (event_groups_controller.rb:115-117) is never returned.

cases.title: Cloning a soft-deleted (in_active) event answers 1122
cases.why: The one state where 1122 is actually reachable.
cases.setup: An event in status in_active.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/create_clone`. 1. POST create_clone.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 1122 'Only active or withdrawn events can be cloned.' — the policy passes (not draft), the state check refuses (event_groups_controller.rb:111-113).

cases.title: Asking for a scheduled template without the feature is silently ignored
cases.why: No error tells the buyer their recurrence was dropped.
cases.setup: Config-dependent: scheduled_events_enabled OFF. A draft copy with its stage.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH with the publish body plus config {is_scheduled_template: true, schedule: {schedule_type: "daily", time_of_day: "09:00"}}. 2. Read the event.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; the event is published as a normal event — is_scheduled_template is only set when scheduled_events_enabled? (update_service.rb:250), and the schedule keys are stripped from the persisted config (…:247).
cases.oracle: is_scheduled_template false; no ScheduledJob.

cases.title: A time_of_day that is not HH:MM crashes with a 500
cases.why: Format validation by exception.
cases.setup: gate: `scheduled_events_enabled`. A draft copy with its stage.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH with schedule {schedule_type: "daily", time_of_day: "9am"}.
cases.expected: Must be 422. validate_time! raises ArgumentError 'time_of_day must be HH:MM format' (schedule_builder.rb:224) → 500. Note '25:99' passes the regex and fails later.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: Editing line items of a live scheduled template turns it back into a draft and pauses the job
cases.why: A silent pause of a recurring event is easy to miss; this pins the documented behaviour.
cases.setup: gate: `scheduled_events_enabled`. {{eventGroupUuid}} is an ACTIVE scheduled template with an active ScheduledJob.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`. 1. PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} with status draft and a line_items list. 2. Read the event and its job.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; transition_scheduled_template_to_draft flips the event and its active stages to draft and pauses the job (event_group_controller_helper.rb:17-19; trade_controller_helper.rb transition_scheduled_template_to_draft). Republishing resumes it (update_service.rb:541-554).
cases.oracle: Event draft; ScheduledJob paused.

journeys.title: The vendor's bid
journeys.goal: Sign into the supplier portal and submit a priced quote inside the window.

cases.section: How to place a bid in a Technical Stage
cases.title: Vendor submits a Technical Stage response after choosing to participate
cases.why: The technical bid is the vendor's entry into the create→publish→bid→award path; if it cannot be submitted, the buyer has nothing to evaluate before the commercial round.
cases.setup: Vendor (or Broker) invited to a live Technical Stage event; logged in to the vendor dashboard.
cases.steps: 1. Click the Event card to open the Event Overview screen. 2. Click the blue "I will participate" button. 3. On the Technical Stage screen, click "Select an option" and choose a vendor response (e.g. manufacturer, trader, seller). 4. Fill the Vendor Assessments and Line Item Specifications. 5. Scroll to the bottom and click "Submit".
cases.expected: The Technical Stage response is submitted and a confirmation appears at the top of the screen; the response now waits for evaluation by the buyer/technical Evaluator.
cases.oracle: Confirmation shown at the top of the screen after Submit; the vendor's Technical Stage response is recorded for the buyer to evaluate.

cases.section: How to participate in Events as a Vendor?
cases.title: Vendor participates in a live event and submits the Quote sheet
cases.why: This is the vendor bid submission on the core create→publish→bid→award path.
cases.setup: Vendor invited to a live event; logged in to the vendor dashboard where the live event appears as an Event card.
cases.steps: 1. Click the Event Card. 2. On the Event Overview screen, click the blue "I will participate" button. 3. Fill the Quote sheet, scrolling through the sections and filling all the Mandatory fields. 4. Scroll to the bottom and click "Submit".
cases.expected: The response is submitted, a confirmation appears at the top of the screen, and the response waits for evaluation by the buyer.
cases.oracle: Confirmation at the top of the screen after Submit; the submitted response is shown to the vendor.

cases.section: How to do Cost Breakdown as a Vendor?
cases.title: Vendor bids on the Sum Total in the auction and submits a locked cost breakdown
cases.why: Cost breakdown turns a lump-sum auction bid into per-item prices used for PO, audit and comparison; it is money on the award path.
cases.setup: Vendor participating in a live auction in Cost Breakdown Mode, with RFQ quotes already submitted.
cases.steps: 1. In the auction, reduce the Sum Total bid and click "Revise Bid". 2. Wait for the auction submission time to end so the Cost Breakdown Time (CBD time) begins. 3. Review the auto breakdown the system fills in across line items. 4. Click "Submit Cost Breakdown". 5. In the confirmation dialog, click "Yes, Submit".
cases.expected: The cost breakdown is locked and a confirmation message shows that the cost breakdown has been successfully submitted and justified.
cases.oracle: Confirmation message after "Yes, Submit"; item prices are no longer editable.

cases.section: How to do Cost Breakdown as a Vendor?
cases.title: Sum Total reduced by a Fixed Value
cases.why: The reduction method decides the price the vendor commits to; the new bid must equal the total minus the fixed amount.
cases.setup: Vendor in a live auction in Cost Breakdown Mode with a Sum Total (e.g. ₹11,204.34).
cases.steps: 1. In the dropdown next to "Fixed Value", keep "Fixed Value". 2. Enter a reduction (e.g. ₹204.34). 3. Click "Revise Bid".
cases.expected: The vendor sees the new current bid reflecting the fixed-value reduction.
cases.oracle: Current bid equals the Sum Total minus the entered fixed value.

cases.section: How to do Cost Breakdown as a Vendor?
cases.title: Sum Total reduced by a Percentage
cases.why: Percentage discounts are the second reduction method; the computed bid must match the percentage applied.
cases.setup: Vendor in a live auction in Cost Breakdown Mode with a Sum Total.
cases.steps: 1. In the dropdown next to "Fixed Value", select "Percentage". 2. Enter a discount (e.g. 10%). 3. Click "Revise Bid".
cases.expected: The discount is applied on the Sum Total and the new current bid reflects the reduction.
cases.oracle: Current bid equals the Sum Total reduced by the entered percentage.

cases.section: How to do Cost Breakdown as a Vendor?
cases.title: Line item price above the RFQ value is rejected with the amount to reduce
cases.why: The breakdown must never raise any item above what was quoted in the RFQ.
cases.setup: Vendor in Cost Breakdown Time.
cases.steps: 1. Edit one line item's price to a value greater than its RFQ value. 2. Try to submit the cost breakdown.
cases.expected: An error message is shown and the system indicates how much needs to be reduced further.
cases.oracle: Error message visible with the remaining reduction amount; the breakdown is not accepted.

cases.section: How to do Cost Breakdown as a Vendor?
cases.title: Breakdown total that does not match the auction bid is rejected
cases.why: Per-item prices must add up to the price won in the auction, or PO values drift from the award.
cases.setup: Vendor in Cost Breakdown Time.
cases.steps: 1. Edit line item prices so their total exceeds the submitted auction bid. 2. Try to submit the cost breakdown.
cases.expected: An error message is shown and the system indicates how much needs to be reduced further; the total must match the submitted auction bid.
cases.oracle: Error message with the remaining reduction amount; submission only succeeds once the total equals the auction bid.

cases.section: How to do Cost Breakdown as a Vendor?
cases.title: Final-submission warning and lock after "Yes, Submit"
cases.why: Once submitted the per-item prices are final; the vendor must be warned and the lock must hold.
cases.setup: Vendor in Cost Breakdown Time with a valid breakdown.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Submit Cost Breakdown". 2. Read the confirmation dialog. 3. Click "Yes, Submit". 4. Try to edit an item price.
cases.expected: The dialog reads "This is the final submission for item prices. Once submitted, you won't be able to change these item prices."; after "Yes, Submit" the breakdown is locked and item prices cannot be changed.
cases.oracle: Dialog text shown; after submission the item price fields are not editable.

cases.title: An invited vendor sees the event in their Live list
cases.why: If the invitation does not arrive at the portal, nothing else in this section can run, and the cause is on the buyer's side.
cases.setup: A live event with this vendor's company invited by name.
cases.steps: Log in to the portal. Open the events list. Search the event title.
cases.expected: The event is listed under Live with its ref id.
cases.oracle: One matching card; fail loudly rather than falling back to "the first Live event" for any case that asserts something about *this* event.

cases.title: An uninvited vendor does not see the event
cases.why: It is the first half of the isolation promise (PRD §7.2) and it is cheap to check.
cases.setup: A live event; a vendor not on its audience.
cases.steps: Search for the title in that vendor's portal.
cases.expected: No result; direct URL access is refused.
cases.oracle: Zero cards; a direct navigation lands on a refusal, not the event.

cases.title: The stage tab exposes the bid sheet
cases.why: The actual entry to bidding.
cases.steps: Switch to the stage tab. Press "Add bid"/"Place bid" if the build shows one.
cases.expected: The bid sheet renders with the buyer's line items and editable price cells.
cases.oracle: At least one non-disabled price cell exists.

cases.title: The vendor sees the buyer's line items, quantities and locations
cases.why: The vendor prices against them; a wrong quantity is a wrong bid.
cases.setup: A live event with two line items of known quantities.
cases.steps: Read the sheet.
cases.expected: Both items, with the buyer's quantities, units and delivery locations.
cases.oracle: Row-by-row comparison against the buyer's event.

cases.title: The vendor fills price cells and the total computes
cases.why: The total is what the buyer compares, and it is derived — a wrong derivation is invisible to both sides.
cases.setup: A bid sheet with a quantity of 10 and a price cell.
cases.steps: Enter 100.
cases.expected: Total = 1000 (plus GST if the template has it, per its rule).
cases.oracle: Rendered total equals the expected arithmetic.

cases.title: Every price cell on a multi-line sheet is filled
cases.why: Submitting with one row priced can be *allowed* while being an incomplete bid. A test that fills only the first row can pass while creating a bid the buyer cannot use.
cases.setup: A 3-line event.
cases.steps: Fill all three price cells. Submit.
cases.expected: All three prices are on the submitted bid.
cases.oracle: Count the cells filled and assert it equals the row count; then check the buyer's comparison shows three prices.

cases.title: Submitting the bid confirms it
cases.why: The core acceptance criterion of PRD §3.4.
cases.steps: Press Submit and confirm if a modal appears.
cases.expected: A success state — the bid is shown as submitted with its values.
cases.oracle: The portal shows the bid as submitted; the buyer's bid count rises by one. Assert both sides, not just the portal's toast.

cases.title: Submitting an empty bid is refused
cases.why: An empty bid would count as participation without a price.
cases.steps: Open the sheet and press Submit with nothing entered.
cases.expected: Refused — the control is disabled or the attempt is rejected with a message.
cases.oracle: No bid appears on the buyer's side.

cases.title: A negative price is refused
cases.why: The backend has a dedicated refusal ("Please enter a valid price", 106) and the portal should not need it.
cases.steps: Enter `-100`. Submit.
cases.expected: Refused with a readable message.
cases.oracle: No bid created; message shown.

cases.title: Text in a price cell is refused, not coerced
cases.why: A coerced `0` is a winning bid.
cases.steps: Type `abc` into a price cell.
cases.expected: Refused or cleared with a message; never stored as 0.
cases.oracle: No bid with price 0 created.

cases.title: Bidding before the window opens is refused
cases.why: An Upcoming event must not accept bids; the product says "Kindly wait for the auction to start".
cases.setup: An Upcoming event with this vendor invited.
cases.steps: Open it and try to bid.
cases.expected: Cells are not editable, or submission is refused with that message.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: Bidding after the window closes is refused
cases.why: The clearest integrity rule in the product: "Order not active" (33). A late bid that lands is a fairness failure, not a UI bug.
cases.setup: A closed event with this vendor invited.
cases.steps: Open it and try to bid.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: Bid count on the buyer's side unchanged.

cases.title: Bidding on a withdrawn event is refused
cases.why: Withdrawal must be immediate for vendors, not just cosmetic for the buyer.
cases.setup: A withdrawn event.
cases.steps: As an invited vendor, attempt a bid.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: Revising a bid inside the window replaces the value
cases.why: Revision is normal in an auction, and the *latest* bid is what ranks.
cases.setup: A live event with a submitted bid of 100.
cases.steps: Revise to 90 and submit.
cases.expected: The vendor's current bid is 90; the buyer sees 90 as current with 100 in history.
cases.oracle: Buyer's current price = 90; the revision is visible in the bid history.

cases.title: A vendor cannot see another vendor's price
cases.why: PRD §7.2 in the plainest possible form. This is the case you would keep if you could keep only one from this section.
cases.setup: A live event with bids from vendor A (100) and vendor B (90).
cases.steps: As A, inspect every screen the portal offers — sheet, overview, indicators, any comparison.
cases.expected: A sees their own 100 and never B's 90. Rank or a colour is acceptable; a competitor's number is not.
cases.oracle: Scan the rendered page text and the network responses the portal receives for B's price. Checking only the visible DOM is not enough — a price present in the payload is a leak.

cases.title: Two vendors bidding on one event produce two competing bids
cases.why: Everything in §17 needs more than one bid to award between, and a journey that accidentally bids twice as the *same* vendor produces one bid while claiming two — a test asserting "two bids" then passes on a broken fixture.
cases.setup: A live event with two distinct vendor companies invited.
cases.steps: As vendor A, bid 100. As vendor B, bid 90.
cases.expected: Two bids from two different companies.
cases.oracle: The buyer's comparison lists two distinct vendor names — assert the *names differ*, not just that the count is 2.

cases.section: How to not Participate in an Event
cases.title: Vendor declines an event with a reason
cases.why: Declining tells the buyer early that no bid is coming, so the buyer can chase other vendors.
cases.setup: Vendor invited to a live event, on the Event Overview screen (opened from the Event card).
cases.steps: 1. Click the blue "I don't wish to participate" button. 2. In the dialogue box that opens, select a reason for not participating. 3. Confirm by clicking "I will not participate".
cases.expected: The non-participation is recorded and the bottom of the screen shows "You've decided to not participate, Want to change your response?"
cases.oracle: The text "You've decided to not participate, Want to change your response?" is displayed at the bottom of the screen.

cases.section: How to Regret Items in a sourcing events?
cases.title: Regret Item writes "Regret" into every vendor response for the item
cases.why: Item-level regret must be unambiguous to the buyer; every response for the item should read as a regret.
cases.setup: Vendor participating in an event, on the Technical Stage Event tab, with at least one line item.
cases.steps: 1. Click the ⚡ Quick Fill option for a line item. 2. Press "Regret Item".
cases.expected: All Vendor Responses for that item are written as "Regret".
cases.oracle: Each vendor response field for the item shows "Regret".

cases.section: How to Regret Items in a sourcing events?
cases.title: Regretted item is crossed out in the Technical Stage and in later RFQ and RA stages
cases.why: The regret must carry forward; an item reappearing as biddable in RFQ or RA would contradict what the vendor told the buyer.
cases.setup: Vendor who regretted a line item in the Technical Stage of a multi-stage event with RFQ and RA stages.
cases.steps: 1. Regret a line item via ⚡ Quick Fill → "Regret Item" in the Technical Stage. 2. View the item in the Technical Stage. 3. When the RFQ stage and the RA stage open, view the same item there.
cases.expected: The line item is crossed out in the technical stage and in all future stages (RFQ and RA).
cases.oracle: The item is shown struck through in the Technical Stage, the RFQ stage and the RA stage.

cases.section: How to Regret Items in a sourcing events?
cases.title: Regretted item is crossed out in the buyer's QCS
cases.why: The buyer compares bids in the QCS; a regretted item must not look like a missing or zero bid.
cases.setup: Vendor regretted a line item; buyer who owns the event with access to the QCS.
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, regret a line item via ⚡ Quick Fill → "Regret Item". 2. As the buyer, open the QCS for the event.
cases.expected: The regretted line item is crossed out in the QCS for the buyer.
cases.oracle: The item for that vendor is shown struck through in the buyer's QCS.

cases.section: How to Regret Items in a sourcing events?
cases.title: Vendor cannot place a commercial bid for a regretted item
cases.why: The article states a hard restriction; allowing a commercial bid after a regret would corrupt the comparison.
cases.setup: Vendor who regretted a line item in the Technical Stage; the commercial (RFQ/RA) stage is open.
cases.steps: 1. Open the commercial stage of the event. 2. Try to enter a price for the regretted item.
cases.expected: The vendor is not able to place a commercial bid for the item.
cases.oracle: No bid can be entered or submitted for the regretted item.

cases.section: How to participate in Events as a Vendor?
cases.title: All Mandatory fields of the form must be filled before submitting
cases.why: The article instructs vendors to fill every Mandatory field; an incomplete bid reaching the buyer would be unusable.
cases.setup: Vendor on the event's form after clicking "I will participate".
cases.steps: 1. Leave one Mandatory field empty and fill the rest. 2. Scroll to the bottom and click "Submit". 3. Fill the empty Mandatory field and click "Submit" again.
cases.expected: A complete submission requires all Mandatory fields; with all filled, the submission succeeds with the confirmation at the top of the screen.
cases.oracle: Record how the form treats the empty Mandatory field; confirm the submission goes through only once all Mandatory fields are filled.

cases.section: How do I add Subsidiaries as a Broker?
cases.title: Broker adds a supplier with a Tax ID
cases.why: Brokers can only bid on behalf of suppliers they have onboarded; this is how a supplier gets there.
cases.setup: Broker logged in to the Vendor/Supplier Dashboard.
cases.steps: 1. Click the Profile icon on the top-right corner and click "Manage Suppliers". 2. Click the "Add Supplier" button at the top-right. 3. Fill Full Name, Phone Number (select country code and enter number), Email Address, and Business Location (searchable dropdown). 4. Enter the Tax ID in the field that appears for the selected location. 5. Click "Done".
cases.expected: A tooltip confirms "Vendor Created." and the broker is redirected back to the Suppliers List, where the new supplier is visible.
cases.oracle: "Vendor Created." tooltip shown; the new supplier appears in the Suppliers List.

cases.section: How do I add Subsidiaries as a Broker?
cases.title: Broker can bid on behalf of a newly added supplier in a future event
cases.why: Bidding on behalf of suppliers is the purpose of adding them; it touches the bid path.
cases.setup: Broker who has just added a supplier (visible in the Suppliers List); a later event the broker is invited to.
cases.steps: 1. Open the future event as the broker. 2. Place a bid on behalf of the newly added supplier.
cases.expected: The broker can bid on behalf of the supplier in the event.
cases.oracle: The bid is recorded against the supplier (at the article's level of detail; the article gives no further UI steps).

cases.section: How to do Cost Breakdown as a Vendor?
cases.title: During the auction the vendor can only bid on the Sum Total
cases.why: The article restricts auction bidding to the lot total; per-item bidding here would bypass the breakdown step.
cases.setup: Vendor in a live auction in Cost Breakdown Mode.
cases.steps: 1. Open the auction bidding screen. 2. Read the message shown and look for the bid inputs available.
cases.expected: The message reads "You are bidding on the total lot amount we received from your RFQ Quotes. A request for line item-wise cost breakdown will be triggered once the auction submission time ends." and only the Sum Total can be bid on.
cases.oracle: The message text is shown; no per-line-item bid input is available during the auction.

cases.section: How to do Cost Breakdown as a Vendor?
cases.title: Cost Breakdown Time begins automatically when auction submission time ends
cases.why: Vendors must be prompted to break down their bid without any manual trigger, or per-item prices never get captured.
cases.setup: Vendor who placed a Sum Total bid in a Cost Breakdown Mode auction.
cases.steps: 1. Wait for the auction submission time to end.
cases.expected: The Cost Breakdown Time (CBD time) begins automatically and the vendor is prompted to break down the submitted total bid across line items.
cases.oracle: CBD time is shown and the line-item breakdown screen is presented without vendor action.

cases.section: How to do Cost Breakdown as a Vendor?
cases.title: Auto breakdown is pre-filled pro rata and each discount or price is editable
cases.why: The pro-rata default saves effort, but vendors must be able to shape their per-item prices.
cases.setup: Vendor in Cost Breakdown Time after an auction.
cases.steps: 1. Open the breakdown screen and review the pre-filled values. 2. Change the discount applied to one line item. 3. Manually edit the price of another line item.
cases.expected: The system has already filled an auto breakdown (discounts by pro rata distribution); the vendor can manually change each discount and manually edit each price.
cases.oracle: Pre-filled per-item values present on open; edited discount and price are held in the fields.

cases.section: How to do Cost Breakdown as a Vendor?
cases.title: Submitted breakdown can only be revised if the buyer reopens the window or shares counteroffers
cases.why: The lock has two stated exceptions; they must re-enable revision and nothing else should.
cases.setup: Vendor with a submitted cost breakdown; buyer who owns the event.
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, confirm the breakdown cannot be revised. 2. As the buyer, reopen the cost breakdown window (or share counteroffers). 3. As the vendor, try to revise the breakdown again.
cases.expected: The vendor cannot revise the breakdown unless the buyer reopens the window or shares counteroffers.
cases.oracle: Revision blocked before the buyer action and possible after it (buyer-side steps are not described in the article).

cases.title: Opening the event lands on Event Overview
cases.why: It is the tab a test must move *off* of. Filling "the sheet" on the overview finds no cells and reports a missing bid form.
cases.setup: An invited vendor on a live event.
cases.steps: Open the event card.
cases.expected: Event Overview, with the event's details and a stage tab beside it.
cases.oracle: The overview is active; at least one other tab exists.

cases.title: Zero as a price is either refused or accepted deliberately
cases.why: Free-of-charge lines are real in some categories; whichever the product allows, it must be consistent and visible to the buyer.
cases.steps: Enter `0` and submit.
cases.expected: Consistent behaviour, stated on screen.
cases.oracle: If accepted, the buyer's comparison shows 0 rather than blank.

cases.title: A negative quantity in the vendor's quantity column is refused
cases.why: Separate refusal from price ("Quantity must be greater than zero", 35).
cases.steps: Enter `-1` as the offered quantity.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: Offering more than the requested quantity is refused
cases.why: The backend refuses it ("Quantity should be less than requested quantity", 511) and a vendor over-offering distorts the comparison.
cases.setup: A line item requesting 10.
cases.steps: Offer 15.
cases.expected: Refused with that message.
cases.oracle: No bid, or the bid capped and the vendor told.

cases.title: Offering in a different unit is refused
cases.why: "Quantity should be in same unit as requested" (512) — a unit mismatch makes every price incomparable.
cases.steps: Change the unit on the offer.
cases.expected: Refused, or the unit is not editable at all.
cases.oracle: The submitted bid's unit equals the requested unit.

cases.title: A second bid without revising is refused as already placed
cases.why: The backend distinguishes "revise" from "create again" and refuses the second create ("You have already placed a bid for this company.", 99 / "A bid has already been placed by your team", 96).
cases.setup: A vendor with an active bid.
cases.steps: Attempt to create a fresh bid rather than revising.
cases.expected: Refused with that message.
cases.oracle: One active bid remains.

cases.title: Another user from the same vendor company cannot bid twice
cases.why: "A bid has already been placed by your team" — the check is at company level, which is the level that matters commercially.
cases.setup: Two users on the same vendor company; one has bid.
cases.steps: As the second user, try to bid.
cases.expected: Refused, with the existing bid visible instead.
cases.oracle: Still one bid for that company.

cases.title: Rank feedback is shown on a rank-based auction
cases.why: It is the only competitive signal the vendor gets, and it is why the strategy exists.
cases.setup: A live rank auction with two bids.
cases.steps: As the trailing vendor, read the indicator.
cases.expected: A rank (e.g. L2), not a price.
cases.oracle: Rank shown; no competitor price anywhere.

cases.title: Best price is shown on a price-based auction, per configuration
cases.why: Here a number *is* shown deliberately, so the isolation rule and this rule must not be confused with one another.
cases.setup: gate: show-best-price. A live price auction with two bids.
cases.steps: As the trailing vendor, read the indicator.
cases.expected: The best price is shown, without attribution to a vendor.
cases.oracle: The number equals the leading bid; no vendor name accompanies it.

cases.title: A vendor answers the technical questionnaire before pricing
cases.why: It is the RFP half of a two-stage event, and the pricing stage should not be reachable until it is done.
cases.setup: A live RFP + RFQ event with this vendor invited.
cases.steps: Open the technical stage. Answer each question. Submit the response.
cases.expected: The response is submitted and the buyer can see it.
cases.oracle: The buyer's view shows a submitted technical response for this vendor.

cases.title: An incomplete technical response is refused
cases.why: A partial questionnaire cannot be evaluated, and evaluators score against completeness.
cases.steps: Leave a required question blank and submit.
cases.expected: Refused, naming the missing question.
cases.oracle: No submitted response; message identifies the gap.

cases.title: Attaching a document to a bid works and the buyer can open it
cases.why: Bid attachments are contractual (certificates, specs) and a broken link is only discovered at award time.
cases.setup: A live event, bid in progress.
cases.steps: Attach a PDF and submit.
cases.expected: The buyer sees and can download the attachment.
cases.oracle: The file opens from the buyer's side with the original name.

cases.title: A bid survives a portal reload before submission
cases.why: A 40-row sheet lost to a refresh is the vendor's worst experience, and drafts exist to prevent it.
cases.setup: A partially filled bid sheet.
cases.steps: Reload the portal and reopen the event.
cases.expected: Either the draft values are restored, or the vendor is warned before leaving. Not silently emptied.
cases.oracle: Values restored, or a warning was shown.

cases.section: How to place a bid in a Technical Stage
cases.title: Vendor type is chosen from the "Select an option" list
cases.why: The vendor-type answer is part of the vendor assessment the buyer scores; each option must be selectable.
cases.setup: Vendor who has clicked "I will participate" on a Technical Stage event and is on the Technical Stage screen.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Select an option" in the vendor responses. 2. Choose one of the options (manufacturer, trader, seller, etc.). 3. Repeat with each of the other options.
cases.expected: Each listed option (manufacturer, trader, seller, etc.) can be selected and is held as the vendor response.
cases.oracle: The selected option is shown in the vendor response field after selection.

cases.section: How to place a bid in a Technical Stage
cases.title: Quick Fill "Same as requested" copies the buyer's values into all responses
cases.why: Quick Fill is the fast path for compliant vendors; a wrong copy would submit specifications the vendor never agreed to.
cases.setup: Vendor on the Technical Stage screen of an event whose buyer specified values for the questions.
cases.steps: 1. Click the "⚡Quick Fill" option. 2. Select "Same as requested".
cases.expected: The values specified by the buyer are immediately copy-pasted into the vendor's responses for all the specified questions.
cases.oracle: Every vendor response field for the specified questions shows the buyer's requested value.

cases.section: How to place a bid in a Technical Stage
cases.title: Quick Fill "Regret Item" marks an item as not being bid in the Technical Stage
cases.why: Regretting is the vendor's item-level opt-out; the buyer must see that no bid will come for that item.
cases.setup: Vendor on the Technical Stage screen of an event with at least one line item.
cases.steps: 1. Click the "⚡Quick Fill" option for a line item. 2. Press "Regret Item".
cases.expected: The item is regretted, meaning the vendor will not be placing a bid for this item.
cases.oracle: The line item shows as regretted on the Technical Stage screen (at the article's level of detail; see the Regret Items article for the exact effect).

cases.section: How to place a bid in a Technical Stage
cases.title: Technical Stage tab reached manually when not opened automatically
cases.why: If the automatic hop fails, the vendor must still be able to find the Technical Stage form.
cases.setup: Vendor who has clicked "I will participate" on a Technical Stage event but is not automatically taken to the Technical Stage.
cases.steps: 1. Click the tab next to "Details".
cases.expected: The Technical Stage screen opens, where Vendor Assessments and Line Item Specifications are filled.
cases.oracle: The Technical Stage screen with Vendor Assessments and Line Item Specifications is displayed.

cases.section: How to place a bid in a Technical Stage
cases.title: Technical response can be changed and re-submitted while submission time is running
cases.why: Vendors correct mistakes before the deadline; the latest submission must be the one the buyer evaluates.
cases.setup: Vendor who has already submitted a Technical Stage response; the event's submission time is still running.
cases.steps: 1. Reopen the Technical Stage screen. 2. Change one or more responses. 3. Scroll to the bottom and click "Submit" again.
cases.expected: The changes are accepted and the response is re-submitted.
cases.oracle: Confirmation appears at the top of the screen again and the changed values are what the response now holds.

cases.section: How to place a bid in a Technical Stage
cases.title: Broker can place a Technical Stage bid
cases.why: The article names Brokers as a persona for this flow; a broker login must be able to complete it too.
cases.setup: Broker account invited to a live Technical Stage event.
cases.steps: 1. Click the Event card, then "I will participate". 2. Fill the Technical Stage responses. 3. Scroll to the bottom and click "Submit".
cases.expected: The broker's Technical Stage response is submitted, same as for a vendor.
cases.oracle: Confirmation appears at the top of the screen after Submit for the broker login.

cases.section: How to not Participate in an Event
cases.title: Declined vendor undoes the decision with "I will participate"
cases.why: The article promises the decline can be undone at any time; a vendor locked out after a mis-click is lost to the event.
cases.setup: Vendor who has declined the event (bottom bar shows "You've decided to not participate, Want to change your response?").
cases.steps: 1. Click "I will participate".
cases.expected: The non-participation is undone and the vendor is participating in the event.
cases.oracle: The "You've decided to not participate" state is no longer shown and the vendor can proceed as a participant.

cases.section: How to not Participate in an Event
cases.title: Buyer is informed of the vendor's participation choice
cases.why: The article describes the choice as the way the buyer learns the vendor's willingness to participate.
cases.setup: Vendor declined an event with a reason; buyer who owns the event.
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, decline the event with a reason and confirm "I will not participate". 2. As the buyer, open the event and look at that vendor's participation.
cases.expected: The buyer can see that the vendor chose not to participate.
cases.oracle: The buyer's view of the event shows the vendor's non-participation (at the article's level of detail).

cases.section: How to Regret Items in a sourcing events?
cases.title: Regretting one item leaves the vendor participating in the rest of the event
cases.why: Regret is item-level only; it must not knock the vendor out of the whole event.
cases.setup: Vendor participating in an event with two or more line items.
cases.steps: 1. Regret one line item via ⚡ Quick Fill → "Regret Item". 2. Fill responses for the other line items and submit.
cases.expected: Non-participation applies only to the regretted item; the vendor still participates in the rest of the event.
cases.oracle: The other line items keep their responses and are submitted; only the regretted item shows "Regret".

cases.section: How to participate in Events as a Vendor?
cases.title: Quote sheet tab reached manually when not opened automatically
cases.why: If the automatic hop after "I will participate" fails, the vendor must still reach the form to bid.
cases.setup: Vendor who clicked "I will participate" but was not automatically taken to the next tab.
cases.steps: 1. Click the tab next to "Event Overview".
cases.expected: The form to fill and submit (Quote sheet) is shown.
cases.oracle: The Quote sheet / form tab is displayed.

cases.section: How to participate in Events as a Vendor?
cases.title: Quote can be changed and re-submitted while submission time is running
cases.why: Vendors revise their quote before the deadline; the buyer must see the latest version.
cases.setup: Vendor who has already submitted a response; the event's submission time is still running.
cases.steps: 1. Reopen the Quote sheet. 2. Change one or more values. 3. Scroll to the bottom and click "Submit".
cases.expected: The changes are accepted and the response is re-submitted.
cases.oracle: Confirmation appears at the top of the screen again and the changed values are held in the submitted response.

cases.section: How do I add Subsidiaries as a Broker?
cases.title: Manage Suppliers page lists already-onboarded suppliers
cases.why: Brokers need to see which suppliers they can already bid for before adding new ones.
cases.setup: Broker who has onboarded at least one supplier.
cases.steps: 1. Open Profile → "Manage Suppliers".
cases.expected: The Manage Suppliers page shows all suppliers the broker has already onboarded.
cases.oracle: Every previously onboarded supplier appears in the list.

cases.section: How do I add Subsidiaries as a Broker?
cases.title: Business Location India shows a GST Tax ID field
cases.why: The tax identifier must match the supplier's country for compliance.
cases.setup: Broker on the Add Supplier form.
cases.steps: 1. Select India in Business Location.
cases.expected: A Tax ID field labelled GST appears automatically.
cases.oracle: The Tax ID field shown is GST.

cases.section: How do I add Subsidiaries as a Broker?
cases.title: Business Location Estonia shows a VAT Tax ID field
cases.why: Non-Indian suppliers need their own country's tax identifier, not GST.
cases.setup: Broker on the Add Supplier form.
cases.steps: 1. Select Estonia in Business Location. 2. Select another country and note the Tax ID field shown.
cases.expected: For Estonia a Tax ID field labelled VAT appears; other countries show their respective Tax ID.
cases.oracle: The Tax ID field shown is VAT for Estonia and changes with the selected country.

cases.section: How do I add Subsidiaries as a Broker?
cases.title: Supplier without a Tax ID is added with company name, address and city
cases.why: Suppliers without a Tax ID must still be onboardable, with company details captured manually.
cases.setup: Broker on the Add Supplier form; Full Name, Phone Number and Email Address filled.
cases.steps: 1. Click the blue highlighted text under the Tax ID field. 2. Enter Company Name and Company Address. 3. Select City from the searchable dropdown. 4. Click "Done".
cases.expected: The Business Location and Tax ID fields are hidden and Company Name, Company Address and City are shown instead; after Done, "Vendor Created." appears and the supplier is in the Suppliers List.
cases.oracle: Business Location and Tax ID fields disappear after the click; "Vendor Created." tooltip; supplier listed in the Suppliers List.

cases.section: How do I add Subsidiaries as a Broker?
cases.title: Blue highlighted text toggles back to the Tax ID option
cases.why: A broker who switched to manual company details by mistake must be able to return to Tax ID entry.
cases.setup: Broker on the Add Supplier form who has clicked the blue highlighted text (manual company fields shown).
cases.steps: 1. Click the blue highlighted text again.
cases.expected: The form returns to using the Tax ID option.
cases.oracle: Business Location and Tax ID fields are shown again.

cases.title: A negative GST is refused
cases.why: Its own refusal path ("Please enter valid GST", 107).
cases.steps: Enter a negative GST.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: A discount above 100% is refused
cases.why: "Please enter a valid discount" (369) — above 100% inverts the price.
cases.setup: gate: trade credit / discount column present.
cases.steps: Enter 150%.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: Bidding after revoking a previous bid is refused
cases.why: A dedicated rule ("You cannot place a bid after revoking the previous one", 370) that is easy to violate by accident.
cases.setup: A vendor who revoked their bid.
cases.steps: Try to bid again.
cases.expected: Refused with that message.
cases.oracle: No new bid.

cases.section: How do I add Subsidiaries as a Broker?
cases.title: Profile menu shows Manage Suppliers, My Profile and Logout
cases.why: The profile menu is the only entry point to supplier management described for brokers.
cases.setup: Broker logged in to the Vendor/Supplier Dashboard.
cases.steps: 1. Hover over the Profile icon on the top-right corner.
cases.expected: Three options are shown: Manage Suppliers, My Profile, Logout.
cases.oracle: The menu lists exactly "Manage Suppliers", "My Profile" and "Logout".

cases.title: An eligible vendor creates a bid
cases.why: The base case. Everything else in this section is a variation.
cases.setup: A live RFQ stage with the vendor invited.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/bids` with the trade and company.
cases.expected: 200 with a bid uuid.
cases.oracle: Uuid returned; the bid is readable back. ≈ BE-5.1.

cases.title: Bid products carry the price and quantity per line item
cases.why: The bid is a container; the prices live in the products. A bid with no products is a participation with no offer.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/bids/:uuid/create_bid_products` with one entry per line item.
cases.expected: 200; each line item has a price and quantity.
cases.oracle: Product count equals the line-item count; prices as sent.

cases.title: The bid is submitted and the total is what was offered
cases.why: The total is the number the buyer compares and the award is based on. A derivation error here is invisible and expensive.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/bids/:uuid` to submit, with the computed total.
cases.expected: 200; the bid is active with that total.
cases.oracle: Total equals the sum of price × quantity across the products, at the template's precision.

cases.title: A bid with no products is refused on submission
cases.why: The model validates it ("Please bid on at least one product") for non-fast, non-buyer-added bids.
cases.steps: Create a bid, skip the products, submit.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: The bid does not become active. `bid.rb:216-222`.

cases.title: A bid outside the window is refused
cases.why: Code 33 "Order not active" — the single most important fairness rule in the module.
cases.steps: Create a bid on a closed stage, then on an Upcoming one.
cases.expected: Refused both times.
cases.oracle: No bid created in either case.

cases.title: A bid on a withdrawn event is refused
cases.why: Withdrawal must be immediate at the API layer, not just in the UI.
cases.steps: Create a bid on a withdrawn event's stage.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: A vendor not on the audience is refused
cases.why: With an open policy layer, this is where invitation is actually enforced.
cases.setup: A vendor not invited.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/bids`.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid created — a 200 here would be a serious finding.

cases.title: A user cannot bid for a company they are not entitled to
cases.why: `can_place_bid_for_company` is what stops one vendor bidding as another.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/bids` with another company's uuid.
cases.expected: Refused (101).
cases.oracle: No bid created for that company.

cases.title: The buying company cannot bid on its own event
cases.why: Code 165, "Cannot place bid on trade by your own company".
cases.steps: `POST /v1/bids` with the buyer's own company id, as a non-surrogate bid.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: A negative price is refused
cases.why: Code 106, checked on every product in the payload.
cases.steps: `POST` bid products with `price: -100`.
cases.oracle: No bid product created.

cases.title: A negative quantity is refused
cases.why: Code 35, a separate check from price.
cases.steps: `POST` bid products with a negative quantity.
cases.oracle: Nothing created.

cases.title: A non-numeric price is refused, not coerced
cases.why: A coerced `0` is a winning bid.
cases.steps: `POST` bid products with `price: "abc"`.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid product with price 0.

cases.title: A bid on a line item from another event is refused
cases.why: Cross-event writes are the most damaging category of bid bug.
cases.steps: `POST` bid products with a `line_item_uuid` from a different event.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid product created; the other event is untouched.

cases.title: Revising a bid replaces the price and keeps history
cases.why: Revision is normal, and the *latest* value must be what ranks while the earlier one stays auditable.
cases.steps: `PATCH /bids/revise_bid/:id` with a new price.
cases.expected: 200; the current price is the new one, the old one is in history.
cases.oracle: Current price and history both as expected. ≈ BE-5.2.

cases.title: A bid in a terminal state cannot be revised
cases.why: The lookup deliberately excludes revised, rejected, selected, revoked, inactive and draft bids. Revising a *selected* bid would change an award after the fact.
cases.steps: Attempt to revise a selected bid, then a rejected one.
cases.expected: Refused both times (32).
cases.oracle: Neither bid changes.

cases.title: A vendor cannot read another vendor's bid
cases.why: PRD §7.2 at the layer where it is actually enforced (`can_view_bid?`). The UI check in UI-VBID-025 is the symptom; this is the cause.
cases.setup: Two vendors with bids.
cases.steps: As A, `GET /bids/:B_id`.
cases.expected: Refused (32).
cases.oracle: No bid payload for B — assert on the body, not only the status.

cases.title: The bid index is restricted to super admins and Procol employees
cases.why: It is a cross-vendor read by design, so its gate is the only thing standing between it and a full bid dump.
cases.steps: `GET /bids` as a normal buyer, then without `vendor_ids`.
cases.expected: Refused (101) for the buyer; 422 (5) for the missing filter.
cases.oracle: No bid list returned in either case.

cases.title: Two vendors' bids coexist and rank correctly
cases.why: Everything in §11 needs two bids to award between, and ranking is the derived value the whole auction depends on.
cases.setup: A live rank auction with two invited vendors.
cases.steps: Bid 100 as A, then 90 as B. Read the buyer's view.
cases.expected: Two bids from two distinct companies; B ranks ahead of A.
cases.oracle: Two bids with **different** company ids, and the rank order as expected.

cases.section: Open a bid on the pricing round — `POST /v1/bids`
cases.title: Open a bid on the pricing round succeeds
cases.why: Every later check reads a success body; a refusal here is the headline, not a field detail.
cases.setup: A vendor walking the API journey (RFQ only, Technical + RFQ, Technical + Auction), at the step "Open a bid on the pricing round".
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, do “Open a bid on the pricing round” in the API journey (`POST /v1/bids`). 2. Note how the app answers.
cases.expected: The app accepts the request and answers with a success.
cases.oracle: Checked automatically on every API journey run; the report shows what actually came back. Engine check: `status_2xx`, learned from 11 real response(s).

cases.section: Open a bid on the pricing round — `POST /v1/bids`
cases.title: The new bid's bid id is returned
cases.why: It was present in all 11 real response(s); a client reading it would break if it vanished.
cases.setup: A vendor walking the API journey (RFQ only, Technical + RFQ, Technical + Auction), at the step "Open a bid on the pricing round".
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, do “Open a bid on the pricing round” in the API journey (`POST /v1/bids`). 2. Look at the new bid's bid id in the app's response.
cases.expected: The response includes the new bid's bid id.
cases.oracle: Checked automatically on every API journey run; the report shows what actually came back. Engine check: `exists bid_uuid`, learned from 11 real response(s).

cases.section: Open a bid on the pricing round — `POST /v1/bids`
cases.title: The new bid's bid id is a valid Procol reference
cases.why: Downstream steps and the UI parse this value; a malformed one fails far from its cause.
cases.setup: A vendor walking the API journey (RFQ only, Technical + RFQ, Technical + Auction), at the step "Open a bid on the pricing round".
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, do “Open a bid on the pricing round” in the API journey (`POST /v1/bids`). 2. Look at the new bid's bid id in the app's response.
cases.expected: The new bid's bid id is a valid Procol reference — a short code of letters and digits, such as RHBjY3Bj.
cases.oracle: Checked automatically on every API journey run; the report shows what actually came back. Engine check: `format bid_uuid "encodedId"`, learned from 11 real response(s).

cases.title: Price the line item succeeds
cases.why: Every later check reads a success body; a refusal here is the headline, not a field detail.
cases.setup: A vendor walking the API journey (RFQ only, Technical + RFQ, Technical + Auction), at the step "Price the line item".
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, do “Price the line item” in the API journey (`POST /v1/bids/:id/create_bid_products`). 2. Note how the app answers.
cases.expected: The app accepts the request and answers with a success.
cases.oracle: Checked automatically on every API journey run; the report shows what actually came back. Engine check: `status_2xx`, learned from 11 real response(s).

cases.title: Submit the bid succeeds
cases.why: Every later check reads a success body; a refusal here is the headline, not a field detail.
cases.setup: A vendor walking the API journey (RFQ only, Technical + RFQ, Technical + Auction), at the step "Submit the bid".
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, do “Submit the bid” in the API journey (`PATCH /v1/bids/:id`). 2. Note how the app answers.
cases.expected: The app accepts the request and answers with a success.
