cases.expected: Today 200 with bid_uuid: Api::V1::BidsController#create (app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:11-39) and is_allowed_to_create_bid (app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:7-78) never read UserIntent. The UI gates on user_intent_answered; the API does not.
cases.oracle: A draft bid exists while user_intents has no row for the vendor.

cases.title: A vendor who declined to participate can still open a bid
cases.why: The buyer's report would show the vendor as both declined and bidding. (This case records current behaviour: the risk is that today's response is the wrong one.)
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). The vendor recorded a trade_reject intent on {{tradeId}}; stage is live.
cases.steps: 1. POST /user_intents trade_reject. 2. POST /v1/bids with the working body.
cases.expected: Should be refused. Nothing in app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:11-39 or app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:7-78 reads the trade_reject intent, so 200 is expected today; only the legacy surrogate path touches intents (app/controllers/api/bids_controller.rb:521-528, marks them converted).
cases.oracle: Intent still active trade_reject AND a draft bid exists.

cases.title: A vendor who declined can still submit a priced bid
cases.why: The version that changes ranks and savings: a declined vendor can end up L1. (This case records current behaviour: the risk is that today's response is the wrong one.)
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). trade_reject intent recorded; a priced draft bid {{bidUuid}} exists.
cases.steps: 1. PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}} with the working submit body.
cases.expected: Should be refused. update (app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:41-66) → update_bid_helper (app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:367-487) has no intent check; success:true expected today and the declined vendor ranks.
cases.oracle: Bid status active while the intent says trade_reject.

cases.title: An uninvited vendor cannot read a restricted event
cases.why: Specs, quantities and sometimes target prices are competitor-sensitive.
cases.setup: Session: a vendor that deals with the buyer but is NOT on the restricted audience of {{tradeId}}.
cases.steps: 1. GET /trade/{{tradeId}} as that vendor.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 536 'You are not allowed to view this event.' from validate_event (app/controllers/concerns/trade_controller_helper.rb:2219-2221); is_allowed_to_view? is false for a restricted audience (app/models/model_helpers/trade_request_model_helper.rb:366-369).
cases.oracle: No sheets/forms in the body.

cases.title: A vendor cannot read an unpublished (draft) stage
cases.why: Buyers add audiences while drafting; unfinished prices and quantities must stay invisible until publish.
cases.setup: Session: a vendor already added to the audience of a DRAFT stage {{tradeId}}.
cases.steps: 1. GET /trade/{{tradeId}} as the vendor.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 536 'You are not allowed to view this event.' — is_allowed_to_view? denies drafts vendor-side (app/models/model_helpers/trade_request_model_helper.rb:352-353).
cases.oracle: No payload.

cases.title: A technical response cannot be started before the stage opens
cases.why: Same fairness rule as bidding: no head start on the technical stage.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). {{rfpTradeId}} is an Upcoming (published, not yet started) technical stage.
cases.steps: 1. POST /template_responses.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 33 'Order not active' — currently_running_in_bidding_time (app/models/trade_request.rb:222-226) excludes it; app/controllers/concerns/template_responses_controller_helper.rb:132-133.
cases.oracle: No draft response.

cases.title: A technical response cannot be started after the stage closed
cases.why: Late technical responses change who qualifies for the commercial stage after evaluation began.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). {{rfpTradeId}} technical stage bid_end_time has passed.
cases.steps: 1. POST /template_responses.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 33 'Order not active' from app/controllers/concerns/template_responses_controller_helper.rb:132-133.
cases.oracle: No response.

cases.title: A vendor cannot start a technical response in another vendor's name
cases.why: Cross-vendor write: A can seed B's technical response and, since the reason strings are shown to the buyer, tamper with B's qualification. (This case records current behaviour: the risk is that today's response is the wrong one.)
cases.setup: Session: vendor A. {{vendorUuid}} is a DIFFERENT invited vendor B.
cases.steps: 1. As vendor A, POST /template_responses with company_uuid of vendor B.
cases.expected: Should be refused. validate_params_for_trade_request (app/controllers/concerns/template_responses_controller_helper.rb:108-140) never checks company_id belongs to the caller (unlike bids, which call can_place_bid_for_company). Today a draft owned by A for company B is the suspected outcome.
cases.oracle: No draft response exists for company B created by user A.

cases.title: Submitting a technical response with a required answer blank is refused
cases.why: Required technical answers gate qualification; a blank required field must block submission.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A technical response {{templateResponseUuid}} with a required widget left blank.
cases.steps: 1. Save the page with the required field empty. 2. PATCH /template_responses/{{templateResponseUuid}} to submit.
cases.expected: Should be 422 error.code 572 "Please fill '<field>'" from ValidateService#validate_header (app/services/template_responses/validate_service.rb:158-162), reached via revise_for_item_type → revise_template_response_helper (app/controllers/concerns/template_responses_controller_helper.rb:23). The generic submit body cannot force a specific field blank in one run, so no-5xx is the runnable assertion.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 572.

cases.title: A different user cannot submit another user's draft response without edit access
cases.why: The technical response is competitor-sensitive; only its owner or a shared editor may submit it.
cases.setup: Session: a vendor user who did NOT create response {{templateResponseUuid}} and has no editor access-list entry.
cases.steps: 1. PATCH /template_responses/{{templateResponseUuid}} to submit.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2 (draft not found for company) or 101 (not an editor). update (app/controllers/api/template_responses_controller.rb:55-67) scopes to company_id, and unauthorized_template_response_editor? (app/controllers/api/template_responses_controller.rb:402-410) denies non-owners without editor access.
cases.oracle: No state change on the response owned by another user.

cases.title: An uninvited vendor cannot open a bid
cases.why: The core fairness rule: only invited vendors may bid.
cases.setup: Session: a vendor NOT on the audience of {{tradeId}}.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids as the uninvited vendor.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 782 'Bid could not be placed. Please refresh and try again.' from app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:20 (allowed_to_bid? false — company not in audience_ids, app/controllers/concerns/bids_controller_helper.rb:17-31).
cases.oracle: No bid_uuid; no draft bid for the uninvited company.

cases.title: The buyer cannot open an ordinary bid on their own event
cases.why: A buyer self-bid would seed a competing quote on their own event. (This case records current behaviour: the risk is that today's response is the wrong one.)
cases.setup: Session: the BUYER who owns the sandbox event (this is how the platform runner authenticates). Live RFQ stage; company_uuid set to the buyer's own company.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids with company_uuid = the event's own company.
cases.expected: Should be refused. is_surrogate_bidding_and_is_allowed? treats the owner as a surrogate bidder (app/controllers/concerns/bids_controller_helper.rb:2130-2141); a plain self-bid should not create a vendor bid. Uses the buyer's own company id.
cases.oracle: No ordinary (non-surrogate) bid for the buyer's own company.

cases.title: A bid cannot be opened before the window opens
cases.why: Bidding early breaks fairness — the single most important window rule.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). {{tradeId}} is an Upcoming (published, not started) RFQ stage.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 33 'Order not active' from is_allowed_to_create_bid (app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:71-73, !is_running).
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: A bid cannot be opened after the window closes
cases.why: A late bid changes the result after the event closed.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). {{tradeId}} RFQ stage bid_end_time has passed.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 33 'Order not active' from app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:71-73 (is_running false once bid_end_time passed; is_running at app/models/trade_request.rb:1191-1194).
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: A bid cannot be opened on an unpublished (draft) stage
cases.why: Bidding on an unpublished stage writes into an event the buyer is still editing.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A DRAFT RFQ stage {{tradeId}} with the vendor pre-added to the audience.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids on the draft stage.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 33 'Order not active' — a draft has no running schedule, so is_running is false (app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:71-73). A draft is also unviewable to the vendor (is_allowed_to_view? app/models/model_helpers/trade_request_model_helper.rb:352).
cases.oracle: No draft bid on the unpublished stage.

cases.title: A negative price is refused
cases.why: Negative prices are the canonical bad input; whichever path runs, they must not become a valid quote.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A draft bid {{bidUuid}} on the live RFQ stage.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/create_bid_products with a trade_products entry priced -5.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 106 'Please enter a valid price' from filter_invalid_params (app/controllers/api/bids_controller.rb:539-546) — note this guard lives on the legacy Api::BidsController path; the v1 create_bid_trade_products path stores price as a float and relies on floor/ceil, so a negative here may instead pass to validate_bid_product_details.
cases.oracle: No bid_trade_products row with a negative price.

cases.title: A price above the configured ceiling is refused
cases.why: The price cap is a hard business rule; over-ceiling quotes must be blocked.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A draft bid {{bidUuid}} on a stage whose line item has a ceiling (max) price.
cases.steps: 1. POST create_bid_products priced far above the ceiling.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 38 'Price cannot be more than the allowed price' from validate_bid_product_details (app/controllers/concerns/bids_controller_helper.rb:1840-1846), comparing estimated_price to ceil_price_for_user. gate: ceiling price set — no-5xx otherwise.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 38.

cases.title: A vendor cannot price a bid belonging to another company
cases.why: Cross-company write into a competitor's bid.
cases.setup: Session: vendor A. {{bidUuid}} is a draft bid owned by vendor B.
cases.steps: 1. As A, POST /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/create_bid_products.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 32 'Bid not found' — the bid lookup is scoped to Current.allowed_companies (app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:119-121), so B's bid is invisible to A. Requires a bid owned by another company.
cases.oracle: B's bid is unchanged.

cases.title: Submitting a bid with no products is refused
cases.why: A submitted bid with no products is a participation with no offer — the model's own guard.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A draft bid {{bidUuid}} created but never priced (no bid_products).
cases.steps: 1. PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}} to active with the working submit body.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 8 'Model error' 'Please bid on at least one product' from Bid#validate_bid_products (app/models/bid.rb:217-223), which fires for a non-fast, non-buyer-added bid activated from draft. surfaces via error_code 15 in the helper.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; the bid is not active with zero products.

cases.title: Submitting the same bid twice does not create a second active bid
cases.why: Vendors retry submit; a second active bid would double-rank the same company.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A bid {{bidUuid}} already submitted (active).
cases.steps: 1. PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}} to active again.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 34 'A bid has already been placed from your team' — update refuses when bid.active? and status in [active,draft] (app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:45-47).
cases.oracle: Still exactly one active bid for the company.

cases.title: A bid cannot be submitted after the window closes
cases.why: A late submit changes the result after the event closed.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A priced draft bid {{bidUuid}} whose stage bid_end_time has passed.
cases.steps: 1. PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}} to active.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 33 'Order not active' — update_bid_action_helper_v1 returns 33 when !is_running and not a counter-offer/justification (app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:562-571). Requires a closed stage.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 33; the bid stays draft.

cases.title: A vendor cannot submit another company's bid
cases.why: Cross-company submit would let A finalize B's quote.
cases.setup: Session: vendor A. {{bidUuid}} is a draft bid owned by vendor B.
cases.steps: 1. As A, PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}} to active.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 32 'Bid not found' — Bid.not_in_active.for_company(Current.allowed_companies) excludes B's bid (app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:42-44). Requires a bid owned by another company.
cases.oracle: B's bid is unchanged.

cases.title: A second bid from the same company is refused
cases.why: Code 99 / 96 — the check is at company and team level, which is the level that matters commercially.
cases.setup: A vendor with an active bid.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/bids` again.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: One active bid for that company.

cases.title: A bid from a subsidiary of an existing bidder is refused
cases.why: `is_part_of_subsidiary_network?` prevents one corporate group bidding twice under different names — a genuine collusion control.
cases.setup: Two companies in one subsidiary network; one has bid.
cases.steps: Bid as the other.
cases.expected: Refused (96).
cases.oracle: One bid across the network.

cases.title: Bidding after revoking is refused
cases.why: Code 370. Revocation is meant to be final within the event.
cases.setup: A vendor whose bid is revoked.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/bids`.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No new bid.

cases.title: Bidding is refused once the RFQ's auction exists
cases.why: Code 769, "You cannot edit rfq once the auction is created." It is the first guard in the sequence, so it also proves the ordering.
cases.setup: A converted RFQ.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/bids` on the RFQ.
cases.expected: Refused with 769.
cases.oracle: That specific code — not 33 — which is what confirms the guard order.

cases.title: Rebidding is refused where the seller is barred from it
cases.why: `not_allow_rebidding_to_seller?` is a per-event configuration and a silent bypass would let a barred vendor improve their price.
cases.setup: An event configured to bar rebidding.
cases.steps: Bid, then attempt a revision.
cases.expected: The revision is refused (101).
cases.oracle: The original bid is unchanged.

cases.title: A negative GST is refused
cases.why: Code 107 — the third of the three per-product checks, and the one most likely to be forgotten.
cases.steps: `POST` bid products with a negative GST.
cases.oracle: Nothing created.

cases.title: Legacy top-level price and quantity fields are validated too
cases.why: The controller validates both the nested products *and* the older flat fields. An unvalidated legacy path is a real bypass for old clients.
cases.steps: `POST` with a top-level negative `price`, then a negative `quantity`, then a negative `gst`.
cases.expected: Refused each time (106 / 35 / 107).
cases.oracle: Nothing created in any case.

cases.title: Offering more than the requested quantity is refused
cases.why: Code 511 at the bid layer, and over-offering distorts the comparison.
cases.steps: `POST` bid products with quantity above the line item's.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid product above the requested quantity.

cases.title: Offering in a different unit is refused
cases.why: Code 512 — a unit mismatch makes every price incomparable.
cases.steps: `POST` bid products with a different unit.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: Nothing created.

cases.title: Revising a non-existent bid is refused
cases.why: Code 32 "Bid not found" — must not be a nil dereference.
cases.steps: `PATCH /bids/revise_bid/<fabricated>`.
cases.oracle: That code; no 500. ≈ BE-5.7.

cases.title: Rejecting a bid works only on an active bid
cases.why: Rejecting a non-active bid is meaningless and the endpoint guards it explicitly.
cases.steps: `PATCH /bids/:id/reject` on an active bid, then on an already-rejected one.
cases.expected: First succeeds; second refused (101).
cases.oracle: One rejection recorded. ≈ BE-5.3.

cases.title: Accepting a knockout offer twice is idempotent
cases.why: Double submission at round boundaries must not advance the round twice.
cases.setup: A live knockout auction with an open offer.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/accept_knockout_offer` twice.
cases.expected: One acceptance.
cases.oracle: One acceptance recorded; no 500. ≈ BE-5.6.

cases.title: Accepting a dutch offer validates the quantity
cases.why: Three distinct refusals live here — missing (249), non-positive (101) and below-minimum (246) — and they are easy to collapse into one.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/accept_dutch_offer` with no quantity, then `0`, then below the minimum.
cases.expected: 249, 101 and 246 respectively.
cases.oracle: Each specific code; no acceptance in any case.

cases.title: Uploading a bid Excel requires view access to the event
cases.why: A bulk write path — weak authorization here is worth more than any single-bid bypass.
cases.setup: A user without view access.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/:id/upload_bid_excel`.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bids created. ≈ BE-5.8.

cases.title: Anomaly detection flags a wildly out-of-band bid
cases.why: It fires only with three or more bids on a line item, skips surrogate bids, and does not run for knockout, dutch or book-building — a lot of conditions to get wrong, and a false positive blocks a legitimate bid.
cases.setup: A line item with three comparable bids, then a fourth far outside the range.
cases.steps: Submit the outlier.
cases.expected: Flagged as an anomaly with a message and a suggested price, rather than silently accepted or hard-refused.
cases.oracle: The anomaly response is returned; verify a *normal* bid in the same state is not flagged.

cases.title: Declaring intent without the event id is refused
cases.why: item_id links the answer to the event; item_id is NOT NULL, so without the guard this would be a DB error instead of a typed refusal.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). Sandbox stage {{tradeId}} is live and the vendor is invited.
cases.steps: 1. POST /user_intents with the working body minus item_uuid.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 with error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' from Api::UserIntentsController#create app/controllers/api/user_intents_controller.rb:14-15 (item_id blank); no user_intents row.
cases.oracle: Error body {error:{code:2}}; vendor's intent count on the stage unchanged.

cases.title: Declining to participate without any reason is refused
cases.why: Regret reasons feed the buyer's participation report; a reasonless decline loses the signal the feature exists for.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). Live sandbox stage.
cases.steps: 1. POST /user_intents with intent_type trade_reject and neither reason nor remarks.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' from app/controllers/api/user_intents_controller.rb:11-12 — a non-accept intent must carry reason or remarks.
cases.oracle: No intent row; the buyer's participants table still shows no answer.

cases.title: An unknown intent_type does not crash the server
cases.why: Rails enums raise on unknown values and the controller assigns the raw param.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). Live sandbox stage.
cases.steps: 1. POST /user_intents with intent_type 'maybe' and a reason.
cases.expected: Should be a typed 422. intent_type is a Rails enum (app/models/user_intent.rb:33); assigning 'maybe' at app/controllers/api/user_intents_controller.rb:19 raises ArgumentError and nothing rescues it — an untyped 500 is the suspected defect.
cases.oracle: Status < 500 and error.code present.

cases.title: An intent against a made-up item_type does not crash
cases.why: The controller only checks presence of item_type; any string reaches constantize.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). Live sandbox stage.
cases.steps: 1. POST /user_intents with item_type 'QA_Platform_NotAModel_{{stamp}}'.
cases.expected: Should be 422. belongs_to :item, polymorphic: true (app/models/user_intent.rb:29) constantizes item_type during validation; an unknown class raises NameError — 500 suspected. app/controllers/api/user_intents_controller.rb:18
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: An intent on a non-existent event is refused, not silently dropped
cases.why: `render_success_json if save` with no failure branch turns validation errors into a silent 204.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). None.
cases.steps: 1. POST /user_intents with item_uuid 'WrongUuid1='.
cases.expected: Should be a typed 422. If save fails (belongs_to item required) app/controllers/api/user_intents_controller.rb:23 has no else branch, so Rails answers 204 No Content — which every client reads as success.
cases.oracle: Status is a typed 4xx with a body, not an empty 204.

cases.title: A vendor cannot record intent on an event they are not invited to
cases.why: A write path with no authorization check beyond login. (This case records current behaviour: the risk is that today's response is the wrong one.)
cases.setup: Session: a vendor NOT on the audience of {{tradeId}}.
cases.steps: 1. POST /user_intents for {{tradeId}} as the uninvited vendor.
cases.expected: Should be refused (101). app/controllers/api/user_intents_controller.rb:4-23 performs no audience or ownership check before writing.
cases.oracle: Buyer's participants table shows no answer from this vendor.

cases.title: Opening a non-existent event does not crash
cases.why: The nil guard is defeated by a fallback query that returns a Relation.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). None.
cases.steps: 1. GET /trade/WrongUuid1=
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 4 'Request not found'. Api::TradeController#show replaces a nil trade with `TradeRequest.joins(:bids)...` (app/controllers/api/trade_controller.rb:1067-1068), a Relation that is never nil, so validate_event's `trade.void?` (trade_controller_helper.rb:2216) runs on a Relation — NoMethodError/500 suspected.
cases.oracle: Status < 500 with a typed body.

cases.title: The schema of a non-existent event is refused cleanly
cases.why: Contrast case for the /trade/:id crash — same helper, no Relation fallback, correct result.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). None.
cases.steps: 1. GET /v1/trade/WrongUuid1=/schema
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 4 'Request not found' from validate_event (app/controllers/concerns/trade_controller_helper.rb:2215), called by Api::V1::TradeController#event_schema (app/controllers/api/v1/trade_controller.rb:265-277).
cases.oracle: Typed error body.

cases.title: A vendor cannot read the schema of a draft stage
cases.why: The schema carries widget configuration incl. required fields and price validations.
cases.setup: Session: vendor on the audience of a DRAFT stage {{tradeId}}.
cases.steps: 1. GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/schema as the vendor.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 536 'You are not allowed to view this event.' via event_schema → validate_event (app/controllers/concerns/trade_controller_helper.rb:2219-2221).
cases.oracle: No schema payload.

cases.title: A cancelled stage reads as not found
cases.why: Vendors keep links in email; a cancelled event must read as gone.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). {{tradeId}} was cancelled or voided by the buyer.
cases.steps: 1. GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/schema
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 4 'Request not found' from validate_event (app/controllers/concerns/trade_controller_helper.rb:2216-2217).
cases.oracle: Typed error body.

cases.title: Starting a technical response without the stage id is refused
cases.why: The start call returns the id the answer and submit calls hang off; a missing stage must be refused.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). Live technical stage {{rfpTradeId}}.
cases.steps: 1. POST /template_responses without item_uuid.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' from TemplateResponsesController#create app/controllers/api/template_responses_controller.rb:16-17.
cases.oracle: No draft response.

cases.title: A technical response cannot be started on an RFQ (commercial) stage
cases.why: A technical answer on a pricing stage would never be evaluated; the misleading 'Order not active' message is worth pinning.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). {{tradeId}} here is the sandbox RFQ/pricing stage (rfx_mode rfq).
cases.steps: 1. POST /template_responses with item_uuid of the RFQ stage.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 33 'Order not active' — create restricts the lookup to rfi/rfp (app/controllers/api/template_responses_controller.rb:23), so the set is empty and validate_params_for_trade_request returns 33 (app/controllers/concerns/template_responses_controller_helper.rb:132-133).
cases.oracle: No template response on the RFQ stage.

cases.title: The buyer cannot answer their own technical stage as a participant
cases.why: A buyer-company response on its own event pollutes evaluation and could be awarded.
cases.setup: Session: the BUYER who owns the sandbox event (this is how the platform runner authenticates). Live technical stage; company_uuid set to the buyer's own company.
cases.steps: 1. POST /template_responses with company_uuid = the event's own company.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action' from app/controllers/concerns/template_responses_controller_helper.rb:135 (company_id == trade company). Uses the buyer's own company id.
cases.oracle: No response for the buyer's own company.

cases.title: Saving answers with no form id is refused
cases.why: The answer call is keyed by form and page uuids; a missing form must not become a crash.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A technical response {{templateResponseUuid}} has been started.
cases.steps: 1. PUT /template_responses/{{templateResponseUuid}}/create_page_responses with form_uuid removed.
cases.expected: Should be a typed 4xx. create_form_page_responses (app/controllers/api/template_responses_controller.rb:69-95) reads params['page_ids'] and page_responses; a blank/absent form leaves nothing to persist. Must not 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: An answer with a key_attribute that is not on the form is ignored, not crashing
cases.why: A wrong key_attribute is the single most common malformed-answer case; it must be dropped, not saved or crashed.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). Technical response {{templateResponseUuid}} started; {{techPageUuid}} is its line-item page.
cases.steps: 1. PUT create_page_responses with page_responses whose key_attribute is 'NOT_A_WIDGET_{{stamp}}'.
cases.expected: 200 or typed 4xx. create_draft_form_response iterates form_key_attributes and only stores keys present in the header set (app/helpers/api/forms_helper.rb:343-368); an unknown key falls through get_key_attribute_vs_response_data (app/helpers/api/forms_helper.rb:452-457) and is dropped.
cases.oracle: The stored response_data contains no NOT_A_WIDGET key.

cases.title: An attachment answer sent as an object instead of a list does not crash
cases.why: Attachment shape confusion is a known raise site inside a transaction; it must stay a typed error.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). Technical response {{templateResponseUuid}} started.
cases.steps: 1. PUT create_page_responses with an attachment widget value set to {url:...} (an object, not a list).
cases.expected: validate_form_pages_responses_data (app/helpers/api/forms_helper.rb:299-312) raises StandardError 'Invalid Attachments Data' for a non-array, non-string attachment value; that surfaces as a handled error, not a 500 (this widget may be a string field, so no-5xx is the honest assertion).
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: Answers cannot be saved on a stage that is not running
cases.why: A late technical answer edits a response after the window; the window guard must fire.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A response {{templateResponseUuid}} exists on a technical stage that has since closed.
cases.steps: 1. PUT /template_responses/{{templateResponseUuid}}/create_page_responses.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 33 'Order not active' — for a vendor (not the buyer's company) create_form_page_responses checks item.is_running (app/controllers/api/template_responses_controller.rb:78-82). Requires a closed stage; no-5xx if the sandbox stage is still live.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 33.

cases.title: Submitting the same technical response twice does not create a second active response
cases.why: Vendors retry submit on flaky networks; a second active response would double-count in evaluation.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). Response {{templateResponseUuid}} already submitted (active).
cases.steps: 1. PATCH /template_responses/{{templateResponseUuid}} to submit again.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2: update (app/controllers/api/template_responses_controller.rb:59) fetches TemplateResponse.draft, which is empty once the response is active, so a re-submit refuses cleanly. No second active row either way.
cases.oracle: Exactly one active response for the vendor on the stage.

cases.title: Saving answers against a non-existent response is refused cleanly
cases.why: A stale or guessed response id must produce a typed error, not a crash.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). None.
cases.steps: 1. PUT /template_responses/WrongUuid1=/create_page_responses.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 888 'Invalid Parameters' from fetch_template_response (app/controllers/concerns/template_responses_controller_helper.rb:61-62). Must not 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 888.

cases.title: Opening a bid without a company is refused
cases.why: company_id names who the bid is for; blank must be refused before any row.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). Live RFQ stage {{tradeId}}, vendor invited.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids with company_uuid removed.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' from app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:15-16 (company_id blank).
cases.oracle: No bid_uuid returned; no draft bid.

cases.title: Opening a bid without a trade id is refused
cases.why: No stage means no event to bid on; the presence guard must fire.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). Vendor invited.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids with trade_request_uuid removed.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' — trade_request is nil at app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:14-16.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: Opening a bid on a non-existent event is refused
cases.why: A guessed stage id must not open a bid.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). None.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids with trade_request_uuid 'WrongUuid1='.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' — find_by_id returns nil, blank check at app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:14-16.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: A bid on a superseded event version is refused
cases.why: Bidding on a stale version writes to an event nobody is running.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). {{tradeId}} belongs to an event group that has been amended (a newer version exists).
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids on the old version's stage.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action' from app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:18 (event_group.latest? false). Requires an amended event; on a fresh sandbox this stays a clean 4xx.
cases.oracle: No bid on the old version.

cases.title: Two concurrent create calls do not both succeed
cases.why: The submit/create pair is the most retried write; the cache lock prevents a double bid.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). Live RFQ stage; two create calls fire within 3 seconds for the same (trade, company).
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids. 2. Immediately POST /v1/bids again.
cases.expected: The second call should get 422 code 516 'Transaction in Progress' from lock_transaction (app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:168-174; Rails.cache 3s lock keyed t<id>_c<company>).
cases.oracle: At most one draft bid created; the loser gets code 516.

cases.title: A second bid after one is already active is refused
cases.why: Config-dependent: with the lock on, one submitted quote is final.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). The vendor already has an active bid on {{tradeId}} and lock_quote_after_submission is ON.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids again for the same company.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 875 'Revise bid is locked. You cannot edit your quote after submission.' from is_allowed_to_create_bid (app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:74-76) when lock_quote_after_submission? is set. gate: lock_quote_after_submission
cases.oracle: Still one active bid.

cases.title: A vendor who revoked cannot open a new bid
cases.why: Revocation is meant to be final for that vendor.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). The vendor's previous bid on {{tradeId}} is in revoke status.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 370 'You cannot place a bid after revoking the previous one' from app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:54-56.
cases.oracle: No new bid.

cases.title: An unsupported currency code is refused on a multi-currency event
cases.why: Currency drives every price comparison; an invalid code must be rejected.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). {{tradeId}} has a currency_configuration; the vendor sends an out-of-list code.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids with currency_preference.code 'XYZ'.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 15 'Operation failed' 'Please choose a valid currency' from validate_currency_preference (app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:28, app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:191-192). gate: currency_configuration — no-5xx if the sandbox is single-currency.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 with the currency message.

cases.title: A vendor who skipped the technical stage cannot open the commercial bid
cases.why: Two-stage events require technical qualification before commercial bidding.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). The event has a live/closed RFP technical stage the vendor never responded to; {{tradeId}} is the commercial stage.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids without any technical response.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 737 'You cannot quote for this item because you didn't participate in the technical stage' — is_allowed_to_create_bid checks template responses (app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:30-37) → check_participation_in_technical_and_commercial_stage (app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:313-320). gate: a technical (RFP) stage exists.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 737.

cases.title: A zero price is not added as a quote
cases.why: A zero price is a common 'no quote' signal; it must not create a zero-value bid.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A draft bid {{bidUuid}} on the live RFQ stage.
cases.steps: 1. POST create_bid_products with price 0 in the inline sheet.
cases.expected: allowed_to_add (app/controllers/concerns/trade_template_helper.rb:5839-5851) only adds a row when price > 0, so a zero-priced row is dropped and create_bid_trade_product_helper sees blank products → 732 'Invalid Input' (app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:151-156).
cases.oracle: No zero-priced bid_trade_product; ideally 422 code 732.

cases.title: A non-numeric price does not crash
cases.why: String-where-number is a classic fuzz input on the money field.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A draft bid {{bidUuid}}.
cases.steps: 1. POST create_bid_products with price value 'abc'.
cases.expected: 200 or typed 4xx. get_line_item_object coerces with &.to_f (app/controllers/concerns/trade_template_helper.rb:5639) so 'abc' becomes 0.0 and is dropped by allowed_to_add (app/controllers/concerns/trade_template_helper.rb:5841); must not 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: An enormous price is handled without overflow
cases.why: Unbounded price with no ceiling is an integrity risk in the savings/total math.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A draft bid {{bidUuid}} on an event with no ceiling price.
cases.steps: 1. POST create_bid_products with price 1e18.
cases.expected: 200 or a ceiling refusal (38). price is a float column (db/schema.rb bid_trade_products); with no ceil_price the value is stored (app/controllers/concerns/bids_controller_helper.rb:1145). Must not 5xx or overflow.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; any stored total is finite.

cases.title: A price below the configured floor is refused
cases.why: Floor caps stop unrealistically low quotes on forward/sell events.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A draft bid {{bidUuid}} on a stage whose line item has a floor (min) price.
cases.steps: 1. POST create_bid_products priced below the floor.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 41 'Price cannot be less than the allowed price' from the floor branch of validate_bid_product_details (app/controllers/concerns/bids_controller_helper.rb:1848-1855). gate: floor price set.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 41.

cases.title: A quantity above the line quantity is refused when over-quantity is off
cases.why: Over-quantity bids distort awarding when the buyer disallows them.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A draft bid {{bidUuid}}; is_over_quantity_allowed is OFF; line quantity is 10. gate: `is_over_quantity_allowed` must be off for this case's outcome to hold.
cases.steps: 1. POST create_bid_products with participant_quantity 100.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 138 'Quantity cannot be greater than the mentioned quantity.' from validate_bid_product_details (app/controllers/concerns/bids_controller_helper.rb:1902-1904). gate: is_over_quantity_allowed=false (default is true, so this is config-dependent).
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 138.

cases.title: A quantity below the line quantity is refused when under-quantity is off
cases.why: Under-quantity bids are disallowed when the buyer needs the full lot.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A draft bid {{bidUuid}}; is_under_quantity_allowed is OFF; line quantity is 10. gate: `is_under_quantity_allowed` must be off for this case's outcome to hold.
cases.steps: 1. POST create_bid_products with participant_quantity 1.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 139 'Quantity cannot be less than the mentioned quantity.' from validate_bid_product_details (app/controllers/concerns/bids_controller_helper.rb:1906-1908). gate: is_under_quantity_allowed=false.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 139.

cases.title: A quantity not equal to the auction quantity is refused when fixed-quantity bidding is on
cases.why: Fixed-quantity events require an exact-match quantity.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A draft bid {{bidUuid}}; allow_fixed_quantity_for_bidding is ON; line quantity is 10. gate: `allow_fixed_quantity_for_bidding` must be on for this case's outcome to hold.
cases.steps: 1. POST create_bid_products with participant_quantity 9.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 207 'Bid Quantity should be equal to the Auction Quantity' from validate_bid_product_details (app/controllers/concerns/bids_controller_helper.rb:1898-1900). gate: allow_fixed_quantity_for_bidding=true.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 207.

cases.title: A negative quantity is refused
cases.why: Negative quantity is another canonical bad input.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A draft bid {{bidUuid}}.
cases.steps: 1. POST create_bid_products (legacy trade_products form) with quantity -3.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 35 'Quantity must be greater than zero' from filter_invalid_params (app/controllers/api/bids_controller.rb:547-549) on the legacy path.
cases.oracle: No bid product with negative quantity.

cases.title: Pricing with no products is refused
cases.why: A bid with no products is a participation with no offer.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A draft bid {{bidUuid}}.
cases.steps: 1. POST create_bid_products with an empty inline data map.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 732 'Invalid Input' — create_bid_trade_product_helper (app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:151-156) refuses a blank product list unless it is a valid delete.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 732.

cases.title: Pricing a non-existent bid is refused
cases.why: A guessed bid id must not receive prices.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). None.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids/WrongUuid1=/create_bid_products with a valid row.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 error.code 32 'Bid not found' — Bid.draft.for_company(...).where(id: bid_id).last is nil (app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:120-121).
cases.oracle: No products created.

cases.title: Pricing a bid after the window closes is refused
cases.why: Late pricing edits a bid after the window.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A draft bid {{bidUuid}} whose stage bid_end_time has passed.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/create_bid_products.
cases.expected: When not running, create_bid_trade_products routes to is_allowed_to_modify_counter_offer (app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:125-127) which returns 33 'Order not active' unless a counter-offer modification is applicable (app/controllers/concerns/bids_controller_helper.rb:792-793). Requires a closed stage.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 33.

cases.title: A locked event refuses a second submitted quote
cases.why: With the lock on, the first submitted quote is final.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). lock_quote_after_submission is ON; the vendor already has an active bid; {{bidUuid}} is a new draft. gate: `lock_quote_after_submission` must be on for this case's outcome to hold.
cases.steps: 1. PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}} to active.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 875 'Revise bid is locked. You cannot edit your quote after submission.' from update_bid_helper (app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:385-387). gate: lock_quote_after_submission=true.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 875.

cases.title: Submitting a commercial bid that skips technically-qualified lines is refused

cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 300; the active price is unchanged.

cases.steps: 1. PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}} with status removed.
cases.expected: 200 or typed 4xx. With no status the bid stays draft (update_bid_helper draft branch app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:453) and no technical-participation gate fires; must not 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; the bid is not activated by an empty status.

cases.title: A non-numeric gross_total does not crash
cases.why: gross_total is echoed in the orders sheet view — a stored-XSS/type sink.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A priced draft bid {{bidUuid}}.
cases.steps: 1. PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}} with global gross_total value '<script>'.
cases.expected: 200 or typed 4xx. gross_total flows into other_details (app/helpers/api/v1/bids_controller_helper.rb:420); it is display data, not the ranking price. Must not 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Surrogate bids (buyer on behalf of a vendor)
cases.title: A surrogate response after the vendor already responded is refused unless allowed-after-bid is on
cases.why: The buyer must not overwrite a vendor's own submitted response by default.
cases.setup: Session: the BUYER who owns the sandbox event (this is how the platform runner authenticates). Vendor {{vendorUuid}} already has an active technical response on {{tradeId}}; allowed_surrogate_bid_even_after_bid is off. gate: `allowed_surrogate_bid_even_after_bid` must be off for this case's outcome to hold.
cases.steps: 1. POST /template_responses/create_surrogate_response for that vendor.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 30 'Bid already placed for this order' — create_surrogate_trade_request_response (app/controllers/concerns/template_responses_controller_helper.rb:268-272) blocks a second response unless allowed_surrogate_bid_even_after_bid. gate: allowed_surrogate_bid_even_after_bid=false.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 30.

cases.section: Surrogate bids (buyer on behalf of a vendor)
cases.title: A non-surrogate call on a staggered event is refused
cases.why: Serial bidding has its own path; ordinary create must be refused.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). {{tradeId}} is a staggered (serial) auction and the caller is not surrogate.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids on the staggered stage as the vendor.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 508 'Not allowed to bid on this product' — allowed_surrogate_bid_placement (app/controllers/api/bids_controller.rb:426-427) blocks non-surrogate bids on staggered events via this API. gate: staggered/serial auction.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 508.

cases.section: Surrogate bids (buyer on behalf of a vendor)
cases.title: A surrogate RFQ bid with no company is refused
cases.why: The surrogate call still needs to name the vendor it bids for.
cases.setup: Session: the BUYER who owns the sandbox event (this is how the platform runner authenticates). Live RFQ stage.
cases.steps: 1. POST /bids/template_input with company_uuid removed.
cases.expected: Should be a typed 4xx. create_bid reads company_id (app/controllers/api/bids_controller.rb:35); a blank company means can_place_bid_for_company fails (101) or the transform finds no data. Must not 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Regretting a line, cost-breakdown and T&C
cases.title: Regretting with a trade id that is not this bid's trade is refused
cases.why: A regret must apply to the bid's own stage, not an arbitrary one.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A draft bid {{bidUuid}}; the trade id passed belongs to a different stage.
cases.steps: 1. PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/line_items/{{lineItemUuid}}/regret_status with a mismatched trade_request_uuid.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 95 'Trade Request not found' — validate returns 95 when trade_request nil or trade_request.id != bid.trade_request_id (app/services/bids/line_item_regret_service.rb:100, 102). Not on the platform allowlist — reported not-run.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 95.

cases.section: Regretting a line, cost-breakdown and T&C
cases.title: A vendor cannot regret every line item in a lot-split event
cases.why: Regretting the whole lot would leave the vendor participating in nothing.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). A lot-split event where regretting {{lineItemUuid}} would leave no active lines for the vendor.
cases.steps: 1. PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/line_items/{{lineItemUuid}}/regret_status action_type regret.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 844 'You cannot regret all line items in a lot split event' — restrict_lot_event_full_egli_prunning (app/services/bids/line_item_regret_service.rb:115-128). gate: lot-split event. Not on the platform allowlist — reported not-run.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 844.

cases.section: Regretting a line, cost-breakdown and T&C
cases.title: During cost-breakdown time, global price updates are ignored
cases.why: CBD is a cost-justification phase, not a re-quote; global changes must not move the rank.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). {{tradeId}} is in cost-breakdown (CBD) review time; {{bidUuid}} is the vendor's bid.
cases.steps: 1. PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}} with a changed gross_total while CBD is running.
cases.expected: During CBD, parse_components_for_bid drops all but price/serial_number and clears global updates (app/controllers/concerns/trade_controller_helper.rb:6658-6661). The global gross_total change should not alter the ranking price. gate: in_cost_break_down_time.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; the ranking price is unchanged by the global edit.

cases.section: Regretting a line, cost-breakdown and T&C
cases.title: With mandatory T&C on, every clause is treated as required
cases.why: Mandatory T&C is a compliance gate; ignoring it must not yield a valid bid.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). {{tradeId}} has is_tnc_mandatory=true; the vendor submits without accepting a clause. gate: `is_tnc_mandatory` must be on for this case's outcome to hold.
cases.steps: 1. PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}} to active without accepting the mandatory terms.
cases.expected: With is_tnc_mandatory=true, effective_tnc_mode returns 'required' for every clause and attachment (trade_request.rb:998-1003; trade_request_model_helper). A submit that ignores them should be refused. gate: is_tnc_mandatory=true. Documented as no-5xx since the acceptance state cannot be forced in one run.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally the bid is not activated without acceptance.

cases.section: Regretting a line, cost-breakdown and T&C
cases.title: The valid create-bid request stays typed under repeated calls
cases.why: A control case: the base request never 5xxes even when repeated.
cases.setup: Session: the invited VENDOR user of {{vendorUuid}} (not the buyer). Live RFQ stage; a clean create then a duplicate.
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bids. 2. POST /v1/bids again immediately.
cases.expected: The happy path returns 200 with a bid_uuid (app/controllers/api/v1/bids_controller.rb:37); a same-window duplicate returns a typed 4xx (516 lock or 96 duplicate). Neither is a 5xx.
cases.oracle: Both responses are < 500.

journeys.title: Bidding on a vendor's behalf
journeys.goal: Enter a bid for a vendor from the buyer console (a surrogate bid).

cases.section: Price cap and surrogate bids on the Participants tab
cases.title: A price cap added for one vendor caps only that vendor
cases.why: Per-vendor caps are a negotiation tool; leaking a cap to other vendors is a defect.
cases.setup: A live RFQ with two QA vendors.
cases.steps: Add Price Cap X for vendor A; bid above X as A and as B.
cases.expected: A is refused with the cap message; B is accepted.
cases.oracle: Each vendor's bid outcome.

cases.title: The Participants tab of a published event offers Add Bid per vendor
cases.why: It is the entry point, and it lives on a *stage* tab, not the project tab — selecting a stage navigates, so the list arrives with a new page.
cases.setup: A published, live event with invited vendors.
cases.steps: Open the event. Select the stage tab. Open Participants.
cases.expected: The vendor list renders with an Add Bid control on the eligible rows.
cases.oracle: Reaching the list is the success condition — **not** finding an Add Bid control. The list is paginated and only eligible vendors show the control, so a single-vendor event shows a first page of other companies with none. Demanding the control here reports "surrogate bidding is unavailable" when the vendor is simply on another page.

cases.title: A named vendor is found by searching the participant list
cases.why: With 154 vendors, the wanted one is almost never on page one, and a surrogate bid placed for the wrong vendor is worse than none.
cases.setup: A live event with a known vendor on its audience.
cases.steps: Type the vendor's name into the participant search. Wait for the list to narrow.
cases.expected: That vendor's row is visible with its Add Bid control.
cases.oracle: Narrow the list *before* looking for the control; assert the chosen row's text contains the vendor name. Read the name from the row (the `rowItem` ancestor), not from the button's wrapper — the wrapper says only "Add Bid", which makes every vendor look identical and sends every match to the first row.

cases.title: The Add Bid drawer opens with that vendor's sheet
cases.why: The drawer is per-vendor; opening the wrong one attributes the bid to the wrong company.
cases.steps: Click Add Bid on the chosen row.
cases.expected: A drawer with the event's line items and the vendor's name on it.
cases.oracle: Drawer identified by containing the submit control; the vendor name in the drawer matches the row.

cases.title: Submit is disabled until a price is entered
cases.why: It is the product's own guard against an empty surrogate bid, and it doubles as the oracle for "did my values register in the sheet's state".
cases.setup: The drawer open, nothing entered.
cases.steps: Read the submit control.
cases.expected: Disabled.
cases.oracle: Disabled with nothing entered; enabled after one price. If it stays disabled after prices are typed, report exactly that — the values did not register — rather than clicking blindly and reporting "nothing happened".

cases.title: A surrogate bid is submitted and attributed to the vendor
cases.why: The core of PRD §3.4's second half.
cases.steps: Fill every price cell. Submit. Confirm if a modal appears.
cases.expected: The bid is recorded against that vendor, marked as buyer-added.
cases.oracle: The comparison shows a bid for that vendor at that price, flagged surrogate; no error toast after submit.

cases.title: Every price cell in the drawer is filled, not just the first
cases.why: The drawer reuses the data grid, so one priced row is enough to enable submit while leaving an incomplete bid — the same trap as UI-VBID-007, on the buyer's side.
cases.setup: A multi-line event.
cases.steps: Fill all price cells (and the offered-quantity cells the grid exposes). Submit.
cases.expected: A complete bid across every line.
cases.oracle: Count the filled cells; assert the buyer's comparison shows a price on every line.

cases.title: Two unnamed surrogate bids land on two different vendors
cases.why: Without tracking who was already bid for, two "give me any vendor" surrogate bids both pick the first row — the event ends with one bid while a test asserting two passes.
cases.setup: A live event with at least two eligible vendors.
cases.steps: Place a surrogate bid without naming a vendor, twice.
cases.expected: Two bids from two different companies.
cases.oracle: The two chosen row texts differ; the comparison shows two distinct vendors.

cases.title: After expiry, Add Bid depends on the company's post-expiry setting
cases.why: It is the one setting that changes whether late surrogate bids are possible at all, and it has obvious integrity implications.
cases.setup: Two tenants: post-expiry surrogate bidding on and off. A closed event on each.
cases.steps: Open Participants on each.
cases.expected: Offered where the setting is on, absent where it is off.
cases.oracle: Control presence flips with the setting; where absent, a crafted attempt is refused with "Order not active".

cases.title: Surrogate bidding is refused when the company forbids it
cases.why: `is_buyer_not_allowed_to_add_surrogate_bid` exists precisely so some organisations can bar it, and honouring it is a compliance matter.
cases.setup: An event whose config forbids buyer surrogate bids.
cases.steps: Attempt a surrogate bid.
cases.expected: Refused ("You are not allowed to use this functionality", 10).
cases.oracle: No bid created; the control is absent or the attempt refused.

cases.title: Only a valid surrogate bidder may place one
cases.why: The gate is super-admin, a member of a valid bidding team, or the event's own creator. Anyone else placing bids for vendors is a serious problem.
cases.setup: A buyer who is none of those three, on an event they can otherwise see.
cases.steps: Attempt a surrogate bid.
cases.expected: Refused (165).
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: A surrogate bid for a vendor who already bid is refused by default
cases.why: Overwriting a vendor's own bid is the most damaging thing this feature could do; by default it is refused (99) and only a specific config allows it.
cases.setup: A vendor who has submitted their own bid, on a tenant without `allowed_surrogate_bid_even_after_bid`.
cases.steps: Attempt a surrogate bid for them.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: The vendor's own bid is unchanged.

cases.title: Where the config allows it, a later surrogate bid revises rather than duplicates
cases.why: With `allowed_surrogate_bid_even_after_bid` on, the product *revises* the existing surrogate bid. Creating a second one instead would double-count the vendor in the comparison.
cases.setup: gate: `allowed_surrogate_bid_even_after_bid`. A vendor with an existing surrogate bid.
cases.steps: Place another surrogate bid for them at a new price.
cases.expected: One bid, at the new price, with the old value in history.
cases.oracle: Bid count for that vendor is still 1; the current price is the new one.

cases.title: A surrogate bid is visibly marked as buyer-entered
cases.why: At award time it matters enormously whether a price came from the vendor or from the buyer's phone call. If it is not labelled, the audit trail is gone.
cases.setup: An event with one vendor bid and one surrogate bid.
cases.steps: Read the buyer's comparison.
cases.expected: The surrogate bid is labelled as such; the vendor's own is not.
cases.oracle: The label is present on exactly one of the two.

cases.section: Price cap and surrogate bids on the Participants tab
cases.title: Price cap and surrogate bid are offered only after publish
cases.setup: A draft and a live event.
cases.steps: Look for Add Bid / Add Price Cap on each.
cases.expected: Absent on the draft ("Bid & Price Cap can be added after event creation."); present on the live event.
cases.oracle: Control presence.

cases.title: Add Bid is absent on a draft event
cases.why: A bid on an unpublished event has nothing to bid against.
cases.setup: A draft event.
cases.steps: Look for the participant list and the control.
cases.expected: Not offered.
cases.oracle: Zero Add Bid controls.

cases.title: Add Bid is absent on a withdrawn event
cases.why: Withdrawal must close the buyer's path too, not just the vendor's.
cases.setup: A withdrawn event.
cases.steps: Open Participants.
cases.expected: No Add Bid controls.
cases.oracle: Zero controls.

cases.title: Add Bid is offered on an Upcoming event
cases.why: Deliberately wider than the vendor's own window — a buyer can enter a bid received by phone before the event opens.
cases.setup: An Upcoming event.
cases.steps: Open Participants and place a surrogate bid.
cases.expected: Offered and accepted.
cases.oracle: Bid recorded; contrast with UI-VBID-018, where the vendor cannot.

cases.title: Add Bid is absent on a knockout auction
cases.why: Knockout runs on automated offers; a manual surrogate bid has no meaning in it.
cases.setup: A live knockout auction.
cases.steps: Open Participants.
cases.expected: No Add Bid drawer.
cases.oracle: Zero controls.

cases.title: Add Bid is absent on a dutch auction
cases.why: Same reasoning, different strategy.
cases.setup: A live dutch auction.
cases.steps: Open Participants.
cases.expected: No Add Bid drawer.
cases.oracle: Zero controls.

cases.title: A technical stage offers Add Technical Bid, not Add Bid
cases.why: They are different controls with different payloads; conflating them makes a technical surrogate response look impossible.
cases.setup: A live RFP stage.
cases.steps: Open Participants.
cases.expected: A technical-bid control, no price drawer.
cases.oracle: The technical control exists; the price drawer does not.

cases.title: A surrogate technical response can be entered for a vendor
cases.why: It is the technical half of surrogate bidding, and the API has a dedicated endpoint for it.
cases.setup: A live RFP stage with an invited vendor.
cases.steps: Add a technical bid for that vendor: answer both the global and the line-item forms, submit.
cases.expected: Submitted and attributed to the vendor.
cases.oracle: The buyer sees a submitted technical response for that vendor, marked surrogate. Pairs with API-SUR-002.

cases.title: A surrogate bid may require approval before it counts
cases.why: On tenants with a surrogate-bid approval flow, the bid is *requested*, not active — and a test asserting an immediate active bid fails there forever.
cases.setup: gate: surrogate-bid approval configured.
cases.steps: Place a surrogate bid.
cases.expected: It enters an approval-pending state and an approver has a task.
cases.oracle: Bid status is approval-requested; the approver's task list contains it.

cases.title: Reading the surrogate approval flows needs approval-read permission
cases.why: It is the one genuinely gated method on an otherwise open bid policy, which makes it easy to lose.
cases.setup: A buyer without approval-flow read permission.
cases.steps: Trigger the surrogate approval-flow lookup.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: Refusal rather than an empty list — an empty list would look like "no approval needed" and let the bid through. Pairs with API-SUR-011.

cases.title: A surrogate bid is refused with a negative or absent price
cases.why: Same validation as a vendor's bid; the surrogate path must not be the lenient one.
cases.steps: Enter a negative price, then clear the cell entirely, and try to submit each time.
cases.expected: Refused both times.
cases.oracle: Submit stays disabled for the empty case; a message for the negative.

cases.title: A surrogate bid appears to the vendor as their own bid
cases.why: If the vendor cannot see it, they may bid again and the two disagree; if they can, they can query it. Either way, the state must be honest.
cases.setup: An event with a surrogate bid placed for a vendor.
cases.steps: As that vendor, open the event.
cases.expected: The bid is visible with its price, and the product is clear about who entered it.
cases.oracle: The vendor's portal shows a bid at that price.

cases.section: Price cap and surrogate bids on the Participants tab
cases.title: Editing a cap after a bid exists follows the increase/decrease rule (records current behaviour)
cases.setup: A live RFQ with a cap and one bid.
cases.steps: Raise the cap; lower the cap below the bid.
cases.expected: Records what the product allows for each (flow-map Q20).
cases.oracle: trade_controller_helper.rb:469-477.

cases.title: A buyer places a surrogate RFQ bid for a vendor
cases.why: The core capability. It must land as a bid attributed to the vendor, not to the buyer.
cases.setup: A live RFQ stage with a vendor invited; the caller is the event's creator.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/template_input` with the vendor's `company_id` and the trade.
cases.expected: 200; a bid for that vendor.
cases.oracle: The bid's `company_id` is the vendor's and it is flagged as a surrogate bid. `flows/surrogate.ts`.

cases.title: A surrogate bid is refused when the company config forbids it
cases.why: Code 10. Some organisations bar it on principle and honouring that is a compliance requirement, not a preference.
cases.setup: An event whose config sets `is_buyer_not_allowed_to_add_surrogate_bid`.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/template_input`.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: A buyer who is not a valid surrogate bidder is refused
cases.why: Code 165. The permitted set is super admin, valid bidding team, or the event's creator — anyone else placing bids for vendors is a serious problem.
cases.setup: A buyer in the company but none of those three.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/template_input`.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: After expiry, a surrogate bid depends on the post-expiry setting
cases.why: It is the only setting that permits a bid after the window closed, which makes it the highest-integrity switch in this section.
cases.setup: A closed event, on a tenant with the setting off and one with it on.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/template_input` on each.
cases.expected: Refused (33) where off; accepted where on.
cases.oracle: Both outcomes, and where accepted the bid is marked surrogate.

cases.title: A surrogate bid for a vendor who already bid is refused by default
cases.why: Code 99. Overwriting a vendor's own bid is the most damaging thing this feature could do, and it is refused unless a specific config allows it.
cases.setup: A vendor with their own active bid; no `allowed_surrogate_bid_even_after_bid`.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/template_input` for them.
cases.oracle: The vendor's own bid is unchanged.

cases.title: With the config on, a repeat surrogate bid revises rather than duplicates
cases.why: With `allowed_surrogate_bid_even_after_bid`, an existing surrogate bid is *returned for revision* instead of a second one being created. A duplicate would double-count the vendor in the comparison.
cases.setup: gate: `allowed_surrogate_bid_even_after_bid`. A vendor with an existing surrogate bid.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/template_input` again at a new price.
cases.expected: One bid, at the new price, with history.
cases.oracle: Bid count for that vendor is still 1. `bids_controller_helper.rb:2670-2677`.

cases.title: A surrogate bid validates prices exactly like a vendor's
cases.why: The surrogate path must not be the lenient one — a negative price entered by a buyer is as wrong as one entered by a vendor.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/template_input` with a negative price, a negative quantity and a negative GST in turn.
cases.expected: 106, 35 and 107 respectively.
cases.oracle: Nothing created in any case.

cases.title: A surrogate bid is distinguishable from a vendor's own bid
cases.why: At award time it matters enormously which is which. If the flag is not set, the audit trail is gone.
cases.setup: One vendor bid and one surrogate bid on the same event.
cases.steps: Read both.
cases.expected: Exactly one is marked as a surrogate/buyer-added bid.
cases.oracle: The flag differs between the two.

cases.title: A surrogate bid cannot be placed for a vendor who is not on the event
cases.why: Otherwise the buyer could manufacture a bid from an uninvited company.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/template_input` with a company that is not on the audience.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid created for that company.

cases.title: A buyer places a surrogate technical response for a vendor
cases.why: The technical half, with its own endpoint and its own payload covering both the global and line-item forms.
cases.setup: A live RFP stage with a vendor invited.
cases.steps: `POST /template_responses/create_surrogate_response` with both forms' pages.
cases.expected: 200; a submitted response attributed to the vendor.
cases.oracle: The response exists for that vendor and is marked surrogate.

cases.title: The event's creator can place a surrogate bid
cases.why: The positive half of API-SUR-005; without it the gate could be refusing everyone.
cases.setup: The event's creator, not a super admin, not on a bidding team.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/template_input`.
cases.expected: Accepted.
cases.oracle: Bid created for the vendor.

cases.title: A surrogate bid is accepted on an Upcoming event
cases.why: Deliberately wider than a vendor's own window — a buyer records a bid received offline before the event opens. Contrast with API-BID-005.
cases.setup: An Upcoming event.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/template_input`.
cases.expected: Accepted.
cases.oracle: Bid created while a vendor's own bid on the same stage is refused with 33.

cases.title: Reading surrogate approval flows requires approval-read permission
cases.why: One of only two genuinely gated bid-policy methods. An empty list would read as "no approval needed" and let the bid straight through, so a refusal is the correct behaviour and an empty 200 is a finding.
cases.setup: A buyer without approval-flow read permission.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/approval_workflows_for_surrogate_bid_create`.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: A refusal, not an empty array. ≈ BE-5.5.

cases.title: A surrogate bid requiring approval enters a requested state
cases.why: On approval-configured tenants the bid does not count yet, and a test asserting an active bid fails there permanently.
cases.setup: gate: surrogate-bid approval configured.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/template_input` with approval remarks.
cases.expected: The bid is approval-requested; an approval record carries the remarks.
cases.oracle: Bid status approval-requested; remarks stored.

cases.title: A surrogate bid with no products is refused
cases.why: Buyer-added bids are exempt from *some* product validation, so this case establishes what the exemption actually covers rather than assuming it covers everything.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/template_input` with no trade products.
cases.expected: Refused, or accepted-and-documented — with the resulting state recorded.
cases.oracle: Record the behaviour; if a bid with no products becomes active, that is a finding worth raising against `bid.rb:216-222`'s `is_buyer_added_bid?` exemption.

cases.title: A buyer-edited bid is labelled as such
cases.why: `BidContextLabelService` stamps a `buyer_edit` context, and that label is what a later auditor reads.
cases.setup: A vendor's bid, edited by the buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH` the bid as the buyer.
cases.expected: The bid carries a buyer-edit context entry.
cases.oracle: The context's latest key is a buyer-edit key.

cases.title: A surrogate bid appears in the vendor's own view
cases.why: If the vendor cannot see it they may bid again, and the two records disagree. Whatever the product's intent, the state must be honest.
cases.setup: A surrogate bid placed for a vendor.
cases.steps: As that vendor, read their bids on the event.
cases.expected: The bid is visible with its price.
cases.oracle: The vendor's read returns a bid at that price.

cases.section: Enter the vendor's price on their behalf — `POST /bids/template_input`
cases.title: Enter the vendor's price on their behalf answers within 10 seconds
cases.why: A regression that makes a core call several times slower is a defect even when the body is right.
cases.setup: A buyer walking the API journey (RFQ only, Technical + RFQ), at the step "Enter the vendor's price on their behalf".
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, do “Enter the vendor's price on their behalf” in the API journey (`POST /bids/template_input`). 2. Time the answer.
cases.expected: The app answers within 10 seconds.
cases.oracle: Checked automatically on every API journey run; the report shows what actually came back. Engine check: `max_ms 10000`, learned from 4 real response(s).
