cases.title: Enter the vendor's technical response on their behalf answers within 10 seconds
cases.why: A regression that makes a core call several times slower is a defect even when the body is right.
cases.setup: A buyer walking the API journey (Technical + RFQ), at the step "Enter the vendor's technical response on their behalf".
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, do “Enter the vendor's technical response on their behalf” in the API journey (`POST /template_responses/create_surrogate_response`). 2. Time the answer.
cases.expected: The app answers within 10 seconds.
cases.oracle: Checked automatically on every API journey run; the report shows what actually came back. Engine check: `max_ms 10000`, learned from 1 real response(s).

cases.title: A surrogate bid is refused on an offline-trading event
cases.why: The recognition logic explicitly excludes offline trading, so the call falls through to the normal path and is refused as a self-company bid.
cases.setup: An offline-trade stage.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/template_input` as the buyer.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: The approval-flow lookup requires a trade request id
cases.why: Code 2 — a missing id must not be a nil dereference.
cases.steps: `POST` the same endpoint with no `trade_request_id`.
cases.expected: 422, code 2.
cases.oracle: That code; no 500.

cases.title: The approval-flow lookup applies the surrogate permission checks too
cases.why: It runs the same `allowed_surrogate_bid_placement` guard, so a buyer barred from surrogate bidding must not be able to enumerate the approval flows either.
cases.setup: A buyer refused by API-SUR-005.
cases.steps: `POST` the approval-flow endpoint.
cases.expected: The same refusal.
cases.oracle: Same error code as the bid attempt.

cases.title: A surrogate bid is exempt from anomaly detection
cases.why: Anomaly detection deliberately skips surrogate bids; if it did not, a buyer recording a genuinely low offline quote would be blocked.
cases.setup: Three comparable bids and a surrogate bid far outside the range.
cases.steps: Place the surrogate bid.
cases.expected: Accepted without an anomaly flag.
cases.oracle: No anomaly response; the same price as a vendor's own bid *is* flagged.

cases.title: A surrogate bid picks up the vendor's first make where makes exist
cases.why: When the vendor has alternative makes, the surrogate path assigns the first one automatically. Without it the bid is unattributable to a make and the comparison is incomplete.
cases.setup: A vendor with alternatives mapped on the event group.
cases.steps: `POST /bids/template_input` without an alternatives mapping.
cases.expected: The bid carries the vendor's first active make.
cases.oracle: The mapping id on the bid equals the lowest-id active mapping for that vendor.

journeys.title: Awarding and negotiating
journeys.goal: Compare bids on Master QCS, counter-offer, and award the event to a vendor.

cases.title: Master QCS is reachable on a closed event with bids
cases.why: It is the door to awarding; if it does not open, nothing else here runs.
cases.setup: A published event with at least one submitted bid.
cases.steps: Open the event → Master QCS tab.
cases.expected: The comparison grid renders with the line items and the bidding vendors.
cases.oracle: The grid is present and lists the expected vendor(s).

cases.title: The comparison shows every bid, per line item, with totals
cases.why: It is the decision surface. A missing or misattributed bid here produces a wrong award.
cases.setup: An event with two vendors' bids at known prices.
cases.steps: Read the grid.
cases.expected: Both vendors, both prices, correct per-line and total amounts.
cases.oracle: Compare every rendered price against the fixture; assert the vendor names are the real ones and not placeholders.

cases.title: Start Awarding enters the awarding flow
cases.why: The first of the two entry controls.
cases.setup: An event with bids and no proposal yet.
cases.steps: Press Start Awarding.
cases.expected: The awarding screen opens for this event.
cases.oracle: URL moves to the awarding route with the event's id.

cases.title: Bid Selection Proposal re-enters the flow once a draft proposal exists
cases.why: Without this, awarding appears to work once per event and then vanish.
cases.setup: An event with a draft proposal.
cases.steps: Return to Master QCS and read the entry control.
cases.expected: "Bid Selection Proposal" with a Draft tag, and it re-enters the flow.
cases.oracle: The second control exists and navigates; the first is absent.

cases.title: Awarding is blocked while a selected or requested proposal exists
cases.why: Two live proposals on one event would award it twice.
cases.setup: An event with a submitted (requested) proposal.
cases.steps: Try to start a new award.
cases.expected: Blocked, with the existing proposal offered instead: Master QCS does not show "Start Awarding" at all and shows the proposal's status "Approval in Progress".
cases.oracle: No "Start Awarding" button; the status "Approval in Progress" is shown; no second proposal is created. Pairs with API-AWD-005.

cases.title: Allocating a line item to a vendor moves the item counter
cases.why: It is one of the two counters, and it is the one that says *what* is being awarded.
cases.setup: The awarding grid with two line items.
cases.steps: Allocate one line item to a vendor.
cases.expected: "Tot. selected line items" reads 1/2.
cases.oracle: Read the app's own counter — it is a more honest oracle than inferring which checkbox belongs to which vendor from the DOM.

cases.title: Awarding a vendor moves the vendor counter
cases.why: It is the counter the Create Proposal validation actually checks, and the one that was mistaken for an unrelated toggle.
cases.steps: Tick the control that awards the vendor.
cases.expected: "Awarded Vendors" rises to 1.
cases.oracle: Both counters must be non-zero before Create Proposal; assert each separately so a failure says which one is missing.

cases.title: Create Proposal is refused with no vendor awarded
cases.why: It is the exact failure the two-counter confusion produced: "Please award for at least one Vendor".
cases.setup: Line items allocated but no vendor awarded.
cases.steps: Press Create Proposal.
cases.expected: Refused with that message.
cases.oracle: Message shown; no proposal created.

cases.title: Create Proposal produces a draft proposal
cases.why: Creation and submission are deliberately separate — which is why the Master QCS control changes — and a draft proposal is not an awarded event.
cases.steps: Allocate, award, Create Proposal.
cases.expected: A draft proposal exists with the allocation on it.
cases.oracle: Proposal exists in draft with the expected vendor and line items. A missing submit control must be reported, not treated as success.

cases.title: Submitting the proposal sends it into the approval workflow
cases.why: PRD §3.5 — the award goes through a proposal *and* an approval workflow. Submission is the point of no return.
cases.steps: Submit the draft proposal.
cases.expected: Status moves to requested; approvers have tasks.
cases.oracle: Proposal status requested; approver task exists.

cases.title: An approver approves and the award completes
cases.why: It is the last step of the whole catalog and the one that changes commercial reality.
cases.setup: A submitted proposal and its approver.
cases.steps: As the approver, open the task and approve.
cases.expected: The proposal is selected; the event shows as awarded to that vendor.
cases.oracle: Event state awarded; the awarded vendor and quantity match the allocation.

cases.title: Partial awarding splits one line item across vendors
cases.why: It is the whole reason line-item awarding mode exists, and the quantities must add up.
cases.setup: A line-item-awarding event with a quantity of 100 and two bids.
cases.steps: Award 60 to A and 40 to B.
cases.expected: Both allocations recorded; total awarded = 100.
cases.oracle: Sum of awarded quantities equals the requested quantity; neither vendor exceeds their offered quantity.

cases.title: Awarding more than the requested quantity is refused
cases.why: Over-awarding creates a commitment the requisition never covered.
cases.setup: A quantity of 100.
cases.steps: Try to award 60 + 60.
cases.expected: Refused with a readable message.
cases.oracle: No proposal with 120 awarded.

cases.title: After the first bid a vendor column appears with rank and amounts
cases.setup: A live RFQ; the QA vendor bids.
cases.steps: Open Master QCS.
cases.expected: One column for the vendor: Qty Offer, Rank 1, Auction/RFQ Amount = price × quantity, rate per unit, Sum Total in the Final section.
cases.oracle: Figures equal the bid the API holds.

cases.title: Ranks follow the amounts: lowest total is rank 1 on a buy event
cases.setup: Two QA vendors bidding different totals.
cases.steps: Open Master QCS.
cases.expected: The lower total shows Rank 1, the other Rank 2.
cases.oracle: rank_calculator.rb `ranking_for_scores`.

cases.title: The downloaded report equals the screen
cases.why: The report is what gets shared and approved; it must never disagree with the screen.
cases.setup: A closed RFQ with two bids.
cases.steps: Open Master QCS; Download Report.
cases.expected: For every vendor and line: Rate, Gross Amount and Rank in the file equal Master QCS at download time; Sum Total equals the sum of line amounts.
cases.oracle: Parse the workbook; compare cell by cell.

cases.title: Sum Total in Auction Final equals the sum of the line amounts
cases.setup: A bid with two lines.
cases.steps: Read Master QCS.
cases.expected: Sum Total = Σ line amounts (exact decimals).
cases.oracle: Independent recomputation (integrity rules).

cases.title: A disabled awarding control explains itself
cases.why: Awarding is gated by `is_awarding_allowed` and the button carries a tooltip saying why — a live event, a stage still in draft, or a superseded version. That reason is worth reporting instead of discovering as a dead click.
cases.setup: A live event whose bidding is still open.
cases.steps: Hover the awarding control.
cases.expected: Disabled, with a tooltip naming the reason.
cases.oracle: Report the tooltip text; do not click through.

cases.title: Awarding is blocked while this user holds a draft proposal
cases.why: The gate is per-user for drafts, which is subtly different from the previous case.
cases.setup: The same buyer with a draft proposal on the event.
cases.steps: Try to start a fresh award.
cases.expected: Blocked; the draft is offered.
cases.oracle: Proposal count unchanged.

cases.title: A rejected proposal returns the event to awardable
cases.why: Otherwise a rejection deadlocks the event.
cases.setup: A submitted proposal.
cases.steps: As the approver, reject with remarks.
cases.expected: The event can be awarded again; the rejection and remarks are recorded.
cases.oracle: Awarding controls re-enable; the rejection is in the history.

cases.title: Discarding a draft proposal re-enables awarding
cases.why: It is the escape hatch from UI-AWD-007, and it must actually clear the gate.
cases.setup: A draft proposal.
cases.steps: Discard it.
cases.expected: Awarding is available again.
cases.oracle: The Start Awarding control returns.

cases.title: Awarding the whole lot on a partial-lot RFQ is refused
cases.why: The backend refuses it in words ("You cannot award entire lot when RFQ was done for partial lot.", 503) and the reason is genuinely non-obvious.
cases.setup: An RFQ run as partial lot.
cases.steps: Try to award the entire lot to one vendor.
cases.expected: Refused with that message.
cases.oracle: Message shown; no proposal.

cases.title: Closing the bid to select a winner is refused outside the allowed window
cases.why: `close_bid` has its own timing gate ("Unable to close the order at this time. Please wait for the bidding to end", 9), and closing early would cut off bids that were still permitted.
cases.setup: A live event still inside its bidding window.
cases.steps: Attempt to close the bid and select a winner.
cases.expected: Refused with that message.
cases.oracle: The event stays live; no winner is set.

cases.title: The awarding report downloads and matches the screen
cases.why: The report is what leaves the building — it goes to finance and to the vendor. A mismatch with the screen is the most consequential inconsistency in the module.
cases.setup: An awarded event.
cases.steps: Download the awarding sheet.
cases.expected: A file whose vendors, line items, quantities and prices match the grid.
cases.oracle: Parse the file and compare the numbers cell by cell against the rendered grid.

cases.title: Master QCS reads "No bids are placed yet!" until the first bid
cases.setup: A live RFQ with no bids.
cases.steps: Open Master QCS.
cases.expected: The empty message; no vendor columns.
cases.oracle: Text on screen.

cases.title: Two vendors tied at the best price (records current behaviour)
cases.why: The code gives every tied vendor rank 2 and nobody rank 1; the product team must say whether that is intended (flow-map Q23).
cases.setup: Two QA vendors bidding the same total.
cases.steps: Open Master QCS.
cases.expected: Records the ranks shown.
cases.oracle: rank_calculator.rb:26-29.

cases.title: The report's summary block describes the event correctly
cases.setup: As UI-FQCS-005.
cases.steps: Read the summary rows.
cases.expected: Event link, id, title, template name, date, start, end, duration, creator, vendors invited and participated, closed-at all match the event.
cases.oracle: config.rb SUMMARY_COLUMNS vs the API's event.

cases.title: The report version follows the client's setting (records which)
cases.setup: Each client.
cases.steps: Download the report; read its file name.
cases.expected: Records V1–V4 or a report template per client (flow-map Q24).
cases.oracle: master_qcs_report_selector.rb; file name `<ref>_Master_QCS_Report_V4`.

cases.title: A vendor invited but not bidding (records current behaviour)
cases.setup: Two QA vendors invited, one bids.
cases.steps: Download the report.
cases.expected: Records whether the silent vendor appears, and with what in its cells (flow-map Q25).
cases.oracle: The workbook's vendor columns.

cases.title: A proposal is created for an eligible company
cases.why: The first of the four calls, and the one the gate applies to.
cases.setup: A closed event with at least one submitted bid.
cases.steps: `POST /proposal` with the event group.
cases.expected: 200 with a proposal uuid, in draft.
cases.oracle: Uuid returned; status draft. ≈ BE-6.1. `flows/awarding.ts`.

cases.title: An award response allocates a line item to a vendor
cases.why: It is the actual allocation; a proposal with no responses awards nothing.
cases.setup: A draft proposal and a submitted bid on the line item.
cases.steps: `POST /proposal/:uuid/add_response` with the vendor, line item and quantity.
cases.expected: 200; the allocation is on the proposal.
cases.oracle: The proposal's responses contain that vendor and quantity.

cases.title: Adding a response with no submitted bid is refused
cases.why: Awarding a vendor who never bid is the clearest possible integrity failure in this section.
cases.setup: A vendor with no bid.
cases.steps: `POST add_response` for them.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No allocation created for that vendor.

cases.title: The approval workflow is readable for a proposal
cases.why: Submission needs the flow's uuid, so an empty or wrong flow makes submission impossible — and a *silently* empty one makes it look approved.
cases.steps: `GET /proposal/:uuid/approval_workflows`.
cases.expected: At least one flow with steps and approvers.
cases.oracle: A flow uuid and at least one approver uuid.

cases.title: Submitting the proposal moves it to requested and blocks further awarding
cases.why: PRD §3.5 — the award goes through a proposal and an approval workflow, and one event must not carry two live proposals.
cases.steps: `POST /proposal/:uuid/submit` with the approval flow uuid. Then attempt a second proposal.
cases.expected: Submitted; the second proposal is refused.
cases.oracle: `should_allow_awarding` is false afterwards. ≈ BE-6.2.

cases.title: Awarding is blocked before the close window is reached
cases.why: Awarding while bidding is still legally open would cut off bids that were still permitted.
cases.setup: A live event whose latest commercial stage has not reached its close window.
cases.steps: Read `config.should_allow_awarding`; attempt a proposal.
cases.expected: The flag is false and the proposal is refused.
cases.oracle: Both. `event_group_controller_helper.rb:629-648`.

cases.title: A caller from another company cannot add a response
cases.why: `add_response?` is the policy method behind show, submit and the approval lookup, so a hole here opens four endpoints at once.
cases.setup: A caller whose allowed companies exclude the proposal's company.
cases.steps: `POST add_response`.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No allocation created. ≈ BE-6.5.

cases.title: Partial awarding splits a line item across vendors and the quantities add up
cases.why: It is why line-item awarding exists, and the arithmetic is what gets billed.
cases.setup: A line item of 100 with two bids.
cases.steps: `add_response` 60 to A and 40 to B, then submit.
cases.expected: Both allocations recorded; total awarded = 100.
cases.oracle: Sum of awarded quantities equals the requested quantity; neither vendor exceeds their offered quantity.

cases.title: Awarding more than the requested quantity is refused
cases.why: Over-awarding creates a commitment the requisition never covered.
cases.steps: `add_response` 60 and 60 on a quantity of 100.
cases.expected: The second is refused.
cases.oracle: Total awarded never exceeds 100.

cases.title: Awarding more than a vendor offered is refused
cases.why: A vendor who offered 40 cannot be awarded 60; the validation is per-vendor, not just per-line.
cases.setup: A vendor who offered 40.
cases.steps: `add_response` 60 for them.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No allocation above the offered quantity.

cases.title: Closing the bid selects the winning bid
cases.why: The positive half; it is what actually marks a bid selected.
cases.setup: A closed event with bids.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/:id/close_bid` naming the winning bid.
cases.expected: That bid becomes selected.
cases.oracle: The bid's status is selected and no other bid is.

cases.title: A selected bid can no longer be revised
cases.why: It is the guarantee that an award is final; revision after selection would change the awarded price.
cases.steps: Attempt `PATCH /bids/revise_bid/:id` on the selected bid.
cases.expected: Refused (32).
cases.oracle: The selected bid's price is unchanged.

cases.title: The awarded event reports its awarded state consistently
cases.why: Several read paths derive from the award; if they disagree, the buyer and the vendor see different outcomes.
cases.steps: After the award, read the event group, the stage and the bid.
cases.expected: All three agree on the awarded vendor and quantity.
cases.oracle: Three-way consistency check.

cases.title: The full chain runs end to end
cases.why: It is the acceptance test for PRD §3 as a whole, and it is what the existing suite already drives — create, publish, bid, award.
cases.setup: A buyer, a vendor, and a live event.
cases.steps: Create the draft → create the stage(s) → activate → vendor technical response → vendor bid → close → proposal → response → approval flow → submit.
cases.expected: Every step succeeds and the event ends awarded to the bidding vendor.
cases.oracle: Assert each step's own oracle, and finally that the awarded vendor equals the vendor who bid.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: Scoring with no form object is refused
cases.why: Second ANDed condition of valid_params?; the lock identifier also reads params.dig(:form, :id), so a missing form must not break the before_action either.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}"}`. 1. POST /evaluations with trade_request_uuid and company_uuid only.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 — @options[:form].present? is false (app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:45). No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: A score with no form identifier is refused
cases.why: The journey sends form.uuid, which ParamsAuth rewrites to form.id; a client that forgets it must get code 2, not a score on 'no form'.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"score": 3, "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. POST /evaluations with form {score: 3, remark} and no uuid/id.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 — valid_form? needs form[:id].present? (app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:61). No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: Scoring a form assigned to another evaluator is refused as bad parameters
cases.why: Scoring someone else's form surfaces as a PARAMS error, which is why the journey sees 'Insufficient parameters' when it picks the wrong form. A regression that moves the form check into validate_evaluator would change the code the UI keys on.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; the caller evaluates a DIFFERENT line item's form; the body deliberately keeps the non-existent form Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw== instead of {{evalFormUuid}}.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==", "score": 3, "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. As evaluator A, POST /evaluations with the form uuid assigned to evaluator B (here the non-existent Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==).
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (not 101) — form[:id].in?(get_allowed_forms_for_user(...).pluck(:id)) is part of valid_form? (app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:63), which runs before validate_evaluator. No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2 and the other evaluator's form still shows no score from A.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: A form with no score is refused
cases.why: A missing score must not be stored as nil: nil scores drop out of QCS averages and silently raise a vendor's mean.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. POST /evaluations with form {uuid, remark} and no score.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 — form[:score].present? is false (app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:64). No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: A score sent as text is refused
cases.why: Form inputs are strings by default; a client that forgets to parseInt gets 'Insufficient parameters' with no hint the TYPE is the problem.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "score": "3", "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. POST /evaluations with form.score = "3" (string).
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 — form[:score].instance_of?(Integer) is required unless the event is vendor-onboarding v2 (app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:65). No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: A score one above the highest label is refused (journey root cause)
cases.why: ROOT CAUSE of the journey's intermittent 'Insufficient parameters': eventJourney.ts scores randInt(1,10), so every draw of 6-10 is refused. The score is NOT 'out of 10' — it is a label key.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; the RFP uses the default evaluation_score_label_mapping (scores 0-5); form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "score": 6, "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. POST /evaluations with form.score = 6 (one above the highest default label).
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 — form[:score].in?(event_group.get_evaluation_score_vs_label.keys) is false; the default mapping has keys 0..5 (db/migrate/20250209130259_set_evaluation_score_label_mapping.rb, app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:66). No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2; the same call with score 5 passes the params check.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: A TNA (zero) score with a blank reason is refused
cases.why: Score 0 is TNA (technically not accepted) in the default mapping — the one score that disqualifies a vendor from awarding. An empty-string remark is the easy bypass of the mandatory justification.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; not vendor-onboarding v2; form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "score": 0, "remark": ""}}`. 1. POST /evaluations with form.score = 0 and remark = "".
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 — a zero score is only valid when form[:remark].present? (app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:67-69); "" is not present. No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: Every score is refused when the RFP carries no label mapping
cases.why: CONFIG trap: no code path writes evaluation_score_label_mapping into a NEW RFP's config (only the 2025-02 backfill migration did). If new RFPs lack it, scoring is impossible and every attempt reads as 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; the RFP's config has no evaluation_score_label_mapping key (EventGroup#evaluation_score_label_mapping uses the RFP's config whenever an RFP exists, and TradeRequest#evaluation_score_label_mapping returns [] when the key is absent); form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "score": 3, "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. POST /evaluations with a normally valid score 3.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 for EVERY score — get_evaluation_score_vs_label.keys is [] (app/models/event_group.rb:718-735, app/models/model_helpers/trade_request_model_helper.rb:912-914). The company-level MasterConfiguration default is never consulted once an RFP exists. No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2 for scores 0..5 alike; GET /v1/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/schema trade_config.evaluation_score_label_mapping is empty.

cases.section: Scoring — wrong state, wrong actor, wrong time
cases.title: Scoring before the technical round closes is refused
cases.why: Two-envelope confidentiality: scoring while vendors can still edit would let a score leak and responses change after it.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; the RFP is still accepting responses (bid_end_time in the future).
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "score": 3, "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. POST /evaluations with a valid body while the RFP is live.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 33 'Order not active' — render_error_json(33) if trade_request.bid_end_time > Time.now (app/controllers/api/evaluations_controller.rb:25). No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.

cases.section: Scoring — wrong state, wrong actor, wrong time
cases.title: A vendor cannot score itself
cases.why: Self-scoring is the most direct fraud on a technical evaluation.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; caller is the VENDOR user.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "score": 5, "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. Log in as the vendor. 2. POST /evaluations scoring itself 5.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 33 — the lookup is scoped to company_id: Current.workspace.id (app/controllers/api/evaluations_controller.rb:14); the vendor's workspace owns no RFP. No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 33 and the vendor's score is unchanged.

cases.title: An uninvited vendor cannot read the technical round
cases.why: The schema carries sheets.forms with evaluator assignments and extra_closing_time; an uninvited vendor must not read another vendor's technical round.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; caller is a vendor user who is NOT in the RFP's audience.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/schema?response_type=template&additional_fields=order_details`. 1. GET the RFP schema as that vendor.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 536 'You are not allowed to view this event.' — validate_event checks trade.is_allowed_to_view?(Current.user) (app/controllers/concerns/trade_controller_helper.rb:2219-2221).

cases.title: Submitting evaluations before close is refused (PATCH)
cases.why: Same guard as EVAL-QCS-001 but on the route that actually exists (PATCH).
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time is in the future; the evaluator has draft scores.
cases.steps: `PATCH /evaluations/submit` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}"}`. 1. PATCH /evaluations/submit before the RFP closes.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 33 — trade_request.bid_end_time > Time.now (app/controllers/api/evaluations_controller.rb:42). No Proposal created by create_proposal_for_evaluations.

cases.title: Submitting with one vendor unscored is refused
cases.why: A half-scored submission would create a technical proposal that disqualifies the unscored vendor by omission.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time passed; two vendors responded; the evaluator scored only one.
cases.steps: `PATCH /evaluations/submit` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}"}`. 1. PATCH /evaluations/submit.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 571 'Please, evaluate on all fields' — rfp_evaluation_count_invalid? compares expected (participants × items) with draft/peer_review scores (app/helpers/api/evaluations_helper.rb:811-832, returned at app/helpers/api/evaluations_helper.rb:609).
cases.oracle: 422 + code 571; evaluations stay draft.

cases.title: Re-evaluation items cannot be listed outside evaluation time
cases.why: Re-evaluation is only meaningful during evaluation time; listing items outside it invites requests that will all fail.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; the RFP is still live (before bid_end_time).
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/line_items_for_reevaluation`. 1. GET /v1/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/line_items_for_reevaluation.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 101 — render_error_json(101) unless trade_request.in_evaluation_time? (app/controllers/api/v1/trade_controller.rb:1316); in_evaluation_time? is the window bid_end_time..extra_closing_time.

cases.title: Re-evaluation cannot be requested while vendors are still responding
cases.why: 'Only during evaluation time' rule.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; the RFP is still live.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/request_tr_reevaluation` with body `{"form_uuids": ["{{evalFormUuid}}"], "remarks": "QA_Platform_reeval_{{stamp}}"}`. 1. PATCH request_tr_reevaluation with a form uuid and remarks.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 101 (app/controllers/api/v1/trade_controller.rb:1352). No AdditionalRequest created.

cases.title: Re-evaluation cannot be requested after the evaluation window
cases.why: Upper bound of the same rule; contrast with first-time scoring, which has no upper bound.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; now is after extra_closing_time.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/request_tr_reevaluation` with body `{"form_uuids": ["{{evalFormUuid}}"], "remarks": "QA_Platform_reeval_{{stamp}}"}`. 1. PATCH request_tr_reevaluation.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 101 — in_evaluation_time? (alias of is_auction_in_extra_closing_time?, app/models/trade_request.rb:968) is false after the window (app/controllers/api/v1/trade_controller.rb:1352).

cases.title: Re-evaluation of a form you cannot see is refused
cases.why: Re-evaluation resets another evaluator's score; it must be limited to forms the requester can see.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; inside evaluation time; the caller can see some forms.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/request_tr_reevaluation` with body `{"form_uuids": ["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="], "remarks": "QA_Platform_reeval_{{stamp}}"}`. 1. PATCH request_tr_reevaluation with form_uuids = [Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==].
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 786 'Select correct line items for reevaluation' — (form_ids & allowed ids) != form_ids (app/controllers/api/v1/trade_controller.rb:1364-1366).

cases.title: Re-evaluation of an item whose TR is not submitted is refused
cases.why: 'Only TR-submitted items' rule: you cannot send back something that was never handed in.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; inside evaluation time; the form's evaluation is still DRAFT (evaluator has not submitted TR); form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/request_tr_reevaluation` with body `{"form_uuids": ["{{evalFormUuid}}"], "remarks": "QA_Platform_reeval_{{stamp}}"}`. 1. PATCH request_tr_reevaluation for that form.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 786 — get_item_status returns reevaluation_disabled_reason 'TR is Pending' for evaluation_status draft (app/controllers/concerns/trade_controller_helper.rb:5680-5691), refused at app/controllers/api/v1/trade_controller.rb:1379-1381.

cases.title: Only the asked evaluator can accept a re-evaluation
cases.why: Only the evaluator who owns the score can agree to re-open it.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; inside evaluation time; a pending re-evaluation is addressed to evaluator B; caller is buyer A.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/resolve_tr_reevaluation_request/{{evalFormUuid}}` with body `{"request_action": "accept", "remarks": "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}"}`. 1. As A, PATCH resolve with request_action accept.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 101 — return 101 if user.id != additional_request.requested_from_id (app/helpers/additional_request_resolution_helper.rb:1160).
cases.oracle: 422 + code 101; score status unchanged.

cases.title: A client cannot regenerate master QCS
cases.why: Regeneration re-runs PrecomputationEngine over every bid; a client must not be able to trigger it.
cases.setup: Caller is an ordinary client buyer (not a Procol employee on the ALLOWED_USER_IDS_TO_REGENERATE_MASTER_QCS list).
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/regenerate_master_qcs` with body `{"event_group_uuids": ["{{eventGroupUuid}}"]}`. 1. POST /event_groups/regenerate_master_qcs with event_group_uuids [{{eventGroupUuid}}].
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action' — EventGroupPolicy#regenerate_master_qcs? requires is_procol_employee? and the allow-list (app/policies/event_group_policy.rb:92-97), rescued by app/controllers/concerns/api_auth.rb:16,117-118.

cases.title: A vendor cannot read the award proposal
cases.why: The proposal carries every vendor's allocation and price — the QCS in award form.
cases.setup: {{proposalUuid}} is the sandbox award proposal; caller is the vendor.
cases.steps: `GET /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}`. 1. GET /proposal/{{proposalUuid}} as the vendor.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 455 — ProposalPolicy#show? → add_response? requires record.company_id in Company.allowed_companies(user) (app/policies/proposal_policy.rb:10-23).

cases.section: Counter offers — raise, bulk, revoke, vendor response
cases.title: A counter offer on a non-existent bid does not crash
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING: a well-formed but unknown id crashes the before_action; the nil guard is on the wrong side of the dereference.
cases.setup: Authenticated buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /additional_request/raise_additional_request` with body `{"item_uuid": "Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==", "item_type": "counter_offer_for_bid", "sheets": {"inline_components": {"data": [{"status": {"value": "active", "key": "status"}, "creator_quantity": {"value": "10", "configuration": {"unit_type": "KG", "suffix": "KG"}, "key": "creator_quantity"}, "participant_quantity": {"value": "10", "configuration": {"unit_type": "KG", "suffix": "KG"}, "key": "participant_quantity"}, "price": {"value": 90, "key": "price"}, "product": {"value": "product", "uuid": "{{productUuid}}", "unit_type": "KG", "event_group_line_item_uuid": "{{lineItemUuid}}", "key": "product"}, "variant": {"uuid": "{{productQualityUuid}}", "key": "variant"}}]}}, "remarks": "QA_Platform_co_{{stamp}}"}`. 1. POST raise_additional_request with item_uuid Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw== (well-formed, id 999999999, no such bid).
cases.expected: Must be 422 code 4. Today transform_product does Bid.find_by_id(bid_id).trade_request on nil (app/controllers/concerns/trade_template_helper.rb:5550) → NoMethodError → 500; create_additional_request_for_bid would also call nil.status (app/helpers/api/additional_requests_helper.rb:157-158).
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Counter offers — raise, bulk, revoke, vendor response
cases.title: A second counter offer while one is pending is refused
cases.why: Two open counter offers on one bid would race on accept.
cases.setup: {{bidUuid}} already has a pending counter offer (bid status requested).

cases.title: Submitting an award twice is refused
cases.why: Double submit must not start a second approval; the code is 2, which clients must not show as 'fill all fields'.
cases.setup: {{proposalUuid}} was already submitted (status requested or selected).
cases.steps: `POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/submit` with body `{"attachments": [], "remarks": "QA_Platform_award_{{stamp}}", "step_uuid_vs_user_uuid": {}}`. 1. POST submit again.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 'Insufficient parameters' — the lookup requires status: :draft (app/controllers/api/proposal_controller.rb:82-83), so the second submit reads as a missing proposal, not 573 'already submitted'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2; one approval_requests row.

cases.title: Submitting after un-awarding everyone is refused
cases.why: responses_hash is present but its data is empty — the SECOND of the two 683 guards.
cases.setup: {{proposalUuid}} had one allocation which was then removed via add_response action remove.
cases.steps: `POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/submit` with body `{"attachments": [], "remarks": "QA_Platform_award_{{stamp}}", "step_uuid_vs_user_uuid": {}}`. 1. POST submit.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 683 'Proposal cannot be empty. Please award the vendors again.' — responses_hash['data'] is {} (app/controllers/api/proposal_controller.rb:84-86). The proposal stays draft; no approval_requests row.

cases.title: Submitting without approver overrides does not crash
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING: an optional field is mandatory by crash; every API client must send {}.
cases.setup: {{proposalUuid}} is a populated draft.
cases.steps: `POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/submit` with body `{"attachments": [], "remarks": "QA_Platform_award_{{stamp}}"}`. 1. POST submit without step_uuid_vs_user_uuid.
cases.expected: Must be 200/422. Today params[:step_uuid_vs_user_uuid].to_enum.to_h on nil (app/controllers/api/proposal_controller.rb:93) raises NoMethodError → 500 before authorize.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: Submitting without a flow when approval is configured is refused
cases.why: Skipping approval by omitting the flow; without 570 close_bids would award immediately.
cases.setup: destructive — acts on the sandbox copy only and must run last: if the company has NO award approval configured, this body awards the proposal for real via close_bids. {{proposalUuid}} is a populated draft on the sandbox copy; the company HAS an award (close_event_group) approval configured.
cases.steps: `POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/submit` with body `{"attachments": [], "remarks": "QA_Platform_award_{{stamp}}", "step_uuid_vs_user_uuid": {}}`. 1. POST submit with no approval_flow_uuid.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 570 'Approval Flow not found' — check_proposal_approval returns 570 when is_approval_exists?(close_event_group) and no flow was sent (app/helpers/api/proposal_approval_helper.rb:40). The proposal stays draft; no approval_requests row.

cases.title: A malformed approval flow id is treated as no flow
cases.why: A garbage flow id is treated as absence, not as an error — safe only while an approval exists.
cases.setup: destructive — acts on the sandbox copy only and must run last: if the company has NO award approval configured, this body awards the proposal for real via close_bids. {{proposalUuid}} is a populated draft on the sandbox copy; the company HAS an award approval.
cases.steps: `POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/submit` with body `{"attachments": [], "remarks": "QA_Platform_award_{{stamp}}", "step_uuid_vs_user_uuid": {}, "approval_flow_uuid": "WrongUuid1="}`. 1. POST submit with approval_flow_uuid 'WrongUuid1='.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 570 — the uuid decodes to approval_flow_id nil, identical to 'no flow' (app/helpers/api/proposal_approval_helper.rb:11,40). If the company had NO approval configured the same body awards straight away via close_bids.

cases.title: A second buyer's submit after a colleague's does not crash
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING: every other error in submit_proposal is a Hash; this one is an Integer, so the one race the guard exists for crashes.
cases.setup: Two buyers each opened a draft on the same event; buyer B submitted first (B's proposal requested). Caller is buyer A with a populated draft {{proposalUuid}}.
cases.steps: `POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/submit` with body `{"attachments": [], "remarks": "QA_Platform_award_{{stamp}}", "step_uuid_vs_user_uuid": {}}`. 1. As A, POST submit.
cases.expected: Must be 422 code 573 'The proposal has already been submitted'. Today submit_proposal does `return proposal, 573` (a bare Integer, app/helpers/api/proposal_helper.rb:128) and the controller reads error[:code] (app/controllers/api/proposal_controller.rb:98) → 573[:code] → TypeError → 500.
cases.oracle: Status < 500 and A's proposal stays draft.

cases.title: Submitting an award on a revised bid is refused
cases.why: Awarding a stale price.
cases.setup: {{proposalUuid}} awards a bid that the vendor has since revised (old bid status revised).
cases.steps: `POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/submit` with body `{"attachments": [], "remarks": "QA_Platform_award_{{stamp}}", "step_uuid_vs_user_uuid": {}}`. 1. POST submit.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 1126 'A few bids have been revised. Please re-award to continue.' (app/helpers/api/proposal_helper.rb:241-250). The proposal stays draft; no approval_requests row.

cases.section: Letter of Award preview and PO preconditions
cases.title: PO forms need every line awarded when partial line awarding is disallowed
cases.why: CONFIG-dependent PO precondition.
cases.setup: Config: disallow_partial_line_item_awarding on; the event has 2 lines and {{proposalUuid}} awards 1.
cases.steps: `POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/create_po_form`. 1. POST create_po_form.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 791 'Please ensure all line items are awarded before continuing.' (app/helpers/api/proposal_helper.rb:219-231).

cases.title: Awarding is blocked while the caller holds a draft proposal
cases.why: The gate is per-user for drafts, which is subtly different from the selected/requested rule.
cases.setup: The same buyer with a draft proposal.
cases.steps: `POST /proposal` again.
cases.expected: Refused, or `should_allow_awarding` already false.
cases.oracle: Proposal count unchanged. ≈ BE-6.3.

cases.title: Discarding a draft proposal re-enables awarding
cases.why: It is the escape hatch from API-AWD-006 and it must actually clear the flag.
cases.steps: Discard the draft. Re-read the event group.
cases.expected: `should_allow_awarding` is true again.
cases.oracle: The flag flips back; a new proposal can be created. ≈ BE-6.6.

cases.title: A Procol employee passes the proposal policy unconditionally
cases.why: A deliberate support back door; it must work for them and for nobody else.
cases.setup: A Procol employee.
cases.steps: `GET /proposal/:id`.
cases.expected: Allowed.
cases.oracle: Readable; then confirm a non-employee outside the company is refused.

cases.title: Awarding a zero or negative quantity is refused
cases.why: PRD §5's positive-quantity rule, at the last step where it matters.
cases.steps: `add_response` with `0`, then `-10`.
cases.expected: Refused both times.
cases.oracle: No allocation created.

cases.title: Closing the bid to select a winner is refused outside the window
cases.why: Code 9, "Unable to close the order at this time. Please wait for the bidding to end."
cases.setup: A live event inside its window.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/:id/close_bid`.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No winner selected. ≈ BE-6.7.

cases.title: The awarding sheet downloads for a valid uuid and is refused for an invalid one
cases.why: It is a data-export endpoint; a permissive one leaks a whole event's commercials.
cases.steps: `GET /reports/download_awarding_sheet/:uuid` with a valid uuid, then a fabricated one, then another company's.
cases.expected: The first succeeds; the others are refused.
cases.oracle: No file content in the refused cases. ≈ BE-6.8.

cases.title: A rejected proposal returns the event to awardable
cases.why: Otherwise a rejection deadlocks the event and there is no route out.
cases.setup: A submitted proposal.
cases.steps: Reject it through the approval workflow. Re-read the event group.
cases.expected: `should_allow_awarding` is true; a new proposal can be created.
cases.oracle: The flag and a successful new proposal.

cases.section: Read the approval workflow for the award — `GET /proposal/:id/approval_workflows`
cases.title: (retired) Each approval flow's "stop expiry during approval" setting is returned
cases.why: Retired: the app does not promise this setting on every approval flow. A flow without it is treated as "off", and only some ways of creating a flow write it — Demo Account 2 has such a flow, so the check failed there on every run while PROCOL DEMO passed. Where the setting is present, API-FAWDFLOW-060 still checks that it is a yes/no value.
cases.setup: A buyer walking the API journey (RFQ only, Technical + RFQ, Technical + Auction), at the step "Read the approval workflow for the award".
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, do “Read the approval workflow for the award” in the API journey (`GET /proposal/:id/approval_workflows`). 2. Look at each approval flow's "stop expiry during approval" setting in the app's response.
cases.expected: Not checked any more: a flow may leave the setting out, and that means "off".
cases.oracle: Retired 2026-10-03 — `exists [*].config.stop_expiry_in_approval` was learned from 15 PROCOL DEMO responses only; procol-backend reads the key with `dig` and a missing key as false (approval_request.rb:155, approval_step_helper.rb:6, approval_request_view.rb:820), and only tr_matrix/approval_creation_service.rb:79 and the bulk-upload params write it.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: Scoring without naming the vendor is refused
cases.why: company_id is the first of the three ANDed conditions in valid_params?; without it the score has no vendor to attach to.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; caller is an assigned evaluator.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "score": 3, "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. Log in as the evaluator. 2. POST /evaluations with the journey body minus company_uuid. 3. Assert 422 code 2 and no row.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' — Evaluations::ValidateService#valid_params? requires @options[:company_id].present? (app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:44). No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2; GET schema afterwards shows no score for the vendor.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: A form id sent as text is refused
cases.why: Only form.uuid is decoded to an Integer; a raw form.id must be a JSON integer. The Integer check is what stops '10abc'-style coercion matching an allowed id.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"id": "10", "score": 3, "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. POST /evaluations with form.id sent as the string "10" (no uuid).
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 — form[:id].instance_of?(Integer) is false for a string (app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:62); ParamsAuth only decodes keys containing 'uuid', so 'id' is passed through untouched. No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: A fractional score is refused
cases.why: Scores are discrete label keys; a half-score would not map to any label (TNA/T1/T2…) and would break display_value_for_evaluation_score.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "score": 3.5, "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. POST /evaluations with form.score = 3.5.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 — 3.5 is a Float, not Integer (app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:65), and not a label key (app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:66). No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: A negative score is refused
cases.why: A negative score would pull a weighted QCS total below zero.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "score": -1, "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. POST /evaluations with form.score = -1.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 — -1 is not a label key (app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:66). No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: A TNA score with a reason is accepted
cases.why: Pairs with the two refusals above: the rule is 'zero needs a reason', not 'zero is forbidden'.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator; 0 is a key of the event's evaluation_score_label_mapping (TNA in both defaults).
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "score": 0, "remark": "QA_Platform_TNA_reason_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. POST /evaluations with form.score = 0 and a real remark.
cases.expected: 200 success:true — 0 is a label key and the remark is present, so valid_form? passes; a draft evaluation_score of 0 with a Remark row is written. (app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:67-69, app/helpers/api/evaluations_helper.rb:1099)
cases.oracle: success:true and the vendor shows TNA on the evaluator's form.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: The highest label score is accepted, and may mean Regret
cases.why: The top of the range is a boundary AND, depending on which mapping the RFP carries, a disqualification — the same number means T1 in the company default and Regret in the per-RFP default.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; 5 is a key of the event's evaluation_score_label_mapping; form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "score": 5, "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. POST /evaluations with form.score = 5 (highest default label key).
cases.expected: 200 success:true — 5 is a key of both default mappings (app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:66). NOTE the per-RFP mapping from the 2025-02 migration makes 5 = 'Regret', which BLOCKS awarding when restrict_awarding_for_tna_vendors is on (app/helpers/api/proposal_helper.rb:1271-1280). If the event's mapping tops out below 5 this becomes code 2.
cases.oracle: success:true; then check which label the vendor now shows.

cases.section: Scoring — every way POST /evaluations answers 'Insufficient parameters'
cases.title: A numeric remark does not crash scoring
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING: the remark is never type-checked; only strings have html_safe.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator.

cases.expected: Must be a 422, not a 500. Today valid_form? passes (remark is only checked for score 0) and find_or_create_remark calls message.html_safe on an Integer (app/helpers/api/evaluations_helper.rb:1120), which raises NoMethodError → 500.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; no half-saved evaluation row with a nil remark.

POST /evaluations with trade_request_uuid = the RFQ stage ({{tradeId}}) instead of {{rfpTradeId}}.

cases.section: Scoring — wrong state, wrong actor, wrong time
cases.title: Scoring a vendor who never responded is refused
cases.why: Scoring a non-respondent invents a qualification for a vendor who never qualified; code 101, not 2, is the tell that the params were fine.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; {{vendorUuid}} was invited but never submitted a technical response (or it was deleted).
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "score": 3, "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. POST /evaluations for that vendor with the evaluator's assigned form.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action' — allowed_to_evaluate_participant? requires trade_request.template_responses.active.exists?(company_id:) (app/services/evaluations/validate_service.rb:79). No evaluations / evaluation_scores row is written.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 101 (not 2 — the params were valid).

cases.section: Scoring — wrong state, wrong actor, wrong time
cases.title: A double-clicked score is saved once
cases.why: Without the lock two draft Evaluation rows are created for the same vendor (the find-or-new at app/helpers/api/evaluations_helper.rb:25-36 is not atomic).
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time has passed; form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "score": 3, "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. Fire two identical POST /evaluations within 3 seconds.
cases.expected: The second returns HTTP 422 code 516 'Transaction in Progress' — lock_evaluation_create keys on trade/company/form/user for 3s (app/controllers/api/evaluations_controller.rb:126-132). Exactly one evaluation_score row.
cases.oracle: One 200, one 516; one evaluation_scores row.

cases.section: Scoring — wrong state, wrong actor, wrong time
cases.title: Scoring after the evaluation window closes is not time-guarded
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING: re-evaluation is explicitly limited to in_evaluation_time? (app/controllers/api/v1/trade_controller.rb:1352) but first-time scoring is not, so a late score changes QCS after the window everyone relied on.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; now is AFTER extra_closing_time (the evaluation window has ended) but the stage is still status active.
cases.steps: `POST /evaluations` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}", "company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "form": {"uuid": "{{evalFormUuid}}", "score": 3, "remark": "QA_Platform_eval_{{stamp}}"}}`. 1. POST /evaluations with a valid body.
cases.expected: Today the create action only checks the LOWER bound (bid_end_time > now → 33, app/controllers/api/evaluations_controller.rb:25); nothing refuses a score after extra_closing_time. Expected per product rules: refused. Must never 5xx.
cases.oracle: Record the status; if 200, the score changed after the window closed.

cases.title: The evaluator schema for a non-existent round is refused
cases.why: The evaluator's first call; a nil trade must be a clean 4, not a nil dereference in the Dynamo logging that follows.
cases.setup: Caller is the evaluator.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/schema?response_type=template&additional_fields=order_details`. 1. GET /v1/trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/schema (decodes to id 999999999).
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 4 'Request not found' — validate_event returns 4 when trade is nil (app/controllers/concerns/trade_controller_helper.rb:2215), called from app/controllers/api/v1/trade_controller.rb:276-277.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 4.

cases.title: A double-submitted evaluation creates one proposal
cases.why: find_or_initialize_draft_proposal is not atomic; the 3s cache lock is the only guard against two proposals.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; bid_end_time passed; every vendor scored.
cases.steps: `PATCH /evaluations/submit` with body `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}"}`. 1. Fire two PATCH /evaluations/submit within 3s.
cases.expected: Second call → HTTP 422 code 516 (app/controllers/api/evaluations_controller.rb:113-119). One draft technical proposal.
cases.oracle: One success, one 516.

cases.title: Requesting re-evaluation without naming forms does not crash
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING: the only params guard is id.blank? (app/controllers/api/v1/trade_controller.rb:1349); form_ids is never presence-checked.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; inside evaluation time; line-item (not lot) evaluation.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/request_tr_reevaluation` with body `{"remarks": "QA_Platform_reeval_{{stamp}}"}`. 1. PATCH request_tr_reevaluation with remarks only.
cases.expected: Must be 422 code 2/786. Today form_ids is nil and `(form_ids & form_objects.pluck(:id))` raises NoMethodError (app/controllers/api/v1/trade_controller.rb:1364) → 500.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; no AdditionalRequest.

cases.title: Re-evaluation cannot be requested twice for the same item
cases.why: Two pending requests on one score would each flip it back to draft on accept.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; inside evaluation time; a re-evaluation for this form is already pending; form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/request_tr_reevaluation` with body `{"form_uuids": ["{{evalFormUuid}}"], "remarks": "QA_Platform_reeval_{{stamp}}"}`. 1. PATCH request_tr_reevaluation for the same form again.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 786 ('Reevaluation is already requested', app/controllers/concerns/trade_controller_helper.rb:5688-5689) or, if the status check is bypassed, 787 'Reevaluation already Requested' (app/helpers/api/additional_requests_helper.rb:555).
cases.oracle: 422 with 786/787; still exactly one requested AdditionalRequest.

cases.title: Re-evaluation without a reason is not refused by the backend
cases.why: 'Reason required' is enforced client-side only — an API caller can send an evaluator's score back with no justification.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; inside evaluation time; TR submitted for the form; form.uuid is {{evalFormUuid}}, the form assigned to the evaluator.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/request_tr_reevaluation` with body `{"form_uuids": ["{{evalFormUuid}}"]}`. 1. PATCH request_tr_reevaluation with no remarks.
cases.expected: Per product rules the reason is mandatory; the backend stores request_remark: remarks || '' (app/helpers/api/additional_requests_helper.rb:574) and accepts it. Record: 200 means the rule lives only in the UI. Never 5xx.
cases.oracle: If 200, the AdditionalRequest has request_remark ''.

cases.title: An unknown re-evaluation decision is refused
cases.why: Invalid enum on the call that either resets or keeps a score.
cases.setup: {{rfpTradeId}} is the TECHNICAL (RFP) stage of the sandbox event; inside evaluation time; a pending re-evaluation exists; caller is the requested evaluator.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/resolve_tr_reevaluation_request/{{evalFormUuid}}` with body `{"request_action": "approve", "remarks": "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}"}`. 1. PATCH resolve_tr_reevaluation_request with request_action = "approve".
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 — return 2 if !action.in?(['accept','reject']) (app/helpers/additional_request_resolution_helper.rb:1146).
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2; request still requested.

cases.title: Resolving a re-evaluation that is not pending is refused

cases.oracle: 422 + code 4.

cases.title: Only the requester can withdraw a re-evaluation
cases.why: Revoking a re-evaluation restores the old score; only its requester or the owner may do it.
cases.setup: A re-evaluation request exists, raised by buyer A; caller is buyer B (not requester, not super admin, not event owner). The request id is supplied by the runner.
cases.steps: `PATCH /additional_request/revoke_additional_requests` with body `{"item_type": "reevaluation", "requests": [{"id": "Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==", "status": "revoke"}]}`. 1. PATCH /additional_request/revoke_additional_requests with item_type reevaluation.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 5 'Not authorized' when the id is real (app/controllers/api/additional_requests_controller.rb:199-203); code 4 for the ghost id (app/controllers/api/additional_requests_controller.rb:182-185).
cases.oracle: 422 with 5 (real id) or 4 (ghost).

cases.section: Counter offers — raise, bulk, revoke, vendor response

POST raise_additional_request without item_type.

POST raise_additional_request with item_type = "QA_Platform_bogus".

Score once with a breakdown {"technical": {"q1": 3}}. 2. Re-score the same form without the breakdown key.

journeys.title: Converting an RFQ to an auction
journeys.goal: Turn a published RFQ into an auction, carrying its quotes over as starting bids.

cases.title: The converted auction publishes with the RFQ's data
cases.why: The whole point: carry the RFQ's quotes and participants into an auction without re-entering anything.
cases.steps: On the conversion screen, invite vendors and publish.
cases.expected: An auction event linked to the RFQ, with the same line items.
cases.oracle: Redirect to a project id; no error toast; line items match the RFQ's.

cases.title: Convert to Auction is offered on a published RFQ
cases.why: The entry point is behind the event Settings menu and is gated three ways: published (not draft), vendor masking off, and the tenant allowing it.
cases.setup: A published RFQ; vendor masking off.
cases.steps: Open the event → Settings (`event-settings-button`) → read the menu.
cases.expected: "Convert to Auction" is listed.
cases.oracle: The item exists. If Settings opens and simply does not list it, report that the feature is gated off on this tenant — not that the automation is wrong.

cases.title: Conversion opens a prefilled create screen in a new tab
cases.why: It `window.open`s with `isRfqToAuction=true&draftStageIds=…`; a test driving the original tab watches a page that never changes.
cases.steps: Settings → Convert to Auction → Continue.
cases.expected: A new tab on the create screen with the conversion query params, the RFQ's template and sheet already in place.
cases.oracle: Handle the new page object; assert `isRfqToAuction=true` in its URL.

cases.title: The template picker is locked during conversion
cases.why: Changing the schema would invalidate the carried-over quotes.
cases.setup: A conversion screen.
cases.steps: Try to open the template dropdown.
cases.expected: Disabled.
cases.oracle: Dropdown disabled.

cases.title: "All invited" carries every RFQ participant, not just the bidders
cases.why: The toggle switches the audience source, and the difference decides who can bid in the auction.
cases.setup: An RFQ where 2 of 5 invited vendors bid.
cases.steps: Convert with the toggle off, then (on a second conversion) with it on.
cases.expected: Off: only the 2 bidders carry forward as bidding participants. On: all 5 carry, with the bidders flagged.
cases.oracle: Participant counts 2 and 5 respectively; the bid-placed flag set on the right ones.

cases.title: Converting the same RFQ twice is refused
cases.why: The model enforces at most one non-cancelled auction per parent RFQ, so the second attempt must be refused rather than creating an orphan.
cases.setup: An already-converted RFQ.
cases.steps: Try to convert again.
cases.expected: Refused ("An auction has already been made for this trade.").
cases.oracle: Message shown; still exactly one auction child.

cases.title: The RFQ becomes uneditable once its auction exists
cases.why: The backend refuses RFQ edits after conversion ("You cannot edit rfq once the auction is created.", 769) and the UI must not offer them.
cases.setup: A converted RFQ.
cases.steps: Try to edit the RFQ's sheet or schedule.
cases.expected: Refused or unavailable.
cases.oracle: No successful edit; a readable refusal if attempted.

cases.title: Convert to Auction is hidden when vendor masking is on
cases.why: Masking and conversion are incompatible, and the control's visibility is the whole enforcement.
cases.setup: gate: `isVendorMaskingEnabled`. A published RFQ.
cases.steps: Open Settings.
cases.expected: No Convert to Auction item, regardless of the RFQ's state.
cases.oracle: Item absent.

cases.title: Vendors carried into the auction can bid immediately
cases.why: The conversion is only useful if the carried audience can act, and audience-carry bugs show up here first.
cases.setup: A converted auction, live.
cases.steps: As a carried-over vendor, open the auction and bid.
cases.expected: The bid is accepted.
cases.oracle: Bid submitted; visible to the buyer on the auction.

cases.title: The RFQ's bids remain visible after conversion
cases.why: The RFQ's history is the baseline the auction's savings are measured against.
cases.setup: A converted RFQ that had bids.
cases.steps: Open the RFQ stage on the project.
cases.expected: Its bids are still there, read-only.
cases.oracle: Bid count on the RFQ unchanged after conversion.

cases.title: TNA vendors are included or excluded per the flag
cases.why: gate: `allowTnaVendorsToBid`. Getting it wrong either bars legitimate bidders or admits ones who should not bid.
cases.setup: An RFQ audience containing TNA vendors.
cases.steps: Convert with the flag off, then on.
cases.expected: Excluded when off, included when on.
cases.oracle: The TNA vendor's presence in the bidding audience flips with the flag.

cases.title: Conversion on a draft RFQ is not offered
cases.why: There are no quotes to carry from a draft, so the control must not appear.
cases.setup: A draft RFQ.
cases.steps: Open Settings.
cases.expected: Not offered.
cases.oracle: Item absent.

cases.title: Conversion is refused on a superseded event version
cases.why: Same staleness problem as UI-PUB-011, on a path that creates a new trade record.
cases.setup: An RFQ whose event group has a newer version.
cases.steps: Attempt the conversion.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No auction created.

cases.title: Fast bidding needs more than one line item
cases.why: The backend refuses with a specific message ("CBD mode requires at least two active line items."), which is only meaningful if the UI surfaces it.
cases.setup: gate: fast bidding. A single-line-item RFQ.
cases.steps: Convert with fast bidding on.
cases.expected: Refused with that message.
cases.oracle: Message shown; no auction created.

cases.title: An active RFQ converts to an auction
cases.why: The happy path, and it is the only way to reach knockout and dutch strategies at all.
cases.setup: A published RFQ with bids.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/move_to_auction` with the RFQ's trade id and an auction config.
cases.expected: 200; a new auction trade as a child of the RFQ.
cases.oracle: The new trade's `parent_id` is the RFQ's id. ≈ BE-7.1.

cases.title: Converting the same RFQ twice is refused
cases.why: Code 94. The model enforces at most one non-cancelled auction per `(parent_id, event_group_id)`, and a second one would split the event's bids.
cases.steps: Convert, then convert again.
cases.oracle: Still exactly one auction child. ≈ BE-7.2.

cases.title: Converting a non-existent trade is refused
cases.why: Code 95 — the first guard, and it must not be a nil dereference.
cases.steps: `PATCH` with a fabricated trade id.
cases.oracle: That code. ≈ BE-7.3.

cases.title: A caller from neither the owning nor the broker company is refused
cases.why: The company check is separate from the policy check, and brokers are a legitimate third party — so the rule is narrower than "same company".
cases.setup: A caller from an unrelated company with create permission.
cases.steps: `PATCH move_to_auction`.
cases.expected: Refused (101).
cases.oracle: No auction created. ≈ BE-7.6.

cases.title: Conversion requires both create permission and view access
cases.why: `move_to_auction?` is `create? && allowed_to_view_event?` — two independent gates, and passing one is not enough.
cases.setup: A user with create permission but no view access to this event, and the reverse.
cases.steps: `PATCH move_to_auction` as each.
cases.expected: Both refused.
cases.oracle: No auction created in either case.

cases.title: A line-item to lot closing-mode switch on a multi-product trade is refused
cases.why: Code 503, "You cannot award entire lot when RFQ was done for partial lot." — a genuine commercial constraint, not a technical one.
cases.setup: A multi-product RFQ run as line-item.
cases.steps: `PATCH move_to_auction` with `auction_closing_mode: lot`.
cases.oracle: No auction created. ≈ BE-7.8.

cases.title: The RFQ becomes bid-restricted once its auction exists
cases.why: Code 769. It is the state change conversion makes to the *parent*, and it is easy to overlook because the new auction is what everyone looks at.
cases.steps: Convert, then attempt a bid on the RFQ.
cases.expected: Refused with 769.
cases.oracle: That specific code.

cases.title: The RFQ's bids survive the conversion
cases.why: They are the baseline the auction's savings are computed against; losing them changes every number afterwards.
cases.steps: Convert an RFQ that had two bids. Read the RFQ.
cases.expected: Both bids still present and readable.
cases.oracle: Bid count on the RFQ unchanged.

cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No auction created. ≈ BE-7.4.

cases.title: Converting an already-auctioning trade is refused

cases.steps: `PATCH move_to_auction` on an auction.
cases.oracle: That specific code, not 94. ≈ BE-7.5.

cases.title: Fast bidding requires more than one active or closed trade product
cases.why: Code 798 — "CBD mode requires at least two active line items."
cases.setup: A single-product RFQ.
cases.steps: `PATCH move_to_auction` with fast bidding enabled.
cases.oracle: No auction created. ≈ BE-7.7.

cases.steps: `PATCH move_to_auction`.
cases.expected: Refused with the price-validation error.
cases.oracle: No auction created.
