cases.section: A Full Tour of the Purchase Requisitions Page
cases.title: "Group On" groups PR line items by PR Number
cases.why: Grouping lets a buyer see every line of one requisition together instead of a flat list of line items.
cases.setup: Buyer on the PR page with line items from more than one PR.
cases.steps: 1. Open the PR page (all PR line items are listed). 2. Click the "Group On" button.
cases.expected: The PR page is organised with line items grouped by their PR Number.
cases.oracle: Line items appear under PR Number groups rather than as one flat list.

cases.section: A Full Tour of the Purchase Requisitions Page
cases.title: Columns window: Hide All / Show all, and column visibility persists
cases.why: Column visibility is a per-user setting that the article says persists across the platform until changed.
cases.setup: Buyer on the PR page.
cases.steps: 1. Click the "👁️ Columns (N/N)" button. 2. Use "Hide All", then "Show all"; then hide one or more columns. 3. Switch to another page or module and return to the PR page.
cases.expected: The window lists all columns of the PR line item table; Hide All / Show all hide and restore columns; the chosen visibility persists after navigation.
cases.oracle: The table shows only the columns left visible, and the button count reflects them after returning.

cases.section: How do I assign PRs to my Team?
cases.title: Assignee dropdown is scrollable and searchable in both individual and bulk flows
cases.why: In organisations with many users, finding the assignee depends on the dropdown's search.
cases.setup: Purchase manager on the PR page.
cases.steps: 1. Open "Add Assignee" from a single line item's "+" icon; scroll the dropdown and type a user's name in the search bar. 2. Repeat from the bulk "Add Assignee" button with several items selected.
cases.expected: In both flows a scrollable dropdown opens and typing in the search bar finds the user.
cases.oracle: The dropdown narrows to the matching user in both the individual and the bulk flow.

cases.section: How do I start processing my PRs
cases.title: Purchase Items and Create Project buttons show the number of selected items
cases.why: The count is the buyer's confirmation of what is going into the project.
cases.setup: Buyer on the PR page.
cases.steps: 1. Select three PR line items. 2. Read the "🛒 Purchase Items" button. 3. Click it and read the "Create Project" button in the side panel.
cases.expected: Both buttons show the number of items selected.
cases.oracle: Both buttons display 3.

cases.section: How to Create Budgets and Manage Budgets
cases.title: "Show More" reveals additional customizable budget fields
cases.why: Client-specific budget fields are hidden behind Show More; they must be reachable.
cases.setup: Budget owner on the Budget Creation page.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Show More".
cases.expected: Additional customizable fields that were hidden are revealed.
cases.oracle: More fields are visible after the click than before.

cases.title: "Show More" reveals additional customizable contract fields
cases.why: Client-specific contract fields sit behind Show More.
cases.setup: User on the Contract creation page.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Show More".
cases.expected: Additional customizable fields are revealed.
cases.oracle: More fields are visible after the click than before.

cases.title: Configurable PR Dashboard: saved view persists per user
cases.why: The workbook records this edge case for Configurable PR Dashboard: "Saved view persists per user".
cases.setup: Persona: Buyer. Plan: tenant on Growth (lowest plan with access; Plan Required: Growth, Enterprise). Status: GA.
cases.steps: 1. Sign in as a Buyer on the tenant described in Setup. 2. Set up the situation the note describes: "Saved view persists per user". 3. Use Configurable PR Dashboard to arrange, freeze, hide, filter, and save their PR dashboard view. 4. Observe how the feature handles the situation from step 2.
cases.expected: Configurable PR Dashboard behaves as the workbook states: "Saved view persists per user".
cases.oracle: The observed outcome for the situation in step 2 matches the note; if Procol behaves differently, raise it against FEAT-PR-002 quoting the note.

journeys.title: Sourcing events as the product defines them
journeys.goal: Run a multi-stage sourcing project — technical evaluation, commercial RFQ with counter offers, comparison on Master QCS, and award.

cases.section: How to create a Single Stage Event (RFP, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Create and publish a Single Stage RFQ event end to end
cases.why: Single-stage create → publish is the entry point of the core sourcing path; if it breaks no vendor can bid.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager; at least one product in the catalogue with mapped vendors; a predefined template available.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the **Events** page from the left navigation panel. 2. Click the "+ New Event" button. 3. In the panel that opens, choose "Single Stage". 4. Click the **Rank on Line** badge and choose **RFQ (Request for Quotation)** in the side drawer; set the Awarding Type (Lot or Line). 5. Click Select Template and choose a predefined template. 6. Add products by clicking the cell beneath the "Products" column and selecting from the dropdown. 7. Fill in all mandatory fields in the template table. 8. Click the blue "Invite Vendors" in the green tip to add the suggested vendors as participants. 9. Click the blue "Publish Event" button, review the event details in the pop-up and click the blue "Publish" button.
cases.expected: The event is published and is now Live; an email notification is sent to all added participants inviting them to participate.
cases.oracle: "You Have Successfully Published your Event" confirmation; the event shows as live on the Events page; each invited participant receives the invitation email.

cases.section: How to create a Sourcing Project (Technical Stage, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Create and publish an eRFX Project with a Technical Stage and an RFQ
cases.why: The multi-stage project is the main create → publish path for technical + commercial sourcing.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager; products in the catalogue with mapped vendors; RFQ and RFP templates available; a user who can be assigned as technical evaluator.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the **Events** page and click "+ New Event". 2. In the panel that opens, choose "eRFX Project". 3. In the side drawer, search and add Line Items via the search bar on top. 4. Click the blue "Create Project" button on the bottom right. 5. Select the Technical Stage and RFQ events and click "Create Project" again. 6. On the RFQ, click Select Template, choose a predefined template, and fill mandatory fields like Delivery Location. 7. Click on Technical Stage, click Select Template to apply an RFP template to all line items via Bulk Action. 8. Under the "Vendor Assessment" section click select template; click "+ Add Evaluator" under each line item and search the user to assign. 9. Scroll to the bottom of the RFQ page and click the blue "Invite Vendors" in the green tip. 10. Click the blue "Publish Event" button at the top right, review the pop-up and click the blue "Publish" button.
cases.expected: A Project is created with the selected stages (Technical Stage and RFQ); on publish, an email notification is sent to all added participants inviting them to the event that is now Live.
cases.oracle: Project creation screen shows both stages; "You Have Successfully Published your Event" confirmation; participants receive the invitation email.

cases.section: How to Edit Currencies in my Event
cases.title: Bids in another currency convert to the default currency in the QCS
cases.why: Award comparison depends on correct conversion; a wrong factor misranks vendors.
cases.setup: Published RFQ or Auction configured with Multi Currency and a conversion factor; a participating vendor.
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, place a bid in one of the added currencies. 2. As the buyer, open the RFQ/Auction QCS.
cases.expected: The bid is converted to the default currency using the defined conversion rate and populates the QCS.
cases.oracle: QCS value equals vendor bid × configured conversion factor, shown in the default currency.

cases.section: How to add Terms and Conditions for my Vendors in my Events?
cases.title: Mandatory T&Cs must be accepted by vendors before submitting bids
cases.why: Compliance gate: a vendor must not be able to bid without accepting mandatory terms.
cases.setup: Buyer publishes an event whose event-level T&Cs are marked mandatory; a participating vendor.
cases.steps: 1. As buyer, in 'Edit Terms and Conditions' mark all T&Cs as mandatory, click Done and publish. 2. As vendor, open the event and try to submit a bid without accepting the T&Cs. 3. Accept the T&Cs and submit the bid.
cases.expected: Vendors are required to accept the T&Cs before submitting bids.
cases.oracle: Bid submission is not possible until the T&Cs are accepted; after acceptance the bid submits.

cases.section: How to set up an RFQ (Request for Quotation)?
cases.title: Set up and publish an RFQ awarded at line-item level
cases.why: RFQ create → publish is the core entry to the bid → award path.
cases.setup: Buyer on the event setup screen (Event Type defaulting to Rank on Line); products with mapped vendors; a predefined template.
cases.steps: 1. Click the **Rank on Line** badge and choose **RFQ (Request for Quotation)** in the side drawer. 2. Under "Choose how you will award (to the vendors) in the event", select "I may partially award the event to multiple vendors". 3. Click Select Template and choose a predefined template. 4. Add products beneath the "Products" column and fill in all mandatory fields. 5. Click the blue "Invite Vendors" in the green tip (or add vendors via Participants). 6. Click the blue "Publish Event" button, review the pop-up and click the blue "Publish" button.
cases.expected: The RFQ runs at line item level; on publish an email notification is sent to all added participants inviting them to the event, which is now Live.
cases.oracle: "You Have Successfully Published your RFQ Event" confirmation; the event is live on the Events page; participants receive the invitation email.

cases.section: How do you run an RFQ Event?
cases.title: L1 (lowest) price is highlighted in green per line item; savings icon vs previous bid
cases.why: L1 highlighting drives the award decision; a wrong highlight points the buyer at the wrong vendor.
cases.setup: Buyer; a published RFQ with at least two vendors who have quoted, one of whom has revised a bid.
cases.steps: 1. On the RFQ Responses tab, scroll through the line items. 2. Compare the prices from different vendors. 3. Look at the percentage icon next to the revised bid.
cases.expected: The lowest price on each line item is automatically highlighted in green as **L1 (Lowest)**; the percentage icon shows the savings compared to that vendor's previous bid.
cases.oracle: The green-highlighted cell on each line item holds the minimum price; the percentage equals the change from the vendor's previous bid.

cases.section: How do you run an RFQ Event?
cases.title: Reject Quote removes the quote from the comparison view and the QCS
cases.why: A rejected quote must not be awarded or influence comparison.
cases.setup: Buyer; a published RFQ with vendor quotes.
cases.steps: 1. Click the **three-dot menu** next to a vendor's name in their quote. 2. Select **Reject Quote**, keeping the box checked so the seller is allowed to bid again.
cases.expected: The quote is removed from the comparison view and the Quote Comparison Sheet (QCS); the seller is allowed to bid again.
cases.oracle: The vendor's quote no longer appears in the comparison view or the QCS; the vendor can still submit a new bid.

cases.section: How do you run an RFQ Event?
cases.title: After evaluation, awarding starts from the MQCS tab
cases.why: Awarding is the end of the core path; the article routes it through the MQCS tab.
cases.setup: Buyer; an RFQ whose evaluation is complete and counter offers sent.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the **MQCS** tab of the RFQ. 2. Proceed with the awarding process.
cases.expected: The MQCS tab is available to award the RFQ once evaluation is complete.
cases.oracle: MQCS tab opens with the evaluated quotes for awarding (details are in the separate "Awarding Process" article).

cases.title: Unlock bids "For Myself" with a second-user OTP
cases.why: Compliance: bids must stay sealed until a two-person unlock completes.
cases.setup: Buyer on an event whose submission window has closed; a second pre-set user (typically another department) with registered email/SMS.
cases.steps: 1. Open the **"Responses"** tab of the event. 2. Click or hover the settings icon and select **"Unlock Bids"**. 3. In the dialog choose **For Myself**. 4. Choose the second user as OTP recipient and click **"Send OTP"**. 5. Obtain the OTP from that user, enter it and click **"Submit OTP"**.
cases.expected: The recipient receives the OTP via email/SMS; on successful verification the bids are unlocked and visible only to the initiating user.
cases.oracle: "The bids have been unlocked" confirmation; vendor responses are visible to the initiator and still hidden for other users with access.

cases.title: Unlock bids "For Everyone"
cases.why: Unlock scope decides who can see sealed bids.
cases.setup: Buyer on an event whose submission window has closed; a pre-set OTP recipient; a third user with access to the event.
cases.steps: 1. From the Responses tab, settings icon › **"Unlock Bids"**. 2. Choose **For Everyone**, select the OTP recipient and click **"Send OTP"**. 3. Enter the OTP and click **"Submit OTP"**.
cases.expected: Bids are unlocked for all users with access to the event.
cases.oracle: The third user can view the vendor responses after the unlock.

cases.title: Bids cannot be unlocked before the submission window closes
cases.why: Stated compliance restriction against premature access and collusion.
cases.setup: Buyer on a live event whose submission deadline has not passed.
cases.steps: 1. Open the Responses tab. 2. Attempt to start **"Unlock Bids"** from the settings icon.
cases.expected: Unlocking bids before the submission deadline is not permitted.
cases.oracle: The unlock does not proceed and bids remain hidden (the article does not name the message shown).

cases.title: Neither party can view bids independently before the OTP is submitted
cases.why: The two-person rule is the point of the feature; the initiator alone must not see bids.
cases.setup: Buyer (initiator) and a second pre-set user; an event whose submission window has closed.
cases.steps: 1. As initiator, start **"Unlock Bids"** and click **"Send OTP"** but do not submit the OTP. 2. Check whether bids are visible to the initiator. 3. Check whether bids are visible to the OTP recipient.
cases.expected: Bids stay restricted for both users until the OTP is verified.
cases.oracle: Vendor bid values are not visible to either user until "Submit OTP" succeeds.

cases.section: How do I use Request for Best Offer?
cases.title: Request Best Offer from all vendors during Evaluation
cases.why: Final price negotiation before award decisions.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager; an RFQ event in the **Evaluation** stage with vendor quotes.
cases.steps: 1. Open the event card from the **Events** tab and click **Settings** on the left panel. 2. Click "Request for Best Offer". 3. In the right-hand side panel, enter the duration for Best Offer submission. 4. Invite all vendors. 5. Click "Send Request".
cases.expected: Vendors receive system notifications and emails; the event is tagged **Best Offer Requested** and each vendor's bid card or row reflects this status; real-time updates appear as vendors submit new quotations.
cases.oracle: "Best Offer Requested" tag on the event and on each vendor row; vendors receive the email.

cases.section: How to Split Line Items into Lots in an RFQ Event
cases.title: Split line items into lots and publish, creating a Master QCS per lot
cases.why: Lots are evaluated, awarded and turned into POs independently; the QCS split is the award surface.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager; an RFQ event in the evaluation stage with several line items.
cases.steps: 1. Go to the RFQ Event, **Settings** tab, and select **Split Line Items into Lots**. 2. In the **Manage Lots** panel, use the dropdown next to line item serial numbers to move items into other lots. 3. Go to each lot header and click **Publish Lot**. 4. Click close in the bottom right.
cases.expected: Line items shift to the selected lots; after publishing, a separate **Master QCS** tab exists for each lot and the original unified Master QCS is no longer visible.
cases.oracle: One Master QCS tab per lot; no unified Master QCS tab; "You've successfully split your RFQ into Lots".

cases.section: How Vendors Review and Update Charges After Lot Splitting
cases.title: Vendor reviews lot adjustment and revises Other Charges
cases.why: Vendor charges must be re-quoted per lot or lot totals are wrong at award.
cases.setup: Vendor participating in an RFQ whose line items have been split into lots during evaluation.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the **Live Events** tab on the supplier dashboard. 2. Note the **"Bid Adjustment Pending"** tag above the event card and click into the specific **Lot RFQ**. 3. At the top banner (**Review Lot Adjustment and Update Charges**), click **View Item Distribution**. 4. Return, scroll to the bottom of the main table and update the **Other Charges** section. 5. Click **Revise Quote**.
cases.expected: The revised lot-specific quotation is submitted and the banner disappears.
cases.oracle: "You have successfully reviewed your bids after Lot Splitting"; banner gone; buyer sees the revised charges on the lot.

cases.section: How do I convert an RFQ to an Auction
cases.title: Convert a concluded RFQ to an auction using RFQ quotations as starting bids
cases.why: RFQ → auction conversion is on the core path to drive competitive pricing before award.
cases.setup: Buyer; a concluded RFQ event with vendor quotations.
cases.steps: 1. In the RFQ event, go to the **Settings** tab and click **Convert to Auction**. 2. In the prompt, leave the checkbox selected to use the RFQ quotations as starting bids. 3. On the Auction Setup screen, set auction timings and configure available auction settings. 4. Click **Save**. 5. Click **Publish**, review auction details and scheduling, then click **Publish** again.
cases.expected: The auction goes live and is added to the same project; vendors who submitted bids in the RFQ are automatically enrolled with their previous quotations already considered.
cases.oracle: Auction stage visible in the same project; RFQ bidders are participants; their starting bids equal their RFQ quotations.

cases.section: How to set up a Reverse Auction?
cases.title: Create and publish a reverse auction event end to end
cases.why: Setting up and publishing an auction is the entry to the create→publish→bid→award path; if it breaks, no auction can run.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager with access to the Create Event screen; at least one product with mapped vendors exists.
cases.steps: 1. On the **Create Event** screen select **Auction** as the event type. 2. Choose how you will award (partial award to multiple vendors, or entire lot to a single vendor). 3. Click on Select Template and choose a predefined **template**. 4. Add products under the "Products" column from the dropdown and fill in all **mandatory fields** in the template table. 5. Click the blue "Invite Vendors" in the green tip (or add vendors via Participants). 6. Click the blue "Publish Event" button. 7. In the pop-up, review the event details and click the blue "Publish" button.
cases.expected: The event is now Live and an email notification is sent to all added participants inviting them to participate.
cases.oracle: The confirmation "You Have Successfully Published your Auction Event !!" is shown, and each invited participant receives the invitation email.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: Open a published auction and reach the Auction Responses tab
cases.why: Monitoring live bids is the core of running an auction.
cases.setup: Buyer with a published rank-based auction event.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the **Events** tab on the left-hand menu. 2. Find and click on the card for the published event.
cases.expected: The buyer is directed to the Auction Responses tab where vendor quotes can be monitored and managed.
cases.oracle: The Auction Responses tab is open showing vendor quotes.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: Award the auction from the MQCS tab
cases.why: Awarding closes the create→publish→bid→award path.
cases.setup: Buyer who has completed evaluation and sent counter offers on the auction.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the **MQCS** tab. 2. Follow the awarding process (described in the "Awarding Process" article).
cases.expected: The auction can be awarded from the MQCS tab.
cases.oracle: A tester confirms the award is started from the MQCS tab (details live in the awarding article).

cases.title: Convert an RFQ to an auction with Cost Breakdown Mode enabled
cases.why: Cost breakdown captures lump-sum auction prices yet still yields item prices for PO and audit.
cases.setup: Buyer / Purchaser with an RFQ that has vendor quotes.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the RFQ to convert and click **"Convert to Auction"**. 2. On the auction creation page, click the **Event Type** with "Rank on line" below it. 3. Select the checkbox **"Enable Cost Breakdown Mode"**. 4. Configure other auction settings and launch the auction.
cases.expected: The auction launches with vendors placing a lot-level bid during the auction and line-item pricing requested during the CBD window.
cases.oracle: The live auction shows submissions as Auto-breakdown bids on the Sum Total.

cases.title: Submit Cost Breakdown locks item prices after confirmation
cases.why: The final item prices feed PO and audit and must be locked.
cases.setup: Vendor during CBD time with a valid breakdown.
cases.steps: 1. Click **Submit Cost Breakdown**. 2. Read the confirmation dialog and click **Yes, Submit**.
cases.expected: The dialog says "This is the final submission for item prices. Once submitted, you won't be able to change these item prices."; after confirming, the breakdown is locked and a success confirmation is shown.
cases.oracle: The vendor sees the confirmation that the cost breakdown was successfully submitted and justified; prices are no longer editable.

cases.section: How to create Serial Bidding events
cases.title: Create and publish a serial bidding auction
cases.why: Serial bidding runs each line item on its own clock; setup errors break the whole sequence.
cases.setup: Buyer able to create events.
cases.steps: 1. Create a new event in Procol. 2. In the **Event Type** dropdown, select **Auction**. 3. Enable the **Serial Bidding** toggle checkbox. 4. Enter the **duration** for each Line Item. 5. Add the required **Line Items**. 6. Publish the event.
cases.expected: The auction is published with line items opening one at a time, each with its own submission duration.
cases.oracle: On the vendor side only one line item is active at a time.

cases.section: How to Run a Price - Based Auction
cases.title: Create and publish a Price Based auction
cases.why: Main setup flow for the price-based strategy on the core auction path.
cases.setup: Buyer able to create events; vendors to invite.
cases.steps: 1. Create a new event in Procol. 2. In the **Event Type** dropdown, select **Auction**. 3. Select the "Price Based" Auction Strategy. 4. Click on Save and Publish the Event.
cases.expected: The Price Based auction is published.
cases.oracle: The event is live with the Price Based strategy shown.

cases.section: How to Run a Traffic Light Auction
cases.title: Create and publish a Traffic Light auction
cases.why: Main setup flow for the traffic-light strategy on the core auction path.
cases.setup: Buyer able to create events; vendors to invite.
cases.steps: 1. Create a new event in Procol. 2. In the **Event Type** dropdown, select **Auction**. 3. Select the "Traffic Light" Auction Strategy. 4. Choose the grouping condition. 5. Make sure awarding is on the entire lot. 6. Configure the ranges. 7. Click on Save and Publish the Event.
cases.expected: The Traffic Light auction is published with the configured ranges.
cases.oracle: The event is live with the Traffic Light strategy and the configured bands.

cases.section: How to Run a Knockout Auction
cases.title: Create and publish a Knockout auction
cases.why: Main setup flow for the knockout strategy on the core auction path.
cases.setup: Buyer able to create events; vendors to invite.
cases.steps: 1. Create a new event in Procol. 2. In the **Event Type** dropdown, select **Auction**. 3. Select the Knockout auction strategy. 4. Choose on which entity offers should be based. 5. Add the Starting price, Tick Size and Time difference between each consecutive offer. 6. Click on Save and Publish the Event.
cases.expected: The Knockout auction is published.
cases.oracle: The Responses tab shows the current round, upcoming offers and list of bidders.

cases.section: How to Run a Knockout Auction
cases.title: Award a Knockout bid and request approval
cases.why: Awarding is the money step that closes the knockout.
cases.setup: Buyer on a Knockout auction with bidders still in the running.
cases.steps: 1. On the right side, view the list of bidders still in the running. 2. Click **Select Bid** on the vendor to award. 3. In the full-screen awarding window, confirm the proposal amount. 4. Choose an **approval workflow**. 5. Click **Next → Review → Request Approval**.
cases.expected: The bid is sent for approval and the system completes the awarding process.
cases.oracle: The awarding proposal shows as sent for approval.

cases.section: How to Run a Knockout Auction
cases.title: Purchase Order is generated automatically after award approval
cases.why: The PO is the downstream money document of the auction.
cases.setup: Knockout award sent for approval.
cases.steps: 1. Have the approval completed. 2. Look for the PO.
cases.expected: A **Purchase Order (PO)** is generated automatically after approval.
cases.oracle: A PO exists for the awarded vendor and amount.

cases.section: How to Run a Dutch Auction.
cases.title: Create and publish a Dutch auction
cases.why: Main setup flow for the Dutch strategy on the core auction path.
cases.setup: Buyer able to create events; vendors to invite.
cases.steps: 1. Create a new event in Procol. 2. In the **Event Type** dropdown, select **Auction**. 3. Select the Dutch auction strategy. 4. Choose on which entity offers should be based. 5. Choose on which condition the event should close. 6. Configure the Starting Price, Ending Price, Tick Size and Time Difference. 7. Click on Save and Publish the Event.
cases.expected: The Dutch auction is published.
cases.oracle: The Responses tab shows the current round (with End Price), upcoming offers and list of bidders.

cases.section: How to Run a Dutch Auction.
cases.title: First vendor to accept closes the auction and is awarded
cases.why: First-come, first-serve awarding is the defining Dutch rule and a money outcome.
cases.setup: Live Dutch auction with two or more vendors.
cases.steps: 1. As one vendor, click **Accept** on the current offer.
cases.expected: The auction is closed and the vendor who accepted is awarded the bid.
cases.oracle: The auction shows closed with the bid awarded to the accepting vendor; other vendors can no longer accept.

cases.section: How do I approve a TR (Technical Recommendation)?
cases.title: Approve a Technical Recommendation through all approvers
cases.why: TR approval is the gate that releases technical rankings to the buyer.
cases.setup: Approver (e.g. Department Head, Procurement Manager or CXO) on the workflow of a submitted TR.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the **Approvals** tab from the left-hand panel. 2. Click **"Pending on Me"**. 3. Locate the approval entry and click the **arrow icon** to open the proposal. 4. Review the proposal, enter remarks in the comment box and click **"Approve"**. 5. Repeat as each remaining approver in the workflow.
cases.expected: Once all approvers have approved, the proposal is marked as approved and the buyer can see the technical rankings in the event.
cases.oracle: The TR shows approved and the buyer's event view shows the technical rankings.

cases.section: How do I approve a TR (Technical Recommendation)?
cases.title: Approval moves the TR to the next approver
cases.why: Multi-stage workflows must route in order.
cases.setup: TR with a workflow of two or more approvers; first approver logged in.
cases.steps: 1. As the first approver, open the TR from "Pending on Me", add remarks and click **"Approve"**. 2. Log in as the second approver and open "Pending on Me".
cases.expected: The proposal moves to the next approver in the workflow.
cases.oracle: The TR appears in the second approver's "Pending on Me"; the workflow stage advances.

cases.section: How do I approve a TR (Technical Recommendation)?
cases.title: Reject a TR; the evaluator revises and resends it
cases.why: Rejection is how incorrect technical evaluations are corrected before they reach the buyer.
cases.setup: Approver on the workflow of a submitted TR; the evaluator who submitted it.
cases.steps: 1. As approver, open the TR from "Pending on Me", enter remarks and click **"Reject"**. 2. As the evaluator, revise the evaluation and resend it for approval.
cases.expected: The proposal is rejected; the evaluator can revise and resend it for approval.
cases.oracle: The TR shows rejected, then reappears in the approvers' queue after resending.

cases.section: How do I approve a TR (Technical Recommendation)?
cases.title: Technical rankings are hidden from the buyer until the TR is approved
cases.why: Technical approval is required before buyers can view technical evaluations.
cases.setup: Event whose TR is submitted but not fully approved; buyer of that event.
cases.steps: 1. As buyer, open the event while the TR is pending approval. 2. After all approvers approve, open it again.
cases.expected: The buyer cannot view technical evaluations before approval, and can see the technical rankings after it.
cases.oracle: Rankings are absent before full approval and present after.

cases.section: Surrogate Bidding: How to Place Bids on Behalf of Vendors
cases.title: Buyer places a surrogate bid for a vendor in the RFQ stage
cases.why: Surrogate bidding lets a buyer enter bids vendors sent offline (phone, email) so those vendors still compete; a bid that fails to land or lands against the wrong vendor corrupts the comparison and the award.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. An RFQ event with at least one participating vendor who has not bid on the platform; an offline record of that vendor's bid (screenshot, call log or email) to attach.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the project details page for the event. 2. Go to the RFQ stage tab. 3. Click on the Participants section to view the list of vendors. 4. Locate the vendor (use the search bar if needed). 5. Click the "➕ Add Bid" button next to the vendor's name. 6. Enter the vendor's response in the bid form that opens. 7. Add Supplier Remarks if the vendor stated specific instructions. 8. Attach a Surrogate Bid Reference (the offline record). 9. Click Submit. 10. Open the QCS.
cases.expected: The surrogate bid is placed for that vendor and appears correctly in the QCS with the values entered.
cases.oracle: In the QCS the vendor's column/row shows the entered values and is marked "Surrogate Bid" under the vendor's name in blue text, next to the currency.

cases.section: How to Send and Manage Counter Offers?
cases.title: Buyer sends a price counter offer to a vendor from the QCS
cases.why: Counter offers are the core price-negotiation tool; a counter offer that is not delivered or not flagged in the QCS breaks the negotiation and the eventual award value.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. An RFQ event with at least one vendor bid visible in the QCS.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the RFQ tab of the sourcing event. 2. Open the QCS (Quote Comparison Sheet). 3. Identify the vendor and click the blue **"Counter Offer"** button beneath their name. 4. In the dialog, select the Price field. 5. Input the new value to propose. 6. Click **"Send Counter Offer"**.
cases.expected: The counter offer is sent to the vendor and the QCS marks the vendor as having a pending counter offer.
cases.oracle: A tooltip notification confirms the counter offer was sent successfully; a **"Counter Offer Requested"** tag appears above the vendor's name in the QCS with a "Revoke Counter Offer" option, and the changed values are highlighted showing original vs counter offer values.

cases.section: How to Send and Manage Counter Offers?
cases.title: Vendor accepts the counter offer — buyer QCS shows accepted tag
cases.why: Acceptance fixes the negotiated price that will feed the award; the buyer must see it unambiguously.
cases.setup: Buyer and Vendor personas. A counter offer sent by the buyer to the vendor on an RFQ event.
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, open the RFQ event and accept the counter offer. 2. As the buyer, open the QCS on the RFQ tab.
cases.expected: The vendor's bid reflects the accepted counter offer.
cases.oracle: A tag reads "Accepted Counter Offer Bid" with a green thumbs up icon for that vendor in the QCS.

cases.section: How to Send and Manage Counter Offers?
cases.title: Vendor rejects the counter offer — buyer QCS shows rejected tag
cases.why: A rejected counter offer means the vendor's earlier bid stands; the buyer must not award at the countered price.
cases.setup: Buyer and Vendor personas. A counter offer sent by the buyer to the vendor on an RFQ event.
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, open the RFQ event and reject the counter offer. 2. As the buyer, open the QCS on the RFQ tab.
cases.expected: The vendor's response is shown as a rejection.
cases.oracle: A tag reads "Last Counter Offer Rejected" for that vendor in the QCS.

cases.section: How to Send and Manage Counter Offers?
cases.title: Vendor modifies the counter offer — buyer QCS shows modified tag and new value
cases.why: A re-counter introduces a third price (between the original bid and the counter); the buyer must see the new value and the vendor's reason.
cases.setup: Buyer and Vendor personas. Vendor's original bid ₹90; buyer sent a counter offer of ₹80 on Price.
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, modify the counter offer to ₹85 and provide a remark explaining the adjustment. 2. As the buyer, open the QCS on the RFQ tab.
cases.expected: The vendor's bid shows the modified value ₹85 with the vendor's remark.
cases.oracle: A tag reads "Modified Counter Offer Bid" with an orange thumbs up icon; the price shows ₹85 and the remark is visible.

cases.section: How to Send Bulk Counter Offers?
cases.title: Buyer sends a bulk counter offer to all vendors
cases.why: Bulk counter offers push one negotiation ask to every vendor at once; a partial send leaves some vendors un-negotiated and skews the comparison.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. An RFQ event with several vendor bids in the QCS.
cases.steps: 1. Click on Settings and find "Send Bulk Counter Offers". 2. Decide the counter offer to send to all vendors and click Send. 3. Select the field to apply the counter offer on (e.g. Price). 4. Input the new value to propose. 5. Click **"Send Counter Offer"**.
cases.expected: The counter offer is sent to all vendors.
cases.oracle: A tooltip confirms the counter offer was sent successfully; a **"Counter Offer Requested"** tag appears above every vendor's name in the QCS, with changed values highlighted as original vs counter offer.

cases.section: How do I Modify Counter Offers as a Vendor?
cases.title: Vendor submits a modified bid (re-counter) against a buyer counter offer
cases.why: The re-counter is the vendor's side of price negotiation; if it is not submitted or not reflected in the buyer's QCS, the negotiated price is lost.
cases.setup: Vendor persona. An RFQ event where the buyer sent a counter offer (e.g. original price ₹90, buyer offered ₹80).
cases.steps: 1. Open the RFQ event where the counter offer was received. 2. Observe the Counter Offer Banner. 3. Click on the counter offer Decline option. 4. Choose the **"Modify Counter Offer"** option instead of rejecting. 5. Enter the updated value in the editable field (e.g. ₹85). 6. Click the "Place Modified Bid" blue button. 7. Add a remark explaining the reason for the modification. 8. Click the blue **"Place Modified Bid"** button to confirm.
cases.expected: The modified counter offer is submitted and the QCS is updated for the buyer, resolving the counter offer action.
cases.oracle: The vendor's tag displays **"Modified Counter Offer Bid"** with an orange thumbs-up icon; the buyer's QCS shows ₹85 for the vendor.

cases.section: How to Award Vendors and Submit Proposal for Approval
cases.title: Start Awarding opens the awarding screen with proposal value summary
cases.why: The awarding screen totals drive the proposal value that goes for approval; L1 vs non-L1 split is a compliance signal.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. Event with completed negotiation on the latest commercial stage.
cases.steps: 1. Open the **Master QCS** tab on the latest commercial stage. 2. Click the **"Start Awarding"** button on the top right.
cases.expected: The buyer is redirected to the awarding screen.
cases.oracle: Awarding screen shows Total selected line items, Proposal value, L1 proposal value and Non-L1 proposal value.

cases.section: How to Award Vendors and Submit Proposal for Approval
cases.title: Buyer awards a line item to a vendor
cases.why: Awarding decides who supplies what at what value — the core money step of sourcing.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. Awarding screen open for an event with vendor bids on line items.
cases.steps: 1. For a vendor under a line item, select the checkbox to initiate awarding. 2. In the dialog, confirm awarding. 3. Click **"Award"**.
cases.expected: The line item is awarded to the selected vendor and the awarding summary updates.
cases.oracle: The vendor's checkbox for that line item is selected and the awarding screen totals (Total selected line items, Proposal value, L1 / Non-L1 proposal value) reflect the award.

cases.section: How to Award Vendors and Submit Proposal for Approval
cases.title: Create Proposal opens the Note for Approval screen
cases.why: The Note for Approval (NFA) is the document approvers decide on; missing sections mean approvals are made blind.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. Awarding completed on the awarding screen.
cases.steps: 1. Click **"Create Proposal"** on the top right. 2. Fill out any required additional information. 3. Review the screen sections.
cases.expected: A **Note for Approval** screen opens with the event's details for review.
cases.oracle: Note for Approval screen shows Event overview, Allocation summary, Comparison sheets and List of participants and allocations.

cases.section: How to Award Vendors and Submit Proposal for Approval
cases.title: Buyer submits the award proposal into an approval workflow
cases.why: Submitting routes the award into internal compliance approval; the wrong workflow or chain means the wrong people approve spend.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. Note for Approval screen completed for an awarded event; at least one approval workflow configured.
cases.steps: 1. Click **"Submit Proposal"** on the top right. 2. In the dialog, select the appropriate approval workflow. 3. Review the proposal details (line items, values, type) and add closing remarks if needed. 4. Scroll down to verify the approval chain. 5. Click **"Submit Proposal"** on the bottom right.
cases.expected: The proposal is submitted and the buyer is taken to the **Approval Screen**.
cases.oracle: Approval Screen shows the generated note for approval, event overview and allocation details, and the full approval chain listed on the right.

cases.section: How to Award Vendors and Submit Proposal for Approval
cases.title: Approver approves the award proposal from the Approval Screen
cases.why: Approval is the compliance gate before a purchase order is raised.
cases.setup: A user who is an approver in the proposal's approval chain; a submitted award proposal.
cases.steps: 1. Open the proposal's **Approval Screen**. 2. Review the note for approval, event overview, allocation details and approval chain. 3. Take the **Approve** action.
cases.expected: The approver's approval is recorded on the proposal.
cases.oracle: The approval chain on the right shows this approver as approved.

cases.section: How to Award Vendors and Submit Proposal for Approval
cases.title: Approver rejects the award proposal
cases.why: Rejection must stop the award from proceeding to a purchase order.
cases.setup: A user who is an approver in the proposal's approval chain; a submitted award proposal.
cases.steps: 1. Open the proposal's **Approval Screen**. 2. Take the **Reject** action.
cases.expected: The proposal is rejected by this approver and no purchase order is requested for it.
cases.oracle: The approval chain shows this approver as rejected; no purchase order for the event appears in the "Purchase Orders" tab.

cases.section: How to Award Vendors and Submit Proposal for Approval
cases.title: All approvals received triggers a purchase order request to the ERP
cases.why: Award → PO is the hand-off from sourcing to P2P; the article states it happens automatically once every approval is in.
cases.setup: An award proposal with its full approval chain; all approvers available.
cases.steps: 1. Have every approver in the chain approve the proposal. 2. Open the **"Purchase Orders"** tab.
cases.expected: The system automatically sends a request to the ERP to generate a purchase order, and the purchase orders requested from the awarded event are listed.
cases.oracle: The "Purchase Orders" tab lists the purchase orders requested from the event just awarded.

cases.section: How to approve an Awarding proposal?
cases.title: Approver approves an awarding proposal from the Approvals tab
cases.why: Approval of the award proposal is the final gate before a purchase order is requested.
cases.setup: A user who is an approver on an awarding proposal that has been created and submitted for a sourcing project.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the **"Approvals"** tab in the left navigation panel. 2. Click on the event to view for approval. 3. Review the NFA and Proposal and leave remarks. 4. Approve.
cases.expected: The approval is recorded; once all approvals are received the purchase order is requested for generation.
cases.oracle: The proposal shows the approver's approval; after the final approval the "Purchase Orders" tab lists the purchase orders requested from the awarded event.

cases.section: How to approve an Awarding proposal?
cases.title: Approver rejects an awarding proposal from the Approvals tab
cases.why: The article lets the approver reject after review; a rejected award must not move forward.
cases.setup: A user who is an approver on a submitted awarding proposal.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the **"Approvals"** tab and click on the event. 2. Review the NFA and Proposal and leave remarks. 3. Reject.
cases.expected: The proposal is rejected by the approver.
cases.oracle: The proposal shows the rejection with the approver's remark; no purchase order for the event appears in the "Purchase Orders" tab.

cases.section: How to approve an Awarding proposal?
cases.title: Purchase order requested after all approvals is visible in the Purchase Orders tab
cases.why: The article states the system automatically sends a PO request to the ERP when all approvals are in; this is the sourcing → P2P hand-off.
cases.setup: An awarding proposal whose approval chain has been fully approved.
cases.steps: 1. After the last approval, open the **"Purchase Orders"** tab. 2. Look for purchase orders from the awarded event.
cases.expected: The purchase orders requested from the event just awarded are listed.
cases.oracle: The "Purchase Orders" tab lists purchase orders requested from the awarded event.

cases.title: Buyer enables Vendor Masking on a live RFQ event
cases.why: Vendor masking eliminates bias and reduces collusion risk by hiding vendor identities during evaluation and negotiation — a compliance control.
cases.setup: Buyer on a live RFQ event with at least two participating vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Go to the **RFQ** event screen where the event is live. 2. Click the **Actions** button. 3. Select **Enable Vendor Masking**.
cases.expected: All vendor names are hidden until bidding ends and replaced with Vendor 1, 2, 3 … N.
cases.oracle: Vendor names on the event screen/QCS read Vendor 1, Vendor 2, … instead of the real names.

cases.section: How to create a Single Stage Event (RFP, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Each event type asks for its own configurations
cases.why: Awarding type and auction strategy decide how bids are ranked and awarded; missing or extra config fields break the award path.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager on the Single Stage event setup screen with the event-type side drawer open.
cases.steps: 1. Select **RFP** and note the configurations shown. 2. Select **RFQ** and note the configurations shown. 3. Select **Reverse Auction** and note the configurations shown.
cases.expected: RFP: no configurations required. RFQ: Awarding Type (Lot or Line) and an optional Delivery Date. Reverse Auction: Auction Strategy (Rank Based, Price Based, Traffic Light, Knockout, Dutch), Awarding Type (Lot or Line), optional Rank Type Configurations and optional Serial Bidding.
cases.oracle: The configuration fields rendered for each selected event type match the article's table.

cases.section: How to create a Single Stage Event (RFP, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Line items are limited to 65 per event
cases.why: The article states a hard limit; exceeding it silently could lose line items from the event.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager on the Single Stage event setup screen with a template selected; at least 66 products available.
cases.steps: 1. Add products row by row beneath the "Products" column (a new row is added automatically each time). 2. Continue adding until 65 line items are present. 3. Attempt to add a 66th line item.
cases.expected: Up to 65 line items can be added; the product can not go beyond the stated limit of 65 line items.
cases.oracle: Count of line-item rows in the template table never exceeds 65 (the article does not state the exact UI reaction at the limit — tester records what happens).

cases.section: How to create a Single Stage Event (RFP, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Buyer cannot fill shaded vendor-side fields in the template table
cases.why: Vendor-owned fields (e.g. price) must stay vendor-owned; a buyer pre-filling them would corrupt quotes.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager on the event setup screen with a template and at least one product added.
cases.steps: 1. Locate the shaded-out fields in the template table. 2. Try to click into and type in a shaded-out field.
cases.expected: Shaded-out fields cannot be filled in by the buyer; they are for the Vendor to fill.
cases.oracle: The shaded cell does not accept input from the buyer.

cases.section: How to create a Single Stage Event (RFP, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Suggested vendors are added as participants via "Invite Vendors"
cases.why: The vendor-suggestion shortcut is how most events get their participants; a broken mapping means an event with nobody to bid.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager; products added to the template that have vendors mapped to them.
cases.steps: 1. After adding products, find the green tip showing suggested vendors mapped to the products. 2. Click the blue "Invite Vendors".
cases.expected: The vendors mapped to the added products are automatically added as participants.
cases.oracle: The suggested vendors appear in the event's Participants list.

cases.section: How to create a Sourcing Project (Technical Stage, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: An RFQ and an Auction cannot be created together; max 2 stages at creation
cases.why: Stated restriction on project structure; the auction must come from converting the RFQ.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager at the stage-selection step after clicking "Create Project" in the cart.
cases.steps: 1. Select the RFQ stage. 2. Attempt to also select the Auction stage. 3. Attempt to select more than 2 stages in total.
cases.expected: Only one of RFQ or Auction can be chosen; at most 2 stages can be chosen during creation.
cases.oracle: The stage selector does not allow RFQ and Auction together nor a third stage.

cases.section: How to create a Sourcing Project (Technical Stage, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Technical evaluator must be assigned on every line item
cases.why: The technical stage cannot be evaluated (T1/T2/T3 or TA/TNA) without an evaluator on each line item; the article says "without fail".
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager on the Technical Stage of a project with multiple line items; an internal user to assign as evaluator.
cases.steps: 1. Under the "Vendor Assessment" section, click select template. 2. Click "+ Add Evaluator" under the first line item and search the user. 3. Repeat for all line items.
cases.expected: Each line item has the assigned technical evaluator; that evaluator is the user who will assess vendor responses in this stage and can assign ranks (T1, T2, T3) or TA (Technically Accepted) / TNA (Technically Not Accepted).
cases.oracle: Every line item lists the evaluator; the tester records what happens if one line item is left without an evaluator (not stated in the article).

cases.section: How to create a Sourcing Project (Technical Stage, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Vendor suggestion does not appear on the Technical Stage tab
cases.why: Stated behaviour; testers must look for suggestions on the right tab.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager on a project with a Technical Stage and an RFQ; products with mapped vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Open the Technical Stage tab and scroll to the bottom. 2. Open the RFQ tab and scroll to the bottom.
cases.expected: The vendor suggestion green tip with "Invite Vendors" does not appear on the Technical Stage tab; it appears only on RFQ and Auction tabs.
cases.oracle: Presence of the suggestion tip on RFQ tab, absence on Technical Stage tab.

cases.section: How to create a Sourcing Project (Technical Stage, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Participants are project-level and common to all stages
cases.why: A vendor invited on the RFQ must also be in the Technical Stage; divergence would let unqualified vendors bid.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager on a project with a Technical Stage and an RFQ.
cases.steps: 1. On the RFQ tab, add vendors (via "Invite Vendors" or Participants). 2. Open the Technical Stage tab and view Participants.
cases.expected: Participants added are on a project-level and are common for all stages.
cases.oracle: The same vendor list is shown for both stages.

cases.section: How to set Savings references in an Event?
cases.title: Gross Total savings with default references (Budget, Historical Price, Existing Proposal)
cases.why: Savings references are the baseline for measuring cost savings during evaluation and awarding.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement manager creating a new event.
cases.steps: 1. While creating a new event, click the "Savings" option at the bottom-left corner. 2. In the side panel, select **Gross Total**. 3. Enter a single reference value for one or more of Budget, Historical Price and Existing Proposal.
cases.expected: The side panel shows saving calculation settings with three default Savings References; with Gross Total a single reference value per category is accepted for the full event.
cases.oracle: The saved panel shows Gross Total selected and the entered reference values.

cases.section: How to Edit Currencies in my Event
cases.title: Set up Multi Currency with conversion factors
cases.why: Lets foreign vendors bid in their currency while the buyer compares in the default currency.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement manager creating a new event.
cases.steps: 1. Click the "Edit Currencies" option at the bottom-left of the page. 2. In the pop-up panel, select **Multi Currency**. 3. Tick the checkbox next to each currency to add. 4. Add a conversion factor in the input box next to each currency. 5. Click OK.
cases.expected: The event keeps its default currency and allows vendors to bid in the added currencies at the defined conversion rates.
cases.oracle: Reopening "Edit Currencies" shows Multi Currency with the ticked currencies and their conversion factors.

cases.section: How to Edit Currencies in my Event
cases.title: Change the event's Base Currency
cases.why: The base currency is what all vendors bid in and what the buyer compares in.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement manager creating a new event.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Edit Currencies" and select **Base Currency**. 2. Click "Select Base Currency" and choose the new currency from the dropdown. 3. Add a conversion factor in the input box below the dropdown. 4. Click OK.
cases.expected: The default or base currency of that event changes to the selected currency.
cases.oracle: The event shows the new base currency; reopening the panel shows it with the conversion factor.

cases.section: How to add Terms and Conditions for my Vendors in my Events?
cases.title: Add project-level T&Cs from previous sets, own text and uploads
cases.why: T&Cs ensure vendors formally acknowledge commercial and legal expectations before participating.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Event Creation screen; T&Cs used previously under other projects or events exist; a PDF to upload.
cases.steps: 1. Next to the event title, click the 'Add T&Cs' button. 2. In the side panel, use the checkboxes to select previously used T&Cs. 3. Type terms in the text box labeled 'Add your own terms and conditions' and click the plus (+) button. 4. Upload a file using the **Upload** button. 5. Click **Done** at the bottom right.
cases.expected: The selected, typed and uploaded T&Cs are attached at project level and apply to all events under the project.
cases.oracle: Reopening 'Add T&Cs' shows all added items; each event under the project carries them.

cases.section: How to add Terms and Conditions for my Vendors in my Events?
cases.title: Add event-specific T&Cs via 'Edit Terms and Conditions'
cases.why: Stage-level T&Cs apply only to a specific RFQ, Auction or Technical Round.
cases.setup: Buyer on the event configuration screen.
cases.steps: 1. Click the 'Edit Terms and Conditions' button towards the bottom left. 2. Select from recent or previously used T&Cs and manually enter new terms. 3. Upload files or documents if needed. 4. Click **Done** at the bottom right.
cases.expected: The T&Cs are added to that event only.
cases.oracle: The event's T&C panel lists the added terms; other stages of the same project do not show them.

cases.section: How do I Schedule Events and change Event Duration?
cases.title: Start Now with a preset duration
cases.why: The default schedule decides when vendors can bid and when bidding closes.
cases.setup: Planner / Buyer / Procurement manager on the event creation page.
cases.steps: 1. Click the date range label beside the "Schedule" option at the bottom-right corner. 2. In the side panel, under Start Time keep "Start Now". 3. Under End Time, open the "Duration" drop-down and choose a preset (30 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours or 1 day).
cases.expected: The side panel shows Start Time, End Time and Evaluation Time; with Start Now the event starts immediately at the current date and time shown, and ends after the chosen duration.
cases.oracle: The schedule label shows a range from now to now + chosen duration.

cases.section: How do I Schedule Events and change Event Duration?
cases.title: Schedule for Later with a chosen start date and time
cases.why: Future-dated events must not go live early.
cases.setup: Planner / Buyer / Procurement manager with the Schedule side panel open.
cases.steps: 1. Under Start Time, change the drop-down to **Schedule for Later**. 2. Click the date field and pick a future date in the calendar widget. 3. Click the time field and type or pick a time.
cases.expected: The event is set to start at the chosen future date and time.
cases.oracle: The schedule label shows the chosen start; the event does not go live before it.

cases.section: How do I add additional columns to a Template?
cases.title: Add a Creator column (e.g. Price Cap) and fill it as buyer
cases.why: Creator columns enforce pricing rules such as price caps and tick sizes on the event.
cases.setup: Buyer / Purchaser on the RFQ Event Creation page with line items added.
cases.steps: 1. Click "+Add Columns" above the RFQ Sheet on the right side. 2. Choose **Creator**. 3. Pick a column from the list (Price Cap, Creator Attachments, Tick Size, Min Quantity, Custom Column, Tick Size Percentage). 4. Fill in values in the new column's cells.
cases.expected: The dropdown offers Creator and Participant; the Creator list shows the six options; the selected column shows up in the RFQ/Auction Sheet and the buyer can fill its cells.
cases.oracle: New column header visible in the sheet with the buyer-entered values.

cases.section: How do I add additional columns to a Template?
cases.title: Add a Participant column (e.g. Freight Charges) for the vendor to fill
cases.why: Participant columns collect extra vendor data such as freight and attachments.
cases.setup: Buyer / Purchaser on the RFQ Event Creation page; a participating vendor to verify.
cases.steps: 1. Click "+Add Columns" and choose **Participant**. 2. Pick a column (Freight Charges, Participant Attachments, Custom Column). 3. Publish and, as the vendor, open the event.
cases.expected: The column shows up in the RFQ/Auction Sheet and is filled in by the vendor.
cases.oracle: Column visible in the buyer's sheet and editable by the vendor when bidding.

cases.section: How do I fill my tempate by uploading an Excel Sheet?
cases.title: Fill the product sheet by uploading a filled Excel template
cases.why: Bulk upload is how large RFQs get their line items.
cases.setup: Buyer on the RFQ Event Creation page; Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel available.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Upload Sheet" above the RFQ Sheet on the right side. 2. In the pop-up click "Download template". 3. Open the sheet, fill in the line item details, and download it as an .xlsx file. 4. Upload the filled file in the modal and click OK.
cases.expected: The Product Sheet is updated with the filled in details.
cases.oracle: RFQ sheet rows match the rows in the uploaded .xlsx.

cases.section: How to set up an RFQ (Request for Quotation)?
cases.title: RFQ awarded as an entire lot to a single vendor runs at Lot level
cases.why: The awarding choice is the only RFQ configuration and decides whether the award can be split.
cases.setup: Buyer on the event setup screen with RFQ chosen as Event Type.
cases.steps: 1. Observe the configurations offered for RFQ. 2. Select "I'll award the entire lot to a single vendor". 3. Complete template, products, vendors and publish.
cases.expected: There is just one configuration to set when starting an RFQ (how you will award); selecting the entire-lot option runs the RFQ at a Lot Level.
cases.oracle: The published RFQ shows lot-level awarding (tester verifies at award time that the whole lot goes to one vendor).

cases.section: How do you run an RFQ Event?
cases.title: Open a published RFQ lands on the RFQ Responses tab
cases.why: The Responses tab is where the buyer monitors and manages vendor quotes.
cases.setup: Buyer; a published RFQ event.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the **Events** tab on the left-hand menu. 2. Find and click on the card for the published event.
cases.expected: The buyer is directed to the RFQ Responses tab where vendor quotes can be monitored and managed.
cases.oracle: RFQ Responses tab is active and shows the vendor quotes.

cases.section: How do you run an RFQ Event?
cases.title: Reject Quote with the box unchecked blocks the seller from bidding again
cases.why: Stated option that controls whether a rejected vendor can re-enter the event.
cases.setup: Buyer; a published RFQ with a vendor quote; the vendor's login to verify.
cases.steps: 1. Click the three-dot menu next to the vendor's name and select **Reject Quote**. 2. Uncheck the box that allows the seller to bid again and confirm. 3. As the vendor, try to bid again.
cases.expected: The seller is not allowed to bid again.
cases.oracle: The vendor cannot submit a new bid on the event (the article does not state the vendor-side message — tester records it).

cases.section: How do you run an RFQ Event?
cases.title: Edit Quote updates vendor global fields such as taxes or delivery terms
cases.why: Missing taxes or delivery terms distort landed-cost comparison.
cases.setup: Buyer; a published RFQ with a vendor quote missing a global field (e.g. taxes).
cases.steps: 1. Click the three-dot menu next to the vendor's name. 2. Select **Edit Quote** and update the global field (taxes or delivery terms). 3. Save.
cases.expected: The specific global fields are updated on the vendor's quote.
cases.oracle: The quote shows the edited value in the comparison view.

cases.section: How do you run an RFQ Event?
cases.title: Counter Offer button opens the counter offer interface
cases.why: Counter offers are the RFQ negotiation lever before award.
cases.setup: Buyer; a published RFQ with vendor quotes.
cases.steps: 1. Locate the vendor name in the comparison view. 2. Click the **Counter Offer** button under the vendor name.
cases.expected: The buyer is taken to the counter offer interface to configure and send revised expectations to the vendor.
cases.oracle: The counter offer interface opens for that vendor.

cases.section: How do you run an RFQ Event?
cases.title: Actions › Show Best Prices shows suppliers the best price and adds a lowest-bid row in the QCS
cases.why: Revealing best prices changes vendor behaviour; the QCS row must reflect the true lowest bid.
cases.setup: Buyer; a published RFQ with quotes from several vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Click the **Actions** button. 2. Select **Show Best Prices**.
cases.expected: Suppliers are shown the exact best price for each line item; an extra row per line item displays the lowest bid across vendors in the QCS.
cases.oracle: QCS shows the extra lowest-bid row with the minimum price per line item; a vendor login shows the best price.

cases.section: How do you run an RFQ Event?
cases.title: View-Only Mode blocks counter offers, quote edits and surrogate bids until disabled
cases.why: Stated restriction that freezes the evaluation against changes.
cases.setup: Buyer; a published RFQ with vendor quotes.
cases.steps: 1. Click **Actions** › **Enable View-Only Mode**. 2. Try to send a counter offer, edit a quote and place a surrogate bid. 3. Click the same action again to disable the mode and retry.
cases.expected: While enabled, users cannot send counter offers, edit quotes or place surrogate bids; after disabling, these actions are available again.
cases.oracle: Counter Offer / Edit Quote / surrogate bid are unavailable in view-only mode and available after it is disabled.

cases.section: How do you run an RFQ Event?
cases.title: Send Bulk Counter Offers to all vendors from Settings
cases.why: Bulk negotiation across all vendors in one step.
cases.setup: Buyer; a published RFQ with several vendor quotes.
cases.steps: 1. Click on Settings and find "Send Bulk Counter Offers". 2. Decide the counter offer to send to all vendors and click Send.
cases.expected: The counter offer is sent to all vendors.
cases.oracle: Every vendor shows a received counter offer (tester checks at least two vendor logins).

cases.title: OTP recipient dropdown lists only pre-set users
cases.why: Stated restriction that controls who can act as the second authenticator.
cases.setup: Buyer at the "Select OTP Recipient" step of Unlock Bids; the configured set of pre-set users known.
cases.steps: 1. Open the OTP recipient dropdown. 2. Compare the listed users with the configured pre-set users.
cases.expected: The dropdown shows only the specified number of pre-set users.
cases.oracle: No user outside the pre-set list appears.

cases.section: How do I use Request for Best Offer?
cases.title: Request Best Offer from selected vendors only
cases.why: Buyers focus the final round on the most competitive vendors.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager; an RFQ in Evaluation with at least three vendor quotes.
cases.steps: 1. Settings › "Request for Best Offer". 2. Set a duration and choose specific vendors instead of all. 3. Click "Send Request".
cases.expected: Only the chosen vendors are invited to submit a Best Offer.
cases.oracle: Only the selected vendors' rows show the Best Offer Requested status and receive the notification.

cases.section: How do I use Request for Best Offer?
cases.title: Vendor sees the Best Offer banner and revises line items within the window
cases.why: The vendor side must be able to respond or the request is pointless.
cases.setup: A Best Offer request sent to a participating vendor.
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, open the event. 2. Revise applicable line items and submit during the configured window.
cases.expected: The vendor sees a prominent banner/notification requesting a **Best Offer** and can revise line items directly during the window.
cases.oracle: Banner visible on the vendor side; the revised quote is accepted.

cases.section: How do I use Request for Best Offer?
cases.title: Buyer reviews Best Offer submissions and continues or awards
cases.why: The revised prices feed the award decision.
cases.setup: Buyer; at least one vendor has submitted a Best Offer.
cases.steps: 1. Open the Supplier's Best Offer section / comparison view. 2. Compare the revised prices with the vendor's previous bid. 3. Send another best offer request or proceed to awarding.
cases.expected: Revised prices and fields are visible in the comparison view; the buyer can validate improvement and either request again or award.
cases.oracle: Comparison view shows the new values alongside the ability to re-request or award.

cases.section: How do I use Request for Best Offer?
cases.title: Request for Best Offer is only available once Evaluation has started
cases.why: Stated restriction in both the Best Offer and Run-an-RFQ articles.
cases.setup: Buyer; an RFQ still in its submission window.
cases.steps: 1. Open Settings on the live RFQ. 2. Look for / attempt "Request for Best Offer". 3. Repeat after the event enters Evaluation.
cases.expected: Best Offer can be requested only once Evaluation time has started.
cases.oracle: The request cannot be sent before Evaluation and can be sent after (the article does not state the UI state before Evaluation).

cases.section: How to Split Line Items into Lots in an RFQ Event
cases.title: All line items start in Lot 1; maximum of 4 lots
cases.why: Stated default and upper limit for lot splitting.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager; an RFQ in evaluation with at least five line items.
cases.steps: 1. Open Settings › **Split Line Items into Lots**. 2. Check which lot each line item is in. 3. Open the lot dropdown next to a line item serial number.
cases.expected: By default all line items are in **Lot 1**; lot numbers can be chosen up to a maximum of 4 lots.
cases.oracle: Initial lot for every item is Lot 1; the dropdown offers no lot beyond 4.

cases.section: How to Split Line Items into Lots in an RFQ Event
cases.title: Lots cannot be published during the submission window
cases.why: Stated restriction: restructuring must not happen while vendors are still submitting.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager; an RFQ still in its submission window.
cases.steps: 1. Open Settings › **Split Line Items into Lots** (if offered). 2. Try to click **Publish Lot**.
cases.expected: The option to publish lots is not available during the submission window; lots can only be published during the evaluation stage.
cases.oracle: Publish Lot is unavailable while the submission window is open.

cases.section: How to Split Line Items into Lots in an RFQ Event
cases.title: After a lot split, other operations wait until vendors adjust charges
cases.why: Stated gate: global/other charges must be re-apportioned before the buyer continues.
cases.setup: Buyer; an RFQ whose lots have just been published; vendors have not yet reviewed.
cases.steps: 1. After publishing lots, attempt another operation on the lot RFQ (e.g. counter offer or award).
cases.expected: Vendors are prompted to adjust their global / Other charges; only after vendors do this (or review is skipped) can the buyer go ahead with other operations.
cases.oracle: Buyer operations are blocked while vendor adjustment is pending (the article does not name the blocking message).

cases.section: How to Skip Vendor Review in Lot Splitting
cases.title: Skip vendor review with pro-rata allocation of global charges
cases.why: Keeps evaluation moving when a vendor cannot revise charges after a lot split.
cases.setup: Buyer; a Lot RFQ where lot splitting is complete and a vendor's **Lot Adjustment** is pending.
cases.steps: 1. Open the **Lot RFQ** and locate the vendor card with the pending Lot Adjustment. 2. Click **"Skip Vendor Review"** under the vendor's name. 3. In the side panel, choose **Pro-rata allocation** (by line item value or quantity). 4. Enter a reason (e.g. Vendor not responding). 5. Click **"Confirm & Skip Review"**.
cases.expected: The vendor review is skipped and global charges are allocated pro-rata across the lots.
cases.oracle: Confirmation tooltip that the vendor review has been skipped; the vendor's lot charges reflect the pro-rata split.

cases.section: How to Skip Vendor Review in Lot Splitting
cases.title: Skip vendor review with manual entry of global charges per lot
cases.why: Alternate allocation where the buyer sets each lot's charges.
cases.setup: Buyer; a Lot RFQ with a vendor whose Lot Adjustment is pending.
cases.steps: 1. Click **"Skip Vendor Review"** under the vendor's name. 2. Choose **Manual entry** and enter global charge values for each lot. 3. Enter a reason and click **"Confirm & Skip Review"**.
cases.expected: The vendor review is skipped with the manually entered charges per lot.
cases.oracle: Confirmation tooltip; the vendor's lots show the entered charge values.

cases.section: How to Skip Vendor Review in Lot Splitting
cases.title: A reason is required to skip vendor review
cases.why: Audit trail: skipping must be justified (the article requires a valid reason and all required fields).
cases.setup: Buyer in the Skip Vendor Review side panel.
cases.steps: 1. Choose an allocation method but leave the reason empty. 2. Try to click **"Confirm & Skip Review"**. 3. Enter a reason (Vendor unavailable / network issues / not responding) and confirm.
cases.expected: Confirm & Skip Review proceeds only once all required fields, including the reason, are filled.
cases.oracle: No skip without a reason; skip succeeds after the reason is entered (exact UI reaction not stated).

cases.section: How do I convert an RFQ to an Auction
cases.title: Convert to Auction with fresh bids (checkbox unchecked)
cases.why: Alternate path where RFQ prices are not carried forward.
cases.setup: Buyer; a concluded RFQ with quotations.
cases.steps: 1. Settings › **Convert to Auction**. 2. Uncheck the checkbox in the prompt. 3. Configure, **Save**, and **Publish** twice.
cases.expected: The auction starts with fresh bids from vendors.
cases.oracle: Auction shows no carried-forward starting bids from the RFQ.

cases.section: How do I convert an RFQ to an Auction
cases.title: Template, products and quantities are locked on the conversion Auction Setup; vendors remain editable
cases.why: Stated restriction preserving comparability between RFQ quotes and auction bids.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Setup screen reached via Convert to Auction.
cases.steps: 1. Try to change the event template. 2. Try to modify products or quantities. 3. Update the list of invited vendors.
cases.expected: The template cannot be changed and products/quantities cannot be modified; the list of vendors invited can still be updated.
cases.oracle: Template and product/quantity controls are locked; vendor list edits save.

cases.section: How do I convert an RFQ to an Auction
cases.title: Knockout and Dutch auctions cannot be selected during conversion
cases.why: Stated restriction: these types do not support pre-existing quotations.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Setup screen reached via Convert to Auction.
cases.steps: 1. Open the auction type / strategy options. 2. Try to select **Knockout** and **Dutch**.
cases.expected: Knockout and Dutch Auctions cannot be selected during conversion.
cases.oracle: Both options are unavailable while other auction settings remain configurable.

cases.section: How to set up a Reverse Auction?
cases.title: Auction strategy cannot be changed after the event goes live
cases.why: Changing visibility/competition rules mid-auction would break fairness for vendors already bidding.
cases.setup: Buyer with a published (live) auction event.
cases.steps: 1. Open the live auction event. 2. Attempt to change the auction strategy.
cases.expected: The strategy cannot be updated once the event is live.
cases.oracle: No strategy change is possible on the live event; the original strategy remains in effect.

cases.section: How to set up a Reverse Auction?
cases.title: Line items are limited to 65 per auction template
cases.why: The article states a hard limit; exceeding it must be handled rather than corrupting the event.
cases.setup: Buyer creating an auction event with a template selected.
cases.steps: 1. Add products row by row in the template table up to 65 line items. 2. Try to add a 66th line item.
cases.expected: Up to 65 line items can be added; the limit is enforced beyond that.
cases.oracle: A tester confirms 65 rows are accepted and checks what happens on the 66th (the article does not state the message).

cases.section: How to set up a Reverse Auction?
cases.title: Shaded vendor fields cannot be filled by the buyer
cases.why: Vendor-owned fields (such as price) must not be pre-filled by the buyer.
cases.setup: Buyer creating an auction event with products added to the template table.
cases.steps: 1. Try to type into a shaded-out field in the template table.
cases.expected: Shaded out fields are for the Vendor to fill; the buyer cannot fill them.
cases.oracle: The shaded field stays non-editable for the buyer.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Strategy drawer offers all five auction strategies
cases.why: Each documented strategy must be selectable or the related auction types cannot run.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Create Event screen with Auction selected.
cases.steps: 1. Click the **Rank on Line** badge to open the strategy side drawer. 2. Review the strategy options.
cases.expected: The strategies Rank Based, Price Based, Traffic Light, Knockout and Dutch Auction are available.
cases.oracle: All five strategy names appear in the side drawer.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Rank Based: vendors see only their rank, not prices
cases.why: Hiding prices is the whole point of rank-based auctions (anti-collusion).
cases.setup: Buyer publishes a Rank Based auction; two or more vendors bid.
cases.steps: 1. As a vendor, place a bid in the Rank Based auction. 2. Look at the vendor bidding screen.
cases.expected: Vendors only see their rank, not actual prices of competitors.
cases.oracle: The vendor screen shows the vendor's rank and no competitor prices.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Price Based: vendors see the lowest bid price, not ranks
cases.why: Price-based auctions depend on vendors knowing the exact price to beat.
cases.setup: Buyer publishes a Price Based auction; two or more vendors bid.
cases.steps: 1. As a vendor, place a bid in the Price Based auction. 2. Look at the vendor bidding screen.
cases.expected: Vendors see the lowest bid price on each item but not ranks.
cases.oracle: The vendor screen shows the lowest price per item and no rank.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Traffic Light: vendors see a colour status only
cases.why: Traffic light auctions must not leak precise positioning.
cases.setup: Buyer publishes a Traffic Light auction; vendors bid.
cases.steps: 1. As a vendor, place a bid in the Traffic Light auction. 2. Look at the vendor bidding screen.
cases.expected: Vendors see a colour-coded status (Green/Amber/Red) based on their bid range; no ranks or prices are shown.
cases.oracle: The vendor screen shows only a colour status, without rank or competitor price.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Knockout: vendors can only accept or reject a target price
cases.why: Knockout auctions test acceptance of a fixed offer; free-form bidding would defeat that.
cases.setup: Buyer publishes a Knockout auction; vendors invited.
cases.steps: 1. As a vendor, open the Knockout auction.
cases.expected: Vendors are shown a target price and can only accept or reject it.
cases.oracle: The vendor screen offers only accept/reject actions against the shown price.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Dutch: award goes first-come, first-serve at the pre-set price
cases.why: The first vendor to accept must win; any other rule changes who gets the award.
cases.setup: Buyer publishes a Dutch auction; vendors invited.
cases.steps: 1. As a vendor, accept the current pre-set price.
cases.expected: Items are awarded first-come, first-serve to the vendor willing to accept the pre-set price.
cases.oracle: The first accepting vendor is the one awarded.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Rank Based: show rank for individual items
cases.why: Line-item-level events need per-item ranks rather than a single sum-total rank.
cases.setup: Buyer creating a Rank Based auction with awarding type "partially award event to multiple vendors".
cases.steps: 1. Enable **"Show rank to vendor for individual item."** 2. Publish; as a vendor, bid on several line items.
cases.expected: Vendors see their rank for each line item rather than their rank on the Sum Total.
cases.oracle: The vendor screen shows a rank against each line item.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Rank Based: minimum revisions before rank is shown
cases.why: Rank visibility gated on revisions forces vendors to engage before getting feedback.
cases.setup: Buyer creating a Rank Based auction.
cases.steps: 1. Enable **"Set Minimum revision to show Rank"** and enter n in the input box that appears. 2. Publish; as a vendor, revise the price fewer than n times, then n times.
cases.expected: Ranks are shown to the vendor only after they have revised their price at least n times.
cases.oracle: Rank is hidden before the nth revision and visible after it.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Price Based: minimum revisions before best price is shown
