cases.section: The request and the file itself
cases.title: 1,000 rows upload within the request and every row is processed
cases.why: Parsing and the staging insert happen inside the web request (the PR doc warns about an 11,000-row load). 1,000 tripwired rows measure it without creating anything.
cases.setup: Data: creates nothing (every row stops in validation). Fixture: `procol test/fixtures/vendor-bulk-upload/VBU-023.xlsx`.
cases.steps: 1. 1,000 tripwired rows 2. POST and time it 3. Wait until no row is in_progress
cases.expected: HTTP 200 in well under 60 s; all 1,000 rows end failed 'Invalid Status'; none left in_progress.
cases.oracle: HTTP time, staged count 1000, every error 'Invalid Status'.

cases.section: The request and the file itself
cases.title: Two uploads by the same user at the same moment get separate jobs
cases.why: The job id is 'this user's job count + 1', read before the insert, so two uploads at the same time can share an id — their rows, status and error sheet then mix.
cases.setup: Data: creates nothing (every row stops in validation). Fixture: `procol test/fixtures/vendor-bulk-upload/VBU-024.xlsx`.
cases.steps: 1. POST two different tripwired sheets at the same moment 2. Read the job id of every staged row
cases.expected: Two jobs with one row each. Today the two rows can land in one job id.
cases.oracle: vendor_bulk_upload_jobs.job_id of both rows.

cases.section: Who may upload, and the template / status / error-sheet endpoints
cases.title: The template's sample row lines up with its headers
cases.why: The sample row is written by position from a fixed list in the flag-OFF order. When contactless moves columns, 'Procol Contact' lands under Tax Type and the email under Tax No. A buyer who edits the sample row uploads garbage.
cases.setup: Data: creates nothing (every row stops in validation).
cases.steps: 1. Download the template 2. Compare row 4 with row 3
cases.expected: Row 4: Company Name=Procol, POC - Full Name=Procol Contact, POC - Email Address=example@procol.in, City=Gurgaon, Address=Platina Tower.
cases.oracle: Cell-by-cell comparison.

cases.section: Who may upload, and the template / status / error-sheet endpoints
cases.title: Each dropdown sits on its own column
cases.why: The Vendor Profile dropdown range is hard-coded to D4:D100 unless vendor_invitation_v2 is on; with the contactless layout D is Business Location, so D gets two conflicting lists and Vendor Profile gets none.
cases.setup: Data: creates nothing (every row stops in validation).
cases.steps: 1. Download the template 2. Read the data-validation ranges from the sheet XML
cases.expected: Vendor Profile list on the Vendor Profile column; Tax Type, Business Location, Status, Vendor Onboarding Required each on their own column; no column with two lists.
cases.oracle: sqref of each <dataValidation> vs the header position.

cases.section: Who may upload, and the template / status / error-sheet endpoints
cases.title: With contactless on, only Company Name is in the Mandatory block
cases.why: The flag moves POC Name, POC Email and Vendor Profile out of the mandatory group; the template must show that, or buyers keep filling fields they don't need.
cases.setup: gate: allow_contactless_vendor_upload is on. Data: creates nothing (every row stops in validation).
cases.steps: 1. Download the template 2. Read the row-1 group of each column
cases.expected: Mandatory Details: Company Name (+ the With Tax No. trio). POC - Full Name, POC - Email Address, Vendor Profile, City, Address under Optional Details.
cases.oracle: Row-1 grouping.

cases.section: Who may upload, and the template / status / error-sheet endpoints
cases.title: Error sheet of a failed job lists the failed rows with their error
cases.why: The error sheet is how a buyer fixes a big upload; it must hold every failed row and an Error column.
cases.setup: Data: creates nothing (every row stops in validation). Fixture: `procol test/fixtures/vendor-bulk-upload/VBU-039.xlsx`.
cases.steps: 1. Upload one tripwired row 2. GET the error sheet for that job 3. Read it
cases.expected: HTTP 200 excel_url; the file's first column is 'Error' = 'Invalid Status', followed by the row's values.
cases.oracle: Parsed error sheet.

cases.section: Who may upload, and the template / status / error-sheet endpoints
cases.title: disable_manual_vendor_creation blocks the upload for client users

cases.section: Who may upload, and the template / status / error-sheet endpoints
cases.title: Uploading the error sheet back re-checks the rows (its Error column is ignored)
cases.why: The normal way to fix a big upload is: download the error sheet, correct it, upload it again. The error sheet has an extra 'Error' column first; it must not break the re-upload.

cases.expected: The re-uploaded job has the same rows with the same error ('Invalid Status').
cases.oracle: Rows of both jobs.

cases.title: A city that is not in the master (no tax number) does not become a random city
cases.why: Old code: 'Invalid City Name'. QA doc A5: 'Success. Record created with no city'. The company builder defaults a missing city to id 38 ('-'). Status=rejected keeps the row mail-free if it is created.

cases.title: A one-letter city ('a') is not fuzzy-matched to some real city
cases.why: City lookup falls back to name ILIKE '%a%' and takes the first alphabetically — any typo becomes a real, wrong city.

cases.expected: Either refused 'Invalid City Name' or stored with no city — never a city the buyer didn't name. Today: the first city containing 'a'.
cases.oracle: companies.city_id → cities.name.

cases.expected: One row success, the other failed 'This email is already invited.'. Two successes = race defect.
cases.oracle: Job rows.

cases.title: Same POC email with a tax number becomes a subsidiary — and keeps 'No'
cases.why: Error 689 routes to SubsidiaryService, whose invitation other_details has no skip_vendor_onboarding, so a non-PQ subsidiary still triggers the 'new prospect' mail. Real-mail tier because of exactly that mail.

cases.expected: Row success as a subsidiary; mapping Active; its invitation carries skip_vendor_onboarding=true, so no prospect mail. Code today omits the flag.
cases.oracle: invitations.other_details of the subsidiary.

cases.section: Data fidelity — what the parser does to the values
cases.title: A 17-digit bank account number typed as a number is not turned into scientific notation
cases.why: Indian bank accounts run to 17 digits. Typed into Excel as a number, the cell reaches Roo as a Float, and Ruby prints a Float of 17+ digits as '1.23456789012345e+16' — that string is what gets stored. (Excel itself keeps only 15 significant digits, so the cell should be text; the product should refuse or warn rather than store scientific notation.)
cases.setup: Data: creates nothing (every row stops in validation). Fixture: `procol test/fixtures/vendor-bulk-upload/VBU-165.xlsx`.

cases.oracle: Job data.

cases.section: The request and the file itself
cases.title: excel_data sent as null is refused
cases.why: JSON null reaches Rails as nil — same guard as a missing key; proves the guard is `nil?` and not `key?`.
cases.setup: Data: creates nothing (every row stops in validation).
cases.steps: 1. POST /v1/bulk_create_vendor with body {"excel_data": null}
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: The request and the file itself
cases.title: A PNG image is refused
cases.why: Binary non-zip, non-OLE input — the second Roo fallback must raise Ole::Storage::FormatError, which is the only error the helper rescues there.
cases.setup: Data: creates nothing (every row stops in validation). Fixture: `procol test/fixtures/vendor-bulk-upload/VBU-006.png`.
cases.steps: 1. Base64 a 1×1 PNG 2. POST it as excel_data
cases.expected: HTTP 422 'Invalid file format'.
cases.oracle: 4xx; no 5xx.

cases.section: The request and the file itself
cases.title: base64 with the data-URL prefix left on is refused cleanly
cases.why: The web app strips 'data:…;base64,' before sending; any other client that forgets gets junk bytes in front of the zip.
cases.setup: Data: creates nothing (every row stops in validation). Fixture: `procol test/fixtures/vendor-bulk-upload/VBU-009.xlsx`.
cases.steps: 1. Take a valid tripwired sheet 2. Prefix its base64 with data:application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet;base64, 3. POST
cases.expected: A clean 4xx — 422 'Invalid file format', or the sandbox firewall's bare 403 (seen 2026-09-29); never a 500.
cases.oracle: 4xx; no 5xx.

cases.section: The request and the file itself
cases.title: A new-format sheet with just one old column (POC 2 - Mobile) is also refused

cases.oracle: Job row + companies lookup.

journeys.title: Re-checking every vendor's documents on a schedule
journeys.goal: Set a client's revalidation config, let the nightly run (or a QA trigger) re-check each vendor's GST, PAN, MSME and bank, and see one final status per vendor — with the reasons — on the listing, the vendor page and the Excel download.

cases.title: No revalidation happens when it is OFF for the client
cases.why: Disabled client — Negative case from the manual sheet.
cases.setup: Revalidation is OFF for the client (default for every client). Test data: Any client with revalidation OFF.
cases.steps: 1. Ask dev to run the scheduler for the day 2. Login as the client's buyer and open Vendors listing 3. Open any vendor detail page
cases.expected: No run for this client. No validation columns or filters in listing. Vendor detail has no validation section.
cases.oracle: The screen (buyer dashboard on UAT), and the revalidation rows where the steps ask dev for them.

cases.title: Revalidation runs for a client once enabled
cases.why: Enabled client — Positive case from the manual sheet.
cases.setup: Ops enable revalidation for Gmmco with GST, PAN, MSME, Bank, start date = today. Test data: Gmmco (47053).
cases.steps: 1. Ask dev to trigger the revalidation run for Gmmco (or wait for the 11 pm IST run) 2. Login as Gmmco buyer and go to Vendors listing 3. Check Validation Status, Last Validated, Errors and Missing Documents for the vendor
cases.expected: Run happens. Validation columns appear and are filled.
cases.oracle: The screen (buyer dashboard on UAT), and the revalidation rows where the steps ask dev for them.

cases.title: The same run is not started twice on one date

journeys.title: What the screen shows versus what the API sent
journeys.goal: Open an event's screens — list, details, each stage's responses and overview, Master QCS — and confirm every value the backend sent is shown, in the right place, with the same meaning.

cases.title: Searching the list by title shows exactly the events the API returned for that search
cases.why: When the list shows other events while the search box still holds the title, the buyer concludes the event does not exist — or opens a wrong one.
cases.setup: As UI-XCHK-001. Run it twice: once after the list has loaded ("settled") and once typing as soon as the search box appears ("typed straight away").
cases.steps: 1. Open Events. 2. Search for the event's title. 3. Read which events the list shows.
cases.expected: The rows are exactly the events the search returned — here, the one event — and nothing else.
cases.oracle: The RFX references on screen equal the references in the search response. When they differ, the run states which list request was sent before the search but answered after it.

cases.title: The Line Items table lists every line item the API returns, with its material code, category, subcategory and quantity
cases.why: Line items are what is being bought. A missing row or a wrong quantity or unit changes what vendors quote for.
cases.setup: A published event with line items.
cases.steps: 1. Open the event. 2. Read the Line Items count and table.
cases.expected: The count next to "Line Items" equals the API's count; every line item the API returned for the page has a row; Material Code, Category, Subcategory and Quantity (number and unit) match.
cases.oracle: Map `02-summary.json`: count + one row per item + each value in its column.

cases.title: The Responses grid has a column for every bidder and shows every quoted value exactly as the API returns it
cases.why: This grid is where a buyer compares quotes. A price, quantity or tax shown differently from what the vendor submitted decides the award.
cases.setup: A stage with at least one submitted bid.
cases.steps: 1. Open the stage's tab (Responses opens first). 2. Read each bidder's columns on each line item's row.
cases.expected: Every bidder the API lists has a column group; every value in each bidder's quote (price, quantity available, tax, other template fields) is shown in that bidder's column, on that line item's row, under the template's own column name. A column the buyer has hidden with "Hide fields" is noted, not failed.
cases.oracle: Template-driven: the stage schema names the columns, each bidder's quote supplies the values.

cases.title: Master QCS has a column for every bidder and shows every bid value (quantities, rates, amounts, rank, totals) as the API returns it
cases.why: Master QCS is the award decision screen. Every number on it is used to choose a vendor.
cases.setup: An event with at least one submitted bid.
cases.steps: 1. Open the event. 2. Click Master QCS. 3. Read each bidder's column for each line item.
cases.expected: Every bidder has a column; on each row (named by the template field), the bidder's value equals the API's — quantity offered and awarded, rank, rates, amounts, savings — and each bidder's Sum Total matches.
cases.oracle: Template-driven, map `05-qcs.json`, special `qcs-cells`. Rows hidden with "Hide fields" are noted, not failed. No bids means inconclusive, never passed.

cases.title: No screen of the event looks fine while a request behind it failed, and none reports an error while its requests succeeded
cases.why: A screen that silently drops a failed request shows a partial picture as if it were whole; one that shows an error over good data stops work.
cases.setup: Runs on every screen the other cases open.
cases.steps: Open each screen and watch its requests and messages.
cases.expected: Every failed request the screen depends on is visible to the user as an error; no success message appears for a failed request; no error appears when all requests succeeded.
cases.oracle: Captured response statuses versus the app's own toasts and on-screen error text. Background calls (preferences, chat counters, viewing stats) excluded unless they fail with a server error.

cases.section: The Overview's Product Sheet and Bidding Summary
cases.title: The Bidding Summary lists every rank's vendor and quoted price, best first, as the API ranks them
cases.why: A summary that puts the second-best vendor under "Best Market Price" points the buyer at the wrong vendor.
cases.setup: A pricing stage with at least two bids.
cases.steps: 1. Open the stage's Overview. 2. Read "Line Item Wise" in the Bidding Summary.
cases.expected: Under "Best Market Price", "Rank 2 Market Price" … the vendor and price of that rank.
cases.oracle: Each rank's value in its position on the row, left to right.

cases.title: The proposal's Overview shows the selected line items, total, L1 and non-L1 proposal values the API computed
cases.why: Approvers decide on these totals. A total that differs from what the system computed means money is approved on a wrong figure.
cases.setup: A published event with bids and an award proposal.
cases.steps: 1. Open the event. 2. Open Master QCS. 3. Click "Bid Selection Proposal". 4. Read the Overview panel.
cases.expected: "Tot. selected line items" reads awarded items out of all items; "Tot. Proposal Value", "Tot. L1 Proposal Value" and "Tot. Non L1 Proposal Value" are the amounts the system computed for the proposal.
cases.oracle: Each value next to its label; amounts compared as numbers.

cases.title: The Allocation Summary lists every awarded vendor with the items selected and total amount the API returns
cases.why: This table is the award: which vendor gets how many items for how much. A wrong amount on a vendor's row is an award letter with the wrong value.
cases.setup: As UI-XCHK-PROP-001; ideally a split award to three vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Open the proposal. 2. Read the Allocation Summary.
cases.expected: One row per awarded vendor; "Total Items selected", "Total Amount" (and the L1 columns when present) match the proposal.
cases.oracle: Each value in its column on the vendor's row.

cases.title: The proposal's Order Allocation shows each awarded vendor's offered and awarded quantity, rates and totals as the API returns them
cases.why: "Qty Awarded" is what the vendor will be asked to deliver.
cases.setup: As UI-XCHK-PROP-001.
cases.steps: 1. Open the proposal. 2. Read the Order Allocation grid.
cases.expected: A column per vendor; Qty Offer, Qty Awarded, rates and Sum Total match the proposal sheet (hidden fields excepted).
cases.oracle: Each value on its row (the template's field name) in the vendor's column, below the Order Allocation heading.

cases.title: Each bidder's rank badge and each line's Rank cell show the rank the API gives
cases.why: In an auction the rank is the whole game: the buyer awards and negotiates on it. A badge that says 1 for the second-best bidder is a costly error.
cases.setup: An auction (or rank-showing RFQ) with at least two QA vendors' bids.
cases.steps: 1. Open the auction stage. 2. Read the badge by each bidder's name and the Rank cell on each line.
cases.expected: Badge and Rank cell show the system's current rank for that bidder. Where the console hides the badge by its settings, the case says so instead.
cases.oracle: The number next to the bidder's name and in the bidder's Rank column, using the same source the console uses (live rank indicators first).

cases.title: The event's card in the list shows its title, reference, creator and item count as the API returns them
cases.why: The list is how a buyer finds an event. A card that shows the wrong reference or item count sends the buyer into the wrong event.
cases.setup: A published event the signed-in buyer can see.
cases.steps: 1. Open Events. 2. Type the event's title into the search box and press Enter. 3. Read the event's card.
cases.expected: The card shows the event's title, its RFX reference, the creator's name and "N items", exactly as the backend returned them for this search.
cases.oracle: Map `01-list.json`: each value must be inside the card (DOM row) that carries the event's reference; the item count on the card's first line.

cases.title: Each stage line on the event's card shows the stage code, title, participation and timeline the API returns
cases.why: The stage line is where a buyer sees, at a glance, how many vendors are active and whether a stage is overdue. A wrong count here is acted on.
cases.setup: As UI-XCHK-001.
cases.steps: 1. Search the list for the event. 2. Read each stage's line on its card.
cases.expected: Each stage line shows its stage code, stage title, "active/invited" participants and timeline phrase (e.g. "Overdue by") as returned by the API.
cases.oracle: Map `01-list.json`: values on the same visual line as the stage code.

cases.title: The Published Stages table shows each stage's code, title, participation and bidding window as the API returns them
cases.why: The bidding window on this table is what buyers tell vendors. A start or end time off by an hour (time zone) or a swapped column is a real loss.
cases.setup: A published event with at least one stage.
cases.steps: 1. Open the event. 2. Read each row of Published Stages.
cases.expected: One row per stage the API returns; under each column — Stage Title, Participants, Bidding Starts At, Bidding Ends At — the API's value for that stage.
cases.oracle: Map `02-summary.json`: row count equals the API's stage count; each value in its column on the stage's row.

cases.title: The Participants table lists every invited vendor the API returns, with location, invitation type and each stage's bid status
cases.why: This table answers "who has bid?". A vendor shown with the wrong status is chased for a bid it placed, or forgotten while it still could bid.
cases.setup: A published event with invited vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Open the event. 2. Read the Participants table.
cases.expected: One row per vendor the API returns; Location and Type match; each stage column shows the vendor's status in that stage in the product's own words (Bid placed / Pending / Rejected / Not invited).
cases.oracle: Map `02-summary.json`: the status labels are the ones the API itself publishes for its participant filter.

cases.title: The stage's status chip agrees with the stage's status and bidding window in the API
cases.why: "Live" versus "Expired" decides whether a buyer waits for more bids or starts evaluating.
cases.setup: A published event; open each stage.
cases.steps: 1. Open the event. 2. Click the stage's tab. 3. Read the status chip.
cases.expected: The chip is the status the API's status and times imply at that moment (upcoming, live, evaluation time, expired, closed, withdrawn).
cases.oracle: The console's own rule applied to the API's times; the chip must be that word, and must not be another status word.

cases.title: The Bidding Summary names the best (L1) vendor and price for each line item as the API returns them
cases.why: L1 is the default award candidate.
cases.setup: A stage with at least one bid.
cases.steps: 1. Open the stage's Overview. 2. Read Bidding Summary.
cases.expected: For each line item, the L1 vendor and price match the API.
cases.oracle: Map `04-overview.json`.

cases.title: Order Configurations show the stage's start time, duration, evaluation time, type, mode and template as the API returns them
cases.why: This is the schedule as the product records it. A duration shown wrongly makes a buyer extend or close a stage for no reason.
cases.setup: A published stage.
cases.steps: 1. Open the stage's Overview. 2. Read Order Configurations.
cases.expected: Started At (India time), Order Duration (end minus start), Evaluation Time (extra closing time minus end), Order Type, Order Mode, Template and Event Title match the API.
cases.oracle: Map `04-overview.json`: durations parsed and compared in seconds, within the unit the screen writes.

cases.title: The vendor's view of the event shows the title, line items, quantities and closing time the buyer's API returns
cases.why: The vendor bids on what its screen shows. If it differs from what the buyer published, the bid answers a different question.
cases.setup: A published event with an invited test vendor whose sign-in does not send mail to a real address.
cases.steps: 1. Sign in to the supplier portal as the invited vendor. 2. Open the event. 3. Read title, line items, quantities and closing time.
cases.expected: They equal the buyer-side API's event, line items and stage end time.
cases.oracle: Same comparison rules; reference values from the buyer's API capture.

cases.title: The vendor's bid form offers exactly the fields of the stage's template, with the buyer's quantities and units
cases.why: A field missing from the vendor's form is a value the buyer will never receive.
cases.setup: As UI-XCHK-060, inside the bidding window.
cases.steps: 1. Sign in as the vendor. 2. Open the event's bid form. 3. Read its columns and the quantity requested per line.
cases.expected: Every participant field of the template is a column; quantities and units equal the buyer's.
cases.oracle: Template widgets (participant fields) versus the form's headers.

cases.section: The Overview's Product Sheet and Bidding Summary
cases.title: The Product Sheet shows each line item's requested quantity, unit, delivery location and other buyer values as the API returns them
cases.why: The Product Sheet is the buyer's own record of what was asked for.
cases.setup: A published pricing stage.
cases.steps: 1. Open the stage. 2. Click Overview. 3. Read the Product Sheet.
cases.expected: For every line, each buyer column (Quantity Requested with its unit, Delivery location, Product Variant …) matches the stage.
cases.oracle: Each value under its column on the product's row.

cases.section: The Overview's Product Sheet and Bidding Summary
cases.title: When savings are compared on the whole lot, the Overview's Savings Summary shows the same savings the stage's Responses tab shows
cases.why: A buyer who reads "–" for savings on the Overview and ₹30 on the Responses tab for the same stage cannot tell which one to report.
cases.setup: A pricing or auction stage whose savings are compared on the whole lot (not per line item), with a bid below the reference price.
cases.steps: 1. Open the stage. 2. Read the savings on the Responses tab. 3. Click Overview. 4. Read Savings Summary.
cases.expected: The Savings Summary shows the same savings amount as the Responses tab.
cases.oracle: The amount next to "Savings" equals the stage's computed savings. The console reads the first bidder's own savings record here, so a difference means the two values the system sends disagree.

cases.title: While a stage is live, the header timer shows the time left to the API's closing time
cases.why: Vendors and buyers act on the countdown; a timer off by minutes makes people miss the close.
cases.setup: A stage that is open for bidding when the screen is read (or in its extra closing time).
cases.steps: 1. Open the live stage. 2. Read the timer in the header.
cases.expected: The time left equals the closing time minus now, within a few seconds.
cases.oracle: Timer text in seconds against the closing time and the moment the screen was read (15 seconds' slack plus the measured clock difference).

cases.section: The technical stage's responses and evaluation
cases.title: Every vendor that responded to the technical stage has a column, with the time its response was submitted
cases.why: Evaluators must see every response; the submission time settles disputes about late responses.
cases.setup: A published technical + pricing event where a QA vendor submitted a technical response.
cases.steps: 1. Open the event. 2. Click the technical stage's tab. 3. Read the vendor columns and the time under each vendor's name.
cases.expected: A column per responding vendor; the submission time (India time, to the minute) is the one the system recorded.
cases.oracle: Vendor name on screen; the time beside it, allowing for the console's own clock adjustment.

cases.section: The technical stage's responses and evaluation
cases.title: Every answer and evaluation score a vendor gave is shown on its question's row, in that vendor's column
cases.why: Evaluators score what they see. An answer on the wrong row, or in the wrong vendor's column, gets the wrong score.
cases.setup: As UI-XCHK-TECH-001.
cases.steps: 1. Open the technical stage. 2. For each question, read the vendor's answer.
cases.expected: Each answer on the row titled with the question (and its description), under the vendor who gave it; a score shows its label.
cases.oracle: Answer text on the question's line inside the vendor's column.

cases.title: The overview shows the event's title, project ID and creation time as the API returns them
cases.why: The project ID is quoted in every conversation about an event; the creation time is used in audits.
cases.setup: A published event.
cases.steps: 1. Open the event. 2. Read the title, "Project ID" and "Created at".
cases.expected: Title, project ID and creation time (India time, to the minute) match the API.
cases.oracle: Map `02-summary.json`: values next to their labels.

cases.title: The Participation counter shows bids placed out of vendors invited, as the API counts them
cases.why: "1 / 38" is the buyer's whole sense of how the event is going.
cases.setup: A published stage.
cases.steps: 1. Open the stage's tab. 2. Read "Participation".
cases.expected: "bids placed / invited" equals the API's bidder delivery counts.
cases.oracle: Map `03-responses.json`.

cases.title: The savings strip shows the savings amount and percentage the API computed
cases.why: Savings are reported upward; a wrong sign or figure misreports the event.
cases.setup: A stage with a bid and a savings reference (e.g. last purchase price).
cases.steps: 1. Open the stage's tab. 2. Read the savings strip at the bottom.
cases.expected: Savings amount and percentage match the API.
cases.oracle: Map `03-responses.json`.

cases.title: The Participation Summary shows the participant, bid and counter-offer counts the API returns
cases.why: These counts are the stage's audit summary.
cases.setup: A published stage.
cases.steps: 1. Open the stage's tab. 2. Click Overview. 3. Read Participation Summary.
cases.expected: Total and active participants, total, revised and rejected bids, counter offers (all, active, accepted) and dynamic time extended match the API.
cases.oracle: Map `04-overview.json`: each value next to its label.

cases.title: The Savings Summary shows the reference price, savings amount, percentage and per-line savings the API computed
cases.why: As UI-XCHK-023, in the place savings are usually read from.
cases.setup: A stage with a bid and a savings reference.
cases.steps: 1. Open the stage's Overview. 2. Read Savings Summary.
cases.expected: Reference, savings amount, percentage and each line item's savings match the API.
cases.oracle: Map `04-overview.json`.

cases.section: The proposal's status on Master QCS
cases.title: Master QCS shows the award proposal's button with the status the API gives the proposal
cases.why: "Approval in Progress" versus "Draft" tells the buyer whether the award has left their hands.
cases.setup: A published event with an award proposal.
cases.steps: 1. Open the event. 2. Open Master QCS. 3. Read the tag on "Bid Selection Proposal".
cases.expected: The tag reads the proposal's status in the console's words (Draft, Approval in Progress, Rejected, or the purchase-order status once selected).
cases.oracle: Status next to the button label.

cases.title: The stage's Participants tab lists every vendor invited to the stage, with the email the API returns
cases.why: This is where a buyer checks who was invited and enters a bid on a vendor's behalf; a missing vendor cannot be bid for.
cases.setup: A published stage with QA vendors invited.
cases.steps: 1. Open the stage. 2. Click Participants. 3. Turn on "Show only selected vendors". 4. Read the list.
cases.expected: Every invited vendor is listed, with its email.
cases.oracle: Vendor name on screen; its email on the same line.

cases.title: The proposal names the event's RFX number, who recommended it, and its approval workflow and conditions as the API returns them
cases.why: The approval conditions explain why this approver was asked; a wrong threshold in the sentence misleads the approver.
cases.setup: As UI-XCHK-PROP-001, with an approval workflow that applies.
cases.steps: 1. Open the proposal. 2. Read "RFX No", "Proposal Recommended By", "Approval Workflow Name" and "Approval Workflow Conditions".
cases.expected: The values match the proposal; the conditions read as the console writes them, e.g. "Total Proposal Value is more than 1".
cases.oracle: Values next to their labels; the conditions sentence rebuilt with the console's own rule and compared.

cases.title: The proposal's Participants panel lists every invited vendor, numbered 1, 2, 3 …, with each stage's bid status
cases.why: Approvers check who was invited and who bid before approving. A row without a number, or a wrong status, undermines that check.
cases.setup: As UI-XCHK-PROP-001.
cases.steps: 1. Open the proposal. 2. Open the Participants panel. 3. Read "S No.", Location, Type and each stage's column for every vendor.
cases.expected: Rows numbered 1, 2, 3 … in order; location, invitation type and each stage's status ("Bid placed", "Not Participated" …) as the system records them.
cases.oracle: Each value in its column on the vendor's row; the serial number is the row's position.

cases.section: The technical stage's responses and evaluation
cases.title: Each section of the technical sheet shows the line item's code and quantity, its evaluation status and its evaluator as the API returns them
cases.why: "TR Submitted" against the wrong section, or the wrong evaluator, sends the evaluation to the wrong person.
cases.setup: As UI-XCHK-TECH-001, after the evaluation was submitted.
cases.steps: 1. Open the technical stage. 2. Read each section header.
cases.expected: Item code, quantity, status ("TR Submitted" when scored) and the evaluator's name match the stage.
cases.oracle: Each value on the page in the console's words.

cases.title: Price Trends Details lists every past deal the API returns with its price, quantity, location, vendor and closing time in India time
cases.why: Buyers use past prices to judge today's bids.
cases.setup: A pricing stage for a product with past deals.
cases.steps: 1. Open the stage. 2. Click Price Trends. 3. Read the chart legend and the first page of "Price Trends Details".
cases.expected: The legend counts the deals per product; the first ten deals, newest first, each show price, quantity, location and vendor on the row with its closing time.
cases.oracle: A row found by its closing time; every other value on that row.

cases.title: Contact Info shows the buyer's name, email and phone as the API returns them
cases.why: Vendors are told to contact this person.
cases.setup: A published event.
cases.steps: 1. Open the event. 2. Read Contact Info.
cases.expected: Buyer name, email and phone match the API.
cases.oracle: Map `02-summary.json`: values next to their labels.

cases.section: The Overview's Product Sheet and Bidding Summary
cases.title: Order Details show the stage's location as the API returns it
cases.why: Vendors price delivery to this location.
cases.setup: A published stage.
cases.steps: 1. Open the stage's Overview. 2. Read "Location" under Order Details.
cases.expected: The stage's location text (the console takes it from the stage's description).
cases.oracle: Value next to the label.

cases.title: The Note for Approval shows the note the buyer wrote, as the API stores it
cases.why: The note is the buyer's justification to the approver.
cases.setup: As UI-XCHK-PROP-001, with a note.
cases.steps: 1. Open the proposal. 2. Read "Note for Approval".
cases.expected: The note's text, as written.
cases.oracle: The stored rich-text note turned into plain text is on the page.

journeys.title: Choosing a template and checking every field it defines
journeys.goal: Pick a template the client really has for the kind of round, build a sandbox round from it, and check each column: what cannot be filled is refused, what is entered is checked by the server — or, where only the screen checks it, the gap is recorded.

cases.section: The template and the valid baselines
cases.title: The chosen template opens
cases.why: A buyer who picks a template for a round first has it opened; if opening it fails, nobody can use it. The product model found four templates that fail to open (three on PROCOL DEMO, one on Demo Account 2).
cases.setup: Signed in as a buyer of the client. The template is one the client is offered for this kind of round.
cases.steps: 1. Open the template as the event-creation screen does.
cases.expected: The template opens and lists its columns (or, for a technical template, its pages and questions).
cases.oracle: GET /templates/:uuid answers 2xx; 5xx = defect.

cases.section: The template and the valid baselines
cases.title: A pricing round saves with every buyer column filled correctly
cases.why: The baseline for every buyer case: if a correct round is refused, every negative case is refused for the wrong reason.
cases.setup: A sandbox draft event with one line item (a catalogue product with a quality, in one of the client's units, a delivery location).
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round using the template, with the template's own columns. 2. Fill every buyer column with a valid value. 3. Save the round as a draft.
cases.expected: The round is saved and comes back with its id.
cases.oracle: POST /trade/template_input 2xx with a uuid.

cases.section: The template and the valid baselines
cases.title: The vendor saves their line with every vendor column valid
cases.why: The vendor-side baseline: if a correct line is refused, every vendor case is refused for the wrong reason.
cases.setup: A round built from the template is published to the client's test vendor, who is signed in and has started a bid.
cases.steps: 1. Fill every vendor column with a valid value (quantity = requested, a price inside any limit). 2. Save the line.
cases.expected: The line is saved.
cases.oracle: POST /v1/bids/:uuid/create_bid_products 2xx.

cases.section: The template and the valid baselines
cases.title: A technical round saves with the template's pages and questions unchanged
cases.why: The baseline for every technical-round case.
cases.setup: A sandbox draft event; an evaluator of the client exists.
cases.steps: 1. Add a technical (RFP) round using the template, with its pages and questions as the template defines them. 2. Save it as a draft.
cases.expected: The round is saved and comes back with its id.
cases.oracle: POST /trade/template_input (rfx_mode rfp) 2xx with a uuid.

cases.section: The template and the valid baselines
cases.title: The vendor submits the technical answers with every question answered
cases.why: The baseline for every missing-answer case.
cases.setup: A technical round built from the template is published to the test vendor, who has opened it. Templates with a required file-upload question cannot be answered by this check (no file is uploaded) — the case is then reported as not run.
cases.steps: 1. Answer every question on every page. 2. Submit the response.
cases.expected: The response is submitted.
cases.oracle: PATCH /template_responses/:uuid (status active) 2xx.

cases.section: The template and the valid baselines
cases.title: A pricing round that names a template which does not exist is refused
cases.why: A round must be built from a real template of the client. If the server stores a round against a template that does not exist, later steps that read the template break — the engine journey saw an award fail with "Bid not present on this line item" after such a round was accepted.
cases.setup: A sandbox draft event with one line item.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round exactly like the valid one, but naming a template id that does not exist. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: The round is refused with a clear message and is not stored.
cases.oracle: POST /trade/template_input with a made-up template_uuid → 4xx. A 2xx is the defect.

cases.section: The line item: product, unit, delivery location
cases.title: A line item without a product is refused cleanly
cases.why: Every line item is a product of the client's catalogue; a line without one cannot be quoted or awarded — and must be refused with a message, not a crash.
cases.setup: A sandbox draft event.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with the line item's product left out (unit and quantity still given). 2. Save it.
cases.expected: The round is refused with a clear message ("Product not found"), not a server error.
cases.oracle: 4xx; 5xx = defect.

cases.section: The line item: product, unit, delivery location
cases.title: A line item without a unit is refused
cases.why: Quantities and prices are per unit; without one the round cannot be compared or awarded.
cases.setup: A sandbox draft event.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with the quantity's unit left empty. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: The round is refused: "Unit cannot be blank".

cases.section: The line item: product, unit, delivery location
cases.title: A line item in a unit the client does not have is refused
cases.why: The unit must be one of the client's own active units. The default Procol templates assume KG, which Demo Account 2 does not have.
cases.setup: A sandbox draft event; a unit symbol that is not among the client's units (from the product model).
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with the quantity in that unit. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: The round is refused: "The unit … is not present".
cases.oracle: 422, code 495, message names the unit.

cases.section: The line item: product, unit, delivery location
cases.title: A product linked to another company's unit cannot be quoted in that unit
cases.why: Some products are linked to a unit that belongs to another company (GMMCO, Demo Account 2, PROCOL DEMO all have such products). The screen pre-selects the product's first linked unit without checking it, so the buyer hits a refusal they cannot explain.
cases.setup: A product of the client whose only linked unit is not one of the client's units (from the product model), with a quality.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round for that product, in its linked unit. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: The round is refused: "The unit … is not present" — and the screen should not offer that unit.

cases.title: A required buyer column left empty
cases.why: The screen refuses to publish while a required buyer cell is empty ("Sheet partially filled, please check again."); the server does not check "required" on pricing-sheet cells.
cases.setup: A template with a required buyer column other than product, quantity and delivery location.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with that column empty and everything else valid. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: Accepted by the API — only the screen stops it (a gap). No server error.
cases.oracle: no 5xx; 2xx recorded as a gap.

cases.title: A negative price cap, floor price or minimum quantity is refused
cases.why: Buyer limits steer every bid; a negative limit would reject every honest bid or none.
cases.setup: A template with a price cap, floor price or minimum quantity column.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with −10 in that column. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: Refused: "Price Cap cannot be negative" / "Floor Price cannot be negative" / "Floor Quantity cannot be negative".

cases.title: The vendor leaves a required column empty
cases.why: A bid line without a required value cannot be compared.
cases.setup: A published round; the vendor has started a bid.
cases.steps: 1. Fill the line validly except one required vendor column. 2. Save the line.
cases.expected: No server error; the server's answer is recorded (an empty price is refused today, "Invalid Input").
cases.oracle: no 5xx.

cases.title: The vendor offers more than the requested quantity on a round that does not allow it
cases.why: When over-quantity is off, a vendor may not offer more than asked for. A round that says nothing allows it (the server's default is "allowed").
cases.setup: A published round with over-quantity NOT allowed. If the round cannot be set up that way (on UAT the setting comes from the company's trade configuration), the case is reported as not run with the reason.
cases.steps: 1. Fill the line with the requested quantity + 1,000. 2. Save the line.
cases.expected: Refused: "Quantity cannot be greater than the mentioned quantity."

cases.title: The vendor quotes above the buyer's price cap
cases.why: The price cap is the buyer's upper limit. Many stored templates carry the rule "base price below ceiling price" with its comparison sign damaged in storage ("u003c"); the server's own price-cap check does not read that text, so it must still hold.
cases.setup: A template with a price cap column; the published round's price cap is 100.
cases.steps: 1. Fill the line with a price of 150. 2. Save the line.
cases.expected: Refused: "Price cannot be more than the allowed price".

cases.title: The vendor quotes below the buyer's floor price
cases.why: The floor price is the buyer's lower limit.
cases.setup: A template with a floor price column; the published round's floor price is 10.
cases.steps: 1. Fill the line with a price of 5. 2. Save the line.
cases.expected: Refused: "Price cannot be less than the allowed price".

cases.title: The vendor submits technical answers with a required question left empty
cases.why: A required question must be answered before the response counts; the server checks it on submit.
cases.setup: A technical round built from the template, published to the test vendor, who has opened it.
cases.steps: 1. Answer every question except one required question. 2. Submit the response.
cases.expected: Refused: "Please fill '<question>'" naming that question. A refusal naming another question is "couldn't tell".
cases.oracle: 422, code 572, message contains the question's name.

cases.title: The vendor offers less than the buyer's minimum quantity
cases.why: The buyer set a minimum quantity per vendor; a smaller offer must be refused.
cases.setup: A template with a minimum-quantity column; the published round's minimum is 10.
cases.steps: 1. Fill the line with a quantity of 1. 2. Save the line.
cases.expected: Refused: "Quantity cannot be less than the allowed quantity".

cases.title: Text typed into a buyer number column
cases.why: Text in a number column breaks totals and comparisons; the screen silently drops it.
cases.setup: A template with a buyer number, quantity or percentage column.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with "abc" in that column. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: Accepted by the API — only the screen stops it (a gap). No server error.
cases.oracle: no 5xx; 2xx recorded as a gap.

cases.title: A negative number in a buyer number column (including the requested quantity)
cases.why: A negative quantity or amount turns totals and savings upside down.
cases.setup: A template with a buyer number column.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with −5 in that column. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: Accepted by the API — only the screen stops it (a gap). No server error.
cases.oracle: no 5xx; 2xx recorded as a gap.

cases.title: A value outside a buyer column's choice list
cases.why: A dropdown offers only its listed values; anything else breaks reports and comparisons.
cases.setup: A template with a buyer dropdown column.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with "QA not an option" in that column. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: Accepted by the API — only the screen stops it (a gap). No server error.
cases.oracle: no 5xx; 2xx recorded as a gap.

cases.title: An impossible date (31 February) in a date column
cases.why: Dates drive delivery and contract terms; an impossible date must not crash the save or be stored silently.
cases.setup: A template with a buyer date column.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with 31-02-2026 in the column. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: No server error; the server's answer is recorded.
cases.oracle: no 5xx.

cases.title: The buyer sends a value for a calculated column
cases.why: Calculated columns (totals) are worked out; nobody should be able to type them.
cases.setup: A template with a calculated line-item column.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with 999999 in the calculated column. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: Accepted by the API — only the screen makes the column read-only (a gap). No server error.
cases.oracle: no 5xx; 2xx recorded as a gap.

cases.title: The buyer fills a column that belongs to the vendor
cases.why: A value the buyer puts in a vendor column could pre-fill or skew the vendor's bid.
cases.setup: A template with vendor columns.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with a value in a vendor column. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: No server error; whether the value is kept or ignored is recorded.
cases.oracle: no 5xx.

cases.title: A minimum quantity above the requested quantity is refused
cases.why: No vendor could meet a minimum larger than what is asked for.
cases.setup: A template with a minimum-quantity column.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with the minimum 1,000 above the requested quantity. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: Refused: "Floor Quantity cannot be greater than the Total Quantity".

cases.title: A value outside the limits the template sets on a column
cases.why: A template can set a minimum and maximum on a column; the screen puts the value back with the template's message.
cases.setup: A template whose column declares a min/max validation.
cases.steps: 1. Fill the column with one more than the maximum (or one less than the minimum). 2. Save.
cases.expected: Accepted by the API — only the screen stops it (a gap). No server error.
cases.oracle: no 5xx; 2xx recorded as a gap.

cases.section: The line item: product, unit, delivery location
cases.title: A line item without a delivery location is handled cleanly
cases.why: A missing delivery location once made a later event update fail with an unexplained server error on UAT.
cases.setup: A sandbox draft event.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with the delivery location left out. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: No server error; the server's answer is recorded (today: refused, "Delivery location not found").
cases.oracle: no 5xx.

cases.title: The vendor types text into a number column
cases.why: Text in a price or quantity breaks ranking.
cases.setup: A published round; the vendor has started a bid.
cases.steps: 1. Fill the line validly but with "abc" in a vendor number column. 2. Save the line.
cases.expected: No server error; an accepted value is recorded as a gap.
cases.oracle: no 5xx.

cases.title: The vendor sends a negative number
cases.why: A negative price or quantity would rank a bid first.
cases.setup: A published round; the vendor has started a bid.
cases.steps: 1. Fill the line validly but with −5 in a vendor number column. 2. Save the line.
cases.expected: No server error; an accepted value is recorded as a gap.
cases.oracle: no 5xx.

cases.title: The vendor changes a column that belongs to the buyer
cases.why: The requested quantity is the buyer's; a vendor changing it could make an offer look complete when it is not.
cases.setup: A published round; the vendor has started a bid.
cases.steps: 1. Fill the line validly but send the requested quantity 500 higher. 2. Save the line.
cases.expected: No server error; whether the change is kept or ignored is recorded.
cases.oracle: no 5xx.

cases.title: The vendor sends a value for a calculated column
cases.why: A vendor typing a total could make a bid look cheaper than it is.
cases.setup: A published round; the vendor has started a bid.
cases.steps: 1. Fill the line validly but with 999999 in the calculated total. 2. Save the line.
cases.expected: Accepted by the API — only the screen makes it read-only (a gap). No server error.
cases.oracle: no 5xx; 2xx recorded as a gap.

cases.title: A technical round with a page that has no name is refused cleanly
cases.why: Each page needs a name; a nameless page gives vendors a form nobody can navigate — and must be refused with a message, not a crash.
cases.setup: A sandbox draft event; a technical template.
cases.steps: 1. Add a technical round using the template with the first page's name removed. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: Refused: "Please fill all the required fields". Not a server error.
cases.oracle: 422, code 792; 5xx = defect.

cases.title: A technical round with a question that has no key is refused
cases.why: Answers are stored against the question's key; a keyless question cannot be answered or scored.
cases.setup: A sandbox draft event; a technical template.
cases.steps: 1. Add a technical round with the first question's key removed. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: Refused: "Please fill all the required fields".

cases.title: A technical round with a question that does not say who fills it is refused
cases.why: Each question must say whether the vendor or the buyer answers it.
cases.setup: A sandbox draft event; a technical template.
cases.steps: 1. Add a technical round with "who fills it" removed from the first question. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: Refused: "Please fill all the required fields".

cases.title: The vendor answers a question with a value outside its choices
cases.why: An answer outside the list breaks comparison and scoring.
cases.setup: A technical round with a choice question, published to the test vendor.
cases.steps: 1. Answer that question with "QA not an option" and every other question validly. 2. Submit.
cases.expected: Accepted by the API — only the screen stops it (a gap). No server error. A refusal because another required answer is missing is "couldn't tell".
cases.oracle: no 5xx.

cases.title: The vendor sends a value outside a column's choice list
cases.why: A dropdown offers only its listed values.
cases.setup: A template with a vendor dropdown column; a published round.
cases.steps: 1. Fill the line validly but with "QA not an option" in that column. 2. Save the line.
cases.expected: Accepted by the API — only the screen stops it (a gap). No server error.
cases.oracle: no 5xx; 2xx recorded as a gap.

cases.title: More decimals than a buyer column allows
cases.why: Columns carry a precision; extra decimals change totals by rounding.
cases.setup: A template whose buyer number column sets a precision.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with three more decimals than allowed. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: Accepted (the server only rewrites precision) — the screen rounds. No server error.
cases.oracle: no 5xx.

cases.title: Accented, Chinese, Japanese, emoji and HTML characters in a text column
cases.why: Buyers type names and specifications in many scripts; the save must not crash or mangle them.
cases.setup: A template with a buyer text column.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with that text in the column. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: No server error; the text is stored as sent.
cases.oracle: no 5xx.

cases.title: A very long text (about 5,200 characters) in a text column
cases.why: A pasted specification can be long; the save must not crash on it.
cases.setup: A template with a buyer text column.
cases.steps: 1. Add a pricing round with a 5,200-character text in the column. 2. Save it.
cases.expected: No server error.
cases.oracle: no 5xx.

cases.title: The vendor sends more decimals than a column allows
cases.why: Extra decimals change totals by rounding.
cases.setup: A published round; the vendor has started a bid.
cases.steps: 1. Fill the line validly but with three more decimals than allowed. 2. Save the line.
cases.expected: No server error.
cases.oracle: no 5xx.

journeys.title: Several vendors, bids on a vendor's behalf, and the clock
journeys.goal: Invite several vendors and have each bid through its own login; bid on a vendor's behalf only when the rules allow; keep the technical round inside the pricing round; refuse bids once the submission time is over, let them in again after an extension, and award by the rules.

cases.section: Several vendors bid through their own login
cases.title: Every invited vendor can open the event and bid
cases.why: Inviting three vendors is pointless if only the first one can actually see the event and bid.
cases.setup: Three QA vendors with an active link. A pricing round (RFQ) open for about three minutes with all three invited.
cases.steps: 1. Publish the event. 2. Sign in as each vendor in turn. 3. Each opens a bid, prices the line (₹100, ₹110, ₹120) and submits.
cases.expected: All three bids are accepted and submitted.
cases.oracle: Each vendor's open, price and submit calls succeed.

cases.section: The buyer bids on a vendor's behalf
cases.title: The buyer can bid for a vendor before bidding starts; the vendor cannot
cases.why: Surrogate bids are entered from paper quotes, often before the window opens; vendors themselves must wait for the start.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO or Demo Account 2. A pricing round that starts in about 80 seconds, three QA vendors invited.
cases.steps: 1. Before the start, enter a price on vendor 1's behalf. 2. Before the start, vendor 3 tries to open a bid.
cases.expected: The surrogate bid is accepted; vendor 3 is refused because bidding has not started.
cases.oracle: Surrogate call succeeds; vendor open refused with code 33.

cases.section: The buyer bids on a vendor's behalf
cases.title: The buyer cannot bid for a vendor who already bid
cases.why: A surrogate bid must never overwrite what the vendor submitted.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-010, after the start; vendor 3 has submitted its own bid.
cases.steps: 1. Enter a price on vendor 3's behalf.
cases.expected: Refused: the vendor has already bid.
cases.oracle: Refusal with code 96.

cases.section: The buyer bids on a vendor's behalf
cases.title: The buyer bids for a vendor that is not invited to the event (suspected defect)
cases.why: Only invited vendors should be in an event; code reading shows no audience check on the surrogate path.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-010; vendor 4 deals with the buyer but is not invited.
cases.steps: 1. Enter a price on vendor 4's behalf.
cases.expected: Refused. If accepted, the suspected defect is confirmed.
cases.oracle: Probe S7-NO-AUDIENCE-CHECK: accepted = defect confirmed.

cases.section: The buyer bids on a vendor's behalf
cases.title: The buyer cannot bid for a vendor after the bid end time
cases.why: The submission deadline applies to on-behalf bids too (no post-expiry setting on these clients).
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-010, after the bid end, during the extra closing time.
cases.steps: 1. Enter a price on vendor 2's behalf.
cases.expected: Refused: the submission time is over.
cases.oracle: Refusal with code 33.

cases.section: The buyer bids on a vendor's behalf
cases.title: A vendor cannot price the RFQ before answering the RFP
cases.why: The technical round gates the pricing round for invited vendors.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-018.
cases.steps: 1. Vendor 1 opens a bid on the pricing round before answering the technical round.
cases.expected: Refused: no technical response.
cases.oracle: Refusal with code 737.

cases.section: The buyer bids on a vendor's behalf
cases.title: A vendor enters a technical response for another company (suspected defect)
cases.why: A supplier must only answer for itself; the surrogate technical endpoint has no company check.
cases.setup: Technical round with two QA vendors invited.
cases.steps: 1. As vendor 1, send a technical response for vendor 2's company.
cases.expected: Refused. If accepted, the suspected defect is confirmed. Seen on PROCOL DEMO: refused by the app gate — the supplier app may not call this endpoint at all.
cases.oracle: Probe TECH-FOR-ANY-COMPANY.

cases.section: The clock: before, during, after, extended
cases.title: In the extra closing time a vendor cannot change its price
cases.why: "The vendor should not be able to submit a bid after submission time is over."
cases.setup: A pricing round whose bid end has passed and whose extra closing time is still running; two vendors bid earlier.
cases.steps: 1. Vendor 1 opens a bid. 2. Prices the line. 3. Submits.
cases.expected: A draft may open; pricing is refused (508) or submitting is refused (33). The price never changes.
cases.oracle: Open: accepted or 33; price: 508 or 33; submit: 33.

cases.section: The clock: before, during, after, extended
cases.title: After the extra closing time a vendor cannot even open a bid
cases.why: Once the event is closed nothing should start a bid.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-030, after the extra closing time.
cases.steps: 1. Vendor 2 opens a bid.
cases.expected: Refused: the order is not active.
cases.oracle: Refusal with code 33.

cases.section: The clock: before, during, after, extended
cases.title: Extending the submission time reopens bidding
cases.why: "There is sometimes an option to extend submission time, then you can place the bid."
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO (users may reopen events). A closed pricing round where vendor 1 bid and vendor 2 did not.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, extend the bid end by about two minutes. 2. Read the round's times back. 3. Vendor 2 bids. 4. Vendor 1 revises.
cases.expected: The extension is accepted, the bid end moves and the extra closing time follows it; both bids are accepted.
cases.oracle: Trade PATCH succeeds; bid end ≈ the new time; vendor calls succeed.

cases.section: The clock: before, during, after, extended
cases.title: An event whose technical round ends after its pricing round cannot be published
cases.why: Business rule: the RFP's end must not exceed the RFQ's.
cases.setup: Technical round ending about 90 seconds after the pricing round.
cases.steps: 1. Publish the event.
cases.expected: Refused: the RFP duration exceeds the RFQ end time.
cases.oracle: Refusal with code 712.

cases.section: The clock: before, during, after, extended
cases.title: Extending only the technical round past the pricing round is refused
cases.why: The same rule holds after publishing.
cases.setup: A live event whose technical round ends before its pricing round.
cases.steps: 1. Extend the technical round to two minutes after the pricing round's end.
cases.expected: Refused (712).
cases.oracle: Refusal with code 712.

cases.title: After converting an RFQ to an auction the vendor bids in the auction before the award
cases.why: The award goes to a vendor of the latest round; without an auction bid it is refused (826).
cases.setup: The RFQ-then-auction journey.
cases.steps: 1. The vendor bids on the RFQ. 2. The buyer converts the round to an auction. 3. The vendor bids in the auction. 4. The buyer awards.
cases.expected: The auction bid and the award are accepted.
cases.oracle: convert_auction step (with its auction bid) and award succeed; no 826.

cases.title: Submitting an evaluation that leaves a responding vendor unscored is refused
cases.why: If one of two responses could be skipped, a vendor could be dropped from the technical shortlist without ever being judged.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-061, after the technical round's bid end.
cases.steps: 1. The evaluator scores vendor 1's response (the top score on the event's scale). 2. The evaluator submits the evaluation.
cases.expected: The score is recorded; the submit is refused because vendor 2 also responded and has no score yet (“Please, evaluate on all fields”).
cases.oracle: Score accepted; submit refused with code 571.

cases.title: Once every response is scored the evaluation is submitted
cases.why: This is the normal end of a technical evaluation with several vendors.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-062.
cases.steps: 1. The evaluator scores vendor 2's response (the lowest accepted score on the event's scale). 2. The evaluator submits the evaluation.
cases.expected: Accepted. The result comes back as a proposal: “draft” where an approval flow applies (Demo Account 2), “selected” otherwise (PROCOL DEMO).
cases.oracle: Both calls succeed; proposal status draft or selected.

cases.section: The buyer edits a vendor's bid
cases.title: The buyer can change a buyer-editable price while bidding is open
cases.why: This is the edit the setting exists for.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-066.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, change vendor 1's price to ₹95. 2. Read vendor 1's active bid back.
cases.expected: Accepted. The vendor's active bid is a new bid at ₹95 (the old one is kept as revised).
cases.oracle: HTTP 200; the active bid's price (database read) equals ₹95.

cases.section: Several vendors bid through their own login
cases.title: The buyer sees the lowest price as the best bid
cases.why: The comparison a buyer awards from must point at the cheapest vendor.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-001, after all three bids.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, open the event's comparison (indicators and line prices).
cases.expected: The ₹100 vendor is marked best bidder, the other two are not; the line's lowest (L1) price is ₹100.
cases.oracle: event_indicators best_bidder flag per vendor; schema l1_prices.

cases.section: Several vendors bid through their own login
cases.title: A vendor does not see its own rank on an RFQ
cases.why: In a sealed RFQ a vendor must not learn where it stands; ranks are for auctions only.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-001.
cases.steps: 1. As the ₹100 vendor, open the pricing round.
cases.expected: The vendor's view carries no rank.
cases.oracle: No rank value in the vendor's trade view.

cases.section: Several vendors bid through their own login
cases.title: An award can be split across three vendors
cases.why: Splitting a line between suppliers is common; with partial awarding on it must be accepted.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO (partial awarding on). The round and its extra closing time have ended.
cases.steps: 1. Open an award proposal. 2. Award 10 of 30 to each vendor. 3. Submit it into its approval workflow.
cases.expected: The three-way award is accepted and submitted.
cases.oracle: add_response and submit succeed.

cases.section: Several vendors bid through their own login
cases.title: Over-award with a stated quantity when partial awarding is off (suspected gap)
cases.why: Code reading suggests the quantity check is skipped when a quantity is sent and partial awarding is off, so twice the line could be awarded.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-006.
cases.steps: 1. Open a proposal. 2. Award the full quantity to vendor 1. 3. Also award the full quantity to vendor 2, stating it (twice the line in total). 4. Leave the proposal unsubmitted.
cases.expected: Refused (the total exceeds the line). If accepted, the suspected gap is confirmed.
cases.oracle: Probe AWARD-QTY-GAP: accepted = defect confirmed.

cases.section: The buyer bids on a vendor's behalf
cases.title: A second surrogate bid for the same vendor is refused
cases.why: Without the "revise surrogate bid" setting, the buyer must not replace an on-behalf bid.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-010; a surrogate bid exists for vendor 1.
cases.steps: 1. Enter another price on vendor 1's behalf.
cases.expected: Refused: a bid is already placed on this vendor's behalf.
cases.oracle: Refusal with code 99.

cases.section: The buyer bids on a vendor's behalf
cases.title: A vendor can revise the bid the buyer entered for it
cases.why: The vendor stays in control of its own price once it signs in.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-012.
cases.steps: 1. Sign in as vendor 1. 2. Open a bid, price it lower and submit.
cases.expected: The vendor's revision is accepted.
cases.oracle: Vendor open, price and submit succeed.

cases.section: The buyer bids on a vendor's behalf
cases.title: The buyer cannot bid for a company it does not deal with
cases.why: A buyer must not create bids for strangers.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-010; a QA vendor of the other demo client.
cases.steps: 1. Enter a price on that company's behalf.
cases.expected: Refused: not allowed.
cases.oracle: Refusal with code 101.

cases.section: The buyer bids on a vendor's behalf
cases.title: A surrogate price without a technical response (suspected gap)
cases.why: A vendor cannot price an RFQ without answering the RFP; the surrogate path has no such check.
cases.setup: Technical round and pricing round, two QA vendors; vendor 2 never answers the technical round.
cases.steps: 1. Enter a price on vendor 2's behalf on the pricing round.
cases.expected: Refused like the vendor path (737). If accepted, the gap is confirmed.
cases.oracle: Probe S11-NO-TECH-CHECK.

cases.section: The buyer bids on a vendor's behalf
cases.title: The buyer cannot enter a technical response over the vendor's own
cases.why: The vendor's submitted answers must not be overwritten.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-018; vendor 1 has submitted its technical response.
cases.steps: 1. Enter a technical response on vendor 1's behalf.
cases.expected: Refused: an active response exists.
cases.oracle: Refusal with code 30.

cases.section: The clock: before, during, after, extended
cases.title: Reopening an expired round is refused where the client does not allow it
cases.why: Only some clients let users reopen an expired event.
cases.setup: Demo Account 2 (reopen not allowed). A closed pricing round.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, extend the bid end.
cases.expected: Refused: reopening is not allowed.
cases.oracle: Refusal with code 496.

cases.section: The clock: before, during, after, extended
cases.title: A bid revised after it was put on a proposal blocks the proposal
cases.why: The buyer must not approve a price the vendor has since changed.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-032, bidding open again; vendor 1's bid is added to a proposal.
cases.steps: 1. Vendor 1 revises. 2. The buyer submits the proposal.
cases.expected: The submit is refused because the bid changed. Seen on PROCOL DEMO (1 Oct 2026): the revision takes the old bid off the proposal, so the refusal is "Proposal cannot be empty. Please award the vendors again." (683) rather than 1126 — either way the changed price cannot be approved.
cases.oracle: Refusal with code 1126 or 683.

cases.section: The clock: before, during, after, extended
cases.title: The time cannot be extended once a proposal exists
cases.why: Reopening bidding under an award in progress would let prices change under it.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-034.
cases.steps: 1. Extend the bid end again.
cases.expected: Refused because a proposal exists (801). Seen on PROCOL DEMO (1 Oct 2026): refused by the RFQ-changes guard instead, whose message — "You cannot edit rfq once the auction is created" (769) — names an auction the event does not have. Misleading message; 801 is never reached for an RFQ in an event project.
cases.oracle: Refusal with code 801 or 769; 769's wording is the defect.

cases.section: The clock: before, during, after, extended
cases.title: Extending the technical round together with the pricing round is accepted
cases.why: The supported way to give more time to both rounds.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-037.
cases.steps: 1. Extend the technical round with "extend the pricing round too". 2. Read the pricing round's end.
cases.expected: Accepted; the pricing round now ends at or after the new technical end.
cases.oracle: PATCH succeeds; pricing round bid end ≥ the new time.

cases.title: In an English auction a price that does not beat the best is refused
cases.why: Each new bidder must beat the current best price.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO. An auction round with three QA vendors; vendor 1 bid ₹100.
cases.steps: 1. Vendor 2 bids ₹100. 2. Vendor 2 bids ₹99. 3. The buyer enters ₹100 for vendor 3.
cases.expected: ₹100 from vendor 2 is accepted as a tie or refused (38); ₹99 is accepted; ₹100 for vendor 3 is refused (38) only when the line has a ceiling price — the English-auction rule (best − tick) is applied only then (trade_product.rb:170). The matrix's rounds set no ceiling price, so ₹100 is accepted there.
cases.oracle: Codes 38 / 98 as listed; vendor 2 sees rank 1.

cases.title: A QA vendor invited with "skip onboarding" lands active and can sign in
cases.why: Multi-vendor tests need safe vendors; this is the path that gives an active link and a working login.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO or Demo Account 2; a new qa_…@example.com address.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, invite the vendor with "skip vendor onboarding". 2. Sign in as the vendor with the emailed code. 3. Complete the vendor signup. 4. Read the link, membership and invitation. 5. Sign in again.
cases.expected: Link active after the invite; after signup the user belongs to the invited company and the invitation is accepted; both sign-ins work.
cases.oracle: buyer_seller_company_mappings status 1; user_company_mappings active; invitations status accepted.

cases.title: The evaluator cannot score while the technical round is still open
cases.why: Scores given before every vendor has had the chance to answer would judge an incomplete round.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO or Demo Account 2. A technical round (open about 75 seconds) followed by a pricing round, three QA vendors invited; vendors 1 and 2 have submitted their technical responses. The evaluator named on the technical round is signed in.
cases.steps: 1. Before the technical round's bid end, the evaluator scores vendor 1's response with a score from the event's own scale.
cases.expected: Refused: evaluation opens only after the technical round's bid end. (The app's message, “Order not active”, does not say that; the wording is misleading.)
cases.oracle: Code 33.

cases.title: A vendor that never responded cannot be scored
cases.why: A score for a vendor with no answer would be invented data.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-062; vendor 3 was invited to the technical round and did not respond.
cases.steps: 1. The evaluator scores vendor 3.
cases.expected: Refused: there is no response from this vendor to score.
cases.oracle: Code 101.

cases.section: The buyer edits a vendor's bid
cases.title: Saving a vendor's bid without changing anything is refused
cases.why: An "edit" that changes nothing would still create a new revision and a buyer-edit label on the vendor's bid.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO. A pricing round open about 100 seconds with an extra closing time of 60 seconds; on this QA round only, the price field is marked buyer-editable. Vendor 1 bid ₹100, vendor 2 bid ₹110.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, save vendor 1's bid with exactly the same values.
cases.expected: Refused: “No changes found”.
cases.oracle: Code 758.

cases.section: The buyer edits a vendor's bid
cases.title: The buyer cannot change a field that is not buyer-editable
cases.why: Only the fields the template hands to the buyer may be changed on a vendor's bid; the rest is the vendor's own word.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-066.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, add 18% GST to vendor 1's bid (GST is not buyer-editable).
cases.expected: Refused: “You can only edit the buyer editable fields.”
cases.oracle: Code 747.

cases.section: The buyer edits a vendor's bid
cases.title: The buyer can still edit in the extra closing time
cases.why: The extra closing time is the window for clean-up after bidding ends; buyer edits are meant to be allowed there.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-068, after the bid end and before the end of the extra closing time.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, change vendor 1's price to ₹92. 2. Read the active bid back.
cases.expected: Accepted; the active bid is now ₹92.
cases.oracle: HTTP 200; active bid price ₹92.

cases.section: The buyer edits a vendor's bid
cases.title: The buyer cannot edit once the extra closing time is over
cases.why: After the round has fully closed, bids must stay as they are for evaluation and award.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-069, after the extra closing time.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, change vendor 1's price to ₹90.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: Code 101.

cases.title: A last-minute bid that changes first place extends the auction by one minute
cases.why: Dynamic closing stops vendors from sniping at the last second: a rank-changing bid near the end gives the others time to answer.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO or Demo Account 2. An auction round (rank based) open about 200 seconds with dynamic closing on: trigger the last 1 minute, extension 1 minute, rank limit 1. Vendor 2 bid ₹110, then vendor 1 bid ₹100.
cases.steps: 1. Inside the last minute, vendor 2 bids ₹95 (takes first place). 2. Read the bid end. 3. After the original bid end, vendor 1 bids ₹90.
cases.expected: The bid end moves out by one minute; vendor 1's bid after the original end is accepted (and, again changing first place in the last minute, extends the end by another minute).
cases.oracle: Bid end read back +60 s (±5 s); vendor 1's open, price and submit succeed.

cases.section: Several vendors bid through their own login
cases.title: Two equal best prices are both shown as best
cases.why: With a tie, the buyer must see both vendors as best rather than one picked silently.
cases.setup: Demo Account 2, two QA vendors, both bid ₹100.
cases.steps: 1. Both vendors bid the same price. 2. As the buyer, open the comparison.
cases.expected: Both vendors are marked best bidder; L1 price ₹100.
cases.oracle: best_bidder flags.

cases.section: Several vendors bid through their own login
cases.title: An award line sent without a quantity awards nothing, yet the proposal can be submitted
cases.why: A buyer who leaves the quantity out should be told so; an award worth ₹0 should not go to approval.
cases.setup: Demo Account 2 (partial awarding off). Two vendors each quoted the full quantity; the round has ended.
cases.steps: 1. Open a proposal. 2. Add both vendors with no quantity on the line. 3. Submit.
cases.expected: Seen on 1 Oct 2026: both adds and the submit were accepted, and the proposal's awarded value is ₹0 (no quantity was awarded). Desired: refused — either "award a quantity" or, if the quoted quantities are meant, 561 because together they exceed the line.
cases.oracle: add_response and submit status; proposals.meta_data total_l1_proposal + total_non_l1_proposal = 0.

cases.section: The buyer bids on a vendor's behalf
cases.title: The buyer cannot use the vendor's own bid endpoint
cases.why: Buyers must go through the surrogate path, which records who entered the bid.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-010.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, call the vendor's "open a bid" request for vendor 2.
cases.expected: Refused — either by the app gate (the web console may not call the supplier API) or by the bid guard. Seen on both demo clients: the app gate refuses ("This app is not authorized to use this API"), and the buyer's web-console session stops working right after (the next request answers "Authentication failed").
cases.oracle: Refusal with app_error_auth_failed or code 33; the run reopens a fresh buyer session afterwards.

cases.section: The clock: before, during, after, extended
cases.title: Awarding while bidding is still open (suspected, possibly intended)
cases.why: Awards are blocked during bidding only when a setting is on, which no client has.
cases.setup: Demo Account 2. A pricing round open for four minutes; one vendor bid.
cases.steps: 1. While the round is open, open a proposal and award the vendor.
cases.expected: Refused while bidding is open (720) — unless that is intended.
cases.oracle: Probe AWARD-DURING-BIDDING.

cases.section: The clock: before, during, after, extended
cases.title: A best-price request for one vendor lets another vendor revise (suspected)
cases.why: A window opened for vendor 1 only should not let vendor 2 in.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO. A closed pricing round with two bids.
cases.steps: 1. Ask vendor 1 only for a best price for two minutes. 2. Vendor 2 opens a bid.
cases.expected: Vendor 2 is refused. If accepted, the restriction is UI-only.
cases.oracle: Probe REVIEW-WINDOW-UI-ONLY.

cases.title: A declined invitation does not stop a bid (suspected); a decline needs a reason
cases.why: A vendor that declined should not appear as a bidder; a decline without a reason is refused.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO, a live pricing round with two QA vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Vendor 1 declines with no reason. 2. Declines with a reason. 3. Opens a bid.
cases.expected: No reason: refused (2). With a reason: recorded. The bid after declining should be refused; if accepted, the decline is not enforced.
cases.oracle: Code 2; probe DECLINE-NOT-ENFORCED.

cases.section: The buyer edits a vendor's bid
cases.title: Buyer edits are only tried where the company allows them
cases.why: Where the company has switched buyer edits off, every edit is refused and the edit cases say nothing new.
cases.setup: Demo Account 2 (the setting “buyer can edit a vendor's bid” is off there).
cases.steps: 1. Read the company's settings.
cases.expected: The buyer-edit cases are skipped with the reason stated. On PROCOL DEMO the setting is on and is copied onto each new pricing round.
cases.oracle: Dashboard configuration can_buyer_edit_bid; the round's trade_config.can_buyer_edit_bid.

cases.section: The buyer edits a vendor's bid
cases.title: A cost-breakdown request is answered through the normal bid; another vendor can also revise (suspected)
