cases.why: The design asked whether vendors send a cost breakdown through a call of its own. They do not: they re-bid. And a window opened for one vendor should not let a second vendor in.
cases.setup: As API-XMAT-070 (the round is closed).
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, ask vendor 1 only for a cost breakdown, for two minutes. 2. Vendor 1 opens a bid, prices it and submits. 3. Vendor 2 (not asked) opens a bid, prices it and submits.
cases.expected: Steps 1 and 2 are accepted. Step 3 should be refused; if it is accepted, the one-vendor restriction exists only in the screens.
cases.oracle: HTTP 200 for steps 1–2; probe CBD-WINDOW-UI-ONLY on step 3.

cases.title: Extending the submission time also moves the end time stored on bids already placed
cases.why: Bids carry their own end time (shown to vendors as "valid till"); a stale value would say the bid had expired while the round is open again.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO or Demo Account 2. A closed pricing round where vendor 1 bid before the close.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, extend the submission time. 2. Read vendor 1's bid back.
cases.expected: The bid's stored end time equals the round's new bid end.
cases.oracle: bids.end_time (database read) within 5 seconds of the new bid end.

cases.title: A dynamic-closing trigger longer than half the remaining time is refused when the auction is created
cases.why: A trigger of two minutes on a three-minute auction would make every bid an extension.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO or Demo Account 2. A draft event.
cases.steps: 1. Add an auction round with dynamic closing on, a trigger of the last 2 minutes and a 3-minute window.
cases.expected: Refused: “Invalid Trigger Time for Dynamic Time Extension.”
cases.oracle: Code 501.

journeys.title: Comparing quotes: L1, savings and the comparison sheet
journeys.goal: After the bids are in, read the comparison the way a buyer does — who is L1 on each line and overall, what was saved against which baseline, what the sealed-bid rules hide before the close — and export it, with nothing shown that the buyer may not see.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: The savings card appears only when the stage has savings and bids are not masked
cases.why: The comparison asks for aggregate savings only when `savings_configuration` is an object and `trade_config.show_bidding_stats` is false — a stage relying only on custom savings never shows its savings.
cases.setup: Three stages: (a) lot-based savings with a Budget reference; (b) no savings configuration but company custom savings on; (c) as (a) while masked for the viewer.
cases.steps: Open each stage's comparison as the buyer; watch the network tab for `/aggregate_savings`.
cases.expected: (a) Savings card with Budget amount and %. (b) No call, no card (gap vs API-XDQCS-014). (c) No call, no card until bid end.
cases.oracle: Presence of the request and of the card.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: Lot savings show one row per savings basis, with a sane percentage
cases.why: Each strategy (Budget, Historical, Existing Proposal, Last Purchase Price, Default) is rendered from savings_amount / savings_percent; a 0 reference produces 'Infinity%' text today.
cases.setup: Lot-based savings with Budget = 1,00,000 and Last Purchase Price left at 0; one bid of 90,000.
cases.steps: Open the stage; hover the savings card.
cases.expected: Budget: ₹10,000 (10%). Last Purchase Price: blank or 0% — never 'Infinity%' / 'NaN%'.
cases.oracle: Rendered strings in the savings card.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: The L1 vendor is highlighted per line in the comparison, including ties
cases.why: The green L1 highlight comes from `event_indicators` best_bidder per line. On a tie both vendors are highlighted, and the rank shown is 2 for both (rank shift).
cases.setup: RFQ with three vendors; vendors A and B tie at the lowest price on line 1; C cheapest on line 2.
cases.steps: Open the comparison as the buyer.
cases.expected: Line 1: A and B highlighted as best bidder, rank label 2 for both; line 2: C highlighted. Confirm the tie is explained (tooltip/badge).
cases.oracle: Highlight per cell vs API-XDQCS-032.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: 'Unlock bids' is offered only for locked RFQs after bid end
cases.why: The settings menu shows 'Unlock bids' only when `lock_bid_by_default` is on, the stage is a trade stage, and status is buffer; it is disabled in view-only dashboards, old versions and on-hold projects.
cases.setup: Client `lock_bid_by_default` ON; RFQ live, then past bid end.
cases.steps: Open the stage settings menu during live and after bid end; repeat in a view-only dashboard.
cases.expected: Live: no menu item. Buffer: item present. View-only/old version/on hold: present but disabled.
cases.oracle: Menu item visibility/disabled state.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: Unlock bids modal guides the finance-user OTP flow
cases.why: Send OTP stays disabled until a finance user is chosen; Verify needs a 6-digit OTP; the visibility choice (Everyone / Only me) comes from `unlock_bids_restriction_options`.
cases.setup: Client `lock_bid_by_default` ON; RFQ in buffer; (a) company with finance users, (b) without.
cases.steps: Open Unlock bids; choose user; send OTP; type 5 digits then 6.
cases.expected: (a) Users listed with name and email; Verify enabled only at 6 digits; success unlocks the grid. (b) 'No finance users found', Send disabled.
cases.oracle: Button states; grid visible after success.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: 'Download logs' is visible only to Procol staff and never on RFP stages
cases.why: `trade_config.can_download_logs` = Procol employee and not RFP; client buyers must never see it (the API refuses them — API-XDQCS-076).
cases.setup: Same RFQ viewed by a client buyer and by a Procol support user; also an RFP stage.
cases.steps: Open the settings menu.
cases.expected: Client buyer: no 'Download logs'. Procol user on RFQ: present, opens the logs modal and a file. RFP stage: absent for everyone.
cases.oracle: Menu item presence; modal opens fileUrl.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: Master QCS 'Start awarding' is disabled with the right reason
cases.why: Awarding is blocked while any stage (of the lot) is draft, when this is not the latest version, when the project is on hold, or when the lot is not awardable; the tooltip must say which.
cases.setup: Event with (a) a draft stage, (b) an older version open, (c) lot not yet closed, (d) everything closed.
cases.steps: Open the Master QCS tab and hover 'Start awarding'.
cases.expected: (a) disabled — 'event not yet published' text; (b) 'Awarding is only allowed for the latest version'; (c) live-events text; (d) enabled.
cases.oracle: Button state + tooltip text.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: Master QCS 'Download Report' exports the master QCS of the current lot
cases.why: From the project's Master QCS tab the button posts `/reports/download_report` with item_type event_group, report_category master_qcs_report and the lot; with locked bids the API answers 831.
cases.setup: Event with two lots and bids; then the same with bids locked.
cases.steps: Open Master QCS for lot 2; click Download Report.
cases.expected: A file for lot 2 only. Locked bids: an error toast 'Unlock Bid to Download Report', no file.
cases.oracle: Request body (lot_no 2); downloaded content; toast text.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: Each lot has its own Master QCS showing only that lot's stages and proposal
cases.why: Per-lot tabs filter stages and proposals by lot_no; a proposal of lot 1 must never appear in lot 2's QCS.
cases.setup: Event split into 2 lots; lot 1 awarded.
cases.steps: Open Master QCS for lot 1 and lot 2.
cases.expected: Lot 1 shows its proposal status tag; lot 2 shows no proposal and its own vendors/lines only.
cases.oracle: Proposal tag and lines per tab.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: A masked buyer sees no savings and no unread-chat count during live bidding
cases.why: `show_bidding_stats` hides savings and the unresolved-chat badge for masked buyers; both return after bid end.
cases.setup: Client `event_masking_on_rfqs` ON; non-owner, non-super-admin buyer; live RFQ with bids.
cases.steps: Open the stage as that buyer; then after bid end.
cases.expected: Live: no savings card, no chat count, bids masked. After end: both visible.
cases.oracle: Card/badge presence.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: Line-wise savings table appears only for line-item savings
cases.why: The LineItemSavings table renders only when `savingsComparisonOn` is line-item; lot savings must not also produce a per-line table.
cases.setup: Two stages: line-item savings and lot savings, both with bids.
cases.steps: Open each stage's details panel.
cases.expected: Line-item stage: a table with one row per line and the best vendor's saving. Lot stage: no table.
cases.oracle: Table presence and rows.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: A technical (RFP) stage tab does not show price ranks
cases.why: The screen calls event_indicators for every stage whose rfx_mode is not 'rfi', which includes RFP stages.
cases.setup: RFP+RFQ event with responses on the RFP stage.
cases.steps: Open the RFP stage tab; watch for `/event_indicators`.
cases.expected: No rank/best-price badges on technical responses; no error toast.
cases.oracle: Badges and toasts on the RFP tab.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: Rejected bids modal: empty state and currency
cases.why: The modal shows each rejected bid with its total; in multi-currency stages the toggle 'Show in native currency' switches currency and precision.
cases.setup: (a) Stage with no rejected bids. (b) Multi-currency stage where a USD bid was rejected.
cases.steps: Open 'Rejected bids' from the comparison.
cases.expected: (a) Empty illustration with the 'no rejected bids' text. (b) INR amount by default; USD with USD precision when native currency is on.
cases.oracle: Modal content.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: 'Download bid template' appears only when the client enables it and never on RFP/RFI
cases.why: Gate: `show_bid_template_download_button_on_client_side` AND not RFP/RFI (PROCOL DEMO: OFF).
cases.setup: Client with the setting ON and OFF; an RFQ and an RFP stage.
cases.steps: Open the stage header.
cases.expected: ON + RFQ: button present, downloads an Excel. OFF or RFP/RFI: no button.
cases.oracle: Button presence; downloaded file.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: The Leaderboard tab exists only for alternate-bidding stages and refreshes itself
cases.why: The tab is filtered out unless `isAlternateBiddingAllowed`; when shown it polls the leader board.
cases.setup: Two RFQs: alternate bidding ON and OFF.
cases.steps: Open both stages; on the ON stage leave the Leaderboard tab open and add a bid from another session.
cases.expected: OFF: no tab. ON: tab lists ranked alternatives and updates without reload.
cases.oracle: Tab presence; row update.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: Counter-offer drawer marks the L1 line and loads L1 data for bulk percent offers
cases.why: The legend 'L1 bid on a line item' explains the highlight; for bulk counter offers in percent the drawer loads `l1_data_for_event` to compute targets.
cases.setup: Live RFQ with two vendors; bulk counter offer with percentage allowed.
cases.steps: Open the counter-offer drawer for one vendor, then the bulk counter-offer drawer.
cases.expected: Single: L1 cells highlighted with the legend. Bulk %: values computed from the L1 vendor's line values; no error toast when no bids yet.
cases.oracle: Highlighted cells; network call to `/l1_data_for_event`.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: Paged BOQ quote opened from a proposal keeps the proposal snapshot
cases.why: `getBidForVendor` appends `?proposal_uuid=` with a second '?' when paging filters are present, so the backend never sees proposal_uuid and the paged quote shows live data instead of the proposal snapshot.
cases.setup: BOQ RFP with tabs, an approved proposal, and a later re-evaluation.
cases.steps: From the proposal, open a vendor's quote and switch to page 2 of a tab.
cases.expected: Page 2 still shows the proposal snapshot. **Suspected defect:** URL like `?tab=0&page=2?proposal_uuid=…`.
cases.oracle: Request URL in the network tab; values vs snapshot.

cases.section: Screens — comparison, savings, sealed bids, Master QCS
cases.title: Vendor names are masked in the comparison while vendor masking is on
cases.why: With `is_vendor_masking_enabled` the comparison, rejected bids and remarks show generic vendor labels during the event for non-super-admins.
cases.setup: Stage with vendor masking ON; live; non-super-admin buyer.
cases.steps: Open comparison, rejected bids modal and remarks.
cases.expected: Generic labels everywhere during live; real names after close (or for super admin when 'everyone except super admin').
cases.oracle: Displayed names.

cases.section: When a technical round closes itself
cases.title: An RFI should not close when the first vendor's evaluation is submitted
cases.why: The RFI closes itself as soon as any one evaluation is active, so evaluators of the other vendors are locked out.
cases.setup: RFI with three QA vendors' responses and their evaluations in draft.
cases.steps: Submit the evaluation of vendor 1; try to submit vendor 2's.
cases.expected: The RFI status becomes closed (closing time = now) right after vendor 1's evaluation; vendor 2's submission then meets a closed round.
cases.oracle: `Evaluation#close_trade_request` after every save (`evaluation.rb:36, 40-48`) → `is_evaluated?` for RFI = any active evaluation (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:1281-1282`). Round status in the stage read.

cases.section: When a technical round closes itself
cases.title: A line-level RFP should not close until every vendor on every line is scored
cases.why: The RFP closes (and its evaluation window ends) when each line has a score from one vendor, while other vendors on the same lines are still unscored — they then go to the price round without a technical verdict.
cases.setup: RFP with line-level scoring, 2 lines, vendors A and B responded.
cases.steps: Score A on both lines; read the round; then try to score B.
cases.expected: After A's two scores the round is closed, closing time now, and the evaluation window ends now.
cases.oracle: `check_if_eglis_evaluated` needs one vendor with `evaluation_score` per line (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:1305-1330`); `EvaluationScore#update_trade` closes and ends the extra closing schedule (`evaluation_score.rb:151-164`).

cases.title: Publishing an amendment closes every open round of the previous version
cases.why: Vendors must not keep bidding on the old version once the new one is live.
cases.setup: Event with a technical round, an RFQ, an auction from it and a lot round, all open; PR items linked.
cases.steps: Publish an amendment; immediately bid on each old round as the QA vendor; read the old rounds and the PR links.
cases.expected: Only the old version's last technical round and latest non-lot price round are force-closed (the earlier RFQ and the lot round stay open), and the close runs in a background job, so bids are accepted until it runs.
cases.oracle: `update_previous_version_data` (`event_group.rb:703-709` → `Versions::EventGroupWorker`); `versions/event_group.rb:91-113` closes `[rfp, latest_non_lot_commercial_stage]` only; PR links `:116-210`, `event_group_line_item.rb:277-294`. Skipped for recurring templates and events with no previous version.

cases.title: A team buyer who is not the owner cannot see savings while an RFQ is still live
cases.why: Event masking on RFQs is the client's promise that nobody but the owner/super admin sees price movement during bidding. Savings is price movement.
cases.setup: Company setting `event_masking_on_rfqs` ON (PROCOL DEMO: ON). A second buyer of the same company who is neither super admin nor shared as owner. Sandbox RFQ live with at least one bid. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: 1. Log in as the second buyer. 2. `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/aggregate_savings`. 3. Repeat `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/best_line_wise_savings`.
cases.expected: Both refused: HTTP 422 code 577 'Savings will be visible after bidding ends'. After the bid end time both answer 200.
cases.oracle: 422 + 577 during bidding; 200 after close.

cases.title: A vendor cannot read the buyer's savings
cases.why: Savings reveal the buyer's budget / last purchase price. A vendor who knows the reference knows how far to push.
cases.setup: Vendor invited to the sandbox RFQ, logged in with a vendor session. No runnable twin: needs a vendor session.
cases.steps: As the vendor: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/aggregate_savings` and `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/best_line_wise_savings`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action' — the policy requires the stage's company to be one of the caller's companies.
cases.oracle: 422 + 455 for both.

cases.title: An invited vendor cannot read the L1 competitor's prices
cases.why: `l1_data_for_event?` is only `show?` and validate_event lets any invited vendor view the stage. The response contains the L1 vendor's negotiable values per line — during a live sealed RFQ that is the competitor's price.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ live with two vendors' bids; caller is the other (non-L1) invited vendor with a vendor session. No runnable twin: needs a vendor session.
cases.steps: As vendor B: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/l1_data_for_event`.
cases.expected: Refused (expected 455 or `{}`). **Suspected defect:** the code returns the L1 vendor's line values to vendor B.
cases.oracle: Response must not contain vendor A's price values.

cases.title: An invited vendor cannot get competitors' L1 prices through the schema
cases.why: `l1_prices` is computed for any caller who can view the stage and the serializer always emits it — no team-order or masking check. A vendor adding `l1_prices=true` to the schema call they already make sees the lowest price and line total of the market during a sealed RFQ.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ live; vendor A and vendor B have bid; caller is vendor B (vendor session). No runnable twin: needs a vendor session.
cases.steps: As vendor B: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/schema?response_type=template&l1_prices=true`.
cases.expected: `l1_prices` absent or empty for a vendor. **Suspected P0 leak:** it contains vendor A's price/total_amount per line.
cases.oracle: l1_prices content in vendor B's response.

cases.title: A real bid cannot be opened through a different stage
cases.why: Quote ids must be scoped to the stage in the URL — otherwise anyone who can view stage X could read a bid from stage Y.
cases.setup: `{{bidUuid}}` belongs to the journey RFQ; `{{tradeId}}` is the sandbox RFQ (different event).
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/quote_details/{{bidUuid}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 32 'Bid not found' (lookup is by bid id AND stage id).

cases.title: A vendor cannot open another vendor's quote
cases.why: `can_view_bid?` allows the bid's own user, the client's team, or the bid's company/broker. A competitor must get 'Bid not found'.
cases.setup: Two vendors bid; caller is vendor B (vendor session); quote id = vendor A's bid. No runnable twin: needs a vendor session.
cases.steps: As vendor B: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/quote_details/<vendor A bid uuid>`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 32 'Bid not found'.

cases.section: Sealed bids — masking, bid lock, unlock OTP, bid visibility
cases.title: A wrong OTP never unlocks bids
cases.why: Guessing must not open sealed bids.
cases.setup: `lock_bid_by_default` OFF; run's own buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/verify_otp_for_unlocking_bids` with body `{"user_uuid": "{{buyerUserUuid}}", "otp": "000000", "bid_visibility": "everyone"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 10 'You are not allowed to use this functionality' (not finance / not locked). With locking on and a finance user: 422 code 6 'Invalid OTP'. Visibility unchanged.

cases.section: Sealed bids — masking, bid lock, unlock OTP, bid visibility
cases.title: While bids are locked every price read is masked; 'self' unlocks only for one user
cases.why: Locked bids must be consistent across savings, schema, report and quote reads; 'self' must not unlock for colleagues.
cases.setup: `lock_bid_by_default` ON; bids in; then unlock with `bid_visibility: self` by buyer X via a finance user. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: Before unlock (any buyer): aggregate_savings, quote_details, download_report. After unlock: repeat as buyer X and as buyer Y.
cases.expected: Before: 577 / 32 / 831 'Unlock Bid to Download Report'. After: X sees everything; Y still masked. With 'everyone': both see.
cases.oracle: Status codes per user before/after.

cases.section: Exports — bid template, comparison report, vendor logs, master QCS regeneration
cases.title: A vendor cannot download a competitor's bid through the bid template
cases.why: `company_uuid` is taken from the request without checking it is the caller's company, and the Excel is pre-filled with that company's latest bid — including DRAFT bids. Policy is only 'can view the event', which every invited vendor passes.
cases.setup: Two invited vendors; vendor A has a draft or submitted bid; caller is vendor B (vendor session). No runnable twin: needs a vendor session.
cases.steps: As vendor B: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/download_event_details?company_uuid=<vendor A company uuid>`; open the Excel.
cases.expected: Refused, or the Excel contains only B's data. **Suspected P0 leak:** the Excel contains A's prices.
cases.oracle: Excel cell values vs vendor A's bid.

cases.section: Exports — bid template, comparison report, vendor logs, master QCS regeneration
cases.title: A client buyer cannot download vendor bidding logs
cases.why: Vendor logs (IP, timestamps, every bid revision) are Procol-internal; the menu is shown only to Procol employees and the API must agree.
cases.setup: Run's buyer (client user, not a Procol employee). `{{pricingTradeUuid}}` closed.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{pricingTradeUuid}}/trade_history`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action'.
cases.oracle: 422 + 455; no file URL.

cases.section: Event times, numbers, rounds and summary
cases.title: The event's start, end and current round follow its live rounds
cases.why: The event card's dates and "current stage" decide where a buyer lands; a cancelled round must not drag them.
cases.setup: Event with a technical round (Mon 10:00 → Tue 10:00), a price round (Wed 10:00 → Thu 10:00) and a cancelled round (Sun → Fri).
cases.steps: Read the event on Sun, Mon 12:00, Tue 12:00 (between rounds), Wed 12:00 and Fri.
cases.expected: Start Mon 10:00, end Thu 10:00 (the cancelled round is ignored). Current round: Sun → technical (first not started), Mon 12:00 → technical (running), Tue 12:00 → technical (the previous one, the next has not started), Wed 12:00 → price round, Fri → price round (last). Reports show "Total Duration" = start → end.
cases.oracle: Event read `current_active_stage` uuid (`event_group/show_serializer.rb:201`); `starting_from` / `ending_at` / `current_active_stage` / `total_duration` (`event_group.rb:439-447, 671-673`); rounds exclude void and cancelled (`:62`, `trade_request.rb:256-259`).

cases.section: Event times, numbers, rounds and summary
cases.title: Reports of an event with no price round are produced, not crashed
cases.why: Technical-only events (or events whose price rounds were all withdrawn) still need their Master QCS and auction reports; the report header looks up "the latest price round" without checking that one exists.
cases.setup: Event A with only a technical round, evaluated. Event B whose only price round was withdrawn. Event C with a round that has no start time.
cases.steps: Download the Master QCS (and the auction report) for each.
cases.expected: A and B: the summary raises on `nil.template` (no price round); C: `nil.strftime` on the start; an event with a round whose closing time is empty raises in `max` (unverified that an empty closing time occurs).
cases.oracle: `get_summary_data` (`event_group.rb:813-838`) called by `master_qcs_report.rb:54`, `master_qcs_report_v1.rb:43`, `auction_report.rb:43`; `ending_at` uses `max` without `compact` (`:444-447`). Report status "failed" or never ready.

cases.title: Scoring scale and mode come from the last live technical round
cases.why: Evaluators can only use the labels of the scale in force; picking a withdrawn round's scale accepts or refuses the wrong scores.
cases.setup: Event with technical round T1 (scale 0–5, line-level), later T2 (scale 0–10, lot-level) withdrawn; second event with no technical round.
cases.steps: Submit a score of 7 on each event; read the scoring mode.
cases.expected: Event 1 uses T1 (T2 is withdrawn): 7 refused, mode line-level. A draft or closed technical round does count as "live" for this. Event 2 uses the company scale (none → no labels).
cases.oracle: `get_valid_rfp_trade_request` (`event_group.rb:973-975`), scale fallback (`:726-735`, `company.rb:1040-1042`), modes (`:963-971`). Score refusal HTTP 422 code 2 (see brief: scores must be keys of the label map).

cases.section: When a technical round closes itself
cases.title: A lot-level RFP closes when every active response has a score; with both modes on, the lines must be scored too
cases.why: Lot-level closing counts scored vendors against active responses; a withdrawn response must not keep it open forever, and in "both" mode a lot score alone must not close it.
cases.setup: RFP lot-level, three responses (one later withdrawn). Second RFP with both lot and line scoring.
cases.steps: Score the two active vendors at lot level; read the round. On the second RFP give lot scores only, then line scores.
cases.expected: First: closed after the 2nd lot score (2 scored = 2 active). Second: still open after lot scores; closed after every line is scored. Each score marks the line and the event as "has evaluations".
cases.oracle: `trade_request_model_helper.rb:1286-1294, 1462-1469`; both-mode check `evaluation_score.rb:151-158`; `has_evaluations` writes `:213, 228, 267-269`. Lot score count reads `get_precomputed_data`, which is the older data block when the platform flag MQCS_GROUPING_ENABLED is off while scores are written only to the newer block — then a lot RFP would never close (unverified which value the flag has on UAT).

cases.section: When a technical round closes itself
cases.title: A re-evaluated score clears that line's score, and a TNA score clears the vendor's line rank
cases.why: After "re-evaluate" the old score must not keep the vendor qualified; a TNA vendor must not hold a rank on that line.
cases.setup: Line-level RFP; vendor A scored 4 with remark "ok"; vendor B scored TNA.
cases.steps: Request re-evaluation of A's score and complete it; read the line's data for A and B.
cases.expected: A: score and remark empty until a new active score is given (then that score and its remark). B: its line rank score is empty. Only active or re-evaluated scores update the line data; inactive scores and remarks are ignored. On a service RFP grouped by PR item, the same score and remark appear on the sibling activity lines of that PR item.
cases.oracle: `evaluation_score.rb:68-71, 87-89, 231-239`; `evaluation.rb:31-32`.

cases.section: When a technical round closes itself
cases.title: Section-wise total: Σ score × weight / 100, and a later draft must not override an approved score
cases.why: The weighted total is the vendor's technical score; today the most recently edited score per section wins even if it is another evaluator's unsent draft.
cases.setup: Section-wise RFP: section S1 weight 60, S2 weight 40. Evaluator E1 submits S1 = 8, S2 = 5 (active). Evaluator E2 then saves S1 = 2 as a draft.
cases.steps: Read the vendor's total after E1's submission and after E2's draft.
cases.expected: After E2's draft the total becomes 2 × 0.6 + 5 × 0.4 = 3.20 (draft, requested and peer-review scores are included; latest update wins).
cases.oracle: `compute_weighted_total_score` (`evaluations_helper.rb:897-922`, statuses `:915`, order `:919`); stored `evaluation.scoring_info.total_weighted_score` (`evaluation_score.rb:183-192`); wait `evaluations_helper.rb:954-973`; TNA `evaluation_score.rb:248-251`.

cases.section: When a technical round closes itself
cases.title: Re-evaluating a score that sits in a pending technical award points the award to the new score
cases.why: The approver must approve the new score, not the old one; and a re-evaluation must not end in a server error after the data is saved.
cases.setup: Technical award proposal in "requested" holding vendor A's and B's scores; B has no active evaluation (e.g. withdrawn).
cases.steps: Re-evaluate A's score on line 1; read the proposal's score list.
cases.expected: For B (no active, peer-review or draft evaluation) the rewrite hits `nil.evaluation_scores` in an after-commit hook → HTTP 500 after the re-evaluation was already saved (unverified live).
cases.oracle: `Evaluation#update_proposal_data` (`evaluation.rb:50-76`), write with `update_columns` (`:75`).

cases.title: A vendor's first technical submission is time-stamped, replaces its drafts and adds it to the participants
cases.why: The submission time is evidence of on-time response; a leftover draft must not be scored instead of the submission.
cases.setup: Technical round; QA vendor with two drafts (one per alternative is out of scope — same alternative).
cases.steps: Submit one draft; read the vendor's responses, the round's participants and the vendor's pending tasks.
cases.expected: Submitted response has a submission time (set only on the first draft → submitted move); the other draft is inactive; the vendor is in the round's participant list; its "submit response" task is completed. Later revisions keep the first submission time.
cases.oracle: `template_response.rb:62, 87-89, 294-296, 562-599`; `misc.bid_company_ids`; latest/valid statuses `:95, 100`.

cases.title: Technical answers pre-fill the price round's "fetched from RFP" columns
cases.why: Vendors should not retype make, model or lead time; the price round must show what they answered in the RFP.
cases.setup: Price round with columns set to fetch "make" from the RFP; vendor answers "make = Siemens" on the global form and per line.
cases.steps: Submit the RFP answer; open the price round as the vendor.
cases.expected: The make column shows "Siemens" (global answer at event level, line answer per line). A price round with no such columns is untouched.
cases.oracle: `template_response.rb:86, 113-161`; columns in `config.auto_fetch_from_rfp_widget_keys`.

cases.title: An amendment copies the technical round and one price round, never lot rounds
cases.why: Buyers expect the amended draft to contain what they will re-run; a lot round left out (or an older price round copied) changes the event.
cases.setup: Event with technical round, RFQ, auction made from the RFQ, and a lot round; second event raised from a PR.
cases.steps: Amend each; read the amended draft's rounds.
cases.expected: Technical round = the last live one; price round = the latest non-lot price round (the auction) — for a PR amendment the RFQ is preferred; no lot rounds.
cases.oracle: `versions/event_group.rb` (per `R-MEG-014-4`, lines 50+).

cases.title: The amended draft keeps each window's length and their order
cases.why: Every copied window restarts at the moment of amendment, so the evaluation window (normally after bidding) now starts with bidding and can end before it.
cases.setup: Event with RFP bidding 2 days followed by a 1-day evaluation window.
cases.steps: Amend at time A; read the draft's windows.
cases.expected: Both start at A: bidding A → A + 2 days, evaluation A → A + 1 day (each keeps its configured length). Whether publishing the amendment re-times them is (unverified).
cases.oracle: `replicate_trade_schedules` (`versions/trade_request.rb:111-130`).

cases.section: Lines, PR links, last PO and terms
cases.title: Publishing or withdrawing an event updates the "in progress" quantity on its PR items
cases.why: PR owners see how much is already being sourced; stale numbers cause double buying.
cases.setup: Event from a PR with 3 items (one later deleted); BOQ event from a BOQ PR with 2 items.
cases.steps: Publish each; withdraw each; read the PR items' in-progress quantity.
cases.expected: BOQ: only the last item of the last PR is recomputed; the other keeps a stale value (unverified that BOQ PRs carry several items).
cases.oracle: `event_group.rb:988-999`; `update_in_progress_quantity_worker.rb:18-21`.

cases.section: Lines, PR links, last PO and terms
cases.title: Each vendor's current bid across price rounds comes from the latest round
cases.why: The award report compares each vendor's latest bid; taking an RFQ bid after an auction understates the auction result.
cases.setup: RFQ (vendor A bid 100) then auction from it (A bid 95); a withdrawn RFQ with A's bid 90.
cases.steps: Download the award proposal report.
cases.expected: A's bid = 95 (later round wins; withdrawn/void/cancelled rounds and non-active bids ignored).
cases.oracle: `get_vendor_vs_latest_bid` (`event_groups_helper.rb:78-100`), used by `awarding_proposal_report_data_model.rb:240`.

cases.title: Savings for a stage that does not exist is a clean 'not found'
cases.why: The savings widget is polled on every refresh of the comparison; a missing stage (deleted, wrong link) must not crash the poll or leak another stage's numbers.
cases.setup: Any authenticated buyer of PROCOL DEMO. `Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` decodes to id 999999999 (no such stage).
cases.steps: Ask for the aggregate savings of a stage id that does not exist: `GET /v1/trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/aggregate_savings`.
cases.expected: Refused before any savings maths runs. HTTP 422, error code 4, message 'Request not found'.
cases.oracle: Status 422 + code 4; body has no `savings` key.

cases.title: A closed RFQ with no savings set up reports 'no savings', not zero and not an error
cases.why: Most RFQs are created without a savings reference. The buyer must see an empty savings card, never a fabricated 0% or a crash.
cases.setup: `{{pricingTradeUuid}}` = the journey's closed RFQ: one submitted bid, award proposal submitted, created with `savings_configuration: null`. Company setting `custom_savings_array_config` decides whether custom savings still apply.
cases.steps: Read the aggregate savings of the closed journey RFQ: `GET /v1/trade/{{pricingTradeUuid}}/aggregate_savings`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. Bidding is over so masking is off; `show_aggregate_savings?` is false (no lot/line savings, and custom savings off) so the answer is `{"savings": null}`. If the client has custom savings switched on, a list of custom (Realised/Unrealised) savings comes back instead. Never a 5xx.
cases.oracle: 200; `savings` is null (or a list of custom savings objects each with savings_amount, savings_percent, reference).

cases.title: Savings on a live RFQ with no bids yet do not crash and do not invent numbers
cases.why: While bidding is open the savings card is either hidden (masking) or empty. A live stage with no bids is exactly when nil best-amounts can reach the maths.
cases.setup: `{{tradeId}}` = sandbox RFQ, published, bid window open, no bids.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/aggregate_savings`.
cases.expected: No 5xx. For the stage owner the answer is `{"savings": null}` (no savings configuration). For a buyer who is not the owner while event masking on RFQs is on, 422 code 577 'Savings will be visible after bidding ends'.
cases.oracle: 200 with savings null, or 422 + code 577.

cases.title: A savings reference of zero must not show 'Infinity %'
cases.why: When a buyer picks a savings basis (Budget, Last Purchase Price…) but leaves its value at the default 0, the percentage is amount / 0. Ruby float division gives Infinity / NaN, which is rounded and sent as text.
cases.setup: A lot-based savings configuration with a strategy whose reference value is 0 (the template default `value: 0.0`), at least one bid. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/aggregate_savings` after a bid is in.
cases.expected: No 5xx. The savings_percent for that strategy should be blank or 0 — today the code computes `savings / 0` and returns the string "Infinity" / "-Infinity" / "NaN" (defect-in-waiting).
cases.oracle: `savings[i].savings_percent.value` for the zero-reference strategy.

cases.title: Line-wise savings for a stage that does not exist is 'not found'
cases.why: The line-savings table is loaded per stage; a stale link must not 500.
cases.setup: Any buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/best_line_wise_savings`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.title: Line-wise savings on a closed RFQ without savings set up is an empty map
cases.why: The line-savings table must be empty (not error) when no per-line reference exists.
cases.setup: `{{pricingTradeUuid}}` closed, one bid, no savings configuration.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{pricingTradeUuid}}/best_line_wise_savings`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 `{}` — configuration blank and no custom savings ⇒ early empty answer. With custom savings on, a map keyed by line uuid.
cases.oracle: 200; `{}` or a map keyed by trade-product uuid.

cases.title: L1 data for a stage that does not exist is 'not found'
cases.why: The counter-offer drawer loads L1 data when it opens; a bad id must give a clean error.
cases.setup: Any buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/l1_data_for_event`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.title: L1 data after the award does not crash
cases.why: Once a proposal is approved the winning bid lines move to status 'selected'. `get_l1_data_for_event` only loads bid lines in status active/requested, then calls `.select` on the per-line list — nil for an awarded line ⇒ NoMethodError ⇒ HTTP 500. The scores used for ranking still include the awarded vendor.
cases.setup: `{{pricingTradeUuid}}` = the journey's closed RFQ with one bid and a submitted proposal. When no approval flow applies, the proposal is approved at submit and the bid lines become 'selected'.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{pricingTradeUuid}}/l1_data_for_event`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with the L1 vendor's line values (or `{}`), never 5xx. **Suspected defect:** if the bid lines are 'selected' this 500s at trade_template_helper.rb:402.
cases.oracle: Status code; if 200, one entry per line keyed by line uuid.

cases.title: A masked team buyer does not get L1 prices during live bidding
cases.why: When masking hides bids from a non-owner buyer, the same buyer must not be able to read L1 prices from the schema.
cases.setup: Company setting `event_masking_on_rfqs` ON; second buyer (not owner, not super admin); live RFQ with bids. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: As that buyer: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/schema?response_type=template&l1_prices=true`.
cases.expected: `show_bidding_stats` true and no L1 prices. Today the code computes `l1_prices` regardless of masking (suspected leak).
cases.oracle: `trade_config.show_bidding_stats` vs `l1_prices`.

cases.title: Whole-event L1 vs per-line L1
cases.why: On a lot-closing event the L1 is the vendor with the best gross total, and every line takes that vendor's price; on a line-closing event each line has its own L1 vendor. Mixing them gives an auction start price nobody bid.
cases.setup: Two vendors: A cheapest on line 1, B cheapest on line 2, B cheapest on gross total. Run once with `auction_closing_mode` lot_based, once line_item_based. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/schema?response_type=template&l1_prices=true` in both runs.
cases.expected: Lot-based: `lot_based.gross_total` = B's gross total and both lines carry B's prices. Line-based: line 1 = A's price, line 2 = B's price, lot_based empty.
cases.oracle: l1_prices per line vs the bids.

cases.title: A regretted line shows REGRET and the regretting vendor is not L1 on it
cases.why: A vendor that regrets (declines) a line must not appear as the cheapest bidder on that line with a zero/blank price.
cases.setup: Two vendors; vendor A regrets line 2 in the technical stage; both quote line 1. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: Open the RFQ comparison (`GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/schema?response_type=template`) and indicators (`GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/event_indicators`).
cases.expected: Line 2 status label 'REGRET' for A; best_bidder on line 2 is B.
cases.oracle: Status label for A's line 2; best_bidder flags.

cases.title: With a single bid, that vendor is the best bidder on every line
cases.why: The simplest L1 oracle: one bid ⇒ rank 1 and best_bidder true for that vendor on every line.
cases.setup: `{{pricingTradeUuid}}` closed with one submitted bid from the QA vendor.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{pricingTradeUuid}}/event_indicators`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; exactly one key in `auction_identifiers_data` (the QA vendor's company uuid); for each line `inline[line].rank.best_bidder` = true and rank value "1" when ranks are shown.
cases.oracle: One vendor key; best_bidder true per line.

cases.title: Tied L1 vendors are both 'best bidder' and both show rank 2
cases.why: When two vendors quote the same best price, `ranking_for_scores` adds 1 to every rank so nobody is shown as 1. Buyers and vendors read '2' and assume someone is cheaper. The best_bidder flag (value == min rank) is still true for both.
cases.setup: Two vendors quote the identical lowest price on a line (company `is_tie_bid_allowed` ON so the tie is accepted). No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/event_indicators`.
cases.expected: Both vendors: rank value "2", best_bidder true; third vendor rank "3". Confirm with product that 'no rank 1 on a tie' is intended and that the QCS shows a tie badge.
cases.oracle: rank.value and rank.best_bidder per vendor per line.

cases.title: An invited vendor cannot read every competitor's rank and best price
cases.why: `event_indicators?` is only `show?`; masking does not apply to vendors (the masking rule only looks at the buyer's own companies). The vendor gets a map keyed by every bidding company's uuid with rank, best_bidder and best_price.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ live; three vendors bid; caller is one of them (vendor session). No runnable twin: needs a vendor session.
cases.steps: As the vendor: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/event_indicators`.
cases.expected: Only the caller's own entry (or rank-only per configured indicators). **Suspected leak:** all three companies' entries, including who is best_bidder.
cases.oracle: Number of company keys in auction_identifiers_data.

cases.title: A masked buyer gets an empty indicators body during live bidding
cases.why: Masking must hide ranks too, not only prices.
cases.setup: Company setting `event_masking_on_rfqs` ON; second buyer (not owner/super admin); live RFQ with bids. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: As that buyer: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/event_indicators`.
cases.oracle: Empty body.

cases.title: Rejected bids for a stage that does not exist is 'not found'
cases.why: The rejected-bids modal opens from the comparison; a stale stage must not 500.
cases.setup: Any buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/rejected_bids`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.title: A vendor cannot read other vendors' rejected bids or remarks
cases.why: Both actions authorize only `show?` on the class and do not filter by the caller's company. An invited vendor can read every vendor's rejected bid amounts and free-text remarks (which often contain prices and conditions).
cases.setup: Two vendors bid; buyer rejected vendor A's bid; caller is vendor B (vendor session). No runnable twin: needs a vendor session.
cases.steps: As vendor B: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/rejected_bids` and `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/bidder_remarks`.
cases.expected: Only vendor B's own data (or refused). **Suspected leak:** vendor A's rejected bid and remarks come back (names masked only if vendor masking is on).
cases.oracle: Company keys / entries in both responses.

cases.title: Paging a quote on an event without tabs does not crash
cases.why: `set_pagination_for_line_items` runs whenever `tab` and `page` are both present and does `trade.tabs[params['tab'].to_i]` with no blank check. `tabs` is nil on non-BOQ events ⇒ NoMethodError ⇒ 500. The master-QCS twin of this helper guards `return if tabs.blank?`; this one does not.
cases.setup: `{{pricingTradeUuid}}` closed non-BOQ RFQ (no tabs) with bid `{{bidUuid}}`.
cases.steps: Open the vendor's quote with paging parameters: `GET /v1/trade/{{pricingTradeUuid}}/quote_details/{{bidUuid}}?tab=0&page=1`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with the quote (paging ignored), never 5xx. **Suspected defect:** 500 at trade_controller_helper.rb:6341.
cases.oracle: Status code.

cases.title: Opening a quote that does not exist says 'Bid not found'
cases.why: The quote drawer is opened from links; a stale bid id must be a clean error.
cases.setup: `{{pricingTradeUuid}}` closed.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{pricingTradeUuid}}/quote_details/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 32 'Bid not found'.

cases.title: A masked buyer cannot open quotes during live bidding (except a pending surrogate bid)
cases.why: Masking returns 32 for quote details unless the bid is a surrogate bid waiting for approval (the approver must see what they approve).
cases.setup: Company setting `event_masking_on_rfqs` ON; non-owner buyer; live RFQ with a normal bid and a surrogate bid pending approval. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/quote_details/<normal bid>` then `<surrogate bid>`.
cases.expected: Normal bid: 422 code 32. Pending surrogate bid: 200.
cases.oracle: Status per bid.

cases.title: Leader board for a stage that does not exist does not crash
cases.why: Any stale or mistyped link to the leaderboard tab produces a server error today.
cases.setup: Any buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/alternate_bidding_leader_board`.
cases.expected: A clean 4xx (422 code 4 like the sibling actions). **Suspected defect:** HTTP 500 — `authorize nil` raises Pundit::NotDefinedError.
cases.oracle: Status code.

cases.title: A vendor cannot read the alternate-bidding leader board
cases.why: The policy requires the stage's company to be the caller's; the board ranks every vendor's alternatives.
cases.setup: Alternate-bidding stage; caller is an invited vendor. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: As the vendor: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/alternate_bidding_leader_board`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action'.

cases.section: Sealed bids — masking, bid lock, unlock OTP, bid visibility
cases.title: Finance users for unlocking cannot be listed when bids are not locked
cases.why: The unlock flow exists only for stages that lock bids; otherwise the list of finance users (names + emails) must not be served.
cases.setup: Company setting `lock_bid_by_default` OFF (PROCOL DEMO). Sandbox RFQ live.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/get_users_for_bid_visibility`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 10 'You are not allowed to use this functionality'.

cases.section: Sealed bids — masking, bid lock, unlock OTP, bid visibility
cases.title: Requesting an unlock OTP without choosing a finance user is refused
cases.why: The OTP must go to a named finance user; an empty request must not default to anyone.
cases.setup: Any buyer; sandbox RFQ.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/send_otp_for_unlocking_bids` with body `{}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. No OTP is sent.

cases.section: Sealed bids — masking, bid lock, unlock OTP, bid visibility
cases.title: An unlock OTP cannot be sent to someone who is not a finance user
cases.why: Only finance users may authorise opening sealed bids; a buyer naming themselves must be refused.
cases.setup: `lock_bid_by_default` OFF; the run's own buyer `{{buyerUserUuid}}`.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/send_otp_for_unlocking_bids` with body `{"user_uuid": "{{buyerUserUuid}}"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 10 'You are not allowed to use this functionality' (not a finance user, or bids not locked — same code either way). No OTP is sent.

cases.section: Sealed bids — masking, bid lock, unlock OTP, bid visibility
cases.title: Verifying an unlock without an OTP is refused
cases.why: No OTP, no unlock — the visibility must not change.
cases.setup: Any buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/verify_otp_for_unlocking_bids` with body `{"user_uuid": "{{buyerUserUuid}}", "bid_visibility": "everyone"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 'Insufficient parameters'; bid_visibility unchanged.

cases.section: Sealed bids — masking, bid lock, unlock OTP, bid visibility
cases.title: Sealed bids cannot be unlocked while bidding is still live
cases.why: The dashboard offers 'Unlock bids' only in the buffer state (after bid end), but the API only checks that the stage is active — it does not check that bidding is over. A finance user could open sealed bids mid-RFQ.
cases.setup: Company setting `lock_bid_by_default` ON; RFQ live (before bid end) with bids; a finance user. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: Send OTP, then verify with the right OTP and `bid_visibility: everyone`, while the RFQ is still live.
cases.expected: Refused until bid end (expected). **Suspected gap:** accepted; bids visible to the team during live bidding.
cases.oracle: After verify: does `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/aggregate_savings` stop answering 577 before bid end?

cases.section: Sealed bids — masking, bid lock, unlock OTP, bid visibility
cases.title: Bids cannot be unlocked before technical evaluation when the client requires it
cases.why: `restrict_unlock_bid_before_evaluation` keeps commercial bids sealed until the technical stage is evaluated (two-envelope procurement).
cases.setup: Company setting `restrict_unlock_bid_before_evaluation` ON (PROCOL DEMO: OFF); RFP+RFQ event, RFP not evaluated; bids locked. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/send_otp_for_unlocking_bids` for a finance user.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 790 'Bids can't be unlocked until technical evaluation is done'. After evaluation: OTP sent.
cases.oracle: 422 + 790, then success.

cases.section: Sealed bids — masking, bid lock, unlock OTP, bid visibility
cases.title: Closed-envelope bidding masks even super admins while running
cases.why: `closed_envelope_bidding_for_rfqs` is the stricter mode: masking applies to everyone in the client including super admins (unless part of the auction team).
cases.setup: Company setting `closed_envelope_bidding_for_rfqs` ON (PROCOL DEMO: OFF); live RFQ with bids; super-admin buyer. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/aggregate_savings`, `/event_indicators`.
cases.expected: 577 and `{}` during bidding; data after close.
cases.oracle: Status/body during vs after.

cases.section: Sealed bids — masking, bid lock, unlock OTP, bid visibility
cases.title: Another company's buyer cannot list this company's finance users
cases.why: The finance-user list contains names and emails; the lookup is scoped to the caller's workspace.
cases.setup: Buyer of another client (e.g. Demo Account 2) with the PROCOL DEMO stage uuid. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/<PROCOL DEMO stage>/get_users_for_bid_visibility` as that buyer.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.section: Exports — bid template, comparison report, vendor logs, master QCS regeneration
cases.title: Bid template for a company that does not exist does not crash
cases.why: `company_uuid` is decoded and used as `Company.find_by(id:)` with no nil check; the Excel service then calls `@current_workspace.id` in its constructor ⇒ NoMethodError ⇒ 500.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ live (status active).
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/download_event_details?company_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: A clean 4xx (company not found). **Suspected defect:** HTTP 500. Nothing should be written (the crash happens before the Report row).
cases.oracle: Status code; no new report.

cases.section: Exports — bid template, comparison report, vendor logs, master QCS regeneration
cases.title: Master QCS regeneration is refused before the input is even checked
cases.why: Policy runs first: a client must get 'not authorized' even for an empty list (not 'insufficient parameters', which would tell them the endpoint is usable).
cases.setup: Run's client buyer (not on the regeneration allow-list).
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/regenerate_master_qcs` with body `{"event_group_uuids": []}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action'.

cases.section: Master QCS sheets and MQCS report templates
cases.title: Master QCS ignores a proposal that belongs to another event
cases.why: `proposal_uuid` is looked up by company only, not by event; a proposal from event X must not drive the awarded quantities shown on event Y.
cases.setup: `{{proposalUuid}}` = the journey event's proposal; `{{eventGroupUuid}}` = the sandbox event (different).
cases.steps: `GET /sheets/schema?view_type=awarding_view&event_group_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}&proposal_uuid={{proposalUuid}}`.
cases.expected: No 5xx. Expected: the foreign proposal is ignored or refused. Record whether awarded-quantity widgets show the journey's allocation on the sandbox grid (suspected mix-up).
cases.oracle: Status; awarded widgets on the sandbox layers.

cases.title: Exchange rates cannot be set on a single-currency stage
cases.why: Rates on a stage without multi-currency would silently change nothing — or worse, create a half configuration.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ created without a currency configuration (single currency, like the journey).
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/currency_exchange_rates` with body `{"currency_rates": [{"USD": "-5"}]}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 879 'Multi-currency is not configured for this trade request.' Nothing saved.
cases.oracle: 422 + 879; GET schema still shows currency_configuration null.

cases.title: Exchange rates cannot change after a bid is in
cases.why: Changing the rate after bids would reorder the comparison and move the L1 after the fact.
cases.setup: `{{pricingTradeUuid}}` closed with one bid.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{pricingTradeUuid}}/currency_exchange_rates` with body `{"currency_rates": [{"USD": "-5"}]}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422: code 879 if the stage is single-currency, otherwise 877 'Exchange rates cannot be updated after bids have been placed.' Nothing saved.

cases.title: Comparisons are in base currency for the team and in bid currency for others
cases.why: `convert_to_original_currency` flips for non-team viewers in quote details and rejected bids; totals and L1 must be computed on base-converted values.
cases.setup: Multi-currency RFQ (base INR); vendor A bids in USD 1.00 (rate 83), vendor B in INR 80. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: Buyer: indicators + quote details; vendor A: own quote details.
cases.expected: Buyer sees A = ₹83 and B = ₹80, B is L1. Vendor A sees its own quote in USD.
cases.oracle: best_bidder and displayed amounts.

cases.section: Legacy comparison reads — stage show, auction report, event summary
cases.title: Bid history for a bid that does not exist does not crash the stage read
cases.why: `last_valid_bid_for_bid_uuid` is decoded and looked up on the stage; the result is used as `bid.status` with no nil check ⇒ NoMethodError ⇒ 500.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ live.
cases.steps: `GET /trade/{{tradeId}}?last_valid_bid_for_bid_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: 422 code 32 'Bid not found' (expected). **Suspected defect:** 500 at trade_controller.rb:1113.
cases.oracle: Status code.

cases.section: Event times, numbers, rounds and summary
cases.title: Event numbers are "RFX-n", gain ".1", ".2" on each amendment, and can be searched
cases.why: The event number is how buyers and vendors refer to an event across amendments; a reused number points two teams at different events.
cases.setup: Company with n events; event E numbered RFX-n. `gate: show_reference_id` on and off.
cases.steps: 1. Create an event. 2. Amend E twice. 3. Search the events list for "RFX-n.2".
cases.expected: The new event is RFX-(n+1) and no two of the company's events share a number. E's versions read RFX-n.1 then RFX-n.2; search by "RFX-n.2" finds the second amendment. With reference display on, titles read "Title [RFX-n]".
cases.oracle: `add_ref_id` = "RFX-" + count of the company's latest events (`event_group.rb:429-433`) — a count, not a sequence, so reuse after a count drop is possible (unverified in data); versioned ref (`versioning/methods.rb:86-95`), order (`item_version.rb:55, 102-105`); search ILIKE (`event_group.rb:90-92`); `title_ref` (`:228-230, 319-321`).

cases.section: Event times, numbers, rounds and summary
cases.title: Event-level money uses the latest price round's base currency and precision
cases.why: Event totals in reports are shown in one currency; using the company default when the price round is in USD mislabels every amount.
cases.setup: Event 1 with no price round; event 2 whose latest price round is multi-currency (base USD, adjusted precision 3); event 3 whose price round has no currency setup.
cases.steps: Read the event-level currency and precision (Master QCS header / event totals).
cases.expected: 1: company default currency with its default precision. 2: USD, precision 3 (adjusted). 3: the price round's default currency, default precision.
cases.oracle: `event_group.rb:640-668`.

cases.section: Event times, numbers, rounds and summary
cases.title: An event lists its rounds in stage order, without cancelled ones, and its price rounds newest first
cases.why: The console's round tabs and "latest price round" for awarding are taken from these lists; a withdrawn round must still be shown (as withdrawn), a cancelled one not at all.
cases.setup: Event with technical (stage 1), price round (2, withdrawn), price round (3, live), and a cancelled draft round.
cases.steps: Read the event.
cases.expected: Rounds in stage order 1, 2, 3 (withdrawn and draft rounds included, cancelled/void excluded). The latest price round is stage 3 (withdrawn, draft and inactive rounds are never the latest). The latest proposal is the newest selected or requested one.
cases.oracle: `event_group.rb:62, 68-76, 149-154`; `trade_request.rb:256-259`. Twin EDGE-EVRMEG-005 reads the sandbox event (one round) and must succeed.

cases.title: Score labels: fractional scores show the whole-number label; "TNA" and "Regret" are matched exactly
cases.why: A 2.5 shown as "2 – Fair" and a label spelt "tna" not recognised as Technically Not Acceptable change who goes to the price round.
cases.setup: Scale {0: TNA, 1: Poor, 2: Fair, 3: Good}; a second scale whose TNA label is spelt "Tna".
cases.steps: Score a vendor 2.5 on a line; score another vendor TNA on both scales.
cases.expected: 2.5 shows "Fair". On the first scale the TNA vendor is treated as TNA; on the second it is not (exact "TNA" only). A line with no evaluations yet returns no score for anyone.
cases.oracle: `event_group.rb:688-692, 718-724, 737-741`; `evaluation_score.rb:52`; `event_group_line_item.rb:133-145`.

cases.title: A vendor that regretted every line is shown as regretted, not as "technically not acceptable"
cases.why: The price round's invite list and the L1 price use the "all lines TNA" test; a vendor that simply declined is labelled as failing technically.
cases.setup: Technical round with 3 lines; vendor A regrets all 3; vendor B scored TNA on all 3; vendor C TNA on 2 and regretted 1.
cases.steps: Open the price round's vendor list (TNA status) and the L1 price.
cases.expected: A is TNA too: after dropping regretted lines nothing is left and `all?` on an empty list is true.
cases.oracle: `all_line_items_tna_for_vendor?` (`event_group.rb:795-811`), used by `trade_request.rb:1098-1107` (audience TNA status) and `trade_controller_helper.rb:5793` (L1). Regretted list `event_group_line_item.rb:147-149`; lot-level score `event_group.rb:683-686`.

cases.section: When a technical round closes itself
cases.title: A line waits on its evaluator, and on the owner during peer review
cases.why: "Pending on" tells everyone whose turn it is; a line stuck on the wrong person is never finished.
cases.setup: Line-level RFP; line 1 has evaluator E and owner O; E is a section in-charge.
cases.steps: Read pending-on before scoring; after E scores; after a score goes to peer review; after a score is requested back.
cases.expected: Before: E. Peer review: O. Section in-charge with a requested score, or line already scored for any vendor: O. Lines in "quote in evaluation" list their evaluators as pending.
cases.oracle: Line `meta_data.pending_on_evaluator_ids` (`evaluation_score.rb:51, 63-66`; `evaluations_helper.rb:739-747`); rules `event_group_line_item_trade_mapping.rb:57-67`; pending list `event_group.rb:314-317`.

cases.section: When a technical round closes itself
cases.title: A score change refreshes the draft award's snapshot
cases.why: The award approver reads the snapshot; a score changed after the proposal was drafted must show the new value.
cases.setup: Technical award proposal in draft with A's line score 3 (section-wise variant too).
cases.steps: Change A's score to 4; read the proposal snapshot.
cases.expected: Snapshot shows 4 (empty if the new score is not active). The section-wise path must not fail when the vendor is only in the unfiltered data.
cases.oracle: `evaluation_score.rb:106-134` (Form path `:126-128` writes without a presence check).

cases.title: Submission mails go to the buyer side only when the company asks for them
cases.why: Owners and intake creators want to know when a vendor answers; nobody else should be mailed.
cases.setup: Needs a readable buyer mailbox. `gate: send_new_bid_mail_to_intake_creator` on; RFP raised from an intake; an RFI where the vendor was invited by the buyer.
cases.steps: Vendor submits the RFP; vendor submits the RFI (first time, then revised).
cases.expected: RFP: the event owner and intake creators with an email get the submission mail. RFI: "complete" mail on the first submission only (not on a revision), plus the form-submission mail to the inviter.
cases.oracle: Mailbox; `template_response.rb:579-615`, `company.rb:292-294`.

cases.title: A surrogate technical answer is marked as surrogate and can be scored
cases.why: Answers typed by the buyer on a vendor's behalf must be labelled; scoring one must not fail on an answer without extra details.
cases.setup: Buyer submits a surrogate technical answer for the QA vendor; an older answer saved without extra details.
cases.steps: Read both answers; score both.
cases.expected: An answer with no extra details raises when asked whether it is a surrogate (unverified which answers lack them).
cases.oracle: `template_response.rb:107-111, 390-392`.

cases.title: A second amendment while another buyer's draft amendment exists is refused clearly
cases.why: Two people amending at once must get "a draft already exists", not a server error — especially when the second one is a PR amendment.
cases.setup: Buyer A starts an amendment (draft). Buyer B amends the same event; separately a PR change triggers a PR amendment.
cases.steps: B creates an amendment; the PR amendment runs.
cases.expected: The API's "is latest" check shields B (unverified wording); the PR amendment calls version creation directly and hits the unique index → untyped 500 (unverified live). Version chains are cached 24 h and refreshed on every version save.
cases.oracle: `versioning/methods.rb:131-147`, `item_version.rb:95-100`; API check at `:888` (per digest).

cases.title: Forms of deleted lines do not reappear as extra sections in the amendment
cases.why: A form copied without its line is treated as an event-level section, adding an unexpected section (and weight) to the technical total.
cases.setup: Line-level RFP with a form on line 3; delete line 3; amend.
cases.steps: Read the amended technical round's sections and weighted total.
cases.expected: The form is copied without a line link and can show up as an extra section (unverified live).
cases.oracle: Per `R-MEG-015-6`; unmapped forms count as sections in `evaluations_helper.rb:897-904`.

cases.section: Lines, PR links, last PO and terms
cases.title: A line's quantity, unit and closed quantity read from what the buyer entered
cases.why: Quantity drives totals and partial awards; a line whose stored data is empty must not crash the event.
cases.setup: Line with quantity 100 KG; second line whose quantity was set only on its price-round line (80); a third with no data; award 30 of line 1 then 20 more.
cases.steps: Read each line's quantity, unit symbol and closed quantity.
cases.expected: Line 1: 100, "KG", closed 30 then 50. Line 2: 80 (from the last active/closed price-round line). Line 3: 0 and no unit — never a server error.
cases.oracle: `event_group_line_item.rb:62-106` (`precomputed_data.dig` without a nil guard at `:63, 101` → 500 for a line with null data, unverified reachability).

cases.section: Lines, PR links, last PO and terms
cases.title: A line is linked to one PR item at a time, and relinking replaces the old link
cases.why: Each line's PR item drives in-progress quantity and PO creation; two active links double-count.
cases.setup: Line L linked to PR item P1.
cases.steps: Relink L to P2; try to link L to P2 again; read L's PR item and the event's PRs.
cases.expected: P1 link inactive, P2 active; the duplicate is refused ("Reference has already been taken") — not a server error; L shows P2 (if no active link, the most recent one). Only active links count as the event's PRs.
cases.oracle: `purchase_request_trade_mapping.rb:28-44`; `event_group_line_item.rb:166-170`; `event_group.rb:64-65`.

cases.section: Lines, PR links, last PO and terms
cases.title: Refreshing last-PO prices is allowed only when switched on, for live events with PR-linked lines
cases.why: The refresh rewrites reference prices used for savings; it must not touch awarded lines or run twice at once.
cases.setup: `gate: allow_lpo_update` off, then on; live event with 2 PR-linked lines, one already in a selected award.
cases.steps: Refresh last-PO data; refresh again while the first is in progress.
cases.expected: Off: "You are not allowed to perform this action". On: status "in progress", only the non-awarded line refreshed; the second request queues nothing. A draft event or one with no PR-linked line is refused.
cases.oracle: HTTP 422 code 101 (`event_groups_controller.rb:1109`); `event_group.rb:909-929`, `company.rb:891-893`.

cases.section: Lines, PR links, last PO and terms
cases.title: Last-PO details on a line: date formats and the vendor looked up by its padded code
cases.why: Buyers compare offers with the last PO; a wrong date or vendor makes the comparison useless.
cases.setup: Lines with last-PO data: date "20250315", date "2025-03-15", date "00000000"; vendor code "12345" mapped to an active vendor (stored as 0000012345); another code of an inactive vendor.
cases.steps: Read each line's last-PO fields (and the line report).
cases.expected: 15 Mar 2025 for both formats; no date for "00000000"; vendor name/city found for 12345; nothing for the inactive vendor; missing PR details show "-" in the report.
cases.oracle: `event_group_line_item.rb:172-187, 301-388`.

cases.section: Lines, PR links, last PO and terms
cases.title: Event terms: mandatory on the first round makes every clause required; one-round events fall back to the round's terms
cases.why: Vendors must accept required clauses before bidding; a wrong mode lets them skip one.
cases.setup: Event with structured terms (one clause "optional"); first round with "terms mandatory"; a second event with no event terms and one round with terms and an attachment; a third with two rounds and no event terms.
cases.steps: Read each event's terms (structured and plain).
cases.expected: 1: every clause "required". 2: the round's clauses and attachment (signed link). 3: empty. Plain-text clauses get ids "legacy_<event>_<n>", mode "none", HTML escaped; the plain form is empty when there are no clauses and no attachments.

cases.section: Lines, PR links, last PO and terms
cases.title: "Owned by" filter uses the event's owner, falling back to its creator
cases.why: After a hand-over the event must appear under the new owner, not the creator.
cases.setup: Event created by A, handed to B (owner access list). Another event by A with no owner row.
cases.steps: Filter the events list by owner B, then by A.
cases.expected: B: the handed-over event. A: only the event without an owner row.
cases.oracle: `owned_by_users` (`event_group.rb:133-136`).

cases.section: Lines, PR links, last PO and terms
cases.title: After award, the event's start and close times are set from its rounds and open rounds are pulled in
cases.why: The event's closing time is what reports and spend dashboards use; rounds still open after the award must end.
cases.setup: Event with RFP and RFQ, awarded while an evaluation window is still open; a technical-only event; an event whose rounds are all withdrawn.
cases.steps: Award (PO/order created); read the event's start/close and the rounds' end times.
cases.expected: Start = earliest round start; close = latest price-round close; rounds closing later are pulled to that time and the technical round's future windows end now. Technical-only: close = latest close of RFIs / evaluated RFPs. All withdrawn: their latest close. A withdrawn event never gets these times (only live events are processed).
cases.oracle: `event_groups_helper.rb:7-69`, `event_group_update_worker.rb` (loads `EventGroup.active`).

cases.section: Lines, PR links, last PO and terms
cases.title: Lot participants and lot membership use only active lots
cases.why: A lot report must list the vendors of that lot; a cancelled lot must not claim lines.
cases.setup: Event split into lots 1 and 2; lot 2 cancelled; lot 1 with 2 participants.
cases.steps: Read lot 1's participants; read which lot line X (moved from lot 2) belongs to.
cases.expected: Lot 1: its 2 participants (falls back to the event's participants only if lot data is missing). Line X belongs to no lot while lot 2 is cancelled. Events without lots answer "no lot" rather than failing.
cases.oracle: `event_group.rb:757-770, 1042-1067`; `event_group_line_item.rb:199-205`.

cases.title: Savings with an id that does not even decode is still 'not found', not a crash
cases.why: A malformed uuid decodes to nil (ParamsAuth#check_for_uuid); `find_by_id(nil)` must stay nil and must not fall through to `authorize nil` (which would be a Pundit NotDefinedError = HTTP 500).
cases.setup: Any buyer. `WrongUuid1=` decodes to nil.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/WrongUuid1=/aggregate_savings`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 4 'Request not found'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 4.

cases.title: Savings asked for a technical (RFP) stage are simply empty
cases.why: The comparison screen polls savings for every stage tab; a technical stage has no prices and must answer empty, not error.
cases.setup: rfp_rfq run: `{{rfpTradeId}}` = the sandbox's technical stage.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/aggregate_savings`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 `{"savings": null}` (no savings configuration on an RFP). Never 5xx.
cases.oracle: 200; savings null.

cases.title: Realised savings before anything is awarded is zero, not an error
cases.why: Custom 'Realised' savings sum the selected (awarded) bid lines. Before award there are none — the card must show 0, not crash on a nil total.
cases.setup: Company setting `custom_savings_array_config` ON with Realised + Unrealised; RFQ closed with bids, no award yet. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/aggregate_savings`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. Realised savings amount 0 (nothing awarded); Unrealised uses the best possible bid. After award, Realised equals reference − awarded total.
cases.oracle: Values before vs after award.

cases.title: Line-wise savings is empty when savings are compared on the whole lot
cases.why: Lot-based savings are shown once for the event; the per-line table must not double-count them.
cases.setup: Stage created with `savings_configuration.savings_comparison_on = lot_based`, bids in. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/best_line_wise_savings`, then `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/aggregate_savings`.
cases.expected: Line-wise answers `{}`; aggregate answers one entry per strategy (savings_amount, savings_percent, reference).
cases.oracle: Line-wise `{}`; aggregate list length = number of strategies.

cases.title: A line won through a counter offer shows no line saving (current behaviour to confirm)
cases.why: After a negotiated (counter-offered) price the best bid line may have no active/selected bid row; the code skips it (`next if bid_products.blank?`). Buyers may read 'no savings' on exactly the line they negotiated hardest.
cases.setup: Line-item savings configured; vendor accepted a counter offer on line 1. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/best_line_wise_savings`.
cases.expected: No 5xx. Record whether line 1 is missing from the map; if missing, raise with product (negotiated savings should arguably count).
cases.oracle: Presence of line 1's uuid in the response.

cases.title: Custom savings exist in the API but the screen never asks for them without a savings reference
cases.why: With `custom_savings_array_config` on and no savings configuration, the API returns custom savings, but the dashboard only calls the endpoint when `savings_configuration` is an object — the buyer never sees them.
cases.setup: Company setting `custom_savings_array_config` ON; stage without savings configuration; bids in. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/aggregate_savings` — note the custom savings list. 2. Open the stage in the dashboard.
cases.expected: API returns a non-empty list; the screen shows no savings card. File as UI gap (see UI-XDQCS-001).
cases.oracle: API list non-empty vs no card on screen.

cases.title: Line savings follow the chosen basis: per-unit price vs line total
cases.why: `line_item_savings_on` = price compares unit prices; = total_amount compares quantity × price. Mixing them overstates savings by the quantity factor.
cases.setup: Two stages with line-item savings, one on price and one on total amount, same reference and same bid (qty 10, price 90, reference 100). No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/<stage>/best_line_wise_savings` for both.
cases.expected: Price basis: saving 10 per unit (10%). Total basis: reference is the line total, saving 100 (10%). The percentage matches, the amount differs by the quantity.
cases.oracle: savings_amount and savings_percent per strategy for the line.

cases.title: Savings use the stage's base currency symbol or code
cases.why: In a multi-currency event the savings must be expressed in the base currency, labelled the way the stage is configured (symbol vs code).
cases.setup: Multi-currency stage, base USD, `default_currency_label_type` = code; one INR bid. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/aggregate_savings`.
cases.expected: savings_amount.configuration prefix is `USD` (code), amounts in USD after conversion at the stage's rate.
cases.oracle: configuration prefix and converted value.

cases.title: L1 data on a live RFQ with no bids is an empty map
cases.why: Before any bid there is no L1; the drawer must open empty.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ live, no bids.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/l1_data_for_event`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 `{}` (event_score_for_participants is blank).

cases.title: L1 prices on the comparison schema are empty before any bid
cases.why: The RFQ→auction conversion screen pre-fills start prices from `l1_prices`; with no bids it must be empty, not crash.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ live, no bids.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/schema?response_type=template&additional_fields=order_details&l1_prices=true`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; `l1_prices` = `{"lot_based": {}, "line_item_based": {}}`.
cases.oracle: l1_prices object with two empty maps.

cases.title: `l1_prices=false` still computes L1 prices
cases.why: The action checks `if params["l1_prices"]` — any non-empty string, including "false" and "0", turns the computation on. A client that sends false to save work (or to hide prices) still gets them.
cases.setup: `{{pricingTradeUuid}}` closed with one bid.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{pricingTradeUuid}}/schema?response_type=template&additional_fields=order_details&l1_prices=false`.
cases.expected: No 5xx. Record that `l1_prices` is present in the response although false was asked (param-parsing quirk; expected absent).
cases.oracle: Presence of l1_prices with the journey bid's price.

cases.title: On a weighted event L1 is the best score, not the lowest price
cases.why: Ranking uses `get_ranking_key` (weighted score when weights apply). The counter-offer drawer and indicators must agree on the same L1.
cases.setup: RFQ with weightage parameters; vendor A lowest price, vendor B best weighted score. No runnable twin: needs a second user or a company setting the run cannot switch.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/event_indicators` and `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/l1_data_for_event`.
cases.expected: Both name B as L1; l1_data returns B's line values.
cases.oracle: best_bidder flag and l1_data vendor_uuid (when requested).
