cases.title: Pending bid justifications block the conversion popover
cases.why: Converting while justifications are pending would freeze unexplained quotes as auction bids.
cases.setup: An RFQ with a vendor whose bid justification is pending.
cases.steps: 1. Settings → Convert to Auction.
cases.expected: The Pending Bid Justification modal opens instead of the popover.
cases.oracle: Modal visible.

cases.title: Auction-team users are sent through the edit flow and the auction goes to the team
cases.why: The success message differs and the auction lands as a draft (API-XDAUC-013).
cases.setup: A company with an auction team; once as a team member, once as a non-member.
cases.steps: 1. Convert an RFQ and publish.
cases.expected: Non-member → toast "Event sent to Auction Team successfully", auction draft. Member → "Event created successfully", redirect to the auction (or the project page with eRFX).
cases.oracle: Toast text; redirect; stage status.

cases.title: The live timer turns red under ten minutes and offers "Extend time"
cases.why: The buyer's only live cue that the close is near and the manual extension entry point.
cases.setup: A live auction with 12 minutes left.
cases.steps: 1. Watch the header timer across the 10-minute mark. 2. Hover the plus icon. 3. Let it end.
cases.expected: Ring turns red below 10 minutes; tooltip "Extend time"; "Ended" after close; toast "Your auction is live" on the upcoming→live change.
cases.oracle: Visual state; toast.

cases.title: The Analytics tab is hidden for RFI/RFP and says "No bids placed yet." without bids
cases.why: The report must not render empty charts or leak live bidding stats.
cases.setup: An RFP, an auction with no bids, an auction with bids.
cases.steps: 1. Look for the Analytics tab; open it.
cases.expected: Absent on the RFP; "No bids placed yet." on the empty auction; an "Auction Report" iframe otherwise; hidden while live when show_bidding_stats hides the audience.
cases.oracle: Tab/iframe presence.

cases.title: The bidding-summary rank filter only offers sensible limits
cases.why: The API refuses rank_limit ≤ 0 (API-XDAUC-091); the screen must never send it.
cases.setup: An auction with 3 active participants.
cases.steps: 1. Open Event Details → Bidding Summary → rank menu. 2. Choose "All Vendors".
cases.expected: Options Top 1 and Top 2 Vendors and All Vendors only; "All" sends no rank_limit; the panel refreshes every 30 s.
cases.oracle: Menu items; request URL.

cases.title: Knockout buyer view: round countdown, extension limit, everyone knocked out
cases.why: The buyer runs the rounds from this screen.
cases.setup: A running knockout with two vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Watch "Next round in mm:ss"; 2. extend the round beyond the event end; 3. let both vendors decline.
cases.expected: Countdown with + icon; "Extend your auction time in order to extend current round's time!" when past the end; "All participants are knocked out!" with tags Knocked Out per vendor.
cases.oracle: Texts/tags.

cases.title: The live page refreshes from the socket and falls back to polling
cases.why: Ranks and extensions must reach the buyer within seconds; there is no dedicated "time extended" banner, so the refresh is the only signal.
cases.setup: Live auction; then block the websocket.
cases.steps: 1. Have a vendor bid; watch the buyer page. 2. Block the socket; bid again.
cases.expected: TradesChannel message with auction_identifiers/bid_identifiers triggers a refetch of details, bids and indicators; with the socket closed the page polls every 30 s.
cases.oracle: Network refetches; timing.

cases.title: The converted auction links back to its RFQ
cases.why: The buyer must be able to compare RFQ quotes with auction results.
cases.setup: auction.convert journey.
cases.steps: 1. Open the auction's header.
cases.expected: A "Linked RFQ" tag linking to the parent RFQ.
cases.oracle: Tag present; link target = {{pricingTradeUuid}}.

cases.section: Converting an RFQ into an auction — which stage, which state, which order
cases.title: Converting the same RFQ a second time is refused
cases.why: Two auctions on one RFQ split the vendors' bids, and awarding requires the vendor to be in the latest stage (826) — the second auction would orphan the first.
cases.setup: Run with auction.convert ticked: {{pricingTradeUuid}} is the journey RFQ already converted into {{auctionTradeUuid}}. Base body (backstop included).
cases.steps: 1. Send the base body with `trade_request_uuid = {{pricingTradeUuid}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 94 (An auction has already been made for this event.) while the RFQ is still status active — the normal case, conversion does not change the RFQ's status; code 95 if the award has closed it. Never a second child.
cases.oracle: 422; `GET /trade/{{pricingTradeUuid}}` unchanged; still one auction stage on the event.

cases.section: Converting an RFQ into an auction — which stage, which state, which order
cases.title: Converting a running RFQ closes it immediately for every vendor
cases.why: The RFQ's open schedules are cut to "now" the moment the auction is created — a vendor typing a quote in the RFQ loses it. Buyers convert early "to save time" without knowing this.
cases.setup: A published RFQ whose window is still open, with one QA vendor bid (cannot run here: a successful conversion of a shared event is destructive).
cases.steps: 1. Convert the RFQ with a valid body. 2. As the vendor, try to revise the RFQ quote. 3. Read the RFQ.
cases.expected: RFQ schedules with end_time > now are set to now; misc.is_rfq_converted_to_auction true; closed_at now; status stays active. The vendor's RFQ revision is refused as closed (33/101). The vendor's RFQ quote reappears as their first auction bid only if `use_rfq_quotes_as_bids` was true and they are in the audience.
cases.oracle: `GET /trade/<rfq>` schedules and misc; vendor revision refusal.

cases.section: Bidding in a live auction (needs a vendor session — markdown only)
cases.title: A revision that moves the price by less than the tick is refused
cases.why: The tick stops penny-shaving that churns ranks without real savings.
cases.setup: Live rank auction, tick_size 10 on the line; vendor's active bid at 1000.
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, revise to 995.
cases.expected: 422 code 214 'Quoted price difference must be greater than the tick size'. Revise to 990 → accepted.
cases.oracle: 422 + 214 / new bid at 990.

cases.section: Bidding in a live auction (needs a vendor session — markdown only)
cases.title: Bids above the ceiling or below the floor are refused
cases.why: The ceiling is the buyer's budget cap in a reverse auction; the floor stops dumping.
cases.setup: Line ceil_price 1000, floor_price 500.
cases.expected: 1001 → 38 'Price cannot be more than the allowed price'; 499 → 41 'Price cannot be less than the allowed price'; the bounds themselves accepted (comparison after currency rounding).
cases.oracle: Codes; accepted bids.

cases.section: Bidding in a live auction (needs a vendor session — markdown only)
cases.title: Raising the price in a reverse auction is refused when increases are off
cases.why: The core reverse-auction contract; in a forward (sell) auction the mirror rule refuses decreases.
cases.setup: Live buy auction with config is_price_increase_allowed false; vendor at 1000.
cases.steps: 1. Revise to 1010. 2. On a sell auction with is_price_decrease_allowed false, revise down.
cases.expected: 1 → 300 'You cannot increase the price'; 2 → 301 'You cannot decrease the price'. With approval required instead, the revision becomes a pending approval request.
cases.oracle: Codes / additional request.

cases.section: Dynamic extension during a live auction (markdown only)
cases.title: A bid in the last N minutes pushes the end out by the configured minutes
cases.why: The anti-sniping promise made to every vendor.
cases.setup: Live rank auction: extension on, trigger 2 minutes, extend 3, strategy rank_based, rank limit 3.
cases.steps: 1. With 90 s left, a vendor moves from rank 4 to rank 2. 2. Read the schedules.
cases.expected: A dynamic_extra_time schedule from the old end to old end + 3 min; closed_at moved; every bid's end_time updated; misc.dynamic_time_extension_count +1.
cases.oracle: `GET /trade/<id>` schedules/end time.

cases.section: Dynamic extension during a live auction (markdown only)
cases.title: Extension switched on with no extension length breaks the vendor's last-minute bid
cases.why: The journey's own body sends `time_extension_value: null`; with extension on, the trigger path computes `nil * 60` in an after-commit callback — the vendor's bid is saved but the request errors and no extension happens.
cases.setup: Auction with extension on, trigger 2, time_extension_value null (template_input accepts it).
cases.steps: 1. With 60 s left, a vendor improves rank.
cases.expected: Desired: refused at set-up (or default 3 minutes, as update_dynamic_closing_schedule does). Today: NoMethodError in `trigger_dynamic_time_extension` after commit → 5xx to the vendor, bid saved, no extension.
cases.oracle: Vendor reply; bid present; schedules unchanged.

cases.section: What a vendor sees: rank, price, colour, ties (markdown only)
cases.title: Which indicator each auction type shows vendors
cases.why: The fairness contract: a vendor must see exactly what the strategy promises.
cases.setup: One live auction per type, plus a knockout and a dutch on an eRFX company.
cases.steps: 1. As a vendor, read each auction's indicators. 2. As the buyer, toggle "Show Rank" / "Show Best Prices".
cases.expected: rank/rank_and_price → rank shown; price/rank_and_price → best price shown; traffic light → colour (and rank only for rank-based traffic light, v1 layouts); knockout/dutch → rank hidden from vendors, shown to the buyer; the buyer's toggles add rank/best_price via other_auction_indicators_config.
cases.oracle: event_indicators per caller.

cases.section: Reports and reads during and after an auction
cases.title: The auction report for a stage that does not exist crashes
cases.why: The sibling reports answer 4 for the same input; this one dereferences nil through `T.must` (sorbet-runtime is loaded) and 500s.
cases.setup: Read-only.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/auction_report` (same for `WrongUuid1=`).
cases.expected: A 4xx (4 'Request not found'). Today TypeError "Passed `nil` into T.must" → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Which auction types exist, and what the conversion accepts
cases.title: Converting with an auction type that does not exist crashes instead of being refused
cases.why: "Serial bidding", "english" or "Rank" are words buyers and integrators use, but none is an `auction_config` value. The conversion has no allow-list, so the bad value reaches an enum assignment and the buyer gets an untyped server error instead of "invalid auction type".
cases.setup: {{tradeId}} is the sandbox RFQ (published, window open, one KG line, no bids). Base conversion body with the safety backstop.
cases.steps: 1. Send the base conversion body with `configurations.auction_config = "serial_bidding"` to `POST /trade/move_to_auction`. 2. Read the status.
cases.expected: A clean 4xx naming the bad type. Today: `change_rfq_info` assigns the value to the enum, Rails 7.0 raises ArgumentError ("'serial_bidding' is not a valid auction_config"), which is not a CustomException, is re-raised and is not rescued → HTTP 500. The transaction rolls back; the sandbox RFQ is untouched.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; `GET /trade/{{tradeId}}` still shows the RFQ open and not converted.

cases.section: Converting an RFQ into an auction — which stage, which state, which order
cases.title: Converting a stage that does not exist is refused
cases.why: The correctly-keyed version of the not-found case (the older AUC-CONV-001 sends `trade_request_id`, which is never decoded, so it cannot tell a missing stage from a mis-keyed one).
cases.setup: None beyond the buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. Send the base body with `trade_request_uuid = "Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 95 'Trade Request not found'. Nothing created.

cases.section: Converting an RFQ into an auction — which stage, which state, which order
cases.title: Converting the auction itself is refused
cases.why: An auction of an auction would copy auction bids as starting bids and reset the rounds.
cases.setup: auction.convert ticked; {{auctionTradeUuid}} is the closed auction.
cases.steps: 1. Send the base body with `trade_request_uuid = {{auctionTradeUuid}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 93 (Trade is already of auction type) while the auction is status active; code 95 once the award has closed it.
cases.oracle: 422; no new stage.

cases.section: Converting an RFQ into an auction — which stage, which state, which order
cases.title: A knockout start price is not checked at all when the RFQ has no quotes
cases.why: The 966 guard ("start price cannot be more than L1") is the only protection against a typo of extra zeros, and it silently disappears for an RFQ with no ranked bids.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ (no bids); `rfx_project_enabled` is ON; base body with the backstop.
cases.steps: 1. Send the base body as a knockout: `bulk_price 999999999, price_difference 10, time_difference 60`.
cases.expected: Today HTTP 422 code 125 'Delivery location not found' — no start-price check fired. Desired: some upper bound (or at least the dashboard's tick ≤ base check) server-side.

cases.section: Converting an RFQ into an auction — which stage, which state, which order
cases.title: With an auction team, the converted auction is created as a draft and RFQ quotes wait
cases.why: Companies that route auctions to an auction team get a DRAFT auction; RFQ quotes are not copied until the auction team activates it, and both stages are shared with the auction team as owner. If activation never copies the quotes, vendors start the auction with nothing.
cases.setup: A company with an active team of type auction; the converting buyer is not in it (cannot run here).
cases.steps: 1. Convert an RFQ with bids and `use_rfq_quotes_as_bids: true`. 2. Read the auction. 3. As an auction-team user, activate it. 4. Read the auction's bids.
cases.expected: Step 2: status draft, no bids, access lists for the auction team on RFQ and auction. Step 4: the quotes are present after activation. The dashboard toasts "Event sent to Auction Team successfully".
cases.oracle: Stage status, bids before/after activation.

cases.section: Converting an RFQ into an auction — which stage, which state, which order
cases.title: Vendors who marked every line "TNA" are dropped from the auction when TNA bidding is off
cases.why: With `allow_tna_vendors_to_bid: false` such vendors are removed from the audience AND their RFQ quotes are not carried over; with true they stay. The dashboard defaults the checkbox to true.
cases.setup: An RFQ with two invited vendors, one of which marked all lines TNA (needs vendor sessions).
cases.steps: 1. Convert with `allow_tna_vendors_to_bid: false`, both vendors in the audience, quotes as bids. 2. Repeat on a copy with true.
cases.expected: False → only the non-TNA vendor is in the auction audience and has a bid; misc.allow_tna_vendors_to_bid false. True → both are present.
cases.oracle: `GET /event_groups/<id>/get_audience`; auction bids.

cases.section: Conversion request shapes the controller does not guard
cases.title: A conversion without its settings block says "Order not active"
cases.why: Support chases the wrong problem: the stage IS active; the body simply lacks `configurations`.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ. Refused before CreateService.
cases.steps: 1. Send the base body without `configurations`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 33 'Order not active' (transform_trade_product finds no settings and no stage id). Desired: 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

cases.section: Conversion request shapes the controller does not guard
cases.title: An empty line row crashes the conversion
cases.why: The unit check assumes every row has a product hash; one malformed row gives a 500.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ. Refused before CreateService.
cases.steps: 1. Send the base body with `data = [{}, <valid row>]`.
cases.expected: A 4xx (574 'Unit cannot be blank'). Today: `item[:product][:unit_type]` on nil → NoMethodError → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Conversion request shapes the controller does not guard
cases.title: A line row without its variant crashes the conversion
cases.why: EDGE-AWD-083/084 dropped the variant too but were stopped by the unit check first, so this crash was never reached by the library.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ; the row keeps a valid KG unit.
cases.steps: 1. Send the base body with the row's `variant` removed.
cases.expected: A 4xx. Today `item[:variant][:id]` on nil → NoMethodError → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Conversion request shapes the controller does not guard
cases.title: Settings sent as text crash the conversion
cases.why: On a line-wise RFQ the 503 guard digs into `configurations` before anything checks its type.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ (closes line-item-wise).
cases.steps: 1. Send the base body with `configurations = "rank"`.

cases.section: Conversion request shapes the controller does not guard

cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 798 'CBD mode requires at least two active line items. Please add more line items to continue.'

cases.section: Conversion request shapes the controller does not guard
cases.title: A conversion without an auction window crashes

cases.expected: A 4xx. Today `create_trade_schedule` compares the copied RFQ `closed_at` with a nil end → ArgumentError → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; sandbox RFQ unchanged.

cases.section: Conversion request shapes the controller does not guard
cases.title: An auction that ends before it starts is accepted
cases.why: Sharper than EDGE-AWD-088 (which only asks for no 5xx): proves the inverted window passes every check — the RFP-vs-RFQ comparison is the only schedule check and it is skipped for rfq_then_auction.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ; base body with the backstop.
cases.expected: Today HTTP 422 code 125 'Delivery location not found' (only the backstop stops it). Desired: a time validation error (507-style) before line-item creation.

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: Extension switched on with no trigger window is refused
cases.why: Runnable twin of STG-063 (template_input, held out): the same rule must hold on conversion.

cases.steps: 1. Send `is_dynamic_closing_time_allowed: true`, `last_n_minutes_for_time_extension: null`, strategy rank_based, extend 2 min, rank limit 3.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 501 'Invalid Trigger Time for Dynamic Time Extension.' (inside CreateService, rolled back).

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: A zero-minute extension trigger is refused
cases.why: Lower boundary of the 1-minute floor.
cases.steps: 1. Send the extension on with trigger 0.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 501.

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: A trigger window sent as text crashes the conversion
cases.why: Runnable twin of STG-066; form-encoded clients send strings.
cases.steps: 1. Send the extension on with `last_n_minutes_for_time_extension: "5"`.
cases.expected: A 4xx or the number accepted. Today `"5" < 1` raises ArgumentError → 500 (rolled back).
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: A negative extension length is stored without any check
cases.why: In the live auction a last-minute bid would move the end time BACK — anti-sniping turned into an early close.
cases.steps: 1. Send the extension on, trigger 1, `time_extension_value: -5`.
cases.expected: Today HTTP 422 code 125 'Delivery location not found' (value accepted). Desired: refused (> 0).

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: A text rank limit for the extension is stored and blows up in the final minutes
cases.why: The bad value is accepted at set-up; the live price-based check compares an Integer rank with it and raises on the vendor's last-minute bid.
cases.setup: As 029, strategy price_based.
cases.steps: 1. Send the extension on, trigger 1, `rank_limit_for_time_extension: "top"`.
cases.expected: Today HTTP 422 code 125 'Delivery location not found'. Desired: refused (positive integer).

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: A traffic-light conversion without colour bounds is refused
cases.why: Without bounds every vendor's colour is undefined.

cases.steps: 1. Send `auction_config: traffic_light`, `traffic_light_config: price`, no `traffic_light_ranges`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 269 'You have not provided valid traffic light ranges.'

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: Equal traffic-light bounds are refused although the screen accepts them
cases.why: The dashboard only blocks lower > upper; the server needs lower < upper for buy. The buyer gets a server error for input the form accepted.
cases.steps: 1. Send lower_bound = upper_bound = 100 on a buy auction.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 269 'You have not provided valid traffic light ranges.' Pair with UI-XDAUC-012.

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: A knockout starting at zero is refused

cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 106 'Please enter a valid price'.

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: Knockout rounds shorter than 30 seconds are refused

cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 248 'Time difference cannot be less than 30 seconds'.

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion

cases.expected: A 4xx. Today `"60" < 30` raises ArgumentError → 500 (rolled back).

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: A knockout without a price step is refused
cases.why: Without a step the rounds never move the price.
cases.steps: 1. Send knockout with bulk 1000 and time_difference 60, no `price_difference`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 237 'Please enter all the required entries for creating the auction.'

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion

cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: A dutch auction whose start is above its end is refused with the wording reversed
cases.why: The rule fires because the start is GREATER than the end on a buy auction, but the message says it cannot be LESS — the buyer lowers the start and hits the same error. 241 has the mirror problem for sell.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ; base body with the backstop.
cases.steps: 1. Send dutch buy with `bulk_price 1000, end_price 500, price_difference 10, time_difference 60`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 242 'Start Price cannot be less than End Price' (wording to be fixed to "greater").

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: A serial-bidding item scheduled outside the auction window is refused
cases.why: Each serial item must fit inside the event; an item before the start would open early.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ. Refused before CreateService.
cases.steps: 1. Send `auction_closing_mode: line_item_based, staggered: true`, window 2100-01-01 00:00–01:00, and the row with start 23:40 the evening before and end 00:20.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 507 'Invalid Time Input'.

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: A serial-bidding item with no times crashes the conversion
cases.why: Rows are not checked for their own times before `Time.at`.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ.
cases.steps: 1. Send the staggered settings of 048 with a row that has no start_time/end_time.
cases.expected: A 4xx (507). Today `Time.at(nil)` → TypeError → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: A knockout start price above the RFQ's L1 is refused
cases.why: The only server-side link between RFQ quotes and the auction's opening price. EDGE-AWD-086 targets the sandbox, which has no quotes, so it can never fire there.
cases.setup: A published RFQ with one ranked quote of total T, no auction yet, `rfx_project_enabled` ON (needs the journey RFQ before conversion — not available to edge cases).
cases.steps: 1. Convert as knockout with `bulk_price = T` (equal) and again with T − 1.
cases.expected: Equal → 422 code 966 'Starting price cannot be more than the lowest RFQ (L1) Sum Total' (the check is `<=`). T − 1 → passes this check. Dutch: end price above L1 → 968.
cases.oracle: 422 + 966 / acceptance.

cases.title: The converted auction reads back as an auction stage linked to its RFQ
cases.why: The read-back oracle for every conversion case.
cases.setup: auction.convert ticked.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /trade/{{auctionTradeUuid}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200: rfx_mode rfq_then_auction, current status auctioning, auction_config rank, stage number one after the RFQ, parent = the RFQ, the QA vendor's RFQ quote carried over as a bid.
cases.oracle: Field values in the reply.

cases.title: The RFQ reads back closed for bidding and flagged as converted
cases.why: Proves conversion cuts the RFQ window immediately.
cases.setup: auction.convert ticked.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /trade/{{pricingTradeUuid}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200: bidding schedule ends at the conversion time, misc.is_rfq_converted_to_auction true, status still active (only MarkEventClosedWorker closes a stage, when all its lines are closed).
cases.oracle: Field values.

cases.title: Knockout and dutch conversions create their first round for the active, non-broker audience
cases.why: A vendor missing from round 1 can never accept an offer (458).
cases.setup: Successful knockout conversion published active, audience = two vendors + one broker.
cases.steps: 1. Convert. 2. Read the auction's trade rounds.
cases.expected: Round 1 starts at the auction start with the start price, participants = the two active vendors (not the broker). A draft (auction-team) conversion creates no rounds.
cases.oracle: trade_rounds rows.

cases.section: Auction set-up on the create screen (template_input — not runnable here)
cases.title: An auction stage without an order type is refused
cases.why: Order type decides reverse vs forward auction and the direction every price rule takes.
cases.setup: template_input on a draft event, web client (mobile is exempt).
cases.steps: 1. Add a rank auction stage without `order_type`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 53 'Order Type not mentioned'. (Note: without order_type the price-increase rule would default to allowed — `get_config_for_new_trade` else-branch.)

cases.section: Auction set-up on the create screen (template_input — not runnable here)
cases.title: Ceiling, floor and tick size per line are stored without cross-checks
cases.why: A ceiling below the floor makes every bid impossible (38 above, 41 below); a tick and a tick percentage on the same line are both enforced.
cases.setup: template_input auction stage, one row with ceil_price 90, floor_price 100, tick_size 5, tick_size_percentage 2.
cases.steps: 1. Create the stage. 2. Read the line validations.
cases.expected: Stage created; validations.default holds all four values unchanged. Desired: refuse ceil < floor and tick > ceil−floor. (The dashboard's conversion screen leaves only these three columns editable.)
cases.oracle: Line validations in `GET /trade/<id>`.

cases.section: Bidding in a live auction (needs a vendor session — markdown only)
cases.title: Re-submitting exactly the same price is not stopped by the tick rule
cases.why: A zero difference is explicitly skipped, so a vendor can re-submit to bump the timestamp (and in the last minutes trigger an extension under the rank strategy).
cases.steps: 1. Revise at 1000 again.
cases.expected: Not refused by 214 (`!price_difference.zero?`). Record whether a new bid row and an extension result.
cases.oracle: Bid history; schedules.

cases.section: Bidding in a live auction (needs a vendor session — markdown only)
cases.title: The tick is measured against the vendor's own last bid, in either direction
cases.why: The tick is not relative to L1, and `abs` means an INCREASE by more than the tick also passes the tick rule (only the price-increase rule, 300, can stop it).
cases.setup: As 065; vendor A at 1000, vendor B (L1) at 900; `is_price_increase_allowed` true on the stage.
cases.steps: 1. A revises to 989 (beats own by 11, still above L1). 2. A revises to 1100.
cases.expected: Step 1 accepted (tick vs own bid). Step 2 passes the tick rule; accepted because increases are allowed.
cases.oracle: Bid outcomes.

cases.section: Bidding in a live auction (needs a vendor session — markdown only)
cases.title: A percentage tick is converted to a value from the previous bid
cases.why: 2 % of the previous price, not of the start; a cheaper bid needs a smaller absolute move.
cases.setup: tick_size_percentage 2 on the line; vendor at 1000.
cases.steps: 1. Revise to 985. 2. Revise to 980.
cases.oracle: 422 + 214 / accepted.

cases.section: Bidding in a live auction (needs a vendor session — markdown only)
cases.title: In the last five minutes a single-line bid can never go up — measured on the original end time
cases.why: Applies to every non-sell stage (RFQs too) and uses `bid_end_time`, not the extended end — after a dynamic extension the window may be wrong.
cases.setup: Single-line live auction, increases allowed; vendor at 1000; 4 minutes left.
cases.steps: 1. Revise to 1010. 2. After a dynamic extension pushes the end out, repeat.
cases.expected: 300 'You cannot increase the price' in both cases while within 5 minutes of bid_end_time; record which end time is used after an extension.
cases.oracle: Codes.

cases.section: Bidding in a live auction (needs a vendor session — markdown only)
cases.title: A bid at a price another vendor already holds is refused when ties are off
cases.why: With ties off, the second vendor must quote a different price.
cases.setup: Live auction, config is_tie_bid_allowed false; vendor B holds 900.
cases.steps: 1. Vendor A bids 900 (single line, then a multi-line stage).
cases.expected: 98 'A bid at this price already exists, please quote a different price.' in both layouts; RFQ and offline stages are exempt; re-quoting your OWN price is not a tie.

cases.section: Bidding in a live auction (needs a vendor session — markdown only)
cases.title: Quantity rules in an auction bid
cases.why: Fixed-quantity auctions must be bid for the full quantity; floor quantity protects minimum lots.
cases.setup: Lines with allow_fixed_quantity_for_bidding, floor_quantity 5, over/under quantity off.
cases.steps: 1. Bid quantity ≠ auction quantity. 2. Above. 3. Below. 4. Below floor.
cases.expected: 207 'Bid Quantity should be equal to the Auction Quantity'; 138; 139; 39.
cases.oracle: Codes.

cases.section: Bidding in a live auction (needs a vendor session — markdown only)
cases.title: A bid after the auction has ended is refused
cases.why: The window is the auction; anything after it is a buyer action (surrogate in extra closing time) or a counter-offer flow.
cases.setup: Auction just ended; vendor session.
cases.steps: 1. Revise the bid.
cases.expected: 422 code 33 (or 101 when the buyer can edit bids). A buyer surrogate bid is allowed only during the auction's extra closing time.
cases.oracle: Codes.

cases.section: Dynamic extension during a live auction (markdown only)
cases.title: There is no cap on the number of extensions
cases.why: Two vendors trading bids can extend forever; the only brake is a sealed-bid suggestion shown after 5 extensions.
cases.steps: 1. Trigger 6 extensions. 2. Read the stage as the buyer.
cases.expected: All 6 applied; config.show_sealbid_feature_notification true after the 6th.
cases.oracle: Extension count; config flag.

cases.section: Dynamic extension during a live auction (markdown only)
cases.title: Rank-based extension fires only when the change touches the top N
cases.why: Movement below the limit must not keep the auction open.
cases.setup: As 075, rank limit 2.
cases.steps: 1. In the trigger window, a vendor moves from rank 5 to 4. 2. Another from 3 to 1.
cases.expected: 1 → no extension; 2 → extension.
cases.oracle: Schedules.

cases.section: Dynamic extension during a live auction (markdown only)
cases.title: Price-based extension needs a better price within the rank limit
cases.why: A worse re-bid must not extend.
cases.setup: Strategy price_based, rank limit 3.
cases.steps: 1. In the window, a rank-2 vendor improves its price. 2. A rank-5 vendor improves. 3. A rank-1 vendor re-bids higher (increase allowed).
cases.expected: Only 1 extends.
cases.oracle: Schedules.

cases.section: Dynamic extension during a live auction (markdown only)
cases.title: Price-based extension with no rank limit breaks the vendor's last-minute bid
cases.why: `new_rank <= nil` / the Integer sig on `dynamic_time_extension_applicable_for_price?` raise for a missing limit — and nothing at set-up requires the limit.
cases.setup: Extension on, price_based, rank_limit_for_time_extension null.
cases.steps: 1. In the window, a vendor improves price.
cases.expected: Desired: limit required at set-up. Today: error during save_scores_on_line_item (after commit).
cases.oracle: Vendor reply; extension absent.

cases.section: What a vendor sees: rank, price, colour, ties (markdown only)
cases.title: Two vendors tied at the best price are both shown rank 2 — nobody is rank 1
cases.why: There is no timestamp tie-break: ranks are dense, and when more than one vendor holds the best score every rank shifts by one. Vendors read "rank 2" as "someone beat me" and cut again.
cases.setup: Live rank auction, ties allowed; vendor A 900, vendor B 900, vendor C 950.
cases.steps: 1. Read each vendor's rank (vendor view and buyer bid cards).
cases.expected: A → 2, B → 2, C → 3 (sorted unique scores [900, 950] → 1, 2; best rank shared → +1). Confirm this is the intended product rule; if "earlier bid wins" is expected, this is a defect.
cases.oracle: Rank values in indicators and bid list.

cases.title: Accepting a knockout offer on a stage that is not a knockout is refused
cases.why: The accept endpoints have no permission check at all; the stage lookup is the first line of defence.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ (auction_config defaults to rank). Refused before any write.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /bids/accept_knockout_offer` with `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{tradeId}}", "accepted_round_no": 1}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 95 'Trade Request not found'.

cases.title: Accepting a dutch offer on a stage that is not a dutch auction is refused
cases.why: A dutch acceptance creates AND closes (awards) a bid in one call — the most destructive single request in the auction family.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ. Refused before any write.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /bids/accept_dutch_offer` with `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{tradeId}}", "accepted_round_no": 1, "participant_quantity": 10}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 95 'Trade Request not found'.

cases.title: Accepting a round that is not running, or as a non-participant, is refused
cases.why: Only the current round's participants may take its price.
cases.setup: A running knockout; vendor V in round 2's participants, vendor W knocked out.
cases.steps: 1. V accepts round 1 (finished). 2. W accepts round 2. 3. The buyer accepts round 2.
cases.expected: 1 → 457 'No such offer exists!'; 2 and 3 → 458 'You cannot participate in this offer !'.
cases.oracle: Codes.

cases.title: The same round cannot be accepted twice; a dutch price only once in total
cases.why: Double acceptance would double the vendor's bid revisions or awards.
cases.setup: Running knockout and dutch auctions.
cases.steps: 1. In the knockout, V accepts round 2 twice. 2. In the dutch, V accepts round 1 then round 2.
cases.expected: 1 → second call 459 'You have already accepted this offer, please wait for the next one.'; 2 → second call 458.
cases.oracle: Codes; one acceptance recorded.

cases.section: Reports and reads during and after an auction
cases.title: The auction report renders for the converted, closed auction
cases.why: Post-auction analytics are what the buyer shows management.

cases.expected: HTTP 200 with the QA vendor's carried-over and auction bids in prices_graph_data and the auction's end.
cases.oracle: Reply content.

cases.why: The data behind the buyer's rank/colour cards.

cases.expected: HTTP 200 with auction_identifiers + auction_identifiers_data including the rank indicator ({} only when event masking applies to the caller).
cases.oracle: Reply content.

cases.why: `authorize(nil)` runs before the nil check; Pundit cannot find a policy for nil and raises NotDefinedError, which is not rescued (only NotAuthorizedError is).

cases.steps: 1. `GET /v1/trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/alternate_bidding_leader_board`.
cases.expected: A 4xx. Today 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Reports and reads during and after an auction
cases.title: Bidding summary for a user who cannot view the event returns an empty success
cases.why: The action does `return 510, 422` instead of rendering the error, so Rails falls through to an implicit render — the caller gets an empty 2xx (or a template error) instead of 510 'You are not allowed to view this event'.
cases.setup: A buyer of the same company with no view access to the event (needs a second user).
cases.steps: 1. As that user, `GET /trade/<id>/event_summary`.
cases.expected: Desired 422 code 510. Record the actual status/body (likely 204 or an HTML missing-template error).
cases.oracle: Status + body.

cases.section: Auction terms acceptance and live audience changes
cases.title: The buyer cannot accept the auction terms on a vendor's behalf
cases.why: Only a participant company can accept; the buyer passes the policy but no participant company resolves for them.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ (no technical responses; buyer's company not in the audience). Refused before the write.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/accept_auction_tnc` with `{}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'; misc.tnc_popup_acceptances unchanged.

cases.section: Auction terms acceptance and live audience changes
cases.title: Accepting the auction terms is recorded but never enforced
cases.why: The acceptance is stored once per company (the first acceptance is kept forever, later users are no-ops) and only surfaced to the client; the bid endpoints do not check it, so an API client can bid without accepting.
cases.setup: Live auction with is_tnc_mandatory true; vendor who has not accepted (vendor session).
cases.steps: 1. Place a bid via the API without calling accept_auction_tnc. 2. Accept as user A, then as user B of the same company.
cases.expected: Desired: bid refused until accepted. Today: bid accepted. Step 2: only A's acceptance stored.
cases.oracle: Bid outcome; misc.tnc_popup_acceptances.

cases.section: Auction terms acceptance and live audience changes
cases.title: Vendors can still be added to an auction that has ended
cases.why: There is no time check — only status active/draft. Added vendors are mailed "update_audience" for an event that is over.
cases.setup: auction.convert ticked; no vendor list sent, so nothing can be added.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /v1/trade/add_audience?id={{auctionTradeUuid}}` with only update_remarks.
cases.expected: Refused — today with code 2 (every other gate passed) while the auction is still status active; code 95 once the award closed it. Desired: refused as ended.
cases.oracle: 422 + which code.

cases.section: Auction terms acceptance and live audience changes
cases.title: Adding a vendor to a draft knockout crashes
cases.why: Draft knockouts have no rounds yet (rounds are created only when published active), but adding audience edits the rounds and `T.must(nil)` raises — the buyer cannot prepare a knockout's audience before publishing.
cases.setup: A draft knockout auction (auction-team conversion).
cases.steps: 1. add_audience one QA vendor.
cases.expected: Desired: vendor added; rounds built on activation. Today: TypeError from T.must → 500.
cases.oracle: Status; audience.

cases.section: Which auction types exist, and what the conversion accepts
cases.title: A conversion with no auction type silently becomes a rank auction
cases.why: A client bug that drops the type should be refused; instead the buyer gets a rank auction they did not choose, with rank visibility rules for the vendors.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ; base body with the backstop.
cases.steps: 1. Send the base body with `configurations.auction_config = null`. 2. Read the error.
cases.expected: Today the request passes every configuration check (the type defaults to rank) and is stopped only by the bogus delivery location: HTTP 422 code 125 'Delivery location not found'. A future "type is required" guard would change this message — then update the case.
cases.oracle: 422 + 125 proves the request reached line-item creation.

cases.section: Which auction types exist, and what the conversion accepts
cases.title: Book building can be chosen through the conversion although the screen never offers it
cases.why: The dashboard's conversion screen has no book-building tab, and the create path guards book building in baskets (474), but the conversion accepts it. A book-building auction behaves completely differently (booked quantity, no prefilled values).
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ; base body with the backstop.
cases.steps: 1. Send the base body with `configurations.auction_config = "book_building"`.
cases.expected: Today HTTP 422 code 125 'Delivery location not found' — book building only forces line-item closing and passes. Desired: refused as not allowed for a conversion.

cases.section: Which auction types exist, and what the conversion accepts
cases.title: "Rank and price" exists in the API but cannot be chosen in the dashboard
cases.why: `rank_and_price` (vendor sees both rank and best price) is a valid type that drives rank and best-price widgets, but the dashboard's strategy tabs offer only rank, price, traffic light, knockout and dutch. An event created through the API or MCP in this mode shows indicators the buyer cannot reproduce or edit.
cases.setup: Needs `POST /trade/template_input` (cannot run here) for creation; reading works.
cases.steps: 1. Create an auction stage with `auction_config: "rank_and_price"` via template_input. 2. Open it in the dashboard's configuration drawer. 3. As a vendor, open the live auction.
cases.expected: Backend accepts it; vendor sees rank AND best price (`should_show_rank?`, `is_best_price_required?`). The drawer shows no matching tab — record what it shows (it should not silently switch the strategy on save).
cases.oracle: `GET /trade/<id>` → auction_config rank_and_price; drawer state.

cases.section: Which auction types exist, and what the conversion accepts
cases.title: The English-auction flag is ignored unless the template allows English auctions
cases.why: `is_english_auction_enabled: true` is only honoured when the template configuration carries `is_english_auction_allowed`; otherwise it is silently dropped and the buyer believes vendors see the best price.
cases.setup: template_input (cannot run here). Two templates: one with `is_english_auction_allowed: true`, one without.
cases.steps: 1. Create a rank auction with `is_english_auction_enabled: true` on each template. 2. Read both stages.
cases.expected: Allowed template → config.is_english_auction_enabled true and `other_auction_indicators_config.best_price` true. Other template → flag absent, no error returned to the buyer.
cases.oracle: `GET /trade/<id>` config of each stage.

cases.section: Which auction types exist, and what the conversion accepts
cases.title: Knockout and dutch auctions never appear in a vendor's "participated auctions" list
cases.why: The vendor feed of running auctions filters out auction_config 4 and 5, so a vendor in a knockout or dutch auction cannot find it from that list on mobile.
cases.setup: Needs a vendor session and a running knockout auction the vendor has bid in.
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, `GET /v1/trade/get_participated_auctions` during a running rank auction and during a running knockout auction.
cases.expected: The rank auction is listed; the knockout auction is not (by design of the query). Confirm with product whether this is intended.
cases.oracle: participated_auctions contents.

cases.section: Converting an RFQ into an auction — which stage, which state, which order
cases.title: A conversion request with no stage id is answered "not found", not "missing parameter"
cases.why: The one mandatory field has no presence check; client bugs that drop it look like a deleted stage.
cases.setup: None.
cases.steps: 1. Send the base body without `trade_request_uuid`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 95 'Trade Request not found' (where(id: nil)). Desired: code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

cases.section: Converting an RFQ into an auction — which stage, which state, which order
cases.title: A multi-item line-wise RFQ cannot become a lot auction, and the message talks about awarding
cases.why: The refusal is correct but reuses code 503 "You cannot award entire lot when RFQ was done for partial lot." — a buyer converting (not awarding) cannot understand it.
cases.setup: A published multi-item RFQ closed line-item-wise (cannot run here: the sandbox has one item).
cases.steps: 1. Convert with `configurations.auction_closing_mode = "lot_based"`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 503 before any row checks. Desired: a conversion-specific message.

cases.section: Converting an RFQ into an auction — which stage, which state, which order
cases.title: Unaccepted unregistered-vendor quotes are not carried into the auction
cases.why: Quotes from unregistered vendors count only after the buyer accepted them; carrying the rest would rank a vendor nobody approved.
cases.setup: An RFQ with one unregistered-vendor quote not accepted (needs the unregistered flow).
cases.steps: 1. Convert with quotes as bids. 2. Read the auction's bids.
cases.expected: That quote is absent from the auction; accepted ones are present.
cases.oracle: Auction bids list.

cases.section: Conversion request shapes the controller does not guard
cases.title: Line rows sent as one object instead of a list crash the conversion
cases.why: No type check on `data` before iterating it.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ.
cases.steps: 1. Send the base body with `data` = the row object itself (not wrapped in an array).
cases.expected: A 4xx. Today each key/value pair is an Array and `Array#[](:creator_quantity)` raises TypeError → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Conversion request shapes the controller does not guard
cases.title: Line rows sent as text crash the conversion
cases.why: Same gap as 019 with a scalar.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ.
cases.steps: 1. Send the base body with `data = "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}"`.
cases.expected: A 4xx. Today String has no `each` → NoMethodError → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Conversion request shapes the controller does not guard
cases.title: A line row without a quantity crashes the conversion
cases.why: Quantity is mandatory for an auction line but nothing checks it is present when the unit comes from `product.unit_type`.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ.
cases.steps: 1. Send the base body with `creator_quantity` removed and `product.unit_type = "KG"`.
cases.expected: A 4xx. Today `item[:creator_quantity][:value]` on nil → NoMethodError → 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Conversion request shapes the controller does not guard
cases.title: Two unknown units are both named in the refusal
cases.why: EDGE-AWD-084 pins the singular message; this pins the plural branch and the lower-casing the buyer actually sees.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ.
cases.steps: 1. Send two rows with units `QA_PLATFORM_U1` and `QA_PLATFORM_U2`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 495 with 'The units qa_platform_u1, qa_platform_u2 are not present'.
cases.oracle: 422 + exact text.

cases.section: Conversion request shapes the controller does not guard
cases.title: An auction window entirely in the past is accepted
cases.why: Conversion closes the RFQ; pairing that with an auction that is already over leaves the vendors no round at all.
cases.setup: Sandbox RFQ; base body with the backstop.
cases.expected: Today HTTP 422 code 125 'Delivery location not found'. Desired: refused as a past window.

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: A trigger window longer than half the remaining auction is refused
cases.why: The half-window rule is the only time check the conversion runs on its own window.
cases.setup: As 029; window placed in 2000 so half of the remaining time is negative.
cases.steps: 1. Send the extension on with trigger 600 minutes and end 2000-01-01 01:00.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 501.

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: The extension flag sent as the text "false" switches extension ON
cases.why: A client that serialises booleans as text turns anti-sniping on when it meant off, and the buyer then gets a trigger-window error they never asked for.
cases.steps: 1. Send `is_dynamic_closing_time_allowed: "false"` and no trigger window.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 501 — the string is truthy. Desired: cast to boolean.

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: A one-minute trigger with a long window passes the extension check
cases.why: Boundary pair with 030: 0 refused, 1 accepted.
cases.setup: As 029; window in 2100.
cases.steps: 1. Send the extension on with trigger 1, extend 2, rank limit 3.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 125 'Delivery location not found' — the extension check passed. A 501 here is a regression.

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: An unknown extension strategy is stored and the extension never fires
cases.why: Neither the rank_based nor the price_based branch matches in the live auction, so the protection the buyer switched on silently does nothing.
cases.steps: 1. Send the extension on, trigger 1, `dynamic_closing_time_strategy: "qa_platform_strategy"`.
cases.expected: Today HTTP 422 code 125 'Delivery location not found'. Desired: refused (rank_based | price_based).

cases.section: The auction configuration block, as validated by the conversion
cases.title: A dutch price step bigger than the whole range is refused
cases.why: Runnable conversion twin of STG-052.
cases.steps: 1. Send dutch buy 100 → 200 with `price_difference 500`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 243 'Invalid Tick Size'.

cases.title: Savings set-up is not carried into the auction, and a lost reference is only logged
cases.why: The auction starts with savings_data/savings_configuration removed; if the RFQ's reference prices do not survive, the buyer gets no error — only a Sentry event — and savings reports go blank.
cases.setup: An RFQ with a lot-based savings configuration (needs template set-up).
cases.steps: 1. Convert. 2. Read the auction's savings configuration and the savings report.
cases.expected: Savings re-derived for the auction from the request; any missing reference key raises "Savings configuration is not present in Auction" to Sentry and the request still returns 200.
cases.oracle: Auction misc.savings_configuration vs RFQ.

cases.title: Weighted scoring is copied only when asked
cases.why: A weighted RFQ converted without `transfer_weights` ranks the auction on plain price.
cases.setup: A weighted RFQ (line-item weights).
cases.steps: 1. Convert with transfer_weights false; 2. on a copy with true.
cases.expected: True → weightages duplicated per new line; false → none.
cases.oracle: Weightage rows on the auction.

cases.title: Auction reminder mails are scheduled 24 hours and 30 minutes before the start
cases.why: Vendors join late without them; a start under 30 minutes away gets no reminder at all.
cases.setup: Successful conversions with starts 2 days, 2 hours and 10 minutes ahead.
cases.steps: 1. Convert each. 2. Inspect scheduled EmailNotificationWorker jobs.
cases.expected: 2 days → both reminders; 2 hours → only the 30-minute one; 10 minutes → none.
cases.oracle: Sidekiq scheduled set.

cases.title: Only one live auction per RFQ — but a draft auction does not block a second at model level
cases.why: The controller's 94 guard counts drafts; the model validation does not (`not_draft_or_cancelled_or_withdrawn`). Any path that bypasses the controller (MCP, clone) can create a second auction while the first is a draft.
cases.setup: An auction-team company (draft conversions).
cases.steps: 1. Convert (draft). 2. Convert again via the controller. 3. Via any non-controller creation path.
cases.expected: Step 2 → 94. Step 3 should also be refused; record what happens.
cases.oracle: Number of children of the RFQ.
