cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 570 (Approval Flow not found), or 455 when the caller lacks approval-flow read permission (checked first).
cases.oracle: 422 with code 570 or 455.

cases.section: Starting an approval by hand and reading flows
cases.title: The approval types on offer depend on the company's modules and settings
cases.why: Award approval (close_event_group) and technical-evaluation approval are only offered when `rfx_project_enabled` is on; bid selection, creation and surrogate approvals need the trade module.
cases.setup: Buyer session.
cases.steps: `GET /approval_workflow/approval_flows/trigger_conditions`. 1. Read the approval types.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with approvals_types including create_trade and close_trade; close_event_group only when rfx_project_enabled is on. Never 5xx.
cases.oracle: Keys present.

cases.title: Reading a delegation that does not exist is refused
cases.why: The delegation drawer loads by id.
cases.setup: None.
cases.steps: `GET /delegations/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`. 1. Read delegation 999999999.
cases.expected: HTTP 404, code 679 'Delegation not found' (lookup before the policy).

cases.title: A delegation without a start time crashes
cases.why: `Time.at(params['start_time'])` with nil raises TypeError → 500 instead of 422.
cases.setup: v2 company; caller has no active delegation. Not twinned: if the crash is fixed by defaulting, a real delegation would be created for the run's buyer.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /delegations` with `delegation_type: all_approvals`, a delegatee and an end_time but no start_time.
cases.expected: Should be 422. Today: 500.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: A user can delegate approvals to themselves
cases.why: No check that delegatee differs from delegator; the delegation is created and every pending approval gets a duplicate approver row for the same user.
cases.setup: v2; caller without delegations.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /delegations` with delegatee_uuid = own uuid.
cases.expected: Should be refused. Today: created.
cases.oracle: Delegation exists with delegator = delegatee.

cases.title: An escalated-to user sees the request but cannot decide it
cases.why: Escalation is notify-only: it logs the escalation and mails the target; it does not add an approver identifier.
cases.setup: Escalation matrix module on; a rule escalating step approver X to user E; step expired.
cases.steps: 1. E lists view_type escalated_to_me. 2. E resolves the approver row.
cases.expected: 1 lists it; 2 → 422 code 4.
cases.oracle: As above.

cases.title: An e-mail rejection without a comment is acknowledged but does nothing
cases.why: The controller answers success after queuing the worker; the worker then returns `requires_comment` without rejecting. The approver believes they rejected.
cases.setup: Email approvals enabled; a pending award approval.
cases.steps: 1. Reply "reject" with no comment.
cases.expected: Approver is told a comment is required; today the API said success and the approval stays pending.
cases.oracle: Approval still pending.

cases.title: An e-mail decision by someone who is not an approver fails with an unrelated message
cases.why: The worker raises code 701, whose text is about editing a Procol employee.
cases.setup: Email approvals enabled; a reply from a user who is not on the current step.
cases.steps: 1. Send an approve reply from that address.
cases.expected: Refused — with a message about not being an approver; today 701 'You are not allowed to edit details of Procol Employee'.
cases.oracle: Worker log / notification text.

journeys.title: Turning purchase requests into an event
journeys.goal: Pick approved purchase-request lines — all or some, all or part of their quantity — pull them into a draft event, and keep each request's open quantity right as the event is awarded, withdrawn or the line is closed.

cases.title: The cart caps quantity at the line's open quantity and locks the unit
cases.why: Partial selection happens here: the buyer can lower a line's quantity but not exceed what is open or change the unit.
cases.setup: A material PR line with 100 open.
cases.steps: Open the cart; type 150, then 0, then 40; try the unit dropdown.
cases.expected: The number box clamps to 100 max and 0.1 min; the unit select is disabled and shows the PR unit; 40 is kept.
cases.oracle: Field value after blur; request body `quantity.value` = 40, `unitSymbol` = PR unit.

cases.title: "Purchase Items" appears only on the Open tab and only with PR collation on
cases.why: It is the only entry from the PR page into sourcing; showing it elsewhere (e.g. In progress) would let buyers re-source lines already in events.
cases.setup: gate: `is_pr_collation_enabled`. A buyer with PR lines in Open and In-progress.
cases.steps: Open the PR page; switch tabs; select a line on each.
cases.expected: The shopping-cart "Purchase Items (n)" button shows only on Open, with the selected count. With collation off it never shows.
cases.oracle: Button presence per tab; count tag equals selection.

cases.title: "Purchase Items" is disabled with a reason for lines that cannot be sourced together
cases.why: The screen is the first line of defence for rules the API does not enforce (see API-XDPRE-040).
cases.setup: Lines that are dormant-locked (dormant feature on), rejected / send-back pending, two BOQ PRs, a BOQ plus a material PR, services plus materials with service grouping on.
cases.steps: Select each combination and hover the button.
cases.expected: Disabled with: "Dormant locked PR cannot be purchased" · "Rejected or Send Back Pending PR cannot be purchased" · "Multiple BOQ-based PR cannot be purchased together" · "BOQ-based PR cannot pe purchased along with Material PR" (typo "pe" is in the product) · "Services and Materials cannot be purchased together".
cases.oracle: Tooltip text and disabled state.

cases.title: "Add to Draft Project" is offered only when four conditions hold
cases.why: The option depends on `allow_draft_project_creation`, a non-BOQ selection, no service lines AND `group_service_activities_in_rfp` being on. The last condition hides the option for every company without service grouping — confirm with product whether that is intended.
cases.setup: Toggle each of the four conditions.
cases.steps: Open the Purchase Items menu.
cases.expected: "Start New Project" always; "Add to Draft Project" only when all four hold; with the contract module on, both sit under a "Purchase Item" sub-menu next to "Purchase Contract".
cases.oracle: Menu items present.

cases.title: Clearing a cart quantity sends no quantity at all
cases.why: An emptied number box sends `value: null`: "Start New Project" then creates a rate-only line (API-XDPRE-056) and "Add Items" fails with a generic toast (API-XDPRE-031).
cases.setup: A material PR line in the cart.
cases.steps: Clear the quantity box; use each action.
cases.expected: Desired: the action is blocked until a quantity is entered. Today: as described.
cases.oracle: Request body; resulting line / toast.

cases.title: "Add Items" reports success with the draft's reference and refreshes the PR list
cases.why: The PR list must show the moved quantities without a manual reload.
cases.setup: gate: `allow_draft_project_creation`. A PR-based draft; an open PR line.
cases.steps: Add the line to the draft.
cases.expected: Toast "Items successfully added to draft <ref>"; the line's open quantity drops; on failure "Failed to add items to draft <ref>" and nothing changes.
cases.oracle: Toast; PR row values.

cases.title: "Start New Project" creates a draft and opens the creation screen pre-filled
cases.why: The PR-to-event hand-off; the draft's line ids must be matched back to PR lines.
cases.setup: eRFX workspace; two material PR lines.
cases.steps: Start New Project; choose stages.
cases.expected: Loading message "Redirecting to project creation screen..."; redirect to quick-create with `fromPR=true&projectCreation=true` (plus `boqProject=true` for BOQ); each line linked to its PR line.
cases.oracle: URL; `POST /event_groups` body carries `pr_line_item_uuid` per line.

cases.title: "Partially Closed" appears only where and when it should
cases.why: Closure is irreversible; it must be offered only with the feature on, with a selection, and never on a mixed selection.
cases.setup: gate: `is_pr_partial_closure_enabled` with a custom `closure_label`.
cases.steps: In-progress tab → Actions; Open tab → assignment menu; select lines of two closure types.
cases.expected: The item shows the configured label (default "Partially Closed"), is disabled with no selection, and a mixed selection shows "Selected items have different closure types".
cases.oracle: Menu state; warning text.

cases.title: The partial-closure drawer insists on a reason and remarks
cases.why: Matches the API rungs (reason, then remarks) with friendlier words.
cases.setup: Feature on with configured reasons.
cases.steps: Submit with no reason; with spaces-only remarks; then valid.
cases.expected: "Please select a closure reason"; submit disabled while remarks are blank after trimming; success "Items marked as partially closed successfully".
cases.oracle: Messages; request sent only on the valid attempt.

cases.title: Service and activity lines cannot have their quantity edited in the cart
cases.why: Service quantities come from activities; editing them in the cart would desync.
cases.setup: A service PR line with activities.
cases.steps: Open the cart.
cases.expected: The quantity box is greyed and disabled for service and activity lines; the label shows the short text instead of code | name.
cases.oracle: Disabled state.

cases.title: The cart's create button waits for content
cases.why: Double clicks or an empty cart must not create empty drafts.
cases.setup: Cart with lines, then remove all; a BOQ line whose BOQ data is still loading.
cases.steps: Watch the create / Add Items buttons.
cases.expected: Disabled when the cart is empty, while a create is in flight, or while BOQ data has not loaded.
cases.oracle: Disabled state.

cases.title: The draft picker lists only PR-based drafts and says so when none match
cases.why: Buyers search their drafts by name; an empty result must explain why a draft they know exists is missing (it has no PR lines).
cases.setup: One PR-based draft and one catalog-only draft.
cases.steps: "Add to Draft Project" → open the picker; search both names.
cases.expected: Only the PR-based draft is listed; the other search shows "You don't have any PR based draft projects named <query>".
cases.oracle: Options; empty-state text.

cases.title: A PR-created event locks template choice and Recreate
cases.why: PR-created events take their layout from the PR; switching templates or recreating would lose the PR link.
cases.setup: A PR-created event (BOQ, or with tabs); a published PR-created event.
cases.steps: On creation, open template selection; on the live event, open the settings menu.
cases.expected: Template selection disabled; "Recreate" disabled. PR-created is detected by the PR-number widget on the stage.
cases.oracle: Disabled controls.

cases.title: Savings reference is frozen to historical price when the company asks
cases.why: `freeze_pr_savings_reference` keeps savings on PR events measured against the PR's last price.
cases.setup: gate: `freeze_pr_savings_reference` ON; a PR-created event.
cases.steps: Open "Add Savings".
cases.expected: The historical-price strategy is locked.
cases.oracle: Strategy control state.

cases.title: The assignee can only be changed while every selected line is fully open
cases.why: Once part of a line is in an event the assignee is the person running that event.
cases.setup: Two lines: one fully open, one partly in a draft.
cases.steps: Select each and open the assign control.
cases.expected: Enabled only when every selected line's open quantity equals its requested quantity.
cases.oracle: Disabled state.

cases.title: "Map to Existing Event" lists only eligible live events
cases.why: The drawer is the screen side of pr_linking (section 9).
cases.setup: gate: `pr_linking_enabled`; open PR lines; a matching active non-PR event.
cases.steps: Select lines → Map to Existing Event.
cases.expected: The option is disabled without a selection or with the setting off; the drawer lists active non-PR events from the search API; the submit button stays disabled until an event is chosen.
cases.oracle: Menu and drawer states; `POST /event_groups/search` called with the line uuids.

cases.title: Selection checkboxes appear only for multi-select users or the purchase team
cases.why: Without selection there is no way into the cart; the gate must match the role.
cases.setup: A user with `canSelectMultiplePrs` off and not in a purchase team; then one in a purchase team.
cases.steps: Open the PR page.
cases.expected: No checkboxes for the first user; checkboxes for the second.
cases.oracle: Checkbox column present.

cases.section: Moving an RFQ to auction or lots
cases.title: Bids carried from the RFQ into the auction keep only the auction's lines and start clean
cases.why: Vendors start the auction from their RFQ price; a carried bid with the RFQ's approval state, a TNA line or a line not in the auction distorts the opening rank.
cases.setup: RFQ with 3 lines; vendor A bid on all 3 (line 3 scored TNA for A); vendor B bid only on line 3; A's RFQ bid was approved. Auction with fast bidding made from lines 1–3; a second auction with lines 1–2.
cases.steps: Move to auction; read the carried bids.
cases.expected: Line saves are not checked (`save` without a result check), so a failed line leaves an empty id in the bid's line list (unverified).
cases.oracle: `create_duplicate_bids` (`bids_controller_helper.rb:1745-1800`).

cases.section: Pulling PR lines into an event that is not a draft
cases.title: PR lines cannot be pulled into a published event
cases.why: "Add to draft" is only defined for drafts. If a live event could grow new PR-backed lines, vendors would be bidding on a sheet that changed under them and the PR would show quantity reserved by an event that never asked for it.
cases.setup: The sandbox event is published (active, window open, no bids). `{{prItemId}}` is a real PR line; the request is refused before any write.
cases.steps: Send exactly what the PR screen's "Add Items" button sends, aimed at the live event: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/pri_to_draft_project` with `{"line_items":[{"status":"draft","quantity":{"unitSymbol":"Nos","value":1},"product_uuid":"{{productUuid}}","product_quality_uuid":"{{productQualityUuid}}","pr_line_item_uuid":"{{prItemId}}"}]}`. Then read the PR back.
cases.expected: Refused as bad input; nothing is added to the event and the PR line's open quantity does not move. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters' — the target is looked up only among DRAFT events of the workspace, so the live event is "not found" and the blank guard answers before the PR service is built.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2; `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_line_items` unchanged; `GET /purchase_requests/{{prId}}` shows the same open quantity as before. Note: the older PR-EVT-005 sends a huge quantity to this same sandbox expecting 557 — it can only ever get this code 2.

cases.section: Pulling PR lines into an event that is not a draft
cases.title: A live event's own line cannot be pulled into the PR flow by its uuid
cases.why: The line `uuid` field is the most dangerous field in this body: on a draft target, the line lookup is NOT scoped to the target event, so a known line uuid is re-homed (see API-XDPRE-047). The draft guard is what keeps a running event's line safe.
cases.setup: Published sandbox; `{{lineItemUuid}}` is one of its active lines.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/pri_to_draft_project` with one line carrying `"uuid": "{{lineItemUuid}}"` and a bogus PR reference. Read the event's lines back.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. The sandbox line stays where it is, still active.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2; `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_line_items` unchanged.

cases.section: Who may add PR lines to a draft
cases.title: A user without event-create permission cannot pull PR lines
cases.why: The very first line of the action authorises "create event"; a planner or viewer who can see PRs must not be able to build events from them.
cases.setup: A console user whose teams lack `trade: create_record`; a QA draft in the same company. No twin: needs a second, restricted user session.
cases.steps: As that user, `POST /event_groups/<draft>/pri_to_draft_project` with a valid body.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action' (Pundit's NotAuthorizedError handler). Nothing written.
cases.oracle: 455; the draft's lines and the PR line unchanged.

cases.section: Who may add PR lines to a draft
cases.title: Another company's draft cannot be targeted, even with its real uuid
cases.why: The draft lookup is scoped to the caller's workspace; this is the tenancy wall for the whole endpoint.
cases.setup: A draft uuid from a different client company (e.g. Demo Account 2's QA draft). No twin: needs a second tenant's draft uuid.
cases.steps: As the PROCOL DEMO buyer, `POST /event_groups/<foreign draft>/pri_to_draft_project`.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters' — identical to a missing id.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2; the foreign draft is unchanged.

cases.section: Quantities when pulling into a draft
cases.title: Pulling part of a PR line reserves exactly that part
cases.why: The everyday flow: source 40 of a 100-unit line now, keep 60 open for later. The PR page must show 40 in progress and 60 open straight away.
cases.setup: gate: `allow_draft_project_creation` ON. A QA draft that already has one line; a QA PR line of 100 Nos, fully open. No twin: needs a draft and a disposable PR line.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/<draft>/pri_to_draft_project` with that PR line at quantity 40. Then read the PR in the Open and In-progress tabs.
cases.expected: 200 `{"message":"success"}`. The draft gains one line of 40 linked to the PR line; the PR line's `meta_data.draft_projects_quantity_data[<draft id>] = 40`, its quantity in progress becomes 40, open becomes 60, and its status moves to in_progress.
cases.oracle: `GET /purchase_requests?filters={"status":["active"]}` shows quantity_open 60; `{"status":["in_progress"]}` shows 40 with the draft in event_details.

cases.section: Quantities when pulling into a draft
cases.title: More than the open quantity (plus tolerance) is refused
cases.why: Sourcing more than was requisitioned is an approval bypass.
cases.setup: Tolerance 0; a QA PR line with 100 open; a QA draft with one line. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull the line at 101.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 557 'Purchase request items are not valid' (no hint WHICH line or why). Nothing written.
cases.oracle: 557; PR line still 100 open.

cases.section: Quantities when pulling into a draft
cases.title: A negative quantity is accepted (no sign check)
cases.why: Once published, line quantities are SUMMED into the PR's in-progress figure, so a negative line lowers it and inflates the PR's open quantity — the same requisition can then be sourced twice.
cases.setup: A QA PR line of 100; a QA draft with one line. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull the line at -5; read the draft; publish it; read the PR.
cases.expected: Desired: HTTP 422 refusal. Today the validator only checks "more than allowed" and the line is stored with -5 (record as a defect if so).
cases.oracle: Draft line quantity; PR open/in-progress after publish.

cases.section: Quantities when pulling into a draft
cases.title: The first PR lines into a draft that has never had a line skip every check
cases.why: The validator returns "valid" immediately when the draft has no lines at all, so the quantity cap, the "already in this draft" rule and the "PR line exists" rule are all skipped. The dashboard's BOQ drafts and freshly emptied drafts hit this.
cases.setup: A QA BOQ draft created with no line items (workspace allows BOQ-in-eRFX); a QA PR line of 100. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull the PR line at 1,000.
cases.expected: Desired: 557. Today: accepted and 1,000 reserved against a 100-unit line (record as defect).
cases.oracle: PR line's draft reservation and open quantity.

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: The same PR line in a second draft is limited to what is left
cases.why: Buyers split one requisition across events; the second event must only get the remainder, and the PR must show both drafts.
cases.setup: QA PR line of 100; draft A holds 70 of it; draft B has one other line. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull the line into draft B at 31, then at 30.
cases.expected: 31 refused (557); 30 accepted. The line's draft reservations read {A: 70, B: 30}; open 0.
cases.oracle: PR line meta and Open/In-progress tabs.

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: A PR line on hold slips into a draft that has no stage yet, and loses its hold
cases.why: Holding a line is how a requisitioner stops sourcing (and tells the ERP). The PR service only excludes in_active lines, and the reservation recalculation rewrites status from quantities alone — so pulling a held line silently turns it back to in_progress.
cases.setup: gate: `is_pr_hold_enabled` ON. A QA PR line on hold with open quantity; a QA draft with lines but no stage yet (created by POST /event_groups only). No twin.
cases.steps: Pull the held line into the draft. Read the PR line's status.
cases.expected: Desired: refused (557 or a dedicated "on hold" code). Today: accepted and the line's status becomes in_progress (record as defect).
cases.oracle: PR line status and Hold tab.

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: Another company's PR line can be pulled into my draft (no tenant scope)
cases.why: Neither the PR-line lookup nor the validator filters by company. A buyer who knows a foreign PR line id can pull it into their own draft and reserve quantity on the other tenant's PR.
cases.setup: A QA PR line in Demo Account 2 (32461); a QA draft in PROCOL DEMO. No twin: cross-tenant write.
cases.steps: As the PROCOL DEMO buyer, pull the foreign line's uuid into the draft. Read the foreign PR as its own buyer.
cases.expected: Desired: refused (557 or 101). Today the code accepts it and reserves quantity on the foreign line — a cross-tenant write. Treat as a security defect if reproduced.
cases.oracle: Foreign PR line's draft reservations and open quantity.

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: A dormant-locked PR line can be pulled into an existing draft
cases.why: The dormant lock (code 1125) is enforced only when a draft is CREATED; the "Add to draft" path has no dormant check, so the lock is bypassed by adding to an older draft.
cases.setup: gate: `pr_dormant_threshold_days` set; a QA PR older than the threshold, not unlocked; an existing QA draft with lines. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull a line of the dormant PR into the draft.
cases.expected: Desired: HTTP 422, code 1125 "PR(s) <numbers> are dormant and locked from sourcing events". Today: accepted (record as defect).
cases.oracle: Response; PR line reservations.

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: Sending another event's line uuid moves that line into my draft
cases.why: The line lookup in the draft update is `EventGroupLineItem.where(id: …)` with no event or company scope; the found row is given this draft's event and status and upserted. A buyer can pull a line out of any live event (even another tenant's) into their draft.
cases.setup: QA draft D (with one line) and a separate QA live event E with line X; a QA PR line with open quantity. No twin: moving lines between events is a destructive write.
cases.steps: Pull `{"uuid": "<X>", "status":"draft", "pr_line_item_uuid": "<QA PR line>", …}` into D. Read E.
cases.expected: Desired: refused (or a NEW line created in D, X untouched). Today the code reassigns X to D and sets it draft — E loses a live line. Security defect if reproduced.
cases.oracle: `GET /event_groups/<E>/get_line_items` before/after.

cases.section: What the PR shows as the event moves on
cases.title: Publishing moves the line from "reserved by a draft" to "in progress in an event"
cases.why: On publish the draft reservation is cleared and in-progress is derived from the live mapping; a mistake double-counts (draft + live) or drops the line back to Open.
cases.setup: A QA draft holding 40 of a QA PR line of 100. No twin.
cases.steps: Publish the draft; read the PR.
cases.expected: Draft reservation for that event gone; in progress 40; open 60; status in_progress.
cases.oracle: PR line meta + tabs.

cases.section: The PR list as the read-back oracle
cases.title: Asking for Open and In-progress together must not crash the PR list
cases.why: The PR list is how every case in this file reads quantities back. The status filter only handles exactly one of active / in_progress / approval_in_progress; any mix returns a nil relation that the next line calls `.distinct` on.
cases.setup: QA buyer; read only.
cases.steps: `GET /purchase_requests?page=1&filters={"status":["active","in_progress"]}`.
cases.expected: No 5xx (union of both buckets, or a 422). Suspected today: untyped 500.
cases.oracle: Status code.

cases.section: Mapping PR lines onto an existing non-PR event
cases.title: Another company's event can be the mapping target
cases.why: The PR lines are checked against the user's company, but the target event is fetched with a bare `find_by(id:)`; PR mappings can be written onto another tenant's event.
cases.setup: Setting ON; a QA event uuid from Demo Account 2; a matching PROCOL DEMO QA PR line. No twin: cross-tenant write.
cases.steps: Map the line onto the foreign event.
cases.expected: Desired: 836 'Event group not found'. Today: mapped if a line matches (security defect if reproduced).
cases.oracle: Foreign event's PR mappings.

cases.section: Draft events built from PR items
cases.title: PR items show the right open and in-progress quantity while the event is draft, live or withdrawn
cases.why: Procurement uses the open quantity to decide what still needs sourcing; a withdrawn event must give its quantity back.
cases.setup: PR item P (quantity 100) linked to a draft event's line (quantity 100).
cases.steps: 1. Read P. 2. Publish the event and read P. 3. Withdraw the event and read P and its history.
cases.expected: Draft: 100 in the draft. Published: 0 counted from the draft (the line is no longer draft). Withdrawn: quantity back to open, history entry "event withdrawn – reopened" with the open quantity (respecting `gate: open_pr_quantity_on_partial_order`). Links are found whatever their status.
cases.oracle: `event_groups/update_service.rb:411-430, 450-472`.

cases.section: Draft events built from PR items
cases.title: Deactivating one PR item should not throw away the whole draft event
cases.why: A draft built from ten PR items is discarded when one of them is deactivated; the other nine lose their draft quantity and the buyer's work.
cases.setup: Draft event with lines from PR items P1, P2, P3.
cases.steps: Deactivate P2; read the draft and P1/P3.
cases.expected: The whole draft is discarded and P1/P3 lose their draft quantity.
cases.oracle: `purchase_request_item.rb:537-541` → `discard_draft_project`.

cases.section: Draft events built from PR items
cases.title: PR items added to an empty draft are checked like any other batch
cases.why: The checks for quantity, duplicates and inactive PR items are skipped for the first batch into an empty draft — which is exactly how Clara builds events.
cases.setup: Empty draft event (as Clara creates it); PR items: one with quantity 0, one inactive, the same item twice.
cases.steps: Pull the items into the draft (Clara flow, then the normal "add PR items" action).
cases.expected: All three accepted into the empty draft (unverified live).
cases.oracle: Per `R-LIF-019-6`: `event_groups/pr_to_erfx_service.rb` rule 1; Clara creates the event with no lines (`mcp/purchase_request_tools/handler.rb:316-333`). Refusal code 557 per digest.

cases.section: Rounds built in the quick (Clara / PR) flow
cases.title: A quick-flow round starts at the scheduled publish time and its evaluation ends after bidding
cases.why: The evaluation end is counted from the start, not from the bid end; a company whose bidding lasts longer than its evaluation days gets an evaluation window that ends before bidding.
cases.setup: Company policies: bid duration 5 days, evaluation 4 days. Event scheduled to publish tomorrow 10:00; second event with a past schedule; a round added from an existing RFQ.
cases.steps: Build a round in each; read its times.
cases.expected: Evaluation end = start + 4 days, i.e. 1 day before the bid end (unverified whether saving the schedule refuses it).
cases.oracle: `trade_requests/base.rb:57-76, 87-105, 219-244`; `event_group.rb:279-281`.

cases.section: Rounds built in the quick (Clara / PR) flow
cases.title: A multi-currency quick-flow round derives each currency's precision from its rate
cases.why: A currency worth 83 base units needs more decimals in base terms; too few decimals round vendors' prices.
cases.setup: Company with multi-currency on, base INR, USD rate 83, JPY rate 0.55; a currency not in the company catalogue; a second company with no rates.
cases.steps: Build a round; read its currency setup.
cases.expected: INR rate 1; USD precision 2 + floor(log10 83) = 3; JPY 2 + floor(log10 0.55) = 1; the unknown currency skipped; mode "multiple currencies". No rates → no currency setup. A failure while building leaves the round without currency setup (not a failed round).
cases.oracle: `trade_requests/base.rb:246-297`.

cases.section: Rounds built in the quick (Clara / PR) flow
cases.title: A price round built from PR items carries each item's location, unit, number and reference prices
cases.why: Vendors quote per delivery location and unit; the PR number and line number link the PO back to the PR.
cases.setup: Draft event with line 1 from PR "RFQ/24/001 " item 10 (location Pune, unit KG, budget 50, historical 48, custom dropdown "Grade A"), line 2 with no PR item (unit symbol "NOS").
cases.steps: Build the price round; read its lines.
cases.expected: Line 1: location Pune, unit KG, item no 10, material code = product code, PR number "RFQ/24/001" (trimmed), dropdown mapped to its option id, references budget 50 and historical 48. Line 2: the company's first active location, unit matching "NOS" (empty if none). Title "RFQ", no ceiling/floor/tick. Lines in serial order. A round added from another round copies its vendors and is restricted to them.
cases.oracle: `trade_requests/create/rfq.rb:22-137`; `base.rb:159-172`.

cases.section: Rounds built in the quick (Clara / PR) flow
cases.title: A technical round built from PR items asks one question per quality parameter and names an evaluator
cases.why: The technical form must ask what the PR specifies, and someone must be responsible for scoring each line.
cases.setup: PR item with quality parameters "Grade" and "Size" and item text; created by user U. Second PR item with no creator whose fund center has planner P. Third with neither.
cases.steps: Build the technical round; read its forms and evaluators.
cases.expected: One form per line: "Grade" and "Size" required multi-line answers, "Item Text" (only when the PR has it), optional "Attach additional documents if any" and "Remarks". Evaluators U, P, none. Title "Technical Stage"; template = the company's last default RFI template. A line with no PR item is refused cleanly (today it would raise on `nil.product`; PR flows always have one).
cases.oracle: `trade_requests/create/rfp.rb:35-80`; `base.rb:190-193`.

cases.title: Cloning an event whose live round had a line deleted should not fail
cases.why: Deleting a line on a live event leaves its price-round line active; the clone then looks up the deleted line and crashes.
cases.setup: Published event with 3 lines; line 2 deleted while live. Vendors invited (one hidden).
cases.steps: Clone the event; read the clone.
cases.expected: The deleted line is not skipped (only missing/inactive are), `nil.id` raises → untyped HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: `trade_product.rb:325-343` (skip only missing/in_active at `:328-329`, `.id` at `:333`); `event_groups/update_service.rb:188-192`; audience copy `trade_request_replication_base.rb:24-26`.

cases.title: An amended round's bidding window is its configured length, wherever extensions happened
cases.why: Every copied schedule (including old auto-extension rows) restarts at the same moment, so the amended round's end depends on which copied row is last rather than on the configured duration.
cases.setup: Auction (configured 1 h) that got two 2-minute auto-extensions, followed by an evaluation window of 1 day.
cases.steps: Amend the event; read the amended auction's windows.
cases.expected: All rows start now; extension rows end at now + 2 min and the evaluation window now + 1 day, so the auction's end = the latest of these (now + 1 h, by the max rule) while the evaluation starts with bidding (unverified live).
cases.oracle: `versions/trade_request.rb:111-130`; inactive rows copied too (`trade_request.rb:111`).

cases.section: Moving an RFQ to auction or lots
cases.title: The auction made from an RFQ inherits its settings and renumbers lines when some were dropped
cases.why: The auction must keep the RFQ's columns, locations and terms; with service grouping, dropped lines must not leave gaps in line numbers.
cases.setup: RFQ with custom columns, a delivery location and terms; service-grouped RFQ with lines 1–4, line 2 inactive.
cases.steps: Move each to auction; read the auction's settings and lines.
cases.expected: Columns, location and terms as in the RFQ unless the request overrides them. Service-grouped: lines numbered 1–3 and section ranges resynced.
cases.oracle: `rfq_to_auction/create_service.rb:14, 32-44, 110-128`.

cases.section: Moving an RFQ to auction or lots
cases.title: A failed move to auction is a typed refusal, never a server error
cases.why: A half-made auction or a 500 leaves the buyer unsure whether vendors were moved.
cases.setup: RFQ whose technical weights include a line not carried to the auction; an RFQ where a step fails with a known code.
cases.steps: Move each to auction.
cases.expected: Unexpected errors are re-raised (untyped 500); a weight on a dropped line is inserted with an empty line reference (unverified whether the column allows it).

cases.section: Moving an RFQ to auction or lots
cases.title: A lot split that failed must not be reported as done
cases.why: A save error during the split rolls everything back but answers "success", so the buyer believes lots exist and vendors are not moved.
cases.setup: RFQ with bids; a split request that makes one lot round fail to save (e.g. a lot whose round fails validation); a vendor whose old line totals are all 0.
cases.steps: Split into lots; read the event's lots.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 success with no lot created (lots back to draft): the controller checks only for an error code and the service returns a message-only error.
cases.oracle: `create_event_lots/create_service.rb:40-75` (rescue returns `{message}`), `trade_controller.rb:1831-1834` (`render_error_json` only when `error[:code]`); NaN per `R-LIF-032-4` (b).

cases.section: Bids from vendors who are not registered yet
cases.title: Accepting or rejecting an unregistered vendor's bid
cases.why: Bids that arrive by mail from unregistered vendors must be confirmed by the buyer before they count.
cases.setup: Live event with an unregistered vendor's bid (and a technical answer) flagged "unregistered"; a normal bid; pending-unregistered count 1.
cases.steps: 1. Send an invalid status; act on the normal bid. 2. Accept the unregistered bid; accept it again. 3. On another event, reject one.
cases.expected: 1: "Insufficient parameters" for both; a deactivated vendor contact → "User does not exist". 2: accepted — the contact's email marked verified, all its unregistered links become normal, count 1 → 0; the second accept changes nothing and succeeds. 3: bid, its lines and trade rejected; count never below 0; the contact deactivated only if it has no other active bid or answer in the buyer's other live events. The buyer gets the "unregistered bid" notification after each action.
cases.oracle: HTTP 422 code 2 / code 70; `poc_bid_action_service.rb:14-130`; `email_bid_unregistered_helper.rb:99-115`; controller `template_responses_controller.rb:220`.

cases.section: Bids from vendors who are not registered yet
cases.title: An unregistered vendor's bid cannot be rejected after it was accepted, or twice
cases.why: Reject has no state check: rejecting an accepted bid silently removes a valid bid and deactivates the vendor contact, and each repeat lowers the pending count again.
cases.setup: Unregistered bid B1 accepted; unregistered bid B2 already rejected; pending count 2 for other bids.
cases.steps: Reject B1; reject B2 again; read the bids, the contact and the pending count.
cases.expected: B1 becomes rejected after acceptance, the contact may be deactivated, and the count drops on each call.
cases.oracle: `poc_bid_action_service.rb:79-98` (no guard; approve has one at `:52`).

cases.section: Bids from vendors who are not registered yet
cases.title: Accepting or rejecting a contact's bid applies to its other bids in the event and restores the registered bid
cases.why: The same contact may have bid on several rounds; rejecting it must give back the vendor's last bid made by a registered user, but never leave two active bids.
cases.setup: Vendor V: registered user's bid R (later revised), then unregistered contact's bid U on the RFQ and an answer on the RFP; a second round with another U bid.
cases.steps: Reject U; read V's bids on each round. Repeat with accept on a copy.
cases.expected: Siblings run outside the primary transaction (a failure leaves the primary rejected, siblings untouched) and the restore does not check for an existing active bid (two active bids possible).
cases.oracle: `poc_bid_sibling_action_service.rb:24-205`; `poc_bid_action_service.rb:81-100`.

cases.title: Updating a technical answer merges data and keeps remarks unless they are changed
cases.why: Saving one section should not erase others; today a save without remarks clears the vendor's saved remarks.
cases.setup: Draft answer with sections A and B filled and remark "see attachment"; masked round with 2 responding vendors; service-grouped RFP with 2 activities in one service.
cases.steps: Save section A only, without remarks; submit; read as the buyer. Submit the service RFP with only one activity form answered.
cases.expected: The remark is cleared (remarks always taken from the call).
cases.oracle: `template_responses/update_service.rb:33-59, 86-91, 103-119`; `forms_helper.rb:290-297`.

cases.title: Submitting a technical answer checks required answers, groups and conditions
cases.why: A vendor must not submit with a required question blank; a buyer condition that makes a field required must be enforced.
cases.setup: Technical round: question group "Certificate no + expiry" (optional, two members), a condition "if ISO = yes then certificate required".
cases.steps: Submit with no answers and no remarks; with no company; with certificate number but no expiry; with ISO = yes and no certificate.
cases.expected: First two: "Insufficient parameters". Group partly filled → every member checked (expiry required). ISO = yes → certificate required. Multi-row groups checked per row.
cases.oracle: HTTP 422 code 2 (and the field-level codes 572/773 per digest); `template_responses/validate_service.rb:11-14, 51-53, 80-147`.

cases.title: The direct answer check refuses blank required fields and unknown fields cleanly
cases.why: An answer that names a field the form does not have should be refused, not crash the submission.
cases.setup: Technical round whose form has required field "make".
cases.steps: Submit with no data; with "make" blank; with an extra unknown field "colour".
cases.expected: The unknown field has no configuration and `nil["is_required"]` raises → untyped 500 (unverified live).
cases.oracle: `template_responses/validate_service.rb:26-41`; code 2.

cases.section: Counter-offer tasks, AI audit, knockout rounds and draft awards
cases.title: A counter offer creates one task per bid, due at the evaluation end, and the due date follows extensions
cases.why: Vendors see "respond by"; a task due at the wrong time or never closed sends false reminders.
cases.setup: Price round with an evaluation window; QA vendor bid; a second round with a participant review window.
cases.steps: Raise a counter offer; raise another on the same bid; extend the round; resolve; on round 2 extend and read the task.
cases.expected: Round 2 (with a review window): the due date is not moved; a deleted bid makes the task update raise.
cases.oracle: `pending_tasks/additional_requests/raise_counter_offer.rb:18-83`; `push_notification.rb:3197-3212`; `additional_request.rb:577-584`; `trade_schedule.rb:195-203`.

cases.title: Deleting one activity of a service deletes all of that service's activities
cases.why: Service RFPs are evaluated per service; removing one activity must not leave a partial service, but must also not touch other services.
cases.setup: Service-grouped event: service S1 with activities a, b, c; service S2 with d.
cases.steps: Delete activity a; read the lines and forms. Delete d on an event without service grouping.
cases.expected: a, b, c (active or draft) deleted and their forms marked deleted; d untouched. Without grouping (or no siblings found) only the requested line is deleted.
cases.oracle: `event_groups/service_line_item_deletion.rb:10-72`.

cases.section: Pulling PR lines into an event that is not a draft
cases.title: Pulling into an event id that does not exist is refused the same way
cases.why: A missing event must get the same typed refusal as a non-draft one. A 404 or 500 here means the service was built with no event (it immediately reads the event's company).
cases.setup: Path id `Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` (well-formed, event 999999999 does not exist); PR reference bogus.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/pri_to_draft_project` with one valid-shaped line.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

cases.section: Pulling PR lines into an event that is not a draft
cases.title: A raw numeric event id gives no hint whether the event exists elsewhere
cases.why: Raw integer ids are the classic probe for other tenants' drafts. The answer must be identical for "someone else's draft" and "no such draft", and must never reach the service.
cases.setup: Path id `999999999` (integer, not a uuid); PR reference bogus.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/999999999/pri_to_draft_project` with one valid-shaped line.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. An integer-looking id skips uuid decoding (unless the uuid-enabled version flag is on), but the lookup is scoped to the caller's company and to drafts either way.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Pulling PR lines into an event that is not a draft
cases.title: Line items sent as an object are refused, not crashed
cases.why: On a DRAFT target this body would crash: the service constructor calls `pluck(:pr_line_item_id)` on the payload outside its own error handling. Only the draft lookup stands in front of it, so this case pins that order.
cases.setup: Published sandbox.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/pri_to_draft_project` with `line_items` as a JSON object (`{"first": {…}}`) instead of an array.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. Never a 500.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Pulling PR lines into an event that is not a draft
cases.title: A negative quantity aimed at a live event is refused (by state, not by any quantity rule)
cases.why: Documents that nothing but the state guard stops a negative quantity here — the draft-side quantity rule only checks "more than allowed" (API-XDPRE-027).
cases.setup: Published sandbox.
cases.steps: Same request as 001 with `quantity.value = -5` and a bogus PR reference.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Who may add PR lines to a draft
cases.title: With draft projects switched off for the company, pulling is refused
cases.why: `allow_draft_project_creation` is the company switch for the whole draft-project feature; when it is off the PR screen hides "Add to Draft Project", and the API must agree.
cases.setup: gate: `allow_draft_project_creation` OFF (and no Clara AI access for the user); an existing QA draft. No twin: needs a company setting change.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/<draft>/pri_to_draft_project` with a valid body from the dashboard.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action'. Note the check runs AFTER the draft lookup, so a non-draft target still answers code 2 first.
cases.oracle: 455; nothing written.

cases.section: Who may add PR lines to a draft
cases.title: An auction-team member cannot pull PR lines even when drafts are allowed
cases.why: Companies that route auctions to a separate team keep that team out of draft creation; the rule is "any user with the auction team type", regardless of other teams.
cases.setup: gate: `allow_draft_project_creation` ON; the workspace has an active auction-type team and the caller belongs to it. No twin: needs that user.
cases.steps: As that user, pull a PR line into a QA draft.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 455.
cases.oracle: 455; nothing written.

cases.section: Who may add PR lines to a draft
cases.title: A colleague can add PR lines to someone else's draft (owner is not checked)
cases.why: Drafts are personal work in progress. The policy only checks "can create events" and "same company", not "is the draft's owner" — so buyer B can push PR lines (and their quantity reservations) into buyer A's draft.
cases.setup: Two buyers in one company, both with create permission; buyer A owns a QA draft. No twin: needs a second buyer.
cases.steps: As buyer B, `POST /event_groups/<A's draft>/pri_to_draft_project` with a valid PR line.
cases.expected: Accepted (200 "success"); A's draft gains B's line. Desired: refused for a non-owner unless the user is super admin / CSM. Record as a defect to confirm with product.
cases.oracle: A's draft line list; the PR line now shows A's draft in its event details.

cases.section: Quantities when pulling into a draft
cases.title: Exactly the open quantity plus the over-quantity tolerance is accepted
cases.why: The limit is open × (1 + tolerance%), compared with "greater than", so the boundary itself must pass — an off-by-one here blocks buyers who source the full allowance.
cases.setup: gate: `over_quantity_tolerance_percentage` = 10. A QA PR line with 100 open; a QA draft with at least one line. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull the line at 110, then (in another draft) at 110.01.
cases.expected: 110 is accepted; 110.01 is refused with HTTP 422, code 557 'Purchase request items are not valid'.
cases.oracle: 200 then 557; reservation 110 recorded only for the first.

cases.section: Quantities when pulling into a draft
cases.title: With a tolerance set, pending reorders and other drafts reduce what can be pulled
cases.why: Two different formulas are used: with tolerance 0 the stored open quantity is used; with tolerance > 0 it is recomputed from active events, other drafts' reservations and reorders still awaiting PO or approval. A line with a pending reorder can therefore be over-pulled when tolerance is 0 if the stored figure is stale.
cases.setup: A QA PR line of 100 with a reorder of 30 pending approval. Run once with `over_quantity_tolerance_percentage` 0 and once with 1. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull the line at 80 into a QA draft that already has a line.
cases.expected: With tolerance 1: refused 557 (open is 70, limit 70.7). With tolerance 0: the answer depends on whether the stored quantity_in_progress already includes the 30 — both runs must agree.
cases.oracle: Compare both runs; any disagreement is a defect.

cases.section: Quantities when pulling into a draft
cases.title: A zero quantity is accepted and reserves nothing
cases.why: `0 > limit` is false, so zero passes; the line becomes rate-only and the reservation for that draft is removed. The PR line then looks untouched although an event holds it, and it can be pulled in full into another event.
cases.setup: A QA PR line of 100 open; a QA draft with one line. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull the line at quantity 0. Read the PR.
cases.expected: 200; the draft has a rate-only line; the PR line still shows 100 open. Desired: either refuse zero or treat it as an explicit "rate-only" choice that still marks the line in progress.
cases.oracle: PR open quantity 100; draft line `is_rate_only` true.

cases.section: Quantities when pulling into a draft
cases.title: A unit different from the PR's unit is stored on the line but ignored by the stage
cases.why: The cart greys out the unit, but the API takes `quantity.unitSymbol` / `display_unit` as sent. The event line then shows the client's unit while the RFQ stage is rebuilt with the PR's unit — vendors and the buyer see different units for one line.
cases.setup: A QA PR line in Nos; a QA draft with an RFQ stage. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull the line with `unitSymbol: "KG"`; open the draft and its stage.
cases.expected: Desired: refused (559 'Quantity should be in same unit as requested', as on the stage path). Today: accepted; line shows KG, stage line shows Nos.
cases.oracle: Line precomputed creator quantity unit vs trade product unit.

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: The same PR line cannot be pulled twice into one draft
cases.why: Two lines for one requisition line would double-count it.
cases.setup: A QA draft that already holds PR line L (active mapping). No twin.
cases.steps: Pull L again into the same draft.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 557 'Purchase request items are not valid'.
cases.oracle: 557; still one line for L.

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: A PR line on hold is refused when the draft already has a pricing stage
cases.why: The stage rebuild uses the stricter "active or in progress, with open quantity" rule; the outcome for the same line therefore depends on whether the draft has a stage yet (compare 037).
cases.setup: As 037 but the draft has an RFQ stage. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull the held line.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 557. Nothing written (the transaction rolls back).
cases.oracle: 557; hold status unchanged.

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: A completed PR line cannot be pulled
cases.why: Fully ordered lines have nothing left to source.
cases.setup: A QA PR line with quantity_closed = requested (status completed); a draft with lines. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull it at 1.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 557 (open is 0).

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: Rejected or send-back-pending PR lines are blocked only by the screen
cases.why: The PR page refuses to put "Rejected or Send Back Pending PR" lines in the cart, but the API rule only excludes in_active lines; a client calling the API directly can source them.
cases.setup: A QA PR line in status rejected (or approval_in_progress) with open quantity; a stage-less draft. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull it.
cases.expected: Desired: refused like the UI. Today: accepted (record as defect if so).
cases.oracle: Response code; PR line status afterwards.

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: A PR line deleted in the ERP (in_active) cannot be pulled
cases.why: Deleted lines must never re-enter sourcing.
cases.setup: A QA PR line set in_active; a draft with lines. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull it.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 557 (the line is not found among valid lines).

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: PR lines from a team the buyer cannot see can still be pulled
cases.why: With team filtering on, the PR list only shows PRs tagged to the user's teams (and assignee visibility may narrow further). The pull path has no such filter.
cases.setup: gate: `is_pr_teams_filtering_enabled` ON; a non-super-admin buyer; a QA PR line tagged to a team the buyer is not in. No twin.
cases.steps: Confirm the line is absent from the buyer's PR list; pull it by uuid into the buyer's draft.
cases.expected: Desired: refused. Today: accepted (record as defect to confirm).
cases.oracle: PR list (absent) vs draft (present).

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: A pulled line can carry another company's product
cases.why: The product lookup is `Product.active.where(id:)` with no company filter; the PR line says one material, the event line another tenant's product.
cases.setup: A product uuid from another client; a QA PR line; a draft with lines. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull the PR line with the foreign `product_uuid`.
cases.expected: Desired: refused. Today: accepted (record as defect).
cases.oracle: Draft line product vs PR line material.

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: Adding PR lines to a draft that already has a catalog line and a stage fails with a raw message
cases.why: The RFQ stage rebuild reads the PR line of EVERY draft line; a catalog line has none, so the rebuild hits `nil.buyer_hub_id` and the buyer gets an internal error instead of their lines.
cases.setup: A QA draft with one catalog (non-PR) line and an RFQ stage; a QA PR line. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull the PR line into the draft.
cases.expected: Today: HTTP 422, code 15 "undefined method 'buyer_hub_id' for nil"; everything rolled back. Desired: mixed drafts supported or refused with a readable reason.
cases.oracle: 422 code 15; draft unchanged.

cases.section: Creating a draft straight from PR lines
cases.title: A draft can be created against a PR line that does not exist
cases.why: "Start New Project" creates the draft with `pr_line_item_uuid` on each line. Create never checks that the PR line exists, so a stale cart produces a draft whose failure only shows when the buyer builds the stage.
cases.setup: QA buyer; catalog product; PR reference `Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` (does not exist). Creates a new QA_Platform_ draft only.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups` with `{"status":"draft","title":"QA_Platform_DPRE_051_<stamp>","line_items":[{"product_uuid":…,"product_quality_uuid":…,"quantity":{"unitSymbol":"Nos","value":10},"pr_line_item_uuid":"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="}]}`.
cases.expected: No 5xx. Today: 200 and a draft whose line carries the dangling PR reference; the stage build later answers 557. Desired: 422 code 557 at create.
cases.oracle: Status code; returned line's PR reference.

cases.section: Creating a draft straight from PR lines
cases.title: The same PR line twice in one create is not stopped
cases.why: Duplicated cart rows double-count a requisition line.
cases.setup: As 051; both lines reference the same (bogus) PR line.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups` with two lines, both `pr_line_item_uuid = Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: No 5xx. Today: 200 with two lines on one PR line (only the pull path checks duplicates).
cases.oracle: Status code; line count.

cases.section: Creating a draft straight from PR lines
cases.title: A raw numeric PR line id is stored without any check
cases.why: Raw ids bypass uuid decoding and are how a client could point a draft at another tenant's PR line; create stores them unchecked.
cases.setup: As 051 with `"pr_line_item_id": 999999999`.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups` with that line.
cases.expected: No 5xx. Today: 200 with the raw id stored. Desired: 557.
cases.oracle: Status code.

cases.section: Creating a draft straight from PR lines
cases.title: A PR line created with zero quantity becomes a rate-only line
cases.why: Zero is the boundary between "buy" and "ask for a rate". A PR line silently turning rate-only reserves nothing on the PR.
cases.setup: As 051 with quantity 0.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups` with that line.
cases.expected: No 5xx. Today: 200 with the line marked rate-only.
cases.oracle: Status code; `is_rate_only` on the line.

cases.section: Creating a draft straight from PR lines
cases.title: A PR line created with a negative quantity should be refused
cases.why: Same inflation risk as API-XDPRE-027, on the create path; there is no sign check anywhere on create.
cases.setup: As 051 with quantity -5.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups` with that line.
cases.expected: No 5xx. Desired: 422. If accepted, read the draft back and record the negative line as a defect.
cases.oracle: Status code; stored quantity.

cases.section: Creating a draft straight from PR lines
cases.title: A dormant PR blocks the create, names the PR and writes nothing
cases.why: Deeper than API-EG-006: the refusal has its own body shape — the message lists the PR numbers and a `dormant_pr_ids` array that the screen uses to offer "Request unlock" — and it is raised before the event row is saved. Unlocking must make the same request succeed.
cases.setup: gate: `pr_dormant_threshold_days` set; a QA PR older than the threshold, never unlocked. No twin: needs a dormant PR.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups` with one of its lines; then `POST /purchase_requests/unlock_dormant` as a manager; repeat the create.
cases.expected: First: HTTP 422 `{"error":{"code":1125,"message":"PR(s) <rfq_no> are dormant and locked from sourcing events"},"dormant_pr_ids":[…]}`, no event row. After unlock: 200.
cases.oracle: Body shape; event count for the title before/after.

cases.section: Creating a draft straight from PR lines
cases.title: Creating the draft alone reserves nothing on the PR
cases.why: Create stores the PR reference only in the line's data; no PR mapping or reservation is made until the stage is built (or the line is pulled through pri_to_draft_project). A buyer who abandons the create screen leaves the PR untouched — and two buyers can both start a project from the same open line.
cases.setup: A QA PR line of 100 open. No twin (uses a real PR line in a successful write).
cases.steps: Create a draft from it via "Start New Project"; read the PR before building any stage; then build the RFQ stage; read again.
cases.expected: Before the stage: PR still 100 open. After the stage: in progress by the line quantity.
cases.oracle: PR Open / In-progress tabs at both points.

cases.section: Creating a draft straight from PR lines
cases.title: Building the pricing stage re-checks the PR line (557 / 558 / 559)
cases.why: The stage build is the strict gate for PR-created drafts: status must be active or in progress with open quantity (557), quantity within open × (1 + tolerance) (558), and the unit must match the PR's (559).
cases.setup: QA drafts created from QA PR lines in each state. No twin (stage creation is held out of runs).
cases.steps: Build the RFQ stage with (a) a held line, (b) quantity above the cap, (c) a different unit.
cases.expected: (a) 557 'Purchase request items are not valid'; (b) 558 'Quantity should be less than open quantity'; (c) 559 'Quantity should be in same unit as requested'.
cases.oracle: Codes; no trade products created.

cases.section: Creating a draft straight from PR lines
cases.title: The unit check treats the unit as a search pattern, so "%" passes any PR unit
cases.why: The 559 check is `data->>'uom' NOT ILIKE <sent unit>`; a unit of "%" (or "_" for one-character units) matches everything and bypasses the unit rule.
cases.setup: A QA draft from a QA PR line in Nos. No twin (stage creation is held out).
cases.steps: Build the stage with the line's `unit_symbol` = "%".
cases.expected: Desired: 559. Today: accepted (record as defect).
cases.oracle: Response code; stage line unit.

cases.section: Creating a draft straight from PR lines
cases.title: Lines already reserved in this draft skip the quantity cap when the stage is rebuilt
cases.why: When a PR line is already "part of this draft project", the 558 check is skipped entirely; raising the quantity in the stage sheet after pulling is not bounded by the PR.
cases.setup: A QA draft with a PR line pulled at 40 of 100. No twin.
cases.steps: Rebuild the RFQ stage with that line at 400.
cases.expected: Desired: 558. Today: accepted.
cases.oracle: Response; reservation after save.

cases.section: What the PR shows as the event moves on
cases.title: Discarding the draft releases its reservation
cases.why: Abandoned drafts must not hold requisitions hostage.
cases.setup: As 063, before publishing. No twin.
cases.steps: Discard the draft; read the PR.
cases.expected: Reservation removed; PR mappings in_active; line back to 100 open, status active.
cases.oracle: PR line meta + Open tab.

cases.section: What the PR shows as the event moves on
cases.title: Removing a PR line from a draft returns its quantity
cases.why: Partial selection must be reversible line by line.
cases.setup: A QA draft with two PR lines. No twin.
cases.steps: Delete one line from the draft; read the PR.
cases.expected: That line's mapping goes in_active and its quantity returns to open; the other stays.
cases.oracle: PR tabs.

cases.section: What the PR shows as the event moves on
cases.title: Removing a PR line from a live event returns its quantity after the deletion job
cases.why: On live events deletion is asynchronous; the PR must catch up.
cases.setup: A published QA event with two PR lines, no bids on the removed line. No twin.
cases.steps: Delete one line; wait (bounded, 60 s) for the deletion job; read the PR.
cases.expected: The removed line's PR quantity returns to open; activity log "deleted from event".
cases.oracle: PR tabs + activity log.

cases.section: What the PR shows as the event moves on
cases.title: Awarding alone does not close PR quantity; the purchase order does
cases.why: Buyers expect "awarded" to complete the PR; in fact closed quantity grows only when a PO is generated, by the PO's quantity, and the line completes when closed equals requested.
cases.setup: A published QA event holding a QA PR line fully; award to the QA vendor. No twin.
cases.steps: Submit the award; read the PR. Generate the PO; wait (bounded) for the quantity job; read again.
cases.expected: After award: still in progress. After PO: closed += ordered quantity; completed if equal.
cases.oracle: PR Completed tab.

cases.section: What the PR shows as the event moves on
cases.title: A partial order reopens the rest only when the company says so
cases.why: `open_pr_quantity_on_partial_order` decides whether the un-ordered remainder of a line goes back to Open or stays in progress with the event.
cases.setup: A QA event line of 100 from a QA PR line; a PO for 60. Run with the setting ON and OFF. No twin.
cases.steps: Generate the PO; read the PR.
cases.expected: ON: 60 closed, 40 open, activity "partial award reopened". OFF: 60 closed, 40 in progress.
cases.oracle: PR tabs + activity log.

cases.section: What the PR shows as the event moves on
cases.title: A hold placed during a live event is not consistently preserved
cases.why: The event-status job deliberately skips held lines, but the quantity job rewrites status from quantities and has no hold branch — so the next recalculation can silently undo a hold.
cases.setup: gate: `is_pr_hold_enabled` ON. A published QA event on a QA PR line. No twin.
cases.steps: Hold the line; trigger a recalculation (e.g. remove another line of the same event, or close the stage); read the PR line.
cases.expected: Desired: still on hold. Today: may flip to in_progress (record as defect if so).
cases.oracle: PR line status / Hold tab.

cases.section: The PR list as the read-back oracle
cases.title: An unknown status must not crash the PR list
cases.why: A renamed tab key on the client would take the PR page down.
cases.setup: Read only.
cases.steps: `GET /purchase_requests?page=1&filters={"status":["QA_Platform_bogus"]}`.
cases.expected: No 5xx (empty list or 422). Suspected today: 500 (no branch matches, nil relation).
cases.oracle: Status code.

cases.section: The PR list as the read-back oracle
cases.title: A status sent as text must not crash the PR list
cases.why: The view service already accepts a string status, but the query runs first and does `array & "active"`, a TypeError.
cases.setup: Read only.
cases.steps: `GET /purchase_requests?page=1&filters={"status":"active"}`.
cases.expected: No 5xx; ideally treated as ["active"].
cases.oracle: Status code.

cases.section: The PR list as the read-back oracle
cases.title: An unknown closure type must not crash the Completed tab
cases.why: Closure type separates partially-closed, PO-closed and deleted lines; an unknown value falls through to a branch that returns nil.
cases.setup: Read only.
cases.steps: `GET /purchase_requests?page=1&filters={"status":["completed"],"closure_type":["QA_Platform_bogus"]}`.
cases.expected: No 5xx (empty page). Suspected today: 500.
cases.oracle: Status code.

cases.title: A real PR line cannot be partially closed without a reason
cases.why: Uses the key the dashboard really sends (`pr_item_uuids`, decoded by ParamsAuth). The older PR-PCL cases send uuids under `pr_item_ids`, which are never decoded and can only ever reach 528. This proves a reason-less closure is impossible on a real line.
cases.setup: `is_pr_partial_closure_enabled` ON. `{{prItemId}}` is a real line; no reason can match "".
cases.steps: `PATCH /purchase_requests/partial_close` with `{"pr_item_uuids":["{{prItemId}}"],"remarks":"QA_Platform_no_reason_<stamp>"}`. Read the PR back.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 2 'Invalid closure reason' (861 if the feature is off). No closure metadata on the line.
cases.oracle: 422 + message; `GET /purchase_requests/{{prId}}` shows no partial closure.

cases.title: No line ids at all is refused at the first rung
cases.why: Missing (not empty) list; the 2 must come from the first rung so the reason and remarks rungs are never consulted.
cases.setup: `is_pr_partial_closure_enabled` ON.
cases.steps: `PATCH /purchase_requests/partial_close` with only `closure_reason` and `remarks`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + message.

cases.section: Draft events built from PR items
cases.title: A line's quantity keeps its unit whether the PR sends a number or a quantity object
cases.why: The quantity and its unit are what vendors quote against; a lost unit turns "100 KG" into "100".
cases.setup: Two PR items pulled into a draft event: one whose quantity arrives as {value 100, unit KG}, one as the plain number 50 with display unit "NOS".
cases.steps: Read both lines of the draft.
cases.expected: Line 1: 100 KG. Line 2: 50 NOS (the display unit).
cases.oracle: Line `precomputed_data.creator_fields.creator_quantity` = {value, unitSymbol} (per `R-LIF-001-4`, `event_groups/create_service.rb`).

cases.section: Rounds built in the quick (Clara / PR) flow
cases.title: A quick-flow round starts as a draft with safe default settings
cases.why: The quick flow publishes with little buyer review, so its defaults decide the event.
cases.setup: Clara/PR quick flow; company with `gate: show_variant_widget` on and off.
cases.steps: Build a round; read its settings, columns and savings strategies.
cases.expected: Draft status, sheet layout; terms not mandatory, English auction off, alternate bidding off, pickup off, dynamic closing price based, end price 0, auction on base price, closing mode single. Columns added when the template has none: material code, line number, PR number, product variant (editable only with the variant setting on, else hidden). Savings strategies Budget and Historical Price, per line.

cases.section: Rounds built in the quick (Clara / PR) flow
cases.title: A quick-flow auction uses fixed 2-day bidding and 4-day evaluation whatever the company policy
cases.why: A company that set 5-day bidding gets 2 days on auctions only; buyers should know or the policy should apply.
cases.setup: Company policies: bid duration 5 days, evaluation 6 days; auction strategy policy "rank".
cases.steps: Build an auction in the quick flow.
cases.expected: Title "Auction", strategy rank, bid end = start + 2 days, evaluation end = start + 4 days (policy ignored), order type from the template. A template without an order type should be refused cleanly, not raise.
cases.oracle: `trade_requests/create/auction.rb:23-44`.

cases.section: Rounds built in the quick (Clara / PR) flow
cases.title: Adding PR items to a draft round fills the new lines the same way as a fresh round
cases.why: Lines added later lose the PR columns and evaluators that a freshly built round would have, so the same event looks different depending on when an item was added.
cases.setup: Draft event with a price round and a technical round built from PR items; then a new PR item (with custom columns, creator U) is added.
cases.steps: Re-sync the rounds; read the new line and the new form.
cases.expected: New line's custom columns empty and material code taken from the product; new form has no evaluator.
cases.oracle: `trade_requests/update/rfq.rb:58-64` vs `create/rfq.rb:89, 97-125`; `update/rfp.rb:48-64` vs `create/rfp.rb:57-72`; `update/auction.rb:8-10`.

cases.section: Rounds built in the quick (Clara / PR) flow
cases.title: Removing lines re-numbers the round's sections and drops empty ones
cases.why: Section tabs show ranges of lines ("1–5"); after removing lines the ranges must still match.
cases.setup: Round with 6 lines in sections 1 (lines 1–3, child 1.1 = 2–3) and 2 (lines 4–6), one tab each.
cases.steps: Remove lines 2 and 4–6; read the tabs.
cases.expected: Section 1 = 1–2, child 1.1 = 2–2; section 2 and its tab dropped. Nothing removed → tabs unchanged.
cases.oracle: `trade_requests/tab_range_resync.rb:17-90`.

cases.title: An amended technical round copies live forms and active evaluators, without stray questions
cases.why: Forms of deleted lines come along without a line and are then treated as the round's global form — vendors see a question about an item that no longer exists.
cases.setup: Technical round with forms on lines 1–3 (line 3 deleted), evaluator E1 active and E2 removed on line 1.
cases.steps: Amend; read the amended round's forms and evaluators; open it as the QA vendor.
cases.expected: Line 3's form (status deleted) is copied without a line link and can be picked as the global form (unverified live).
cases.oracle: `versions/trade_request.rb:70-107`; `form.rb:37`; global-form pick in `TradeRequests::Update::Rfp` (per digest).

cases.title: A PR amendment closes the previous version immediately
cases.why: Unlike a manual amendment (closed by a background job), a PR amendment closes the old version in the same request; both must leave the old version unbiddable.
cases.setup: Live event from a PR; change the PR so that an amendment is created and published.
cases.steps: Immediately after the amendment, bid on the old version as the QA vendor.
cases.expected: Refused: the old version's technical round and latest price round already ended.
cases.oracle: `purchase_requests/amendment_service.rb:366` calls `update_previous_version_data` synchronously; compare API-EVRMEG-025.

cases.section: Moving an RFQ to auction or lots
cases.title: A lot's evaluation end follows the company default, then the latest sibling lot, then the parent
cases.why: Lots split from one RFQ should evaluate on a common timetable.
cases.setup: RFQ evaluation ends Friday; company default lot evaluation 2 days (second company with none); an earlier lot whose evaluation ends Thursday (future).
cases.steps: Split a new lot in each company.
cases.expected: Company with default: now + 2 days. Without: Thursday (latest sibling lot, still future); if no future sibling: Friday (parent).
cases.oracle: `create_event_lots/create_service.rb:229-240`.

cases.title: Starting a technical answer reuses the vendor's draft and carries its last submitted answers
cases.why: A vendor revising its answer should start from what it submitted; two drafts for the same vendor would split the work.
cases.setup: QA vendor with a submitted answer on the technical round; a draft award proposal with the same numeric id as the round (rare; for part c).
cases.steps: 1. Start a revision; read its answers. 2. Start again with different extra details. 3. Start a surrogate revision with a remark twice.
cases.expected: The surrogate remark is added again on every call; the draft lookup ignores what kind of item it is for, so a draft on a round and one on a proposal with the same id are the same row (unverified live).
cases.oracle: `template_responses/create_service.rb:52-110`.

cases.section: Counter-offer tasks, AI audit, knockout rounds and draft awards
cases.title: Saving the AI counter-offer audit reports failure when nothing was saved
cases.why: The audit is the record of AI-suggested vs final prices; "saved successfully" when it was not hides gaps in the audit trail.
cases.setup: AI counter-offer suggestion on the sandbox round; a request whose snapshot is invalid (e.g. missing vendor).
cases.steps: Save the audit for both.
cases.expected: Invalid snapshot → "Audit deltas saved successfully" (`create` without a check); other exceptions → code 15 "Error in saving audit deltas: …".
cases.oracle: `ai_auditor/counter_offer_auditor.rb:10-35`.

cases.section: Counter-offer tasks, AI audit, knockout rounds and draft awards
cases.title: A knockout round that cannot be saved is reported, not returned as if created
cases.why: The round builder returns an unsaved round with no error; callers continue as if the round exists.
cases.setup: Knockout auction with round 2 active; build another active round 2.
cases.steps: Build the round; read the auction's rounds.
cases.expected: No error; the duplicate is silently not saved.
cases.oracle: `trade_rounds/create_service.rb:22-35`; uniqueness `trade_round.rb:43-45`.

cases.title: One form per service activity, shown once, and duplicate PR links tidied
cases.why: The vendor answers one form per service; duplicates and extra links confuse the PR quantity.
cases.setup: Service S with activities a and b; a form sent for a; line L with two links to the same PR item.
cases.steps: Build the forms; list them; read L's links.
cases.expected: Forms for a and b; the list shows only the first per service; L keeps the oldest link not owned by another line, the rest retired.
cases.oracle: `event_groups/service_activity_line_item_mapper.rb:21-78`; `forms_helper.rb:13`; `trade_form_helper.rb:255`.

cases.title: Open-tender search matches title or number literally, and the list sorts only on allowed fields
cases.why: A vendor searching "100%" or "A_B" gets unrelated events because % and _ act as wildcards.
cases.setup: Open-tender events "Steel 100% recycled", "Steel 1000 MT", "A_B pipes", "AXB pipes"; an amended event RFX-n.1; vendor login.
cases.steps: Search the open tenders for "100%", "A_B", "rfx-n.1", and with a created-from/to range; sort the buyer's events list by "title" and by "created_at asc".
cases.expected: "100%" also matches "Steel 1000 MT"; "A_B" also matches "AXB pipes". Most event lists apply only the sort (the text filter is used on the open-tender list).
cases.oracle: `event_groups/search_query.rb:5-42`; `event_group.rb:90-107, 216-218`; `event_group_controller_helper.rb:2512`; Procol DB shows amended `ref_id` like "RFX-12830.1" (so the digest's claim that the shown ref finds nothing is wrong).

cases.section: Pulling PR lines into an event that is not a draft
cases.title: Line items sent as a plain string are refused, not crashed
cases.why: Same constructor-time crash risk as API-XDPRE-004 (`String#pluck` does not exist).
cases.setup: Published sandbox.
cases.steps: Same request with `"line_items": "QA_Platform_not_a_list_<stamp>"`.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Pulling PR lines into an event that is not a draft
cases.title: Line items that are strings inside the array are refused, not crashed
cases.why: Element-level type confusion: on a draft, `"text"[:pr_line_item_id]` raises a TypeError in the constructor — an untyped 500.
cases.setup: Published sandbox.
cases.steps: Same request with `"line_items": ["QA_Platform_a_<stamp>", "QA_Platform_b_<stamp>"]`.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Pulling PR lines into an event that is not a draft
cases.title: A 100-line batch aimed at a live event is refused quickly
cases.why: There is no batch-size cap on this endpoint (partial close has 20). A big cart must still be refused in constant time on a non-draft.
cases.setup: Published sandbox; 100 lines with bogus PR references.
cases.steps: Send the 100-line body; time the reply.
cases.expected: Refused promptly; HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2 within normal latency.

cases.section: Pulling PR lines into an event that is not a draft
cases.title: The purchase-cart read is refused for a live event
cases.why: `purchase_cart_params` is the read that pairs with "add to draft"; it must agree that a live event is not a cart.
cases.setup: Published sandbox.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/purchase_cart_params`.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. No PR data returned.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Pulling PR lines into an event that is not a draft
cases.title: The purchase-cart read is refused for an unknown event
cases.why: The policy call must never run with a nil record.
cases.setup: Path id `Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/purchase_cart_params`.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.

cases.section: Pulling PR lines into an event that is not a draft
cases.title: The "Add to draft project" picker list reads cleanly and shows only PR-based drafts
cases.why: This list decides which drafts a buyer can add PR lines to; a crash blocks the whole flow, and a draft without PR links is (by design) never offered.
cases.setup: QA buyer; read only.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/draft?listing_view=true`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; every event group listed is a draft with at least one linked purchase request. A draft made from catalog products only does not appear. Never a 5xx.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; each listed event shows a PR reference.

cases.section: Who may add PR lines to a draft
cases.title: A draft built from grouped service PR lines refuses further PR lines
cases.why: With service grouping on, a draft that already holds service-activity lines is laid out as RFP forms per service; adding more PR lines through this path is blocked outright.
cases.setup: gate: `group_service_activities_in_rfp` ON; a QA draft created from a service PR (its `meta_data.pr_item_details` has activity lines with a service id). No twin: needs a service PR.
cases.steps: Pull any PR line into that draft.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (the same code as "not a draft", which gives the buyer no hint why).
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2; draft unchanged.

cases.section: Who may add PR lines to a draft
cases.title: A draft with both an RFQ and an auction stage refuses PR lines with a readable reason
