cases.why: The service guards against a stage mix it cannot rebuild; the reason is returned in plain words.
cases.setup: A QA draft holding an RFQ stage and an auction stage. No twin: needs that draft.
cases.steps: Pull a valid PR line into it.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 15 with message "rfq and auction cannot both be present in rfx_modes". Nothing written (the check runs before the transaction).
cases.oracle: 422 + code 15 + that message.

cases.section: Who may add PR lines to a draft
cases.title: A discarded draft no longer accepts PR lines
cases.why: Discarding a draft sets it in_active and releases its reservations; it must not be revived by a stale "Add Items" tab.
cases.setup: A QA draft that was discarded (status in_active). No twin: needs a discarded draft.
cases.steps: Pull a PR line into it.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2; the PR line's reservations unchanged.

cases.section: Who may add PR lines to a draft
cases.title: Outside the Procol dashboard app the pull is refused unless the user has Clara AI
cases.why: The draft tab is a dashboard feature: the permission check returns false for any other app context unless the workspace grants the user Clara AI access.
cases.setup: gate: `allow_draft_project_creation` ON; a session whose current app is not the Procol dashboard; user without Clara AI access. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull a PR line into a QA draft from that session.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 455.

cases.section: Quantities when pulling into a draft
cases.title: A decimal quantity on a "Nos" line is accepted as-is
cases.why: No integer rule exists for count units; 2.5 Nos is reserved as 2.5. Buyers relying on whole units must not assume the API rounds.
cases.setup: A QA PR line in Nos; a QA draft with one line. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull the line at 2.5.
cases.expected: 200; reservation 2.5; PR open drops by 2.5.
cases.oracle: PR open quantity.

cases.section: Quantities when pulling into a draft
cases.title: A quantity sent as text fails with a raw Ruby message
cases.why: `"5" > 10.0` raises "comparison of String with Float failed"; the service rescues it and returns the exception text to the buyer.
cases.setup: A QA draft with one line; a QA PR line. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull with `"quantity": {"value": "5"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 15 (not 500) — but with an internal Ruby message. Desired: code 2 or 557 with a readable message.
cases.oracle: 422 code 15; message text recorded.

cases.section: Quantities when pulling into a draft
cases.title: A quantity sent as a bare number (not an object) fails with a raw Ruby message
cases.why: The validator digs `quantity.value`; a bare number has no `dig`, so a client that sends `"quantity": 5` gets an internal error string.
cases.setup: As 029. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull with `"quantity": 5`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 15 with a NoMethodError message. Desired: accept the bare number (the create path does) or refuse with code 2.
cases.oracle: 422 code 15.

cases.section: Quantities when pulling into a draft
cases.title: A cleared quantity (null) fails with a raw Ruby message
cases.why: Clearing the cart's number box sends `value: null` (UI-XDPRE-005); `nil > limit` raises and the buyer sees "Failed to add items to draft" with no reason.
cases.setup: As 029. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull with `"quantity": {"unitSymbol":"Nos","value": null}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 15. Desired: code 2 "quantity required".
cases.oracle: 422 code 15.

cases.section: Quantities when pulling into a draft
cases.title: An astronomically large quantity is refused or fails cleanly
cases.why: `1e400` parses to Infinity. On a draft with lines it is above the cap (557); on an empty draft it slips past validation and the reservation SQL writes `'Infinity'::jsonb`, which Postgres rejects.
cases.setup: One QA draft with lines, one without. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull a QA PR line with `"value": 1e400` into each.
cases.expected: First: 422 code 557. Second: 422 code 15 with a database message (desired: 557). Never 500.
cases.oracle: Codes as above; no reservation written in either.

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: A draft line with no PR reference is refused on this path
cases.why: This endpoint is for PR lines; a "draft" line without a PR reference is the one shape the validator explicitly blocks.
cases.setup: A draft with lines. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull `{"status":"draft", …}` with no `pr_line_item_uuid`.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 557.

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: A line with no status and no PR reference slips in as a plain catalog line
cases.why: The "needs a PR reference" rule only fires when `status` is "draft"; omit the status and a non-PR line is added through the PR endpoint, then breaks the stage rebuild (see 050).
cases.setup: A draft with lines. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull a line with product and quantity but no status and no PR reference.
cases.expected: Desired: 557. Today: accepted.
cases.oracle: Draft line list.

cases.section: Which PR lines may be pulled
cases.title: A pulled line without a product fails with a raw Ruby message
cases.why: The dashboard always sends the product; a client that does not gets "undefined method 'id' for nil" back as the error message.
cases.setup: A draft with lines; a QA PR line. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull the PR line with no `product_uuid`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 15 with the Ruby message (desired: code 80 'Product not found' or take the product from the PR line). Nothing written.
cases.oracle: 422 code 15.

cases.section: Creating a draft straight from PR lines
cases.title: An undecodable PR reference degrades to a plain draft
cases.why: A garbled uuid must mean "no PR link", not a crash.
cases.setup: As 051 with `pr_line_item_uuid = "WrongUuid1="`.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups` with that line.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; an ordinary draft whose line has no PR reference.
cases.oracle: 200; line's PR reference empty.

cases.section: Creating a draft straight from PR lines
cases.title: A text PR line id does not crash the create or its response
cases.why: The query casts the text to NULL harmlessly; the risk is the response serializer trying to encode a non-numeric PR reference.
cases.setup: As 051 with `"pr_line_item_id": "QA_Platform_x_<stamp>"`.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups` with that line.
cases.expected: No 5xx (a 422 is fine).
cases.oracle: Status code.

cases.section: What the PR shows as the event moves on
cases.title: Withdrawing logs which PR lines reopened and by how much
cases.why: Deeper than API-LC-006: besides returning the quantity, withdrawal writes an "event withdrawn – reopened" activity per line that was in progress, with the reopened open quantity — the requisitioner's only explanation of why the line came back.
cases.setup: A published QA event holding 40 of a QA PR line. No twin.
cases.steps: Withdraw with a remark; read the PR line's activity log.
cases.expected: Line back to open; one `event_withdrawn_reopened` entry naming the event ref and quantity.
cases.oracle: Activity log.

cases.section: What the PR shows as the event moves on
cases.title: A PR line deactivated by the ERP discards every draft that holds it
cases.why: When a PR line goes in_active, every draft holding it is discarded as a whole — including the buyer's other lines in those drafts.
cases.setup: A QA draft holding QA PR line L plus another line. No twin.
cases.steps: Mark L in_active (ERP sync); read the draft.
cases.expected: The whole draft is in_active; all its reservations released. Record whether the buyer is told.
cases.oracle: Draft status; other line's PR quantities.

cases.section: The PR list as the read-back oracle
cases.title: The partial-closure filter is silently dropped when the feature is off
cases.why: With partial closure off, the filter value is removed and the Completed list comes back UNFILTERED — a report built on it would count every completed line.
cases.setup: Read only; behaviour depends on `is_pr_partial_closure_enabled`.
cases.steps: `GET /purchase_requests?page=1&filters={"status":["completed"],"closure_type":["partial_closure"]}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 either way; ON: only partially-closed lines; OFF: all completed lines.
cases.oracle: Status code; row count vs the unfiltered Completed tab.

cases.section: The PR list as the read-back oracle
cases.title: Filtering PR lines by a non-PR event returns nothing
cases.why: "Which PR lines does this event consume?" is the read-back for every pull case; it must be exact and must not crash on an event built from the catalog.
cases.setup: Read only; the sandbox was built from the catalog.
cases.steps: `GET /purchase_requests?page=1&filters={"status":["in_progress"],"rfx_uuids":["{{eventGroupUuid}}"]}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200, empty list.
cases.oracle: Status code; zero rows.

cases.section: The PR list as the read-back oracle
cases.title: Searching PR lines by event reference treats % as a wildcard
cases.why: The event-reference search binds the value safely but does not escape % and _, so "%" lists every PR line linked to any event (unlike PR-number search).
cases.setup: Read only.
cases.steps: `GET /purchase_requests?page=1&filters={"status":["in_progress"],"rfx_id_ilike":"%"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 (all linked lines). No 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status code.

cases.section: The PR list as the read-back oracle
cases.title: An unknown event status filter is harmless
cases.why: The event-status column filter on In-progress is how buyers find lines whose event was awarded; unknown values must match nothing.
cases.setup: Read only.
cases.steps: `GET /purchase_requests?page=1&filters={"status":["in_progress"],"event_statuses":["QA_Platform_bogus"]}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200, empty.
cases.oracle: Status code; zero rows.

cases.section: The PR list as the read-back oracle
cases.title: The event list's PR-number options accept a wildcard safely
cases.why: Feeds the "PR number" filter on the events list; must stay read-only and crash-free.
cases.setup: Read only.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/pr_number_options?page=1&search_query=%25`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with PR numbers linked to ACTIVE events only.
cases.oracle: Status code.

cases.section: The PR list as the read-back oracle
cases.title: A negative page for PR-number options is clamped to the first page
cases.why: Negative paging must clamp, not raise.
cases.setup: Read only.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/pr_number_options?page=-5`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200, first page.
cases.oracle: Status code.

cases.title: Remarks made only of markup count as no remarks
cases.why:
The drawer trims remarks before sending; the API strips HTML tags from every string, so "

" must land on the same "Remarks are required" verdict.
cases.setup: Bogus line id, so nothing can be closed even if a rung regressed.
cases.steps:
`PATCH /purchase_requests/partial_close` with `{"pr_item_uuids":["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="],"closure_reason":"budget_cut","remarks":"

"}`.
cases.expected: Refused (never 5xx): 861 (off), 2 'Invalid closure reason' (reason not configured), 2 'Remarks are required', or 528 — depending on the company's reason list.
cases.oracle: Non-2xx, no 5xx.

cases.title: A reason sent as an object is refused with a readable message
cases.why: Posting the whole option (key + label) instead of the key is a realistic client bug.
cases.setup: `is_pr_partial_closure_enabled` ON; real line `{{prItemId}}` (refusal guaranteed).
cases.steps: `PATCH /purchase_requests/partial_close` with `closure_reason = {"key":"budget_cut"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Invalid closure reason'. Not a 500.
cases.oracle: 422 + message; PR unchanged.

cases.title: A comma-separated uuid string is accepted as a list
cases.why: Every `*_uuids` parameter silently accepts "a,b" as two ids; it must still go through every rung.
cases.setup: `is_pr_partial_closure_enabled` ON; bogus ids only.
cases.steps: `PATCH /purchase_requests/partial_close` with `pr_item_uuids = "Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==,Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="` and an unconfigurable reason.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Invalid closure reason' (the two ids de-duplicate to one first).
cases.oracle: 422 + message.

cases.title: Line ids sent as an object do not crash the closure service
cases.why: `Array(object)` wraps rather than converts; the service must still answer with a typed refusal.
cases.setup: `is_pr_partial_closure_enabled` ON; bogus ids only.
cases.steps: `PATCH /purchase_requests/partial_close` with `pr_item_ids = {"a": 999999999}` and an unconfigurable reason.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Invalid closure reason'.
cases.oracle: 422 + message.

cases.title: A line on hold can be partially closed through the API
cases.why: The screen offers closure only from Open / In-progress selections; the service excludes in_active, deleted and completed lines but not held ones, so a held line can be closed (and the ERP told) without being reopened first.
cases.setup: gate: `is_pr_hold_enabled` and partial closure ON; a QA PR line on hold with open quantity; a configured reason. No twin (a successful close is a real write).
cases.steps: Partially close the held line.
cases.expected: Desired: refused (or documented as allowed). Today: closed.
cases.oracle: Line closure metadata; Hold tab.

cases.title: Partial closure accepts any number of attachments
cases.why: Code 864 'Number of attachments exceed the maximum allowed limit' exists, but the closure service never applies it; every attachment is copied into the line's metadata.
cases.setup: Partial closure ON; a QA PR line; a configured reason. No twin.
cases.steps: Close it with 200 attachment entries.
cases.expected: Desired: 864 over a limit. Today: accepted.
cases.oracle: Line metadata size.

cases.title: Closing the last open line completes the parent PR
cases.why: The PR header status is derived; after the last line is closed the PR must move to completed and the requisitioner be notified.
cases.setup: A QA PR whose other lines are completed; partial closure ON. No twin.
cases.steps: Partially close its last open line.
cases.expected: Line completed; PR completed; one notification job.
cases.oracle: PR status; activity log `partially_closed`.

cases.title: Closing in-progress quantity while the event is still live leaves the two out of step
cases.why: Without PO integration, closing an only-in-progress line zeroes its in-progress figure while the event still holds it; the next recalculation re-derives in-progress from the live mapping.
cases.setup: No PO integration; partial closure ON; a QA PR line fully in a live QA event. No twin.
cases.steps: Close it; then withdraw the event; read the PR.
cases.expected: Record final open/closed/in-progress; any line showing open > 0 after being fully closed is a defect.
cases.oracle: PR tabs over time.

cases.title: A partially closed line cannot then be pulled into a draft
cases.why: Closure is meant to be final for the closed part; open becomes 0.
cases.setup: A QA PR line partially closed; a draft with lines. No twin.
cases.steps: Pull it at 1.
cases.expected: Refused; HTTP 422, code 557.

cases.title: Offline-PO closure has its own switch and batch cap
cases.why: "Add PO & Close" is a different endpoint with different rules; mixing them up gives the wrong error.
cases.setup: `offline_pr_closure_enabled` OFF, then ON. No twin (`PATCH /purchase_requests/close` is not on the run allowlist).
cases.steps: Close with a PO number: (a) setting off; (b) 21 lines; (c) a foreign or completed line.
cases.expected: (a) 824; (b) 823; (c) code 2 "Invalid PR items or items already processed".
cases.oracle: Codes.

cases.section: Mapping PR lines onto an existing non-PR event
cases.title: Mapping is refused when PR linking is off
cases.why: `pr_linking_enabled` gates "Map to Existing Event".
cases.setup: Setting OFF. No twin (`POST /event_groups/pr_linking` is not on the run allowlist).
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups/pr_linking` with a QA PR line and a QA event.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 837 'PR linking is disabled for your organization'.

cases.section: Mapping PR lines onto an existing non-PR event
cases.title: Lines the user cannot see are refused with a misleading message
cases.why: Visibility failures answer 834 'Purchase request item has no product' — wrong words for "not your PR".
cases.setup: Setting ON; a PR line from a team the user is not in (or another tenant). No twin.
cases.steps: Map it.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 834 (message to be fixed).

cases.section: Mapping PR lines onto an existing non-PR event
cases.title: Held or completed lines cannot be mapped
cases.why: Mapping is sourcing; same status rule as the stage build.
cases.setup: Setting ON; a held QA PR line. No twin.
cases.steps: Map it.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 838.

cases.section: Mapping PR lines onto an existing non-PR event
cases.title: An event that already has an active award proposal cannot take mapped lines
cases.why: Mapping after awarding would attach PR lines to an award they were never part of.
cases.setup: Setting ON; a QA event with an active proposal. No twin.
cases.steps: Map a matching QA PR line.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 835 'Event group already has an active proposal'.

cases.section: Mapping PR lines onto an existing non-PR event
cases.title: No matching event line returns internal ids in the message
cases.why: A line matches only on product + location code + quantity within the open allowance. The 836 message embeds the internal PR item id, product name and location.
cases.setup: Setting ON; a QA event whose line has a different location. No twin.
cases.steps: Map the QA PR line.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 836 "No matching event group line item found for purchase request item ID <internal id> …" (internal id leaked — should be the PR number).
cases.oracle: 836 + message.

cases.section: Counter-offer tasks, AI audit, knockout rounds and draft awards
cases.title: A draft award proposal records the event, lot and Excel mode
cases.why: The draft award must stay tied to its event and lot; companies with an allocation summary template get the new summary.
cases.setup: Event with lots; company with an allocation summary template.
cases.steps: Start an award for lot 2 by Excel; read the draft proposal.
cases.expected: Draft proposal on the event, creator = buyer, event number, lot 2, awarding-by-Excel flag, allocation summary v1 on.
cases.oracle: `proposals/create_draft_service.rb:15-29`.

journeys.title: Sourcing a bill of quantities
journeys.goal: Build an event from a BOQ template with its sections and hundreds of lines, replace lines when the BOQ changes, let vendors price every line, and award it — within the line limits the workspace allows.

cases.section: Screens — creating a BOQ project and uploading the BOQ
cases.title: A good BOQ upload builds the tabbed grid and saves the lines to the project
cases.why: The upload is two calls (parse, then save lines). If the save fails silently the grid shows lines that the project does not have.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A BOQ project; a valid 2-tab sample sheet.
cases.steps: 1. Upload the sheet. 2. Watch network calls. 3. Inspect the grid.
cases.expected: `POST /templates/product_sheet_params` with `excel_type: "multistage"`, then `PATCH /event_groups/<id>` with the lines; toast "Product sheet updated"; tabs shown, section header rows (section number, widgets, description), line numbers like A.1, notes rows with a file icon.
cases.oracle: Network order; grid rows vs sheet; project line count via `get_line_items` after a stage exists.

cases.section: Screens — creating a BOQ project and uploading the BOQ
cases.title: Publishing a BOQ over the line limit is blocked; exactly at the limit is allowed
cases.why: This is the only place the BOQ cap is enforced. 500 must pass, 501 must be blocked with the message.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON; `allowed_maximum_line_items` default (BOQ 500). Two sheets: 500 and 501 priced lines.
cases.steps: 1. Upload the 501-line sheet and try to publish. 2. Upload the 500-line sheet and publish.
cases.expected: 501: publish blocked with "Maximum no of product addition reached". 500: publishes.
cases.oracle: Error shown; publish request sent only for 500.

cases.section: Screens — creating a BOQ project and uploading the BOQ
cases.title: "BOQ based RFX Project" appears in New Event only when BOQ is allowed
cases.why: The menu item is the only door into BOQ; it must follow the company's BOQ permission (switch + an active BOQ template) in both directions.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed`. Two QA buyers: one in a workspace where it is ON, one where it is OFF; eRFX allowed in both.
cases.steps: 1. Events page → open "New Event". 2. Read the menu items.
cases.expected: ON: three items — "Single Stage", "eRFX Project", and "BOQ based RFX Project" ("Source BOQ via a project approach"). OFF: only the first two.
cases.oracle: Menu item titles; the dashboard config `boq_in_erfx_allowed` from `/v1/dashboard_configuration`.

cases.section: Screens — creating a BOQ project and uploading the BOQ
cases.title: Choosing the BOQ project creates an empty BOQ draft and opens the BOQ template picker
cases.why: The draft is created on page load with the BOQ flag; the picker must then offer only BOQ templates.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON; at least one BOQ template.
cases.steps: 1. New Event → "BOQ based RFX Project". 2. Watch network calls. 3. Open the template picker.
cases.expected: URL has `projectCreation=true&boqProject=true`; one `POST /event_groups` with `config.boq_based_rfx: true`; the picker requests `GET /templates?type_identifier=boq&hide_onboarding_v2_templates=true` and lists only BOQ templates. Banner: "Please choose a template and upload a BOQ sheet to proceed".
cases.oracle: Network log; picker contents; banner text.

cases.section: Screens — creating a BOQ project and uploading the BOQ
cases.title: Upload Sheet modal: file types, disabled OK, and the BOQ sample download
cases.why: The sample must be the BOQ sample (`boq_items_sheet`), or the buyer fills the wrong layout.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A BOQ project with a BOQ template chosen.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Upload Sheet". 2. Check OK before choosing a file. 3. Click "Download Template". 4. Open the file chooser.
cases.expected: Title "Upload Excel"; OK disabled until a file is chosen; Download calls `GET /templates/excel_template/<template>?sheet_type=boq_items_sheet` and downloads the returned `excel_url`; the chooser accepts .csv, .xlsx, .xls.
cases.oracle: Button state; network call; accept attribute.

cases.section: Screens — creating a BOQ project and uploading the BOQ
cases.title: A section-numbering error from the server is shown as a toast
cases.why: The frontend has no BOQ-specific messages; the server's text is the only guidance the buyer gets.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A sheet starting at section "B".
cases.steps: 1. Upload.
cases.expected: Toast "Invalid section, current section B, expected section A, Please Add Valid one"; the grid is unchanged.
cases.oracle: Toast text equals the API message (API-XDBOQ-057).

cases.section: Screens — creating a BOQ project and uploading the BOQ
cases.title: Re-uploading a BOQ replaces the existing one without any warning
cases.why: A re-upload deletes every line not in the new sheet (and resets draft awards). There is no confirm dialog; a buyer who uploads the wrong file loses the BOQ.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A BOQ project with an uploaded 3-line sheet.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Upload Sheet" again and upload a 2-line sheet.
cases.expected: No confirmation; the grid shows the 2 new lines; the 3 old ones are gone. Should: a "this will replace the current BOQ" confirmation. Record as a UX gap.
cases.oracle: Grid; project lines.

cases.section: Screens — creating a BOQ project and uploading the BOQ
cases.title: A company-specific limit overrides the default
cases.why: Raising a customer to 1,000 BOQ lines is done by overriding `allowed_maximum_line_items.boq` for that company; the dashboard must use it.
cases.setup: A QA company with `allowed_maximum_line_items` = `{boq: 1000, non_boq: 65}`. A 1,000-line and a 1,001-line sheet.
cases.steps: 1. Publish each.
cases.expected: 1,000 publishes; 1,001 shows "Maximum no of product addition reached".
cases.oracle: As above.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: Comparison grid for a BOQ: Event Summary first, tab totals, section rows with notes
cases.why: Buyers compare BOQ bids by tab and section totals; the summary tab must agree with the API totals.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A live BOQ project with two QA vendors' bids.
cases.steps: 1. Open the comparison/QCS. 2. Switch tabs. 3. Toggle notes on a section.
cases.expected: First tab "Event Summary" with one row per tab/section and each vendor's total; each tab ends with a "<tab> Total" row; section rows show number, title and widgets with "Hide Notes"/"Show Notes"; "Other Charges" rows hidden on tabs; a tab with a pending task shows a red info icon. Totals equal `quote_summary` (API-XDBOQ-091), rounded for display.
cases.oracle: Grid totals vs API.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: The buyer's surrogate bid upload for BOQ
cases.why: Buyers enter offline BOQ quotes on a vendor's behalf; the upload button follows a company setting.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON; `is_bid_sheet_upload_enabled` ON (and a second QA company with it OFF). A live BOQ stage.
cases.steps: 1. Open "Add Bid" for the QA vendor. 2. Download the template. 3. Upload it filled.
cases.expected: ON: "Upload Excel" shown; download calls `GET /v1/trade/<stage>/download_event_details?company_uuid=…`; the upload accepts only .xlsx/.xls, calls `POST /v1/trade/<stage>/upload_bid_excel` and shows "Excel Uploaded Successfully"; prices fill the drawer but no bid is placed until "Place bid" ("Bid placed on behalf of <vendor>"). OFF: no Upload Excel button.
cases.oracle: Button presence; network; bid count before/after.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: Awarding a BOQ is vendor-level only
cases.why: The server widens any BOQ award to the whole BOQ (API-XDBOQ-095); the screen must not pretend otherwise by offering line selection.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A closed BOQ project with two vendors' bids.
cases.steps: 1. Start Awarding (manual). 2. Try to select individual lines. 3. Submit with no vendor selected.
cases.expected: No per-line selection; vendor columns say "Select for awarding"/"Awarded"; no "Select All"; submitting empty shows "Please award for at least one Vendor"; the request is `POST /proposal/<id>/add_response?lot_no=…` without line ids.
cases.oracle: UI elements; request body.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: "Awarding with Excel" appears for BOQ when sheet awarding is allowed
cases.why: It is the only item-wise route for BOQ (API-XDBOQ-096); its steps and messages must be clear.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON; `allow_sheet_awarding` ON. A closed BOQ project.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Start Awarding". 2. Choose "Awarding with Excel". 3. Download, then upload a filled sheet and submit. 4. On the awarding page, click "Discard Proposal".
cases.expected: Dropdown "Manual Award" / "Awarding with Excel"; drawer "Upload File" with "Download the Awarding sheet" and "Upload filled sheet"; toasts "Generating template", "Report is ready for download", "File uploaded successfully", "Awarding sheet submitted successfully"; submitting without a file: "Please upload a file before submitting"; the awarding page tag "Awarding is done via the award sheet. To change it, upload a revised sheet."; discard → "Draft proposal discarded".
cases.oracle: Texts and network sequence.

cases.section: Screens — creating a BOQ project and uploading the BOQ
cases.title: An ordinary eRFX project never offers BOQ templates
cases.why: A BOQ template on an ordinary project produces a stage with tabs but a project that is not BOQ (mixed rules).
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON; a BOQ template and an ordinary template.
cases.steps: 1. New Event → "eRFX Project". 2. Open the pricing-stage template picker.
cases.expected: BOQ-labelled templates are absent.
cases.oracle: Picker contents vs `GET /templates?type_identifier=trade` reply.

cases.section: Screens — creating a BOQ project and uploading the BOQ
cases.title: A BOQ project hides the line-item controls an ordinary project has
cases.why: BOQ lines come only from the sheet; manual line editing would desynchronise the BOQ.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A new BOQ project draft.
cases.steps: 1. Look at the project header and the technical (RFP) stage form. 2. Open stage configuration.
cases.expected: No "Items" button/count; no "Line Items" section on the RFP stage; evaluation offers only "I'll do vendor wise evaluation" (no line-item-wise option); no AI RFP generator; no fast-bidding option.
cases.oracle: Elements absent.

cases.section: Screens — creating a BOQ project and uploading the BOQ
cases.title: Rejected rows are listed under "View failed entries"
cases.why: Buyers fix uploads row by row; each failing cell must say why.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A sheet the server returns with `in_valid` rows (ordinary template-product sheet; for BOQ `in_valid` is normally empty — see API-XDBOQ-063).
cases.steps: 1. Upload. 2. Click "View failed entries".
cases.expected: "Failed to upload N entries." with "Click here"/"View failed entries"; a "Failed Entries" modal with each bad cell's error message as a tooltip.
cases.oracle: N equals `in_valid.length`.

cases.section: Screens — creating a BOQ project and uploading the BOQ
cases.title: A limit config with only one key disables the other limit
cases.why: If the override is `{boq: 1000}` (no `non_boq`), the selector returns `nonBoq: undefined`, and `count > undefined` is always false — ordinary events lose their limit entirely. Missing config falls back to 500/65.
cases.setup: A QA company with `allowed_maximum_line_items` = `{boq: 1000}` only.
cases.steps: 1. Create an ordinary event with 70 lines and publish.
cases.expected: Publishes (no limit). Should: fall back to 65 for the missing key.
cases.oracle: Publish succeeds with 70 lines.

cases.section: Screens — creating a BOQ project and uploading the BOQ
cases.title: Recreate Event counts lines differently from create
cases.why: Create and live edit compare `data.length - 1` (the sheet has a trailing empty row); Recreate compares `data.length`, so a BOQ of exactly the limit is refused on recreate. One hard-coded company is exempt in three places.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON; default limit 500. A closed QA BOQ event with exactly 500 lines.
cases.steps: 1. Recreate the event from its menu and continue.
cases.expected: "You can have at max 500 line-items in an event" although the original had 500. Should: same rule as create.
cases.oracle: Error shown.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: The BOQ sheet grid: no row delete, no pagination, line numbers from the BOQ
cases.why: BOQ rows must keep their identity; deleting or auto-filling single rows would break section totals.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A BOQ project with an uploaded 2-tab sheet.
cases.steps: 1. Inspect the sheet grid on the create screen.
cases.expected: Tabs at the top (first auto-selected, hidden tabs skipped); row numbers shown as the BOQ line numbers; no delete-row column; no pagination; no drag-to-fill; product cell is plain text; quantities show value + unit.
cases.oracle: DOM checks.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: Switching tabs pages the quote by tab
cases.why: Large BOQs are fetched per tab and page; a wrong tab index shows another tab's rows (API-XDBOQ-081).
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A BOQ stage with 3 tabs and one vendor bid.
cases.steps: 1. Open the vendor's quote. 2. Switch to tab 3 and scroll.
cases.expected: Requests `GET /v1/trade/<stage>/quote_details/<bid>?tab=<index>&page=<n>` with the selected tab's index; rows shown belong to tab 3 only.
cases.oracle: Network params; row line numbers.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: A partial surrogate BOQ bid is allowed unless the stage closes as a lot
cases.why: Matches the server (API-XDBOQ-089): required fields are only enforced on rows with a price, unless lot closing.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. Two live BOQ stages: line-item closing and lot closing.
cases.steps: 1. In "Add Bid", price only 2 of 5 lines and place the bid on each stage.
cases.expected: Line-item closing: accepted. Lot closing: blocked by the drawer's validation. At least one priced row is always required.
cases.oracle: Validation message; bid created or not.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: Controls hidden on a BOQ event
cases.why: These features have no BOQ meaning (or break with tabs); they must stay hidden.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A live BOQ event and an ordinary one.
cases.steps: 1. Compare the event header, action bar, create footer and auction configuration.
cases.expected: On BOQ: no "View by" dropdown, no Price Trends tab, no bidding/default currency toggle, no Savings footer button on create, no basket-auction config, no auction strategy tabs (unless a service template).
cases.oracle: Elements present on ordinary, absent on BOQ.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: The BOQ report is offered only for BOQ events
cases.why: The BOQ report has its own fixed format; offering it elsewhere produces empty files.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A BOQ event and an ordinary event.
cases.steps: 1. Open "Download Report" on each.
cases.expected: "BOQ Report" listed only on the BOQ event, with its format selector disabled.
cases.oracle: Report list.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: No line-item delete in a BOQ project's details
cases.why: Deleting one BOQ line by hand bypasses the sheet; on the API side even one-line deletes reach the unscoped deletion path (API-XDBOQ-031).
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A BOQ project and an ordinary project.
cases.steps: 1. Open project details → line items → row menu.
cases.expected: "Delete" absent on BOQ, present on ordinary.
cases.oracle: Menu items.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: Convert to auction and new version keep the BOQ context
cases.why: Both flows reopen the creation screen; losing `boqProject=true` there turns a BOQ auction into an ordinary one.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A closed BOQ RFQ project.
cases.steps: 1. "Convert to auction". 2. Back, then "Create new version".
cases.expected: Both navigations carry `boqProject=true`; the screens show the BOQ grid (tabs), not the line-item form.
cases.oracle: URL; grid.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: BOQ PRs cannot be put in the cart with other PRs
cases.why: One BOQ PR becomes one BOQ project; mixing would create a project with two BOQs or a BOQ plus material lines.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. Two QA BOQ PRs and one QA material PR.
cases.steps: 1. Select both BOQ PRs → purchase. 2. Select one BOQ + the material PR → purchase.
cases.expected: 1: "Multiple BOQ-based PR cannot be purchased together". 2: "BOQ-based PR cannot pe purchased along with <type> PR" (note the typo "pe" — log it).
cases.oracle: Messages.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: Marking a template as BOQ hides the delivery-location column
cases.why: BOQ lines use a "Free Text" location created by the upload; a buyer-hub column would demand a real location per line.
cases.setup: A QA buyer with template permissions.
cases.steps: 1. Templates → new pricing template. 2. Tick "BOQ". 3. Save; open the template list.
cases.expected: The buyer_hub widget disappears when BOQ is ticked; the list labels the template "BOQ"; after saving, the company's `boq_in_erfx_allowed?` can become true (if the switch is set).
cases.oracle: Widget list; label.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: Editing the sheet of a live BOQ event respects the limit
cases.why: Live edits are allowed for BOQ (even after close on the API side); the line limit must still apply.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON; default limit 500. A live BOQ event with 499 lines.
cases.steps: 1. Edit the event sheet and add two lines; save.
cases.expected: "You can have at max 500 line-items in an event"; nothing saved.
cases.oracle: Message; stage unchanged.

cases.section: Screens — the BOQ grid, bidding and awarding
cases.title: A BOQ project from a PR keeps the PR's template and lets the sheet be edited
cases.why: A BOQ PR fixes the template (it carries the BOQ sheet); the sheet must still be editable before publish.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A QA BOQ PR with an attached BOQ sheet.
cases.steps: 1. Convert the PR into a project. 2. Try to change the template. 3. Edit a quantity in the sheet.
cases.expected: The template selector is locked; the sheet is unlocked and editable; on publish the PR is linked (API-XDBOQ-039).
cases.oracle: Selector state; PR mapping after publish.

cases.title: A BOQ project with real line items is still refused when BOQ is switched off
cases.why: The dashboard hides "BOQ based RFX Project" when the switch is off, but a hand-made request could try to sneak a BOQ project in by also sending ordinary line items. The BOQ gate must win.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` OFF for the workspace (switch not set, or no active BOQ template). Buyer session; a catalog product and variant.
cases.steps: 1. Create a draft event with the BOQ flag on and one catalog line item: `POST /event_groups` `{"status":"draft","title":"QA_Platform_DBOQ_001_{{stamp}}","config":{"boq_based_rfx":true},"line_items":[{"product_uuid":"{{productUuid}}","product_quality_uuid":"{{productQualityUuid}}","quantity":{"unitSymbol":"Nos","value":10}}]}`. 2. Read the error.
cases.expected: Refused; no event is created. HTTP 422, code 101 "You are not allowed to perform this action".
cases.oracle: 422 + code 101; the Draft tab shows no `QA_Platform_DBOQ_001_…` event.

cases.section: Re-uploading the BOQ sheet — PATCH /event_groups line items on a BOQ project
cases.title: Re-uploading on a draft BOQ project replaces every line
cases.why: A buyer fixing a typo in the BOQ re-uploads the whole sheet; the old lines must disappear completely (lines, their stage rows, forms and PR links), or vendors see duplicates.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A draft QA BOQ project with a BOQ RFQ stage built from a 3-line sheet (lines L1–L3), linked to a QA BOQ PR.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/<uuid>` with `line_items` = two NEW rows (no ids). 2. `GET /event_groups/<uuid>/get_line_items`. 3. Read the stage (`GET /trade/<stage>`).
cases.expected: 200; reply `event_group_line_item_ids` = the 2 new ids. L1–L3 become in_active (draft project), their stage rows become void, their forms and form mappings in_active, their line-to-stage mappings in_active, and their PR mappings in_active with PR quantities recomputed. get_line_items count 2.
cases.oracle: Line count 2; stage shows no rows for L1–L3; PR open quantity restored.

cases.section: Re-uploading the BOQ sheet — PATCH /event_groups line items on a BOQ project
cases.title: Re-uploading on a live BOQ project deletes the old lines and can close the stage
cases.why: On a live project the old lines are marked deleted and their forms deleted; a stage left with no active line is closed on the spot — vendors in the middle of bidding lose the event.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A LIVE QA BOQ project (lot-based, with `lot_config`), one BOQ RFQ stage, 3 lines, QA vendor invited.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/<uuid>` with two new rows. 2. Read lines, the stage and the PR activity log.
cases.expected: 200; L1–L3 status deleted; their forms deleted; an activity entry "deleted_from_event" on the linked PR items; any lot stage that no longer has an active line is set to closed with closed_at now.
cases.oracle: get_line_items count 2; stage status (closed when its lines were all replaced); PR item activity log.

cases.section: Re-uploading the BOQ sheet — PATCH /event_groups line items on a BOQ project
cases.title: Re-uploading is refused when a live proposal includes the old lines
cases.why: Once lines are in an active, submitted or approved award, deleting them would orphan the award.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A QA BOQ project with a proposal in status active/requested/selected that covers L1.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/<uuid>` with a fresh set of rows (L1 omitted).
cases.expected: Refused, nothing changes (the new rows are rolled back). HTTP 422, code 711 "You cannot delete this line item from the project".
cases.oracle: 422 + 711; get_line_items unchanged.

cases.section: Changing a live event's BOQ nature and the line-item deletion guards — PATCH /event_groups
cases.title: PATCH can turn an ordinary live event into a BOQ project without the BOQ switch
cases.why: Create checks `boq_in_erfx_allowed?`; update does not. The update service merges any `config` keys into the stored config, so `{"config":{"boq_based_rfx":true}}` flips an ordinary event to BOQ in a workspace that has not bought BOQ — and from then on every line edit replaces ALL lines (section 2).
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` OFF. A live QA ordinary event with two lines. Changes what the event is, so no twin on the shared sandbox (it would change the deletion rules for every later case).
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/<uuid>` `{"config":{"boq_based_rfx":true}}`. 2. `GET /event_groups/<uuid>`. 3. `PATCH` with one new line row.
cases.expected: Should: 422 code 101, config unchanged. Today (likely defect): 200, config.boq_based_rfx true, and step 3 deletes both original lines.
cases.oracle: Config read-back; get_line_items after step 3.

cases.section: Changing a live event's BOQ nature and the line-item deletion guards — PATCH /event_groups
cases.title: Two "deleted" rows get past the one-line guard and empty the event
cases.why: The guard only fires when the request has exactly one row. Sending the same line twice (or the line plus any junk row) deletes the event's only line.
cases.setup: A live QA ordinary event with exactly one line L1 (not the shared sandbox — this case destroys its line).
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/<uuid>` `{"line_items":[{"uuid":"L1","status":"deleted"},{"uuid":"L1","status":"deleted"}]}`. 2. Read lines and the stage.
cases.expected: Should: 422 code 711. Today (likely defect): 200; L1 deleted, its forms deleted, and a lot stage with no active line is closed.
cases.oracle: get_line_items count 0; stage status.

cases.section: Changing a live event's BOQ nature and the line-item deletion guards — PATCH /event_groups
cases.title: A line item of ANOTHER event can be pulled into mine by sending its id
cases.why: `create_line_items` loads existing lines by the ids in the request with no event or company filter, then sets their event group to mine and upserts them. Any buyer who knows (or enumerates — raw integer `id` is accepted) a line id can move another event's line, even another company's, into their own event. Cross-tenant write.
cases.setup: Two QA events in the same QA company, A (mine) and B (one line LB). Never use a real event.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/<A>` `{"line_items":[{"uuid":"<LB uuid>","product_uuid":"{{productUuid}}","product_quality_uuid":"{{productQualityUuid}}","quantity":{"unitSymbol":"Nos","value":1}}]}`. 2. Read lines of A and of B.
cases.expected: Should: 422 (line does not belong to this event), B untouched. Today (likely defect): 200; LB now belongs to A (event_group_id overwritten, serial and quantity replaced) and has disappeared from B.
cases.oracle: get_line_items of A includes LB; of B no longer does.

cases.section: Changing a live event's BOQ nature and the line-item deletion guards — PATCH /event_groups
cases.title: A line item of ANOTHER event can be deleted by sending its id with status "deleted"
cases.why: The ordinary deletion path looks lines up by the request ids with no event filter (`EventGroupLineItem…where(id: egli_ids)`) and marks them deleted, deletes their forms, and on a draft voids their stage rows. The only authorisation is on MY event.
cases.setup: Two QA events in the same QA company: A (mine, two lines so the one-line guard does not fire) and B (two lines, LB1, LB2).
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/<A>` `{"line_items":[{"uuid":"<LB1 uuid>","status":"deleted"}]}`. 2. Read B.
cases.expected: Should: 422, B untouched. Today (likely defect): 200 and LB1 (event B) is deleted with its forms.
cases.oracle: get_line_items of B count drops to 1.

cases.title: Uploading a sheet for a DYNAMIC BOQ template crashes on the unit lookup
cases.why: `insert_units` calls `get_hash_value(line_item, unit_col, ["Unit", …])` with the fallback list as a third positional argument, but the helper takes it as a keyword (`fallback_keys:`). On Ruby 3.2 that raises ArgumentError for any sheet with at least one priced row — dynamic BOQ upload cannot succeed.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A QA BOQ template of template_type "dynamic"; a sheet with one priced row.
cases.steps: 1. Upload with `excel_type=multistage`.
cases.expected: Should: 200 with the row in `valid.data`. Today (likely defect, from reading the code): HTTP 500 ArgumentError.
cases.oracle: Status and body.

cases.section: Reading BOQ lines and tab pages
cases.title: Asking for a tab page on an ordinary stage crashes the quote view
cases.why: The dashboard sends `tab` and `page` when it pages a BOQ sheet. The stage version of the paging helper has no "no tabs" guard (the project version has one), so tab/page on any stage without tabs is a 500 — and it runs before the quote is even looked up.
cases.setup: The sandbox stage {{tradeId}} (no tabs). (Not on the default allowlist; a read.)
cases.steps: 1. `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/quote_details/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==?tab=1&page=1`.
cases.expected: Should: 422 code 4 (no such quote) or the tab params ignored. Today (likely defect): HTTP 500 (`nil['range']`). Never 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: A BOQ award always gives the whole BOQ to the chosen vendor
cases.why: On a BOQ project the server overwrites each vendor's line selection with every line that vendor quoted; a partial or item-wise payload is silently widened, not refused. Buyers who think they awarded part of a BOQ have in fact awarded all of it.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A closed QA BOQ project with one RFQ stage, QA vendor quoted 5 lines.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /proposal` for the project. 2. `POST /proposal/<id>/add_response` naming the vendor with `egli_uuids` of 2 lines. 3. Read the proposal.
cases.expected: 200; the proposal holds all 5 lines for the vendor; no error.
cases.oracle: Proposal's line ids for the vendor.

cases.title: A null BOQ flag with no line items is "insufficient parameters"
cases.why: Only a BOQ project may start empty. A null flag must fall back to the ordinary rule.
cases.setup: Any `boq_in_erfx_allowed` state. Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /event_groups` with `config.boq_based_rfx: null` and no line items.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 2 "Insufficient parameters".
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2; nothing created.

cases.title: An explicit "not BOQ" with no line items is "insufficient parameters"
cases.why: `boq_based_rfx: false` must keep the line-items requirement of an ordinary event.
cases.setup: Any `boq_in_erfx_allowed` state. Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /event_groups` with `config.boq_based_rfx: false` and no line items.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 2 "Insufficient parameters".
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.title: A BOQ project starts empty when line items are null
cases.why: This is exactly what the dashboard sends when a buyer opens "BOQ based RFX Project": an empty BOQ draft is created on page load and the lines arrive later from the sheet upload.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON (switch set and an active BOQ template exists). Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /event_groups` `{"status":"draft","title":"QA_Platform_DBOQ_006_{{stamp}}","config":{"boq_based_rfx":true},"line_items":null}`.
cases.expected: A draft BOQ project with no line items. HTTP 200; `config.boq_based_rfx` true; no line-item ids.
cases.oracle: Reply config + empty `event_group_line_item_ids` (the project and line reads answer 455 until a stage exists — see API-XDBOQ-016).

cases.title: A BOQ project seeded with one catalog line keeps it, numbered 1
cases.why: BOQ projects created from a PR or a clone arrive with lines; the BOQ flag must not drop them, and serial numbers are what the BOQ grid prints next to each line.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A catalog product and variant.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /event_groups` with the BOQ flag on and one line (10 Nos). 2. Read the reply.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with exactly one line-item id; the line's serial number is 1 and its variant is the one sent.
cases.oracle: Reply: one id, and the serialized line shows serial_number 1 (the line read needs a stage first).

cases.title: Exactly 500 BOQ lines (the default cap) are created in one request
cases.why: 500 is the default BOQ limit the dashboard enforces. #15339 reworked the create path to bulk-insert so a BOQ this size no longer times out; a slow or failed create here is a performance regression.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON; `allowed_maximum_line_items` at its default (BOQ 500).
cases.steps: 1. `POST /event_groups` with the BOQ flag on and 500 catalog lines (quantities 1..500). 2. Time the reply.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with 500 ids, serial numbers 1..500, well inside the request timeout. The server applies no cap.
cases.oracle: Reply has 500 ids with serials 1..500.

cases.title: The switch alone is not enough: no active BOQ template means no BOQ project
cases.why: `boq_in_erfx_allowed?` also requires an active `t-boq` template. A company whose only BOQ template is deactivated loses the menu item and the create — support tickets look like "BOQ disappeared".
cases.setup: A QA company with `boq_in_erfx_allowed` set; deactivate (or never create) every BOQ template. Needs a company-configuration change, so no twin.
cases.steps: 1. Read `GET /v1/dashboard_configuration` → `boq_in_erfx_allowed`. 2. `POST /event_groups` with the BOQ flag on. 3. Re-activate one BOQ template and repeat.
cases.expected: Without a template: config shows false; create refused with code 101 "You are not allowed to perform this action". With a template: config true; create 200.
cases.oracle: The two replies differ only by the template's status.

cases.title: Read-back of a fresh BOQ project
cases.why: Every later BOQ screen keys off `config.boq_based_rfx` from the project read; if the flag is lost on read-back the dashboard renders an ordinary project (Items button, line-item delete, line evaluation).
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A BOQ draft from API-XDBOQ-006 (needs that uuid, so no twin).
cases.steps: 1. `GET /event_groups/<uuid>`. 2. `GET /event_groups/<uuid>/get_line_items`.
cases.expected: Before a stage exists both reads are refused: HTTP 422, code 455 "You are not authorized to perform this action" — `show?` and `get_line_items?` require a stage the user can see. After the BOQ stage is added (template_input) the project read shows `config.boq_based_rfx` true and the line read returns the BOQ lines with total_pages ≥ 1.
cases.oracle: 455 before the stage; config flag and line count after.

cases.section: Re-uploading the BOQ sheet — PATCH /event_groups line items on a BOQ project
cases.title: Rows that carry an existing id are updated in place, only the omitted ones are deleted
cases.why: The dashboard may resend existing lines with their ids; those must be kept (same id, same bids) and only the lines missing from the request deleted — otherwise every re-upload wipes vendor quotes.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A draft QA BOQ project with lines L1, L2, L3.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/<uuid>` with rows `{uuid: L1, …new quantity}`, `{uuid: L2, …}` and one new row.
cases.expected: 200; L1 and L2 keep their ids with updated quantity/serial; a new id for the third row; L3 in_active. Serial numbers are 1, 2, 3 in request order.
cases.oracle: get_line_items: ids L1, L2, new; L3 absent.

cases.section: Re-uploading the BOQ sheet — PATCH /event_groups line items on a BOQ project
cases.title: Re-uploading clears the draft award of each lot
cases.why: A draft award that points at deleted lines would submit garbage; the update service resets draft proposals (responses emptied, snapshot reset) — the buyer has to award again.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A QA BOQ project with a DRAFT proposal for lot 1 (not section-form based).
cases.steps: 1. Re-upload (PATCH with new rows). 2. Read the draft proposal.
cases.expected: 200; the draft proposal's responses are empty and its meta reset to the project ref and lot number.
cases.oracle: Proposal read shows empty responses_hash.

cases.section: Re-uploading the BOQ sheet — PATCH /event_groups line items on a BOQ project
cases.title: On a BOQ project the client's "deleted" flags are ignored
cases.why: BOQ deletion is computed by the server (everything not in the new set). A client that sends `"status":"deleted"` rows expecting the ordinary behaviour still loses every omitted line.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A draft QA BOQ project with L1, L2.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH` with `[{uuid: L1, status: "deleted"}]` only.
cases.expected: No non-deleted rows → no new ids → every line of the project (L1 and L2) is in the deletion set; with one request row and two active lines the 711 guard does not fire, so both lines go. Should: refuse an upload that leaves the BOQ empty.
cases.oracle: get_line_items count 0 afterwards.

cases.section: Re-uploading the BOQ sheet — PATCH /event_groups line items on a BOQ project
cases.title: A live re-upload does not touch the stage's own rows
cases.why: The project-level PATCH changes project lines and forms; the stage sheet the vendors bid on is edited separately (PATCH /trade/:id). If the two drift, vendors quote on lines the project no longer has.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A LIVE QA BOQ project with one RFQ stage; the QA vendor has a draft bid.
cases.steps: 1. Re-upload via `PATCH /event_groups/<uuid>`. 2. Read the stage sheet and the vendor's bid.
cases.expected: Project lines replaced (deleted/new); stage rows are not voided by this request (void only happens on a draft project); the dashboard then saves the stage sheet with `PATCH /trade/<stage>` — check both end in the same set.
cases.oracle: get_line_items vs the stage's trade products.

cases.section: Changing a live event's BOQ nature and the line-item deletion guards — PATCH /event_groups
cases.title: Switching a BOQ project back to ordinary hides its tabs everywhere
cases.why: `EventGroup#tabs` and `tabs_summary` return nil when the flag is off, so vendor tab totals and the BOQ grid vanish while the stage still has tabs — a half-BOQ event.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A live QA BOQ project with a BOQ stage and one vendor bid.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/<uuid>` `{"config":{"boq_based_rfx":false}}`. 2. Read the project, the master QCS and the vendor's quote summary.
cases.expected: Should: refused once a BOQ stage exists. Today: 200; project tabs nil; the stage itself still reports `is_boq_event` true — record the mismatch.
cases.oracle: Project read vs stage read.

cases.section: Changing a live event's BOQ nature and the line-item deletion guards — PATCH /event_groups
cases.title: Deleting the only line item of a live event is refused
cases.why: An event with no lines cannot be bid on or awarded.
cases.setup: The sandbox: live, one pricing stage, exactly one active line item {{lineItemUuid}}, no bids, no proposals.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` `{"line_items":[{"uuid":"{{lineItemUuid}}","status":"deleted"}]}`. 2. `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_line_items`.
cases.expected: Refused; the line is still active. HTTP 422, code 711 "You cannot delete this line item from the project".
cases.oracle: 422 + 711; get_line_items count still 1.

cases.section: Changing a live event's BOQ nature and the line-item deletion guards — PATCH /event_groups
cases.title: Line items sent as text on a PATCH are refused, not a crash
cases.why: Both the BOQ re-upload and ordinary line edits go through this request; malformed input must be refused, not take the server down.
cases.setup: The sandbox.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` `{"line_items":"QA_Platform_not_a_list_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: Should: 422 code 2; sandbox unchanged. Today: HTTP 500 (the service calls `.select` on the string). Never 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; line count unchanged.

cases.section: Changing a live event's BOQ nature and the line-item deletion guards — PATCH /event_groups
cases.title: A PATCH line with an unknown product is refused, not a crash
cases.why: A BOQ re-upload containing a product that was deactivated meanwhile must name the bad row, not fail the whole save.
cases.setup: The sandbox; a catalog variant.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` with one new row whose `product_uuid` is `Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: Should: 4xx (80 "Product not found" or 2); nothing added. Today: HTTP 500 (`product.id` on nil). Never 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; line count unchanged.

cases.section: Linking the BOQ purchase request — PATCH /event_groups with purchase_request_id
cases.title: Linking a purchase request that does not exist is refused
cases.why: Only an active BOQ PR of this workspace may feed a BOQ project.
cases.setup: The sandbox.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` `{"purchase_request_uuid":"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="}`.
cases.expected: Refused; nothing linked. HTTP 422, code 101 "You are not allowed to perform this action" (checked before authorize).

cases.section: Linking the BOQ purchase request — PATCH /event_groups with purchase_request_id
cases.title: Linking an active BOQ PR to a live BOQ project maps it once and marks it in progress
cases.why: This is how a BOQ PR shows "in progress" and later "completed"; double links or a missing worker leave the PR open forever.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A QA BOQ PR (one item) and a LIVE QA BOQ project.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/<uuid>` `{"purchase_request_uuid":"<pr>"}`. 2. Repeat the same request. 3. Read the PR.
cases.expected: Both 200; exactly one project↔PR mapping (find_or_create); the in-progress worker runs; the PR item becomes in_progress (quantity_in_progress 1) while the commercial stage is open, completed once it closes.
cases.oracle: PR read; one mapping row.

cases.section: BOQ templates and the sample sheet — GET /templates
cases.title: The BOQ template picker list comes back well-formed
cases.why: This is the exact call the BOQ project's template picker makes; an error or a non-BOQ template in it sends the buyer down the wrong sheet.
cases.setup: Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /templates?type_identifier=boq&hide_onboarding_v2_templates=true`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with `{default:[…], saved:[…]}`, every entry a `t-boq` template (either list may be empty). When `boq_in_erfx_allowed` is ON the company has at least one active BOQ template, but `saved` only lists those this user may see.
cases.oracle: Every returned template's type identifiers include `t-boq`.

cases.section: BOQ templates and the sample sheet — GET /templates
cases.title: An exclude list sent as plain text is refused, not a JSON crash
cases.why: Ordinary eRFX projects exclude BOQ templates from their picker. A string exclude list goes straight into `JSON.parse`, and the parse error is not rescued.
cases.setup: Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /templates?type_identifier=trade&exclude_type_identifiers=boq`.
cases.expected: Should: 422 code 2. Today (likely defect): HTTP 500 (JSON::ParserError). Never 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: BOQ templates and the sample sheet — GET /templates
cases.title: The BOQ sample sheet has the layout the uploader expects
cases.why: Buyers fill the downloaded sheet and upload it back; if the sample's headers or section numbering don't match the parser's rules (section 6), every first upload fails.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. One active QA BOQ template (needs its id, so no twin).
cases.steps: 1. `GET /templates/excel_template/<template>?sheet_type=boq_items_sheet`. 2. Open the file from `excel_url`. 3. Repeat with `sheet_type=nonsense`.
cases.expected: Step 1: 200 with `excel_url`; the workbook has sheets "Tab 1".."Tab 4"; row 1 is the Buyer/Vendor group header, row 2 the column headers starting with "Section", with "Unit" right after the quantity column and hidden widgets left out; sample sections A (A.1, A.2) and B (B.1, B.2). The download is logged. Step 3: 422 code 2 "Insufficient parameters".
cases.oracle: Workbook structure; the step-3 code.

cases.title: Uploading a BOQ sheet without the file is refused
cases.why: The first line of the upload; a missing file must be refused before any parsing or master-data insert.
cases.setup: Buyer session. (Endpoint not on the runner's default allowlist; refused on its first line.)
cases.steps: 1. `POST /templates/product_sheet_params` `{"template_uuid":"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==","excel_type":"multistage","sheet_type":"boq_items_sheet"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 "Insufficient parameters".
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.title: A BOQ sheet uploaded without excel_type "multistage" crashes instead of being refused
cases.why: The BOQ checks only run for `excel_type=multistage`; the default `"trade"` feeds flat rows into the multistage validator, which calls `.map` on nil. Any client (or a dashboard regression) that forgets the type gets a 500.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A QA BOQ template (template-based, not dynamic) and a valid BOQ sample sheet.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /templates/product_sheet_params` with the sheet and the template, without `excel_type`.
cases.expected: Should: 422 code 15 with a clear message. Today (likely defect): HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: The first section must be "A"
cases.why: Section labels drive the hierarchy (A, A.1, A.1.1). A sheet starting at "B" or "1" is refused with the expected label in the message so the buyer can fix it.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A QA BOQ template; a sheet whose first Section is "B".
cases.steps: 1. Upload with `excel_type=multistage`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 15, message "Invalid section, current section B, expected section A, Please Add Valid one".
cases.oracle: Exact message.

cases.title: Section label rules: duplicate, trailing dot, lowercase, skipped level, non-consecutive
cases.why: Each rule protects the parent/child roll-up of section totals. Run one sheet per rule.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A QA BOQ template; five sheets: (a) "A, A.1, A.1" duplicate; (b) "A." trailing dot; (c) "a" lowercase; (d) "A, A.1.1" skipping A.1; (e) "A, A.1, A.3" skipping A.2; (f) "A, B" with no A.1 between.
cases.steps: 1. Upload each sheet with `excel_type=multistage`.
cases.expected: Each: HTTP 422, code 15, "Invalid section, current section <label>, expected section <x>, Please Add Valid one", where <x> is the next valid label (e.g. "A.2", "A.1"), or "Should include Capital Alphabet" for (c).
cases.oracle: The expected-section part of each message.

cases.title: Sections A.9 → A.10 are accepted as consecutive
cases.why: The checks compare labels partly by string length; BOQs routinely have 10+ items per section and a string comparison mistake refuses every such sheet.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A sheet with A, A.1 … A.12, B, B.1.
cases.steps: 1. Upload with `excel_type=multistage`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200, 13 rows under A in order A.1..A.12, then B.
cases.oracle: `valid.data` order and labels.

cases.title: Uploading a BOQ sheet writes free-text master data
cases.why: The upload — before the buyer even saves — inserts new units, free-text products ("Quality: Free Text" variants), a "BOQ" free-text category and a "Free Text" delivery location into the company. Repeated uploads must reuse them, not multiply them.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A QA company; a sheet with a new unit "QA_Platform_Unit_{{stamp}}" and two new item names.
cases.steps: 1. Upload the sheet twice. 2. Read units, products (free_text) and categories.
cases.expected: One new unit, two free-text products (product_type free_text), at most one "BOQ" free-text category and one "Free Text" location, each created once across both uploads.
cases.oracle: Master-data counts before/after.

cases.title: There is no server-side row limit on a BOQ sheet
cases.why: The 500-line cap is applied only when the event is published in the dashboard; the upload itself accepts any size. Large uploads must still parse in time.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A valid 1,000-row BOQ sheet.
cases.steps: 1. Upload with `excel_type=multistage`. 2. Time it.
cases.expected: 200 with 1,000 rows (no 4xx for size), within the request timeout. The dashboard later blocks publish with "Maximum no of product addition reached" (UI-XDBOQ-012) unless the company's `allowed_maximum_line_items.boq` is ≥ 1000.
cases.oracle: Row count; response time.

cases.section: The BOQ stage — POST /trade/template_input and PATCH /trade/:id
cases.title: A stage is BOQ only when it has tabs AND a BOQ template
cases.why: Everything BOQ-specific (edit after close, tab summaries, BOQ bid upload, BOQ award) keys off `TradeRequest#boq?`. A BOQ template sent without tabs is an ordinary stage; tabs on a non-BOQ template are not BOQ.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A draft QA BOQ project.
cases.steps: 1. Add a stage with the BOQ template and `tabs: []`. 2. Add one with an ordinary template and tabs. 3. Add one with the BOQ template and tabs. 4. Read each with `GET /trade/<id>` (`trade_config.is_boq_event`).
cases.expected: Only stage 3 reports `is_boq_event` true; creating it also sets the project's `boq_based_rfx` true and turns off last-purchase-price savings in its config.
cases.oracle: `is_boq_event` per stage; project config.

cases.section: The BOQ stage — POST /trade/template_input and PATCH /trade/:id
cases.title: Tabs and sections are not validated when the stage is saved
cases.why: `add_ranges_to_sections` trusts the client: a section without `section_no` or `range` crashes (500), an inverted range is silently left out of the parent's roll-up, and child detection is a substring match ("A" also claims "AA"). Totals per section then disagree with the sheet.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A draft QA BOQ project; the BOQ stage body with (a) a section missing `section_no`, (b) a section range [5,3], (c) sections "A" and "AA".
cases.steps: 1. `POST /trade/template_input` with each variant. 2. Read `GET /v1/trade/<id>/quote_summary/<any>`.
cases.expected: Should: 422 for (a) and (b). Today: (a) HTTP 500; (b) 200 with the bad section ignored in the parent range; (c) "AA" counted as a child of "A".
cases.oracle: Status; tab summary ranges.

cases.section: The BOQ stage — POST /trade/template_input and PATCH /trade/:id
cases.title: A CLOSED BOQ stage can still be edited; an ordinary closed stage cannot
cases.why: BOQ stages are deliberately editable after close (quantity corrections before award). The exception must stay limited to BOQ and RFP stages.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A closed QA BOQ RFQ stage with no bids, and a closed ordinary RFQ stage.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/<boq stage>` with edited widgets/rows. 2. Same on the ordinary stage.
cases.expected: BOQ: 200 and the sheet is rebuilt. Ordinary: 422 code 4 "Request not found" (closed is not an editable status, and the bid-end check also refuses).
cases.oracle: Status per stage; BOQ stage rows after edit.

cases.section: Reading BOQ lines and tab pages
cases.title: A search filter that is a JSON list is refused, not a crash
cases.why: With no `filters`, `search` is parsed as the whole filter object; a list then crashes the line filter.
cases.setup: The sandbox.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_line_items?search=[1]`.
cases.expected: Should: 200 (ignored) or 4xx. Today (likely defect): HTTP 500 (`[1]['category_ids']`). Never 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Reading BOQ lines and tab pages
cases.title: Malformed filters AND search together crash the line read
cases.why: `create_filter_params` rescues the parse error but leaves `@filters` nil; the crash moves to the filter step.
cases.setup: The sandbox.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_line_items?filters=notjson&search=notjson`.
cases.expected: Should: 200 or 4xx. Today (likely defect): HTTP 500 (`nil['category_ids']`). Never 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: The bid-sheet upload is open to the buyer team and only returns parsed rows
cases.why: The policy is "can view the event", not "is a vendor": buyers use it for surrogate bids. It must never create or submit a bid on its own, and it does not check the bidding window.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A live QA BOQ stage; the QA buyer; a filled bid template.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, `POST /v1/trade/<stage>/upload_bid_excel` with the sheet. 2. Read the stage's bids. 3. Repeat after the stage closes.
cases.expected: Both uploads 200 with `{inline_components, global}` per tab row; no bid row is created by either; a Report row records each upload.
cases.oracle: Bid count unchanged; Report rows.

cases.title: Missing tab sheets are skipped silently; a missing "Global Fields" sheet is refused
cases.why: A vendor who deletes a tab from the workbook gets a "successful" upload with that tab's prices missing — and only finds out at submit.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A live QA BOQ stage with tabs "Civil" and "Electrical"; a workbook without "Electrical", and one without "Global Fields".
cases.steps: 1. Upload each workbook (QA vendor or buyer).
cases.expected: Workbook 1: 200 with only Civil rows (should: refuse or warn). Workbook 2: HTTP 422, code 794 "Invalid excel file uploaded".
cases.oracle: Rows per tab; error code.

cases.title: Non-numeric and negative rates pass the upload and are only caught at bid create
cases.why: The upload returns rates as text; validation happens only when the bid products are saved. The vendor must see the price error there, mapped to the right BOQ line.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A live QA BOQ stage with a price floor/cap; a workbook with "abc", -5 and a rate above the cap on three lines.
cases.steps: 1. Upload. 2. As the QA vendor, create the bid products from the parsed rows (`POST /v1/bids/<bid>/create_bid_products`).
cases.expected: Step 1: 200, values echoed as text. Step 2: refused, e.g. code 38 "Price cannot be more than the allowed price" / 41 "Price cannot be less than the allowed price" / 578 "Validation Failed" — never a 5xx and never a stored negative rate.
cases.oracle: Error code per row; bid products unchanged.

cases.title: An empty tab sheet or a missing file crashes the bid upload
cases.why: `sheet.last_row` is nil on an empty sheet and the loop compares `3 <= nil`; a missing `excel_data` reaches `Base64.decode64(nil)` after the Report row is saved. Both are 500s.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A live QA BOQ stage; a workbook whose "Civil" sheet is empty.
cases.steps: 1. Upload it. 2. Upload with no `excel_data`.
cases.expected: Should: 422 (794 or 2). Today (likely defect): HTTP 500 in both; step 2 leaves a Report row.
cases.oracle: Status; Report rows.

cases.title: During the cost-breakdown window every bid-sheet upload crashes
cases.why: `parse_components_for_bid` calls `component.slice!` outside the block that defines `component` (NameError) whenever the stage is in its cost-breakdown time — BOQ or not, no vendor can upload a sheet then.
cases.setup: A live QA stage with a cost-breakdown window currently open (`in_cost_break_down_time?` true).
cases.steps: 1. Upload a valid bid sheet.
cases.expected: Should: 200 with only price and serial number kept. Today (likely defect): HTTP 500 NameError.
cases.oracle: Status.

cases.title: A partial BOQ bid is allowed once the vendor passed the technical stage
cases.why: For ordinary events a vendor must quote every line not regretted in the technical stage (748). BOQ skips that line-by-line check — vendors may quote part of a BOQ. Lot-closed sheets still demand all prices on the first bid (372).
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A live QA BOQ project: RFP stage (QA vendor responded) + BOQ RFQ stage (line-item closing); same for an ordinary project.
cases.steps: 1. As the QA vendor, submit a bid pricing 2 of 5 BOQ lines (`PATCH /v1/bids/<bid>` status active). 2. Same on the ordinary project. 3. Repeat 1 on a BOQ stage with lot closing.
cases.expected: 1: accepted. 2: HTTP 422, code 748 "Please enter bid for all line items that are not regretted in technical stage.". 3: HTTP 422, code 372 "Please quote prices for all the products.".
cases.oracle: Status/code per step.

cases.title: On BOQ, technical participation is checked per company, not per line
cases.why: BOQ technical stages are evaluated vendor-wise; a vendor who answered the technical stage may quote any BOQ line. A vendor who did not must be refused.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A live QA BOQ project with RFP + RFQ; QA vendor A responded to the RFP, QA vendor B did not.
cases.steps: 1. As A, create bid products on any line. 2. As B, the same.
cases.expected: A: accepted. B: HTTP 422, code 737 "You cannot quote for this item because you didn't participate in the technical stage".
cases.oracle: Codes.

cases.title: Tab and section totals are plain sums; unquoted and rate-only lines count as 0
cases.why: Totals are what buyers compare first. They are prefix sums of each line's total over ALL the stage's rows in order; no rounding is applied, so a 3-decimal rate can show a long float.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A BOQ stage: tab 1 = A.1 (2 Nos), A.2 (rate only), B.1 (3 Nos); QA vendor quotes A.1 at 10.333 and leaves B.1 empty.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /v1/trade/<stage>/quote_summary/<bid>`.
cases.expected: Section A total 20.666 (no rounding), section B 0, tab total 20.666; A.2 contributes 0. Only top-level sections are listed. Displayed values in the dashboard are rounded to the widget precision.
cases.oracle: tabs_summary values.

cases.title: The BOQ loading factor counts lines the vendor "bid" on in any status
cases.why: BOQ ranks add a loading for lines a vendor did not quote (best price × quantity). The lookup of "did quote" has no status filter, so a draft or withdrawn bid row hides the gap and the vendor ranks better than it should.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A BOQ stage, two QA vendors; vendor A quotes all lines; vendor B quotes all but B.1 in its active bid, but has an old draft row on B.1.
cases.steps: 1. Read rank/scores for both (QCS or event score).
cases.expected: Should: B loaded with best(B.1) × qty(B.1). Today (suspected): no loading for B.
cases.oracle: Event score per vendor.

cases.title: Item-wise BOQ awarding only through the Excel award with the company setting
cases.why: `should_treat_as_boq_item_awarding?` is false only when the award is made with Excel AND `is_awarding_items_wise_in_boq_allowed` is on. Any other combination is whole-BOQ.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A closed QA BOQ project; setting `is_awarding_items_wise_in_boq_allowed` toggled on a QA company.
cases.steps: 1. Setting ON: `POST /proposal {is_awarding_with_excel:true}`, then upload an awarding sheet that splits lines between two vendors. 2. Setting OFF: same. 3. Setting ON, manual (no Excel) partial award.
cases.expected: Only 1 keeps the split. 2 and 3 award each vendor every line it quoted.
cases.oracle: Proposal line ids per vendor.

cases.title: Awarding a vendor with no valid BOQ bid crashes instead of saying so
cases.why: On BOQ the vendor's lines come from its bid; with no bid the list is nil and `nil - [...]` raises before the friendly 826 check.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A closed QA BOQ project; QA vendor B invited but did not bid.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /proposal/<id>/add_response` naming vendor B.
cases.expected: Should: HTTP 422, code 826 "Awarded vendor is not present in the latest stage" (or 715). Today (likely defect): HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status/code.

cases.title: With "close on partial BOQ", the first selected bid closes the whole stage
cases.why: `trade_request_close_on_partial_boq` closes the BOQ commercial stage as soon as one bid is selected — other vendors can no longer be awarded or negotiated on that stage. Without it, the stage closes only when every line is closed.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. Two QA companies or a toggle of `trade_request_close_on_partial_boq`; a BOQ stage with two vendors' bids.
cases.steps: 1. Award vendor A and complete approval (bid selection). 2. Read the stage status.
cases.expected: Setting ON: stage closed with closed_at now after the first selection. OFF: stays open until all lines closed.
cases.oracle: Stage status/closed_at.

cases.title: The Excel award round trip produces the same award as the sheet
cases.why: Awarding with Excel is the only route to item-wise BOQ awards; the quantities in the uploaded sheet must be exactly what the proposal records.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON; `allow_sheet_awarding` ON; `is_awarding_items_wise_in_boq_allowed` ON. A closed QA BOQ project with two vendors' bids.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /reports/download_awarding_sheet/<project>`; poll `GET /reports/status/<report>`. 2. Fill awarded quantities. 3. `POST /proposal {is_awarding_with_excel:true}`. 4. `POST /reports/upload_awarding_sheet/<proposal> {s3_url}`. 5. Read the proposal.
cases.expected: Each vendor's awarded lines and quantities equal the sheet; quantities above the requested quantity are refused with code 561 "You cannot select bid with more than requested quantity.".
cases.oracle: Proposal vs sheet.

cases.title: An empty BOQ flag is read as "BOQ on"
cases.why: The controller reads the flag with Ruby truthiness (`params.dig(...) || false`), so an empty string counts as on. A client that clears the field gets a BOQ create, not an ordinary one.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` OFF. Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /event_groups` with `config.boq_based_rfx: ""` and no line items. 2. Read the error.
