cases.expected: Refused with code 101 (the BOQ gate), because "" is truthy. With a proper boolean the answer would be code 2 "Insufficient parameters" (no line items). Either refusal is acceptable; never a 2xx or 5xx.
cases.oracle: 4xx; nothing created.

cases.title: A BOQ flag sent as an empty object is read as "BOQ on"
cases.why: Same coercion with a wrong type; `{}` is truthy. Wrong-type flags must not produce half-BOQ projects.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` OFF. Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /event_groups` with `config.boq_based_rfx: {}` and no line items.
cases.expected: Refused with code 101; with boolean coercion it would be code 2. Never 2xx/5xx.
cases.oracle: 4xx; nothing created.

cases.title: A BOQ project with line items "" starts empty
cases.why: "" is blank and must behave like "no lines yet" rather than reaching the typed service with a string.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /event_groups` with the BOQ flag on and `line_items: ""`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with no line items.
cases.oracle: Reply shows no line-item ids.

cases.title: Two BOQ lines are numbered 1 and 2 in request order
cases.why: Vendors' quotes are mapped back by line order; a reorder silently swaps prices between items.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /event_groups` with the BOQ flag on and the same product twice (10 Nos, then 20 Nos).
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with two ids; serial numbers 1 (10 Nos) and 2 (20 Nos). The same product twice is allowed.
cases.oracle: Reply: two ids; the serialized lines show serials 1 and 2 matching the quantities.

cases.title: A zero-quantity BOQ line is kept as "rate only"
cases.why: BOQs carry rate-only items (provisional sums). Refusing or dropping them breaks the sheet; they must be stored and then contribute nothing to tab totals or loading.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /event_groups` with the BOQ flag on and one line with quantity 0.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; the stored line is marked rate-only (`is_rate_only` true).
cases.oracle: Reply: the line's meta shows is_rate_only true, quantity 0.

cases.title: The server does not cap an ordinary event at 65 lines
cases.why: The 65-line limit for ordinary events exists only in the dashboard. Anything that bypasses the dashboard (API clients, integrations, PR conversion) can go past it — the team should know which side owns the rule.
cases.setup: Buyer session; the dashboard's default non-BOQ limit (65).
cases.steps: 1. `POST /event_groups` (no BOQ flag) with 66 catalog lines.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with 66 ids — no server-side limit. A 4xx would mean a server cap was introduced. Never 5xx.
cases.oracle: Reply ids count 66.

cases.title: A BOQ flag stored as an empty object stays a non-boolean
cases.why: The raw config is stored as sent. `{}` then reads as BOQ in Ruby and in the dashboard, but any strict `== true` consumer reads it as not BOQ — the project behaves differently per screen.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /event_groups` with `config.boq_based_rfx: {}` and no line items. 2. `GET /event_groups/<new>`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200, project created with `boq_based_rfx: {}`. Should: coerce to true/false or refuse. Never 5xx.
cases.oracle: GET shows config.boq_based_rfx as `{}`.

cases.title: The BOQ gate answers before the permission check
cases.why: In a workspace without BOQ, a user who may not create events at all gets 101 (BOQ not allowed) rather than 455 (not authorised) — the message points support at the wrong problem.
cases.setup: A QA user without trade `create_record` permission, in a workspace with `boq_in_erfx_allowed` OFF. Needs a second user, so no twin.
cases.steps: 1. As that user, `POST /event_groups` with the BOQ flag on. 2. Repeat without the flag but with one line.
cases.expected: BOQ request: 422 code 101. Ordinary request: 422 code 455 "You are not authorized to perform this action" (Pundit). Both refuse; record the order.
cases.oracle: Codes 101 then 455; nothing created.

cases.section: Re-uploading the BOQ sheet — PATCH /event_groups line items on a BOQ project
cases.title: Replacing a one-line BOQ with a different single line is not mistaken for a deletion
cases.why: The "cannot delete the only line" guard counts request rows against ACTIVE lines. On a draft project the lines are draft (active count 0); on a live one the new line is inserted first (active count 2) — either way the replacement passes. A regression in that order would block every one-line re-upload.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A draft QA BOQ project with exactly one line L1.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/<uuid>` with one NEW row.
cases.expected: 200; one new id; L1 in_active. Not 711.
cases.oracle: get_line_items count 1 with the new id.

cases.section: Changing a live event's BOQ nature and the line-item deletion guards — PATCH /event_groups
cases.title: Deleting a line item that doesn't exist is answered "cannot delete" instead of "not found"
cases.why: The guard compares counts, not identity. A wrong id on a one-line event gets the same 711 as a real deletion, which hides client bugs and is the root of API-XDBOQ-029–031.
cases.setup: The sandbox (one active line).
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` `{"line_items":[{"uuid":"WrongUuid1=","status":"deleted"}]}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 711 "You cannot delete this line item from the project"; nothing changes.
cases.oracle: 422 + 711; line count 1.

cases.section: Changing a live event's BOQ nature and the line-item deletion guards — PATCH /event_groups
cases.title: An empty row in a PATCH is refused, not a crash
cases.why: A spreadsheet with trailing blank lines produces empty rows.
cases.setup: The sandbox.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` `{"line_items":[{}]}`.
cases.expected: Should: 4xx; nothing changes. Today: HTTP 500. Never 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Linking the BOQ purchase request — PATCH /event_groups with purchase_request_id
cases.title: An undecodable purchase request uuid is silently ignored
cases.why: The client asked for a link and got a 200 without one; the PR's in-progress quantity is then wrong with no error anywhere.
cases.setup: The sandbox.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` `{"purchase_request_uuid":"WrongUuid1="}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200, nothing changes (the id decodes to nil and the PR check is skipped). Should: 422. Never 5xx.
cases.oracle: 200; event unchanged.

cases.section: Linking the BOQ purchase request — PATCH /event_groups with purchase_request_id
cases.title: A non-numeric raw purchase request id is refused
cases.why: Raw ids skip uuid decoding; they must still be validated and scoped.
cases.setup: The sandbox.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` `{"purchase_request_id":"abc"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 "You are not allowed to perform this action".

cases.section: Linking the BOQ purchase request — PATCH /event_groups with purchase_request_id
cases.title: A material purchase request cannot be linked as the BOQ PR
cases.why: Linking a material PR to a BOQ project would double-count its quantities.
cases.setup: The sandbox; {{prId}} is the workspace's first PR (a REAL record; this request writes nothing to it).
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` `{"purchase_request_uuid":"{{prId}}"}`.
cases.expected: Material/service PR: 422 code 101. A BOQ PR: 200 and no mapping (the sandbox is not a BOQ project). Never 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status; no PR mapping on the sandbox.

cases.section: Linking the BOQ purchase request — PATCH /event_groups with purchase_request_id
cases.title: A BOQ PR with no items crashes the link after the event was already saved
cases.why: The worker is enqueued with `purchase_request_items.first.id`; with no items that raises outside the rescued errors, after the event update committed — the buyer sees an error but the change stuck.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A QA BOQ PR whose only item was removed; a live QA BOQ project.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/<uuid>` `{"title":"QA_Platform_DBOQ_040_{{stamp}}","status":"active","purchase_request_uuid":"<pr>"}`.
cases.expected: Should: 4xx before any write. Today (likely defect): 500 after the update was saved.
cases.oracle: Status; event read shows the new title anyway.

cases.section: Linking the BOQ purchase request — PATCH /event_groups with purchase_request_id
cases.title: A BOQ PR sent with a draft or ordinary event is accepted but never mapped
cases.why: Mapping happens only for an ACTIVE BOQ project. On a draft the link is silently skipped and must be re-sent on publish — the dashboard does so; an API client may not.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A QA BOQ PR; a DRAFT QA BOQ project.
cases.steps: 1. PATCH the draft with the PR. 2. Publish without the PR. 3. Read PR mappings.
cases.expected: Step 1 200 with no mapping; after step 2 still no mapping. Publish with the PR → mapping created.
cases.oracle: Mapping rows per step.

cases.section: BOQ templates and the sample sheet — GET /templates
cases.title: The stored identifier "t-boq" is not a valid filter
cases.why: Clients that mix the stored and the public identifier must get a clear refusal, not an empty list.
cases.setup: Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /templates?type_identifier=t-boq`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 "Insufficient parameters".
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: BOQ templates and the sample sheet — GET /templates
cases.title: "BOQ" in capitals is not a valid filter
cases.why: The membership test is case-sensitive; guards the exact-match contract.
cases.setup: Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /templates?type_identifier=BOQ`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 "Insufficient parameters".
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: BOQ templates and the sample sheet — GET /templates
cases.title: Asking for BOQ templates while excluding BOQ gives empty lists
cases.why: Contradictory filters must give a well-formed, empty answer.
cases.setup: Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /templates?type_identifier=boq&exclude_type_identifiers=["boq"]` (URL-encoded JSON).
cases.expected: HTTP 200, `default: []`, `saved: []`.
cases.oracle: Both arrays empty.

cases.section: BOQ templates and the sample sheet — GET /templates
cases.title: Excluding "t-boq" is refused
cases.why: Same identifier contract on the exclude list.
cases.setup: Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /templates?type_identifier=boq&exclude_type_identifiers=["t-boq"]`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 "Insufficient parameters".
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: BOQ templates and the sample sheet — GET /templates
cases.title: An exclude list sent as an object is refused
cases.why: `Array({"boq":1})` becomes `[["boq",1]]`; wrong shapes must be refused, not half-applied.
cases.setup: Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /templates?type_identifier=boq&exclude_type_identifiers={"boq":1}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 "Insufficient parameters".
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: BOQ templates and the sample sheet — GET /templates
cases.title: "Hide default templates" removes Procol's stock BOQ templates from the picker
cases.why: Companies that only want their own BOQ formats turn on `hide_default_templates`; stock templates must then never appear (and a company with no own BOQ template is left with an empty picker).
cases.setup: A QA company with `hide_default_templates` ON and one own BOQ template. Config change, so no twin.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /templates?type_identifier=boq`. 2. Turn the setting off and repeat.
cases.expected: With the setting on, `default` lists only the company's own default-type BOQ templates (no company_id-nil ones); off, Procol's stock BOQ templates appear too.
cases.oracle: company_id of each `default` entry.

cases.section: BOQ templates and the sample sheet — GET /templates
cases.title: Downloading the BOQ sample sheet of a template that doesn't exist is refused
cases.why: "Download Template" in the BOQ upload modal must fail cleanly for a deleted template.
cases.setup: Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /templates/excel_template/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==?sheet_type=boq_items_sheet`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 "Request not found".
cases.oracle: 422 + code 4.

cases.section: BOQ templates and the sample sheet — GET /templates
cases.title: Downloading the BOQ sample sheet with an undecodable template id is refused
cases.why: Undecodable ids must not reach the Excel builder.
cases.setup: Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /templates/excel_template/WrongUuid1=?sheet_type=boq_items_sheet`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 "Request not found".
cases.oracle: 422 + code 4.

cases.section: BOQ templates and the sample sheet — GET /templates
cases.title: Deactivating the last BOQ template switches BOQ off for the whole company
cases.why: `boq_in_erfx_allowed?` reads template existence live, so deleting one template silently removes the BOQ menu for every buyer and refuses BOQ creates, while existing BOQ projects keep working.
cases.setup: A QA company with `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON and exactly one BOQ template; one existing QA BOQ project.
cases.steps: 1. Deactivate the template (`DELETE /templates/<id>` from the dashboard). 2. Re-read the dashboard config. 3. Try a BOQ create. 4. Open the existing BOQ project and its quote summary.
cases.expected: Config `boq_in_erfx_allowed` false; create refused 101; the existing project still reads and its stage remains a BOQ stage (the stage keeps its own template type).
cases.oracle: Config flag; create code; existing project still shows tabs.

cases.title: Uploading a BOQ sheet against a template that doesn't exist is refused
cases.why: A stale template id must not reach the parser (or create an upload log for nothing).
cases.setup: Buyer session. (Not on the default allowlist; refused at the template lookup, before the upload log.)
cases.steps: 1. `POST /templates/product_sheet_params` with a tiny base64 `excel_data` and `template_uuid` `Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 "Request not found".
cases.oracle: 422 + code 4.

cases.title: A sheet without a "Section" column is refused
cases.why: Without sections there is no hierarchy; the parser must say so.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. The sample sheet with the "Section" column removed.
cases.steps: 1. Upload with `excel_type=multistage`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 15, "Please ensure that Sections are Present".
cases.oracle: Exact message.

cases.title: A missing required buyer column is named with its section
cases.why: Buyers delete columns they think unused; the message must name the column and the section.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. The sample sheet with the quantity column removed.
cases.steps: 1. Upload with `excel_type=multistage`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 15, "<column> is missing at section <A.1>, Please add the required component". Formula, dropdown, attachment and delivery-location columns are not required.
cases.oracle: Message names the column and section.

cases.title: A sheet with no header row is "BOQ sheet not filled"
cases.why: An empty sample uploaded by mistake must get a plain message.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A workbook whose sheets have no row 2.
cases.steps: 1. Upload with `excel_type=multistage`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 15, "Please ensure that the BOQ sheet is filled in". Empty tabs among filled ones are dropped silently.
cases.oracle: Exact message; tab count of a mixed workbook.

cases.title: Rows without a unit become section notes, not priced lines
cases.why: BOQs carry headings and description rows; those must not become lines vendors have to price.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A sheet where A.1 has Unit "Nos" and A.2 has no unit (description only).
cases.steps: 1. Upload with `excel_type=multistage`.
cases.expected: 200; A.1 is a line; A.2 becomes a note/split point of the section (no product row); `in_valid` is null for BOQ.
cases.oracle: `valid.data` rows.

cases.section: The BOQ stage — POST /trade/template_input and PATCH /trade/:id
cases.title: Editing a closed BOQ stage that has bids only changes columns, caps and savings
cases.why: Rows must not be rebuilt under existing bids; only widget, savings and ceiling/floor changes go through, and those are still validated.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A closed QA BOQ stage with one QA vendor bid.
cases.steps: 1. PATCH with a changed row quantity. 2. PATCH with a price cap below an existing bid.
cases.expected: Step 1: rows unchanged. Step 2: HTTP 422, code 15 with a message such as "Price Cap should be greater than or equal to …".
cases.oracle: Stage rows; error text.

cases.section: The BOQ stage — POST /trade/template_input and PATCH /trade/:id
cases.title: A BOQ stage that has started cannot be rescheduled
cases.why: Editing after close is allowed, rescheduling is not — the two must not be confused.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A closed QA BOQ stage.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/<id>` with new `bid_start_time` and `bid_end_time` and no configurations.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 258 "You cannot re-schedule this event!".
cases.oracle: 422 + 258; schedule unchanged.

cases.section: The BOQ stage — POST /trade/template_input and PATCH /trade/:id
cases.title: Serial numbers on BOQ lines come from the Section column, not a running number
cases.why: The grid prints `line_item_no` (e.g. A.1.2); the serial-number column is hidden for tabbed stages. If the section label is lost the vendor cannot tell which BOQ item they are pricing.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A BOQ stage built from a sheet with A.1, A.2, B.1.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /trade/<id>`; read each row's product `line_item_no` and the widgets list.
cases.expected: Rows carry line_item_no A.1, A.2, B.1 in `order`; no serial_number widget is shown.
cases.oracle: Row labels and widget list.

cases.section: Reading BOQ lines and tab pages
cases.title: Reading the line items of a project that doesn't exist is refused
cases.why: The line read is the oracle for every upload/replace case; it must fail cleanly on a bad id.
cases.setup: Buyer session.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /event_groups/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/get_line_items`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 533 "Project does not exist.".

cases.section: Reading BOQ lines and tab pages
cases.title: A negative page on the line read falls back to page 1
cases.why: Big BOQ projects are paged; a bad page must not error.
cases.setup: The sandbox (one line).
cases.steps: 1. `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_line_items?page=-3`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with the one line, total_pages 1, count 1. (When `hide_line_items_from_project_details_vendor_side` is ON the reply is `{}` for everyone, buyer included — that check runs before authorize.)
cases.oracle: count 1.

cases.section: Reading BOQ lines and tab pages
cases.title: The BOQ tab summary of an ordinary stage is refused
cases.why: The tab-total endpoint is BOQ-only and must refuse ordinary stages instead of computing nonsense.
cases.setup: The sandbox stage {{tradeId}} (ordinary RFQ, no tabs). (Not on the default allowlist; a read.)
cases.steps: 1. `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/quote_summary/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 "You are not allowed to perform this action".

cases.section: Reading BOQ lines and tab pages
cases.title: A line-range filter with a text bound is refused, not a crash
cases.why: The `range` filter is the BOQ tab window; client values reach Ruby's Range constructor unchecked.
cases.setup: The sandbox stage.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /trade/{{tradeId}}?filters={"range":{"from":"a","to":1}}`.
cases.expected: 200 (range ignored) or 4xx; never 5xx (`"a"..1` raises ArgumentError on the sheet path).
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Reading BOQ lines and tab pages
cases.title: Project sheet paging: tab -1 jumps to the last tab, page 0 returns the tail of the whole BOQ
cases.why: Ruby negative indexes: `tabs[-1]` is the last tab and an array slice with a negative start wraps to the end. The master QCS then shows rows from another tab under the selected one.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A live QA BOQ project with 3 tabs of 20 lines and one vendor bid.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /sheets/details?event_group_uuid=<uuid>&view_type=summary_view&tab=-1&page=1`. 2. `…&tab=0&page=0`. 3. `…&tab=0&page=99`.
cases.expected: Should: 4xx or tab/page clamped. Today: step 1 returns tab 3's rows; step 2 returns rows from the END of the project (wrong rows, no error); step 3 returns an empty page.
cases.oracle: Line numbers in each reply vs the tab's range.

cases.section: Reading BOQ lines and tab pages
cases.title: Quote paging on a BOQ stage: an unknown tab falls back to the first tab
cases.why: A stale tab index after a re-upload with fewer tabs silently shows tab 1, which the vendor may mistake for the tab they chose.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A BOQ stage with 2 tabs; the QA vendor's bid.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /v1/trade/<stage>/quote_details/<bid>?tab=7&page=1`. 2. `…?tab=1&page=0`.
cases.expected: Step 1: tab 1's rows. Step 2: rows before tab 2's start (the end of tab 1) or empty — no error.
cases.oracle: Row orders vs tab ranges.

cases.section: Reading BOQ lines and tab pages
cases.title: BOQ project defaults force lot-based evaluation, even for the string "false"
cases.why: The flag is read with Ruby truthiness, so `"false"` still gives BOQ defaults.
cases.setup: Buyer with trade create permission. (GET /v1/trade/new_request_config is not on the default allowlist; a read.)
cases.steps: 1. `GET /v1/trade/new_request_config?filters={"for_boq_based_project":"false"}`. 2. Same without the filter.
cases.expected: Both 200; step 1's defaults have `rfp_evaluation_mode` "lot_based" whatever the workspace default is.
cases.oracle: Compare the two replies' default evaluation mode.

cases.title: Uploading a bid sheet for a stage that doesn't exist is refused before anything is stored
cases.why: The upload stores the file (S3) and a Report row before parsing; a stale stage id must be refused first.
cases.setup: Buyer session. (Not on the default allowlist; refused at the active-stage lookup.)
cases.steps: 1. `POST /v1/trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/upload_bid_excel` `{"excel_data":"<tiny base64>","excel_type":"bid"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 "Request not found"; no Report row, no file stored.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 4.

cases.title: Split tabs are merged only when tab collation is on
cases.why: Long BOQs are split into "Civil-1", "Civil-2"; with `tab_collation_enabled` the summary must show one "Civil" total, without it two.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A BOQ stage with tabs "Civil-1", "Civil-2"; collation on in one stage, off in another.
cases.steps: 1. Read both quote summaries.
cases.expected: Collation on: one parent "Civil" with the summed total. Off: two tabs. A tab with no name crashes today (nil `.split`) — should be refused at stage save.
cases.oracle: Tab names and totals.

cases.title: A tab range past the last line crashes the tab summary
cases.why: Ranges are saved unchecked (API-XDBOQ-068); a range ending beyond the row count makes the prefix lookup return nil and the subtraction raise.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A BOQ stage saved with 10 rows but a tab range [1, 12].
cases.steps: 1. `GET /v1/trade/<stage>/quote_summary/<any>`.
cases.expected: Should: refused at save time. Today: HTTP 500 on the summary.
cases.oracle: Status.

cases.title: BOQ reports keep "other charges" and skip the master QCS block
cases.why: The "remove other charges" setting deliberately does not apply to BOQ; the awarding report also omits the master QCS section for BOQ. Totals in BOQ reports therefore include other charges.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed` ON. A QA company with `remove_other_charges` ON; one awarded BOQ project and one ordinary.
cases.steps: 1. `GET /sheets/details` for both. 2. Download the awarding proposal report for both.
cases.expected: BOQ: other charges present; no master QCS block in the awarding report. Ordinary: other charges removed; master QCS present.
cases.oracle: Report contents.

journeys.title: Lots and currencies
journeys.goal: Group lines into lots that close and award on their own, and let vendors quote in their own currency with the buyer's exchange rates applied consistently to comparison, award and order.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: Who sees 'Split line items into lots' and when it is disabled
cases.why: The menu is the only entry to lots in the product; it must appear only where splitting is allowed.
cases.setup: Buyer on the RFQ page of a project event.
cases.steps: Open the RFQ's settings menu on: (a) multi-line RFQ, company switch is_lot_creation_enabled ON; (b) single-line RFQ; (c) switch OFF; (d) a lot RFQ (has a parent); (e) closed RFQ; (f) old version / project on hold; (g) service RFP grouping on.
cases.expected: Shown only for (a) and (e)-(f); disabled for (e) closed, (f) old version or on hold; hidden for (b), (c), (d), (g).
cases.oracle: Menu item presence/disabled state matches.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: 'Publish Lot' needs at least two lots that have items
cases.why: The two-lot rule exists only on this screen (the API accepts a single lot).
cases.setup: Drawer with all items in lot 1 (e.g. fresh smart lots on an event with no bids).
cases.steps: Click Publish Lot on lot 1.
cases.expected: Error toast 'Please assign line item to at least two lots'; no request sent.
cases.oracle: No create_new_lot call in the network log.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: Items in a published lot cannot be selected or moved
cases.why: Moving items out of a live lot RFQ would desynchronise it.
cases.setup: Drawer with lot 1 published, lot 2 draft.
cases.steps: Try to tick a row in lot 1; open 'Move items to' from lot 2.
cases.expected: Lot 1 rows have disabled checkboxes and the lot shows a 'Published' tag; the move list does not offer lot 1; the dropdown is disabled until a row of the current lot is ticked.
cases.oracle: Checkbox/option state.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: Server refusals of a rate change always show 'Failed to update currency rates'
cases.why: DEFECT. The request helper rejects with the raw response TEXT, but the handler reads `err.status` and `err.response.data.message` — both undefined. Every refusal (877 bids placed, 878 bad rate, 879 not multi-currency, 2 base currency) shows the generic 'Failed to update currency rates' and the editor stays open, so the buyer retries a request that can never succeed.
cases.setup: Editing rates on a round where the server will refuse (e.g. a bid arrives after the page loaded).
cases.steps: Save.
cases.expected: The server's message is shown (e.g. 'Exchange rates cannot be updated after bids have been placed.') and the editor closes on 422. Today: generic toast, editor open.
cases.oracle: Toast text equals the API message.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: On a base-currency event the editor offers the base currency and saving always fails
cases.why: DEFECT. The editor lists every currency except the COMPANY's default (from local storage), not except the EVENT's base. On an event whose base currency is USD the editor lists USD and saving sends it; the server refuses a change to the base (code 2), and the screen shows the generic failure.
cases.setup: Company default INR; event created with Base Currency = USD (factor 83); published, no bids.
cases.steps: Click the pencil, change USD's rate, Save.
cases.expected: The base currency is not editable (or the factor can be corrected). Today the pencil shows, Save sends `[{"USD": ...}]` and fails with 'Failed to update currency rates'.
cases.oracle: Network: PATCH answered 422 code 2.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: 'Generate Smart Lot' is disabled once smart lots are in place or a lot is published
cases.why: Regenerating over a published lot is refused by the server (815); the button should not invite it.
cases.setup: Lots drawer open.
cases.steps: Look at the button: (a) plan in smart mode; (b) manual plan, nothing published; (c) a lot published.
cases.expected: (a) disabled; (b) enabled; (c) disabled. The button only shows when lot_state.is_smart_lots_enabled (always true from the server today).
cases.oracle: Button state.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: An empty lot cannot be published
cases.why: Publishing a lot with nothing in it creates an empty RFQ.
cases.setup: Drawer with an empty lot.
cases.steps: Look at the empty lot.
cases.expected: Text 'This Lot can’t be published until it contains at least one item.'; Publish Lot disabled.
cases.oracle: Button disabled.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: A move the server refuses puts the items back
cases.why: The drawer updates optimistically; after a refusal it must not show a plan the server never saved.
cases.setup: Drawer; make the save fail (e.g. offline, or a plan the server refuses with 842).
cases.steps: Move an item to another lot.
cases.expected: Error toast; the item returns to its original lot (state restored when the thunk returns 'error').
cases.oracle: Drawer matches GET get_lots after the failure.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: Lot header totals add up
cases.why: Buyers decide the split from the 'Total L1 Amount' and vendor count in each lot header.
cases.setup: Drawer on an event in evaluation with bids.
cases.steps: Compare each lot header with its rows.
cases.expected: Total L1 Amount = sum of the rows' L1 values; vendor count = number of vendors in the sheet. On multi-currency events L1 values are base-currency amounts with the RFQ's default symbol.
cases.oracle: Header equals the row sum.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: 'Manage Lots' re-opens the drawer and re-reads the lots
cases.why: After closing the drawer the buyer needs a way back; re-opening must show the saved plan (and note: every open is a get_lots call that SAVES smart lots on a fresh event).
cases.setup: Drawer opened once from the settings menu, then closed.
cases.steps: Click the floating 'Manage Lots' button.
cases.expected: Drawer opens with the plan saved on the server.
cases.oracle: Network: one get_lots per open; plan matches.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: When the exchange-rate pencil appears and what the field accepts
cases.why: Rates may only change before bids; the field must stop obvious mistakes.
cases.setup: Published multi-currency RFQ, event details panel.
cases.steps: Check the pencil with 0 bids and with 1 bid; click it and type '-5', 'abc', '1,000', '83.5'.
cases.expected: Pencil only when there is at least one non-default currency and bid count is 0. The field accepts digits and one dot only: '-', letters and ',' are not typed; '83.5' is.
cases.oracle: Typed value.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: The exchange-rate editor refuses empty or zero rates before saving
cases.why: Client-side checks mirror the server's 878.
cases.setup: Editing rates.
cases.steps: Clear a rate, or enter 0 or '.', then Save; separately, let a bid arrive while editing, then Save.
cases.expected: 'All exchange rates must be positive numbers' (editor stays open); if bids now exist: 'Cannot edit rates after bids have been placed' and the editor closes. No request in either case.
cases.oracle: No PATCH sent.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: Currency picker: each ticked currency needs a rate
cases.why: A ticked currency without a rate would create a currency with no conversion (and see API-XSTG-110 for zero).
cases.setup: Event creation → Edit Currencies → Multiple Currency.
cases.steps: Tick USD with no rate → OK; tick nothing → OK; enter 0.000000001 (below the minimum).
cases.expected: 'Please enter price in INR' (company default code); 'Please select atleast one currency.'; the number field clamps to 0.00000001.
cases.oracle: Modal stays open with the error; no currency table saved.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: Currency picker: base-currency mode requires a conversion factor
cases.why: Changing the event's base currency without a factor makes every amount wrong by the exchange rate.
cases.setup: Edit Currencies → Base Currency.
cases.steps: Pick USD without a factor → OK; then factor 0.001 (below min 0.01).
cases.expected: 'Please enter price in INR'; the factor field clamps to 0.01. With a factor the saved table holds USD as base with rate_in_base = the factor.
cases.oracle: Event payload currency_configuration (network).

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: 'Add Bid Currencies' is offered only when allowed
cases.why: Adding currencies after publishing is a configuration change that must respect the company's switch.
cases.setup: Event details panel.
cases.steps: Check with: no currencies yet + edit allowed + enable_multi_currency_flow ON + event base = company default; then change each condition.
cases.expected: Shown only when all four hold; otherwise the 'Multiple bidding currenices are not added' text or nothing.
cases.oracle: Button presence.

cases.section: Screens — lots drawer, currency picker, exchange-rate editor
cases.title: The 'Show Bidding / Default Currencies' switch appears only where it means something
cases.why: On a single-currency or BOQ event, or before any bid, the switch has nothing to switch.
cases.setup: RFQ settings menu.
cases.steps: Check on: multi-currency with bids; multi-currency without bids; single currency; BOQ event.
cases.expected: Shown only for multi-currency, non-BOQ, with bids; the label flips between 'Show Bidding Currencies' and 'Show Default Currencies'.
cases.oracle: Menu item presence and label.

cases.title: Lots of this event cannot be read through another event's RFQ
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING (data exposure + cross-event write). get_lots authorises the event in the URL but then loads whatever RFQ id is in the query, with no check that it belongs to that event or even to the same company, and the service builds and SAVES smart lots on the RFQ's own event. A buyer who can see any one event can read another event's L1 amounts and vendor names, and seed its lot plan.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer. {{pricingTradeUuid}} is the JOURNEY's own RFQ stage (bid window over, one submitted bid from the QA vendor, an award proposal created and submitted); {{tradeProductUuid}} is that stage's quoted line. The two events are different. Run it last: if the defect is present the journey event gets draft smart lots written onto it.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_lots?trade_request_uuid={{pricingTradeUuid}}` (sandbox event, journey RFQ).
cases.expected: Should be refused (422 code 2) like reset_to_smart_lots, which scopes the round by event and company. Today the lookup is `TradeRequest.where(id:, rfx_mode: :rfq).last` (no event_group_id, no company_id) and the journey's lots come back with HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: Status 4xx. If 200: the reply's lots list the JOURNEY's line item and vendor; GET get_lots on the journey event now shows mode smart_lots.

cases.title: An invited vendor cannot read the buyer's lot sheet
cases.why: SECURITY. get_lots and the two lot writes only ask the event policy for show?, which is true for an invited vendor (they can view the stage). The reply carries every bidder's name, the L1 amount per line and each vendor's technical score label — the competitive picture a vendor must never see.
cases.setup: Event in evaluation with two vendors' bids; session of one invited vendor (client_admin_dashboard app allows event_groups#get_lots). No twin: cases only run as the buyer.
cases.steps: As the vendor: `GET /event_groups/<event>/get_lots?trade_request_uuid=<RFQ>`.
cases.expected: Refused (HTTP 422 code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action' or 101). Today EventGroupPolicy#show? passes for anyone who can view a stage and the full sheet (vendor_data per line) is returned.
cases.oracle: Vendor gets 4xx; no vendor names / L1 values in any vendor-visible reply.

cases.section: Saving a draft lot plan — PATCH /event_groups/:id/save_draft_lots
cases.title: Lots of this event cannot be filled with another event's line items
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING (cross-event corruption). The RFQ is inferred from the FIRST item id and never compared with the event in the URL. A plan saved on event A with event B's items passes the count check against B, is saved on A, and the reply shows B's lots. The buyer's real lot plan on A is overwritten with ids A does not own.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer. {{pricingTradeUuid}} is the JOURNEY's own RFQ stage (bid window over, one submitted bid from the QA vendor, an award proposal created and submitted); {{tradeProductUuid}} is that stage's quoted line. Run it last: if the guard is missing the sandbox's lot plan is overwritten and the journey event may get draft smart lots.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/save_draft_lots` with `{"lots": {"1": {"lot_title": "QA_Platform_lot_{{stamp}}", "old_trade_product_uuids": ["{{tradeProductUuid}}"]}}}`.
cases.expected: Should be refused (422 code 2: the item does not belong to this event). Today: HTTP 200, the sandbox's lot_config lot 1 now lists the journey's line, and the reply is the journey event's lots.
cases.oracle: 4xx; GET get_lots on the sandbox unchanged.

cases.section: Saving a draft lot plan — PATCH /event_groups/:id/save_draft_lots
cases.title: An invited vendor or view-only user cannot rearrange the buyer's lots
cases.why: SECURITY. save_draft_lots and reset_to_smart_lots write the event's lot plan but only check show?. A vendor who can view the RFQ, or a buyer user with read-only trade permission, can overwrite the plan the buyer is about to publish.
cases.setup: Event in evaluation with a draft lot plan. Session of the invited QA vendor (or a read-only buyer). No twin: cases run as the buyer only.
cases.steps: As that user: `PATCH /event_groups/<id>/save_draft_lots` with a valid plan for the event's items.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action' (update?/create_record should be required). Today show? passes and the plan is saved.
cases.oracle: Lot plan unchanged after the call.

cases.section: Going back to smart lots — PATCH /event_groups/:id/reset_to_smart_lots
cases.title: Smart lots cannot be regenerated after a lot is published
cases.why: Regenerating would reshuffle items that are already in a live lot RFQ.
cases.setup: Event with at least one published (active) lot. No twin: the sandbox is still bidding and cannot be split.
cases.steps: `PATCH .../reset_to_smart_lots?trade_request_uuid=<parent RFQ>`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 815 'Smart Lot generation failed, a lot has already been published'; plan unchanged.
cases.oracle: 815; GET get_lots unchanged.

cases.title: Lots cannot be published while vendors are still bidding
cases.why: Splitting mid-bidding would move vendors' half-finished quotes into new rounds. The help centre promises the option only during evaluation.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with `{"trade_request_uuid": "{{tradeId}}", "lots": {"1": {...}}}` (the drawer's Publish Lot body).
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 740 'RFQ event cannot be converted to lots as it is still live.'; no lot RFQ is created.
cases.oracle: 740; GET get_lots shows no active lot; the RFQ is still live.

cases.title: The same item in two new lots in one request is not refused
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING. The overlap check only compares new items with items already in active/in-progress lots, and the new list is uniq'd. Two lots in one request that share an item both get it: two lot RFQs, the item awarded twice.
cases.setup: Closed RFQ with items A, B; no lots published. Buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with lot 1 = [A, B] and lot 2 = [B].
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 739 'A lot for one or more items already exists.'. Today both lots are created (HTTP 200).
cases.oracle: After the call each item appears in exactly one active lot (GET get_lots).

cases.title: A lot title with an apostrophe breaks publishing
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING (SQL injection). The lot entry, title included, is written with a raw SQL string `jsonb_set(lot_config, '{<lot_no>}', '<json>'::jsonb)` — no quoting. A title like `Supplier's lot` ends the string literal: the publish fails with a database error, and a crafted title can run SQL. Titles are typed by buyers.
cases.setup: Closed RFQ with a saved draft plan; buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with lot 1 `lot_title` = `QA_Platform_O'Brien lot`.
cases.expected: Should publish with the title stored verbatim (parameterised SQL). Today PG syntax error → HTTP 500 raised from the service constructor (update_event_group_lot_config('in_progress')), before the transaction.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; lot title read back exactly.

cases.title: A lot number that is not a number goes into the SQL path unescaped
cases.why: Same raw SQL: the lot key from the request is pasted into the jsonb path `'{<lot_no>}'`. Keys like `1}', '{}'::jsonb)--` change the statement.
cases.setup: Closed RFQ; buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with lot key `x}'` .
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2 (lot numbers are positive integers). Today a DB error → HTTP 500, or worse.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; lot_config keys are numeric strings only.

cases.section: Living with lots — withdraw, award, extend, hold
cases.title: Withdrawing one lot is blocked only by that lot's own award
cases.why: On a lot event each lot is awarded separately. A submitted award for lot 1 must not freeze lot 2, and lot 2's withdrawal must not touch lot 1's award. The 841 check is per lot.
cases.setup: Lots 1 and 2 published; lot 1 has a selected proposal (meta_data lot_no '1'); lot 2 has none.
cases.steps: Withdraw lot 2's RFQ (`PATCH /trade/<lot 2 RFQ>` status withdrawn), then try lot 1's.
cases.expected: Lot 2: allowed (HTTP 200, lot 2 returns to draft). Lot 1: HTTP 422 code 841 'Cannot withdraw the event as proposals are already submitted.'.
cases.oracle: Lot 1 still active with its proposal; lot 2 draft with stage_ids [].

cases.title: Anyone signed in can move another company's staggered closing times
cases.why: SECURITY (missing authorisation). staggered_time has no `authorize` call and no company filter — it looks up any active trade by id. Any logged-in user (a vendor in the auction, a buyer of another company) can push out the end time of each line, and with it the auction and evaluation schedule. reopen_line_items, next to it, does both checks.
cases.setup: A live staggered line-item auction of company A; session of a vendor invited to it, or a buyer of company B.
cases.steps: As that user: `PATCH /trade/<A's auction>/staggered_time` with a later end time for one line.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 455 (or 4). Today HTTP 200 and the line's end time (and the auction end, if later) moves.
cases.oracle: Trade schedules unchanged after the call.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: Exchange rates cannot change once a bid is in
cases.why: A vendor's quote was converted at the rate published when they bid; changing it afterwards silently re-ranks them.
cases.setup: {{pricingTradeUuid}} is the JOURNEY's own RFQ stage (bid window over, one submitted bid from the QA vendor, an award proposal created and submitted); {{tradeProductUuid}} is that stage's quoted line.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{pricingTradeUuid}}/currency_exchange_rates` with `{"currency_rates": [{"QA_Platform_XYZ": 1}]}`.
cases.expected: Refused, nothing written: HTTP 422 code 877 'Exchange rates cannot be updated after bids have been placed.' on a multi-currency round; 879 on a single-currency one (the journey's case); 4 if the stage is no longer active.
cases.oracle: 4xx; rates unchanged.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: After a rate update the comparison sheet in bidding currency crashes
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING (high impact). The rate is stored as `BigDecimal(rate)`, which Rails writes into the JSON column as TEXT ("95.5"); the spec itself compares with `.to_f`. Several readers divide or multiply by rate_in_base without converting: the master QCS value in the vendor's currency (`value.to_f / currency.rate_in_base`) and the report helper (`value.to_f * currency.rate_in_base`) raise TypeError. So: buyer corrects a rate before bidding opens → a USD vendor bids → the comparison sheet / report in bidding currency fails.
cases.setup: Published multi-currency RFQ (INR base, USD allowed), no bids. Buyer + a vendor bidding in USD.
cases.steps: 1) `PATCH /v1/trade/<id>/currency_exchange_rates` `[{"USD": 95.5}]`. 2) GET /trade/<id>: note rate_in_base's JSON type. 3) Vendor bids in USD. 4) Open the master QCS with 'Show Bidding Currencies'; download the QCS report.
cases.expected: rate_in_base stays a number and every screen works. Today step 2 shows "95.5" (a string) and step 4 fails with HTTP 500 (String can't be coerced into Float).
cases.oracle: Step 2 JSON type is number; step 4 no 5xx.

cases.section: Currency and lots elsewhere — create, update, read, bid, compare, award
cases.title: Bids in different currencies are ranked on the converted value
cases.why: The QCS must compare like with like: 1.2 USD at 83 = 99.6 INR beats 100 INR.
cases.setup: Multi-currency RFQ (INR base, USD rate 83); vendor A bids 1.2 USD/unit, vendor B 100 INR/unit.
cases.steps: Buyer opens the QCS (default view), then toggles 'Show Bidding Currencies'.
cases.expected: Default view: A 99.6 (₹), B 100 (₹), A is L1. Bidding view: A $1.2, B ₹100, ranks unchanged; rounding uses the currency's adjusted precision.
cases.oracle: QCS values and ranks.

cases.title: Asking for lots without naming the RFQ round is refused
cases.why: The Manage Lots drawer always passes the RFQ round; a call without it must say 'missing parameter', not guess a round or build lots for nothing.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: Read the lots of the sandbox event without the round: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_lots`.
cases.expected: A clean refusal; nothing is computed or saved. HTTP 422, error code 2 'Insufficient parameters' — the event passes the latest-version and visibility checks, then the RFQ lookup with no id comes back empty.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2; a later read of the event shows no lots.

cases.title: Asking for lots of the technical (RFP) round is refused
cases.why: Only an RFQ can be split into lots; pointing the lot panel at the technical round must not build a lot sheet from technical answers.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer. This needs an RFP+RFQ run: {{rfpTradeId}} is the sandbox's technical round.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_lots?trade_request_uuid={{rfpTradeId}}`.
cases.expected: Refused, nothing saved. HTTP 422, error code 2 'Insufficient parameters' — the round lookup is filtered to rfx_mode rfq.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.title: Lots of an event that does not exist are refused, not a crash
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING. The controller asks the event whether it is the latest version BEFORE checking that the event was found, so a stale or mistyped link crashes the endpoint instead of answering 'not found'. Any monitoring that counts 500s will page on harmless typos.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer. The event id is the well-formed but non-existent `Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` (id 999999999).
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/get_lots?trade_request_uuid={{tradeId}}`.
cases.expected: Should be a typed refusal (422 code 2 or 4). Today `nil.latest?` raises NoMethodError → HTTP 500, because the latest? check (line 895) runs before the blank check (line 896).
cases.oracle: Status < 500; ideally 422 code 2.

cases.title: Opening the lots of a live RFQ works and builds smart lots
cases.why: The buyer can open Manage Lots any time (only publishing is blocked while bidding). The first read must build a sensible starting split, not crash on an event with no bids yet.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer. The event has never had lots. Run it last: this read SAVES the generated lots on the sandbox.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_lots?trade_request_uuid={{tradeId}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with `lot_state` {is_smart_lots_enabled: true, mode: smart_lots} and lots 1-5. With no bids and no technical round the single item lands in lot 1 described 'Lot Summary: This lot includes items marked as Regret and TNA.'; lots 2-5 are empty. Each lot is status draft, every line shows L1 '-' and 'Not Placed'.
cases.oracle: 200; event_groups.lot_config now holds five draft smart lots (read it back with the same GET: identical answer).

cases.title: Opening the lots must not hide the event's master QCS report
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING. Because get_lots SAVES draft smart lots, the event now has a lot_config. The report list then takes the 'lot event' branch and only lists reports for ACTIVE lots — so merely opening Manage Lots (without publishing anything) makes the single 'QCS-Purchase' and 'Approval Note' entries disappear from the downloads list.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer. Run it after the previous case (it relies on the draft smart lots that read saved). Run it last.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_all_attachments` after get_lots.
cases.expected: Must not 500. Expected: the report list is the same as before the lots were opened (QCS-Purchase present once the event qualifies). Today the lot branch is taken on `lot_config.present?` and every draft lot is skipped, so no master QCS entry is produced.
cases.oracle: No 5xx. Content oracle (manual): compare the report names before and after opening Manage Lots on an event in evaluation; 'QCS-Purchase' must not vanish.

cases.title: A buyer from another company cannot read this event's lots
cases.why: Basic tenant isolation for the lot sheet.
cases.setup: Session of a buyer in a different company. No twin: needs a second company's user.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/<this event>/get_lots?trade_request_uuid=<its RFQ>`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action' — show? requires a visible stage and the other company's user has none. (The event lookup itself is not company-scoped, so the refusal relies entirely on the policy.)
cases.oracle: 455; nothing saved on the event.

cases.title: Smart lots group items by technical outcome
cases.why: Smart lots are the product's suggestion of how to split; a wrong rule puts a single-source item into a competitive lot and the award goes wrong.
cases.setup: RFP+RFQ event in evaluation, three vendors, technical scores entered: item A only one vendor technically accepted; item B all three accepted; item C every vendor TNA or regretted; item D a mix; item E not yet evaluated.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/<id>/reset_to_smart_lots?trade_request_uuid=<RFQ>` then `GET .../get_lots?...`.
cases.expected: Lots in this order, each draft: OEM (single valid vendor) = A; all technically accepted = B; Regret and TNA = C; mixed = D; evaluation pending = E; empty categories are appended after the filled ones. Descriptions match the category.
cases.oracle: Each lot's old_trade_product_uuids and description match the rule in classify_into_lots.

cases.section: Saving a draft lot plan — PATCH /event_groups/:id/save_draft_lots
cases.title: Saving a lot plan with no lots is refused
cases.why: The 'Move items to' dropdown always sends the whole plan; an empty body must not wipe or corrupt the saved plan.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/save_draft_lots` with body `{}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 2 'Insufficient parameters'; the saved plan is unchanged.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2; GET get_lots unchanged.

cases.section: Saving a draft lot plan — PATCH /event_groups/:id/save_draft_lots
cases.title: A lot with no line items is refused
cases.why: The server works out which RFQ the plan belongs to from the first line item it finds; a plan with no items has no RFQ and must be refused.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH .../save_draft_lots` with `{"lots": {"1": {"lot_title": "QA_Platform_lot_{{stamp}}", "description": ""}}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (first_tp_id is blank).
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Saving a draft lot plan — PATCH /event_groups/:id/save_draft_lots
cases.title: A lot naming a line item that does not exist is refused
cases.why: A stale drawer (item deleted in another tab) sends an id that no longer exists; the server must refuse instead of saving a plan with a ghost line.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH .../save_draft_lots` with `{"lots": {"1": {"lot_title": "QA_Platform_lot_{{stamp}}", "old_trade_product_uuids": ["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="]}}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 2 'Insufficient parameters' — the line's RFQ cannot be found.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Saving a draft lot plan — PATCH /event_groups/:id/save_draft_lots
cases.title: Lots sent as a list instead of a map are refused, not a crash
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING. The controller calls `.values` on whatever 'lots' is; a JSON array (the natural shape for a list of lots) has no `.values` and the endpoint crashes.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH .../save_draft_lots` with `{"lots": [{"lot_title": "QA_Platform_lot_{{stamp}}", "old_trade_product_uuids": ["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="]}]}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. Today Array#values → NoMethodError → HTTP 500 (before any write).
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Saving a draft lot plan — PATCH /event_groups/:id/save_draft_lots
cases.title: Saving lots on an event that does not exist is refused, not a crash
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING: the same guard-order slip as get_lots — latest? is asked of a missing event.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/save_draft_lots` with a one-lot body naming a non-existent item.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. Today `nil.latest?` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Saving a draft lot plan — PATCH /event_groups/:id/save_draft_lots
cases.title: A second lot without an item list is refused, not a crash
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING. Only the FIRST item id is checked up front; every lot's list is then counted with `ids.count {}`. A lot whose list is null (a lot the screen emptied) crashes the save.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer. {{pricingTradeUuid}} is the JOURNEY's own RFQ stage (bid window over, one submitted bid from the QA vendor, an award proposal created and submitted); {{tradeProductUuid}} is that stage's quoted line. No sandbox line-item placeholder exists, so lot 1 names the journey's quoted line to get past the first checks (this also exercises the missing event check of the next case).
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/save_draft_lots` with lot 1 = [{{tradeProductUuid}}] and lot 2 = `{"old_trade_product_ids": null}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 (code 2, or 842 'Unable to save lots'). Today, when the journey's stage is still active, validate_lot_config calls `nil.count` → HTTP 500 (before save!, so nothing is written). If the stage is no longer active the request stops earlier with code 2.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Saving a draft lot plan — PATCH /event_groups/:id/save_draft_lots
cases.title: The same line item in two lots is refused
cases.why: An item counted twice would be published in two lot RFQs and awarded twice.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer. {{pricingTradeUuid}} is the JOURNEY's own RFQ stage (bid window over, one submitted bid from the QA vendor, an award proposal created and submitted); {{tradeProductUuid}} is that stage's quoted line. Uses the journey's quoted line (no sandbox line placeholder exists).
cases.steps: `PATCH .../save_draft_lots` with lot 1 = [{{tradeProductUuid}}] and lot 2 = [{{tradeProductUuid}}].
cases.expected: Refused, nothing saved: HTTP 422 code 842 'Unable to save lots' — the duplicated id is counted twice, so 2 ≠ 1 line on the RFQ. (Code 2 if the journey stage is no longer active.)
cases.oracle: 422; lot plan unchanged.

cases.section: Saving a draft lot plan — PATCH /event_groups/:id/save_draft_lots
cases.title: A published lot is not changed by a draft save
cases.why: Once a lot is published its items are in a live lot RFQ; a later draft save must not move them. The code silently skips active lots — the buyer gets HTTP 200 and may believe the move happened.
cases.setup: Event with lot 1 published (active) and lot 2 draft. Buyer session.
cases.steps: `PATCH .../save_draft_lots` moving an item from lot 1 to lot 2.
cases.expected: Lot 1 is unchanged (skipped). Because lot 1's items are still counted, the moved id now appears twice and the save is refused 842 'Unable to save lots'; if the body leaves lot 1 out entirely the item silently stays in lot 1 with HTTP 200. Expected: an explicit refusal naming the published lot.
cases.oracle: GET get_lots: lot 1 still active with its items.

cases.section: Going back to smart lots — PATCH /event_groups/:id/reset_to_smart_lots
cases.title: Resetting without naming the RFQ is refused
cases.why: The 'Generate Smart Lot' button always sends the round; a call without it must not touch the plan.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/reset_to_smart_lots` (no trade_request_uuid).
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 2 'Insufficient parameters' — this is the very first check.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Going back to smart lots — PATCH /event_groups/:id/reset_to_smart_lots
cases.title: Resetting lots of an event that does not exist is refused, not a crash
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING: both ids are present so the blank check passes; the event lookup is empty and latest? is asked of nil one line before the nil check.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/reset_to_smart_lots?trade_request_uuid={{tradeId}}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. Today HTTP 500 (nil.latest?).
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Going back to smart lots — PATCH /event_groups/:id/reset_to_smart_lots
cases.title: Resetting with another event's RFQ is refused
cases.why: This endpoint scopes the RFQ to the event and the company — the correct pattern the other two lot reads/writes lack. It must stay that way.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer. {{pricingTradeUuid}} is the JOURNEY's own RFQ stage (bid window over, one submitted bid from the QA vendor, an award proposal created and submitted); {{tradeProductUuid}} is that stage's quoted line.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/reset_to_smart_lots?trade_request_uuid={{pricingTradeUuid}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 2 'Insufficient parameters'; neither event's lots change.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Going back to smart lots — PATCH /event_groups/:id/reset_to_smart_lots
cases.title: A vendor cannot reset the buyer's lot plan
cases.why: Same show?-only authorisation as save_draft_lots: a viewer can wipe the buyer's manual plan.
cases.setup: Event in evaluation with a manual draft plan; invited vendor session.
cases.steps: As the vendor: `PATCH .../reset_to_smart_lots?trade_request_uuid=<RFQ>`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 455. Today allowed (show?).
cases.oracle: Manual plan still in place.

cases.title: Publishing lots without naming the RFQ is refused
cases.why: Without the RFQ there is nothing to split.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with only `lots`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 95 'Trade Request not found'.

cases.title: Publishing lots for an RFQ that does not exist is refused
cases.why: Stale or forged ids must not reach the split service.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with trade_request_uuid `Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 95 'Trade Request not found'.

cases.title: A technical round cannot be split into lots
cases.why: Only an RFQ (rfx_mode 1) is split; a technical round must be refused, not converted.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer. RFP+RFQ run: {{rfpTradeId}} is the technical round.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with trade_request_uuid {{rfpTradeId}}.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 95 'Trade Request not found'.

cases.title: Splitting is refused once an award is submitted — with a misleading message
cases.why: Once an award proposal for the whole RFQ is submitted, splitting would orphan it. The refusal is right, but the message talks about an auction that does not exist, so buyers raise support tickets.
cases.setup: {{pricingTradeUuid}} is the JOURNEY's own RFQ stage (bid window over, one submitted bid from the QA vendor, an award proposal created and submitted); {{tradeProductUuid}} is that stage's quoted line. Company setting rfx_project_enabled is ON. No twin: if the guard failed the journey's RFQ would really be split (bids moved, round closed), which other cases still use.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with trade_request_uuid {{pricingTradeUuid}} and one lot.
cases.expected: Refused, nothing created: HTTP 422 code 769 'You cannot edit rfq once the auction is created.' — is_rfq_changes_restricted? is true because a requested/selected proposal with no lot exists. Expected wording: 'an award proposal is already submitted'.
cases.oracle: 769; the RFQ is not converted (trade_config.read_only_mode false).

cases.title: Publishing with no lots field is refused, not a crash
cases.why: `params["lots"].to_unsafe_h` runs on nil once the timing checks pass.
cases.setup: An RFQ whose bid window has closed, no proposal, no lots. Buyer session. No twin: the sandbox stops at 740 first.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with only trade_request_uuid.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. Today NoMethodError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: A lot with no items is published
cases.why: The integration spec admits it: 'Currently, the validation for this is missing from BE'. An empty lot RFQ is created and the vendors are notified about a round with nothing to quote.
cases.setup: Closed RFQ; buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with lot 1 = [] (the spec's own payload).
cases.expected: Should be 422. Today the request is accepted (spec test is xit).
cases.oracle: No active lot with zero line items exists.

cases.title: Lots published before the lot panel was ever opened are lost from the event
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING. `jsonb_set(NULL, ...)` returns NULL, so on an event whose lot_config is still empty the lot entries are never written: the lot RFQs are created, bids moved, the parent closed and marked converted — but the event shows no lots. The drawer always reads lots first, so only API/integration clients hit it.
cases.setup: Closed RFQ whose event has never had get_lots/save_draft_lots called (lot_config NULL).
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` straight away with two lots.
cases.expected: Either refuse (code 2) or initialise lot_config. Today HTTP 200 and GET /event_groups/<id> has no lots; the parent RFQ is read-only.
cases.oracle: After the call get_lots lists the published lots as active.

cases.title: Turning lot creation off still lets the API split an RFQ
cases.why: The company switch is_lot_creation_enabled (master config 'Allow users to create RFQ lots', default off) only hides the menu; create_new_lot never reads it. A company that has deliberately disabled lots can still have RFQs split by any integration or old browser tab.
cases.setup: Company setting is_lot_creation_enabled is OFF (the default). Closed RFQ; buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with two valid lots.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 (e.g. 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'). Today the split succeeds.
cases.oracle: No lot RFQs when the setting is off.

cases.title: Items already in a published lot cannot be published again
cases.why: Publishing lot 2 with an item of the already-published lot 1 would put the item in two live RFQs.
cases.setup: Lot 1 published with item A; buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with lot 2 = [A].
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 739 'A lot for one or more items already exists.' (asserted by the integration spec).

cases.title: A member without event-creation permission cannot publish lots
cases.why: Publishing creates new RFQs and notifies vendors; only buyers who may create events should do it.
cases.setup: Member user without the trade create permission; closed RFQ.
cases.steps: As that member: `POST /trade/create_new_lot`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 'You are not authorized to perform this action' (spec 'unauthorized_access'). Note the company check (101) only runs AFTER the timing checks, so another company's buyer learns whether the RFQ is live (740) before being refused.
cases.oracle: 455/101; nothing created.

cases.title: Publishing lots one at a time keeps the remaining items available
cases.why: The drawer publishes ONE lot per click. The first publish closes the parent RFQ's schedule and marks it converted; the second lot must still be publishable from the same parent.
cases.setup: Closed RFQ with a draft plan of lots 1 and 2; buyer.
cases.steps: Publish lot 1, then lot 2 (two create_new_lot calls).
cases.expected: Both succeed; lot 2's round timing copies lot 1 (sibling lot RFQ); each item is in exactly one active lot.
cases.oracle: GET get_lots: lots 1 and 2 active; parent trade_config.read_only_mode true.

cases.title: After a split the vendors are told and asked to review their charges
cases.why: Vendors' global charges were quoted for the whole RFQ; each lot needs its own. The product creates a bid- justification request per moved bid and notifies vendors ('Bid Adjustment Pending').
cases.setup: Closed RFQ with the QA vendor's bid; buyer publishes two lots.
cases.steps: Publish; as the vendor list live events; as the buyer open the lot RFQ.
cases.expected: Vendor sees 'Bid Adjustment Pending' on each lot; one bid-justification request per moved bid; the parent RFQ is read-only (read_only_mode true via is_converted_to_lots).
cases.oracle: Additional requests of type bid_justification exist for each lot RFQ bid; lot split email/push to the QA vendor only.

cases.title: A vendor whose bid totals zero gets 'NaN' charges after a split
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING. Global amount charges are re-split by each lot's share of the vendor's total (new_total / old_total). A vendor who quoted 0 (free sample, or all lines regretted) divides 0 by 0 and their charges become 'NaN' in every lot, breaking totals and the QCS.
cases.setup: Closed RFQ with a global amount charge; one vendor quoted 0 on every line but entered a freight charge.
cases.steps: Publish two lots.
cases.expected: Charges split without NaN (e.g. evenly or kept on the first lot). Today other_details[charge] = 'NaN'.
cases.oracle: Lot RFQ bid other_details contain only numbers.

cases.section: Living with lots — withdraw, award, extend, hold
cases.title: Withdrawing the parent RFQ of a lot event checks every award
cases.why: The parent is not in any lot's stage list, so its lot number is blank and the whole-event proposal check applies.
cases.setup: Lot event; lot 1 has a selected proposal.
cases.steps: Withdraw the parent RFQ.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 841.
cases.oracle: Parent and lots unchanged.

cases.section: Living with lots — withdraw, award, extend, hold
cases.title: Withdrawing a lot's last round returns the lot to draft and frees the parent
cases.why: After a lot is withdrawn its items must be splittable again; when no lot is active the parent must be editable again.
cases.setup: Lot 1 (only lot) published, no proposals.
cases.steps: Withdraw lot 1's RFQ.
cases.expected: lot_config['1'] becomes status draft, stage_ids [], egli_ids removed; parent misc is_converted_to_lots false; a transaction failure answers 422 code 1106 'Failed to update lot configuration. Please try again.'.
cases.oracle: GET get_lots: lot 1 draft; parent trade_config.read_only_mode false.

cases.section: Living with lots — withdraw, award, extend, hold
cases.title: An award for lot 1 is shown against lot 1 whatever type the lot number was sent as
cases.why: The event screen matches proposals to lots by `meta_data['lot_no']` against lot_config keys, which are strings. A proposal created with lot_no 1 (a number, as some clients send) is stored as a number and never matched: the lot shows no proposal and the buyer starts a second one.
cases.setup: Lot 1 published and closed; buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /proposal` with `{"event_group_uuid": <id>, "lot_no": 1}` (number), then GET /event_groups/<id>.
cases.expected: lots['1'].proposal_uuid is the new proposal. Today it is null (only the string '1' matches). (Unknown lot numbers: see API-XAWD-094.)
cases.oracle: GET /event_groups/<id> lots['1'].proposal_uuid not null.

cases.title: Staggered times on a round that is not staggered are refused
cases.why: Per-line closing times only exist on staggered line-item auctions; on an RFQ the call must change nothing.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}/staggered_time` with `{"trade_products_time": {}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 4 'Request not found'.
cases.oracle: 4; schedules unchanged.

cases.title: An unknown line in the staggered times is refused, not a crash
cases.why: `trade_products_time[key]['start_time']` is read for every key sent; a key that is not a line of the round is nil.
cases.setup: Live staggered auction; buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/<id>/staggered_time` with `{"trade_products_time": {"999999999": {"start_time": <now>, "end_time": <now+600>}}}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 (code 507 or 80). Today NoMethodError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: A line's window can only be pushed later, and doing so past the end moves the auction
cases.why: Shortening a line's window after vendors planned for it is unfair; extending the last line beyond the round end must extend the round and the evaluation by the same amount.
cases.setup: Live staggered auction; buyer.
cases.steps: 1) Send an earlier end for a line. 2) Send an end 10 minutes after the round end.
cases.expected: 1) HTTP 422 code 507 'Invalid Time Input'. 2) HTTP 200; auction end = the new line end; evaluation end moved by the same delta; closed_at updated.
cases.oracle: Trade schedules read back.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: A round without multi-currency refuses exchange-rate changes
cases.why: Single-currency rounds have no rates; the call must say so instead of inventing a currency table.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer. The journey creates the RFQ with currency_configuration null, so the round has no currency table unless its pricing template carries one.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/currency_exchange_rates` with `{"currency_rates": [{"QA_Platform_XYZ": 83.5}]}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 879 'Multi-currency is not configured for this trade request.'; nothing written. (If the template does carry a currency table the unknown code gets code 2 instead — still refused.)
cases.oracle: 879; GET /trade/{{tradeId}} still has no currency_configuration.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: A rate written with a thousands separator is refused, not a crash
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING. The positive check uses `rate.to_f` ('1,000' → 1.0, passes) but the store uses `BigDecimal('1,000')`, which raises ArgumentError → 500. Same for '12abc'. A buyer pasting a rate from a spreadsheet crashes the save.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer. The 500 is only reachable on a multi-currency round with no bids where USD is an allowed, non-base currency; on the sandbox (no currency table) the call is refused 879 and this case passes vacuously.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/currency_exchange_rates` with `{"currency_rates": [{"USD": "1,000"}]}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 878 'Invalid exchange rate: rate_in_base must be a positive number.'. Today, on a multi-currency round: HTTP 500 at BigDecimal(rate.to_s), before anything is saved.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: Zero, negative and non-numeric rates are refused
cases.why: A zero rate makes a foreign bid free; a negative one makes it the cheapest by definition.
cases.setup: Published multi-currency RFQ (INR base, USD allowed), no bids. Buyer. No twin: the sandbox has no currency table.
cases.steps: Send USD = 0, then -5, then 'abc'.
cases.expected: Each: HTTP 422 code 878 'Invalid exchange rate: rate_in_base must be a positive number.'; USD rate unchanged (the spec covers 0).
cases.oracle: 878 x3; GET /trade/<id> USD rate_in_base unchanged.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: The base currency's own rate cannot be changed
cases.why: The base is 1 by definition; changing it would rescale every price.
cases.setup: Multi-currency RFQ, INR base, no bids.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (no message says why — the expected wording is 'base currency rate cannot be changed').
cases.oracle: 2; INR still 1.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: Absurd rates are accepted, and an infinite one is stored as empty
