cases.why: There is no upper bound: 830000000 instead of 83 is saved and every USD bid becomes the most expensive. A JSON 1e400 parses to Infinity, passes `> 0`, and BigDecimal('Infinity') serialises to null — the currency then has no rate at all.
cases.setup: Multi-currency RFQ, no bids.
cases.steps: Send USD = 830000000; then USD = 1e400.
cases.expected: Product decision for a sanity bound (e.g. ±50% of the auto-fetched rate). The infinite rate must be refused 878. Today: both HTTP 200; the second leaves rate_in_base null.
cases.oracle: GET /trade/<id> USD rate_in_base after each call.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: A vendor cannot change the buyer's exchange rates
cases.why: Rates decide who is L1; only the buying company may set them.
cases.setup: Multi-currency RFQ, no bids; invited vendor session.
cases.steps: As the vendor: `PATCH /v1/trade/<id>/currency_exchange_rates`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action' (update? requires the trade's company).
cases.oracle: 455; rates unchanged.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: A base-currency event's conversion factor can never be corrected after publishing
cases.why: In 'Base Currency' mode the event's only currency IS the base, with the conversion factor stored as its rate. The update endpoint refuses any change to the base code, so a mistyped factor cannot be fixed without recreating the event — and the screen offers the pencil anyway (see the UI case).
cases.setup: Event created with Edit Currencies → Base Currency = USD, factor 83; published; no bids.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/<id>/currency_exchange_rates` `[{"USD": 84}]`.
cases.expected: A way to correct the factor before bids. Today HTTP 422 code 2.
cases.oracle: Record the status.

cases.section: Currency and lots elsewhere — create, update, read, bid, compare, award
cases.title: The lot plan cannot be written through the event update
cases.why: The lot plan must change only through the lot endpoints (which check the items). A PATCH carrying lot_config must not mass-assign it.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` with only `{"lot_config": {"1": {"status": "active", ...}}}`.
cases.expected: No 5xx; the top-level lot_config is ignored (the update only reads status/title/description/attachments/config/line_items/terms). GET get_lots unchanged.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; no active lot appears.

cases.section: Currency and lots elsewhere — create, update, read, bid, compare, award
cases.title: A vendor's currency choice sent as text or a number is refused, not a crash
cases.why: DEFECT-IN-WAITING. On a multi-currency round the bid create does `T.let(params['currency_preference']['code'], String)`. A plain string preference (`"USD"`) makes `'USD'['code']` nil, and a numeric code fails the type check — both raise TypeError → 500. (An unknown code is covered by API-XBID-054.)
cases.setup: Multi-currency RFQ (INR, USD); invited QA vendor session. No twin: needs the vendor.
cases.steps: As the vendor: `POST /v1/bids` with `currency_preference: "USD"`, then with `{"code": 840}`.
cases.expected: Both HTTP 422 code 15 'Please choose a valid currency'. Today HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; no bid row.

cases.section: Currency and lots elsewhere — create, update, read, bid, compare, award
cases.title: A bid without a currency preference does not break the bid notification
cases.why: On a multi-currency round the notification and participant sheet convert each bid 'to the original currency' using the vendor's preference. A bid that was placed without one (surrogate, excel or email bid) gets a nil currency and `Utils.convert_currency(..., nil)` raises.
cases.setup: Multi-currency (multiple_currencies mode) RFQ; buyer places a surrogate bid for a vendor who never chose a currency.
cases.steps: Open the bid's quote details / trigger the bid notification.
cases.expected: Falls back to the base currency. Today NoMethodError → 500 / failed notification job.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; notification text shows the base currency.

cases.section: Currency and lots elsewhere — create, update, read, bid, compare, award
cases.title: The award value follows the 'show proposal value in base currency' setting
cases.why: Approvers sign off on the award total; it must be in the currency they expect, and a bad rate must not crash the award screen.
cases.setup: Company setting show_proposal_value_in_base_currency is ON; event created in Base Currency mode (USD, factor 83); an award proposal.
cases.steps: Open the proposal (`GET /proposal/<id>`); repeat with the setting OFF; repeat with the factor stored as 0 (accepted at creation, see API-XSTG-110).
cases.expected: ON: totals divided by 83 and shown in $; OFF: totals in the company currency. Factor 0: should fall back, today BigDecimal division by zero → HTTP 500 on the proposal.
cases.oracle: proposal_values.total_proposal_value currency symbol and amount; no 5xx.

cases.title: An unreadable round id in the lot request is refused
cases.why: A corrupted link (copied uuid with a character missing) decodes to nothing; the answer must be a refusal, not lots of some other round.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_lots?trade_request_uuid=WrongUuid1=` (decodes to nil).
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.title: Lots with an unreadable event id are refused, not a crash
cases.why: Same guard-order defect reached through the path id: a uuid that does not decode becomes nil and crashes the endpoint.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/WrongUuid1=/get_lots?trade_request_uuid={{tradeId}}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. Today 500 (nil.latest?).
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: Lots of a draft (never published) event are refused, not a crash
cases.why: A buyer can only split a published RFQ, but the endpoint looks the event up among active/withdrawn events only and then calls latest? on the empty result — a draft event id crashes the endpoint.
cases.setup: A QA_Platform_ draft event with an RFQ stage (not published). No twin: the run's sandbox is always published.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/<draft uuid>/get_lots?trade_request_uuid=<its RFQ>`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. Today 500 — `EventGroup.where(status: VALID_STATUSES_FOR_DASHBOARD)` excludes drafts and `nil.latest?` raises.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: Smart lots return five lots although the product promises at most four
cases.why: The help centre says items can be split into at most four lots, and EventGroup#get_default_lot_config builds exactly four — but smart lots always produce five (one per category, empty ones included) and nothing in save/publish caps the count.
cases.setup: Any RFQ; open lots for the first time.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/<id>/get_lots?trade_request_uuid=<RFQ>`; then save a draft with lot keys 1-9.
cases.expected: Product decision needed: either the limit is real (refuse lot 5+ with a 4xx) or the help text is wrong. Today: 5 smart lots, and 9 manual lots save with HTTP 200; get_default_lot_config is never called.
cases.oracle: Count of lots in the reply; record it against the documented limit.

cases.section: Saving a draft lot plan — PATCH /event_groups/:id/save_draft_lots
cases.title: Lots sent as plain text are refused, not a crash
cases.why: Same unguarded `.values`, reached with a string.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH .../save_draft_lots` with `{"lots": "QA_Platform_lot_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. Today String#values → NoMethodError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Saving a draft lot plan — PATCH /event_groups/:id/save_draft_lots
cases.title: Renaming a lot from the drawer is not saved
cases.why: The drawer's 'Move items to' sends each lot as `{old_trade_product_uuids, status, title}`, but the API reads `lot_title`. Lot names typed by the buyer (or carried from the publish payload) are lost on every move.
cases.setup: Lots drawer open; any move.
cases.steps: Inspect the save_draft_lots request the drawer sends; then GET get_lots.
cases.expected: The name the buyer sees is kept. Today `title` is ignored (only `lot_title` is read) and `status` is ignored too.
cases.oracle: get_lots lot_title after a move equals the title sent.

cases.section: Saving a draft lot plan — PATCH /event_groups/:id/save_draft_lots
cases.title: A lot whose item list is text is refused, not a crash
cases.why: `old_trade_product_ids: "12"` reaches `"12".count {}`, which needs an argument → ArgumentError → 500.
cases.setup: Event in evaluation; lot 1 valid, lot 2 has `old_trade_product_ids` as a string. No twin beyond the null variant above.
cases.steps: `PATCH .../save_draft_lots` with lot 2 `{"old_trade_product_ids": "12"}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. Today HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Saving a draft lot plan — PATCH /event_groups/:id/save_draft_lots
cases.title: Lot names and descriptions are stored safely
cases.why: Lot titles reach PO/NFA documents and emails; markup must be stripped and long text must not break the plan.
cases.setup: Event in evaluation; valid plan.
cases.steps: Save lot 1 with title `QA_Platform_bold O'Brien` + 5,000-character description.
cases.expected: Saved with tags stripped by the global input sanitiser; quotes kept; no length limit is enforced (record the stored length). No 5xx. NOTE: the same title later breaks publishing — see the apostrophe case in section 4.
cases.oracle: GET get_lots returns the stripped title.

cases.section: Going back to smart lots — PATCH /event_groups/:id/reset_to_smart_lots
cases.title: Resetting the sandbox's lots rebuilds smart lots
cases.why: The button's happy path: any manual draft plan is discarded and the smart suggestion rebuilt.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer. Run it last: it rewrites the sandbox's draft lot plan.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/reset_to_smart_lots?trade_request_uuid={{tradeId}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with lot_state.mode 'smart_lots' and the five smart lots (no lot is published, so 815 does not apply).
cases.oracle: 200; GET get_lots returns the same plan.

cases.title: A lot entry without its item list is refused, not a crash
cases.why: The controller tolerates a missing list (flatten of nil) but the split service maps it: `nil.map` crashes inside the service constructor, after nothing has been saved yet.
cases.setup: Closed RFQ, no proposals. Buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with `{"lots": {"1": {"lot_title": "QA_Platform_lot"}}}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. Today HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status < 500; no lot RFQ created.

cases.title: A single lot holding every item is accepted by the API
cases.why: The 'at least two lots' rule exists only in the drawer (toast); the API converts the whole RFQ into one lot, closing the parent for nothing. The spec marks the backend rule as pending.
cases.setup: Closed RFQ; buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with lot 1 = all items.
cases.expected: Product decision: refuse with 'Please assign line item to at least two lots' like the UI. Today HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: Record the status.

cases.title: A lot of a lot is refused, with a misleading message
cases.why: A lot RFQ (parent_id set) cannot be split again; the refusal reuses 739, which talks about items already in a lot.
cases.setup: A published lot RFQ, bid window over; buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/create_new_lot` with the lot RFQ's uuid.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 739 'A lot for one or more items already exists.'.
cases.oracle: 739; no grand-child RFQ.

cases.section: Living with lots — withdraw, award, extend, hold
cases.title: The technical round cannot be extended once lots exist
cases.why: Extending the technical round would also push the RFQ, which has already been split.
cases.setup: RFP+RFQ event with a published lot.
cases.steps: Extend the technical round's end time.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 818 'You cannot extend the RFQ time after lot creation'.
cases.oracle: 818; schedules unchanged.

cases.section: Living with lots — withdraw, award, extend, hold
cases.title: A PR item cannot be put on hold once its event is split into lots
cases.why: Holding a PR line would desynchronise the lot RFQs built from it.
cases.setup: PR item linked to an event with a published lot.
cases.steps: Put the PR item on hold.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 590 'This item cannot be put on hold because the event is split into lots.'.

cases.title: Staggered times on a round that does not exist are refused
cases.why: Bogus ids fail closed.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/staggered_time`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.title: Staggered times sent as text are refused, not a crash
cases.why: Comparing a text time with a stored number raises ArgumentError.
cases.setup: Live staggered auction; buyer.
cases.steps: Send start_time/end_time as strings for a real line.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 507 'Invalid Time Input'. Today valid_time_entries or the >= comparison may raise → 500.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: Empty staggered times are refused with a misleading message
cases.why: A blank payload answers 'Product not found', which sends buyers looking for a missing product.
cases.setup: Live staggered auction; buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/<id>/staggered_time` with `{}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 80 'Product not found' (should be code 2).

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: Exchange rates for a round that does not exist are refused
cases.why: Bogus ids fail closed.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/currency_exchange_rates`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: Exchange rates with an unreadable round id are refused
cases.why: Undecodable path ids become nil and must fail closed.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/WrongUuid1=/currency_exchange_rates`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, error code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: Rates sent as an object instead of a list are refused
cases.why: The screen sends a list of one-key objects; a plain object must be a typed refusal.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/currency_exchange_rates` with `{"currency_rates": {"USD": 83.5}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2 'Insufficient parameters' on a multi-currency round; 879 on the sandbox (no currency table). Nothing written.
cases.oracle: 4xx.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: A rate list holding bare currency codes is refused, not a crash
cases.why: `currency_rates.flat_map(&:to_unsafe_h)` assumes every element is an object; a list of strings crashes.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer. Reachable only on a multi-currency round with no bids; 879 on the sandbox.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/currency_exchange_rates` with `{"currency_rates": ["USD"]}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. Today NoMethodError (String#to_unsafe_h) → HTTP 500 on a multi-currency round.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: A currency that is not on the event is refused
cases.why: Adding a currency is a configuration change, not a rate update.
cases.setup: Multi-currency RFQ with INR+USD, no bids.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 2; no GBP added (spec covers).

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: Two entries for the same currency: the last one silently wins
cases.why: The list is merged into one map before validation, so `[{USD: -1}, {USD: 80}]` passes (the -1 disappears) and `[{USD: 80}, {USD: -1}]` fails. Order-dependent validation hides client bugs.
cases.setup: Multi-currency RFQ, no bids.
cases.steps: Send the two orders.
cases.expected: Both refused (duplicate currency). Today the first is accepted (USD = 80), the second 878.
cases.oracle: Record both statuses.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: Rates of a draft event cannot be changed here
cases.why: The endpoint only finds ACTIVE rounds; a draft round answers 'Request not found', which reads like a broken link. Buyers must use Edit Currencies on the draft instead.
cases.setup: Draft event with a multi-currency RFQ.
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/trade/<draft RFQ>/currency_exchange_rates`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 4 'Request not found' (expected wording: 'publish the event first' or allow drafts).

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: Draft bids do not block a rate change
cases.why: Only active/requested bids freeze the rates. A vendor halfway through a USD bid (draft) sees the rate move under them.
cases.setup: Multi-currency RFQ; the QA vendor has a DRAFT bid in USD.
cases.steps: Buyer updates the USD rate; vendor submits.
cases.expected: Record: today the update succeeds and the submitted bid converts at the new rate. Product decision whether drafts should block or the vendor be warned.
cases.oracle: Converted amount in the QCS uses the new rate.

cases.section: Exchange rates on a published round — PATCH /v1/trade/:id/currency_exchange_rates
cases.title: A failed save is reported as success
cases.why: `trade_request.save` (not save!) — its result is ignored, so a validation failure still answers 200 and the screen shows 'Exchange rates updated successfully'.
cases.setup: Multi-currency RFQ whose trade fails a model validation on save (e.g. data from an older template).
cases.steps: Update a rate.
cases.expected: 4xx when the save fails. Today HTTP 200 with nothing stored.
cases.oracle: GET /trade/<id> rate matches the reply.

cases.section: Currency and lots elsewhere — create, update, read, bid, compare, award
cases.title: A currency on a draft line item is accepted and ignored
cases.why: Integrations send a currency per line (from the PR). The event has no per-line currency: it must be accepted without error and must not become a second currency for that line.
cases.setup: Buyer session; catalog product and quality.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups` with the working draft body plus `"currency": {"code": "USD"}` on the line.
cases.expected: HTTP 200, a QA_Platform_ draft event; the value only lands in the line's meta_data; the round created later uses the event currency.
cases.oracle: 200; the new draft's line shows no currency of its own.

cases.section: Currency and lots elsewhere — create, update, read, bid, compare, award
cases.title: Lot and currency keys in the event's settings do not create lots or currencies
cases.why: Event config is merged as-is; a client cannot create a lot plan or a currency table by stuffing keys into it.
cases.setup: Buyer session.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups` with `config: {"lot_config": {...}, "currency_configuration": {...}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; the keys stay inside config; the event's real lot plan is empty (GET /event_groups/<new> has no lots).
cases.oracle: 200; show reply lots null.

cases.section: Currency and lots elsewhere — create, update, read, bid, compare, award
cases.title: A lot number on a draft line item does not create a lot
cases.why: Some clients send lot numbers with PR lines; only the lot drawer may create lots.
cases.setup: Buyer session.
cases.steps: `POST /event_groups` with `"lot_no": "2"` on the line.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; lot plan empty.

cases.section: Currency and lots elsewhere — create, update, read, bid, compare, award
cases.title: Reading the RFQ returns its currency and lot-creation settings
cases.why: These read-backs are the oracle for every currency and lot case: the currency table, vendor preferences, the lot- creation switch and read-only state.
cases.setup: {{eventGroupUuid}} / {{tradeId}} are the run's SANDBOX: a published (status active) event with one RFQ stage, 30-minute bid window still open, the QA vendor invited, no bids, no proposals. Caller is the run's QA buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /trade/{{tradeId}}?response_type=template`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; trade_config carries is_lot_creation_enabled (false for a lot round or when the company switch is off) and read_only_mode; currency_configuration is null on the sandbox.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; fields present.

journeys.title: Finding, copying and handing over events
journeys.goal: Find an event in the list by tab, search and filters, export the list, clone an event to start a new one, and hand an event to another owner — seeing only the events this user is allowed to see.

cases.title: The list shows Live and History always, Drafts and Recurring only when enabled
cases.why: Tabs that appear without their feature (or vanish with it) confuse buyers and hide work.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO (show_draft_tab ON, scheduled_events_enabled ON) and Demo Account 2 (both OFF).
cases.steps: Open the events page on each company.
cases.expected: PROCOL DEMO: Live, History, Drafts, Recurring. Demo Account 2: Live and History only.
cases.oracle: Visible tab labels per company.

cases.title: Tab badges match the lists underneath
cases.why: The Live badge comes from the Live list's event_group_count; History/Drafts from their own totals. Mismatches are the first sign of the stale tab-count cache.
cases.setup: A buyer with a few live, draft and closed QA events.
cases.steps: Read each badge, then count the cards after scrolling to the end of each tab.
cases.expected: Each badge equals the number of projects in its tab.
cases.oracle: Badge vs card count.

cases.title: Search waits for the user to stop typing and searches title and reference
cases.why: The box is debounced by one second and sends the text as filters.title; it matches event and stage titles and ref ids.
cases.setup: A published QA event with a unique title.
cases.steps: Type part of the title; then type the RFX ref id.
cases.expected: One request per pause (not per keystroke); the event is found by title and by ref id.
cases.oracle: Network log shows one /event_groups call per pause; card present.

cases.title: The date picker cannot choose future dates, and on Live it hides running events
cases.why: The picker disables future days; combined with the backend's closed_at rule, choosing any range on Live drops every event whose stage is still open.
cases.setup: A live QA event created today.
cases.steps: On Live, pick 'This month' (or any range ending today).
cases.expected: Future days are greyed out. The live event should stay visible; today it disappears from the list (and the badge drops).
cases.oracle: Card present before/after picking the range.

cases.title: 'Download report' appears only on History and warns about the default 3-month range
cases.why: The export is History-only; without a chosen range it silently uses the last 3 months, which the drawer must say.
cases.setup: A buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Open each tab; on History click Download report without choosing dates.
cases.expected: The button is visible on History only. The drawer states 'Report will be generated for duration of <3 months ago> to <today>'. Submitting shows 'Processing…' then the server message 'You will receive the report in your email shortly'.
cases.oracle: Button visibility; drawer text; toast text.

cases.title: 'Clone Project' is offered only when the company allows it and the project qualifies
cases.why: The menu item is removed unless allowed_to_clone_project is on, the user is not a planner, and the project is neither draft nor PR-created. Note: the API does not enforce the company setting (see API case on cloning with the feature off), and UI-PUB-021's expectation of a 1122 message for drafts cannot happen on screen because the item is hidden.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO (setting off) and a company with it on; an active, a draft and a PR-created project.
cases.steps: Open the project options menu on each.
cases.expected: Setting off: no Clone item anywhere. Setting on: Clone only on the active non-PR project.
cases.oracle: Menu items per project.

cases.title: Cloning warns about unsupported stages and opens the new draft
cases.why: The modal is the only place a buyer learns auctions are not copied; after success they land on the clone, which is a draft.
cases.setup: Company with cloning on; an active RFQ project.
cases.steps: Clone Project → read the modal → Yes, Clone Project.
cases.expected: Modal text 'Cloning is supported only for the Technical and RFQ stages.'; toast 'Project cloned successfully'; the browser opens the new project's Details tab; it shows as Draft with a new ref id and the same title.
cases.oracle: URL uuid differs from the source; status Draft.

cases.title: 'Change Owner' is offered only with owner-only visibility on and an active commercial stage
cases.why: The item is removed unless is_allowed_to_change_ownership is true: an active RFQ/auction stage, restrict_event_visibility_to_owner ON, caller not on the planning team, caller owner/super admin/Procol employee.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO (setting off) and a company with it on; a project with only an RFP stage live.
cases.steps: Open the options menu as owner, as super admin, as a team-mate.
cases.expected: Setting off: no item. Setting on: item for owner and super admin only, and only when a commercial stage is active.
cases.oracle: Menu items per user.

cases.title: The Change Owner modal lists eligible team-mates and redirects non-admins after success
cases.why: The modal states the consequences, disables the button until a user is picked, and — for non-admins with owner-only visibility — sends them back to the list because they lose access.
cases.setup: Company with restrict_event_visibility_to_owner ON; owner (non-admin) with a QA team-mate.
cases.steps: Open Change Owner; read the text; pick the team-mate; confirm.
cases.expected: Text 'Remove access from the current owner'; Change owner disabled until a pick; list equals GET team_buyers; on success 'Owner changed successfully' and redirect to the events list; the project disappears from the old owner's Live tab.
cases.oracle: Toast, URL after success, card absence.

cases.title: Typing '%' in search shows every event
cases.why: Users expect literal search. Today the backend treats % and _ as wildcards.
cases.setup: Any company with events.
cases.steps: Type '%' in the History search.
cases.expected: Only events whose title contains '%'. Today: the full list.
cases.oracle: Card count vs unfiltered.

cases.title: Live stage radio and History stage radio filter the list
cases.why: All / Live / In-Evaluation / Upcoming on Live; All / Completed / Withdrawn on History.
cases.setup: Events in bidding, in evaluation, closed and withdrawn.
cases.steps: Click each radio option on both tabs.
cases.expected: Each option shows only its bucket; All shows everything.
cases.oracle: Cards per option.

cases.title: The sorter offers only 'RFX Number' and remembers the choice
cases.why: Sort is saved to the user's preference (saveSorters). Only one sortable column exists, which keeps the backend's single-column limit hidden.
cases.setup: Any buyer.
cases.steps: Open the sorter, choose RFX Number ascending, reload.
cases.expected: Only 'RFX Number' is offered; after reload the order is still ascending.
cases.oracle: Order of ref ids after reload.

cases.title: A refused export shows a generic error instead of the reason
cases.why: When a member is blocked (code 10) or the range is missing (code 2), the screen discards the server message and shows 'Some error occurred while exporting report. Please try again.' — the user retries forever.
cases.setup: A member on a company with is_download_bulk_report_disabled_for_members ON.
cases.steps: Click Download report and submit.
cases.expected: The screen should say the export is not allowed for their role. Today: the generic retry message.
cases.oracle: Toast text.

cases.title: A refused owner change shows only 'Failed to change owner'
cases.why: 960 ('New Owner must be in same team as that of current owner') or 2 are replaced by a generic toast; the user cannot tell what to fix.
cases.setup: Force a refusal (e.g. pick a user who left the team between opening and confirming).
cases.steps: Confirm the change.
cases.expected: The toast should carry the server's reason. Today: 'Failed to change owner'.
cases.oracle: Toast text.

cases.title: The Recurring tab's search box does not narrow the list
cases.why: The box sends filters.title but the backend ignores all parameters on this endpoint.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO with two recurring templates.
cases.steps: Type one template's title in the Recurring search.
cases.expected: Only that template. Today: both remain.
cases.oracle: Card count.

cases.title: A cloned project appears at the top of Drafts under today's date
cases.why: Clones are marked as saved drafts so they show up in Drafts; the buyer expects to find their copy there.
cases.setup: Company with cloning on.
cases.steps: Clone a project, go back to the list, open Drafts.
cases.expected: The clone is listed under today's date group with the source's title.
cases.oracle: Card present in Drafts.

cases.title: Live keeps refreshing every 30 seconds only while visible, and the 'new projects' pill scrolls up
cases.why: The Live query polls every 30 s while the tab is active and the page visible; when newer projects exist a pill appears.
cases.setup: Two browser sessions on the same company.
cases.steps: Keep Live open in session 1; publish a QA event in session 2; wait 30 s; switch tab away and back.
cases.expected: The new project shows up (or the pill appears; clicking scrolls to top and reloads). No polling while the browser tab is hidden.
cases.oracle: Network log intervals; pill visibility.

cases.title: Card refresh returns other companies' events when given their ids
cases.why: The refresh loads `EventGroup.where(id: stale_eg_ids)` with no company scope and serialises title, ref id, creator name, company and line-item count. Ids are sequential and the uuid encoding is reversible, so any buyer can read every tenant's event titles and owners. This is a cross-tenant data leak.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. Low event ids (1–5) belong to other companies on UAT.
cases.steps: Call card refresh with raw ids 1–5. `GET /event_groups/update_cards?stale_eg_ids[]=1&…&stale_eg_ids[]=5`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with NO cards from other companies (ideally 422/455 for foreign ids). Today the cards come back with their titles, ref ids, creator names and company.
cases.oracle: Every returned card's company is PROCOL DEMO; any other company = defect (P0).

cases.title: Cloning someone else's company's project is refused
cases.why: create_clone looks the project up by id with no company scope; only the policy's allowed-companies check stops a forged id (the uuid encoding is reversible) from copying another tenant's specs.
cases.setup: Needs a known event id of another company and a correctly encoded uuid for it.
cases.steps: POST /event_groups/<other tenant uuid>/create_clone.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455; nothing created.
cases.oracle: 455; no draft appears.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: A vendor's user cannot be made owner while the owner is active — but can once the owner is deactivated
cases.why: With an active owner the team check (960) blocks vendor users. With an inactive owner validate_new_owner returns 'valid' immediately and the lookup is not company-scoped, so a supplier's user can be made owner of the buyer's event (extends EDGE-PUB-095 to the vendor case).
cases.setup: Needs a super admin, an event whose owner is deactivated, and a QA vendor user id.
cases.steps: POST change_ownership with the vendor user's uuid, first with an active owner, then with the owner deactivated.
cases.expected: Both refused. Today: first 960, second 200.
cases.oracle: Second call's status.

cases.section: Who sees which events — visibility per role and team
cases.title: A member sees their own and their teams' events, not other teams'
cases.why: Team scoping is the default privacy model between buying teams.
cases.setup: Two buyers in different teams; each publishes a QA event (restrict_event_visibility_to_owner OFF).
cases.steps: Each opens Live and History.
cases.expected: Each sees their own event and their team's; not the other team's. A super admin sees both.
cases.oracle: Cards per user.

cases.section: Who sees which events — visibility per role and team
cases.title: With owner-only visibility ON, a member sees only events they own, approve, chat on or were shared
cases.why: restrict_event_visibility_to_owner narrows the list to ownership, approver role, assigned chats and explicit shares.
cases.setup: Company with the setting ON; buyers A (owner) and B (same team, not approver).
cases.steps: B opens Live; then A assigns B a vendor chat; B reopens Live.
cases.expected: First: B does not see A's event. After the chat assignment: B sees it.
cases.oracle: Cards per step.

cases.section: Who sees which events — visibility per role and team
cases.title: A vendor sees only events they are invited to, and never a draft stage
cases.why: The same endpoints serve vendors; audience scoping and the draft-stage skip in the card are the only barriers.
cases.setup: QA vendor invited to the sandbox; another QA event without that vendor.
cases.steps: As the vendor: GET /event_groups, /history, /tab_counts.
cases.expected: Only the sandbox appears; draft stages are not serialised; tab counts match the lists.
cases.oracle: Cards and counts.

cases.title: The Live list answers with its four keys and includes the run's open sandbox event
cases.why: Every buyer lands here after login. If the response shape or the sandbox's presence regresses, the Live tab is empty or broken for everyone and later cases cannot find their own event.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The sandbox event is published (active, bid window open) and still on the Live tab.
cases.steps: Ask for the first page of the Live list with no parameters. `GET /event_groups`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with `event_groups` (at most 10 cards), `cursor`, `updated_projects_present` and `event_group_count`. The sandbox event is one of the cards (newest id first); none of the cards is a recurring template or a closed project.
cases.oracle: Response keys present; a card whose ref id is the sandbox's; `event_group_count` ≥ number of cards.

cases.title: An unknown sort column and direction fall back to newest-first
cases.why: sort_by is turned into a column name for ORDER BY and for the cursor comparison. Anything outside the allow-list must fall back, otherwise the parameter is an injection point.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The sandbox event is published (active, bid window open) and still on the Live tab.
cases.steps: Ask for the Live list sorted by a hostile column name and a nonsense direction. `GET /event_groups?sort_by=title%3BDROP%20TABLE%20event_groups&sort_direction=sideways`
cases.expected: HTTP 200, sorted by id descending, exactly like the baseline. Only id, created_at, updated_at and latest_stage_time are accepted; the direction must be asc or desc.
cases.oracle: Same card order as the baseline; no 500.

cases.title: Unreadable filters and search together crash the Live list
cases.why: `filters` and `search` are both JSON strings. When `filters` does not parse, the code falls back to `search`; when that does not parse either, the filter hash is left as nothing at all and the list code dereferences it. A stale bookmark or a bad client is enough to take the Live tab down with an untyped 500.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The sandbox event is published (active, bid window open) and still on the Live tab.
cases.steps: Ask for the Live list with both parameters unparsable. `GET /event_groups?filters=notjson&search=notjson`
cases.expected: Should answer 200 with the unfiltered list (or a 422). Today: parse_filters swallows the first error and returns nil, the fallback JSON.parse(search) raises inside a rescue, @filters stays nil, and filter_on_date reads @filters["starting_from"] → NoMethodError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: Picking a date range on the Live tab hides every event that is still running
cases.why: The Live tab has the same date picker as History. The chosen 'to' date is clamped to now and then compared with each stage's closed_at — but a running stage closes in the future, so it is filtered out. A buyer who narrows Live to 'this month' sees an empty or partial list and thinks their events vanished.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The sandbox event is published (active, bid window open) and still on the Live tab. The sandbox's bid window ends ~30 minutes in the future.
cases.steps: Ask for the Live list for a range from 1 Jan 2024 to 2100 (the backend clamps the end to now). `GET /event_groups?filters=%7B%22starting_from%22%3A1704067200%2C%22ending_at%22%3A4102444800%7D`
cases.expected: The sandbox (created inside the range) should still be listed. Today it is excluded: create_filter_params clamps ending_at to now and filter_on_date adds `trade_requests.closed_at <= now`, which no open stage satisfies.
cases.oracle: Compare with the baseline: the sandbox card disappears and `event_group_count` drops to events whose stages already closed. A correct fix keeps the sandbox.

cases.title: The 'Live' stage filter keeps the open sandbox and drops events in evaluation
cases.why: The radio buttons All / Live / In-Evaluation / Upcoming become stage_status buckets that the backend expands to event statuses. A wrong mapping silently moves events between buckets.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The sandbox event is published (active, bid window open) and still on the Live tab.
cases.steps: Ask for the Live list filtered to stages in bidding. `GET /event_groups?filters=%7B%22stage_status%22%3A%5B%22bidding%22%5D%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200. The sandbox (bidding open) is listed; events whose stages are all in evaluation are not.
cases.oracle: Sandbox card present; every card has at least one stage whose bid window is open now.

cases.title: History answers with date groups and a total, and never shows the open sandbox
cases.why: History is where buyers audit closed and withdrawn events; it must not leak events that are still running.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Ask for the first History page. `GET /event_groups/history`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with `event_groups` = [{date, data:[cards]}], `event_group_count` and `last_updated_at`. Only closed or withdrawn projects; the sandbox (still open, closed_at empty) is not among them.
cases.oracle: Keys present; no card carries the sandbox's ref id.

cases.title: A text 'statuses' filter crashes History
cases.why: filter_on_statuses assumes an array and calls include?(2) on it. A single status sent as text — a natural mistake for an integrator or an old mobile build — becomes an untyped 500.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Filter History by statuses given as the text "1". `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22statuses%22%3A%221%22%7D`
cases.expected: Should answer 200 (ignored or coerced) or 422. Today: "1".include?(2) raises TypeError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: The Drafts list answers for the run's buyer and contains only their own drafts
cases.why: Drafts are private work in progress; a regression that lists colleagues' drafts leaks unpublished specs and prices.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The run's buyer has at least one saved draft (clones made by the case run land here).
cases.steps: Ask for the Drafts list. `GET /event_groups/draft`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with date groups, `event_group_count`, `last_updated_at`. Every card was created by the caller (unless the caller is an auction-team member or super admin).
cases.oracle: Every card's creator is the run's buyer.

cases.title: SQL-looking search text is treated as plain text
cases.why: The title is bound as :query, so classic payloads must simply find nothing. This guards the binding against a future refactor to string interpolation.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. Company has closed QA_Platform_ events in History.
cases.steps: Search History for "' OR 1=1 --". `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22title%22%3A%22%27%20OR%201%3D1%20--%22%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with no events (or only events literally containing that text). No 500, no full list.
cases.oracle: event_groups empty; no 5xx.

cases.title: Searching for the run's naming prefix finds the closed QA events
cases.why: Positive control: searching by a known title fragment must find events by event title (not only by stage title).
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. Company has closed QA_Platform_ events in History.
cases.steps: Search History for 'QA_Platform_'. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22title%22%3A%22QA_Platform_%22%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200; every card's event title or a stage title/ref id contains 'QA_Platform_' (case-insensitive).
cases.oracle: Non-empty result where QA history exists; every card matches.

cases.title: Tab counts answer live, draft and history numbers when the feature is on
cases.why: The badges are the first numbers a buyer sees. Wrong or missing counts make them distrust the list.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. event_groups_tab_counts_enabled is ON (it is on PROCOL DEMO).
cases.steps: Ask for the tab counts. `GET /event_groups/tab_counts`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 {data:[{key:'live',item_count:n},{key:'draft',…},{key:'history',…}]} with numbers (draft may be null when allow_draft_project_creation is off and the user has no Clara access).
cases.oracle: live item_count ≥ 1 (the sandbox) and equals event_group_count of GET /event_groups with the same saved view.

cases.title: Tab counts ignore an explicit filter once cached, and a filtered call poisons them for 30 minutes
cases.why: The cache key has no filter in it. A call with a filter returns whatever is cached; if the cache was cold, the FILTERED numbers are stored and every later unfiltered call shows them for 30 minutes. The screen only sends no filters, but any other client (mobile, integrations) can make a buyer's badges wrong.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. event_groups_tab_counts_enabled is ON.
cases.steps: Ask for tab counts filtered to a title nothing matches. `GET /event_groups/tab_counts?filters=%7B%22title%22%3A%22QA_Platform_no_match_{{stamp}}%22%7D`. Then ask again without filters.
cases.expected: Filtered call: counts reflect the filter (0). Unfiltered call afterwards: real counts. Today either the first call returns the cached unfiltered numbers, or (cache cold) it stores zeros that the second call then returns.
cases.oracle: Compare the two answers with GET /event_groups event_group_count; any mismatch is the defect.

cases.section: Filter options, open tenders and the Recurring tab
cases.title: A buyer cannot fetch another company's filter options by passing company_id
cases.why: For buyers the company is forced to the current workspace; company_id is only honoured for vendors. Otherwise any buyer could enumerate another tenant's products, locations and users.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Ask for filter options with company_id=1. `GET /event_groups/filter_options?company_id=1`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with the caller's own options (identical to the baseline).
cases.oracle: Response equals the baseline response.

cases.title: Export without a date range is refused
cases.why: Without both dates the report would scan the company's whole history. The guard keeps exports bounded.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. is_download_bulk_report_disabled_for_members is OFF (it is off on PROCOL DEMO).
cases.steps: Request an export with a report category but no dates. `GET /reports/download_bulk_report?report_category=auction_bids_comparison_report`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. Nothing queued, no email.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2; no 'report in your email' message.

cases.title: Export with unreadable filters crashes before any check runs
cases.why: The export controller uses the shared filter parser, which leaves the filter hash empty-handed on bad JSON; the next before-action indexes it. An untyped 500 instead of 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. is_download_bulk_report_disabled_for_members is OFF (it is off on PROCOL DEMO).
cases.steps: Request an export with filters=notjson. `GET /reports/download_bulk_report?report_category=auction_bids_comparison_report&filters=notjson`
cases.expected: Should answer 422 (code 2). Today: create_filter_params rescues and leaves @filters nil, then set_order_type_filter reads @filters["buy_offers"] → NoMethodError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: A member is refused the export when the company disables it for members
cases.why: Some companies restrict bulk exports to super admins. Members must get a clear refusal, and the screen must show it.
cases.setup: Needs a member (not super admin) on a company with is_download_bulk_report_disabled_for_members ON.
cases.steps: As the member, request an export with a valid 7-day range.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 10 'You are not allowed to use this functionality'. The screen today shows the generic 'Some error occurred while exporting report' instead (see UI case).
cases.oracle: 422 + code 10; no report queued.

cases.title: A valid export is queued and emailed to the caller only
cases.why: The export is asynchronous: the API answers with a message and the file arrives by email. It must go to the caller, carry the History filters, and ranges over 30 days must go through approval where configured.
cases.setup: Needs a mailbox for the caller; sends a real email — run manually on a QA account. Use a range ≤ 30 days to avoid the approval flow (which notifies approvers).
cases.steps: Request an export for the last 7 days with category auction_bids_comparison_report and two columns.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 'You will receive the report in your email shortly'. A Report row (status draft, report_type custom) with the filters and column_selection is created and a ReportDownloadLog is written. > 30 days with approval required: '…after export request is approved' and an approval request instead.
cases.oracle: Email received by the caller only; report columns match the selection.

cases.title: The API clones even when the company has cloning switched off
cases.why: The screen hides 'Clone Project' unless allowed_to_clone_project is on, but neither the policy nor the controller reads that setting. Any buyer with create permission can clone through the API on a company that has not bought or enabled the feature.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer (creator of the sandbox). allowed_to_clone_project is OFF (it is off on PROCOL DEMO). The sandbox is active and not from a PR.
cases.steps: Clone the sandbox. `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/create_clone` with `{}`
cases.expected: Should be refused (feature off). Today HTTP 200 {event_group_uuid} and a draft copy appears in Drafts.
cases.oracle: Status; a new QA_Platform_ draft in GET /event_groups/draft = the gate is UI-only.

cases.title: A clone copies line items, technical and RFQ stages, and vendors — and nothing that belongs to the old run
cases.why: Buyers clone to rerun the same sourcing. They expect the same items, stages and invited vendors, and no leftovers (bids, proposals, rankings, closed dates, lots).
cases.setup: Needs the new clone's uuid from the create_clone response (the runner cannot chain it). Source: an active RFP+RFQ event with 2 line items, one inactive line item, invited vendors and an evaluator.
cases.steps: 1. POST create_clone. 2. GET /event_groups/<clone>, /get_line_items, /get_audience, and each stage.
cases.expected: Clone is draft, owned by the cloner, same title, new ref id; only ACTIVE line items (status draft, serial order kept); RFP stage with its forms and evaluator access lists; RFQ stage with its trade products; same vendors; no bids, proposals, precomputed ranks, lot_config, started_at or closed_at; meta_data.source_event_group_id = source id.
cases.oracle: Field-by-field comparison with the source.

cases.title: A clone gets a fresh 21-day bid window — and a 21-day extra closing time
cases.why: Source timings are usually in the past, so the clone resets them. But the extra closing window is also set to 21 days regardless of the source (often minutes or hours), so a buyer who publishes without checking gives vendors three extra weeks after bidding closes.
cases.setup: Needs the clone uuid (see previous case).
cases.steps: Clone an event whose extra closing time is 1 hour; read the clone's schedules.
cases.expected: Bid window: now → now+21 days (clone time). Extra closing: should keep the source's duration; today it is +21 days after the bid end.
cases.oracle: rfq_extra_closing_time / extra_closing_time end − start on the clone.

cases.title: Cloning a withdrawn project produces a project with no stages
cases.why: Withdrawal marks every stage in_active, and the clone copies only stages that are not in_active. The controller explicitly allows withdrawn projects ('Only active or withdrawn events can be cloned.') and buyers use it to relaunch — but the copy has line items and no RFP/RFQ at all.
cases.setup: Needs a withdrawn QA event and the clone uuid; the runner's sandbox is withdrawn only at the very end of a run.
cases.steps: Withdraw a QA_Platform_ event with an RFQ stage; clone it; read the clone's stages.
cases.expected: The clone should carry the RFQ stage as a draft. Today it has zero stages.
cases.oracle: Clone's stages list is empty = defect.

cases.title: Cloning a closed or awarded project copies the setup but none of the award
cases.why: Awarded projects are the common source for a rerun. Proposals, awards and POs must stay with the original.
cases.setup: Needs the journey's own event (closed, one bid, a submitted proposal); its event uuid is not exposed to cases.
cases.steps: Clone the journey's event; read the clone's proposals and bids.
cases.expected: Clone is draft with no proposals, bids, orders or precomputed ranking; the source's award is untouched.
cases.oracle: GET proposals/bids on the clone are empty; source unchanged.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: Making yourself the owner is refused as missing parameters
cases.why: Self-transfer must be a no-op refusal, not a transfer that deactivates and recreates the owner access row and emails the owner about themselves.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer, who created (owns) the sandbox.
cases.steps: Transfer the sandbox to the run's own buyer. `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/change_ownership` with `{"new_owner_uuid": "{{buyerUserUuid}}"}`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. Owner unchanged; no email.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2; GET the event: owner unchanged.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: Transferring to a user id that does not exist is refused
cases.why: A well-formed uuid for no user must not reach the transfer service (which would create an owner row for a ghost).
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer, who created (owns) the sandbox.
cases.steps: Transfer to the bogus uuid. `POST …/change_ownership` with `{"new_owner_uuid": "Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="}`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: The new-owner picker lists the owner's active team-mates, without the owner or planners
cases.why: This list is the only choice the Change Owner modal offers. It must contain exactly the people the backend will accept.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer, who created (owns) the sandbox.
cases.steps: Ask for eligible owners of the sandbox. `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/team_buyers`
cases.expected: HTTP 200, a list of {user_id, user_name}: active users sharing an active team with the owner, minus the owner and minus planners. (If the owner were inactive: every buyer of the company minus planners.)
cases.oracle: The run's buyer is not in the list; every listed user would pass the 960 team check.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: With owner-only visibility OFF, an API transfer 'succeeds' but nothing changes
cases.why: The screen hides Change Owner unless restrict_event_visibility_to_owner is on, but the API accepts the transfer anyway. With the setting off, EventGroup#user ignores the new owner row and keeps returning the creator — so policy, cards and the next transfer still treat the creator as owner, while the creator's draft award proposal is moved to the 'new owner' and both people get 'event assigned/unassigned' emails.
cases.setup: Needs restrict_event_visibility_to_owner OFF (as on PROCOL DEMO) and a SECOND QA buyer on the owner's team — never a real colleague, so not a runnable twin.
cases.steps: 1. Owner has a draft proposal. 2. POST change_ownership to the QA team-mate. 3. GET the event, the Live card and the proposal.
cases.expected: Should be refused when the feature is off (or actually change the owner). Today: 200 'Ownership transferred successfully', card still shows the creator, creator can still transfer again, the draft proposal now belongs to the other user, two emails.
cases.oracle: Card user.name and policy behaviour after the call.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: Transferring to a deactivated user is refused
cases.why: Ownership must never land on someone who cannot log in.
cases.setup: Needs a deactivated QA user id on the company.
cases.steps: POST change_ownership with that user's uuid.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters' — User.active excludes them.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: A user who left the company may still be offered and accepted as the new owner
cases.why: Both the picker and the check use User.active and TeamMember.active; neither checks the user's membership status in THIS company. A person removed from the company but still on a team row could be offered and accepted. (To verify: whether removal also deactivates team memberships.)
cases.setup: Needs a QA user removed from the company (UserCompanyMapping inactive) whose team membership row is still active.
cases.steps: GET team_buyers; POST change_ownership to that user.
cases.expected: The user is neither listed nor accepted.
cases.oracle: Picker contents and the transfer's answer.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: Only the owner, a super admin or a Procol employee can open the picker
cases.why: team_buyers? mirrors change_ownership?. A plain team-mate must not be able to list candidates or transfer.
cases.setup: Needs a second buyer (non-admin) on the owner's team.
cases.steps: As that buyer: GET team_buyers; POST change_ownership.
cases.expected: Both HTTP 422, code 455.
cases.oracle: 455 twice.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: After a transfer the new owner can transfer onwards and the previous owner cannot (owner-only visibility ON)
cases.why: With the setting on, ownership follows the owner access row; the policy compares the caller with record.user_id.
cases.setup: Needs restrict_event_visibility_to_owner ON and two QA buyers on one team.
cases.steps: A transfers to B; A tries to transfer again; B transfers back to A.
cases.expected: A's second attempt: 455. B's attempt: 200. Exactly one active owner row at every step.
cases.oracle: Responses and AccessList rows.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: A transfer hands over open work: draft proposal, submitted proposals, chats
cases.why: The point of a transfer is that the new owner can finish the award. Draft proposals are duplicated, submitted ('requested') ones are re-pointed with their template responses, chat assignments move and the old owner is muted.
cases.setup: Needs two QA buyers and an event with a draft proposal, a requested proposal and a vendor chat.
cases.steps: Transfer; read proposals, chat assignments and participants.
cases.expected: Old draft proposal in_active and a copy owned by the new owner; requested proposals' creator = new owner; chat assignment revised → new active assignment; old owner muted; meta_data.owner_trail has one entry; quotation template cache dropped.
cases.oracle: Each item checked.

cases.section: Who sees which events — visibility per role and team
cases.title: Auction-team users see only auction stages
cases.why: Auction desks should not see RFP/RFQ work.
cases.setup: A user in the auction team; events with RFQ and auction stages.
cases.steps: Open Live and History as that user.
cases.expected: Only auction / RFQ-then-auction stages are listed; Drafts additionally include RFQ-then-auction drafts.
cases.oracle: Stage modes on cards.

cases.section: Who sees which events — visibility per role and team
cases.title: Planners see only technical (RFP/RFI) stages
cases.why: Planner roles evaluate specs; commercial stages are hidden.
cases.setup: A planner-gated user who is not a purchaser.
cases.steps: Open Live and History.
cases.expected: Only RFP/RFI stages; filtered_stages_count shows 'n/m Stage'.
cases.oracle: Stage modes on cards.

cases.section: Who sees which events — visibility per role and team
cases.title: Withdrawn events leave Live and appear in History; removed (in_active) events appear nowhere
cases.why: Withdrawal sets closed_at, so the project moves tabs; only active and withdrawn projects are valid for the dashboard.
cases.setup: A QA event that is then withdrawn.
cases.steps: Withdraw; GET /event_groups and /history?filters={stage_status:[withdrawn]}.
cases.expected: Gone from Live; present in History under Withdrawn; tab counts move by one each (after cache expiry).
cases.oracle: Card positions and counts.

cases.title: A garbage pagination cursor returns an empty page, not an error
cases.why: The cursor is echoed back from the previous page and compared against the sort column; a client that corrupts it (stale tab, manual URL) must get an empty page, never a database error.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The sandbox event is published (active, bid window open) and still on the Live tab.
cases.steps: Ask for the Live list with a non-numeric cursor. `GET /event_groups?latest_cursor=abc`
cases.expected: HTTP 200. The cursor is type-cast to the id column ("abc" becomes 0), so the page holds no cards while `event_group_count` still shows the real total. No 500.
cases.oracle: 200; `event_groups` is empty; `event_group_count` equals the baseline's.

cases.title: Sorting by two columns, the way the screen builds it, is silently ignored
cases.why: The dashboard joins every chosen sorter with commas (sort_by=created_at,id). The backend accepts a single column only, so a multi-sort silently becomes newest-id-first. Today the Sorter offers only 'RFX Number', so this is latent — the day a second sortable column is added, users will see their sort ignored.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The sandbox event is published (active, bid window open) and still on the Live tab.
cases.steps: Ask for the Live list with two sort columns. `GET /event_groups?sort_by=created_at%2Cid&sort_direction=asc%2Cdesc`
cases.expected: HTTP 200, ordered by id descending (the fallback), not by created_at ascending. No error tells the client its sort was dropped.
cases.oracle: Card order equals the baseline order, not the oldest-first order the request asked for.

cases.title: A minimum-quantity filter sent as a list crashes History
cases.why: min_quantity is converted with to_f, which only exists on numbers and strings. A list (what a multi-select widget would send) crashes the whole list.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Filter History with min_quantity [5]. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22min_quantity%22%3A%5B5%5D%7D`
cases.expected: Should answer 200 or 422. Today [5].to_f raises NoMethodError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: A creator filter sent as a list under 'user_id' crashes History
cases.why: The singular user_id filter calls to_i on whatever arrives. The screen sends creator_ids (a list) — a client that reuses the list under the singular key takes the tab down.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Filter History with user_id [1]. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22user_id%22%3A%5B1%5D%7D`
cases.expected: Should answer 200 or 422. Today [1].to_i raises NoMethodError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: A team filter holding objects instead of ids crashes History
cases.why: team_ids is checked to be an array, then every element gets to_i. Objects (e.g. {id, name} pairs straight from a select widget) have no to_i.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Filter History with team_ids [{"id":1}]. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22team_ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22id%22%3A1%7D%5D%7D`
cases.expected: Should answer 200 or 422. Today Hash#to_i raises NoMethodError → HTTP 500. The same shape crashes delivery_zone_ids, vendor_ids, company_ids and product_category_ids, which use the same `.map(&:to_i)` guard.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: A start date millions of years ahead must not reach the database as a timestamp
cases.why: starting_from is an epoch number turned into a Time and sent to Postgres. A value past the database's timestamp range (year 294276) makes Postgres raise, which the app re-raises as a 500.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Filter History from epoch 99999999999999. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22starting_from%22%3A99999999999999%7D`
cases.expected: Should answer 200 (empty) or 422. Expected today: `trade_requests.closed_at >= <year 3170843>` → Postgres out-of-range error → ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid re-raised → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: A legacy 'search' parameter holding a list crashes History
cases.why: When no filters are sent, the old `search` parameter becomes the whole filter object. A JSON list there replaces the filter hash with an array, and the next line indexes it with a string.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Call History with search=[1] and no filters. `GET /event_groups/history?search=%5B1%5D`
cases.expected: Should answer 200 or 422. Today @filters becomes [1] and get_data_for_history_page evaluates [1]["ending_at"] → TypeError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: A legacy 'search' parameter holding plain text crashes History
cases.why: Same path as the previous case but with a JSON string: String#[]= with a substring that is not there raises IndexError.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Call History with search="x" (a JSON string). `GET /event_groups/history?search=%22x%22`
cases.expected: Should answer 200 or 422. Today @filters becomes "x"; `"x"["ending_at"] = now` raises IndexError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: Unparsable filters on History are silently ignored and the full list comes back
cases.why: A broken filter string should either be refused or applied — never silently dropped, because the buyer then trusts an unfiltered list as filtered. This pins today's behaviour so a change is noticed.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Call History with filters=notjson. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=notjson`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with exactly the unfiltered list (same `event_group_count` as the baseline). No hint that the filter was dropped.
cases.oracle: event_group_count equals the baseline; no 5xx.

cases.title: A non-numeric 'last_updated_at' returns an empty page instead of the first page
cases.why: History pages backwards from last_updated_at. Text becomes 0 → 1 Jan 1970, so the 'next page' is empty and infinite scroll stops early. A client bug here makes history look empty.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Call History with last_updated_at=abc. `GET /event_groups/history?last_updated_at=abc`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with an empty `event_groups` list (everything closed after 1970 is excluded). No error.
cases.oracle: event_groups empty while event_group_count is unchanged.

cases.title: The 'Withdrawn' History filter lists only withdrawn projects
cases.why: Withdrawn projects stay in History and buyers relaunch them from here. The bucket maps to in_active/withdrawn stages; a mapping slip would mix completed and withdrawn events.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Filter History to withdrawn. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22stage_status%22%3A%5B%22withdrawn%22%5D%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200; every card has at least one withdrawn/removed stage; no purely completed event appears.
cases.oracle: Every card's stages include a withdrawn one.

cases.title: An unknown stage-status bucket is silently ignored
cases.why: Unknown buckets map to nothing and the filter disappears, returning the whole History. A typo in a saved view therefore shows everything instead of nothing.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Filter History with an unknown bucket. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22stage_status%22%3A%5B%22not_a_bucket%22%5D%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with the unfiltered list (same count as the baseline).
cases.oracle: event_group_count equals the baseline.

cases.title: An event status the user's role may not filter by is dropped, not applied
cases.why: The status list differs for purchasers and planners. Statuses outside the role's list are removed before filtering, so a purchaser cannot use planner-only statuses — and an unknown status silently shows everything.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Filter History by a status that does not exist. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22event_statuses%22%3A%5B%22not_a_status%22%5D%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with the unfiltered list.
cases.oracle: event_group_count equals the baseline.

cases.title: The 'Auction' stage-type filter lists only events with an auction stage
cases.why: stage_type is expanded server-side to rfx modes (auction also means rfq_then_auction). A broken expansion hides converted auctions from the filter.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Filter History to auctions. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22stage_type%22%3A%5B%22auction%22%5D%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200; every card has an auction or RFQ-then-auction stage.
cases.oracle: All listed stages are auction-type.

cases.title: A creator filter with an undecodable id returns nothing rather than everything
cases.why: creator_uuids are decoded inside the filter JSON; an undecodable one becomes nil. The filter must then match nothing — falling open would show every colleague's events to someone who asked for one person's.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Filter History by creator WrongUuid1=. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22creator_uuids%22%3A%5B%22WrongUuid1%3D%22%5D%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with no events (user_id IN (NULL) matches nothing).
cases.oracle: event_groups empty.

cases.title: An unknown auction strategy in the filter does not crash History
cases.why: auction_strategy goes straight into an enum WHERE clause. Unknown enum values must not reach Postgres as a type error.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Filter History by auction_strategy "bogus". `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22auction_strategy%22%3A%22bogus%22%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 (empty or unfiltered), never 500.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: History pages hold 20 stages, so a page can show fewer than 20 events
cases.why: The page limit is applied to stages, then grouped into events. An event with many stages can take a whole page, and the next page's cursor can skip that event's remaining stages — buyers see 'missing' stages on history cards.
cases.setup: Needs a company with an event whose stage count exceeds 20 or several multi-stage events closed in the same window; the sandbox has one stage, so this is not a runnable twin.
cases.steps: Open History; scroll page by page; count events and stages per page.
cases.expected: Each page covers at most 20 stages; every stage of every listed event appears on some page; no event repeats across pages.
cases.oracle: Union of stages across pages equals the set of stages of closed events.

cases.title: 'listing_view=true' keeps only drafts that came from purchase requests
cases.why: The PR screen reuses the Drafts endpoint with listing_view=true to offer 'add to an existing draft'. If the switch stops working, PR items get attached to unrelated drafts.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Ask for the Drafts list in listing view. `GET /event_groups/draft?listing_view=true`
cases.expected: HTTP 200; every card is linked to at least one purchase request.
cases.oracle: No card without a PR link.

cases.title: A text 'statuses' filter crashes the Drafts list too
cases.why: Drafts share apply_all_filters with History, so the same type bug takes this tab down.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Filter Drafts with statuses "1". `GET /event_groups/draft?filters=%7B%22statuses%22%3A%221%22%7D`
cases.expected: Should answer 200 or 422. Today HTTP 500 ("1".include?(2) → TypeError).
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: The Drafts list has no permission check of its own
cases.why: Every other list action calls authorize (index?/history?/all?). draft does not, so a user whose role lacks 'trade read' still gets an answer. Today the data is limited to their own drafts, but the missing check means any future widening of the query leaks immediately.
cases.setup: Needs a second console user whose role has no trade read_record permission — not available to the runner.
cases.steps: As that user, call `GET /event_groups/draft`; then `GET /event_groups/history`.
cases.expected: Both should be refused with 455. Today history is refused (policy history? → index?) but draft answers 200.
cases.oracle: draft and history give the same verdict.

cases.title: Active projects with an unpublished stage show up under Drafts
cases.why: fetch_event_groups_for_draft unions saved drafts with ACTIVE projects that still have a draft stage. Buyers find a live event under Drafts and may think it was unpublished.
cases.setup: Needs an active event with an extra stage saved but not published; the sandbox has none.
cases.steps: Publish an event, add a second stage and save it without publishing; open Drafts and Live.
cases.expected: The project appears on both tabs; the Drafts card shows only the unpublished stage. Recurring templates never appear.
cases.oracle: Card present on both tabs; is_scheduled_template projects absent.

cases.title: Searching '%' matches every event
cases.why: % is an SQL wildcard and is not escaped, so a buyer looking for '10% discount' or just '%' gets the entire list. Search results that ignore the text erode trust in the list.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. Company has closed QA_Platform_ events in History.
cases.steps: Search History for '%'. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22title%22%3A%22%25%22%7D`
cases.expected: Should return only events whose title or ref id contains a literal '%'. Today it returns every event (count equals the unfiltered baseline). '_' behaves the same way as a one-character wildcard.
cases.oracle: event_group_count equals the baseline (defect if so).

cases.title: Unicode search text (accents, CJK, emoji) works
cases.why: Vendors and products are named in many scripts; the search must not break on multi-byte input.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. Company has closed QA_Platform_ events in History.
cases.steps: Search History for 'Ω≈ç√ 中文 😀 ñ'. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22title%22%3A%22%CE%A9%E2%89%88%C3%A7%E2%88%9A%20%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87%20%F0%9F%98%80%20%C3%B1%22%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 (normally no matches). No 500, no encoding error.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: A 2,000-character search does not crash the list
cases.why: There is no length cap on the search text. Very long input should be refused or simply match nothing, not time out or 500.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. Company has closed QA_Platform_ events in History.
cases.steps: Search History for 'QA_Platform_' followed by 1,988 'A's (2,000 characters). `GET /event_groups/history?filters={"title":"QA_Platform_AAAA…"}`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with no matches, answered quickly. No 500 or gateway timeout.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: Script tags in the search text are stripped, not executed or crashed on
cases.why: Every string parameter is HTML-stripped before the controller runs — including the whole JSON filters string. Search text with markup must not break the JSON or crash the list.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. Company has closed QA_Platform_ events in History.
cases.steps: Search History for '<script>alert(1)</script>'. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22title%22%3A%22%3Cscript%3Ealert%281%29%3C%2Fscript%3E%22%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200; the tags are stripped before parsing so the search runs on the remaining text (or nothing). No 500.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: A search value that is a list instead of text does not crash
cases.why: The title is interpolated into a LIKE pattern; a list turns into its printed form ("[\"a\", \"b\"]"). It must not 500.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. Company has closed QA_Platform_ events in History.
cases.steps: Search History with title ["a","b"]. `GET /event_groups/history?filters=%7B%22title%22%3A%5B%22a%22%2C%22b%22%5D%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 (no matches). Ideally a 422 for a non-text title.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: The legacy 'search' parameter still filters when 'filters' is absent
cases.why: Older mobile builds send search={json}. It is the fallback when filters is empty; if it silently stops working, those users see unfiltered lists.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. Company has closed QA_Platform_ events in History.
cases.steps: Call History with search={"title":"QA_Platform_"} and no filters. `GET /event_groups/history?search=%7B%22title%22%3A%22QA_Platform_%22%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with the same result as the filters-based search for 'QA_Platform_'.
cases.oracle: Same event_group_count as the positive search case.

cases.title: With tab counts switched off, the badges come back empty instead of failing
cases.why: Companies without the feature must still get a well-formed answer so the screen renders tabs without numbers.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. event_groups_tab_counts_enabled is OFF (skipped on PROCOL DEMO, where it is on).
cases.steps: Ask for the tab counts. `GET /event_groups/tab_counts`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with the three keys and item_count null for each.
cases.oracle: All item_count values are null.

cases.title: Tab counts stay stale for up to 30 minutes after a new event is published
cases.why: The cache is only cleared when the user's saved view changes. After publishing, the Live badge still shows the old number while the list below already shows the new card.
cases.setup: Needs a before/after around a publish within the same 30-minute window; the case runner builds the sandbox before cases run, so the 'before' value is not observable from a case.
