cases.steps: 1. GET /event_groups/tab_counts and note live. 2. Publish a new QA_Platform_ event. 3. GET tab_counts again and GET /event_groups.
cases.expected: The live count increases by one. Today it stays unchanged until the 30-minute cache expires.
cases.oracle: tab_counts live vs GET /event_groups event_group_count after the publish.

cases.title: The Draft badge is empty when draft creation is off and the user has no Clara access
cases.why: Companies without draft-project creation should not see a misleading 0 on Drafts.
cases.setup: Needs a company with allow_draft_project_creation OFF (PROCOL DEMO has it on; Demo Account 2 has it off).
cases.steps: GET /event_groups/tab_counts on such a company.
cases.expected: draft item_count is null; live and history are numbers.
cases.oracle: draft item_count null.

cases.title: Refreshing cards without naming any card is refused
cases.why: Without ids there is nothing to refresh; the endpoint must say so rather than return the whole company.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Call card refresh with no ids. `GET /event_groups/update_cards`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.title: Card ids sent as one plain value crash the refresh
cases.why: Rails passes a single query value as text; the code calls uniq on it as if it were a list.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Call card refresh with stale_eg_ids=5. `GET /event_groups/update_cards?stale_eg_ids=5`
cases.expected: Should answer 200 (treating it as one id) or 422. Today String#uniq raises NoMethodError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: Refreshing a card that does not exist returns an empty list
cases.why: Deleted or bogus ids must simply drop out.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Call card refresh with the bogus uuid. `GET /event_groups/update_cards?stale_eg_uuids=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw%3D%3D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with `event_groups: []` and `updated_projects_present: false`.
cases.oracle: Empty card list.

cases.title: Refreshing the sandbox card with a garbage 'newest' cursor still returns the card
cases.why: newest_cursor is compared against the sort column to detect new projects; garbage must not 500 or hide the requested card.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The sandbox is live.
cases.steps: Call card refresh for the sandbox with newest_cursor=abc and sort_by=created_at. `GET /event_groups/update_cards?stale_eg_uuids={{eventGroupUuid}}&newest_cursor=abc&sort_by=created_at`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with the sandbox card and `updated_projects_present: false`.
cases.oracle: One card, the sandbox's.

cases.section: Filter options, open tenders and the Recurring tab
cases.title: The filter panel options load for a buyer
cases.why: The filter panel is built from this list; options depend on the user's read permissions (products, categories, locations, PRs, users) plus order type, status, stage type and — with Clara — auto-pilot status.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Ask for the filter options. `GET /event_groups/filter_options`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 {data:[…]} sorted by name; includes Order Type, Status and Stage Type; other groups only where the user may read them.
cases.oracle: Status, Stage Type and Order Type present.

cases.section: Filter options, open tenders and the Recurring tab
cases.title: A buyer cannot call the vendors' open-tender list
cases.why: GET /event_groups/all is the vendor-side 'open tenders' feed. Policy all? refuses buyers outright.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Ask for open tenders as the buyer. `GET /event_groups/all`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action'.

cases.section: Filter options, open tenders and the Recurring tab
cases.title: The Recurring tab ignores search and filters
cases.why: The Recurring tab shows a search box and sends filters/title, but the scheduled action reads no parameters at all and returns every active or paused template. Buyers type in the box and nothing narrows.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. scheduled_events_enabled is ON (it is on PROCOL DEMO).
cases.steps: Ask for recurring events filtered to a title nothing matches. `GET /event_groups/scheduled?filters=%7B%22title%22%3A%22QA_Platform_no_match%22%7D`
cases.expected: Should return only matching templates (none). Today it returns the full list, identical to the unfiltered call.
cases.oracle: Compare with GET /event_groups/scheduled: identical = defect.

cases.section: Filter options, open tenders and the Recurring tab
cases.title: Only live recurring templates are listed; withdrawn ones and finished schedules are not
cases.why: The Recurring tab is the buyer's control panel for repeat events. Withdrawn templates or completed/cancelled schedules should not appear; paused ones should (so they can be resumed).
cases.setup: Needs scheduled templates in several states (active job, paused job, completed job, withdrawn template).
cases.steps: GET /event_groups/scheduled.
cases.expected: Active-job and paused-job templates in status active/draft are listed; completed/cancelled jobs and withdrawn templates are not.
cases.oracle: Listed set equals templates with job status active/paused.

cases.section: Filter options, open tenders and the Recurring tab
cases.title: Recurring templates never appear on the Live tab
cases.why: A template is not a real event; showing it on Live invites bids or edits on the template.
cases.setup: Needs a scheduled template on the company (scheduled_events_enabled ON).
cases.steps: GET /event_groups and GET /event_groups/scheduled.
cases.expected: The template appears only in scheduled; Live excludes is_scheduled_template (also in update_cards).
cases.oracle: Template ref id absent from Live.

cases.title: Export with only a start date is refused
cases.why: Both ends are required; a half-open range is the same unbounded scan.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. is_download_bulk_report_disabled_for_members is OFF (it is off on PROCOL DEMO).
cases.steps: Request an export with only starting_from. `GET /reports/download_bulk_report?report_category=auction_bids_comparison_report&filters=%7B%22starting_from%22%3A1727740800%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.title: Export with a product filter sent as text crashes before the date check
cases.why: set_product_and_delivery_zone_maps_to_filter iterates product_ids with each; text has no each. The crash happens before the date guard, so the request never gets a readable error.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. is_download_bulk_report_disabled_for_members is OFF (it is off on PROCOL DEMO).
cases.steps: Request an export with product_ids "5" and only a start date. `GET /reports/download_bulk_report?report_category=auction_bids_comparison_report&filters=%7B%22product_ids%22%3A%225%22%2C%22starting_from%22%3A1727740800%7D`
cases.expected: Should answer 422 (code 2, the missing end date). Today String#each raises NoMethodError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.title: A category-less export builds the file synchronously and returns a signed link
cases.why: Without report_category the controller builds a data-dump Excel inside the request. On a large company this ties up a web worker for the whole build.
cases.setup: Manual: needs a company with substantial history; measure response time.
cases.steps: Request an export with valid dates and no report_category.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 {report_url: signed S3 URL}; response time recorded (should stay under the gateway timeout).
cases.oracle: Signed URL downloads; time within budget.

cases.title: Cloning a project that does not exist answers 'Project does not exist.'
cases.why: The lookup happens before the policy; a bogus id must give a clean 533, not a 500 from authorising nil.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer (creator of the sandbox).
cases.steps: Clone the bogus project id. `POST /event_groups/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/create_clone` with `{}`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 533 'Project does not exist.'. No project created.

cases.title: Cloning with an undecodable id answers 'Project does not exist.'
cases.why: WrongUuid1= decodes to nil; find_by(id: nil) must not pick up some row with a null id or crash.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer (creator of the sandbox).
cases.steps: Clone id WrongUuid1=. `POST /event_groups/WrongUuid1=/create_clone` with `{}`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 533 'Project does not exist.'.

cases.title: Clone cannot be triggered with GET
cases.why: Only POST is routed. A GET (link prefetch, crawler, image tag) must never create a project.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer (creator of the sandbox).
cases.steps: Send GET to the clone URL of the sandbox. `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/create_clone`
cases.expected: HTTP 404 (no route). No project created.
cases.oracle: Non-2xx, not 5xx; Drafts list unchanged.

cases.title: The project detail config tells the screen whether Clone and Change Owner are offered
cases.why: These two flags are the only thing standing between a buyer and the menu items; they must follow the documented rules (clone: setting on, not planner, not draft, not from PR; change owner: active commercial stage, restrict_event_visibility_to_owner on, caller not on the planning team, caller owner/super admin/Procol employee).
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The sandbox event is published (active, bid window open) and still on the Live tab.
cases.steps: Read the sandbox. `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`
cases.expected: HTTP 200. On PROCOL DEMO (both settings off): config.allowed_to_clone_project is false and config.is_allowed_to_change_ownership is false; config.should_redirect_after_changing_ownership is false.
cases.oracle: Flags match the settings returned by the dashboard configuration.

cases.title: Cloning an RFQ that was converted to an auction drops the auction
cases.why: The clone copies only rfi/rfp/rfq modes. An RFQ converted to rfq_then_auction, or a plain auction stage, is skipped, and the screen only warns 'Cloning is supported only for the Technical and RFQ stages'.
cases.setup: Needs an event with an auction stage.
cases.steps: Clone it and read the stages.
cases.expected: Only technical/RFQ stages are present; the auction stage is absent; the modal warned about it.
cases.oracle: Stage modes on the clone.

cases.title: Cloning a lot event copies only the parent RFQ
cases.why: Lot RFQs are listed in lot_config; the clone excludes them and clears lot_config, so the copy is one un-lotted RFQ.
cases.setup: Needs an event with active lots.
cases.steps: Clone it; read stages and lot_config.
cases.expected: One parent RFQ, no lot RFQs, lot_config empty.
cases.oracle: Stage count and lot_config on the clone.

cases.title: Cloning a recurring template copies the template flag and its job link
cases.why: deep_dup keeps is_scheduled_template and config.scheduled_job_id; nothing resets them. The clone is a draft 'template' pointing at the SOURCE's job — republishing it can resume or alter the original schedule.
cases.setup: Needs scheduled_events_enabled ON and an active template.
cases.steps: Clone a template; read the clone's is_scheduled_template and config.scheduled_job_id; publish the clone.
cases.expected: Clone should be a plain event (flag false, no job id). Today both are copied.
cases.oracle: Clone fields; source job status after the clone is published.

cases.title: Cloning copies stale meta data such as owner history and pending-bid counts
cases.why: Only cloned_event_group_ids is removed from meta_data. owner_trail, pending_unregistered_bids_count, is_auto_created and clara_stuck_reasons ride along, so a brand-new draft shows 'pending unregistered bids' and a previous owner history.
cases.setup: Needs a source whose meta_data has those keys (ownership transferred once; an unregistered bid pending).
cases.steps: Clone; read the clone's card (GET /event_groups/draft) and meta data.
cases.expected: Clone card shows pending_unregistered_bids_count 0 and no owner trail. Today the source values are copied.
cases.oracle: Card counters on the clone.

cases.title: A withdrawn project that came from a purchase request becomes clonable
cases.why: created_from_pr? ignores in_active PR mappings, and withdrawal sets them in_active. So the 'PR events cannot be cloned' rule stops applying after withdrawal. The code comment says this is intended; the clone carries no PR link.
cases.setup: Needs a PR-created event that is then withdrawn.
cases.steps: Withdraw it; clone it.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; the clone has no PurchaseRequestTradeMapping; PR quantities are not consumed twice.
cases.oracle: PR open quantity unchanged by the clone.

cases.title: Two quick clones make two drafts, each pointing back to the source
cases.why: There is no lock; a double click creates two drafts. Each must be complete and independently linked to the source.
cases.setup: Manual double-submit on the screen or two parallel API calls.
cases.steps: Clone twice within a second.
cases.expected: Two drafts, both complete, both with meta_data.source_event_group_id = source; source meta_data unchanged.
cases.oracle: Two clones; no partial one.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: Transferring to an undecodable user id is refused
cases.why: WrongUuid1= decodes to nil; find_by(id: nil) must not match anything.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer, who created (owns) the sandbox.
cases.steps: Transfer to WrongUuid1=. `POST …/change_ownership` with `{"new_owner_uuid": "WrongUuid1="}`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: Transferring to null is refused
cases.why: A cleared select box sends null; it must be the same refusal as a missing field.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer, who created (owns) the sandbox.
cases.steps: Transfer to null. `POST …/change_ownership` with `{"new_owner_uuid": null}`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: A raw numeric user id bypasses uuid decoding and is looked up directly
cases.why: new_owner_id is read straight from params, so a client can skip uuids and pass internal ids. A nonexistent one must still be refused; the case also documents that raw ids are accepted at all.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer, who created (owns) the sandbox.
cases.steps: Transfer to raw id 999999999. `POST …/change_ownership` with `{"new_owner_id": 999999999}`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: A list where one uuid is expected is decoded leniently (here: yourself) and refused
cases.why: decode_data stringifies whatever it gets and Base64-decodes leniently, so ["<uuid>"] decodes like "<uuid>". With the caller's own uuid this lands on the self-transfer refusal; it documents that wrong types are not rejected.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer, who created (owns) the sandbox.
cases.steps: Transfer to a one-element list holding your own uuid. `POST …/change_ownership` with `{"new_owner_uuid": ["{{buyerUserUuid}}"]}`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (either decoded to yourself, or to nothing).
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: Changing the owner of a project that does not exist answers 'Project does not exist.'
cases.why: The lookup is scoped to the workspace and runs before the policy.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer, who created (owns) the sandbox.
cases.steps: Transfer the bogus project. `POST /event_groups/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/change_ownership` with `{"new_owner_uuid": "{{buyerUserUuid}}"}`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 533 'Project does not exist.'.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: Owner change cannot be triggered with GET
cases.why: Only POST is routed.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer, who created (owns) the sandbox.
cases.steps: GET the change-owner URL. `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/change_ownership`
cases.expected: HTTP 404 (no route).
cases.oracle: Non-2xx, not 5xx.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: The new-owner picker for a project that does not exist answers 'Project does not exist.'
cases.why: Scoped lookup before policy, same as the transfer itself.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer, who created (owns) the sandbox.
cases.steps: Ask for eligible owners of the bogus project. `GET /event_groups/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/team_buyers`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 533 'Project does not exist.'.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: Both owners are emailed after a transfer
cases.why: The new owner must learn they own the event; the previous owner must learn they lost it.
cases.setup: Needs two QA buyers with QA mailboxes (example.com addresses are not delivered); manual.
cases.steps: Transfer and check both inboxes.
cases.expected: New owner: 'event assigned'; previous owner: 'event unassigned' naming the new owner. Nobody else.
cases.oracle: Two emails.

cases.section: Changing the owner — POST /event_groups/:id/change_ownership and GET …/team_buyers
cases.title: Two simultaneous transfers leave exactly one owner
cases.why: There is no lock; two concurrent transfers can each deactivate 'the' owner row and create a new one, leaving two active owner rows. EventGroup#user then picks whichever comes first.
cases.setup: Needs two parallel requests to two different QA team-mates.
cases.steps: Fire both transfers at the same moment; read AccessList owner rows.
cases.expected: Exactly one active owner row.
cases.oracle: Count of active owner rows.

cases.section: Who sees which events — visibility per role and team
cases.title: A user without sourcing access gets empty lists, not an error
cases.why: Users of other modules land on the events screen by deep link.
cases.setup: A console user without sourcing-events access.
cases.steps: GET /event_groups and /history.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with no events (or 455 where policy applies); never another user's events.
cases.oracle: Empty lists.

cases.section: Who sees which events — visibility per role and team
cases.title: Old events beyond the user's history window are hidden
cases.why: Users can be limited to recent history (starting_date_for_historical_data); an earlier start date is clamped.
cases.setup: A user with a historical-data start date after some closed events.
cases.steps: GET history with starting_from before that date.
cases.expected: Events closed before the user's start date are not listed.
cases.oracle: Oldest card's date ≥ the user's start date.

cases.section: GET /orders is the purchase-order list, not the events list
cases.title: The PO list answers with orders and its counters
cases.why: Baseline for the shared /orders read used by several platform checks.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The user may read POs.
cases.steps: Ask for the PO list. `GET /orders`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 {data, total_pages, number_of_purchase_orders, number_of_success_po, …}; all orders belong to PROCOL DEMO.
cases.oracle: Keys present.

cases.section: GET /orders is the purchase-order list, not the events list
cases.title: A product filter with non-numeric ids crashes the PO list
cases.why: The product scope casts JSON to bigint in SQL and compares with the raw values; text makes Postgres fail.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The user may read POs.
cases.steps: Filter POs by product_ids ["abc"]. `GET /orders?filters=%7B%22product_ids%22%3A%5B%22abc%22%5D%7D`
cases.expected: Should answer 200 (no match) or 422. Expected today: `(order_items.product->>'id')::bigint in ('abc')` → Postgres invalid input for bigint → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.section: GET /orders is the purchase-order list, not the events list
cases.title: A location filter with non-numeric ids crashes the PO list
cases.why: Same SQL cast in the buyer_hub scope.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The user may read POs.
cases.steps: Filter POs by buyer_hub_ids ["abc"]. `GET /orders?filters=%7B%22buyer_hub_ids%22%3A%5B%22abc%22%5D%7D`
cases.expected: Should answer 200 or 422. Expected today: HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Status is not 5xx.

cases.section: GET /orders is the purchase-order list, not the events list
cases.title: Searching POs for '%' returns every PO
cases.why: The PO search (invoice no, PO number, vendor name) has the same unescaped-wildcard behaviour as the events search.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The user may read POs.
cases.steps: Search POs for '%'. `GET /orders?query=%25`
cases.expected: Should match only literal '%'. Today: every PO (count equals the baseline).
cases.oracle: number_of_purchase_orders equals the baseline.

cases.section: GET /orders is the purchase-order list, not the events list
cases.title: A negative page number is treated as page 1
cases.why: Pagination input from the client must be clamped, not passed to OFFSET.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The user may read POs.
cases.steps: Ask for page -5. `GET /orders?page=-5`
cases.expected: HTTP 200, same first page as the baseline.
cases.oracle: Same data as baseline.

cases.section: GET /orders is the purchase-order list, not the events list
cases.title: A created-at range made of text returns nothing instead of crashing
cases.why: created_at from/to are converted with to_i; text becomes 1970-01-01 for both ends.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO. The user may read POs.
cases.steps: Filter POs created between 'abc' and 'xyz'. `GET /orders?filters=%7B%22created_at%22%3A%7B%22from%22%3A%22abc%22%2C%22to%22%3A%22xyz%22%7D%7D`
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with no orders.
cases.oracle: Empty data.

cases.section: Finding events for purchase-request items — POST /event_groups/search
cases.title: Searching without PR items is refused
cases.why: The search is defined by the PR items; without them there is nothing to match.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Search with an empty body. `POST /event_groups/search` with `{}`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Finding events for purchase-request items — POST /event_groups/search
cases.title: PR items sent as text instead of a list are refused
cases.why: The guard checks the type explicitly; text must be refused, not split or crashed on.
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Search with purchase_request_item_ids "abc". `POST /event_groups/search` with `{"purchase_request_item_ids": "abc"}`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 + code 2.

cases.section: Finding events for purchase-request items — POST /event_groups/search
cases.title: Unknown PR items are refused — with a misleading message
cases.why: When none of the items exist, the code answers 834 whose text is 'Purchase request item has no product' — the user is told the item lacks a product when it does not exist (or belongs to another company).
cases.setup: Signed in as the run's buyer on PROCOL DEMO.
cases.steps: Search with a bogus PR item uuid. `POST /event_groups/search` with `{"purchase_request_item_uuids": ["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="]}`
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 834 'Purchase request item has no product' (a 'not found' message would be correct).

journeys.title: Talking to vendors during an event: clarifications, documents and reminders
journeys.goal: Vendors ask questions and the buyer answers them, documents are attached and read by the right people only, and reminders reach the vendors who still have to act — all while the event is live.

cases.title: A URL pasted as a link is stored with no validation
cases.why: The "upload from URLs" path builds an attachment straight from the text, with no host or scheme check; it becomes the file's `url` and `publicUrl`.
cases.setup: The multiple-attachments control.
cases.steps: Paste `https://files.example.com/x.pdf` (or a `javascript:` string) into the URL box and add it.
cases.expected: The link is added as a file with its name taken from the URL and no check. The server-side gap this feeds is API-EVDDOC-049/050.
cases.oracle: The link object is pushed into `attachments` directly in `uploadLinks`.

cases.title: The drawer shows one card per kind with something pending, with a count
cases.why: The first screen is the overview; empty kinds must not show.
cases.setup: Live RFQ with QA vendor 1 pending (API-EVDREM-001).
cases.steps: Open Send Reminders.
cases.expected: Title "Send Reminders", subtitle "Streamline Follow-ups on Pending Actions"; a single card "Offer submissions" with "1 Pending" and "View".
cases.oracle: Card list equals the non-empty kinds of the list reply.

cases.title: A vendor reminded in the last 10 minutes cannot be selected
cases.why: This greyed checkbox is the ONLY anti-spam guard (the API does not enforce it, API-EVDREM-038).
cases.setup: Right after sending vendor 1 a reminder.
cases.steps: Reopen the drawer → Offer submissions → View; hover the checkbox; tick the header checkbox.
cases.expected: Vendor 1's checkbox is disabled with the tooltip "Retry in 10 mins"; "Last Reminded At" shows the time; select-all selects only remindable rows (none here).
cases.oracle: Disabled checkbox + tooltip; header checkbox selects nothing.

cases.title: A successful send confirms with the right count and noun, closes the drawer and refreshes the list
cases.why: The buyer needs to know who was reminded; the wording uses "Vendor/Vendors", "Evaluator", "Approver" by kind.
cases.setup: Live RFQ, QA vendor 1 pending. Sends a real reminder to QA vendor 1.
cases.steps: Select vendor 1 → Send Reminder.
cases.expected: Toast "Reminders Sent to 1 Vendor"; drawer closes; reopening shows vendor 1 locked. (Two vendors → "2 Vendors"; evaluations → "1 Evaluator".)
cases.oracle: Toast text; request body `{"resource_type": "event_group", "reminder_type": "offer_submissions", "reminders": {"<vendor uuid>": ["<round uuid>"]}}`.

cases.title: The attachment uploader enforces a 20 MB limit the server does not
cases.why: The only size limit a user meets lives in the screen; a different client has none (see API-EVDDOC-020).
cases.setup: The event create / order screen's multiple-attachments control.
cases.steps: Drag a file larger than 20 MB onto the uploader.
cases.expected: The row shows "File size too large" and the file is not uploaded.
cases.oracle: `MAX_FILE_SIZE = 20` and the `fileSize > MAX_FILE_SIZE * 1024 * 1024` guard.

cases.title: The uploader caps the count at 15 files
cases.why: The product limit on attachments per block.
cases.setup: The multiple-attachments control with 15 files already added.
cases.steps: Add a 16th file, or paste 16 links at once.
cases.expected: "You can't upload more than 15 attachments"; the extra files/links are dropped.
cases.oracle: `MAX_NO_OF_ATTACHMENTS = 15` and the two count guards.

cases.title: A failed upload surfaces the server's message
cases.why: The `catch` parses `err` as JSON and reads `error.message`; a non-JSON error throws inside the catch and the row shows nothing useful.
cases.setup: The multiple-attachments control; force an upload failure (e.g. an unsupported type the server refuses with 484).
cases.steps: Upload a `.exe`.
cases.expected: The row shows the server message ("File type not allowed"); if the error body is not JSON the handler itself throws.
cases.oracle: `JSON.parse(err).error.message` in the catch.

cases.title: The RFI builder's image picker accepts types the server refuses
cases.why: The picker allows any `image/*` plus a fixed list, so .gif/.webp/.bmp reach the server and come back "Upload failed" (API-EVDDOC-028) with no hint why.
cases.setup: The RFI / technical template builder, a field with an image.
cases.steps: Pick a `.gif`.
cases.expected: The client accepts it (`file.type.startsWith("image/")`), uploads, and shows a generic "Upload failed!" from the 484.
cases.oracle: `ACCEPTED_FILE_TYPES = "image/*,.pdf,.xls,.xlsx,.csv,.doc,.docx"` and `isValidFileType`.

cases.title: The Reports panel is shown only when bulk report download is enabled
cases.why: The whole panel (and this endpoint call) is gated by a company setting.
cases.setup: The event details page.
cases.steps: Open an event in a company with `allow_bulk_report_download` off, then on.
cases.expected: Off: no Reports panel, no `get_all_attachments` call. On: the panel loads the list.
cases.oracle: `show_reports_table` from the event config drives `{showReportsTable && (<Panel …>)}`.

cases.title: The Reports table filters by name and maps each row to a download
cases.why: The list's `name`, `item_type`, `report_category`, `report_type`, `item_uuid`, `lot_no` feed the download action; a missing field breaks that row's download.
cases.setup: The Reports panel with several reports.
cases.steps: Type in the search box; click Download on a row.
cases.expected: The table filters case-insensitively by name; Download sends the mapped params to the report export.
cases.oracle: `selectProjectReportsTableData` mapping and `handleDownloadReport`.

cases.title: A draft event's empty Reports response must not break the panel
cases.why: The endpoint answers 204 with no body for a draft (API-EVDDOC-069); the selector must treat that as an empty list, not crash.
cases.setup: A draft event with the Reports panel enabled.
cases.steps: Open the panel on a draft.
cases.expected: An empty table, no error; the count tag shows 0.
cases.oracle: `selectProjectReportsTableData` returns `[]` when `reports.data` is not an array.

cases.title: Event-level attachments round-trip through the create screen
cases.why: The create screen reads back `attachments` as `{name, url, publicUrl}`; a malformed stored attachment (API-EVDDOC-046) would break this map.
cases.setup: An event with one event-level attachment, reopened for edit.
cases.steps: Open the event in the create flow.
cases.expected: The attachment shows with its name and links; T&C attachments are read from `terms_and_conditions.attachments` where `type === "t_and_c"` and `value` is a list.
cases.oracle: The two `.map` blocks over `attachments` and `terms_and_conditions.attachments`.

cases.section: Screens — the Messages drawer in the buyer console
cases.title: The Messages button appears only on live events of companies that enabled it
cases.why: The button is the only way into queries; it is gated by the company setting `show_communication_module` and hidden on drafts.
cases.setup: A live and a draft event in a company with `show_communication_module` ON; a company with it OFF.
cases.steps: Open each event's detail page.
cases.expected: Live event, setting ON: "Messages" button visible. Draft: hidden. Setting OFF: hidden everywhere.
cases.oracle: Button presence per case.

cases.section: Screens — the Messages drawer in the buyer console
cases.title: The badge shows open threads and refreshes every 30 seconds
cases.why: Buyers rely on the badge to notice new vendor questions without reopening the drawer.
cases.setup: A live QA event; QA vendor 1 raises a general query while the buyer has the page open.
cases.steps: Keep the event page open for up to 40 seconds.
cases.expected: A dot appears when there is any thread; the number tag shows the unresolved count and updates within one 30-second poll.
cases.oracle: Tag text equals `unresolved_threads_count` from the count call.

cases.section: Screens — the Messages drawer in the buyer console
cases.title: New Message form refuses incomplete queries; planners can only ask technical ones
cases.why: The form is the buyer's validation layer (the API has almost none, see cases 024/027).
cases.setup: A live QA event; a normal buyer and a planner-team user.
cases.steps: Click "Message" and try: no vendor; no "Message Regarding"; technical without a line item; blank text and no file. Repeat as a planner.
cases.expected: Each missing field is outlined red and nothing is sent. Planner: "Message Regarding" is locked to the first option and the request is sent as technical.
cases.oracle: No create request in the network log until all required fields are filled.

cases.section: Screens — the Messages drawer in the buyer console
cases.title: After award the "Message" button is disabled when blocking is enabled
cases.why: The setting `enable_block_message` is meant to stop new queries once the award is decided; the screen enforces it, the API does not (case 031).
cases.setup: Company with `enable_block_message` ON; an event with a submitted proposal.
cases.steps: Open the Messages drawer.
cases.expected: The "Message" button is disabled; existing threads still open.
cases.oracle: Button disabled ↔ event `block_new_message: true`.

cases.section: Screens — the Messages drawer in the buyer console
cases.title: Resolve and reply controls follow the assignment
cases.why: Only the assignee sees "Mark as Resolve"; once resolved the reply box and the assignee picker are disabled with "You can't reply to a resolved message". The assignee picker is shown only when the thread went to a single vendor.
cases.setup: A thread assigned to the owner (single vendor) and a thread sent to two vendors.
cases.steps: Open each as the owner and as a team-mate; resolve one as the owner.
cases.expected: Owner sees "Mark as Resolve", team-mate does not; after resolving, "Closed by <name>" shows and the reply box is disabled; the two-vendor thread shows no assignee picker in the message view.
cases.oracle: Controls per user/state as described.

cases.section: Screens — the Messages drawer in the buyer console
cases.title: The comparison sheet flags vendors with open queries
cases.why: The per-vendor badge lets the buyer clear doubts before awarding; it is skipped when the round hides bidding stats or the module is off.
cases.setup: A live RFQ with a QA vendor bid and an open query from that vendor; a second round with `trade_config.show_bidding_stats` on.
cases.steps: Open each round's comparison sheet.
cases.expected: Round 1: the vendor's column header shows a message badge with the count; clicking it opens the Messages drawer. Round 2: no badge and no count request.
cases.oracle: Badge number equals `unresolved_query_count` for that company.

cases.section: Screens — the Messages drawer in the buyer console
cases.title: A deep link opens the drawer straight on a thread
cases.why: E-mails and notifications link to `?msgVisible=true&id=<thread>&idType=thread`; the drawer must open on that thread and closing it must clear the link parameters.
cases.setup: A live QA event with a thread.
cases.steps: Open the event URL with `?msgVisible=true&id=<thread uuid>&idType=thread`; then close the drawer.
cases.expected: The drawer opens on "Messages Details" for that thread; closing removes `msgVisible`, `id`, `idType` and `q` from the URL.
cases.oracle: URL parameters after close.

cases.title: "Send Reminders" is not offered on a draft event
cases.why: Drafts have no vendors to chase; the option is removed from the event's ⋮ menu.
cases.setup: A draft event of the QA buyer.
cases.steps: Open the event; open the ⋮ options menu.
cases.expected: The menu has no "Send Reminders" entry; on a live event it does.
cases.oracle: Menu items for draft vs live.

cases.title: "Send Reminders" is offered to users who are not allowed to send
cases.why: The menu only checks "not a draft"; a read-only buyer opens the drawer, selects vendors and only learns at the end that they are not authorised.
cases.setup: A read-only buyer on the event's team.
cases.steps: Open the live event → ⋮ → Send Reminders → pick a kind → select a vendor → Send Reminder.
cases.expected: Should hide the option (or disable Send) for users without create permission. Today: the drawer works until Send, which fails with "You are not authorized to perform this action".
cases.oracle: Error toast after Send; no reminder sent.

cases.title: With nothing pending the drawer shows an empty state
cases.why: Closed, withdrawn or fully-bid events answer an empty list; the user must see a clear message, not a blank panel.
cases.setup: Live RFQ where every invited vendor has bid, or a closed event.
cases.steps: Open Send Reminders.
cases.expected: Illustration and "No Pending Actions to Remind"; no Send / Cancel buttons.
cases.oracle: Empty-state text present; footer buttons absent.

cases.title: The recipient table shows the columns the server chose for that kind
cases.why: Vendors show what they owe ("Bid Pending For"); evaluators and approvers show only name and last reminded.
cases.setup: Live RFQ with QA vendor 1 pending.
cases.steps: Open "Offer submissions" → View.
cases.expected: Header "Offer submission Reminders" / "Notify vendors to complete bid submissions"; columns: checkbox, Vendor Name, Bid Pending For (round title as a tag), Last Reminded At ("-" when never).
cases.oracle: Column headers and first row.

cases.title: Send Reminder stays disabled until someone is selected
cases.why: Prevents empty sends (which the API would otherwise "succeed" with 0 recipients, API-EVDREM-061).
cases.setup: Drawer on the Offer submissions table.
cases.steps: Look at the Send Reminder button; tick vendor 1; untick.
cases.expected: Disabled with no selection, enabled with one, disabled again after untick.
cases.oracle: Button state.

cases.title: When the server answers an error inside a 200, the drawer neither confirms nor explains
cases.why: The success handler reads `type` and `recipients_count` from the reply; `{error: true, code: 533}` has neither, so building the toast fails on an undefined kind — the user sees no confirmation and no error, and the drawer stays open.
cases.setup: Open the drawer on a live event, then withdraw the event in another tab (or let an auction reminder hit API-EVDREM-055's path).
cases.steps: Select a vendor → Send Reminder.
cases.expected: Should show a clear error ("event is no longer live"). Today: no "Reminders Sent" confirmation; the success handler throws a TypeError reading `stakeholder` of undefined, so the close-and-refresh step never runs and the drawer stays open (whether any generic error toast appears depends on the app's global mutation error handler — note what is shown).
cases.oracle: Reply `{"error": true, "code": 533}` with HTTP 200; no success toast; drawer still open.

cases.title: Auction reminder cards are split by lot and carry the lot title
cases.why: With several lots the buyer must know which auction they are chasing.
cases.setup: A lot-split auction event, both lots not yet started.
cases.steps: Open Send Reminders; open one auction card.
cases.expected: One card per lot titled "Auction reminders - <lot title>"; the table header "Auction reminders - <lot title> Reminders".
cases.oracle: Two cards, each with its lot's vendors.

cases.title: The approvals card's subtitle says "Notify vendors to approvals"
cases.why: Approvals go to internal approvers, not vendors; the wording is wrong and ungrammatical.
cases.setup: An event with a pending approval.
cases.steps: Open Send Reminders → Approvals → View.
cases.expected: Should read like "Notify approvers to complete their approvals". Today: "Notify vendors to approvals".
cases.oracle: Subtitle text.

cases.title: Back and Cancel reset the selection
cases.why: A selection carried from one kind to another would send the wrong people.
cases.setup: Drawer with at least one card.
cases.steps: View a card → tick vendor 1 → Back → open the same card again; then tick → Cancel → reopen.
cases.expected: After Back the card list returns and the reopened table has nothing ticked; Cancel closes the drawer and reopening starts on the card list.
cases.oracle: No ticked rows after Back/Cancel.

cases.title: Scheduled-template events have no options menu, so no reminders
cases.why: The whole ⋮ menu (including Send Reminders) is hidden for scheduled templates; confirm that is intended.
cases.setup: An event opened as a scheduled template.
cases.steps: Open the event header.
cases.expected: No ⋮ options menu.
cases.oracle: Menu absent.

cases.section: Event-level attachments and the company-folder check — `PATCH /event_groups/:id`
cases.title: Attachments sent as plain links break the event page
cases.why: The reader assumes each attachment is an object; a plain-text item makes every read of the event fail.
cases.setup: The run's own draft event with one RFQ round.
cases.steps: 1. Publish with `attachments: ["https://files.example.com/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf"]` (text, not objects). 2. Read the event back as the buyer.
cases.expected: Should be refused (422: each attachment must be an object with a url). Today the check skips text items, the list is saved, and building the reply calls `['public_url'] = …` on a String → IndexError → HTTP 500; every later GET of the event then fails the same way for buyer and vendors.
cases.oracle: The verify read-back of the event must answer 2xx; a 500 is the defect.

cases.title: A T&C attachment with a text value makes the round page unreadable
cases.why: The reader assumes `value` is a list; a text value makes every read of the round fail for buyer and vendors.
cases.setup: The run's own live RFQ round, no bids.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `attachments: [{type: t_and_c, value: "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf"}]` (value as text). 2. Read the round as the buyer and as QA vendor 1.
cases.expected: The update answers 200 (its reply omits attachments). Should be refused (422). Today the value is saved and every later read calls `value.each` on a String → NoMethodError → HTTP 500 for everyone.
cases.oracle: Both verify read-backs must answer 2xx; a 500 is the defect.

cases.section: The query list on an event — `GET /v1/chats`
cases.title: The buyer opens the Messages list on a live event
cases.why: This is the first call the Messages drawer makes; if it fails the buyer cannot see any vendor query on the event.
cases.setup: A published RFQ (QA vendor 1 invited, no queries yet). Read only.
cases.steps: As the event's buyer, `GET /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}&group_by=thread_id`.
cases.expected: The list opens and is empty (no thread has been raised on a fresh event). HTTP 200 with `[]`.
cases.oracle: 200 and an empty array; never 4xx/5xx for the event's own buyer.

cases.section: The query list on an event — `GET /v1/chats`
cases.title: The list of event 12 also shows queries from events 120–129, 1200–1299 …
cases.why: The list and the "total" count match chats with `context_identifier ILIKE 'EG_<id>%'`. Event ids are global, so the pattern for event 12 also matches `EG_120…`, `EG_1234…` of any company. A buyer or vendor sees their own queries from unrelated events mixed into this event; a user for whom `show_all_chats` is on (an NFA approver of a submitted proposal, a Procol employee) sees EVERY chat of those events — other companies' vendor queries included. A matched chat whose event is not active/withdrawn can also crash the thread view (`chats.first.event_group.id` in the log line).
cases.setup: Needs two events whose ids share a prefix (e.g. ids N and N·10+k) with a query on the longer one, and a user who can see both (or an NFA approver of the shorter one). Ids cannot be chosen on UAT, so manual: find such a pair read-only in the database (`SELECT id FROM event_groups WHERE id::text LIKE '<N>%'`).
cases.steps: 1. Raise a query on the longer-id event (QA vendor + QA buyer only). 2. As the NFA approver / Procol support login of the shorter-id event, `GET /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=<short event uuid>&group_by=thread_id`. 3. Read `GET /v1/chats/get_chats_count_data` for the same event.
cases.expected: Only chats of the requested event (`context_identifier = 'EG_<id>'` or starting with `'EG_<id>_'`). Today the other event's thread is listed and counted.
cases.oracle: A thread whose `line_items` / title belong to a different event appears; `total_threads_count` is larger than the number of threads actually on the event.

cases.title: A vendor raises a general query on a live event
cases.why: The core flow: a vendor asks the buyer a question. The vendor screen sends no recipients, so the code addresses the buyer company itself, assigns the thread to the event owner and e-mails the unmuted participants.
cases.setup: A published RFQ with QA vendor 1 invited; QA buyer as owner. Manual: creating the chat e-mails the owner and pushes to every participant, including the owner's purchase-team colleagues.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `POST /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=:id` with `{"context": "general", "message_body": "QA_Platform_query_<stamp>"}`. Then, as the buyer, open the list.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with the chat (title "General Query", `body.message` = the text, `assignment_status: "active"`, `assigned_to` = the owner). Participants: the owner and his purchase-team members (team members muted), the event's RFP evaluators, and every user of QA vendor 1's company. The owner gets one "query raised" e-mail; muted team-mates get none.
cases.oracle: Buyer list shows one thread from QA vendor 1; `get_chats_count_data` total 1, unresolved 1.

cases.title: A vendor can open a thread with a competing vendor
cases.why: Recipients are taken as given. When a vendor names another company in `message_to_uuids`, that company becomes a participant (all its users), sees the first vendor's question and identity, and is e-mailed. Nothing checks that a vendor may only write to the buyer, or that the recipient is invited.
cases.setup: A live event with QA vendors 1 and 2 invited (use only QA vendors). Manual (writes, e-mails QA vendor 2).
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `POST /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=:id` with `{"context": "general", "message_to_uuids": [":vendor2CompanyUuid"], "message_body": "QA_Platform_x_<stamp>"}`. Then, as QA vendor 2, list the event's threads.
cases.expected: Should be refused (422 455). Today: 200; QA vendor 2 sees QA vendor 1's question and company name.
cases.oracle: QA vendor 2's list contains the thread; participants include both vendor companies.

cases.title: A vendor can reassign the buyer's query — even to itself — and then close it
cases.why: `assign` and `close` only check `ChatPolicy#show?` (any participant) and that the new assignee is a participant. Vendor users are participants, so a vendor can move a buyer's query to another buyer colleague or to itself, then mark it resolved, hiding it from the buyer's unresolved count. The assignee picker only offers the caller's own company, but the API does not enforce that.
cases.setup: A general thread raised by QA vendor 1 on a QA event. Manual.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, `POST /v1/chats/assign?thread_id=:threadUuid&assign_to_uuid=:vendorUserUuid`. 2. `POST /v1/chats/close?thread_id=:threadUuid`.
cases.expected: Both should be 455. Today both 200; the buyer sees the thread "closed by" the vendor and the unresolved badge drops.
cases.oracle: `assigned_to` is a vendor user; `get_chats_count_data` unresolved decreases.

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: A vendor can read the list of competing vendors invited to the event
cases.why: The vendor screen never needs recipients (the code comment says so), yet the participant picker and the "Vendor" filter answer a vendor with every invited vendor's name, vendor code and city — the competitor list of a sealed RFQ.
cases.setup: A live RFQ with QA vendors 1 and 2 invited. Manual (needs vendor 2 invited; the shared direct-runner event invites only vendor 1).
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `GET /v1/chats/get_possible_participants?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=:id` and `GET /v1/chats/filter_options?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=:id`.
cases.expected: Should be refused (455) or limited to the vendor itself. Today 200 listing QA vendor 2 with its vendor code and city.
cases.oracle: QA vendor 2 present in a vendor's answer.

cases.section: Per-vendor unresolved counts on the comparison sheet — `GET /v1/chats/get_unresolved_queries_count`
cases.title: Per-vendor counts have no permission check at all
cases.why: The action never calls `authorize`. Any signed-in user — another company's buyer, or a vendor invited to the round — gets, for that round, the company uuid of every vendor who has submitted a bid AND has an open query, with the count. For a vendor that reveals which competitors bid. It also accepts a raw numeric `event_id`, which makes enumeration trivial.
cases.setup: A live RFQ with QA vendors 1 and 2 bidding and an open query from QA vendor 2 (QA records only; never probe other companies' ids). Manual.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `GET /v1/chats/get_unresolved_queries_count?event_uuid=:roundUuid`.
cases.expected: Should be 455 for anyone who cannot manage the round. Today 200 with `{"<vendor 2 company uuid>": {"unresolved_query_count": 1}}`.
cases.oracle: QA vendor 2's company uuid in a vendor's answer.

cases.section: The pending list per event state — `GET /reminders/:id?resource_type=event_group`
cases.title: A live RFQ with no bids lists the invited vendor under "Offer submissions"
cases.why: This is the drawer's main use: chase vendors who have not quoted while bidding is still open. If the list is empty here, the feature is dead.
cases.setup: A published RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited, bidding open, no bids (recipe `published_rfq`). Read only.
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}?resource_type=event_group` as the event's buyer.
cases.expected: The list answers with one entry per reminder kind. "Offer submissions" holds exactly one vendor — QA vendor 1 — with the RFQ round's title under "Bid Pending For", no last-reminded time, and remindable. Kinds with nobody pending (pending evaluations, counter offers, best offer, cost breakdown, auction reminders) come back empty (null). HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: 200; `offer_submissions.total_count` = 1; `offer_submissions.recipients[0]` has `recipient_uuid` = QA vendor 1's company uuid, `uuids` = [the RFQ round's uuid], `bid_pending_for` = [round title], `last_reminded_at` null, `can_remind` true; `offer_submissions.columns` = Vendor Name / Bid Pending For / Last Reminded At; `pending_evaluations`, `counter_offers`, `best_offer_submissions`, `cost_break_down_submissions`, `auction_reminders` null. `approvals` is null unless the company has a pending approval on this event.

cases.section: Sending a reminder — happy paths and read-backs (all manual: they email)
cases.title: Sending an offer-submission reminder to QA vendor 1
cases.why: The core action: the vendor gets an email asking them to submit before the deadline, and the buyer gets a confirmation.
cases.setup: Live RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited, no bid; list read first (API-EVDREM-001). Manual: writes a reminder row and emails the QA vendor's users.
cases.steps: `POST /reminders/:eventUuid/send_reminder` with `{"resource_type": "event_group", "reminder_type": "offer_submissions", "reminders": {"<vendor 1 company uuid>": ["<RFQ round uuid>"]}}` (exactly what the drawer sends).
cases.expected: HTTP 200 `{"success": true, "message": "Reminders sent successfully.", "recipients_count": 1, "type": "offer_submissions"}`. QA vendor 1's users get an email titled "[<event ref>] [Reminder] Submit Your Offer Before the Deadline." naming the round and its end time.
cases.oracle: Response as above; one `reminders` row (category `OfferSubmission`, recipient `c-<vendor 1 id>`, `reminder_type` manual, channel email); the QA vendor mailbox.

cases.section: What the send does not check (suspected defects, all manual)
cases.title: Rounds from a different event are accepted in the reminder map
cases.why: The round ids are looked up across the whole database (`TradeRequest.where(id: …)`), never limited to this event. A buyer can send, from their own event, an email that carries another event's round title and end time — including another company's.
cases.setup: Two QA-buyer events A and B, QA vendor 1 invited to A. Manual (emails). Use only the QA buyer's own events.
cases.steps: On event A, send `offer_submissions` with `{"<vendor 1 uuid>": ["<round uuid of event B>"]}`.
cases.expected: Should be refused (round not part of this event). Today: 200 success; vendor 1 gets a reminder for event A whose body names event B's round and end time.
cases.oracle: Email content shows B's round title; reminder row on A.

cases.section: What the send does not check (suspected defects, all manual)
cases.title: A vendor who is not invited still gets the reminder
cases.why: The recipient companies are never checked against the event's invitations, so any company id can be mailed details of the event (reference, round title, end time).
cases.setup: Live RFQ with QA vendor 1 invited; QA vendor 2 NOT invited. Manual (emails QA vendor 2).
cases.steps: Send `offer_submissions` with `{"<vendor 2 company uuid>": ["<RFQ round uuid>"]}`.
cases.expected: Should be refused (vendor not on the event). Today: 200 and QA vendor 2's users receive the reminder.
cases.oracle: QA vendor 2 mailbox; reminder row `c-<vendor 2 id>`.

cases.title: A buyer uploads a small T&C document
cases.why: Every attachment on an event is first uploaded through this call; the baseline for all refusals below.
cases.setup: Signed in as the QA buyer. No event. Stores one private 2-byte object.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with `{"name": "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf", "data": "UUE=", "type": "t_and_c"}`.
cases.expected: The file is stored privately under the company's T&C folder; the reply returns the cleaned name, the private storage link and a 2-hour viewing link. HTTP 200, `success: true`, message 'Successfully uploaded File'.
cases.oracle: 200; `url` contains `trade_files/terms_and_conditions/<company>_<id>/`; `public_url` is a signed link.

cases.title: An unknown document type is refused
cases.why: Only `t_and_c` and `product_sheet` map to a folder; any other value must not invent one.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with type `invoice` and a valid name and data.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: An executable is refused
cases.why: Whatever is stored here is later handed to vendors as a signed download link, so the allow-list must hold.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with name `QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.exe`.
cases.expected: Refused, nothing stored. HTTP 422, code 484 'File type not allowed'.

cases.title: An HTML page is refused
cases.why: An HTML file served from Procol storage would run script in whoever opens it.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with name `QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.html`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 484 'File type not allowed'.

cases.title: An SVG image is refused
cases.why: SVG can carry script just like HTML, so it is kept off the list.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with name `QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.svg`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 484 'File type not allowed'.

cases.title: "file.pdf.exe" is judged by its last extension
cases.why: Only the final extension may count.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with name `QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf.exe`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 484 'File type not allowed'.

cases.title: A path in the file name never leaves the company folder
cases.why: `../../` in a name must not move the object into another folder.
cases.setup: QA buyer. Manual: a successful upload stores a file and the runner cannot read the reply name.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with name `../../QA_Platform_x.pdf`.
cases.expected: Stored inside the own company folder; slashes become `_` (name comes back `.._.._QA_Platform_x.pdf`). HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: The returned `url` has the expected folder depth and the own company id.

cases.title: An executable as a template image is refused
cases.why: Template images are shown to every vendor answering the template, so the same allow-list applies.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /templates/upload_attachment` with name `QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.exe`, data `UUE=`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 484 'File type not allowed'.

cases.title: The image link saved in a template question can expire after two hours
cases.why: The reply carries only a signed link (no private storage link) and the builder saves that link into the question; the round reader treats a CDN-signed link as a user link and never re-signs it.
cases.setup: A template with an image question; company uses CDN signing (`USE_CLOUDFRONT_SIGNING` not 'false'). Manual (needs time).
cases.steps: 1. Upload an image in the RFI builder and save the question. 2. Open the round as a vendor more than 2 hours later.
cases.expected: The image fails to load (expired signature). Should store the private link and sign on every read.
cases.oracle: The stored `fileUrl` is a signed link; after 7200 s it answers 403.

cases.section: Opening a stored file by link — `GET /v1/attachments/open`
cases.title: A link with no token must not crash
cases.why: A truncated link from an email or a report PDF must give a clean message.
cases.setup: No event.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/attachments/open`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 'Invalid token'. Today decoding `nil` calls `nil.end_with?` → NoMethodError, not rescued → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any non-5xx passes; a 500 is the defect.

cases.section: Opening a stored file by link — `GET /v1/attachments/open`
cases.title: A well-formed but fake token is refused
cases.why: The token is the only lock; anything that is not a genuine token must be refused cleanly.
cases.setup: No event.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/attachments/open?token=UUFfUGxhdGZvcm0` (base64 of "QA_Platform").
cases.expected: HTTP 422, plain text 'Invalid token'. The app sets no `load_defaults`, so the encryptor is AES-256-CBC with a signature check that raises InvalidSignature (rescued). A 500 would mean an authenticated cipher or a missing secret — neither is rescued, so that too is a defect.
cases.oracle: 422, never a redirect, never 500.

cases.section: Opening a stored file by link — `GET /v1/attachments/open`
cases.title: A token with a made-up signature is refused
cases.why: Confirms a hand-built "message--signature" never opens a file.
cases.setup: No event.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/attachments/open?token=UUFfUGxhdGZvcm0tLTAwMDA` (base64 of "QA_Platform--0000").
cases.expected: HTTP 422, plain text 'Invalid token'.
cases.oracle: 422, no `Location` header.

cases.section: Opening a stored file by link — `GET /v1/attachments/open`
cases.title: A file link never expires and cannot be revoked
cases.why: Tokens are encrypted without an expiry and the endpoint needs no sign-in, so a forwarded link opens the file indefinitely, even after the event is withdrawn or the user leaves.
cases.setup: Company with `attachment_token_url_enabled` ON; a round with a T&C file. Manual.
cases.steps: 1. As a vendor, copy the T&C link (…/api/v1/attachments/open?token=…). 2. Months later, in a fresh window with no session, open it.
cases.expected: 302 to a fresh signed link — the file opens. Should carry an expiry or check access.
cases.oracle: The old link still redirects to the file.

cases.section: Event-level attachments and the company-folder check — `PATCH /event_groups/:id`
cases.title: A percent-encoded folder name skips the company check
cases.why: The tenant-isolation check keys off literal text, so the same path spelled differently is not inspected.
cases.setup: The run's own draft event with one RFQ round (QA vendor 1 in the audience). Publishing notifies QA vendor 1 only.
cases.steps: Publish (`PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` with the publish body) with `attachments: [{"url": "https://procol.s3.amazonaws.com/trade%5Ffiles/terms_and_conditions/QA_Platform_999999999/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf", "name": "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf"}]`.
cases.expected: Should be refused like the plain spelling (EDGE-PUB-024): HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'. Today the literal test misses `trade%5Ffiles`, so the event publishes (200) and the reader decodes the key back to `trade_files/…`.
cases.oracle: 422 code 101 passes; a 200 is the defect.

cases.section: Event-level attachments and the company-folder check — `PATCH /event_groups/:id`
cases.title: A URL on a different host is signed as a Procol file
cases.why: Signing ignores the host and uses the URL's path as a bucket key, so a URL on any host is treated as a Procol object; the check never looks at a non-S3 host.
cases.setup: The run's own draft event with one RFQ round.
cases.steps: Publish with `attachments: [{"url": "https://files.example.com/trade_files/terms_and_conditions/QA_Platform_999999999/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf", "name": "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf"}]`.
cases.expected: Should be refused: HTTP 422, code 101. Today it publishes (200); the check only inspects URLs containing `amazonaws.com/trade_files/`, and the reader signs the path regardless of host. The check should judge the path, not the host string.
cases.oracle: 422 code 101 passes; a 200 is the defect.

cases.section: Event-level attachments and the company-folder check — `PATCH /event_groups/:id`
cases.title: An encoded slash defeats the company-id pattern
cases.why: "No match" is treated as "allowed", so an encoded separator makes the pattern miss and the value pass.
cases.setup: The run's own draft event with one RFQ round.
cases.steps: Publish with `attachments: [{"url": "https://procol.s3.amazonaws.com/trade_files/terms_and_conditions%2FQA_Platform_999999999/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf", "name": "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf"}]`.
cases.expected: Should be refused: HTTP 422, code 101. Today the `/trade_files/<folder>/<name>_<id>/` pattern does not match when the slash is encoded, a non-match is allowed, and the event publishes (200); the signer later decodes `%2F`.
cases.oracle: 422 code 101 passes; a 200 is the defect.

cases.section: Event-level attachments and the company-folder check — `PATCH /event_groups/:id`
cases.title: The company check never runs on a line-item (product) attachment
cases.why: The publish check reads only the top-level `attachments`; a file attached to a line item (`creator_attachment`) is signed on read with no folder check.
cases.setup: A published event whose line item carries a `creator_attachment`. Manual (needs the round's trade-product ids).
cases.steps: Publish or edit with a line item whose `creator_attachment` holds another company's `trade_files` URL, then read the round.
cases.expected: Should be 101 like a top-level attachment. Today the value is stored and signed for readers (`append_signed_url_to_objects`), the folder check never sees it.
cases.oracle: The foreign URL comes back signed in the round's line data.

cases.title: A round T&C file from another company's folder is accepted
cases.why: The event-level check exists for exactly this; the round endpoint lacks it.
cases.setup: The run's own live RFQ round, QA vendor 1 invited, no bids. Saving terms notifies invited vendors (QA vendor 1 only).
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `terms_and_conditions: ["QA_Platform_tnc_{{stamp}}"]` and one `t_and_c` attachment whose `private_url` is `https://procol.s3.amazonaws.com/trade_files/terms_and_conditions/QA_Platform_999999999/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf`.
cases.expected: Should be refused (422 code 101) like EDGE-PUB-024. Today: HTTP 200 and the link is stored; the trade controller runs no company-URL check, and for a real bucket URL the reader signs it for every invited vendor.
cases.oracle: 422 code 101 passes; a 200 is the defect.

cases.title: A javascript: T&C link is served back to the vendor
cases.why: A clickable `javascript:` link on every invited vendor's T&C list is a stored-script risk.
cases.setup: The run's own live RFQ round, QA vendor 1 invited.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `terms_and_conditions: ["QA_Platform_tnc_{{stamp}}"]` and one `t_and_c` attachment whose `private_url` is `javascript:alert(document.domain)`. 2. Read the round as QA vendor 1.
cases.expected: Should be refused (only Procol-stored files or http/https links). Today the update is accepted and the vendor's copy returns the link unchanged as `public_url` — a non-bucket URL counts as a "user link" and is passed through.
cases.oracle: The verify read-back as the vendor asserts `attachments[*].value[*].public_url` is not the javascript: value; today it is, so the case fails (defect confirmed).

cases.title: A T&C attachment with no value makes the round page unreadable
cases.why: A client that drops an empty list must not poison the round.
cases.setup: The run's own live RFQ round, no bids.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `attachments: [{type: t_and_c}]` (no value). 2. Read the round as the buyer.
cases.expected: Should be refused or treated as empty. Today it is saved and every later read calls `nil.each` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: The verify read-back must answer 2xx; a 500 is the defect.

cases.title: Editing only the T&C files wipes the written terms
cases.why: Adding a file to the terms must not erase the terms themselves.
cases.setup: The run's own live RFQ round. Arrange step sets one written clause first.
cases.steps: 1. Set the round's T&C to the clause `QA_Platform_tnc_keep`. 2. `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with ONLY `attachments` (one `t_and_c` file), no `terms_and_conditions`. 3. Read the round back.
cases.expected: The update is accepted (200). The clause should still be there. Today this branch rebuilds the terms from `Array(nil) = []`, so changing only the files deletes every written clause.
cases.oracle: The verify asserts the round's `terms_and_conditions` still contains `QA_Platform_tnc_keep`; today it does not, so the case fails (defect confirmed).

cases.title: Attachments as text crash the round-edit endpoint
cases.why: The line that picks T&C files runs for every round update (extension, title, settings), so any of them crashes when `attachments` is text.
cases.setup: The run's own live RFQ round, no bids.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `attachments: "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf"`.
cases.expected: Should be 422. Today `.select` on the text → NoMethodError → HTTP 500, before anything is saved.
cases.oracle: Any non-5xx passes; a 500 is the defect.

cases.section: Files carried on remarks (withdrawal, surrogate reference)
cases.title: Withdrawing without a files list crashes
cases.why: A client that omits the empty `attachments` list cannot withdraw an event at all.
cases.setup: The run's own live event (one RFQ round, QA vendor 1 invited, no bids). A successful withdrawal notifies QA vendor 1 only.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` with status `withdrawn` and `withdraw_remark: {remarks: "QA_Platform_withdraw_{{stamp}}"}` — no `attachments` key.
cases.expected: Should withdraw (no files is valid) or refuse 422. Today the remark is built with `attachments = nil` and the validation calls `nil.any?` → NoMethodError → HTTP 500; the event stays live.
cases.oracle: Any non-5xx passes; a 500 is the defect.

cases.section: Files carried on remarks (withdrawal, surrogate reference)
cases.title: A withdrawal-notice file on an outside host is refused and the event stays live
cases.why: The remark's file check is the only thing stopping outside links on a withdrawal notice, and it must leave the event untouched when it fires.
cases.setup: The run's own live event with one RFQ round.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` with status `withdrawn` and `withdraw_remark: {remarks, attachments: ["https://files.example.com/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf"]}`. 2. Read the event back.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 472 'failed to add remark' — a remark only accepts Procol-bucket files. The remark is written first, so nothing else changes: the event is still active.
cases.oracle: 422 code 472; the verify read-back shows `status: active`.

cases.section: Files carried on remarks (withdrawal, surrogate reference)
cases.title: A surrogate-bid reference note without a files list crashes after the bid is saved
cases.why: A half-done surrogate bid behind a server error invites a second, duplicate entry.
cases.setup: The run's own live RFQ round, QA vendor 1 invited, no bids; the company allows surrogate (on-behalf) bids. The bid is entered for QA vendor 1.
cases.steps: Enter a surrogate bid for QA vendor 1 with `surrogate_remarks: {remarks: "QA_Platform_ref_{{stamp}}"}` and no `attachments` key.
cases.expected: Should be accepted (a note without files) or refused 422. Today the bid is saved first, then the reference remark is built with `attachments = nil` and its validation calls `nil.any?` → HTTP 500 — the buyer sees an error although the bid now exists.
cases.oracle: Any non-5xx passes; a 500 is the defect. Depends on surrogate bidding being allowed for the company.

cases.section: Files carried on remarks (withdrawal, surrogate reference)
cases.title: A surrogate reference note with an outside-host file leaves a saved bid behind a server error
cases.why: The `# ! POTENTIAL RENDERING ISSUE` comment in the code is real: an invalid file link leaves a saved bid behind a 500.
cases.setup: As EVD2-DOC-061; the company allows surrogate bids.
cases.steps: Enter a surrogate bid for QA vendor 1 with `surrogate_remarks: {remarks: "QA_Platform_ref_{{stamp}}", attachments: ["https://files.example.com/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf"]}`.
cases.expected: Should be refused with 422 code 472 and no bid saved. Today the bid is saved, the remark fails validation, the helper renders 472 and returns nil, and the caller proceeds with a nil bid → HTTP 500 with the bid already stored.
cases.oracle: Any non-5xx passes; a 500 is the defect. Depends on surrogate bidding being allowed.

cases.section: Files carried on remarks (withdrawal, surrogate reference)
cases.title: A counter-offer remark file on an outside host is refused
cases.why: Counter-offer (`raise_additional_request`) remarks go through the same `create_remarks_helper`, so the same file rule applies, and the same "renders after save" pattern exists.
cases.setup: A live RFQ with a submitted bid; a real counter-offer body for the line. Manual (needs the round's trade-product ids to build a valid counter-offer row).
cases.steps: `POST /additional_request/raise_additional_request` for the bid with `attachments: ["https://files.example.com/QA_Platform_x.pdf"]`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 472; no counter offer saved. (If the request is saved first and then renders the error, that is the same defect pattern as EVD2-DOC-062.)
cases.oracle: 472; the bid is still active, not `requested`.

cases.title: A live event lists its stage reports
cases.why: The Reports panel of the event page is built from this list.
cases.setup: The run's own live RFQ event, no bids, read by its owner.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_all_attachments`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 `{data: […]}` with, for the RFQ round, 'RFQ report' (auction_bids_comparison_report) and 'RFQ Counter Offer Report' (counter_offer_report_v2), each with the round uuid and item_type trade_request. No QCS-Purchase yet (needs a participating vendor) and no Approval Note (no selected proposal).
cases.oracle: 200; `data` is a non-empty list including 'RFQ report'.

cases.title: The reports list is refused for an uninvited vendor
cases.why: The report menu must not leak to vendors outside the event.
cases.setup: The run's own live RFQ event with QA vendor 1 invited; read by QA vendor 2, who is NOT invited.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 2, `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_all_attachments`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action' — `show?` needs at least one round visible to the caller; a restricted round hides it from an uninvited vendor.
cases.oracle: 422 code 455. Depends on the round being restricted to its invited vendors.

cases.section: The query list on an event — `GET /v1/chats`
cases.title: An invited vendor opens the Messages list on the same event
cases.why: Vendors raise and read their clarifications from the same list; a vendor invited to the round must pass the event visibility check.
cases.setup: A published RFQ with QA vendor 1 invited. Read only.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `GET /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}&group_by=thread_id`.
cases.expected: The list opens and is empty. HTTP 200 with `[]`. The vendor would only ever see threads its company takes part in (participant filter).

cases.section: The query list on an event — `GET /v1/chats`
cases.title: An unknown round sent as "TradeRequest" crashes every chats request
cases.why: The translation runs as a before-action on every v1 chats action and looks the round up with `find_by_id`, then calls `.event_group_id` on the result without checking it. A stale or mistyped round id is a server error on the list, the counts, the pickers and even "create".
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer; no event needed.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats?module=TradeRequest&module_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: Should be refused cleanly (HTTP 422, code 533 "Project does not exist."). Today `TradeRequest.find_by_id` returns nil and `nil.event_group_id` raises NoMethodError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.section: The query list on an event — `GET /v1/chats`
cases.title: Who sees which threads on the list
cases.why: Confidentiality of vendor queries rests on one filter: participants see their own threads; NFA approvers of a requested/selected proposal and Procol employees see all; planning-team members see all "Tech Query" threads plus their own. A colleague added to the purchase team AFTER a query was raised is not a participant and never sees it.
cases.setup: Event with two threads (QA vendor 1 general query; buyer technical query to QA vendor 2). Users: owner, a team-mate added later, an NFA approver on the submitted proposal, a planning-team user. Manual (needs writes and several users).
cases.steps: As each user, `GET /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=:id&group_by=thread_id`.
cases.expected: Owner: both threads. Late team-mate: none. NFA approver: both. Planning-team user: the technical thread only (plus any it takes part in). QA vendor 1: only its own thread; QA vendor 2: only the technical thread.
cases.oracle: Thread titles per user as listed.

cases.section: The counts on the Messages button — `GET /v1/chats/get_chats_count_data`
cases.title: The buyer's Messages counts on a live event
cases.why: The button polls this every 30 seconds on every event page; it must answer cheaply and correctly.
cases.setup: A published RFQ, no queries. Read only.
cases.steps: As the buyer, `GET /v1/chats/get_chats_count_data?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with `total_threads_count: 0` and `unresolved_threads_count` null (no thread has an active assignment, so the per-event hash has no key for the event).
cases.oracle: 200; total 0.

cases.section: The counts on the Messages button — `GET /v1/chats/get_chats_count_data`
cases.title: A vendor cannot read counts of a draft event
cases.why: Draft events are invisible to vendors; the count accepts drafts, so the permission check is what stops a vendor from probing them.
cases.setup: A draft event with an unpublished RFQ round.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `GET /v1/chats/get_chats_count_data?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}`.
cases.expected: Refused by the event permission check. HTTP 422, code 455 "You are not authorized to perform this action".

cases.section: The counts on the Messages button — `GET /v1/chats/get_chats_count_data`
cases.title: Counts for an event that does not exist crash
cases.why: Unlike the list, the count does not check that the event was found before the permission check; `authorize nil` raises Pundit::NotDefinedError, which is not rescued.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats/get_chats_count_data?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: Should be refused cleanly (422 code 533, as the list does). Today `authorize(nil, :show?)` → Pundit::NotDefinedError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.title: A buyer sends one technical query on a line item to two vendors
cases.why: One query to several vendors becomes one chat per vendor sharing a thread id; each vendor must see only its own copy. Technical queries are pinned to the latest RFP/RFI stage and keep the line-item evaluators unmuted.
cases.setup: A live RFP+RFQ event, QA vendors 1 and 2 invited, an evaluator on the line item's technical form. Manual (writes, e-mails QA vendors and the evaluator).
cases.steps: As the buyer, `POST /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=:id` with `{"context": "technical", "reference_uuids": [":lineItemUuid"], "message_to_uuids": [":vendor1", ":vendor2"], "message_body": "QA_Platform_tq_<stamp>"}`.
cases.expected: Two chats, same `thread_uuid`, title "Tech Query : 1. | <code> | <name>", context `EG_<id>_Stage_<rfp id>_EGLI_<egli id>`; assigned to the line item's first evaluator. Each vendor's list shows one thread; the buyer's list shows one thread with both vendors in `message_to`. A commercial query instead pins to the latest RFQ/auction stage, is assigned to the event owner and carries no evaluators. **Expected (today), worth a defect check.** When the line item has NO evaluator, a technical query gets no assignee at all (the technical branch never falls back to the owner): nobody can "Mark as Resolve" it, and the unresolved badge (which counts only chats with an active assignment) never counts it.
cases.oracle: As vendor 1, `GET /v1/chats/<chat uuid>` → `siblings_count: 1`, `message_to` names only vendor 1. Without an evaluator: `assignment_status` null and `get_chats_count_data` unresolved unchanged.

cases.title: Raising a query on an event that does not exist crashes before anything is saved
cases.why: The event is fetched with `find_by_id` and used straight away (`@event_group.company_id`) when no recipients are given — the vendor-side shape of the request.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer; no event.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` with `{"context": "general", "message_body": "QA_Platform_query_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: Should be refused cleanly (422 code 533). Today `nil.company_id` raises NoMethodError at line 109 → HTTP 500. Nothing is created (the transaction has not started).
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.title: The same unknown event with a recipient named crashes in the permission check
