cases.why: With recipients given (the buyer-side shape) line 109 is skipped and `authorize nil` raises Pundit::NotDefinedError, which only NotAuthorizedError handling would have turned into a 455.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer; no event.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` with `{"context": "general", "message_to_uuids": ["{{vendorUuid}}"], "message_body": "QA_Platform_query_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 533. Today HTTP 500 (NotDefinedError at line 110). Nothing is created.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.title: A buyer can address any company, invited or not — or none
cases.why: The vendor picker only offers invited vendors with an allowed onboarding status, but the API accepts any company id; a typo or a scripted call notifies a company that was never invited. With no recipient at all, the query is "addressed" to the buyer's own company.
cases.setup: A live event; QA vendor 2 NOT invited. Manual (writes, e-mails QA vendor 2).
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, create a general query with `message_to_uuids: [":vendor2CompanyUuid"]`. 2. Create another with no `message_to_uuids`.
cases.expected: Both should be 422. **Expected (today).** 1: 200, QA vendor 2 users become participants and are e-mailed about an event they cannot open. 2: 200, a thread whose only participants are the buyer's team.
cases.oracle: `message_to` of thread 1 names QA vendor 2; thread 2 has no vendor in `message_to`.

cases.title: Line items of another event leak into the query title
cases.why: `reference_uuids` are decoded and looked up with `EventGroupLineItem.where(id:)` / `.find` without checking they belong to this event. The title and "info" of the new chat then carry another company's product code, name and PR number, returned in the reply.
cases.setup: Needs a line-item uuid from a second event of the SAME QA company (never probe other companies). Manual.
cases.steps: As the buyer of event A, create a commercial query on event A with `reference_uuids: [":lineItemOfEventB"]`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 (line item not on this event). Today 200; the title reads "Comm Query : n. | <B's product>" and `info` shows B's PR number; the thread is assigned to B's owner.
cases.oracle: Title / info / `assigned_to` come from event B.

cases.title: New queries are still accepted after award when "block new message" is on
cases.why: With the company setting `enable_block_message` on, the event serializer sets `block_new_message` once the proposal is selected or in approval, and the screen disables the "Message" button. The create endpoint never reads it, so the vendor app or a stale tab can still raise queries on an awarded event.
cases.setup: A company with `enable_block_message` ON (read at `app/serializers/event_group/show_serializer.rb:295`); an awarded event (proposal submitted). Manual (config + writes).
cases.steps: 1. `GET /event_groups/:id` and confirm `block_new_message: true`. 2. As QA vendor 1, raise a general query.
cases.expected: Should be refused (422). Today 200.
cases.oracle: A thread created while `block_new_message` was true.

cases.title: A blacklisted vendor can still raise queries
cases.why: The visibility check deliberately lets blacklisted vendors see events they were invited to (for history); the create endpoint uses that same check, so a blacklisted vendor can keep e-mailing the buyer's team.
cases.setup: A live event with a QA vendor invited, then blacklisted by the buyer company. Manual.
cases.steps: As the blacklisted QA vendor, raise a general query.
cases.expected: Should be 455. Today 200.
cases.oracle: New thread from the blacklisted vendor.

cases.title: A vendor removed from the event cannot raise new queries
cases.why: Positive control for the permission check: once the vendor is no longer in the round's visible audience, `show?` fails.
cases.setup: A live RFQ (restricted audience) with QA vendor 1 invited, then removed (`remove_audience`). Manual.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, raise a general query.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 455 "You are not authorized to perform this action".
cases.oracle: 422 code 455; no thread created.

cases.title: Chats on a vendor-onboarding response skip every permission check
cases.why: The FxResponse branch of create never calls `authorize` and never checks the response exists. Any signed-in user can open a chat on any onboarding response id. Its success reply is also empty: `first_message && return` returns before `render`.
cases.setup: A QA vendor-onboarding response of the QA company. Manual (writes).
cases.steps: As a user with no access to that response, `POST /v1/chats?module=FxResponse&module_uuid=:responseUuid` with `{"context": "general", "message_body": "QA_Platform_fx_<stamp>"}`.
cases.expected: Should be 455. Today the chat is created and the reply has no body (`first_message && return` leaves the action before `render`, so Rails answers 204 No Content); with a context other than "general" nothing is created, `render json: nil` runs and execution falls through to line 128, which raises on the nil event → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Chat row exists for a user without access.

cases.title: A resolved query cannot be replied to
cases.why: Once the assignee marks the thread resolved, both sides must stop adding messages; the screen disables the box with "You can't reply to a resolved message".
cases.setup: A thread resolved by the owner (case 046). Manual.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `POST /v1/chats/:chatUuid/send_message` with `{"message": "QA_Platform_late_<stamp>"}`.
cases.expected: Refused, no message saved, nobody notified. HTTP 422, code 579 "This message is already closed".
cases.oracle: 422 code 579; conversation count unchanged.

cases.title: Someone allowed to view a thread but not a participant crashes when replying
cases.why: `ChatPolicy#show?` also admits Procol employees (support login) and planning-team members on "Tech Query" threads — neither is a participant. The reply looks the participant up and calls `.muted = false` on nil.
cases.setup: A technical thread on a QA event; a planning-team user of the buyer company (designation in `DESIGNATIONS_FOR_PLANNING_TEAM`) who is not a participant, or a Procol support login. Manual.
cases.steps: As that user, open the thread, then `POST /v1/chats/:chatUuid/send_message` with a QA_Platform_ text.
cases.expected: Either refused (422 455/101) or the user is added as a participant and the reply saved. Today `nil.muted=` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.title: A vendor removed from the event keeps reading and replying in its old threads
cases.why: Thread access is "were you ever a participant" — it never re-checks that the vendor can still see the event. A removed (or rejected) vendor keeps a channel into the buyer's team.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 has a thread on a live event, then is removed from the audience. Manual.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `GET /v1/chats/:chatUuid`, then send a reply.
cases.expected: Should be 455. **Expected (today).** 200 for both; the buyer is e-mailed the reply.
cases.oracle: New conversation from a vendor no longer in the audience.

cases.title: Only the current assignee can mark a thread resolved
cases.why: "Mark as Resolve" is shown only to the assignee; the API closes only the caller's own active assignment and refuses everyone else — including a second click by the assignee, which gets the same 101 rather than "already closed".
cases.setup: A general thread assigned to the owner; a team-mate participant. Manual (writes, e-mails on close).
cases.steps: 1. As the team-mate, `POST /v1/chats/close?thread_id=:threadUuid`. 2. As the owner, the same. 3. As the owner, again.
cases.expected: 1: HTTP 422, code 101 "You are not allowed to perform this action". 2: 200, `assignment_status: "closed"`, `closed_at` set, close notification sent. 3: 422 code 101 (not 579).
cases.oracle: Thread list shows `assignment_status: "closed"` after step 2 only.

cases.title: Assigning a query to a technical evaluator opens the commercial round to them
cases.why: Round visibility for a buyer-side user includes "a chat on this event is assigned to me". Assigning any query to a technical-only evaluator (a participant on technical threads) lets them open the RFQ round with prices.
cases.setup: RFP+RFQ event; an evaluator who cannot see the RFQ round; a technical thread where the evaluator is a participant. Manual.
cases.steps: 1. As the evaluator, `GET /trade/:rfqUuid` → refused. 2. Owner assigns the thread to the evaluator. 3. Repeat step 1.
cases.expected: Step 3 still refused. Today step 3 succeeds (unless the evaluator is in the gated planning team).
cases.oracle: RFQ round readable only after the assignment.

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: The buyer's vendor picker lists the event's invited vendors
cases.why: The "Select vendor(s)" box is filled from this call; an error means the buyer cannot ask any vendor anything.
cases.setup: A published RFQ with QA vendor 1 invited. Read only.
cases.steps: As the buyer, `GET /v1/chats/get_possible_participants?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200, a list of `{uuid, name, vendor_code, location}`; it contains QA vendor 1 when its relationship status is one of the company's allowed vendor statuses.
cases.oracle: 200; array.

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: The vendor picker on a draft event crashes
cases.why: Unlike the list, this action does not check the event was found before `authorize`; drafts are filtered out by status, so a draft id is a 500.
cases.setup: A draft event with an unpublished RFQ round, owned by the run's buyer.
cases.steps: As the owner, `GET /v1/chats/get_possible_participants?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 533. Today `authorize(nil, :show?)` → Pundit::NotDefinedError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: The buyer's line-item picker lists the event's line items
cases.why: Technical and commercial queries must name line items; this call fills "Select line item(s)" with label, encoded id and the suggested assignee.
cases.setup: A published RFQ with one line item. Read only.
cases.steps: As the buyer, `GET /v1/chats/get_reference_options?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200, one option `{label: "1. | <code> | <name>", value, info, assignee_uuid}` (assignee empty because no context is sent).
cases.oracle: 200; one option.

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: A vendor cannot list the line items of a draft event
cases.why: This picker looks the event up with no status filter at all, so the permission check alone keeps draft contents from vendors.
cases.setup: A draft event with an unpublished RFQ round.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `GET /v1/chats/get_reference_options?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 455 "You are not authorized to perform this action".

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: The line-item picker for an unknown event crashes
cases.why: `authorize nil` again (no existence check).
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats/get_reference_options?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 533. Today Pundit::NotDefinedError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: On a lot event a vendor sees line items of lots it was not invited to
cases.why: Vendor-side, the picker returns every line item of the event; only buyer planning-team users are narrowed. A vendor invited to lot 1 learns the products and quantities of lot 2.
cases.setup: A live lot event (two lots, QA vendor 1 invited to lot 1 only). Manual.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `GET /v1/chats/get_reference_options?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=:id`.
cases.expected: Only lot-1 line items. Today all line items.
cases.oracle: A lot-2 product in the vendor's options.

cases.section: Per-vendor unresolved counts on the comparison sheet — `GET /v1/chats/get_unresolved_queries_count`
cases.title: The buyer reads per-vendor unresolved counts on a round with a bid
cases.why: The comparison sheet shows a red message badge on each vendor column with open queries; the dashboard calls this with `event_uuid=<round uuid>` once the round has bids.
cases.setup: A live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; no queries. Read only.
cases.steps: As the buyer, `GET /v1/chats/get_unresolved_queries_count?event_uuid={{tradeId}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with `{}` (no vendor has an open query).
cases.oracle: 200; empty object.

cases.section: Personal one-to-one chats — `/chats` (console and vendor apps)
cases.title: Sending into a personal chat you are not part of
cases.why: The participant check is the only thing between a user and someone else's private chat.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /chats/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/send` with `{"message": "QA_Platform_dm_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: Refused, nothing saved. HTTP 422, code 4 "Request not found".
cases.oracle: 422 code 4.

cases.section: Personal one-to-one chats — `/chats` (console and vendor apps)
cases.title: The message "context" type is turned into a class name without an allow-list
cases.why: `item_type` is passed to `constantize` and queried by id with no ownership check. "TradeRequest" or "Bid" with an unknown id crashes on `nil.unit_value`; any model name is accepted and another company's record can be attached as context.
cases.setup: A personal chat between two QA buyers (manual: creating it writes).
cases.steps: `POST /chats/:chatUuid/send` with `{"message": "QA_Platform_dm_<stamp>", "item_type": "TradeRequest", "item_id": 999999999}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 (unknown item). Today `nil.unit_value` → HTTP 500 before save; with an allowed-looking but foreign id the context is saved.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.section: The pending list per event state — `GET /reminders/:id?resource_type=event_group`
cases.title: Once the vendor submits a bid it drops out of the offer-submission list
cases.why: Reminding a vendor who already quoted is noise and makes the buyer look careless; the list must subtract vendors who have bid.
cases.setup: Live RFQ, QA vendor 1 has SUBMITTED a bid, bidding still open (recipe `rfq_with_bid`). Read only.
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}?resource_type=event_group`.
cases.expected: QA vendor 1 is no longer pending, so "Offer submissions" is empty (null); nothing else is pending. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: 200; `offer_submissions` null (vendor 1 is in the round's `bid_company_ids`, added when the bid became active, `app/models/bid.rb:507-508`). If `offer_submissions` still lists vendor 1, the subtraction is broken.

cases.section: The pending list per event state — `GET /reminders/:id?resource_type=event_group`
cases.title: After the round has fully closed there is nothing left to remind
cases.why: Only rounds whose closing time is still in the future are considered; a closed event must not offer "submit your offer" reminders.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 bid, bidding window and extra closing time over (recipe `closed_rfq_with_bid`). Read only.
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}?resource_type=event_group`.
cases.expected: No open round is left, so the reply body is empty (`null`) and the drawer shows "No Pending Actions to Remind". HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: 200 with body `null` (`get_reminder_data` returns nil when no round has `closed_at` in the future). Never a 5xx.

cases.section: The pending list per event state — `GET /reminders/:id?resource_type=event_group`
cases.title: With two invited vendors and one bid, only the vendor who has not bid is listed
cases.why: The subtraction must be per vendor, not "anyone bid → nobody pending".
cases.setup: Live RFQ with QA vendors 1 and 2 invited; only QA vendor 2 has submitted. No recipe leaves exactly one of two vendors without a bid for the direct runner, so manual.
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/:eventUuid?resource_type=event_group`.
cases.expected: "Offer submissions" lists QA vendor 1 only, total 1.
cases.oracle: `offer_submissions.total_count` = 1 and the one `recipient_uuid` is vendor 1's company uuid.

cases.section: The pending list per event state — `GET /reminders/:id?resource_type=event_group`
cases.title: A vendor removed from the event (or hidden from it) is not listed
cases.why: Only active, visible invitations count; reminding a vendor the buyer removed would tell them about an event they were dropped from.
cases.setup: Live RFQ, QA vendors 1 and 2 invited; remove QA vendor 2 (its audience becomes inactive). Changes the event — manual.
cases.steps: 1. Remove QA vendor 2. 2. `GET /reminders/:eventUuid?resource_type=event_group`.
cases.expected: Only QA vendor 1 is pending under "Offer submissions".
cases.oracle: No recipient with vendor 2's company uuid.

cases.section: The pending list per event state — `GET /reminders/:id?resource_type=event_group`
cases.title: Pending evaluations appear only for the first technical stage, and only until its evaluation end time
cases.why: Evaluator reminders are driven by the technical round's closing time, which "send to evaluation" moves to the evaluation end time. After that time — or for a second technical stage — evaluators can no longer be chased from this drawer.
cases.setup: Live RFP+RFQ; QA vendor 1 submitted the technical response; the RFP was sent to evaluation with an end time in the future; an evaluator assigned who has not scored. Manual (needs the evaluation set-up).
cases.steps: 1. `GET /reminders/:eventUuid?resource_type=event_group` while the evaluation window is open. 2. Repeat after the evaluation end time.
cases.expected: 1: "Pending evaluations" lists the evaluator (columns Evaluator Name / Last Reminded At), `bid_pending_for` holds the technical stage title. 2: the kind is gone (the RFP's closing time has passed). With two technical stages only the first one still open is ever considered.
cases.oracle: Step 1 `pending_evaluations.recipients[0].recipient_uuid` = the evaluator's user uuid; step 2 `pending_evaluations` null.

cases.section: The pending list per event state — `GET /reminders/:id?resource_type=event_group`
cases.title: Auction reminders appear only before the auction starts, one entry per live lot
cases.why: The auction reminder is "please join the auction"; it is offered only for an active auction that has not started, the latest auction stage per active lot, with the lot title.
cases.setup: An auction scheduled to start later, QA vendor 1 invited; optionally a lot-split event with two lots. Manual (no auction recipe).
cases.steps: Read the list before the start, then after the auction starts.
cases.expected: Before: "Auction reminders" is a list with one entry per auction (per active lot, carrying `lot_title`), each listing the invited vendors. After start: gone.
cases.oracle: `auction_reminders` is an array; each item has `recipients`, `columns` (Vendor Name / Last Reminded At) and `lot_title`.

cases.title: The vendor app may not read a buyer's reminder list
cases.why: The list names every vendor still pending on the event — competitor names a vendor must never see.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 signed in to the vendor app. Manual: the backend answers a vendor-app call to this action with 401 and signs that session out, so it can never be a runnable twin.
cases.steps: As the vendor, `GET /reminders/:eventUuid?resource_type=event_group`.
cases.expected: Refused as an unauthorised app; no data. HTTP 401.
cases.oracle: 401, no `offer_submissions` in the body.

cases.title: A buyer from another company cannot read the list
cases.why: Vendor names and pending status of a competitor's tender.
cases.setup: A buyer of Demo Account 2 and an event of PROCOL DEMO. Manual (needs a second company's buyer).
cases.steps: As that buyer, `GET /reminders/:eventUuid?resource_type=event_group`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action'.

cases.title: Reading reminders for an event that does not exist crashes instead of "not found"
cases.why: An unknown event id reaches the permission check as "nothing", which the permission library cannot handle; only "not authorised" errors are caught, so the user gets a server error.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer; no event needed (recipe `none`).
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==?resource_type=event_group` (decodes to id 999999999).
cases.expected: Should be refused cleanly (404 or 422 "does not exist"). Today the lookup returns nil and `authorize(nil, :show?)` raises `Pundit::NotDefinedError`, which is not rescued → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect; a 4xx with a readable message is the fix.

cases.section: Sending a reminder — happy paths and read-backs (all manual: they email)
cases.title: After sending, the list shows when the vendor was last reminded and locks them for 10 minutes
cases.why: The lock is what stops a buyer spamming a vendor from the drawer.
cases.setup: Right after API-EVDREM-025. Manual.
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/:eventUuid?resource_type=event_group`.
cases.expected: QA vendor 1 is still pending under "Offer submissions" with "Last Reminded At" set to the send time (format like "3 Oct 2026, 4:05 PM") and not remindable.
cases.oracle: `last_reminded_at` non-null, `can_remind` false.

cases.section: Sending a reminder — happy paths and read-backs (all manual: they email)
cases.title: Sending an auction reminder before the auction starts
cases.why: Auction reminders use their own email and also leave an activity-log entry on the auction stage.
cases.setup: An auction not yet started, QA vendor 1 invited. Manual.
cases.steps: `POST /reminders/:eventUuid/send_reminder` with `reminder_type` `auction_reminders` and the vendor → auction stage map from the list.
cases.expected: 200 success, `type` `auction_reminders`; the vendor gets the auction reminder email; the stage's activity log shows a reminder entry; re-reading the list shows the vendor locked for that auction only.
cases.oracle: Reminder row category `AuctionReminder` with `meta_data.trade_id` = the auction stage id; activity entry category `AuctionReminder`.

cases.section: Sending a reminder — happy paths and read-backs (all manual: they email)
cases.title: Sending a pending-evaluation reminder to an evaluator
cases.why: For evaluations and approvals the recipient is a person, not a company; the stored identifier switches to `u-<user id>`.
cases.setup: As API-EVDREM-007, a QA buyer-side evaluator. Manual.
cases.steps: Send `reminder_type` `pending_evaluations` with the evaluator's uuid → [RFP uuid].
cases.expected: 200 success; the evaluator gets "[<ref>] [Reminder] Technical Requires Your Evaluation."; the list then shows the evaluator locked.
cases.oracle: Reminder row recipient `u-<evaluator id>`, category `PendingEvaluation`.

cases.title: The vendor app may not send reminders
cases.why: A vendor triggering emails to other vendors from the buyer's account would be abuse.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 in the vendor app. Manual: a 401 here signs the vendor session out.
cases.steps: As the vendor, `POST /reminders/:eventUuid/send_reminder` with a valid body.
cases.expected: HTTP 401; nothing sent, no reminder row.
cases.oracle: 401; reminder count unchanged.

cases.title: A buyer from another company cannot send reminders on this event
cases.why: Sending requires the event's company to be one of the caller's companies.
cases.setup: Demo Account 2 buyer; PROCOL DEMO event. Manual.
cases.steps: `POST /reminders/:eventUuid/send_reminder` with a valid body.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action'; nothing sent.
cases.oracle: 422 code 455; no reminder row.

cases.title: A colleague who cannot see the event can still send reminders for it
cases.why: Reading the list requires seeing a stage of the event, but sending only checks "same company + create permission". Anyone in the company can spam an event's vendors they are not allowed to look at.
cases.setup: Second PROCOL DEMO buyer with create permission, not on the event's team (read refused, API-EVDREM-017). Manual: it emails QA vendor 1.
cases.steps: As that buyer, send an offer-submission reminder for QA vendor 1 on the QA buyer's event.
cases.expected: Should be refused (455) like the read. Today: 200 "Reminders sent successfully." (suspected missing authorisation).
cases.oracle: 200 + a reminder row with `sender_id` = the colleague.

cases.section: What the send does not check (suspected defects, all manual)
cases.title: The 10-minute lock exists only in the screen; the API sends again immediately
cases.why: `can_remind` is computed for the list but never checked by the send; a double click, a script or a second tab mails the vendor again.
cases.setup: Right after API-EVDREM-025. Manual (emails QA vendor 1 twice).
cases.steps: Send the same offer-submission reminder again within a minute.
cases.expected: Should be refused ("retry in 10 minutes"). Today: 200 success and a second email.
cases.oracle: Two reminder rows minutes apart; two emails.

cases.section: What the send does not check (suspected defects, all manual)
cases.title: The meaning of a recipient id depends on the reminder kind and is never checked
cases.why: For evaluations and approvals the map keys are treated as USER ids, otherwise as COMPANY ids. Sending a company uuid with `pending_evaluations` mails whatever user happens to have that number.
cases.setup: Manual and only on UAT with care: pick a QA-vendor company uuid whose decoded number equals a QA user id, or inspect the queued job instead of letting it send.
cases.steps: Send `pending_evaluations` with `{"<QA vendor 1 company uuid>": ["<RFP uuid>"]}`.
cases.expected: Should be refused (recipient is not an evaluator of this event). Today: 200; the stored recipient is `u-<company id>` and the worker looks that number up as a user.
cases.oracle: Reminder row `recipient_identifier` = `u-<company id>`.

cases.section: What the send does not check (suspected defects, all manual)
cases.title: An unknown reminder kind is stored and emailed as a generic notification
cases.why: The kind is never validated: "foo" is stored as category "Foo" and sent with the subject "[Reminder] Notification".
cases.setup: Live RFQ, QA vendor 1. Manual (emails).
cases.steps: Send `reminder_type` `QA_Platform_kind` for vendor 1 and the RFQ round.
cases.expected: Should be 422 (unknown kind). Today: 200 success, a reminder row with an invented category, and a generic email (or a mail-template failure in the worker).
cases.oracle: Reminder row category; mailbox.

cases.section: What the send does not check (suspected defects, all manual)
cases.title: If the event's creator has been deactivated, nobody is reminded but the buyer is told it worked
cases.why: The worker looks up the creator's name among ACTIVE users only and crashes on nil; the API has already answered success and stamped the 10-minute lock.
cases.setup: An event whose creator user is inactive (e.g. after ownership transfer and deactivation). Manual.
cases.steps: Send an offer-submission reminder; watch the worker.
cases.expected: Should send (use any name or the current owner). Today: 200 "Reminders sent successfully.", the `ReminderWorker` job fails with `NoMethodError` on `display_name`, no email.
cases.oracle: Sidekiq failure; empty mailbox; reminder row present.

cases.title: A send without the reminders map crashes before doing anything
cases.why: The map is read with `params[:reminders].to_unsafe_h` on the first lines; when it is missing the `|| {}` fallback is never reached and the request dies with a server error.
cases.setup: Live RFQ (recipe `published_rfq`). Nothing is written: the crash is on controller line 18, before the service, the permission check or any email.
cases.steps: `POST /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}/send_reminder` with `{"resource_type": "event_group", "reminder_type": "offer_submissions"}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. Today `nil.to_unsafe_h` raises `NoMethodError` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: 5xx = defect; no reminder row.

cases.title: Sending for an event that does not exist crashes instead of "not found"
cases.why: The service is built first (it quietly finds nothing), then the permission check is handed nil and raises an error nobody catches.
cases.setup: Any buyer, no event (recipe `none`). Crashes at the permission check, before the service's send (no row, no email).
cases.steps: `POST /reminders/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/send_reminder` with `{"resource_type": "event_group", "reminder_type": "offer_submissions", "reminders": {"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==": ["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="]}}`.
cases.expected: Should be a clean 4xx. Today: `EventGroup.find_by` → nil → `authorize(nil, :update?)` → `Pundit::NotDefinedError` (not rescued) → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: 5xx = defect.

cases.title: A send without a reminder kind crashes
cases.why: The kind is not validated; with it missing the code reaches the reminder-row builder and calls `singularize` on nothing.
cases.setup: Live RFQ (recipe `published_rfq`). The map uses unknown ids so it resolves to no round; the crash is inside the row builder's `map` (base service line 40), BEFORE `Reminder.insert_all` (line 54) and before the email (service line 69).
cases.steps: `POST /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}/send_reminder` with `{"resource_type": "event_group", "reminders": {"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==": ["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="]}}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. Today `nil.singularize` → `NoMethodError` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: 5xx = defect; no reminder row.

cases.title: An upload without a file name is refused
cases.why: Name, content and type are checked together before anything is written.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with `{"data": "UUE=", "type": "t_and_c"}`.
cases.expected: Refused, nothing stored. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: An upload without content is refused
cases.why: A file with no content must never create an empty object.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with `{"name": "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf", "type": "t_and_c"}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: An upload without a document type is refused
cases.why: The type decides the storage folder.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with `{"name": "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf", "data": "UUE="}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: A file name of only spaces is refused
cases.why: A blank name would become an extension-less storage key.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with name `" "`, data `UUE=`, type `t_and_c`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: The document type is case-sensitive
cases.why: Pins the exact contract; `T_AND_C` is not `t_and_c`.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with type `T_AND_C`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: A file without an extension is refused
cases.why: It cannot be typed or previewed safely.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with name `QA_Platform_{{stamp}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 484 'File type not allowed'.

cases.title: A look-alike Unicode extension is refused
cases.why: A full-width `ｐ` reads as `.pdf` on screen; the name cleaner replaces every character outside `0-9 A-Z a-z . -` with `_`, so `.ｐdf` becomes `._df` and no longer matches.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with name `QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.ｐdf`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 484 'File type not allowed'.

cases.title: PowerPoint files are not accepted today
cases.why: Buyers often attach `.pptx` specs; recording the real list makes any future change visible.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with name `QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pptx`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 484 'File type not allowed'.

cases.title: Content that is not valid base64 is stored as an empty file
cases.why: A silently empty attachment is only discovered when the other side opens it.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event. Today stores one private 0-byte object.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with a valid name and type and data `!!!!`.
cases.expected: Should be refused (422). Today: HTTP 200 'Successfully uploaded File' and a 0-byte file — the decoder silently drops invalid characters.
cases.oracle: A refusal passes; a 200 is the defect.

cases.title: Numeric content is reported as uploaded although nothing was stored
cases.why: The API says "Successfully uploaded File" for a file it never stored; only the screen's own check of `url` hides it.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event. Nothing is stored.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with data `12345` (a number).
cases.expected: Should be refused (422). Today: HTTP 200, `success: true`, `url: null`, `public_url: null` — decoding a number raises, the helper swallows every error and returns nil, and the controller never checks the result.
cases.oracle: A refusal passes; a 200 with a null url is the defect.

cases.title: A 300-character file name is reported as uploaded although nothing was stored
cases.why: Long, descriptive document names are normal in tenders; the user is told it worked.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event. Nothing is stored.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with a valid type and data and a 300-character name ending `.pdf`.
cases.expected: Should be refused or stored under a shortened name. Today: HTTP 200, `success: true`, `url: null` — the temp file is named `temp_<name>`, exceeding the 255-byte file-name limit; the error is swallowed.
cases.oracle: A refusal passes; a 200 with a null url is the defect.

cases.title: A vendor is allowed to upload and is stopped only by validation
cases.why: Vendors upload bid documents through the same call; a permission regression would show as 455 here.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 on the vendor app (allowed to call this action). No event.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `POST /trade/upload_file` with type `invoice`.
cases.expected: Past the permission check, refused by validation. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2, never 455.

cases.title: There is no size limit on the server
cases.why: The 20 MB limit lives only in the screen; the whole file is decoded in memory.
cases.setup: QA buyer; a 30 MB PDF as base64. Manual (large payload, stores a file).
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with that payload.
cases.expected: Accepted unless the proxy cuts it (413). Should be refused above the product limit.
cases.oracle: Status and stored object size.

cases.title: Two uploads with the same name in the same second overwrite each other
cases.why: The key is `<company>_<epoch seconds>_<name>`; two colleagues uploading "Terms.pdf" in the same second share one key.
cases.setup: Two buyer sessions of one company. Manual (needs parallel requests).
cases.steps: Send two uploads named `QA_Platform_same.pdf` with different content within one second.
cases.expected: Both answer 200 with the same `url`; the first link now opens the second file. Should be unique per upload.
cases.oracle: Identical `url`; the first link returns the second content.

cases.title: A buyer with only intake access can still upload event documents
cases.why: The permission is "can read events OR can read intake requests" — flagged in the code as a temporary hotfix.
cases.setup: A buyer whose role lacks trade read but has intake read. Manual (needs that user).
cases.steps: As that buyer, `POST /trade/upload_file` with a valid small PDF.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. Should be limited to users who can work on events.
cases.oracle: 200 for a user who gets 455 on `GET /event_groups`.

cases.title: An upper-case extension is accepted
cases.why: Scanner and camera files are often `.PDF` / `.JPG`.
cases.setup: QA buyer. Manual (stores a file).
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with name `QA_Platform_x.PDF`.
cases.expected: Accepted (extension compared lower-cased). HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: 200, non-null `url`.

cases.title: Content sent with its "data:…;base64," prefix is stored corrupted
cases.why: The screen strips the prefix; an integration that does not is told it worked and stores a broken file.
cases.setup: QA buyer. Manual (stores a file).
cases.steps: `POST /trade/upload_file` with data `data:application/pdf;base64,UUE=`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; the file starts with bytes decoded from the prefix text. Should be refused or the prefix stripped server-side.
cases.oracle: The file's first bytes are not 'QA'.

cases.title: A template image without a name is refused
cases.why: Baseline validation of the RFI/technical template builder's image upload.
cases.setup: QA buyer (console only; the vendor app may not call this action). No event.
cases.steps: `POST /templates/upload_attachment` with `{"data": "UUE="}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: A template image without content is refused
cases.why: No empty images in a template every vendor will see.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /templates/upload_attachment` with `{"name": "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.png"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: A GIF is refused by the server although the builder offers "any image"
cases.why: The builder's picker accepts any `image/*` file, the server only .jpg/.jpeg/.png among images; the buyer gets a generic failure (see UI-EVDDOC-085).
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event.
cases.steps: `POST /templates/upload_attachment` with name `QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.gif`, data `UUE=`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 484 'File type not allowed'.

cases.title: A failed store is reported as a failure here (unlike the event upload)
cases.why: The correct counterpart of API-EVDDOC-016: this endpoint checks the storage result.
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event. Nothing is stored.
cases.steps: `POST /templates/upload_attachment` with name `QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.png` and data `12345`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 902, message 'Upload failed' (code 902's catalogue text is 'Only active or paused jobs can be cancelled'; the code is reused with a custom message).

cases.title: A name longer than the storage key limit fails cleanly
cases.why: No name-length guard; storage refuses keys over 1,024 bytes and the user sees only "Upload failed".
cases.setup: QA buyer, no event. Nothing is stored.
cases.steps: `POST /templates/upload_attachment` with data `UUE=` and a 1,100-character name ending `.png`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 902, message 'Upload failed'; not a 500.

cases.title: The template image upload has no permission check at all
cases.why: Every other upload asks the policy; this action never calls `authorize`, so any signed-in console user can store files in the company's template folder.
cases.setup: A console user without template create/edit rights. Manual (needs that user).
cases.steps: As that user, `POST /templates/upload_attachment` with a small PNG.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 `{url: …}`. Should be 455 for users who cannot edit templates.
cases.oracle: 200 for a user who gets 455 on `POST /templates`.

cases.title: The vendor app may not call the template image upload
cases.why: Records the app rule; a vendor session sending it is answered 401 and signed out.
cases.setup: Never run automatically: the 401 ends the vendor's session.
cases.steps: From the vendor app, `POST /templates/upload_attachment`.
cases.expected: HTTP 401 'app not authorized' (agribid_website has no templates#upload_attachment entry).
cases.oracle: 401 and the vendor session ends.

cases.section: Opening a stored file by link — `GET /v1/attachments/open`
cases.title: An empty token is refused
cases.why: Baseline refusal for a cut-off link.
cases.setup: No event.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/attachments/open?token=`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, plain text 'Invalid token'; no redirect.

cases.section: Opening a stored file by link — `GET /v1/attachments/open`
cases.title: A token that is not base64 is refused
cases.why: Garbage must be refused, not crash.
cases.setup: No event.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/attachments/open?token=!!!!`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, plain text 'Invalid token' (strict decoding raises ArgumentError, which is rescued).

cases.section: Opening a stored file by link — `GET /v1/attachments/open`
cases.title: A token sent as a list must not crash
cases.why: Unauthenticated endpoints are the first thing scanners probe.
cases.setup: No event.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/attachments/open?token[]=QA`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 'Invalid token'. Today the token is an Array, `Array#end_with?` does not exist → NoMethodError (not rescued) → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any non-5xx passes; a 500 is the defect.

cases.section: Opening a stored file by link — `GET /v1/attachments/open`
cases.title: With no token secret configured every file link is a 500
cases.why: `attachment_encryptor` returns nil when `ATTACHMENT_TOKEN_SECRET` is blank and `open` calls `nil.decrypt_and_verify` unguarded, so all report links break at once.
cases.setup: An environment where the ProcolVariable `ATTACHMENT_TOKEN_SECRET` is empty. Manual (configuration).
cases.steps: Open any `/api/v1/attachments/open?token=…` link.
cases.expected: HTTP 500. Should be a clean refusal and fall back to a signed URL (the link builders already fall back when the secret is missing).
cases.oracle: 500 vs a readable refusal.

cases.section: Opening a stored file by link — `GET /v1/attachments/open`
cases.title: Whether a vendor gets a lasting link depends on the vendor's company
cases.why: The round reader reads `attachment_token_url_enabled` on `Current.workspace`, which for a vendor is the vendor's own company; a buyer who turns it on still sends 2-hour links to vendors whose company does not have it.
cases.setup: Buyer company ON, QA vendor company OFF; a round with a T&C file. Manual (config).
cases.steps: Read the round as the buyer and as the vendor; compare `attachments[*].value[*].public_url`.
cases.expected: Buyer sees a token link, vendor sees a 2-hour signed link. Should follow the event owner's setting.
cases.oracle: Different link kinds for the same file.

cases.section: Event-level attachments and the company-folder check — `PATCH /event_groups/:id`
cases.title: A draft event accepts a foreign-folder attachment (the check runs on publish and edit)
cases.why: The check runs on every `PATCH /event_groups/:id`, including a draft save, so it should refuse the foreign folder before publish too.
cases.setup: A draft event with one line item. Manual: the plan runner's draft save path is not exercised as a decisive twin here; confirm on a fresh draft.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/<draft uuid>` with status `draft` and `attachments: [{"url": "https://procol.s3.amazonaws.com/trade_files/terms_and_conditions/QA_Platform_999999999/QA_Platform_x.pdf"}]`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 (the plain other-company URL is caught before the draft is saved).
cases.oracle: 422 code 101; attachments unchanged.

cases.title: A number inside the attachments list crashes the round-edit endpoint
cases.why: Same unguarded line, a different shape.
cases.setup: The run's own live RFQ round, no bids.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `attachments: [1]`.
cases.expected: Should be 422. Today `1["type"]` raises TypeError → HTTP 500, before anything is saved.
cases.oracle: Any non-5xx passes; a 500 is the defect.

cases.title: T&C files are locked once bidding has closed with a bid in
cases.why: Changing the terms after vendors have bid against them would change the deal after the fact.
cases.setup: The run's own RFQ round: QA vendor 1 has bid and the bid window plus extra closing time is over.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `terms_and_conditions: ["QA_Platform_tnc_{{stamp}}"]` and `attachments: [{type: t_and_c, value: []}]`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found' — terms and files cannot change once a bid exists and the window is over; a closed round is refused with the same code 4. Nothing changes.
cases.oracle: 422 code 4.

cases.section: Files carried on remarks (withdrawal, surrogate reference)
cases.title: Withdrawal-notice files sent as text must not crash
cases.why: Type confusion on the most consequential lifecycle action.
cases.setup: The run's own live event with one RFQ round.
cases.steps: `PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}` with status `withdrawn` and `withdraw_remark: {remarks, attachments: "QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.pdf"}` (text, not a list).
cases.expected: Should be refused (422). The text is cast into the text-array column; depending on the adapter the remark either fails validation (472) or the validation meets a non-list (500). Must not be a 500.
cases.oracle: Any non-5xx passes; a 500 is the defect.

cases.section: Files carried on remarks (withdrawal, surrogate reference)
cases.title: More than ten files on a remark are refused
cases.why: The Remark model caps attachments at 10.
cases.setup: The run's own live event. Manual: needs 11 real Procol-bucket URLs, which the runner cannot mint.
cases.steps: Withdraw with a `withdraw_remark` carrying 11 valid bucket file URLs.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 472 'failed to add remark' (length validation 0..10).
cases.oracle: 472; the event stays live.

cases.title: The reports list for an unknown event is not found
cases.why: An unknown id must be a clean not-found.
cases.setup: QA buyer; no event.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/get_all_attachments` (id decodes to one that does not exist).
cases.expected: HTTP 404 — `EventGroup.find` raises RecordNotFound (the blank check after it never runs).

cases.title: A garbled event id is not found
cases.why: A garbled id must not crash.
cases.setup: QA buyer; no event.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/WrongUuid1=/get_all_attachments` (decodes to nil).
cases.expected: HTTP 404 — the id decodes to nil and `EventGroup.find(nil)` raises RecordNotFound.

cases.title: The reports list for a draft event is empty with no body
cases.why: Records the odd draft contract so a future change is noticed.
cases.setup: The run's own draft event (one line item, no rounds), read by its owner.
cases.steps: `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_all_attachments`.
cases.expected: HTTP 204 No Content with an empty body — the action returns before rendering when the event is a draft, so Rails answers "no content". Clients expecting `{data: []}` must cope with an empty body. Must not be a 500.
cases.oracle: Any non-5xx passes.

cases.title: The reports list is returned to an invited vendor
cases.why: Vendors should not even learn that a comparison or award note exists; `show?` only checks that one round is visible.
cases.setup: The run's own live RFQ event; QA vendor 1 invited and has bid. Read by QA vendor 1 (vendor app).
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_all_attachments`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 and the vendor receives the buyer's report menu for rounds it can see — 'RFQ report', 'RFQ Counter Offer Report' and, once a vendor participates, 'QCS-Purchase', plus 'Approval Note-Purch' once a proposal is selected. Whether each report then downloads for a vendor is decided elsewhere and must be checked manually.
cases.oracle: 200; `data` includes names beyond the vendor's own.

cases.title: The reports list still answers after a withdrawal
cases.why: Buyers need the paper trail of a withdrawn event.
cases.setup: The run's own live RFQ event, withdrawn by the buyer in the arrange step.
cases.steps: 1. Withdraw the event with a remark. 2. `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_all_attachments`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200: a withdrawn event is not a draft, so the list is built; the withdrawn round still shows 'RFQ report' and 'RFQ Counter Offer Report' (stages are listed whatever their status).
cases.oracle: 200; `data` includes 'RFQ report'.

cases.title: A master-QCS report appears only once a vendor is participating
cases.why: `should_include_master_qcs_report?` requires a live commercial stage with at least one participating vendor company.
cases.setup: A live RFQ event where a vendor has submitted a bid vs one with no bids. Manual (the single-event twin in EVD2-DOC-071 covers the with-bid list; this contrasts the two states).
cases.steps: Compare the list on a no-bid event and a with-bid event.
cases.expected: No 'QCS-Purchase' until a vendor participates; present afterwards.
cases.oracle: The entry appears only in the with-bid list.

cases.title: The approval-note report appears only after a proposal is selected
cases.why: `generate_event_group_report_names` adds the approval note only for a `selected` proposal.
cases.setup: An awarded event (proposal selected) vs a live one. Manual (needs an awarded event).
cases.steps: Compare the list before and after award.
cases.expected: 'Approval Note-Purch' (proposal_report, item_type proposal) appears only after selection, carrying the proposal id.
cases.oracle: The entry appears only after award.

cases.section: The query list on an event — `GET /v1/chats`
cases.title: Older screens that pass the round instead of the event still reach the event's list
cases.why: The bids header sends `module=TradeRequest` with the round's uuid when the round has no project metadata; the controller rewrites it to the round's event. A break here empties the drawer on those screens.
cases.setup: A published RFQ. Read only.
cases.steps: As the buyer, `GET /v1/chats?module=TradeRequest&module_uuid={{tradeId}}&group_by=thread_id`.
cases.expected: Same answer as the event-level list: HTTP 200 with `[]`.

cases.section: The query list on an event — `GET /v1/chats`
cases.title: Asking for the event list without an event id
cases.why: A screen that loses its event id must get a clear "bad request", not someone else's chats.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats?module=EventGroup` (no `module_uuid`).
cases.expected: Refused as missing parameters. HTTP 422, code 2 "Insufficient parameters".
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: The query list on an event — `GET /v1/chats`
cases.title: The list for an event that does not exist
cases.why: The list checks the event exists before the permission check, so an unknown id is a readable refusal.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 533 "Project does not exist.".

cases.section: The query list on an event — `GET /v1/chats`
cases.title: A draft event has no Messages list
cases.why: Only live and withdrawn events are looked up (`VALID_STATUSES_FOR_DASHBOARD`), and the screen hides the Messages button on drafts; the API must agree and refuse, not crash.
cases.setup: A draft event with an unpublished RFQ round, owned by the run's buyer.
cases.steps: As the owner, `GET /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}`.
cases.expected: Refused as "not found" for drafts. HTTP 422, code 533 "Project does not exist.".

cases.section: The query list on an event — `GET /v1/chats`
cases.title: A malformed filter on the thread view is a server error
cases.why: The filter text is parsed with a blanket `rescue` that returns nil; the thread view then reads `@filters["thread_id"]` without a nil check. A bad deep link or a hand-edited URL takes the drawer down with a 500 instead of ignoring the filter.
cases.setup: A published RFQ. Read only.
cases.steps: As the buyer, `GET /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}&group_by=thread_id&filters=QA_Platform_not_json`.
cases.expected: Should either ignore the filter (200 `[]`) or refuse it (422 code 2). Today `CommonFunctions.parse_filters` swallows the JSON error and returns nil, and `nil["thread_id"]` raises NoMethodError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect. The same URL without `group_by=thread_id` answers 200 (the nil filter is only read on the thread view).

cases.section: The counts on the Messages button — `GET /v1/chats/get_chats_count_data`
cases.title: Counts are allowed on the owner's draft event
cases.why: Unlike every other read here, the count accepts draft events (`+ [:draft]`). The owner must get zeros, not an error.
cases.setup: A draft event with an unpublished RFQ round, owned by the run's buyer.
cases.steps: As the owner, `GET /v1/chats/get_chats_count_data?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200, `total_threads_count: 0`.

cases.section: The counts on the Messages button — `GET /v1/chats/get_chats_count_data`
cases.title: "Total" and "unresolved" are counted by different rules
cases.why: The badge shows unresolved, the dot shows total. Total uses the prefix pattern (case 009) over all chats; unresolved uses the exact `event_group_id` and only chats whose assignment is active (`status = 1`, no NULL branch). They can disagree in both directions, and resolving the last open thread shows null rather than 0.
cases.setup: Event with three threads: one open (assigned), one resolved, one on a prefix-matching other event. Manual.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats/get_chats_count_data?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=:id` before and after resolving the open thread.
cases.expected: total = 2, unresolved = 1, then unresolved = 0. Today: total counts the foreign thread too, and unresolved becomes null once nothing is open.
cases.oracle: Compare with the thread list's `assignment_status` values.

cases.title: Raising a query without saying which event it is about
cases.why: With no module the controller skips every branch and only fails inside the transaction at `@event_group.user_id`; the request should be refused up front.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/chats` with `{"context": "general", "message_body": "QA_Platform_query_{{stamp}}"}` (no `module`, no `module_uuid`).
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2 "Insufficient parameters". Today NoMethodError on nil at line 128 → HTTP 500; the first write (`Chat.create!`) is never reached.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.title: Raising a query on a draft event crashes
cases.why: Drafts are excluded by the status filter, so a draft id behaves like an unknown event: the buyer gets a 500 instead of "the event is not live yet".
cases.setup: A draft event with an unpublished RFQ round, owned by the run's buyer.
cases.steps: As the owner, `POST /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}` with `{"context": "general", "message_body": "QA_Platform_query_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: Should be refused (422 code 533). Today HTTP 500 at line 109; nothing saved.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.title: A query on a purchase request that does not exist
cases.why: The same endpoint serves purchase-request chats; that branch looks the request up within the caller's company and refuses cleanly.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/chats?module=PurchaseRequest&module_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` with `{"context": "general", "message_body": "QA_Platform_query_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 812 "Purchase Request not found".

cases.title: An unknown "regarding" value with a line item crashes
cases.why: Only general / technical / commercial are understood. Anything else reaches the title builder, which calls `T.must(nil)`. An unknown value should be a validation error.
cases.setup: A published RFQ. Safe to send: the error is raised while building the title, before `Chat.create!`.
cases.steps: As the buyer, `POST /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}` with `{"context": "QA_Platform_context", "reference_uuids": ["{{lineItemUuid}}"], "message_body": "QA_Platform_query_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. Today `get_chat_title` leaves `title` nil and `T.must(nil)` raises TypeError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect; the event's list stays empty afterwards.

cases.title: A query with no "regarding" and no line item is not refused
cases.why: Without a context the code takes the line-item branch with an empty list, loops zero times, creates nothing and still answers as if it succeeded (or crashes serialising a nil chat). The screen would say "Message posted successfully!" for a query that was never saved.
cases.setup: A published RFQ. Safe: the loop body (the only place a chat is created) never runs.
cases.steps: As the buyer, `POST /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}` with `{"message_body": "QA_Platform_query_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: Should be refused, HTTP 422 code 2 "Insufficient parameters". **Expected (today).** No chat is created and the reply is either HTTP 200 with `null` or HTTP 500 from serialising nil (`render json: nil, serializer: ChatSerializer`).
cases.oracle: Any 2xx or 5xx is the defect; the event's list stays empty.

cases.title: Attachments sent as text crash the request
cases.why: The attachments list is mapped with `to_unsafe_h` before anything is validated; a client that sends a string (or a list of strings) gets a 500.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer. The purchase-request module with an unknown id is used so that, if attachments were parsed, the request would still stop at 812 — nothing can be created either way.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/chats?module=PurchaseRequest&module_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` with `{"context": "general", "message_body": "QA_Platform_query_{{stamp}}", "attachments": "QA_Platform_not_a_list"}`.
cases.expected: Should be refused cleanly (422 code 2, or 812). Today `"…".map` raises NoMethodError at line 103 → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.title: An attachment without its file link crashes the request
cases.why: Each attachment value must carry `name` and `private_url`; the value object is built with required keyword arguments, so a missing key is an ArgumentError instead of a validation message.
cases.setup: As case 025 (unknown purchase request; nothing can be saved).
cases.steps: `POST /v1/chats?module=PurchaseRequest&module_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` with `{"context": "general", "message_body": "QA_Platform_query_{{stamp}}", "attachments": [{"type": "chats", "value": [{"name": "QA_Platform_file_{{stamp}}.pdf"}]}]}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 (code 2). Today `AttachmentValue.new(name:)` raises ArgumentError (missing keyword `private_url`) → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.title: An empty query is accepted
cases.why: The screen requires text or a file, but the API never checks `message_body`; a client can post an empty question that notifies the buyer.
cases.setup: A live event, QA vendor 1 invited. Manual (writes and e-mails the owner).
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `POST /v1/chats?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=:id` with `{"context": "general", "message_body": ""}` and no attachments.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. **Expected (today).** HTTP 200, a thread whose first message is blank.
cases.oracle: Thread list shows a thread with an empty `message`.

cases.title: A query on a withdrawn event is saved but nobody is told
cases.why: Create accepts withdrawn events (they are in `VALID_STATUSES_FOR_DASHBOARD`), but the e-mail worker looks the event up with `EventGroup.active` and silently stops. The vendor believes the buyer was notified.
cases.setup: A withdrawn event that QA vendor 1 was invited to. Manual.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, raise a general query on it; check the owner's mailbox.
cases.expected: Either refused (event withdrawn) or delivered. **Expected (today).** 200, thread saved, no "query raised" e-mail.
cases.oracle: Thread present; no mail.

cases.title: With the communication module switched off the API still works
cases.why: `show_communication_module` only hides the Messages button (console) and is passed to the vendor app in the event config; no chats action reads it. A company that turned queries off can still receive them from any client.
cases.setup: A company with `show_communication_module` OFF (read at `app/controllers/api/v1/users_controller.rb:591` and `app/controllers/concerns/event_group_controller_helper.rb:527`). Manual (config).
cases.steps: Confirm the Messages button is absent, then as QA vendor 1 raise a general query through the API.
cases.expected: Should be refused. **Expected (today).** 200.
cases.oracle: Thread created while the module is off.

cases.title: Opening a thread marks it read and tells a vendor how many others got the same query
cases.why: Show queues a "seen" update for every message and returns `siblings_count` (other chats in the same thread). For a vendor that is the number of OTHER vendors who received the buyer's query — competitive information.
cases.setup: A buyer query sent to QA vendors 1 and 2 (case 017). Manual.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `GET /v1/chats/:chatUuid`.
cases.expected: 200 with `body` (first message), later `conversations`, `message_to` = vendor 1 only. **Expected (today).** `siblings_count: 1` reveals a second recipient.
cases.oracle: `siblings_count` > 0 for a vendor.

cases.title: Opening a chat that does not exist
cases.why: Deep links from e-mails carry chat ids; a stale one must be a readable refusal.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 2 "Insufficient parameters" (the code the controller uses for "chat not found" here).
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: A chat without any message crashes the thread view
cases.why: Show reads `all_conversations[0].id` with no guard. The v1 show accepts ANY active chat, including one-to-one personal chats created empty by `GET /chats/get_chat_id`.
cases.setup: A personal chat between two QA buyers created with `GET /chats/get_chat_id?user_id=<colleague id>` and no message sent. Manual (writes a chat).
cases.steps: As either user, `GET /v1/chats/:personalChatUuid`.
cases.expected: Should be 200 with an empty body (or 422). Today `nil.id` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.title: Replying to a chat that does not exist
cases.why: The reply box keeps a chat id from an earlier screen; if the chat is gone the vendor must get a clean refusal.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 signed in.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `POST /v1/chats/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/send_message` with `{"message": "QA_Platform_reply_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: Refused, nothing sent. HTTP 422, code 2 "Insufficient parameters".
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: A reply with attachments sent as text crashes before the chat is even looked up
cases.why: Same unguarded `to_unsafe_h` as create, and it runs first, so even a request for a missing chat answers 500.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/chats/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/send_message` with `{"message": "QA_Platform_reply_{{stamp}}", "attachments": "QA_Platform_not_a_list"}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 (code 2). Today NoMethodError at line 163 → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.title: Muted team-mates get no e-mails but still get a push for every reply
cases.why: Muting is meant to keep the owner's colleagues quiet until a thread is assigned to them. The e-mail worker honours `muted: false`; the push notification sent on every new message goes to all participants.
cases.setup: A thread with a muted purchase-team member who has the mobile app / web push. Manual.
cases.steps: QA vendor 1 replies to the thread.
cases.expected: Muted member: no e-mail and no push. **Expected (today).** No e-mail, but a push.
cases.oracle: Push log for the muted member.

cases.title: Resolving a thread that does not exist
cases.why: A stale "Mark as Resolve" click must be refused clearly.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 signed in.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `POST /v1/chats/close?thread_id=QA_Platform_thread_{{stamp}}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 475 "Chat not found".

cases.title: Reassigning a thread that does not exist
cases.why: Same guard on the assign action; nothing is assigned and nobody is notified.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/chats/assign?thread_id=QA_Platform_thread_{{stamp}}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 475 "Chat not found".

cases.title: Assignee options for a thread that does not exist
cases.why: The assignee picker loads lazily; an unknown thread must not crash it.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats/assignee_options?thread_id=QA_Platform_thread_{{stamp}}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 475 "Chat not found".

cases.title: Closing a single chat that does not exist
cases.why: The per-chat close (`/:id/close_chat`) has its own lookup and code.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/chats/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/close_chat`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 475 "Chat not found".

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: The vendor picker without an event id crashes
cases.why: With the module but no id, no branch sets the participant list and the code maps over nil.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats/get_possible_participants?module=EventGroup`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. Today `nil.map` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: The vendor picker for an unknown onboarding response crashes
cases.why: The FxResponse branch calls `fetch_vendor_details` on the result of `find_by_id` without a nil check (and without any permission check).
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats/get_possible_participants?module=FxResponse&module_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: Should be 422. Today `nil.fetch_vendor_details` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: An invited vendor's line-item picker
cases.why: Vendors raise line-item queries too; the picker must open for an invited vendor.
cases.setup: A published RFQ with QA vendor 1 invited. Read only.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `GET /v1/chats/get_reference_options?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with the event's line item.
cases.oracle: 200; array.

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: The line-item picker for an unsupported module crashes
cases.why: Only EventGroup and PurchaseRequest set the line-item list; any other module name (including FxResponse, which the screen supports) maps over nil.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats/get_reference_options?module=FxResponse&module_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2 (or an empty list). Today `nil.map` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: The line-item picker without an event id
cases.why: This action, unlike the vendor picker, checks for a missing id first.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats/get_reference_options?module=EventGroup`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 2 "Insufficient parameters".
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: Deleted line items are offered for new queries
cases.why: The picker includes line items with status `deleted` (the filter list does not). A vendor can raise a query on an item the buyer already removed, which then lands on a line the buyer no longer sees.
cases.setup: A live event with two line items, one deleted after publishing (QA event). Manual.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, `GET /v1/chats/get_reference_options?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=:id`; compare with `GET /v1/chats/filter_options` (Line Item options).
cases.expected: Only active items. **Expected (today).** The deleted item is offered by the picker but not by the filter.
cases.oracle: Option count differs between the two calls.

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: The buyer's filter options for the thread list
cases.why: The filter bar (Line Item, Vendor, Status, Type) is built from this call.
cases.setup: A published RFQ. Read only.
cases.steps: As the buyer, `GET /v1/chats/filter_options?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200, `data` with four filters: `reference_uuids` (Line Item), `company_uuids` (Vendor), `resolution_status` (Closed/Open), `title` (General / Technical / Commercial).
cases.oracle: 200; four keys in that order.

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: Filter options for an event that does not exist
cases.why: This action does check existence first, so it is the clean counterpart of cases 014/055/061.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats/filter_options?module=EventGroup&module_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 533 "Project does not exist.".

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: Filter options without an event id crash
cases.why: With the module but no id, `eg` stays nil and is passed to a method typed `EventGroup` (and then dereferenced).
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats/filter_options?module=EventGroup`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. Today the Sorbet signature (or `nil.event_group_line_items`) raises → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.section: The pickers behind "New Message" — vendors, line items, filters
cases.title: Filter options on a draft event
cases.why: Drafts are excluded by status; the refusal must be clean.
cases.setup: A draft event with an unpublished RFQ round, owned by the run's buyer.
cases.steps: As the owner, `GET /v1/chats/filter_options?module=EventGroup&module_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 533 "Project does not exist.".

cases.section: Per-vendor unresolved counts on the comparison sheet — `GET /v1/chats/get_unresolved_queries_count`
cases.title: Per-vendor counts for a round that does not exist
cases.why: The round id is the only input; an unknown one must be refused.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats/get_unresolved_queries_count?event_uuid=Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 101 "You are not allowed to perform this action".

cases.section: Per-vendor unresolved counts on the comparison sheet — `GET /v1/chats/get_unresolved_queries_count`
cases.title: A vendor's queries on other events are counted on this round
cases.why: The "general" pattern is `%EG_<id>%` (no end anchor), so for event 12 it also matches general queries of events 120…, 1200…; the result is limited only to vendors who bid on this round. A vendor that asked something on another event shows an unresolved badge here.
cases.setup: Two QA events with prefix-related ids (see case 009) and the same QA vendor bidding on the shorter-id one with an open general query on the longer-id one. Manual.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/chats/get_unresolved_queries_count?event_uuid=:shortEventRound`.
cases.expected: `{}`. Today the vendor shows a count of 1.
cases.oracle: A count with no thread on this event.

cases.section: Personal one-to-one chats — `/chats` (console and vendor apps)
cases.title: Listing my personal chats
cases.why: The older chat inbox (not tied to an event) must open for any signed-in user.
cases.setup: The run's buyer. Read only.
cases.steps: `GET /chats`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with `total_unread_chats` and a `chats` list (possibly empty).

cases.section: Personal one-to-one chats — `/chats` (console and vendor apps)
cases.title: Opening a personal chat that does not exist
cases.why: Clean refusal for a stale deep link.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /chats/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 475 "Chat not found".

cases.section: Personal one-to-one chats — `/chats` (console and vendor apps)
cases.title: Messages of a personal chat that does not exist
cases.why: The conversation call uses a different code from the show call for the same "not found".
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /chats/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/conversations`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 15 "Operation failed".
cases.oracle: 422 code 15.

cases.section: Personal one-to-one chats — `/chats` (console and vendor apps)
cases.title: Starting a personal chat with a user who does not exist
cases.why: Starting a chat creates it on first call; the "may these two users talk" check must refuse before anything is created.
cases.setup: Any signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: `GET /chats/get_chat_id?user_id=999999999`.
cases.expected: Refused, no chat created. HTTP 422, code 101 "You are not allowed to perform this action".

cases.section: The pending list per event state — `GET /reminders/:id?resource_type=event_group`
cases.title: A draft event has nothing to remind
cases.why: The reminder service only looks at published (active) events; a draft must answer cleanly, not crash on rounds that have no schedule yet.
cases.setup: Draft event with an unpublished RFQ round (recipe `draft_rfq`), the caller is its owner. Read only.
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}?resource_type=event_group`.
cases.expected: The owner passes the view check, but the service finds no live event and answers an empty body (`null`). HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: 200 with body `null`. `EventGroup.active.find_by` skips drafts (`status` enum `active: 1, draft: 2`).

cases.section: The pending list per event state — `GET /reminders/:id?resource_type=event_group`
cases.title: An evaluator who has finished drops out; a re-evaluation request brings them back
cases.why: The list should chase only evaluators who still owe a score, including those asked to re-evaluate.
cases.setup: As API-EVDREM-007, one evaluator. Manual.
cases.steps: 1. Evaluator scores every response; read the list. 2. Buyer requests re-evaluation; read the list again.
cases.expected: 1: "Pending evaluations" empty. 2: the evaluator is listed again.
cases.oracle: `pending_evaluations` null after step 1, one recipient after step 2.

cases.section: The pending list per event state — `GET /reminders/:id?resource_type=event_group`
cases.title: Counter offers are listed only while the round's closing time is still ahead
cases.why: A counter offer is usually raised in negotiation after bidding closes; the list only looks at rounds whose closing time is in the future, so vendors sitting on a counter offer for a fully closed round may never be listed.
cases.setup: RFQ where the buyer sent QA vendor 1 a counter offer (bid in "requested" with `additional_request_type` `counter_offer_for_bid`). Read the list (a) while the round's closing time is ahead and (b) after it. Manual.
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/:eventUuid?resource_type=event_group` at (a) and (b).
cases.expected: (a) "Counter offers" lists QA vendor 1 with the round title. (b) Should still list the vendor while the counter offer is unanswered; today the round is filtered out once `closed_at` has passed — confirm whether counter offers extend `closed_at`; if not, record it as a gap.
cases.oracle: `counter_offers.recipients` at (a) and (b).

cases.section: The pending list per event state — `GET /reminders/:id?resource_type=event_group`
cases.title: Best-offer reminders list vendors asked for a best price who have not revised yet
cases.why: Only the vendors the buyer asked, and only those who have not yet sent a best-offer revision, should be chased, and only while the best-offer window is open.
cases.setup: Closed RFQ with bids from QA vendors 1 and 2; buyer requested best price from both; QA vendor 2 submitted its best offer. Manual.
cases.steps: Read the list during the best-offer window, then after it ends.
cases.expected: During: "Best offer submissions" lists QA vendor 1 only. After: empty.
cases.oracle: `best_offer_submissions.recipients` = [vendor 1]; null after the window.

cases.section: The pending list per event state — `GET /reminders/:id?resource_type=event_group`
cases.title: Cost-breakdown reminders list vendors with a quick bid during the cost-breakdown window
cases.why: Vendors who submitted a total-only (fast) bid must be chased for the item breakdown only while that window is open.
cases.setup: An auction with a cost-breakdown request window open; QA vendor 1's active bid is a fast bid. Manual.
cases.steps: Read the list inside and after the window.
cases.expected: Inside: "Cost breakdown submissions" lists QA vendor 1. After: empty.
cases.oracle: `cost_break_down_submissions.recipients`.

cases.section: The pending list per event state — `GET /reminders/:id?resource_type=event_group`
cases.title: Approval reminders list the pending approvers of the current step only
cases.why: Approvers of later steps or who already acted must not be chased.
cases.setup: An event with a pending approval request (two steps), step 1 approver pending. Manual.
cases.steps: Read the list; then approve step 1 and read again.
cases.expected: First read: "Approvals" lists the step-1 approver (columns Approver Name / Last Reminded At). Second read: the step-2 approver instead.
cases.oracle: `approvals.recipients[*].recipient_uuid`.

cases.section: The pending list per event state — `GET /reminders/:id?resource_type=event_group`
cases.title: A withdrawn event lists nothing
cases.why: A withdrawn event must not let the buyer chase vendors.
cases.setup: A withdrawn event of the QA buyer. Manual (no withdrawn recipe for the direct runner).
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/:eventUuid?resource_type=event_group`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with an empty body (`null`) — the view check passes on the withdrawn stages, the service ignores non-active events.
cases.oracle: Body `null`.

cases.title: A colleague who cannot see any stage of the event cannot read the list
cases.why: Viewing requires at least one stage the user may see (team / sharing rules).
cases.setup: A second PROCOL DEMO buyer with read permission but no team or share on the event. Manual.
cases.steps: As that buyer, `GET /reminders/:eventUuid?resource_type=event_group`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action'.

cases.title: A read-only buyer can open the list
cases.why: Reading needs only the read permission on events; a read-only user should see who is pending (sending is a separate permission, API-EVDREM-036).
cases.setup: A buyer with trade read but no create permission, on the event's team. Manual.
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/:eventUuid?resource_type=event_group`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with the same lists the owner sees.
cases.oracle: 200; same `offer_submissions` as the owner's read.
