cases.title: A garbled event id also crashes
cases.why: Same unguarded path with an id that decodes to nothing — the most common shape of a bad link.
cases.setup: Any buyer (recipe `none`).
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/WrongUuid1=?resource_type=event_group`.
cases.expected: Should be a clean 4xx. Today `EventGroup.find_by(id: nil)` → nil → `authorize(nil, …)` → `Pundit::NotDefinedError` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: 5xx = defect.

cases.title: An unknown resource type skips every permission check and reports an error as success
cases.why: With any type other than `event_group` the controller neither authorises nor looks anything up, and answers 200 with an error message — a caller (or monitoring) reading the status sees success.
cases.setup: The live RFQ (recipe `published_rfq`). Read only.
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}?resource_type=trade_request`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with body `{"error": "Reminders does not exist"}` and no permission check at all. Should be a 422 (unsupported resource type).
cases.oracle: 200 + that error text = today's behaviour (suspected defect: an error with a success status); a 5xx would be a new defect.

cases.title: A missing resource type behaves the same way
cases.why: The dashboard always sends the type; a client that forgets it should get a parameter error, not a 200.
cases.setup: Recipe `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}` (no query).
cases.expected: HTTP 200, `{"error": "Reminders does not exist"}`. Should be 422 code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 200 + error text today.

cases.title: The resource type is case-sensitive
cases.why: "EVENT_GROUP" is not recognised and silently gets the same 200-with-error answer, with no authorisation.
cases.setup: Recipe `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}?resource_type=EVENT_GROUP`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200, `{"error": "Reminders does not exist"}`.
cases.oracle: 200 + error text.

cases.title: A resource type sent as a list crashes the list
cases.why: `resource_type[]=…` makes the type an array, and the controller calls `to_sym` on it before anything else — an unguarded crash any client can trigger.
cases.setup: Recipe `published_rfq`. Read only (the crash happens before any lookup).
cases.steps: `GET /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}?resource_type[]=event_group`.
cases.expected: Should be a clean 422. Today `Array#to_sym` raises `NoMethodError` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: 5xx = defect.

cases.section: Sending a reminder — happy paths and read-backs (all manual: they email)
cases.title: The lock lifts after 10 minutes
cases.why: The boundary is "more than 10 minutes since the last reminder"; an off-by-one or a timezone slip would lock vendors for hours.
cases.setup: After API-EVDREM-025. Manual.
cases.steps: Read the list at 9 minutes and at 11 minutes after the send.
cases.expected: At 9 min `can_remind` false; at 11 min true, with the same last-reminded time.
cases.oracle: `can_remind` flips between the two reads.

cases.section: Sending a reminder — happy paths and read-backs (all manual: they email)
cases.title: The lock is per vendor and per kind of reminder, across all rounds
cases.why: The last-reminded time is stored per vendor per kind, not per round: reminding QA vendor 1 about the technical round also locks the reminder about the commercial round for 10 minutes, while a best-offer reminder stays available.
cases.setup: Live RFP+RFQ with both rounds open, QA vendor 1 pending on both. Manual.
cases.steps: Send an offer-submission reminder naming only the RFP round; read the list.
cases.expected: QA vendor 1's single offer-submission row (which lists both rounds under "Bid Pending For") is locked.
cases.oracle: One recipient row with two `uuids`, `can_remind` false.

cases.section: Sending a reminder — happy paths and read-backs (all manual: they email)
cases.title: Every active user of the vendor company receives the reminder
cases.why: The worker emails all active users of the vendor company, not only the contact who was invited; with large supplier companies that is a lot of people.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 company with two active users. Manual.
cases.steps: Send as in API-EVDREM-025.
cases.expected: Both QA vendor users receive the email (confirm this is the intended audience).
cases.oracle: Two mails, one per active user with an email address.

cases.section: Sending a reminder — happy paths and read-backs (all manual: they email)
cases.title: Sending an approval reminder
cases.why: The approval reminder names who asked for the approval; the subject carries the initiator's name.
cases.setup: As API-EVDREM-012. Manual.
cases.steps: Send `reminder_type` `approvals` with approver uuid → [approval request uuid].
cases.expected: 200 success; approver gets "[<ref>] | <initiator> Requires Your approval".
cases.oracle: Reminder row category `Approval`, recipient `u-<approver id>`.

cases.section: Sending a reminder — happy paths and read-backs (all manual: they email)
cases.title: Counter-offer, best-offer and cost-breakdown reminders carry the right subject
cases.why: Each kind has its own subject; a wrong one tells the vendor to do the wrong thing.
cases.setup: States from API-EVDREM-009/010/011. Manual.
cases.steps: Send each kind to QA vendor 1.
cases.expected: Counter offer: "[<ref>] | Action required: Counter Offer Sent by <buyer company>." Best offer: "[<ref>] [Reminder] Submit Your Best Offer Before the Deadline." Cost breakdown: "[<ref>] [Reminder] Submit Your Best Item Cost Breakdown."
cases.oracle: The three mail subjects.

cases.title: A read-only buyer cannot send reminders
cases.why: Sending needs the create permission on events; the drawer still offers the button (UI-EVDREM-063).
cases.setup: Same-company buyer with read but not create permission. Manual.
cases.steps: Send a valid offer-submission reminder.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 455; no reminder row.

cases.section: What the send does not check (suspected defects, all manual)
cases.title: A vendor who already bid can still be told to "submit your offer"
cases.why: The send does not re-check that the vendor is still pending.
cases.setup: Live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted. Manual.
cases.steps: Send `offer_submissions` for vendor 1 and the RFQ round.
cases.expected: Should be refused or skipped. Today: 200 and the vendor is emailed.
cases.oracle: Email received; `recipients_count` 1.

cases.section: What the send does not check (suspected defects, all manual)
cases.title: A reminder for a round whose deadline has passed is still sent
cases.why: "Submit before the deadline" with a deadline in the past confuses vendors.
cases.setup: Closed RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited without a bid. Manual.
cases.steps: Send `offer_submissions` for vendor 1 and the closed round.
cases.expected: Should be refused. Today: 200 and the email shows the past end time.
cases.oracle: Email body end time earlier than the send time.

cases.section: What the send does not check (suspected defects, all manual)
cases.title: The success count includes vendors who were sent nothing
cases.why: `recipients_count` is the number of keys in the map, even when none of a vendor's round ids resolved; the toast says "Reminders Sent to 2 Vendors" while only one was mailed — and a reminder row (with its 10-minute lock) is still written for the other.
cases.setup: Live RFQ, QA vendors 1 and 2. Manual.
cases.steps: Send `offer_submissions` with vendor 1 → [RFQ uuid] and vendor 2 → [`Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`].
cases.expected: Should report 1 recipient (or refuse the bad entry). Today: `recipients_count` 2; only vendor 1 is mailed; two reminder rows.
cases.oracle: Response count vs mailboxes vs reminder rows.

cases.section: What the send does not check (suspected defects, all manual)
cases.title: An approval request without a known requester crashes the send
cases.why: The approval reminder looks up the requester's name with `User.find_by(...).display_name`, unguarded.
cases.setup: A pending approval request whose `requested_by_user_id` is empty or points to a deleted user. Manual.
cases.steps: Send `approvals` with the approver → [that approval request uuid].
cases.expected: Should send with a fallback name. Today: `NoMethodError` → HTTP 500 (before any reminder row is written).
cases.oracle: 5xx = defect.

cases.title: A reminders map sent as text crashes
cases.why: Same line, different hostile shape.
cases.setup: Recipe `published_rfq`. Crashes on line 18, before anything else.
cases.steps: Same request with `"reminders": "QA_Platform_text_{{stamp}}"`.
cases.expected: Should be 422. Today `String#to_unsafe_h` → `NoMethodError` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: 5xx = defect.

cases.title: A reminders map sent as a list crashes
cases.why: A client that sends the recipients as a list (a natural mistake) gets a server error instead of a validation message.
cases.setup: Recipe `published_rfq`. Crashes on line 18.
cases.steps: Same request with `"reminders": ["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="]`.
cases.expected: Should be 422. Today `Array#to_unsafe_h` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: 5xx = defect.

cases.title: Sending with a garbled event id crashes
cases.why: Same path, id decodes to nothing.
cases.setup: Recipe `none`. Crashes at the permission check.
cases.steps: `POST /reminders/WrongUuid1=/send_reminder` with the body of API-EVDREM-051.
cases.expected: Should be a clean 4xx. Today HTTP 500 (`Pundit::NotDefinedError`).
cases.oracle: 5xx = defect.

cases.title: An unknown resource type on the send answers an empty success
cases.why: With no service the controller renders an unassigned variable: HTTP 200 with body `null` — the dashboard would read that as a success with nothing in it.
cases.setup: Recipe `published_rfq`. No service is built, nothing is looked up or sent.
cases.steps: `POST /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}/send_reminder` with `{"resource_type": "trade_request", "reminder_type": "offer_submissions", "reminders": {"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==": ["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="]}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with body `null`; no permission check. Should be a 422.
cases.oracle: 200 + `null` today; a 5xx would be a new defect.

cases.title: Sending on a draft event returns an error inside a success reply
cases.why: The owner passes the permission check, then the service (which only knows live events) returns `{error: true, code: 533}` — but with HTTP 200, so callers that trust the status think it was sent. (The drawer is hidden on drafts, so only API callers hit this.)
cases.setup: Draft RFQ (recipe `draft_rfq`), caller the owner. Returns on service line 35, before the map is read, any row is written or any email is queued.
cases.steps: `POST /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}/send_reminder` with `{"resource_type": "event_group", "reminder_type": "offer_submissions", "reminders": {"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==": ["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="]}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with body `{"error": true, "code": 533}` (533 means 'Project does not exist.'). Should be HTTP 422 with code 533 and its message.
cases.oracle: 200 + that body today (suspected defect: error with a success status); no reminder row.

cases.title: An auction reminder on an event without an auction returns an error inside a success reply
cases.why: The auction branch needs an auction stage in the map; on an RFQ-only event it bails out with code 533 ("Project does not exist." — the wrong meaning) and HTTP 200.
cases.setup: Live RFQ, no auction (recipe `published_rfq`). The map names QA vendor 1 and the RFQ round; the service returns on line 62, BEFORE `create_reminder_records` (line 68) and the email (line 69), so nothing is written or sent.
cases.steps: `POST /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}/send_reminder` with `{"resource_type": "event_group", "reminder_type": "auction_reminders", "reminders": {"{{vendorUuid}}": ["{{pricingTradeUuid}}"]}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 with body `{"error": true, "code": 533}`. Should be a 422 saying the event has no auction to remind about.
cases.oracle: 200 + that body; no reminder row, no email to QA vendor 1.

cases.title: An auction reminder with unknown ids after the round closed returns the same error-as-success
cases.why: Unknown round ids resolve to nothing, so no auction is found; same early return on a closed event.
cases.setup: Closed RFQ with a bid (recipe `closed_rfq_with_bid`). Returns on line 62, before any write or email.
cases.steps: `POST /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}/send_reminder` with `{"resource_type": "event_group", "reminder_type": "auction_reminders", "reminders": {"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==": ["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="]}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200, body `{"error": true, "code": 533}`.
cases.oracle: 200 + that body.

cases.title: A numeric reminder kind crashes
cases.why: Same unvalidated field, a different hostile type.
cases.setup: Recipe `published_rfq`. Crash at base service line 40, before the insert and the email.
cases.steps: As API-EVDREM-057 with `"reminder_type": 5`.
cases.expected: Should be 422. Today `Integer#singularize` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: 5xx = defect.

cases.title: A vendor's round list sent as text crashes
cases.why: Each map value must be a list of round ids; a single id sent as text reaches `.map` on a String.
cases.setup: Recipe `published_rfq`, caller the owner (passes the permission check). Crash on service line 38, before any row or email.
cases.steps: `POST /reminders/{{eventGroupUuid}}/send_reminder` with `{"resource_type": "event_group", "reminder_type": "offer_submissions", "reminders": {"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==": "Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="}}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422. Today `String#map` → `NoMethodError` → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: 5xx = defect.

cases.title: Sending on a withdrawn event returns the error-as-success reply
cases.why: Same as the draft case; the drawer IS shown on withdrawn events, so a user can reach it (see UI-EVDREM-070).
cases.setup: A withdrawn QA-buyer event. Manual (no withdrawn recipe for the direct runner).
cases.steps: Send a valid offer-submission body.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 `{"error": true, "code": 533}`; nothing sent.
cases.oracle: That body; no reminder row.

cases.title: An empty reminders map reports success with zero recipients
cases.why: Nothing is written, but an (empty) email job is still queued and the reply says "Reminders sent successfully." with count 0.
cases.setup: Live RFQ. Manual: the code reaches `send_reminder_email` (it enqueues a worker), which the direct runner must not do.
cases.steps: Send `{"resource_type": "event_group", "reminder_type": "offer_submissions", "reminders": {}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 `{"success": true, "message": "Reminders sent successfully.", "recipients_count": 0, ...}`. Should be 422 (nobody selected).
cases.oracle: Count 0; no reminder row (`create_reminder_records` returns on blank); one no-op `ReminderWorker` job.

journeys.title: Vendors declining lines and buyers rejecting bids
journeys.goal: A vendor declines (regrets) some lines with a reason and the buyer sees it; the buyer rejects a bid and the vendor, the comparison and the award all treat it as rejected.

cases.title: The award cell is disabled and reads "Regretted"
cases.why: This screen guard is the only thing stopping an award of a regretted line (API-EVDRGT-053).
cases.setup: As 050, with an award proposal open.
cases.steps: Try to award vendor 1 on line 2.
cases.expected: The cell is disabled with the text "Regretted".
cases.oracle: No add_response request is sent.

cases.title: 'Remove bid' on a live event shows 'bid discarded' although the bid stays
cases.why: Mirrors API-EVDRJB-028 on the screen the buyer uses.
cases.setup: A live event with QA vendor 1's submitted bid, opened in the edit/audience view.
cases.steps: 1. Remove the vendor's bid from the audience view. 2. Refresh the event.
cases.expected: Today: the success toast appears and the bid is still there after refresh.
cases.oracle: Bid visible after refresh.

cases.title: The comparison cell shows a "Regretted" tag for a regretted line
cases.why: The buyer must see at a glance which vendor declined which line.
cases.setup: As API-EVDRGT-050 (vendor 1 regretted line 2), or 011 (regretted then re-quoted).
cases.steps: Open the event's quote comparison.
cases.expected: Vendor 1's line-2 cell shows the REGRET tag and no "0" quantity filler. In the 011 situation the tag sits next to a live price — the stale-flag defect made visible.
cases.oracle: Tag text equals the server's `status.label`.

cases.title: "Select all items" for awarding skips regretted lines
cases.why: Bulk awarding must not sneak a regretted line in.
cases.setup: As 069, select-all enabled.
cases.steps: Click select-all for vendor 1.
cases.expected: Only line 1 is selected; the master checkbox shows checked once line 1 is awarded.
cases.oracle: Requests sent contain line 1 only.

cases.title: The line-status checkbox is unchecked and inactive for regretted lines
cases.why: Status toggles on a regretted line must not be editable.
cases.steps: Open the comparison sheet; inspect vendor 1's line-2 status cell.
cases.expected: Checkbox unchecked and inactive.
cases.oracle: No toggle request on click.

cases.title: A regretted line shows the event's "Regret" score in the evaluation cell
cases.why: The score shown must match the one the server auto-creates (API-EVDRGT-052).
cases.setup: RFP with evaluation; vendor 1 regretted a line technically; event score mapping with and without a "Regret" entry.
cases.steps: Open the technical evaluation grid.
cases.expected: The cell shows the Regret score; if the mapping has no "Regret" value the score is blank — record it.
cases.oracle: Cell score equals mapping score for "Regret".

cases.title: "Reason for not participating" shows raw list brackets and also acceptance remarks
cases.why: The column prints `reason.to_s + ", " + remarks`; a list of reasons appears as `["Price not feasible"]`, an acceptance with a remark appears as a "reason for not participating", and round-level declines (058) never appear.
cases.setup: A live event; QA vendor 1 declines with `reason: ["A", "B"]` and a remark; another run accepts with a remark.
cases.steps: Open Participants on the event.
cases.expected: Readable reasons ("A, B — remark"); acceptances not shown in this column. Today: brackets and quotes, and accept remarks shown.
cases.oracle: Column text.

cases.title: The participants stage column says "bid placed" for a vendor whose bid vanished through regret
cases.why: After 006 the round shows no bid, but Participants still says the vendor bid.
cases.setup: As API-EVDRGT-006.
cases.steps: Open Participants; read the RFQ stage column for vendor 1; compare with the round's bid count.
cases.expected: Should read "regretted"/"no bid". Today "bid placed" (revised bids count).
cases.oracle: Column value vs `bid_count` 0.

cases.title: The invitation delivery list and the participants table disagree about a decline
cases.why: Delivery stats read round-level and event-level answers; Participants reads event-level only — the same vendor looks declined in one place and silent in the other.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 declines at round level (058).
cases.steps: Open the round's sellers/delivery list (`GET /trade/:id/bidders_delivery_stats`) and the event's Participants.
cases.expected: Both show the decline. Today only the delivery list carries it.
cases.oracle: `user.user_intents[0].intent_type` = "trade_reject" vs empty Participants column.

cases.title: The RFI builder's "Regret Item" column action fills every row with "Regret"
cases.why: This is how a technical-round regret is entered; it feeds API-EVDRGT-054/055 and evaluation auto-scoring.
cases.setup: An RFI/RFP template open in the builder with the default action column.
cases.steps: Use the column header action "Regret Item".
cases.expected: Each row's `rfi_response` becomes "Regret"; on submit the server marks those lines regretted for the vendor.
cases.oracle: Saved form response values "Regret".

cases.title: The reject dialog will not send without a reason
cases.why: The reason is mandatory only in the browser (the API accepts none, API-EVDRJB-007).
cases.setup: A live event with a submitted bid, opened as the buyer.
cases.steps: 1. Open the bid's Reject dialog. 2. Leave the reason empty. 3. Press Reject.
cases.expected: The dialog shows the reason error and sends nothing.
cases.oracle: No PATCH /bids/:id/reject is sent; the field shows its error.

cases.title: 'Allow re-bidding' is ticked by default
cases.why: Blocking a vendor is the exception and must be a deliberate choice.
cases.setup: As UI-EVDRJB-001.
cases.steps: 1. Open the Reject dialog.
cases.expected: The re-bidding box is ticked; unticking shows the 'block supplier' warning.
cases.oracle: Checkbox checked on open.

cases.title: A vendor already blocked cannot be unblocked from the dialog
cases.why: Once blocked, the checkbox is disabled and shows 'supplier blocked'.
cases.setup: A vendor rejected earlier without re-bidding.
cases.steps: 1. Open the Reject dialog for that vendor's next bid.
cases.expected: The checkbox is unticked and disabled, with the blocked message.
cases.oracle: Disabled checkbox.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: A line of another event is accepted and, on submit, written into that event
cases.why: The service finds the line by id across the whole platform and never checks it belongs to the bid's event. A vendor can mark itself "regretted" on any event's line (even one it is not invited to); on submit the raw SQL update writes the vendor id into that line's `participants`, which shows up in the other buyer's comparison, evaluation and AI data.
cases.setup: NOT runnable: the only foreign line id a run could use would be a real record. Use two test events of the run's own buyer, A and B, with QA vendor 1 invited to A only.
cases.steps: 1. On A's draft, regret with B's line id in the path. 2. Price A's line and submit.
cases.expected: Step 1 should be refused (808 or 101). Today 200; after step 2 B's line has `participants[<vendor 1>]` = "regretted".
cases.oracle: DB read of B's line after step 2.

cases.title: A vendor cannot regret a line on another vendor's draft
cases.why: Cross-company tampering with an unsent quote.
cases.setup: A live RFQ with QA vendors 1 and 2 both bidding; QA vendor 2 opens a new draft (round setting `lock_quote_after_submission` off).
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, regret on vendor 2's draft id with `company_uuid` = vendor 1.
cases.expected: Refused: vendor 2's draft is outside vendor 1's companies. HTTP 422, code 32 'Bid not found'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 32; vendor 2's draft unchanged.

cases.title: An uninvited vendor cannot regret in another vendor's name
cases.why: Naming someone else's company must be refused before any lookup.
cases.setup: A live RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited with an open draft; QA vendor 2 not invited.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 2, regret on vendor 1's draft with `company_uuid` = vendor 1.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: The buyer rejects a submitted bid while bidding is open
cases.why: Rejecting a non-compliant quote is the buyer's main lever before the close; if it fails the buyer has to cancel the whole event.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; `disable_reject_bid_in_bidding_time` is off on the round.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject QA vendor 1's bid with a reason, allowing re-bidding: `PATCH /bids/{{bidUuid}}/reject` with `{"rejection_remarks": "QA_Platform_reject_{{stamp}}", "allow_rebidding": true}`.
cases.expected: The bid is rejected and the reason is stored for the vendor. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: HTTP 200; the bid no longer counts as active (see API-EVDRJB-008: a second rejection is refused).

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: Rejecting without allowing re-bidding puts the vendor on the round's block list
cases.why: The block list is the only thing that stops a rejected vendor from quoting again, and the dashboard greys the vendor out from it; if it is not written, the block silently does nothing.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid with `"allow_rebidding": false`. 2. Read the round back as the buyer (`GET /trade/{{tradeId}}?response_type=template`).
cases.expected: The round's settings now list QA vendor 1 as not allowed to re-bid. HTTP 200 on both calls.
cases.oracle: `misc.not_allow_rebidding_to_sellers` in the round reply contains QA vendor 1's company id (the serializer encodes it for the buyer).

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: A vendor blocked from re-bidding cannot place a new bid
cases.why: If the block does not hold, a rejected vendor simply re-quotes and the buyer's decision is undone.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid with `"allow_rebidding": false`. 2. As QA vendor 1, try to place a new bid (open, price, submit).
cases.expected: Step 2 is refused at the first call. HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.
cases.oracle: Step 2 answers code 101; no new bid exists.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: A vendor allowed to re-bid can quote again after the rejection
cases.why: 'Allow re-bidding' is the dialog's default; a vendor wrongly blocked loses the event without being told why.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid with `"allow_rebidding": true`. 2. As QA vendor 1, place a new bid.
cases.expected: Step 2 is accepted — the rejected bid does not count as an existing quote. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: The new bid's submit answers 200.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: Rejecting one vendor's bid leaves the other vendor's bid active
cases.why: A rejection must touch one company only; a wrong scope would wipe every quote on the round.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ with QA vendors 1 and 2, each with a submitted bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject QA vendor 1's bid. 2. Reject QA vendor 2's bid.
cases.expected: Step 2 is accepted — vendor 2's bid was still active after step 1. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: Step 2 answers 200 (the action only accepts an active bid).

cases.section: The vendor discards its own draft bid
cases.title: Another vendor cannot discard my draft
cases.why: One vendor must never be able to wipe another vendor's quote; the lookup is limited to the caller's own drafts.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ; QA vendor 1 opens a bid; QA vendor 2 is a different company.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, open a bid. 2. As QA vendor 2, discard QA vendor 1's draft.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 250 'No such bid exists'.
cases.oracle: Code 250; vendor 1's draft is untouched.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: A buyer of another company cannot reject the bid
cases.why: The policy allows only the owner, a super admin, a CSM or the auction team of a company that can view the event.
cases.setup: A buyer user of a different company. Manual: the run signs in one buyer only.
cases.steps: 1. As the other company's buyer, reject the bid.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action'.
cases.oracle: Code 455; the bid is still active.

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: A vendor regrets a line on its own draft bid
cases.why: This is the "I cannot supply this item" button; if it fails the vendor has to leave the line blank and the buyer cannot tell a decline from a forgotten line.
cases.setup: A live RFQ with QA vendor 1 invited; the vendor has opened a draft bid and priced nothing.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1 (vendor app), `PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/line_items/{{lineItemUuid}}/regret_status` with `{"company_uuid": "{{vendorUuid}}", "trade_request_uuid": "{{tradeId}}", "action_type": "regret"}`.
cases.expected: Accepted. The reply echoes the bid and labels the line as regretted; nothing changes on the line for the buyer yet — the regret only lives in the draft until the vendor saves or submits. HTTP 200 with `bid_uuid` and `status: {"value": "regretted", "label": "REGRET"}`.
cases.oracle: 200; the draft's `meta_data.regretted_eglis` has the line with status "draft" (DB read), and the line's `participants` is unchanged.

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: Undoing a regret before submitting gives a normal bid
cases.why: Vendors change their minds; an undone regret must leave no trace when they then quote and submit.
cases.setup: A live RFQ, QA vendor 1's draft with the line regretted (helper H01).
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH …/regret_status` with `"action_type": "undo_regret"`. 2. Price the line. 3. Submit the bid. 4. As the buyer, read the round.
cases.expected: The undo is accepted (the draft entry is removed; the line was never written as regretted, so nothing else changes), the bid submits normally and the buyer sees one live bid. Undo answers HTTP 200 with `status: {"value": null, "label": null}`.
cases.oracle: Buyer `GET /trade/{{tradeId}}` → `bid_count` is 1.

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: Regretting the only line and submitting leaves the vendor with no live bid
cases.why: The submit says "success" but the bid silently disappears: the vendor thinks it has quoted, the buyer's count of bids drops, yet the buyer's participants list still says "bid placed".
cases.setup: A live one-round RFQ with one line; QA vendor 1's draft with the line regretted (step 1 of this case).
cases.steps: 1. Regret the line. 2. Price it. 3. Submit the bid. 4. As the buyer read the round and the event's participants (`GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_audience`).
cases.expected: The submit is accepted. Right after activating the bid the server writes "regretted" onto the line for this vendor, marks the draft entry "processed", drops the priced line and — because no line is left — turns the whole bid "revised". The buyer's round shows no live bid, while the participants list still counts the vendor under "bid placed" (it includes revised bids). Submit answers HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: Buyer round `bid_count` = 0; `get_audience` → `stages[*].bid_placed_company_uuids` still contains the vendor; DB: the bid's status is revised, the line's `meta_data.participants[<vendor id>]` = "regretted", `participants_data[<vendor id>].flow` = "Regretted in Commercial".

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: Regretting every line on a new draft withdraws an already-submitted bid
cases.why: There is no "withdraw my quote" button for vendors, but this path does exactly that, during bidding, without any buyer approval or audit wording that says "withdrawn".
cases.setup: A live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has a submitted bid; the round's `lock_quote_after_submission` is off and no price-change approval applies.
cases.steps: 1. Open a new draft (it starts with the live bid's lines). 2. Regret the only line. 3. Re-price at 95. 4. Submit. 5. As the buyer, read the round.
cases.expected: The submit is accepted as a revision: the old bid becomes "revised", the new one is activated and then, because its only line is regretted, also turned "revised". The vendor ends with no live bid. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: Buyer round `bid_count` = 0.

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: Undo after submitting is refused because the bid is no longer a draft
cases.why: Once submitted, the regret can no longer be taken back through this button; the vendor needs to be told clearly.
cases.setup: A live RFQ; QA vendor 1 regretted the line, priced it and submitted (the bid is now revised).
cases.steps: `PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/line_items/{{lineItemUuid}}/regret_status` with `"action_type": "undo_regret"` on the submitted bid.
cases.expected: Refused: only draft bids are looked up. HTTP 422, code 32 'Bid not found'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 32; the line stays "regretted".

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: Opening a fresh draft does not let the vendor undo a submitted regret
cases.why: The only remaining route to "un-regret" is a new draft, and it silently does nothing: the line stays regretted for this vendor for the rest of the event.
cases.setup: As 009; then the vendor opens a new draft (a new bid row — the old draft is no longer draft, and a new draft starts with empty `meta_data`).
cases.steps: 1. Open a new draft. 2. `undo_regret` on the line. 3. Read the line's `participants` (DB) or the vendor's round view.
cases.expected: Step 2 answers 200 (status null) but changes nothing: the new draft has no `regretted_eglis` entry, and only a "processed" entry on the same bid resets the line to "participated". Should either reset the line or refuse with a clear message.
cases.oracle: `participants[<vendor id>]` is still "regretted" after a 200.

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: One-round event: the vendor can quote again on a regretted line, but the line stays flagged
cases.why: After a submitted regret the vendor can bid on the same line again and the bid is accepted, yet the line keeps saying "regretted" for this vendor — the buyer's comparison shows a REGRET tag and disables awarding on a line that carries a live price.
cases.setup: A live one-round RFQ; QA vendor 1 regretted, priced and submitted (bid revised, line regretted).
cases.steps: 1–3 as 006. 4. Place a fresh bid on the line (open, price, submit). 5. As the buyer read the round.
cases.expected: The new bid is accepted: in a one-round event neither the price check (736) nor the submit check (800) runs, and the new draft carries no regret. The buyer sees one live bid. The stale "regretted" flag is the defect: the line should no longer be marked regretted once the vendor quotes it.
cases.oracle: Buyer round `bid_count` = 1; DB: `participants[<vendor id>]` still "regretted"; buyer comparison cell shows the REGRET tag (UI-EVDRGT-068).

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: Two-round event: a submitted regret blocks quoting that line again
cases.why: With a technical round, the commercial regret is enforced from then on; the vendor must get the specific "you declined this line" message.
cases.setup: A live RFP+RFQ; QA vendor 1 submitted its technical response, then in the RFQ regretted the line, priced and submitted (bid revised).
cases.steps: 1–3 as 006 in the RFQ. 4. Place a fresh bid on the same line.
cases.expected: The new draft opens, but pricing the line is refused. HTTP 422, code 736 'You have declined to provide this line item; therefore, you are not permitted to quote for it commercially'.
cases.oracle: The place-bid price step answers 422 code 736; buyer `bid_count` stays 0.

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: Saving a draft makes the regret permanent before the vendor submits
cases.why: "Save draft" is not a submission, yet it writes "regretted" onto the line for everyone to see (buyer comparison, evaluation auto-scoring, lot splitting, AI dataset) even if the vendor never submits.
cases.setup: A live RFQ; QA vendor 1's draft with one line regretted. Needs the vendor app's draft-save body (`PATCH /v1/bids/:id` with `status: "draft"` and global data); not runnable from the op list.
cases.steps: 1. Save the draft. 2. Read the line (DB) and the bid's `regretted_eglis`. 3. `undo_regret`.
cases.expected: Step 1 runs the same "mark regretted" step as a submit (it sits after the draft branch), so the line becomes "regretted" and the entry "processed". Step 3 then resets the line to "participated" and clears `participants_data`. Should only take effect on submit.
cases.oracle: After step 1 `participants[<vendor id>]` = "regretted" while the bid is still draft; after step 3 = "participated".

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: Saving a draft after regretting every priced line removes the draft
cases.why: The vendor's draft vanishes on "Save": the clean-up that drops regretted lines also runs for drafts and turns a draft with no remaining line into "revised".
cases.setup: As 014, with every priced line regretted.
cases.steps: 1. Save the draft. 2. Try any further regret or price on it.
cases.expected: Step 1 answers 200 but the bid becomes "revised"; step 2 is refused with 422 code 32 'Bid not found'. Should keep the draft.
cases.oracle: DB bid status revised after a draft save.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: An unknown action is refused
cases.why: Only "regret" and "undo_regret" are meaningful; anything else must not touch the bid. (Vendor-side twin of EDGE-BID-099.)
cases.setup: QA vendor 1's open draft.
cases.steps: `PATCH …/regret_status` with `"action_type": "delete"`.
cases.expected: Refused, bid untouched. HTTP 422, code 805 'Invalid action type'.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: A line that does not exist is refused
cases.why: A guessed line id must not be stored in the bid.
cases.steps: Path `/v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/line_items/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/regret_status`, action regret.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 808 'Line item not found'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 808; `regretted_eglis` empty.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: The round is required
cases.why: The round ties the regret to the bid's own stage.
cases.steps: The 001 body without `trade_request_uuid`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 95 'Trade Request not found'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 95.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: Another round of the same event is refused
cases.why: The regret must apply to the round the bid belongs to, not the technical round next to it.
cases.setup: A live RFP+RFQ; QA vendor 1 submitted its technical response and opened an RFQ draft.
cases.steps: Regret with `"trade_request_uuid": "{{rfpTradeId}}"` (the technical round).
cases.expected: Refused: the round exists but is not the bid's. HTTP 422, code 95 'Trade Request not found'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 95.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: The vendor company is required
cases.why: The company is what gets marked regretted on the line.
cases.steps: The 001 body without `company_uuid`.
cases.expected: Refused by the controller's first check. HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: A bid that does not exist is "Bid not found" (code 32, not 806)
cases.why: Corrects EDGE-BID-100, which expects 806: the controller refuses first with 32, so the service's 806 is dead code.
cases.setup: A live RFQ.
cases.steps: Path bid `Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` with a valid body.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 32 'Bid not found'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 32.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: A submitted bid cannot be regretted directly (code 32, never 807)
cases.why: `VALID_STATUSES_TO_REGRET` lists active/selected/requested too, which suggests submitted bids were meant to be regrettable; the controller only looks at drafts, so 807 'Bid status is not valid' can never be returned.
cases.setup: A live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; no draft open.
cases.steps: Regret on `{{bidUuid}}` (the submitted bid).
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 32 'Bid not found'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 32.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: Any unexpected error inside the regret becomes an untyped 500
cases.why: The catch-all builds its failure with one argument while `failure` needs two, so instead of a readable error the rescue itself raises `ArgumentError` and the vendor gets a 500.
cases.setup: Any path that raises inside `process_regret_action` (a failing `save!`, a nil association in `validate`, see 036).
cases.steps: Trigger the error and send a regret.
cases.expected: Should be a typed 422 ('An unexpected error occurred…'). Today: HTTP 500 — `ServiceResult.failure("An unexpected error occurred: …")` → wrong number of arguments (given 1, expected 2).
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: In a lot-split event, regretting crashes when any line has never been touched by a vendor
cases.why: The lot rule reads `egli.participants[<vendor>]` on every active line; `participants` is nil until a technical response or a regret writes it, so the first regret in such an event raises and (via 035) answers 500.
cases.setup: A lot-split event where at least one active line has no `participants` hash (e.g. no technical round, or a line without a technical form). Needs lot split; no twin.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, regret any line on a draft in a lot stage.
cases.expected: Should be 200 (or 844 when it would regret every line). Today suspected HTTP 500: NoMethodError on nil → rescue → ArgumentError.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: A buyer calling the regret route is refused and signed out
cases.why: Regret is a vendor-app action; a buyer token gets 401 and the backend deactivates the buyer's console session. EDGE-BID-099..102 were written to run as the buyer, so they only ever exercise this refusal.
cases.setup: Manual only (a runnable twin would sign the QA buyer out).
cases.steps: As the buyer (console app), send the 001 request.
cases.expected: HTTP 401 'This app is not authorized to use this API' and the buyer's session becomes inactive.
cases.oracle: 401; the next console call is unauthenticated.

cases.title: A vendor cannot name another company on its own draft
cases.why: Prevents marking a competitor as "regretted" on a line (the company in the body is what gets written onto the line).
cases.setup: A live RFQ; QA vendor 1's open draft.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, regret with `company_uuid` = QA vendor 2.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.

cases.section: State of the event and the round
cases.title: No regret on a withdrawn event
cases.why: After withdrawal every round is inactive; a late regret must not be stored.
cases.setup: A live RFQ; QA vendor 1 opens a draft; the buyer withdraws the event.
cases.steps: As QA vendor 1, regret on the draft.
cases.expected: Refused: the round is no longer active. HTTP 422, code 95 'Trade Request not found'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 95.

cases.section: How the buyer, evaluation and award see a regret
cases.title: The buyer's comparison labels a regretted line "REGRET" for that vendor only
cases.why: Per-vendor labelling: one vendor's regret must not grey the line for others.
cases.setup: Two lines, two QA vendors; vendor 1 regrets line 2 and submits a price for line 1; vendor 2 quotes both. Needs a two-line event.
cases.steps: As the buyer, `GET /trade/{{tradeId}}?response_type=template` and read each vendor's line status.
cases.expected: Vendor 1 line 2: status `{"value": "regretted", "label": "REGRET"}`; vendor 2 line 2: its normal status. Vendor 1 keeps a live bid on line 1.
cases.oracle: The two statuses differ only for vendor 1.

cases.section: How the buyer, evaluation and award see a regret
cases.title: A commercial regret becomes an automatic "Regret" technical score
cases.why: When an evaluator submits the technical evaluation, every vendor listed as "regretted" on a line gets an automatic Regret score — including vendors who regretted only in the RFQ and answered the technical form fully. This can disqualify them from award (EVAL-TNA-004).
cases.setup: RFP+RFQ; QA vendor 1 answers the technical form (no "Regret"), then regrets the line in the RFQ and submits; the event has a "Regret" score label. Needs an evaluator flow.
cases.steps: Submit the technical evaluation without scoring vendor 1 on that line.
cases.expected: An evaluation with the Regret score is created for vendor 1. If the event has no "Regret" label the auto score is nil — record what the evaluation submit then answers.
cases.oracle: `evaluation_scores` row for vendor 1 with the regret score.

cases.section: How the buyer, evaluation and award see a regret
cases.title: Awarding a commercially regretted line is blocked only on screen
cases.why: The server's award check (EDGE-AWD-114) blocks lines by their evaluation SCORE only; a line that is "regretted" in `participants` but never scored passes the API, while the screen greys it out.
cases.setup: Two lines; QA vendor 1 regrets line 2 and later quotes it again (011), so a live price exists; `restrict_awarding_for_tna_vendors` on; no evaluation score. Needs two lines and a proposal.
cases.steps: `POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/add_response?lot_no=` awarding line 2 to vendor 1.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 1136 'One or more selected line items cannot be awarded as they have been marked as Regret'. Today 200 — `validate_tna_for_awarding` reads `evaluation_score_for`, never `participants`.
cases.oracle: Proposal response for line 2 exists after a 200.

cases.section: How the buyer, evaluation and award see a regret
cases.title: A technical "Regret" answer splits the vendor's commercial bid — unless it covers every line
cases.why: The two regret paths behave differently: a commercial regret of every line kills the bid (006), a technical regret of every line leaves the full commercial bid active.
cases.setup: RFP+RFQ; QA vendor 1 has an active RFQ bid on two lines. Needs two lines.
cases.steps: 1. Submit the technical response with "Regret" on line 2. 2. Read vendor 1's bids. 3. Repeat on a fresh event with "Regret" on both lines.
cases.expected: Case 1: the old bid becomes revised and a copy with only line 1 becomes active. Case 2: nothing is dropped — only a recompute runs, the bid stays active on both lines. Should drop (or revise) the bid in case 2 as well.
cases.oracle: Case 2: an active bid still prices both regretted lines.

cases.title: A vendor's event-level decline reaches the buyer's participants list
cases.why: "Reason for not participating" is the buyer's only view of why a vendor said no.
cases.setup: A live RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, `POST /user_intents` with `{"item_uuid": "{{eventGroupUuid}}", "item_type": "EventGroup", "intent_type": "trade_reject", "reason": ["QA_Platform_reason_{{stamp}}"], "remarks": "QA_Platform_decline_{{stamp}}"}`. 2. As the buyer, `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_audience`.
cases.expected: The decline is saved and the vendor's row shows the reason and remark. HTTP 200 `{"success": true}`.
cases.oracle: `vendors[*].user_intent` contains "QA_Platform_decline_{{stamp}}".

cases.title: A declined vendor can still bid, and the buyer sees both answers at once
cases.why: Goes deeper than XMAT-051 / EDGE-BID-016-017: none of the bid routes read the decline, so the buyer's list shows a "reason for not participating" next to a vendor marked "bid placed".
cases.setup: A live RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited.
cases.steps: 1. Event-level decline as in 057. 2. Vendor places a full bid. 3. As the buyer read `get_audience`.
cases.expected: Both accepted; the vendor row keeps the decline text and the stage lists the vendor as bid placed. Either the bid should be refused or the decline cleared when the vendor bids.
cases.oracle: `vendors[*].user_intent` contains the decline remark AND `stages[*].bid_placed_company_uuids` contains `{{vendorUuid}}`.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: Sending 'allow re-bidding' as the text "false" does not block the vendor
cases.why: The code compares the flag with the boolean false only, so any caller sending text booleans (forms, integrations) silently loses the block.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject with `"allow_rebidding": "false"` (text). 2. As QA vendor 1, place a new bid.
cases.expected: Step 2 is accepted — the vendor was not blocked. Should be treated like false (suspected looseness); today HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: Step 2 answers 200; `misc.not_allow_rebidding_to_sellers` is empty.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: A rejection with no reason is accepted by the API
cases.why: The dashboard refuses to send a rejection without a reason, but the API stores one with an empty remark — the vendor is told nothing about why.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid with only `{"allow_rebidding": true}` (no `rejection_remarks`).
cases.expected: Today the rejection is stored with an empty reason (HTTP 200). Should be refused like the dialog does (suspected gap: the Remark model has no presence rule).
cases.oracle: HTTP 200; the rejected-bids list shows the bid with no remark.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: Rejecting the same bid twice is refused
cases.why: A double click or a retried request must not record two rejections or re-run the side effects (remarks, block list, re-activating an older revision).
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid. 2. Reject the same bid again.
cases.expected: Step 2 is refused because the bid is no longer active. HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.
cases.oracle: Step 2 answers code 101.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: A draft bid the vendor has not sent cannot be rejected
cases.why: The buyer must not act on a quote the vendor has not submitted.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ; QA vendor 1 opens a bid and leaves it as a draft.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, open a bid (`POST /v1/bids`). 2. As the buyer, reject that draft.
cases.expected: Step 2 is refused. HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.
cases.oracle: Code 101.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: A bid can be rejected after bidding has closed
cases.why: Buyers reject non-compliant quotes during evaluation; the reject action has no time rule, and the 'disable while bidding' setting applies only while the round runs.
cases.setup: A fresh RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid and the bidding window plus extra closing time are over.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid.
cases.expected: Accepted. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: HTTP 200.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: A bid on a withdrawn event cannot be rejected
cases.why: Withdrawing marks every live round in_active; nothing may change on a withdrawn event afterwards.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, withdraw the event with a remark. 2. Reject the vendor's bid.
cases.expected: Step 2 is refused. HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.
cases.oracle: Code 101; the event stays withdrawn.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: A bid on a submitted award cannot be rejected
cases.why: Rejecting a bid that is already on an award proposal would leave the award pointing at a rejected quote.
cases.setup: A fresh RFQ the QA vendor bid on, closed, and awarded to that vendor (award submitted).
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the awarded vendor's bid.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 785 'Can not reject a bid which is selected for proposal' (or code 101 if submitting the proposal already moved the bid out of the active state).
cases.oracle: A refusal (422), never 200; the proposal is unchanged.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: Blocking one vendor does not block another
cases.why: The block list is per company; a wrong id in it would lock out the wrong vendor.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ with QA vendors 1 and 2, each with a submitted bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject QA vendor 2's bid without re-bidding. 2. As QA vendor 1, revise its bid.
cases.expected: Step 2 is accepted. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: QA vendor 1's revision is submitted.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: The second vendor is blocked as well when it is the one rejected
cases.why: Guards against a block list that only ever holds the first company.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ with QA vendors 1 and 2, each with a submitted bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject QA vendor 2's bid without re-bidding. 2. As QA vendor 2, try to bid again.
cases.expected: Step 2 is refused. HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.
cases.oracle: Code 101.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: Rejecting during bidding is refused where the round disables it
cases.why: The setting exists so buyers cannot knock vendors out mid-round.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid; `disable_reject_bid_in_bidding_time` is ON on the round (a client setting — the twin is reported as couldn't tell where it is off).
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid while bidding is open.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 686 'Bid rejection is disabled while bidding is in progress'.
cases.oracle: Code 686; the bid stays active.

cases.title: The status endpoint rejects a submitted bid while bidding is open
cases.why: The dashboard's services still call this endpoint; it must keep working for the owner of the event.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, `PATCH /bids/update_bid_status/{{bidUuid}}` with `{"status": "rejected", "rejection_remarks": "QA_Platform_reject_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: Accepted; the reply is the bid with status rejected. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: HTTP 200.

cases.title: A rejection through the status endpoint never blocks re-bidding
cases.why: Two rejection paths behave differently: this one writes no block list and no remark row, so the buyer cannot block a vendor through it.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid through the status endpoint. 2. As QA vendor 1, place a new bid.
cases.expected: Step 2 is accepted. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: The vendor's new bid is submitted.

cases.title: An unknown status value is refused
cases.why: Only active, rejected, revoke and in_active may be set from outside; 'selected' would be an award by the back door.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid.
cases.steps: 1. Send `{"status": "selected"}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: Code 2; the bid is unchanged.

cases.title: The status endpoint refuses changes after the close, unlike the reject action
cases.why: The two rejection paths disagree about time: reject works during evaluation (API-EVDRJB-012), the status endpoint does not.
cases.setup: A fresh RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid and the window is over.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, set the bid's status to rejected.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 33 'Order not active'.
cases.oracle: Code 33.

cases.title: 'Remove bid' on a live round answers success but leaves the bid in place
cases.why: The dashboard's 'remove participant bid' sends status in_active and shows 'bid discarded'; on a live round the backend applies in_active only to draft rounds, so nothing changes.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, send `{"status": "in_active"}`. 2. Reject the same bid with the reject action (it only accepts an active bid).
cases.expected: Today step 1 answers HTTP 200 and step 2 is accepted — the bid was still active. Should either remove the bid or refuse (suspected defect: success reported for a change that never happened).
cases.oracle: Step 1 = 200 and step 2 = 200.

cases.title: The buyer cannot revoke a vendor's bid
cases.why: Revoking is the bid author's own action and only where the round allows it.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, send `{"status": "revoke"}` for the vendor's bid.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action' (whether revoking is allowed on the round or not).
cases.oracle: Code 101.

cases.title: A rejected bid can be put back to active while bidding is open
cases.why: Undoing a mistaken rejection without asking the vendor to quote again.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. Reject the bid through the status endpoint. 2. Send `{"status": "active"}`. 3. Reject it with the reject action (only possible when active).
cases.expected: Steps 2 and 3 are accepted. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: Step 3 answers 200.

cases.title: A bid cannot be re-activated for a vendor removed from the round
cases.why: A removed vendor's quote must not come back into the comparison.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid.
cases.steps: 1. Reject the bid through the status endpoint. 2. Remove QA vendor 1 from the round. 3. Send `{"status": "active"}`.
cases.expected: Step 3 is refused. HTTP 422, code 392 'Please add this vendor to audience to re-open bid'.
cases.oracle: Code 392.

cases.section: The vendor discards its own draft bid
cases.title: A vendor discards its own draft bid
cases.why: Vendors abandon half-filled quotes; the draft must go away cleanly.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ; QA vendor 1 opens a bid and does not submit it.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, open a bid. 2. `PATCH /bids/delete_draft_bid/{{bidUuid}}` as QA vendor 1.
cases.expected: Accepted; the draft becomes inactive. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: HTTP 200.

cases.section: The vendor discards its own draft bid
cases.title: After discarding a draft the vendor can quote from scratch
cases.why: A discarded draft must not count as an existing bid.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, open a bid. 2. Discard it. 3. Place a full bid (open, price, submit).
cases.expected: Step 3 is accepted. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: The new bid is submitted.

cases.section: The vendor discards its own draft bid
cases.title: A submitted bid cannot be discarded as a draft
cases.why: A sent quote must not vanish without a revoke trail.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, call the draft-discard on the submitted bid.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 250 'No such bid exists' (only drafts are looked up).
cases.oracle: Code 250; the bid is still active.

cases.title: The rejected-bids list answers after a rejection
cases.why: The list is where the buyer sees who was rejected, why, and re-opens a bid.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid. 2. `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/rejected_bids`.
cases.expected: Step 2 answers HTTP 200 with the rejected bid under QA vendor 1 and its reason.
cases.oracle: HTTP 200 (the twin checks the answer; the content is checked by eye or in API-EVDRJB-069).

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: Rejecting the latest revision brings the vendor's previous quote back
cases.why: The code re-activates the vendor's most recent revised bid when its active bid is rejected, so the buyer may 'reject' a price and find the older one live again.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid at 100 and then revised to 90; rejecting during bidding allowed. Manual: no plan can name the first bid once the revision replaced it.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the 90 bid. 2. Open the comparison / the vendor's quote.
cases.expected: Today the 100 bid becomes the vendor's active quote again (by design per the code comment). Confirm with product that the buyer is told.
cases.oracle: The vendor's active bid after step 1 is the earlier revision (status active, price 100).

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: A vendor cannot call the reject action
cases.why: Only the buyer console may reject; the vendor website is not allowed this action, and a 401 signs the vendor out.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 signed in. Manual: a wrong-app call ends the vendor's session.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, `PATCH /bids/:id/reject` on its own bid.
cases.expected: Refused before the action runs: HTTP 401 (app not authorized).
cases.oracle: 401; the bid is unchanged.

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: Regretting the same line twice is harmless
cases.why: A double click must not create two entries or flip the line back.
cases.setup: As 001, and the line has already been regretted once on this draft.
cases.steps: Send the 001 request a second time.
cases.expected: Accepted again; the draft still holds the line once, as regretted (the entry is keyed by the line id and simply rewritten). HTTP 200, status label "REGRET".
cases.oracle: 200; one key for the line in `regretted_eglis`.

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: "Undo" with nothing to undo is accepted and changes nothing
cases.why: The screen may send undo for a line that was never regretted (stale state); it must not fail or invent a regret.
cases.setup: A fresh draft of QA vendor 1, nothing regretted.
cases.steps: `PATCH …/regret_status` with `"action_type": "undo_regret"`.
cases.expected: Accepted as a no-op: the delete finds nothing and the bid is saved unchanged. HTTP 200, status value null.
cases.oracle: 200; `regretted_eglis` is empty.

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: A line regretted in the draft can still be priced
cases.why: The vendor says "I can't supply this" and then types a price on the same line; the server should either refuse or make one of the two win predictably.
cases.setup: A live RFQ (one round, no technical stage), QA vendor 1's draft with the line regretted.
cases.steps: Price the regretted line (`POST /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/create_bid_products`).
cases.expected: Accepted. The price check that refuses regretted lines (736) reads only the line's saved `participants`, which a draft regret has not touched yet, and it only runs when a technical round exists. The regret wins later, at submit (see 006). HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: 200 on the price step; then 006's outcome on submit.

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: Submitting a regret-only draft (no prices) in a one-round event
cases.why: "Regret everything, quote nothing" is a legitimate way to decline; it must end in a clean answer, never a crash.
cases.setup: A live one-round RFQ; QA vendor 1's draft with the line regretted and no price.
cases.steps: Submit the draft (`PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}` with `status: "active"`).
cases.expected: A clean answer: either refused because nothing is priced (e.g. 372 'Please quote prices for all the products.' on a lot-closing round) or accepted and the bid immediately turned "revised" (the empty bid has no line to keep). Never a 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status below 500; if 200, buyer `bid_count` = 0.

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: Two-round event: a regret-only draft cannot be submitted
cases.why: The vendor declines the only line commercially and submits, and is told to "enter a bid for all lines not regretted in the technical stage" — the commercial regret does not count, so the vendor cannot decline that way.
cases.setup: A live RFP+RFQ; QA vendor 1 submitted its technical response (no "Regret" answer), opened an RFQ draft and regretted the line, priced nothing.
cases.steps: Submit the draft.
cases.expected: Refused: the "every non-regretted line must be priced" check reads only the line's saved `participants` (still "participated" from the technical response), not the draft regret. HTTP 422, code 748 'Please enter bid for all line items that are not regretted in technical stage.'
cases.oracle: 422 code 748. Product decision: should a commercial regret exempt the line?

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: A teammate can regret lines on a colleague's draft
cases.why: Drafts are per user (the open call reuses only the caller's own draft), but the regret lookup is per company, so one user can change another user's unsent quote.
cases.setup: Two users of the same vendor company; user A has a draft. Needs a second vendor user.
cases.steps: As user B, regret a line on A's draft.
cases.expected: 200 — `Bid.draft.for_company(allowed_companies)` finds A's draft. Should be limited to the draft's owner or clearly shared.
cases.oracle: A's draft carries B's regret.

cases.section: Regretting and un-regretting a line on a draft bid
cases.title: A regret can be recorded under a different company than the bid's
cases.why: For users linked to several companies (brokers, groups) the regret stores the company named in the request, and on submit the line is marked regretted for that company — not necessarily the bidder.
cases.setup: A user whose allowed companies include A and B; a draft bid of company B. Needs a multi-company vendor user.
cases.steps: Regret with `company_uuid` = A on B's draft, then submit.
cases.expected: 200, and the line becomes "regretted" for A. Should require the bid's own company.
cases.oracle: `participants[A]` = "regretted" while B's bid is the one submitted.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: A request without an action is refused
cases.why: A dropped field must not default to "regret".
cases.steps: The 001 body without `action_type`.
cases.expected: Refused (nil becomes "", which is not an allowed action). HTTP 422, code 805 'Invalid action type'.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: The action is case-sensitive
cases.why: "REGRET" is the label the server itself returns; a client echoing it back must get a clear refusal, not a silent no-op.
cases.steps: `"action_type": "REGRET"`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 805 'Invalid action type'.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: The action is checked before the line
cases.why: Pins the guard order so a refactor that reorders checks shows up.
cases.steps: `"action_type": "delete"` with the line segment `Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 805 'Invalid action type' (not 808).

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: A garbled line id is refused, not crashed
cases.why: The service decodes the path itself; an undecodable value must still end in a typed refusal.
cases.steps: Line segment `WrongUuid1=`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 808 'Line item not found'.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: The line is checked before the round
cases.why: Guard-order pin.
cases.steps: Line `Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` and no `trade_request_uuid`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 808 'Line item not found' (not 95).

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: An unknown round is refused
cases.why: As 025, with a value that decodes to a missing row.
cases.steps: `"trade_request_uuid": "Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 95 'Trade Request not found'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 95.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: An unknown company is refused as "not allowed", not "not found"
cases.why: The service's 130 'Company not found' can never be reached; the vendor always sees 101.
cases.steps: `"company_uuid": "Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: The company is checked before the bid
cases.why: Guard-order pin for the controller.
cases.setup: A live RFQ; no bid needed.
cases.steps: Path bid `Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`, body without `company_uuid`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action' (not 32).

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: A garbled bid id is refused
cases.why: The path id decodes to nil; the lookup must still refuse.
cases.setup: A live RFQ.
cases.steps: Path bid `WrongUuid1=`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 32 'Bid not found'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 32.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: In a lot-split event, even "undo" is refused once every line is regretted
cases.why: The lot rule runs for both actions and counts the current line as "to be regretted" even when undoing, so a vendor that reached "all regretted" (e.g. through the technical round) cannot undo anything.
cases.setup: A lot-split event; every active line already "regretted" for QA vendor 1, or listed in the draft's `regretted_eglis` (processed entries count too). Needs lot split.
cases.steps: `undo_regret` on one of the lines.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 844 'You cannot regret all line items in a lot split event'. Undo should be allowed.
cases.oracle: 422 code 844 for an undo.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: The lot rule counts the whole event, not the lot
cases.why: The check compares against every active line of the event, so a vendor may regret every line of one lot (its stage ends with nothing quoted) as long as another lot still has a line. Deeper than EDGE-BID-102.
cases.setup: A lot-split event with lots L1 (lines 1–2) and L2 (line 3). Needs lot split.
cases.steps: On the L1 stage draft regret line 1, then line 2.
cases.expected: Both 200 (line 3 keeps the event "not all regretted"). Regretting line 3 on the L2 draft afterwards answers 422 code 844 'You cannot regret all line items in a lot split event'.
cases.oracle: The status sequence 200, 200, 844.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: A bid flagged with price anomalies cannot be regretted
cases.why: Anomaly bids must be fixed before any change.
cases.setup: A draft of QA vendor 1 whose status is anomaly_detected — unreachable through the draft-only lookup today (the controller looks up drafts only), so record whether 473 is ever returned.
cases.steps: Regret a line on that bid.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 32 'Bid not found' (the controller's draft lookup) — 473 'You cannot revise the bid, Please resolve the error prices first' is unreachable from this route.
cases.oracle: 422 code 32.

cases.section: Validation and the order of checks (vendor-side)
cases.title: A subsidiary of a company that already bid cannot regret
cases.why: Group companies must not split one participation across two bids.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 is a subsidiary of (or parent to) a company that already bid on the round. Needs a company hierarchy.
cases.steps: Regret a line on vendor 1's draft.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 96 'A bid has already been placed by your team'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 96.

cases.title: A regret racing a submit is not locked
cases.why: Submit and create take a 3-second lock per round and company; regret does not, so a regret that lands after the submit read the bid is lost or applied half-way.
cases.setup: Two parallel requests (the runner sends one at a time).
cases.steps: Fire the submit and a regret on the same draft within a few milliseconds.
cases.expected: One consistent outcome: either the regret is applied before activation, or it is refused (32) because the bid is no longer a draft. Never a submitted bid whose `regretted_eglis` still says "draft".
cases.oracle: DB: no active bid with a "draft" regret entry.

cases.section: State of the event and the round
cases.title: Regret after the bidding window has closed
cases.why: Nothing in the regret path checks the window; a regret after close still changes the draft.
cases.setup: A short live RFQ; QA vendor 1 opens a draft; the window and extra closing time pass (the round's status stays "active" until award).
cases.steps: Regret on the draft.
cases.expected: A clean answer. Today 200 — no window check exists; product to decide whether it should be 33 'Order not active'. Never a 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status below 500.

cases.section: State of the event and the round
cases.title: Regret on an event that has been superseded by a new version
cases.why: Open, price and submit all refuse non-latest events (101); regret does not, so a vendor keeps editing a dead draft.
cases.setup: A live RFQ; QA vendor 1 opens a draft; the buyer issues a new version (not published).
cases.steps: Regret on the draft of the old version.
cases.expected: Should match the bid routes (422 code 101). Today 200 (no `latest?` check); never a 5xx.
cases.oracle: Status below 500.

cases.section: State of the event and the round
cases.title: Regret on an auction round is stored as "commercial"
cases.why: `VALID_STAGES = %w(commercial)` is declared but never used; every regret is tagged `stage_type: commercial` and applied the same way on auctions (including knockout/dutch rounds whose acceptance logic runs right after).
cases.setup: A live auction (or RFQ converted to auction) with a draft bid of QA vendor 1. Needs an auction.
cases.steps: Regret a line, then place the auction bid.
cases.expected: Product decision; record the outcome. Today 200 and the line is dropped on submit exactly as in an RFQ.
cases.oracle: `regretted_eglis[<line>].stage_type` = "commercial".

cases.section: How the buyer, evaluation and award see a regret
cases.title: A vendor that regretted every line drops out of the comparison data
cases.why: The background recompute removes a fully regretted vendor from the event's participant list (non-lot events), which should match what the round and participants screens show (see 006, UI-EVDRGT-074).
cases.setup: As 006 (one line, fully regretted, submitted).
cases.steps: Wait for recompute; read `event_groups.precomputed_data_v1.participant_vendor_company_ids` (DB) and the buyer's participants list.
cases.expected: The vendor is removed from the precomputed participant list but still listed as "bid placed" in the participants list.
cases.oracle: DB list lacks vendor 1; `get_audience` still has it under bid placed.

cases.section: How the buyer, evaluation and award see a regret
cases.title: Updating the technical response silently cancels a commercial regret
cases.why: Re-submitting the technical response rewrites `participants` for every answered line ("participated" unless "Regret"), wiping a regret the vendor made in the RFQ; the line becomes quotable again without the vendor undoing anything.
cases.setup: RFP and RFQ both open; QA vendor 1 regrets the line in the RFQ and submits (line "regretted"); then edits and re-submits its technical response. Needs a technical response update op.
cases.steps: Read the line's `participants` after the technical re-submit; try to price the line in the RFQ.
cases.expected: `participants[<vendor 1>]` = "participated" and pricing is accepted (no 736).
cases.oracle: DB value flips from "regretted" to "participated".

cases.section: How the buyer, evaluation and award see a regret
cases.title: Lot splitting treats commercially regretted vendors as not participating on that line
cases.why: Lot creation summarises "technically accepted and not regretted" items; a commercial regret made before the split changes which vendors and lines go into each lot.
cases.setup: RFP+RFQ before lot split; QA vendor 1 commercially regretted one line. Needs lot split.
cases.steps: Run lot splitting; read each lot's `tna_regretted_vendors`.
cases.expected: Vendor 1 is listed under the regretted line's `tna_regretted_vendors`.
cases.oracle: Lot summary text "includes a mix of … regretted".

cases.title: A round-level decline never reaches that list
cases.why: The same button can be recorded against the round (`TradeRequest`) — that is what the round page's "answered" flag reads — but the buyer's participants list reads only event-level answers, so the buyer never sees the reason.
cases.setup: A live RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, `POST /user_intents` with `item_type: "TradeRequest"`, `item_uuid: "{{tradeId}}"`, `intent_type: "trade_reject"` and a reason. 2. As the buyer read `get_audience`.
cases.expected: 200, and the vendor's "reason" column stays empty. The two places should read the same answer.
cases.oracle: `vendors[*].user_intent` is null for every row.

cases.title: Declining counts as having answered the participation question
cases.why: The vendor must not be asked again on every visit after saying no.
cases.setup: A live RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited.
cases.steps: 1. Round-level decline as in 058. 2. As QA vendor 1, `GET /trade/{{tradeId}}?response_type=template`.
cases.expected: The round says the vendor has answered. HTTP 200 and `user_intent_answered: true` (the field is left out when false).
cases.oracle: `user_intent_answered` = true.

cases.title: A decline on the technical round does not answer the pricing round
cases.why: Answers are per round (and per company on `/trade`, per user on `/v1/trade/:id/schema`), so a vendor who declined the RFP is asked again on the RFQ of the same event.
cases.setup: A live RFP+RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited to both. Manual: the vendor's read of the RFQ before technical participation may be gated.
cases.steps: 1. Decline `{{rfpTradeId}}`. 2. Read `{{tradeId}}` as the vendor.
cases.expected: `user_intent_answered` is absent on the RFQ. Product to decide whether one decline should cover the event.
cases.oracle: Field absent on the RFQ read.

cases.title: Declining and then accepting: the latest answer wins in the vendor's event view
cases.why: Answers are never superseded (both rows stay active, EDGE-BID-012); the event view must at least show the newest one.
cases.setup: A live RFQ; QA vendor 1 already declined at event level (helper H02).
cases.steps: 1. `POST /user_intents` with `{"item_uuid": "{{eventGroupUuid}}", "item_type": "EventGroup", "intent_type": "trade_accept"}`. 2. As the vendor, `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`.
cases.expected: Accept saved (no reason needed); the event view shows the acceptance. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: `user_intent.intent_type` = "trade_accept".

cases.title: The vendor's own event view shows its decline and remark
cases.why: The vendor app decides from this whether to show the participate prompt or "you declined".
cases.setup: A live RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited.
cases.steps: 1. Event-level decline as in 057. 2. As the vendor, `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; `user_intent` carries the decline and the remark.
cases.oracle: `user_intent.intent_type` = "trade_reject"; `user_intent.remarks` contains "QA_Platform_decline_{{stamp}}".

cases.title: Joining through "participate" after declining records an acceptance the buyer never sees
cases.why: Self-participation writes a `trade_accept` on the event without a company, while the buyer's list filters answers by company — so the buyer keeps seeing the old decline reason for a vendor who joined.
