cases.setup: Buyer company setting `enable_open_tender_events` ON; a live event; QA vendor 1 mapped to the buyer and has declined at event level (H02).
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, `POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/participants`. 2. Vendor reads the event. 3. Buyer reads `get_audience`.
cases.expected: Step 1 HTTP 200 `{"success": true}`; step 2 shows `user_intent.intent_type` = "trade_accept"; step 3 still shows the decline text (the new row has no `company_id`). Should store the vendor's company.
cases.oracle: Steps 2 and 3 disagree.

cases.title: Placing a bid never turns the vendor's decline into "converted"
cases.why: The "converted" status exists for this, but it is only set by the old surrogate path, and there it converts the BUYER's own intent (Current.user), never the vendor's. So declines stay active forever.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 declined the round, then bids (vendor app), or the buyer enters a surrogate bid for it.
cases.steps: Read the vendor's `user_intents` rows (DB) after each.
cases.expected: Still `status: active, intent_type: trade_reject` in both cases.
cases.oracle: No row with status converted.

cases.title: The event view and the event list pick the answer differently
cases.why: The event view takes the newest intent of any status; the event list takes an arbitrary one (indexed by event, last row wins) and also ignores status, so the two can show different answers.
cases.setup: A vendor user with a decline then an accept on the same event.
cases.steps: Compare `GET /event_groups/:id` (`user_intent`) with the vendor's event list card.
cases.expected: Both should show the newest active answer.
cases.oracle: Same intent type in both.

cases.title: A decline unlocks the vendor's stage card exactly like an acceptance
cases.why: The card locks a stage until the vendor answers; "No, I won't participate" opens it just the same, inviting the vendor into a round it declined.
cases.setup: A live one-round event; QA vendor 1 declines at event level.
cases.steps: Read the vendor's event cards.
cases.expected: `is_stage_locked` false after a decline. Product decision whether a decline should keep it locked.
cases.oracle: `is_stage_locked` before (true) and after the decline (false).

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: Leaving out the re-bidding choice allows re-bidding
cases.why: Documents the default an API caller gets when it says nothing.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject the bid without the `allow_rebidding` field. 2. As QA vendor 1, place a new bid.
cases.expected: Step 2 is accepted. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: Step 2 answers 200.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: Rejecting a bid that does not exist
cases.why: An unknown id must be a clean refusal, not a crash.
cases.setup: A signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /bids/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/reject` with a reason.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 250 'No such bid exists'.
cases.oracle: Code 250.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: Rejecting with an id that cannot be decoded
cases.why: The id decodes to nothing; `Bid.find_by_id(nil)` must still be a clean refusal.
cases.setup: A signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /bids/WrongUuid1=/reject` with a reason.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 250 'No such bid exists'.
cases.oracle: Code 250, never 500.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: Script, SQL-like text and emoji in the reason are stored safely
cases.why: The reason is shown to the vendor and printed in reports.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. Reject with a reason containing `<script>`, `' OR 1=1 --`, Chinese text and an emoji.
cases.expected: No server error; tags are stripped on the way in.
cases.oracle: Any 2xx/4xx, never 5xx.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: A very long reason does not crash the rejection
cases.why: The reason goes to a JSON field on the bid and to a remark row.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid; rejecting during bidding allowed.
cases.steps: 1. Reject with a 6,000-character reason.
cases.expected: No server error (stored, or refused cleanly).
cases.oracle: Never 5xx.

cases.title: A status call without a status is refused
cases.why: A call that says nothing must not be read as some default status.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid.
cases.steps: 1. Send only a remark, no status.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: Code 2.

cases.title: Changing the status of a bid that does not exist
cases.why: An unknown id must be a clean refusal, not a crash.
cases.setup: A signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /bids/update_bid_status/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` with status rejected.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 32 'Bid not found'.
cases.oracle: Code 32.

cases.title: Changing the status with an id that cannot be decoded
cases.why: A nil id must be refused before any lookup.
cases.setup: A signed-in buyer.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /bids/update_bid_status/WrongUuid1=` with status rejected.
cases.expected: Refused as missing parameters (the id is empty). HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: Code 2.

cases.title: Setting an active bid to active again is harmless
cases.why: A repeated 're-open' click must not raise an approval or change the quote.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid.
cases.steps: 1. Send `{"status": "active"}` for the active bid.
cases.expected: Accepted; nothing changes. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: HTTP 200.

cases.title: Hostile text in the status endpoint's reason is handled safely
cases.why: The reason is stored on the bid and shown to the vendor.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid.
cases.steps: 1. Reject through the status endpoint with an `` / SQL-like reason.
cases.expected: No server error.
cases.oracle: Never 5xx.

cases.title: A status sent as a list is refused
cases.why: Wrong types must be refused before any lookup, not crash the comparison.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 submitted a bid.
cases.steps: 1. Send `{"status": ["rejected"]}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: Code 2.

cases.section: The vendor discards its own draft bid
cases.title: Discarding the same draft twice is refused
cases.why: A retried click must answer cleanly.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, open a bid. 2. Discard it. 3. Discard it again.
cases.expected: Step 3 is refused. HTTP 422, code 250 'No such bid exists'.
cases.oracle: Code 250.

cases.section: The vendor discards its own draft bid
cases.title: Discarding a bid that does not exist
cases.why: An unknown id must be a clean refusal.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 signed in.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /bids/delete_draft_bid/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` as QA vendor 1.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 250 'No such bid exists'.
cases.oracle: Code 250.

cases.section: The vendor discards its own draft bid
cases.title: A draft can still be discarded after the round closed
cases.why: Records present behaviour: discarding has no time rule (harmless — a draft is not a quote).
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ with a two-minute window; QA vendor 1 opens a bid; the window then closes.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, open a bid. 2. Wait for the close. 3. Discard the draft.
cases.expected: Accepted. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: HTTP 200.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: Rejecting is refused once the RFQ has been turned into an auction
cases.why: After conversion the RFQ is frozen; a rejection would change the auction's starting field.
cases.setup: An RFQ on a project-enabled company converted to an auction. Manual: needs rfx_project_enabled and a conversion.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, reject a bid on the original RFQ.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 769 'You cannot edit rfq once the auction is created.'
cases.oracle: Code 769.

cases.section: The buyer rejects a submitted bid
cases.title: Two rejections sent at the same moment
cases.why: There is no lock on the reject action (unlike creating or editing bids), so two concurrent calls can both pass the 'still active' check.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid. Manual: needs two requests in flight together.
cases.steps: 1. Send two reject calls for the same bid in parallel.
cases.expected: Exactly one succeeds; the other answers code 101. Watch for two remark rows or a duplicated block-list entry.
cases.oracle: One 200 and one 422; one 'bid_rejection' remark.

cases.title: A bid already revoked cannot be changed
cases.why: A revoked bid is final for the vendor.
cases.setup: A round where revoking is allowed and a surrogate bid the buyer revoked. Manual: needs is_revoke_bid_allowed on the round.
cases.steps: 1. Send any status for the revoked bid.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 403, code 151 'Sorry, You cannot perform this action at this time'.
cases.oracle: Code 151.

cases.title: Re-activating a bid the buyer entered for a vendor goes for approval
cases.why: Where surrogate bidding needs approval, putting a buyer-entered bid back to active must raise that approval instead of going live.
cases.setup: A company with a surrogate-bidding approval flow; a surrogate bid that was rejected. Manual: needs an approval flow.
cases.steps: 1. Send `{"status": "active"}` for the surrogate bid.
cases.expected: The bid becomes 'requested' and an approval request is raised. HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: Bid status requested; an approval exists.

cases.title: The vendor website cannot use the status endpoint
cases.why: The vendor app is not allowed this action; a 401 signs the vendor out.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 signed in. Manual (wrong app).
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, `PATCH /bids/update_bid_status/:id` with status revoke.
cases.expected: HTTP 401 (app not authorized).

cases.section: The vendor discards its own draft bid
cases.title: The buyer console cannot use the draft-discard call
cases.why: The console app is not allowed this action; a 401 signs the buyer out of the web console.
cases.setup: Manual (wrong app).
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, `PATCH /bids/delete_draft_bid/:id`.
cases.expected: HTTP 401 (app not authorized).

cases.title: The rejected-bids list shows the reason the buyer typed
cases.why: The reason is the vendor's only explanation.
cases.setup: As API-EVDRJB-050. Manual oracle: the plan language cannot assert inside this reply yet.
cases.steps: 1. Reject with reason R. 2. Open the rejected-bids list.
cases.expected: The entry for QA vendor 1 carries reason R.
cases.oracle: The reply's entry for QA vendor 1 has the remark R.

journeys.title: Rescheduling, per-item timing, weighted bidding and drafts
journeys.goal: Move an event's dates, give items their own closing times, weight price against other factors when ranking bids, and keep a draft safe until it is published.

cases.title: The Reschedule dialog keeps the round's length and shifts the evaluation window
cases.why: The dialog asks only for a new start; the end and the extra closing time are derived, so a buyer cannot change the duration here — and the API's omission trap (API-EVDTME-019) is avoided only because the dialog sends the extra time.
cases.setup: An upcoming RFQ, start S, end S+1 h, extra closing S+1.5 h.
cases.steps: Settings → Reschedule Event; pick S+2 h; OK; watch the PATCH body.
cases.expected: Body `{"bid_start_time": S+2h, "bid_end_time": S+3h, "extra_closing_time": S+3.5h}`; the header shows the new times.
cases.oracle: Network request body; end − start unchanged.

cases.title: The Reschedule dialog refuses a past time and a start after the delivery date
cases.why: The screen is the only guard against a past start (API-EVDTME-017).
cases.setup: An upcoming RFQ with a delivery date D.
cases.steps: 1. Pick today at a time already past. 2. Pick a date after D.
cases.expected: 1. "Scheduled time is invalid!" and no request. 2. "Schedule time should be on or before Delivery Date" (Pickup Date for sell events) and no request. Past days are disabled in the picker.
cases.oracle: No PATCH sent; error text under the field.

cases.title: The Reopen drawer lists only expired lines and sends seconds
cases.why: The drawer decides which lines can be sent and converts the duration; a wrong unit would reopen for hours instead of minutes.
cases.setup: A live staggered auction with lines 1–2 expired, line 3 running; serial duration 10 min.
cases.steps: Open the drawer; try OK with nothing selected and with an empty duration; then select lines 1 and 2, keep 10 minutes, OK.
cases.expected: Only lines 1–2 are listed (with bid counts); errors for no selection / no duration and no request; final body `{"trade_product_uuids": [<line 1>, <line 2>], "reopen_time_extension": 600}`; success message "Line items reopened successfully"; tooltip explains reopened lines move to the end.
cases.oracle: Network body; the reopened lines appear after line 3 in the schedule.

cases.title: "Increase time" on a live staggered round re-times the lines instead of the round
cases.why: This is the only caller of staggered_time; the payload decides which lines move (and explains API-EVDTME-045).
cases.setup: A live staggered auction: line 1 expired, line 2 running, line 3 upcoming.
cases.steps: Settings → Increase time by 10 minutes with a remark; watch the request.
cases.expected: `PATCH /trade/<id>/staggered_time` with `trade_products_time` = { line 2: same start, end + 600; line 3: start + 600, end + 600 }; line 1 omitted; no remark and no `increase_auction_time` in the body. In buffer status the normal extension is sent instead.
cases.oracle: Network body.

cases.title: Changing only the delivery date in the Reschedule dialog does not reschedule
cases.why: With the start unchanged the dialog sends no times, so the request takes the live-edit path (unscoped delivery schedule lookup, API-XDAMD-052) instead of the reschedule path.
cases.setup: An upcoming RFQ with a delivery date.
cases.steps: Open Reschedule; change only the delivery date; OK.
cases.expected: Body contains only `delivery_schedules: [{delivery_by, uuid}]` (no bid times); the round's times are unchanged; no reschedule notification.
cases.oracle: Network request body; no reschedule push to vendors.

cases.title: "Reopen Line Items" is offered only on staggered rounds and only after a line has expired
cases.why: The menu must match the backend rules (staggered only; reopen only expired lines).
cases.setup: A live staggered auction before any line ends, the same after line 1 ends, and a live RFQ.
cases.steps: Open Settings on each.
cases.expected: RFQ: no item. Staggered, no line expired: item disabled with tooltip "Line items can only be reopened if at least one line item has expired". After line 1 ended: enabled. Shown in live and buffer (evaluation) status only.
cases.oracle: Menu item presence/disabled state.

cases.title: The weight button reads Add, Edit or View depending on bids and existing weights
cases.why: The label is the buyer's only hint of what is possible.
cases.setup: Order details → Participants list of a live RFQ: (a) no weights, no bids; (b) weights, no bids; (c) weights and a bid; (d) an RFP stage.
cases.steps: Look at the link next to the vendor search.
cases.expected: (a) "Add Weight Params", (b) "Edit Weight Params", (c) "View Weight Params" (modal read-only, OK disabled), (d) no button.
cases.oracle: Button text / presence.

cases.title: After bids the screen never allows editing, even when the round allows it
cases.why: `getWeightParamsStatus` returns "view" for bids > 0 in both branches, so `allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` / `_auction` have no effect on this screen while the API honours them.
cases.setup: Round with `allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` on, weights saved, one bid.
cases.steps: Open the weight modal.
cases.expected: Editable (setting on). Today: "View Weight Params", read-only.
cases.oracle: OK button disabled.

cases.title: A live RFQ reads the AUCTION edit flag
cases.why: `(info.rfxMode === ORDER_MODE.auction || ORDER_MODE.rfqToAuction)` is always true, so for every non-expired round the screen uses `allow_edit_weight_param_auction`; the RFQ branch is unreachable.
cases.setup: Live RFQ with `allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` on and `allow_edit_weight_param_auction` off (and the reverse).
cases.steps: Inspect `tradeConfig.isAllowedToModifyWeightParams` / the weight sheet's read-only cells.
cases.expected: The RFQ flag decides. Today: the auction flag decides.
cases.oracle: Value of `isAllowedToModifyWeightParams` vs the two flags.

cases.title: An expired round with no bids still offers Add / Edit Weight Params
cases.why: The expired branch sets "view" but the next `if (bidCount === 0)` overwrites it; together with API-EVDWGT-065 the buyer can re-weight an expired event.
cases.setup: Expired RFQ, no bids.
cases.steps: Open Participants.
cases.expected: View only (or hidden). Today: "Add Weight Params" / "Edit Weight Params" and the save succeeds.
cases.oracle: Button text; a save returns success.

cases.title: A relative weight of exactly 100% passes the screen and fails on the server
cases.why: The sheet rule is -100 ≤ x ≤ 100; the server needs -100 < x < 100, so the buyer gets the server's generic "Insufficient parameters".
cases.setup: Weight modal, a relative (%) weight.
cases.steps: Enter 100 for a vendor; OK.
cases.expected: The screen should block 100 with its own message. Today: no screen error, then a server error toast.
cases.oracle: Network: 422 code 2.

cases.title: Reopening the modal shows the key, not the name the buyer typed
cases.why: The name is rebuilt from the key with underscores turned into spaces; a name typed "Freight_Cost (FY25)" comes back as "Freight Cost (FY25)" and is then re-saved under a different key.
cases.setup: Save a weight named "Freight_Cost"; reopen the modal.
cases.steps: Read the name field; save without changes; read the round.
cases.expected: The stored label is shown. Today: "Freight Cost", and the next save sends key "Freight_Cost" with label "Freight Cost".
cases.oracle: `misc.weightage.weightage_names` before and after.

cases.title: "Freight cost" and "Freight_cost" pass the duplicate check but overwrite each other
cases.why: Duplicates are checked on the raw name; the payload key replaces spaces with underscores, so the second weight silently replaces the first.
cases.setup: Weight modal.
cases.steps: Add "Freight cost" (values A) and "Freight_cost" (values B); OK.
cases.expected: Refused as duplicate. Today: saved, only one weight (values B) exists.
cases.oracle: Read the round: one key.

cases.title: The modal blocks an empty name, no weights and an empty sheet
cases.why: These screen checks are what keep the server's generic code 2 from reaching buyers.
cases.setup: Weight modal.
cases.steps: 1. OK with no weights. 2. Add a weight with no name. 3. A named weight with no values.
cases.expected: 1 "Please add at least one weight value"; 2 "Name of weight parameter can't be empty" and the field outlined red; 3 "Please add minium one value for <name>"; nothing sent.
cases.oracle: No PATCH in the network log.

cases.title: The create-screen weight modal sends a payload the server always refuses
cases.why: `updateWeightParams` sends `{key_attributes, weightage_names, values}` (wrapped in `weightages` only for "order detail add") with no `weightage_on`; every such save answers "Insufficient parameters".
cases.setup: Create-order flow → Audience → weights modal on an existing round (edit path).
cases.steps: Change a vendor's weight; OK.
cases.expected: Saved. Today: 422 code 2 toast.
cases.oracle: Network: request body lacks `weightages.weightage_on`; response code 2.

cases.title: The modal sheet and the saved payload can use different modes
cases.why: The sheet is built from the STORED `weightage_on`, but the payload's `weightage_on` comes from the round's closing mode; a lot-weighted round now closing per item submits a one-row lot sheet as line weights for the first product only.
cases.setup: A round with lot weights whose closing mode is item-wise.
cases.steps: Open Edit Weight Params; change a value; OK; read the round.
cases.expected: Mode kept (lot). Today (suspected): saved as line_item with only line 1 populated.
cases.oracle: `weightages.weightage_on` and values after the save.

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: A started round cannot be moved to a later window, and its clock is untouched
cases.why: Moving a live round's start would close bidding under vendors who are quoting; the refusal must also leave the clock exactly as it was.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ whose bidding started when it was published (about 20 minutes open), QA vendor 1 invited, no bids.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{"bid_start_time": {{now+3600}}, "bid_end_time": {{now+7200}}}`. 2. Read the round back (`GET /trade/{{tradeId}}?response_type=template`).
cases.expected: The reschedule is refused and the round still starts in the past and ends at its original time. HTTP 422, code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!'.
cases.oracle: 422 + 258; `starting_from` ≤ now and `ending_at` ≤ now + 30 min (not moved to two hours from now).

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: A buyer of another company: reschedule and reopen are blocked, staggered_time is not
cases.why: The three time actions have three different ownership checks; only one of them is complete.
cases.setup: Buyer B of a second company (console) and a live staggered auction of company A. Needs two companies and a staggered auction; manual.
cases.steps: As B: 1. `PATCH /trade/<A's round>` with a reschedule body. 2. `POST /trade/<A's round>/reopen_line_items`. 3. `PATCH /trade/<A's round>/staggered_time` with a later end for one line.
cases.expected: 1. HTTP 422, code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action' (Pundit `update?` requires A in B's allowed companies). 2. HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found' (the lookup is scoped to B's company). 3. Should be refused the same way; today it is accepted (API-XDLOT-062).
cases.oracle: 455 / 4 / (defect) 200 with A's line end moved.

cases.section: Rescheduling an upcoming round (manual — every recipe starts bidding at publish)
cases.title: An upcoming round can be moved to a later window
cases.why: This is the product's Reschedule Event action; the schedule, close time and vendor view must all follow.
cases.setup: An RFQ published with bid start = now + 2 h, end = now + 3 h, extra closing time now + 3.5 h; QA vendor 1 only (restricted audience); no bids. Manual: no recipe builds an upcoming round.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/<round>` with `{"bid_start_time": <now+4h>, "bid_end_time": <now+5h>, "extra_closing_time": <now+5.5h>}`. 2. `GET /trade/<round>?response_type=template`. 3. As QA vendor 1, open the round.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. `starting_from` = now + 4 h, `ending_at` = now + 5 h, `extra_closing_time` = now + 5.5 h; the vendor sees the new times; QA vendor 1 gets the reschedule push.
cases.oracle: Read-back values equal the sent epochs; trade schedule rows (bidding + extra closing) updated in place, not duplicated.

cases.section: Auction reschedule and extension emails (commit c74ea64581, manual)
cases.title: Rescheduling an upcoming auction emails each invited vendor the old and new times
cases.why: New in #16149: vendors used to learn of an auction reschedule only by push.
cases.setup: An upcoming auction (rfx_mode auction) with a restricted audience of QA vendor 1 and QA vendor 2 only; a company with NO active auction team (or one made only of QA users) — the buyer-side mail goes to every auction-team member.
cases.steps: Reschedule the auction from start S to S+2 h; open QA vendor 1's and 2's mailboxes.
cases.expected: Each QA vendor gets "📅 <ref> | Auction has been rescheduled" with old start/end and new start/end in the vendor's own time zone and the invited count; plus the "Auction has been rescheduled." push (auction_reschedule_to_vendor).
cases.oracle: Mail body old start = S, new start = S+2 h; one mail per vendor user with an email.

cases.section: Auction reschedule and extension emails (commit c74ea64581, manual)
cases.title: Extending a live auction emails vendors "Submission time extended"
cases.why: New in #16149: vendors used to get only a push when an auction was extended.
cases.setup: A live auction (rfx_mode auction, not knockout/Dutch, not BOQ) with QA vendors 1 and 2 only.
cases.steps: Extend it (`PATCH /trade/<round>` with `increase_auction_time` = end + 10 min); open both mailboxes.
cases.expected: Each vendor gets "⏰ <ref>[ Lot-n] | Submission time extended for <mode>" with the new end date/time in its time zone and the line items; plus the "buyer_time_increase" push.
cases.oracle: One mail per vendor; new end in the mail = the read-back `ending_at`.

cases.title: Reopening two expired lines gives each its own slot after the round's end
cases.why: This is the Reopen Line Items drawer; vendors must be able to bid again on exactly those lines, one after another.
cases.setup: A live staggered line-item auction, 3 lines; lines 1 and 2 have ended, line 3 is running; round end E, evaluation end E+30 min; QA vendors only.
cases.steps: 1. `POST /trade/<round>/reopen_line_items` with `{"trade_product_uuids": ["<line 1>", "<line 2>"], "reopen_time_extension": 600}`. 2. Read the round back.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. Line 1: E → E+10 min; line 2: E+10 → E+20 min; both flagged in `misc.trade_products_reopened_status`; round bid end = E+20 min; evaluation end moved by the same 20 min (E+50 min); closed_at = the new evaluation end.
cases.oracle: `misc.trade_products_time` and `ending_at` / `extra_closing_time` in the read-back.

cases.section: Late bids against a moved clock
cases.title: After the end is pulled in, a vendor cannot bid
cases.why: The extension field accepts a time EARLIER than the current end (no check that the new end is later), silently cutting the vendors' window; the bid lock-out must follow the new clock.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ open about 20 minutes, QA vendor 1 invited, no bids. `counter_offer_modification_enabled` is off on the round (otherwise a vendor may still open a draft during the extra closing time).
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{"increase_auction_time": {{now+90}}, "remarks": "QA_Platform_shorten_{{stamp}}"}`. 2. Wait until that end has passed. 3. As QA vendor 1, place a bid (open, price, submit). 4. Read the round back.
cases.expected: Step 1 is accepted (should be refused — an extension to an earlier time is a shortening). Step 3 is refused at the first call: HTTP 422, code 33 'Order not active'.
cases.oracle: Step 3 code 33; `ending_at` ≤ now in the read-back.

cases.title: A buyer from another company is refused
cases.why: Weights decide ranks; only the round's own company may set them.
cases.setup: Buyer of company B; a live round of company A. Manual (two companies).
cases.steps: As B, `PATCH /trade/<A's round>/edit_weight_parameters` with a valid lot weight body.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action'; no weight rows on A's round.
cases.oracle: 422 code 455; A's round `GET` unchanged.

cases.title: Any user of the company can change weights, even one who may not edit the round
cases.why: `edit_weight_parameters?` checks only the company. `update?` on the same round also requires the "create record" trade permission and sourcing-events access; neither the owner nor the team is checked. A view-only colleague can quietly re-rank vendors on someone else's live event.
cases.setup: A second buyer in PROCOL DEMO without the trade create permission (or without sourcing-events access), not in the owner's team. Manual (second user).
cases.steps: As that user, `PATCH /trade/:id/edit_weight_parameters` on the owner's live round.
cases.expected: Should be 455 like `PATCH /trade/:id`. Today: HTTP 200 'Weights added successfully!'.
cases.oracle: Weight rows created; `GET /trade/:id` shows the new weights.

cases.section: First save, re-edits and what the round shows afterwards
cases.title: Adding a lot weight for an invited vendor makes the round a weighted round
cases.why: The basic promise: one save and the round carries the weight list, the vendor's value, and the weighted flag the screens key off.
cases.setup: `published_rfq` (live RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited, no bids, no weights).
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}/edit_weight_parameters` with `{"weightages": {"weightage_on": "lot", "values": {"qa_freight_adj": {"label": "QA_Platform_Freight_{{stamp}}", "input_type": "absolute", "data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": "100"}}}}}`. Then read the round.
cases.expected: Saved. The round now reads as weighted, weights are "lot", the weight list is the new key plus "weighted_total", and QA vendor 1's value is 100. HTTP 200 'Weights added successfully!'.
cases.oracle: `GET /trade/{{tradeId}}?response_type=template`: `trade_config.is_weighted_bid_event` true; `weightages.weightage_on` "lot"; `weightages.key_attributes` contains "qa_freight_adj" and "weighted_total"; `weightages.values.qa_freight_adj.data.<vendor 1>` "100.0"; `misc.weightage.weightage_names` contains the label.

cases.section: First save, re-edits and what the round shows afterwards
cases.title: Saving a new value for the same weight replaces the old one
cases.why: Rows are matched on (round, vendor, key); if a re-save added a second row, the vendor's weight would silently double (the lot read sums every row).
cases.setup: `published_rfq`; arrange: the happy-path save (value 100).
cases.steps: Save the same key for QA vendor 1 with `"250"`, then read the round.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; QA vendor 1's value is 250, not 350.
cases.oracle: `weightages.values.qa_freight_adj.data.<vendor 1>` equals "250.0".

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A line weight can be written onto another round's line item
cases.why: In line mode the line ids come from the request and are never checked to belong to this round. A buyer who knows any trade-product id (of any company) can attach an active weight row to that line under its own round's request — a write across rounds and companies.
cases.setup: Two rounds A (own) and B (another event, ideally another company); B's trade-product id. Manual only — never run against a real record.
cases.steps: On A: line mode, `"data": {<vendor>: {<B's trade-product id>: "500"}}`; then read B's sheet.
cases.expected: Should be 422 (line not in this round). Today (suspected): HTTP 200 and an active Weightage row on B's line, which B's ranking sums in if B is weighted.
cases.oracle: DB: `weightages` row with item_type TradeProduct, item_id = B's line, created by A's request.

cases.section: Bids already in, and the round's state
cases.title: Once a vendor has bid, RFQ weights are locked unless the round allows edits
cases.why: Changing the scoring after prices are in can flip the winner; `allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` (round config, copied from the template / company configuration at creation; absent = off) is the only switch.
cases.setup: Live RFQ with QA vendor 1's submitted bid (recipe `rfq_with_bid`); round `trade_config.allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` off/absent.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}/edit_weight_parameters` with the happy-path body.
cases.expected: Refused, nothing changed. HTTP 422, code 15 'Operation failed' — the same generic code also means "not a rank round" (§6, 068), so the screen cannot say "bids already received".
cases.oracle: 422 code 15; round still unweighted.

cases.section: Ranking, comparison and who can see the weights
cases.title: A vendor can read the weights set for a competitor
cases.why: The round read serialises `weightages` for every caller, with every vendor's company id and value. A vendor opening the round learns which competitors the buyer penalises or favours and by how much — a breach of the fairness contract.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`; the buyer saves weights for QA vendor 1 ("100") and QA vendor 2 ("300").
cases.steps: 1. Buyer saves. 2. QA vendor 1 reads the round (`GET /trade/{{tradeId}}?response_type=template`).
cases.expected: The vendor's read carries no value for QA vendor 2 (ideally no `weightages` at all). Today (suspected): `weightages.values.qa_freight_adj.data.<vendor 2>` = "300.0" is visible to vendor 1.
cases.oracle: Vendor read: path `weightages.values.qa_freight_adj.data.<vendor 2>` absent.

cases.section: Ranking, comparison and who can see the weights
cases.title: Weights change who is L1 in the comparison sheet
cases.why: The point of the feature: vendor A quotes lower but carries a ₹ penalty larger than the gap, so B must rank first in the QCS and the indicators.
cases.setup: Live RFQ, vendors A and B invited, lot absolute weight A = +500, B = 0 saved before any bid; A bids 1000, B bids 1200. Manual (two vendors + weights before bids).
cases.steps: Read the QCS / sheet and `GET /v1/trade/:id/event_indicators`.
cases.expected: "Weighted Total" A = 1500, B = 1200; B ranked L1; the Best Price CTA is hidden on weighted events.
cases.oracle: Ranks from indicators; weighted_total column values.

cases.section: Bidding window, extensions and evaluation windows
cases.title: Automatic award waits for the extended end
cases.why: An auto-award that ran at the original end would award while the auction is still running after an extension.
cases.setup: `gate: auto_awarding_enabled` on an auction round ending at T. A QA vendor.
cases.steps: 1. Trigger an auto-extension (or extend manually) to T + 5 min. 2. Watch the round's auto-award timeline.
cases.expected: At creation the timeline has "enabled". Nothing is awarded at T + 3 s; the award runs only after T + 5 min (timeline "in_progress" then "completed" or "aborted" with a reason).
cases.oracle: `schedule_auto_award_worker` at `bid_end_time + 3 s` (`trade_request.rb:3227-3234`); `AutoAwardWorker` re-schedules itself while `now < bid_end_time` (`auto_award_worker.rb:11-13`); `misc.auto_award_timeline` in the stage read's misc. Note: the digest's gap R-MTR-005-6 ("not moved on extension") is wrong for the outcome — the worker re-checks.

cases.title: Auction-team members cannot open technical or price rounds, but can open shared ones only if allowed
cases.why: Companies that route auctions to a separate team rely on that team not seeing the sourcing (RFQ/RFP) prices.
cases.setup: Buyer company with an auction team; user U in it. Event with a technical round, a price round and an auction. Another price round shared with U through the access list.
cases.steps: As U, open each round.
cases.expected: U is refused on the technical and price rounds and allowed on the auction. Note: the auction-team refusal is checked before sharing, so the shared price round is refused too (Expected (today)); a user outside the buyer workspace is always refused.
cases.oracle: `is_allowed_to_view_client_side?` order: workspace (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:412`) → auction team on RFI/RFP/RFQ → false (`:420-423`) → shared (`:425-428`). Refusal HTTP 422 code 101.

cases.title: A vendor sees an "everyone" round only when its category or location mapping matches the round
cases.why: "Everyone" means every mapped vendor of the matching category/location, not every vendor of the buyer; a wrong match leaks the requirement or hides it from the right vendors.
cases.setup: Round for category C at location L, audience everyone. Vendor V1 mapped to C, V2 mapped to another category only, V3 mapped with no restriction.
cases.steps: As each vendor, list open rounds and open this one.
cases.expected: V1 and V3 see it; V2 does not. A round with no category/location identifiers is visible to every mapped vendor. A restricted round shows only to listed vendors; "everyone except" hides the listed ones. Inactive vendors or inactive user mappings never see it.
cases.oracle: Vendor `is_allowed_to_view?` (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:358-361, 454-468`); audience lists `trade_request.rb:1413-1437`; identifiers per (category ancestors, location, zone) `:1543-1596`; NULL identifiers visible to all (`:183-190`); team match rules `:2865-2893`.

cases.title: Vendor-name masking follows "everyone" or "everyone except super admins"
cases.why: Masking keeps evaluators unbiased; a super admin should see names only when the setting says so.
cases.setup: Masked round with `gate: is_vendor_masking_allowed_for_everyone_except_super_admin`; second round with `…_for_everyone`; third with neither. A super admin and a normal buyer.
cases.steps: Read each round's settings and bid list as both users.
cases.expected: Except-super-admin: names masked for the normal buyer, shown to the super admin. Everyone: masked for both. Neither: shown to both. Buyer user names next to actions are hidden when the round says "do not show user names" (price rounds are created with it off).
cases.oracle: `is_vendor_masking_enabled_for_user` in the stage settings (`trade_template_serializer.rb:129`); readers `trade_request_model_helper.rb:924-930, 1223-1230`; `is_show_user_name` false on RFQ create (`trade_controller_helper.rb:3574`).

cases.section: Quantities, line counts, attachments and price limits
cases.title: A vendor-specific floor price wins over the default; minimum quantity has no vendor-specific value
cases.why: Floor prices protect the buyer per vendor; using the wrong one lets a vendor bid below its floor.
cases.setup: Line with default floor 100.456 and vendor-specific floor 120 for vendor A; default minimum quantity 10 and an attempted vendor-specific minimum 5 for A.
cases.steps: As A and as vendor B read the line limits; as A bid 110.
cases.expected: A's floor 120 (bid 110 refused), B's floor 100.46 (2 decimals). Minimum quantity 10 for both. The buyer sees the default floor.
cases.oracle: `floor_price_for_user` vendor > default (`trade_product.rb:228-237`), called by bid validation `bids_controller_helper.rb:1848`; `floor_quantity_for_user` column else default (`:213-225`); readers round to 2 dp (`:533-549`).

cases.section: Partial updates to a draft round
cases.title: Moving a draft technical round's end past the pricing round's end does not break the server
cases.why: This is exactly what a buyer (or an integration) does while preparing a two-round event, and the publish-time rule (code 712) can only be exercised if the draft can be edited first. A 500 here hides the rule and leaves the buyer with no message.
cases.setup: A fresh draft event with a technical (RFP) round and a pricing (RFQ) round, not published.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, `PATCH /trade/{{rfpTradeId}}` with `{"increase_auction_time": <RFQ end + 3600>, "remarks": "QA_Platform_extend_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: The change is applied or refused cleanly (a 4xx with a message). Never a server error. Today: HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 2xx/4xx passes; a 5xx is the defect.

cases.section: Partial updates to a draft round
cases.title: Moving a draft technical round's end to before the pricing round's end does not break the server
cases.why: The legal direction must work too; it shows the crash is not about the 712 rule.
cases.setup: A fresh draft event with an RFP round and an RFQ round.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, `PATCH /trade/{{rfpTradeId}}` with `increase_auction_time` = RFQ end − 60 s and a remark.
cases.expected: Applied or refused cleanly; never a 5xx. Today: HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Partial updates to a draft round
cases.title: A remark alone sent to a draft technical round does not break the server
cases.why: Pins the trigger: no time field at all.
cases.setup: A fresh draft event with an RFP round and an RFQ round.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, `PATCH /trade/{{rfpTradeId}}` with only `{"remarks": "QA_Platform_extend_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: Applied or refused cleanly; never a 5xx. Today: HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Partial updates to a draft round
cases.title: An empty update to a draft technical round does not break the server
cases.why: The smallest possible request: if this breaks, every partial edit of a draft round does.
cases.setup: A fresh draft event with an RFP round and an RFQ round.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, `PATCH /trade/{{rfpTradeId}}` with `{}`.
cases.expected: Refused cleanly (e.g. missing parameters) or a no-op; never a 5xx. Today: HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Partial updates to a draft round
cases.title: Moving a draft pricing round's end in a two-round event does not break the server
cases.why: Shows the crash is not specific to technical rounds.
cases.setup: A fresh draft event with an RFP round and an RFQ round.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` (the RFQ round) with `increase_auction_time` = its end + 3600 and a remark.
cases.expected: Applied or refused cleanly; never a 5xx. Today: HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Partial updates to a draft round
cases.title: Moving the end of a draft RFQ-only round does not break the server
cases.why: The most common event type; rules out the two-round layout as the cause.
cases.setup: A fresh draft RFQ-only event, not published.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `increase_auction_time` = its end + 3600 and a remark.
cases.expected: Applied or refused cleanly; never a 5xx. Today: HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Partial updates to a draft round
cases.title: An empty update to a draft RFQ-only round does not break the server
cases.why: Same as 004 on a pricing round.
cases.setup: A fresh draft RFQ-only event.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{}`.
cases.expected: Refused cleanly or a no-op; never a 5xx. Today: HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Partial updates to a draft round
cases.title: After a failed partial update the draft round is unchanged
cases.why: The draft branch deactivates the round's forms, access lists and line-item mappings before it rebuilds them (`delete_previous_forms_and_access_lists`, `delete_draft_trade_products_and_associations`). It runs inside a transaction, so a crash should roll everything back — if it does not, the draft silently loses its line items or questionnaire.
cases.setup: A fresh draft RFP + RFQ event. Manual: the plan runner stops at the first server error, so the read-back cannot follow it yet.
cases.steps: 1. Send API-EVDDRF-004's empty update (HTTP 500). 2. `GET /trade/{{rfpTradeId}}?response_type=template` and `GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_line_items`. 3. Publish the event.
cases.expected: The round still has its form and the event its line item; publishing works as on an untouched draft.
cases.oracle: Same form/line counts as before step 1; publish 200.

cases.section: Partial updates to a draft round
cases.title: The publish-time rule still refuses a technical round that ends after the pricing round
cases.why: The rule the ticket was about (code 712) is checked at publish, and draft rounds are skipped while editing (`trade_controller_helper.rb:643`). With partial draft edits broken, the only way to set up the scenario is to build the technical round with the later end time in the stage body itself.
cases.setup: A draft RFP + RFQ event whose RFP round was CREATED (POST /trade/template_input) with bid_end_time after the RFQ's. Manual: stage bodies are not runnable in the plan language.
cases.steps: 1. Publish the event (`PATCH /event_groups/:id` status active with both draft round ids).
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 712 'RFP duration exceeds RFQ end time. Please adjust.'; both rounds stay draft.
cases.oracle: Code 712; `GET /event_groups/:id` status draft.

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: Sending only a new start time is silently ignored
cases.why: The reschedule branch needs BOTH times; with one of them the request falls through to the generic save and answers success, so an integration or a stale screen believes the reschedule worked.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ, bidding started at publish, no bids.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{"bid_start_time": {{now+3600}}}`. 2. Read the round back.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 and nothing changes — the round still starts in the past. Should be refused (422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters') so the caller knows nothing happened.
cases.oracle: 200; `starting_from` ≤ now.

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: Sending only a new end time does not extend the round
cases.why: `bid_end_time` on its own is neither a reschedule nor an extension (that is `increase_auction_time`); a caller "extending" this way gets a success while vendors are still cut off at the old time.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ open about 20 minutes, no bids.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{"bid_end_time": {{now+7200}}}`. 2. Read the round back.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 but the end does not move. Should be refused (code 2) or applied.
cases.oracle: 200; `ending_at` ≤ now + 30 min (not two hours from now).

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: A started technical round cannot be rescheduled
cases.why: Technical rounds take a slightly different path (evaluator handling runs first, closed is an allowed status); the started rule must still hold and nothing must be written before it.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFP+RFQ event; both rounds started at publish; QA vendor 1 invited to both.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{rfpTradeId}}` with `{"bid_start_time": {{now+3600}}, "bid_end_time": {{now+7200}}}`.
cases.expected: Refused. The evaluator step that runs before the guard only acts when `forms` are sent, so it writes nothing. HTTP 422, code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!'.

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: A closed technical round answers the same "cannot re-schedule"
cases.why: Technical rounds stay editable after close, so only the started rule stops a "reschedule" from reopening a finished technical round and wiping its evaluation timeline.
cases.setup: A fresh RFP+RFQ event whose technical response is in and whose windows are both over.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{rfpTradeId}}` with `{"bid_start_time": {{now+3600}}, "bid_end_time": {{now+7200}}}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!'.

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: A closed pricing round cannot be rescheduled
cases.why: A closed commercial round must never be reopened through the reschedule path.
cases.setup: A fresh RFQ whose bidding window and extra closing time are over; QA vendor 1 invited, no bids.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{"bid_start_time": {{now+3600}}, "bid_end_time": {{now+7200}}}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422 with code 4 'Request not found' once the round's status is closed (closed RFQ rounds are not editable), or code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!' if the close job has not flipped the status yet.
cases.oracle: Any 422 without a 5xx; the code is 4 or 258.

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: An awarded round cannot be rescheduled
cases.why: Moving the clock of a round whose award proposal is submitted would orphan the award.
cases.setup: A fresh RFQ where QA vendor 1 bid, the round closed, and an award proposal was created and submitted.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{"bid_start_time": {{now+3600}}, "bid_end_time": {{now+7200}}}`.
cases.expected: Refused (HTTP 422): code 769 'You cannot edit rfq once the auction is created.' where the company has rfx projects on (a requested/selected proposal restricts RFQ changes — misleading wording, see API-XMAT-035), otherwise code 4 'Request not found' (closed) or 258.
cases.oracle: 422 without a 5xx.

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: The vendor app cannot reschedule, re-time lines or reopen lines
cases.why: A bidder moving its own deadline is a fairness breach; the block is the app gate, not the policy.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1's session on the vendor website, invited to a live round. Manual: the backend answers a vendor-app call to a console-only action with 401 and SIGNS THAT SESSION OUT, so this can never be a runnable twin.
cases.steps: As the vendor (vendor website), send each of: `PATCH /trade/<round>` with a reschedule body, `PATCH /trade/<round>/staggered_time`, `POST /trade/<round>/reopen_line_items`.
cases.expected: Each is refused at the app gate: HTTP 401 'app not authorized', and the vendor's session ends. No schedule changes. (So the "vendor in the auction" attacker of API-XDLOT-062 cannot reach staggered_time; the realistic attacker is a console user of another company, API-EVDTME-013.)
cases.oracle: 401 on all three; round times unchanged when read by the buyer.

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: "Rescheduling" a draft round is a full draft rewrite
cases.why: A draft is diverted to the draft editor before the reschedule branch; that editor rebuilds the round from the body — with only two times in it, the round's lines are voided and its config rebuilt.
cases.setup: A draft event with an RFQ round and one line. Manual (destructive to the draft; API-XPUB-066 already checks the same path does not 5xx).
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/<draft round>` with only `{"bid_start_time": <now+3600>, "bid_end_time": <now+7200>}`. 2. Read the round and the event's line items back.
cases.expected: Either refused by the draft editor's own checks or 200 with the round's lines voided (`delete_draft_trade_products_and_associations`) and any draft bids made inactive. Should only change the times, or be refused with a clear code.
cases.oracle: Round line count before vs after; no 5xx.

cases.section: Rescheduling an upcoming round (manual — every recipe starts bidding at publish)
cases.title: An upcoming round can be "rescheduled" to a start in the past
cases.why: The 258 guard checks the round's CURRENT start, not the new one, and `edit_trade_schedules` has no lower bound — the round goes live immediately with a start in the past and vendors get a "new trade" push instead of a scheduled-auction notice. The screen blocks this (UI-EVDTME-002); the API does not.
cases.setup: An upcoming RFQ as API-EVDTME-016.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/<round>` with `{"bid_start_time": <now-3600>, "bid_end_time": <now+3600>}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; the round is running at once. Should be 422 code 195 'Invalid time.'.
cases.oracle: `starting_from` < now after the call.

cases.section: Rescheduling an upcoming round (manual — every recipe starts bidding at publish)
cases.title: An end before (or equal to) the start is accepted
cases.why: There is no end-after-start check and no minimum duration anywhere on the reschedule path (TradeSchedule has no validations); a round with end ≤ start never runs and is closed by the close job at its "end".
cases.setup: An upcoming RFQ as API-EVDTME-016.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/<round>` with `{"bid_start_time": <now+4h>, "bid_end_time": <now+3h>}`. 2. Repeat with end = start.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 both times. Should be 422 code 195 'Invalid time.' (or 507 'Invalid Time Input').
cases.oracle: Read-back `ending_at` ≤ `starting_from`; a vendor can never bid (code 33).

cases.section: Rescheduling an upcoming round (manual — every recipe starts bidding at publish)
cases.title: Leaving out the extra closing time silently drops the evaluation window
cases.why: `edit_trade_schedules` marks an existing extra closing schedule inactive whenever the reschedule body has no `extra_closing_time`; the dashboard always sends it, but any other caller loses the evaluation window without a word.
cases.setup: An upcoming RFQ with an extra closing time (as API-EVDTME-016).
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/<round>` with only `{"bid_start_time": <now+4h>, "bid_end_time": <now+5h>}`. 2. Read the round back.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; `extra_closing_time` is gone and closed_at = the new bid end. Should keep the window (shifted) or refuse.
cases.oracle: `extra_closing_time` absent/null in the read-back; the extra closing trade schedule row has status in_active.

cases.section: Rescheduling an upcoming round (manual — every recipe starts bidding at publish)
cases.title: An upcoming pricing round cannot end before its technical round
cases.why: Business rule: the RFP must not end after the RFQ; the reschedule path runs the same check as publish.
cases.setup: A live RFP+RFQ event where the RFQ is still upcoming (start in 2 h) and the RFP ends in 3 h.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/<rfq round>` with `{"bid_start_time": <now+2h>, "bid_end_time": <now+2.5h>}`.
cases.expected: Refused; nothing moves (the transaction is left early and rolled back). HTTP 422, code 712 'RFP duration exceeds RFQ end time. Please adjust.'.
cases.oracle: 422 + 712; RFQ schedule unchanged.

cases.section: Rescheduling an upcoming round (manual — every recipe starts bidding at publish)
cases.title: An upcoming technical round cannot be moved past its pricing round
cases.why: The same rule from the other side.
cases.setup: A live RFP+RFQ event where the RFP is upcoming and the RFQ ends in 3 h.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/<rfp round>` with `{"bid_start_time": <now+1h>, "bid_end_time": <now+4h>}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 712 'RFP duration exceeds RFQ end time. Please adjust.'.

cases.section: Rescheduling an upcoming round (manual — every recipe starts bidding at publish)
cases.title: Adding "from_mcp" to the body skips the RFP-before-RFQ rule
cases.why: The flag meant for the internal assistant is read straight from request params, so any console caller can bypass the 712 rule on a reschedule (the extension path reads it from code options instead and cannot be bypassed).
cases.setup: As API-EVDTME-021.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/<rfp round>` with `{"bid_start_time": <now+1h>, "bid_end_time": <now+4h>, "from_mcp": true}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; the RFP now ends after the RFQ. Should be 712 regardless of the flag.
cases.oracle: RFP `ending_at` > RFQ `ending_at` after the call.

cases.section: Rescheduling an upcoming round (manual — every recipe starts bidding at publish)
cases.title: Text times on an upcoming round crash the request
cases.why: `Time.at` is called on the raw parameter; a string raises TypeError, which is not rescued.
cases.setup: An upcoming RFQ as API-EVDTME-016.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/<round>` with `{"bid_start_time": "2026-10-10 10:00", "bid_end_time": "2026-10-10 12:00"}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 195 'Invalid time.'. Today HTTP 500 (TypeError in `Time.at`; in an RFP+RFQ event it already fails in the 712 check).
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Rescheduling an upcoming round (manual — every recipe starts bidding at publish)
cases.title: A staggered auction's line times shift only by the change in start
cases.why: `reschedule_trade_products_time` adds (new start − old start) to every line and ignores the new end: lengthening the round leaves the tail with no open line; shortening leaves the last lines open after the round has ended.
cases.setup: An upcoming staggered line-item auction, 3 lines of 20 min each (start S, end S+60 min), QA vendors only.
cases.steps: 1. Reschedule to start S+1 h, end S+1 h+30 min (shorter). 2. Read `misc.trade_products_time` back. 3. Separately, reschedule to start S+1 h, end S+3 h (longer).
cases.expected: Lines move by exactly +1 h in both cases: in 1 the third line ends 30 min after the round; in 3 the round has 2 h with no open line. Should rescale the lines or refuse a duration change on a staggered round.
cases.oracle: Max line end vs `ending_at`.

cases.section: Rescheduling an upcoming round (manual — every recipe starts bidding at publish)
cases.title: After a reschedule, a vendor cannot bid at the old start time
cases.why: The bid lock follows the moved clock: a vendor who prepared for the original start must be told to wait, not allowed in early.
cases.setup: An upcoming RFQ with QA vendor 1, originally starting at T; rescheduled to start at T+1 h.
cases.steps: At T + 1 min, as QA vendor 1, `POST /v1/bids` for the round.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 33 'Order not active' (not running).
cases.oracle: 422 + 33; at T+1 h the same call succeeds.

cases.section: Auction reschedule and extension emails (commit c74ea64581, manual)
cases.title: The buyer-side reschedule mail goes to the owner and the auction team and names who rescheduled
cases.why: The owner must know another user moved their auction.
cases.setup: As API-EVDTME-029; a second QA buyer (not the owner) does the reschedule; auction team = QA users only.
cases.steps: Reschedule as the second buyer; open the owner's and auction-team mailboxes.
cases.expected: The owner gets "📅 <ref> | Auction has been rescheduled by <second buyer>"; each other auction-team member gets the same mail once; the owner is not mailed twice; push "Auction rescheduled" to owner + team.
cases.oracle: Recipients = owner ∪ auction team, de-duplicated; "by" = the rescheduling user (falls back to the owner when the user id is missing).

cases.section: Auction reschedule and extension emails (commit c74ea64581, manual)
cases.title: The 24-hour and 30-minute start reminders follow the new start
cases.why: Without re-planning, vendors would be reminded for the old start; the old jobs are left queued and must drop themselves.
cases.setup: An upcoming auction starting in 3 days; QA vendors only.
cases.steps: Reschedule to start in 2 days; watch the Sidekiq schedule and QA vendor mailboxes at the old and new reminder times.
cases.expected: New jobs at new start − 24 h and − 30 min; the old jobs fire at their time and do nothing (the worker skips a reminder more than one minute away from start − 24 h / − 30 min); each vendor receives exactly one 24-hour and one 30-minute reminder.
cases.oracle: Mail count per vendor = 1 per reminder type.

cases.section: Auction reschedule and extension emails (commit c74ea64581, manual)
cases.title: An RFQ-then-auction rescheduled with its evaluation time sends each start reminder twice
cases.why: For rfq_then_auction rounds `edit_trade_schedules` already queues the 24 h / 30 min reminders whenever `extra_closing_time` is sent (and the dashboard always sends it), and the new `reschedule_auction_reminder_jobs` queues them again; both pass the ±1 minute check, so vendors get duplicates.
cases.setup: An upcoming RFQ-then-auction round with an extra closing time, start more than 24 h away; QA vendors only.
cases.steps: Reschedule it via the dashboard dialog (body includes `extra_closing_time`); count the reminder mails each QA vendor receives.
cases.expected: One 24-hour and one 30-minute reminder per vendor. Today: two of each (suspected defect from #16149).
cases.oracle: Sidekiq schedule holds two `auction_reminder_24h_before` jobs for the round at the same time.

cases.section: Auction reschedule and extension emails (commit c74ea64581, manual)
cases.title: Force-ending an auction emails vendors "Submission time extended"
cases.why: Force-close during submission is implemented as `increase_auction_time = now`, which sets the same flag as an extension; after #16149 every vendor receives "Submission time extended" at the moment the auction is ended early.
cases.setup: A live auction with QA vendors only; company config `trade_force_close` on.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/<round>` with `{"force_end": true, "remarks": "QA_Platform_force_end"}`; open the vendors' mailboxes.
cases.expected: The auction ends; vendors are told it ended. Today they also receive "⏰ … | Submission time extended for Auction" showing the new (past) end time (suspected defect).
cases.oracle: Presence of the submission-extended mail after a force end.

cases.section: Auction reschedule and extension emails (commit c74ea64581, manual)
cases.title: Pulling an auction's end earlier also emails "Submission time extended"
cases.why: The extension field accepts an earlier time (API-EVDTME-066); the email does not distinguish and tells vendors their time was extended when it was cut.
cases.setup: A live auction ending in 30 min, QA vendors only.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/<round>` with `increase_auction_time` = now + 5 min; open the mailboxes.
cases.expected: 200; vendors get "Submission time extended" with the earlier end. Should be refused (or worded as a change, not an extension).
cases.oracle: Mail subject vs new `ending_at` < old.

cases.section: Auction reschedule and extension emails (commit c74ea64581, manual)
cases.title: After an extension, vendors get the expiry reminder again at the new 80% point
cases.why: #16149 re-plans expiry reminders on extension so a vendor reminded before the extension is reminded again before the new end.
cases.setup: A live auction (start S, 60 min) with QA vendors; round config `send_event_expiry_reminder_to_vendor` = true and `event_expiry_reminder_times` = [0.8] (key read at trade_request.rb:2208-2211).
cases.steps: 1. Wait until S + 50 min (the 80% reminder has fired). 2. Extend to S + 120 min. 3. Watch mailboxes. 4. On a second auction, extend at S + 30 min (before the 80% point).
cases.expected: 1–3: a second reminder at S + 96 min (80% of the new length). 4: no new job is queued; the original job fires at S + 48 min, sees the new 80% point is ≥ 2 min away and re-times itself to S + 96 min — one reminder in total. With the config not exactly `true` (e.g. "true" text) no vendor reminder is re-planned.
cases.oracle: Reminder mail times per vendor.

cases.title: Extending a live staggered auction from the screen tells nobody and keeps no remark
cases.why: On a live staggered round the "Increase time" dialog calls staggered_time instead of the normal extension (UI-EVDTME-006); that action sets no extension flag, so vendors get no push or email, the bids' stored end time is not updated, and the remark typed in the dialog is never sent.
cases.setup: A live staggered line-item auction with QA vendors 1 and 2 (each bid on line 1); line 2 running.
cases.steps: In the buyer console, Settings → Increase time by 10 min with a remark; then check vendor notifications/mail, the round's remarks and the bids' end time.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; running and upcoming lines move +10 min (and the round + evaluation end if the last line now ends later); no vendor notice, no remark, bids' end_time unchanged. Should notify vendors and record the remark like a normal extension.
cases.oracle: No `buyer_time_increase` push; `remarks` without the new entry.

cases.title: A normal extension of a staggered round leaves every line closed at its old time
cases.why: `increase_auction_time` moves the round's end but not the per-line windows; after the generic save the line hash is only re-validated, so the extra time has no open line and vendors still cannot bid (suspected — confirm the line-level bid check).
cases.setup: A live staggered auction (3 lines); QA vendor 1 invited; the last line ends with the round.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/<round>` with `increase_auction_time` = end + 15 min. 2. Read `misc.trade_products_time`. 3. 5 minutes after the old end, QA vendor 1 tries to bid on line 3.
cases.expected: Step 1: 200; step 2: line times unchanged; step 3: refused (line closed). Should extend the running/last line (as the screen's per-line path does) or refuse the plain extension on staggered rounds.
cases.oracle: Max line end < `ending_at` after the call.

cases.title: Reopening during the evaluation window needs the right to reopen an expired event
cases.why: The drawer is offered in the "buffer" (evaluation) state, but once the round's bidding has ended the schedule update applies the reopen rule; buyers without that right get a refusal the screen does not explain.
cases.setup: A staggered auction whose bidding has ended and whose evaluation window is running; a buyer who is not super admin / Procol, company without `user_allowed_to_reopen_event`.
cases.steps: Reopen one expired line for 10 min.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 496 'You are not allowed to reopen an expired event'. With the right: 200 and the line runs from NOW (not from the old end) for 10 min.
cases.oracle: 496 / line start ≈ request time.

cases.title: A numeric extension sent as text crashes the reopen
cases.why: "600" passes the `.to_i > 0` check but is then added to an integer time unconverted.
cases.setup: A live staggered auction with one expired line.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/<round>/reopen_line_items` with `{"trade_product_uuids": ["<line>"], "reopen_time_extension": "600"}`.
cases.expected: Should be 200 (or 422). Today HTTP 500 (TypeError: String can't be coerced into Integer); the transaction is rolled back.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: An unknown line id crashes the reopen
cases.why: The validator silently drops ids that are not lines of the round, then the loop writes into a missing entry.
cases.setup: A live staggered auction with one expired line.
cases.steps: Reopen `["<expired line>", "Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="]` for 600 s.
cases.expected: Should be 422 (code 80 'Product not found' or 2). Today HTTP 500 (NoMethodError on nil) — rolled back.
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: A null line list crashes before the controller runs
cases.why: `trade_product_uuids` is the exact key the drawer sends; the id decoding that runs before every action calls `.map` on any key ending in "uuids", so null from a bad client is a server error (same class as API-XPUB-011, on this endpoint).
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ (not staggered), QA vendor 1 invited, no bids.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/{{tradeId}}/reopen_line_items` with `{"trade_product_uuids": null, "reopen_time_extension": 600}`.
cases.expected: Should be refused cleanly (422; code 4 here since the round is not staggered). Today HTTP 500 (NoMethodError: undefined method `map` for nil).
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.section: Late bids against a moved clock
cases.title: A draft opened before the end was pulled in cannot be priced after it
cases.why: A vendor half-way through a quote when the clock moves must not finish it after the new end.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ open about 20 minutes, QA vendor 1 invited, no bids.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, open a draft bid. 2. As the buyer, pull the end in to now + 90 s. 3. Wait until it has passed. 4. As QA vendor 1, price the line on the draft from step 1.
cases.expected: Step 4 is refused (HTTP 422): code 32 'Bid not found' once the end-of-bidding job has discarded drafts, otherwise code 33 'Order not active' (or 508 'Not allowed to bid on this product' where counter-offer modification is on and the round is in its extra closing time).
cases.oracle: Step 4 is a 422, never 2xx or 5xx.

cases.section: Late bids against a moved clock
cases.title: A vendor who already bid cannot revise after the end is pulled in
cases.why: Revisions follow the moved clock too; a vendor must not slip a better price in after the new end.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ where QA vendor 1 has submitted a bid, bidding still open; `counter_offer_modification_enabled` off on the round.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, pull the end in to now + 90 s. 2. Wait until it has passed. 3. As QA vendor 1, place a new bid. 4. Read the round back.
cases.expected: Step 3 is refused: HTTP 422, code 33 'Order not active'. The earlier bid remains the vendor's quote.
cases.oracle: Step 3 code 33; `ending_at` ≤ now.

cases.section: The request shape and finding the round
cases.title: A request without the weightages object is refused
cases.why: The whole weight table must sit under `weightages`; a flat payload must not half-apply.
cases.setup: A live RFQ round with no bids and no weights (recipe `published_rfq`).
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}/edit_weight_parameters` with `{"weightage_on": "lot", "values": {…one valid weight…}}` (no `weightages` wrapper).
cases.expected: Refused, nothing saved, the round stays unweighted. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2; `GET /trade/{{tradeId}}` shows no `weightages` and `trade_config.is_weighted_bid_event` false.

cases.section: The request shape and finding the round
cases.title: The older payload shape (key list + name list, no "weight on") is refused
cases.why: The legacy create-screen modal still builds `{key_attributes, weightage_names, values: {vendor: [..]}}`; the server must refuse it cleanly rather than store a half-understood table.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}/edit_weight_parameters` with `{"weightages": {"key_attributes": ["qa_freight_adj"], "weightage_names": ["QA_Platform_Freight_{{stamp}}"], "values": {"{{vendorUuid}}": ["100"]}}}`.
cases.expected: Refused because "weight on" is missing. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2; round still unweighted.

cases.section: The request shape and finding the round
cases.title: Weights cannot be added to a draft round through this action
cases.why: The lookup is `TradeRequest.active`, so a draft round (status draft) is invisible here. Buyers preparing an event must set weights in the create flow instead; the refusal reads "Insufficient parameters", which does not say why.
cases.setup: A draft event with an unpublished RFQ round (recipe `draft_rfq`).
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}/edit_weight_parameters` with a valid lot weight body.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2; the draft round has no weights afterwards.

cases.section: The request shape and finding the round
cases.title: A withdrawn event's round cannot be weighted
cases.why: Withdrawal marks every stage in-active; scoring changes on a cancelled event would confuse any later audit.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`, then the event is withdrawn with a remark (arrange step `withdraw_event`; QA vendor 1 is the only invitee).
cases.steps: 1. Withdraw the event. 2. `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}/edit_weight_parameters` with a valid lot weight body.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: The vendor app may not call this action, and trying signs the vendor out
cases.why: Vendors must never edit weights; the app-level block is the guard, and its side effect (session ended) must be known.
cases.setup: QA vendor 1 session (vendor app). Manual: the app answer is 401 and it ends the session, so it is never a twin.
cases.steps: As the vendor, `PATCH /trade/:id/edit_weight_parameters` with a valid body.
cases.expected: HTTP 401 (app not authorized for this action); the vendor session is marked in-active.
cases.oracle: 401; the vendor must log in again; no weight rows.

cases.section: First save, re-edits and what the round shows afterwards
cases.title: The first weight save also locks vendors' quantities (allow_fixed_quantity_for_bidding)
cases.why: The first save quietly turns on `allow_fixed_quantity_for_bidding` on a live round and drops participant quantity from the partial-closing widgets. Vendors who could quote partial quantities a minute ago are now refused with code 207 'Bid Quantity should be equal to the Auction Quantity' (`bids_controller_helper.rb:1898-1900`), and nothing tells the buyer.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: The happy-path save, then read the round.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; `trade_config.allow_fixed_quantity_for_bidding` is true afterwards. Product confirmation needed that a weight save should change bidding rules; at minimum the screen should say so.
cases.oracle: `trade_config.allow_fixed_quantity_for_bidding` true after the save.

cases.section: First save, re-edits and what the round shows afterwards
cases.title: Vendors are told which criteria they are weighted on
cases.why: The vendor's terms gain the sentence "Your evaluation for this event will depend on … along with the Gross Total"; this is how a vendor learns the criteria exist.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`; the happy-path save.
cases.steps: Save, then read the round as QA vendor 1.
cases.expected: The vendor's terms include a line naming "QA_Platform_Freight_…". Today the list also names the synthetic "Weighted Total" column ("depend on QA_Platform_Freight_…, Weighted Total along with the Gross Total") — cosmetic defect.
cases.oracle: Vendor `GET /trade/{{tradeId}}`: some `terms_and_conditions` entry contains the label.

cases.section: First save, re-edits and what the round shows afterwards
cases.title: Leaving a weight out of the next save removes it
cases.why: The screen's "Delete" works by omission; the dropped weight must stop counting.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`; arrange: save two weights (qa_freight_adj and qa_quality_pen).
cases.steps: Save again with only qa_freight_adj; read the round.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; the weight list is qa_freight_adj + weighted_total only; qa_quality_pen is gone from the values (its rows are set in-active).
cases.oracle: `weightages.key_attributes` has 2 entries; `weightages.values.qa_quality_pen` absent; `misc.weightage.key_attributes` has 2 entries.

cases.section: First save, re-edits and what the round shows afterwards
cases.title: Switching a round from lot weights to line-item weights
cases.why: The closing mode can change after weights exist; the second save must replace the lot rows, not add line rows beside them.
cases.setup: A live RFQ with two line items and lot weights saved; the trade-product ids from the round read (no recipe exposes them, so manual).
cases.steps: Save the same key with `"weightage_on": "line_item"` and `{vendor: {<tp1>: "10", <tp2>: "20"}}`; read the round.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; `weightages.weightage_on` "line_item"; per-line values shown. The old lot rows should be in-active.
cases.oracle: Round read; DB: `weightages` rows with item_type TradeRequest for that key are in_active.

cases.section: First save, re-edits and what the round shows afterwards
cases.title: After a lot → line switch the old lot weights keep counting in the ranking
cases.why: `handle_removed_weight_keys` deactivates only keys that disappeared, and only on the storage of the OLD mode. If the key names stay the same, the round-level (lot) rows stay active; the lot score still adds them through `get_weight_for_participant` (which sums every active row of the round, regardless of the current mode) while the line score adds the new line rows. The vendor is penalised twice.
cases.setup: As API-EVDWGT-019, then two vendors bid (or `allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` ON and bids already in). Manual.
cases.steps: Compare the vendor's weighted total in the QCS with price + new line weights.
cases.expected: Only the line weights count. Today (suspected): the stale lot amount is still added.
cases.oracle: DB: active Weightage rows of item_type TradeRequest for the round after the switch; QCS weighted total ≠ expected.

cases.section: First save, re-edits and what the round shows afterwards
cases.title: Line-item weights for each line and vendor
cases.why: The line mode is what multi-line RFQs with per-item freight differences use; each line's value must land on that line only.
cases.setup: Live RFQ with two lines, two invited vendors, no bids; trade-product ids from the round read. Manual (needs trade-product ids).
cases.steps: Save `{"weightage_on": "line_item", "values": {"qa_freight_adj": {"label": "…", "input_type": "absolute", "data": {<v1>: {<tp1>: "10", <tp2>: "20"}, <v2>: {<tp1>: "5"}}}}}`; read the round and the buyer schema.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; values come back per line per vendor; the buyer's line sheet gets one column per weight plus "Weighted Price" (named after the ranking key).
cases.oracle: `weightages.values.qa_freight_adj.data.<v1>.<tp1>` "10.0" etc.; schema inline widgets include the weight keys.

cases.section: First save, re-edits and what the round shows afterwards
cases.title: Weights do not stop the vendor from bidding
cases.why: Turning a round into a weighted round changes bidding config (fixed quantity); a vendor must still be able to submit afterwards.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: 1. Buyer saves the happy-path weight. 2. QA vendor 1 opens, prices and submits a bid. 3. Read the round.
cases.expected: Both succeed; the round is still weighted.
cases.oracle: Step 1 HTTP 200, step 2 accepted; `trade_config.is_weighted_bid_event` true.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: "Weight on" must be lot or line_item
cases.why: Any other value would store rows nobody reads.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with `"weightage_on": "vendor"`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2; round unweighted.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A table with no weights is refused
cases.why: "Weight on" alone would make the round weighted with only the synthetic total.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: `{"weightages": {"weightage_on": "lot"}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2; round unweighted.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A weight needs a name
cases.why: The name is the column header in the sheet and the criterion in the vendor's terms; a blank one is meaningless.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with `"label": " "`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: The weight type must be absolute or relative
cases.why: The type decides whether the value is ₹ or %; an unknown type has no maths.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with `"input_type": "percentage"`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A weight sent as a JSON number is refused (only text numbers pass)
cases.why: The value check is `instance_of?(String) || instance_of?(Numeric)`; no JSON number is ever an *instance of* Numeric (it is an Integer or Float), so `100` is refused while `"100"` is accepted. Any integration sending numbers gets "Insufficient parameters" with no hint.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with `"data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": 100}` (number, not text).
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. Should be accepted (`is_a?(Numeric)`).
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A relative weight of exactly 100% is refused
cases.why: The server range is -100 < x < 100 (exclusive), while the screen allows -100…100 inclusive (UI-EVDWGT-005). The boundary must be known.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with `"input_type": "relative"` and value `"100"`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A non-numeric absolute weight is stored as zero
