cases.why: An absolute value is only checked for being text, then saved with `to_f`; "abc" (or "") becomes 0 with a success message, so a typo silently removes a vendor's penalty.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Absolute, value `"abc"`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 'Weights added successfully!' and the vendor's value is 0.0. Should be HTTP 422 code 2.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; a read shows "0.0" for the vendor.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: Line-item weights must be given per line, not as one number per vendor
cases.why: In line mode each vendor's value must be a map of line → value.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: `"weightage_on": "line_item"`, `"data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": "100"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2; round unweighted.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A weight can be set for a vendor who is not invited to the round
cases.why: Vendor keys are decoded to a company id and stored without checking the round's audience, so weights pile up for companies that never see the event and appear in every read of the round.
cases.setup: `published_rfq` (QA vendor 2 is NOT invited).
cases.steps: Happy-path body with `"data": {"{{vendor2Uuid}}": "100"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 and a weight row for QA vendor 2. Should be refused (vendor not in audience).
cases.oracle: No 5xx; read shows a value under QA vendor 2.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A weight for a company that does not exist reports success but saves nothing
cases.why: `Weightage#save` fails validation (no such company) and its result is ignored; the buyer is told "Weights added successfully!" and the round becomes weighted with an empty column.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with `"data": {"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==": "100"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 'Weights added successfully!'; no weight row; round marked weighted. Should be 422.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; read shows the key but no vendor value.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A line weight for a line that does not exist reports success but saves nothing
cases.why: Same silent failure in line mode: the line id is not checked against the round.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Line mode, `"data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": {"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==": "100"}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; nothing stored; round now "line_item" weighted. Should be 422.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: weightages sent as text (or a number) is refused, not a crash
cases.why: The first line reads `weightages[:weightage_on]`; on a String or Integer that raises TypeError before any check.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: `{"weightages": "QA_Platform_weights_{{stamp}}"}` (also try `{"weightages": 5}` by hand).
cases.expected: Should be HTTP 422 code 2. Today the code path at trade_controller.rb:1779 raises TypeError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Any 5xx is the defect.

cases.title: weightages sent as a list is refused, not a crash
cases.why: Same unguarded index on an Array.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: `{"weightages": ["lot"]}`.
cases.expected: Should be HTTP 422 code 2. Today `Array#[](:weightage_on)` raises TypeError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: The weight list sent as text crashes the validator
cases.why: `values` only has to be present; the validator then calls `.each` on it.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: `{"weightages": {"weightage_on": "lot", "values": "QA_Platform_text"}}`.
cases.expected: Should be HTTP 422 code 2. Today `String#each` → NoMethodError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: A weight's vendor values sent as text crash the validator
cases.why: `data` is only checked for blankness, then iterated.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with `"data": "QA_Platform_text"`.
cases.expected: Should be HTTP 422 code 2. Today `String#each` → NoMethodError → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: A weight list sent as key/value pairs passes validation, writes rows, then crashes
cases.why: `[["qa_freight_adj", {…}]]` iterates exactly like a hash, so validation passes and the weight rows are committed; then `weights.keys` fails on the Array. The buyer sees an error, but the vendor's weight row is live while the round is not marked weighted.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: `{"weightages": {"weightage_on": "lot", "values": [["qa_freight_adj", {"label": "QA_Platform_Freight_{{stamp}}", "input_type": "absolute", "data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": "100"}}]]}}`.
cases.expected: Should be HTTP 422 code 2 with nothing written. Today (suspected): HTTP 500 (NoMethodError `keys` for Array) after the Weightage row is saved.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; DB: no Weightage row for the round.

cases.title: A garbled line id in line mode crashes the save
cases.why: A line id that decodes to nothing is passed as `item_id: nil` into a Sorbet-typed method that requires an Integer.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Line mode, `"data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": {"WrongUuid1=": "100"}}`.
cases.expected: Should be HTTP 422 code 2. Today (suspected): TypeError from the `item_id: Integer` signature → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: Script text in a weight name is stripped before it is stored
cases.why: The name is echoed into the sheet header and the vendor's terms; it must never come back as markup.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with `"label": "QA_Platform_<script>alert(1)</script>_{{stamp}}"`; read the round.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; the stored name is "QA_Platform_alert(1)_…" (tags removed).
cases.oracle: `misc.weightage.weightage_names` contains "QA_Platform_alert(1)_{{stamp}}".

cases.section: Bids already in, and the round's state
cases.title: With allow_edit_weight_param_rfq on, weights can be added after bids
cases.why: The other side of the switch: companies that enable it expect the save to go through.
cases.setup: `rfq_with_bid` on a company whose template sets `allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` true.
cases.steps: Happy-path save.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 'Weights added successfully!'.
cases.oracle: 200; round weighted.

cases.section: Bids already in, and the round's state
cases.title: Editing weights after bids does not re-rank the bids already in
cases.why: The weighted path only updates rows and `misc`; it never recalculates `event_score_for_participants` (the publish path does, trade_controller_helper.rb:4575-4577). Ranks and the vendor's own rank stay on the old weights until some vendor saves a bid again.
cases.setup: `allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` ON; two QA vendors bid; weights saved, then changed to flip the order. Manual (setting + two bids).
cases.steps: Change the weights; read indicators / QCS before and after a vendor revises.
cases.expected: Ranks follow the new weights immediately. Today (suspected): unchanged until the next bid save.
cases.oracle: `GET /v1/trade/:id/event_indicators` rank unchanged right after the edit.

cases.section: Bids already in, and the round's state
cases.title: A closed round with a bid refuses weight changes
cases.why: After close, the bid lock (or the closed status) must hold.
cases.setup: `closed_rfq_with_bid`; `allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` off.
cases.steps: Happy-path save.
cases.expected: Refused: HTTP 422 code 15 'Operation failed' while the round is still active, or code 2 'Insufficient parameters' once it is closed.
cases.oracle: Non-2xx, no 5xx.

cases.section: Bids already in, and the round's state
cases.title: An awarded round refuses weight changes
cases.why: Re-weighting after award would make the award contradict the ranking.
cases.setup: `awarded_rfq` (bid in, closed, proposal submitted); `allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` off.
cases.steps: Happy-path save.
cases.expected: Refused: 422 code 15 or code 2 (see 066). With the setting on and the round still active the API would accept — there is no award check.
cases.oracle: Non-2xx, no 5xx.

cases.section: Bids already in, and the round's state
cases.title: Price-based, knockout, Dutch and rank-and-price auctions cannot get weights after creation
cases.why: The first save requires a rank or traffic-light round. A price-based auction refuses with the generic "Operation failed", which looks like a server fault.
cases.setup: Live auctions of each strategy, no weights, no bids. Manual (no auction recipe).
cases.steps: Happy-path save on each.
cases.expected: rank / traffic_light: HTTP 200. price / rank_and_price / knockout / dutch / book_building: HTTP 422 code 15 'Operation failed'.
cases.oracle: Codes per strategy.

cases.section: Bids already in, and the round's state
cases.title: Auctions and RFQ-then-auction rounds use allow_edit_weight_param_auction after bids
cases.why: Auctions have their own switch; an RFQ-then-auction stage follows the auction switch, not the RFQ one.
cases.setup: Rank auction and RFQ-then-auction stage with one bid each; `allow_edit_weight_param_auction` off, then on. Manual.
cases.steps: Happy-path save on each, both settings.
cases.expected: Off: HTTP 422 code 15 'Operation failed'. On: HTTP 200.
cases.oracle: As stated; `allow_edit_weight_param_rfq` has no effect on these rounds.

cases.section: Ranking, comparison and who can see the weights
cases.title: Relative weights are a percentage of the vendor's own score
cases.why: A relative weight adds score × value / 100 (4-decimal precision by default), not a flat amount; a -10% on a 2000 bid must read 1800.
cases.setup: As 072 with relative weights A = -10, B = +5; bids A 2000, B 1800. Manual.
cases.steps: Read weighted totals.
cases.oracle: Weighted totals in the sheet.

cases.section: Weights set while creating the round (POST /trade/template_input) — catalog only
cases.title: Line weights sent at creation are matched to lines by weight identifier
cases.why: At creation the lines have no ids yet; the create flow maps each line's `meta_data.weight_identifier` to its new trade-product id before saving weights.
cases.setup: Create an RFQ with `weightages` (line mode) whose inner keys are the lines' weight identifiers. Manual (create flow).
cases.steps: `POST /trade/template_input` with weights; read the new round.
cases.expected: Round created weighted from the start; values per new line id.
cases.oracle: `weightages.values` keyed by the new trade-product ids.

cases.section: Owner, open tender and a second auction
cases.title: The owner of every round is the owner of the event, not the colleague who added it
cases.why: Cancel, close and "my events" checks compare against the round owner; if a colleague who added a round kept owner rights after a hand-over, the new owner could not act.
cases.setup: Buyer A owns an event; colleague B (same company, no admin rights) adds a price round. Then A hands the event to buyer C.
cases.steps: 1. As B, try to cancel the round. 2. As C (new owner), open, close and cancel the round.
cases.expected: B is treated as not the owner (refused unless another permission allows it). C acts as the owner of every round immediately after the hand-over, with no change to the rounds themselves.
cases.oracle: `TradeRequest#user`/`#user_id` return the event's owner (`trade_request.rb:3017-3023`); `allowed_to_cancel?`, `is_created_by_user?` compare `user_id` (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:148-150, 444`). Refusal: HTTP 422 code 101 "You are not allowed to perform this action".

cases.section: Owner, open tender and a second auction
cases.title: A price round can be moved to auction only once
cases.why: Two live auctions made from the same RFQ split the vendors and give two "winning" prices.
cases.setup: Closed price round with bids; it has already been moved to an auction that is live (not draft, cancelled or withdrawn).
cases.steps: Move the same price round to auction again.
cases.expected: Refused with "An auction has already been made for this event."; no second auction round exists. After the first auction is withdrawn or cancelled, a new move is allowed.
cases.oracle: `validate_unique_auction_for_parent` (`trade_request.rb:3100-3105`) adds a base error on create of a rfq_then_auction round whose parent already has one outside draft/cancelled/withdrawn; the HTTP status/code with which move_to_auction reports a base error is (unverified).

cases.section: Bidding window, extensions and evaluation windows
cases.title: The stored end of a round always equals the end of its live schedule
cases.why: Lists, filters and reminders use the stored end; if it lagged behind an extension, the round would show as expired while vendors can still bid.
cases.setup: Live price round ending at T.
cases.steps: 1. Extend the round to T + 2 h. 2. Read the round and find it in the events list filtered by end time.
cases.expected: The round's end time is T + 2 h everywhere (stage read, list, filter). For a price round the end is the last price-round schedule; for a technical round the last bidding schedule; for an auction the latest of the auction, auto-extension and sealed-bid-extension schedules. A cancelled (void) schedule never counts.
cases.oracle: `before_save :set_bid_end_time` (`trade_request.rb:277, 3096-3098`); `bid_end_time` per mode (`:828-838`), `bid_start_time` (`:723-733`); `trade_schedules` excludes status 5 (`:111`).

cases.section: Bidding window, extensions and evaluation windows
cases.title: An auction's end includes automatic extensions; an RFQ's end does not
cases.why: If the auction's end ignored the extension, the round would close (and rank) while the last vendor is still inside the extra minutes.
cases.setup: Live reverse auction with auto-extension: last 2 minutes, extend by 2 minutes. A QA vendor.
cases.steps: 1. Bid 60 seconds before the end. 2. Read the round's end time and the extension count.
cases.expected: The end moves to the original end + 2 minutes, the extension count goes from 0 to 1, and bids are accepted until the new end. On a price round (RFQ) no such schedule is added to the end.
cases.oracle: `bid_end_time` for auctioning = max end of `auction`, `dynamic_extra_time`, `sealbid_extension_time` (`trade_request.rb:830-832`); `misc.dynamic_time_extension_count` (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:1003-1014`).

cases.section: Bidding window, extensions and evaluation windows
cases.title: Draft bids that were never sent are discarded when bidding ends
cases.why: A half-filled draft must not appear in the comparison, and the vendor must see that it was not sent.
cases.setup: Live price round; a QA vendor saves a draft bid without submitting.
cases.steps: 1. Let the round end (or end it). 2. As the buyer read the bid list; as the vendor read its bid.
cases.expected: After the end the draft is inactive and never listed for the buyer; the round status turns closed at its closing time and the event's status refreshes within seconds.
cases.oracle: `DeleteDraftBidsWorker` at `bid_end_time` marks `bids.draft` → in_active only when `bid_end_time <= now` (`delete_draft_bids_worker.rb:7-21`); scheduled on closed_at change unless status changed to active (`trade_request.rb:304, 3199-3203`); `MarkEventClosedWorker` at closed_at (`:358-361`). Whether the job is queued when the end is set at publish in the same save as the activation is (unverified).

cases.section: Bidding window, extensions and evaluation windows
cases.title: Extending a technical round moves its evaluation window and keeps its length
cases.why: Evaluators planned a fixed evaluation period; an extension must not shorten it or start it before bidding ends.
cases.setup: Technical round (RFP) bidding ends T, evaluation window T → T + 2 days.
cases.steps: 1. Extend bidding to T + 1 day. 2. Read the round's end and evaluation end.
cases.expected: Bidding ends T + 1 day; the evaluation window starts at T + 1 day and ends at T + 3 days (same 2-day length). Every active, pending or requested response gets the new closing time. The stored evaluation duration equals evaluation end − bidding end (2 days).
cases.oracle: `shift_schedule_after_self_schedule` keeps duration (`trade_schedule.rb:154-170`); stage `extra_closing_time` (`trade_request.rb:934-942`, serializer `:534-542`); `config.evaluation_duration` (`trade_request.rb:1388-1391`).

cases.section: Bidding window, extensions and evaluation windows
cases.title: With a cost-breakdown review window, an extension shifts the review window first and the evaluation after it
cases.why: Vendors need their full cost-breakdown time after the real end of bidding, and evaluation must start after that.
cases.setup: Price round ending T, cost-breakdown review window T → T + 1 h, evaluation window T + 1 h → T + 1 day.
cases.steps: 1. Extend bidding by 30 minutes (or trigger an auto-extension on an auction). 2. Read the three windows.
cases.expected: Bidding T + 30 min; review T + 30 min → T + 1 h 30 min; evaluation T + 1 h 30 min → T + 1 day 30 min. Counter-offer task due dates follow the moved window.
cases.oracle: `check_for_auction_extra_closing_time` (`trade_schedule.rb:216-222`); auto-extension path `increase_extra_closing_time_on_extension` (`:190-204`).

cases.section: Bidding window, extensions and evaluation windows
cases.title: With a best-offer review window, an extension should not make evaluation overlap the review
cases.why: Today a manual extension shifts only the evaluation window, so it starts at the new bidding end while vendors are still sending best offers.
cases.setup: Price round ending T, best-offer review window T → T + 1 h, evaluation window T + 1 h → T + 1 day.
cases.steps: 1. Extend bidding by 30 minutes (manual edit, not an auto-extension). 2. Read the windows.
cases.expected: Only a cost-breakdown review window is shifted on this path; the evaluation window is moved to start at T + 30 min, overlapping the unchanged best-offer window.
cases.oracle: `trade_schedule.rb:219` shifts the review window only when `is_cost_breakdown_time`; else `:224-225` shifts the evaluation window straight after the bidding schedule. Compare the auto-extension path `:196-199`, which handles both.

cases.section: Bidding window, extensions and evaluation windows
cases.title: Best-offer review times are shown only to the buyer and the vendors asked for a best offer, and only during the window
cases.why: A vendor that was not asked must not learn that others got extra time; a cost-breakdown request, by contrast, is public to all participants.
cases.setup: Closed price round, two QA vendors; best-offer review window for vendor A only. Second round with a cost-breakdown window.
cases.steps: 1. During the window, read the round as the buyer, as A and as B. 2. Repeat after the window. 3. Read the cost-breakdown round as B before, during and after its window.
cases.expected: Best offer: during the window the buyer and A see the review end time and type, B sees neither; after the window nobody gets them. While the window is open, "price increase allowed" reads false for everyone. Cost breakdown: start, end and type are returned to everyone at any time.
cases.oracle: Stage read `response_review_end_time_for_participant`, `response_review_time_for` (`trade_template_serializer.rb:529-532, 973-975`); readers `trade_request.rb:778-825`; window = last schedule of that type, inclusive bounds (`:808-810, 1185-1189`); allowed vendors = flattened `config.allowed_participants_to_edit_in_bid_review_time` (`:1206-1209`); `is_price_increase_allowed` forced false (`trade_template_serializer.rb:148`).

cases.section: Send to evaluation and evaluation status
cases.title: "Send to evaluation" is offered only after bidding ended and before any evaluation window exists
cases.why: Sending too early cuts bidding short; sending twice creates two evaluation windows.
cases.setup: Technical round with manual send-to-evaluation (`gate: send_rfp_to_evaluation_manually`); a buyer with purchase mode and one without (e.g. view-only mode).
cases.steps: 1. Read the round's configuration while bidding is open, after it ends, after sending to evaluation, and after withdrawing a second such round. 2. As the user without purchase mode, try to extend evaluation time before sending.
cases.expected: The button flag is false while bidding is open, true after the end, false again once an evaluation window exists and false for a withdrawn round. The user without purchase or customer-success mode may not extend evaluation time until the round has been sent; everyone else may.
cases.oracle: `show_send_to_evaluation_button` (`trade_request.rb:1382-1386`) = enabled for user ∧ expired ∧ not in_active ∧ no extra_closing_time (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:1184-1189`); `allowed_to_extend_evaluation_time?` (`:1176-1182`).

cases.section: Send to evaluation and evaluation status
cases.title: The event card shows evaluation as pending, overdue or completed at the right moments
cases.why: Evaluators work from the "overdue" flag; a technical round marked done before every response is scored hides pending work.
cases.setup: Event with a technical round (lot-level scoring, two responses) and a technical round with line-level scoring; an RFI.
cases.steps: Read the event card while bidding runs, after it ends, after scoring one of two responses, after scoring both, after the evaluation end passes with one unscored, and for line-level after asking for re-evaluation of one line.
cases.expected: While upcoming or running: no evaluation status. After the end: pending, then overdue once the closing time passes. Lot-level: completed only when every active response has a score. Line-level: completed only when every active line has a score and none is "re-evaluation requested". RFI: completed as soon as any active evaluation exists. A closed round or one moved to auction: completed.
cases.oracle: Card `evaluation_status` from `evaluation_status_hash` (`trade_request.rb:396-419`, `buyer_card_serializer.rb:9, 63-64, 300`); `is_evaluated?` (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:1281-1330`).

cases.title: A Procol employee sees a client's round only as that client's CSM inside that client's workspace
cases.why: Support staff must not browse any client's prices; and a support call without a workspace must be refused, not crash.
cases.setup: Procol employee E who is CSM for client X only.
cases.steps: 1. As E in workspace X, open X's round. 2. As E in workspace Y, open X's round. 3. As E with no workspace selected, open X's round.
cases.expected: Allowed in X; refused in Y; refused (not a server error) with no workspace.
cases.oracle: `trade_request_model_helper.rb:402-410`; `Current.workspace.id` without a guard (`:404`) — step 3 outcome (unverified: whether the API always sets a workspace for an employee).

cases.title: Saving a round whose product has no category should not crash
cases.why: The round's category/location identifiers are rebuilt on every save; a product without a category makes that rebuild fail and the whole save returns a server error.
cases.setup: A product with no category (if the client allows creating one), used on a price round at a delivery location.
cases.steps: Save (or publish) the round.
cases.expected: Untyped HTTP 500 (`all_category_ids.each` on nil). Unverified whether this client lets a product exist without a category.
cases.oracle: `generate_identifier_hash` returns early only when both category ids and location are nil (`trade_request.rb:1582-1592`), called from after-save `update_team_identifier` (`:1576-1580`).

cases.title: A vendor cannot read a round's activity log
cases.why: The activity log lists every buyer action (extensions, invitations, who opened bids); it is buyer-only.
cases.setup: Live sandbox round; the invited QA vendor.
cases.steps: As the buyer read the round's activity log; as the vendor do the same.
cases.expected: Buyer: returned. Vendor: refused (never a server error).
cases.oracle: `trade_request.rb:2545-2553` (read permission + view access; CSM or buyer-company user). The vendor half is (unverified): which app may call the activity-log route.

cases.title: In a masked live round, the buyer gets only placed-bid counts when "bidding stats in masked events" is on
cases.why: The setting exists so a buyer can watch participation without seeing who bid what while the round is live.
cases.setup: Masked live round with `gate: show_bidding_stats_in_masked_events`; a second live round with `show_placed_bids_stats` set false; a super admin.
cases.steps: Read the participation statistics as the buyer, as the super admin, and after the end.
cases.expected: Round 1 while live: stats-only for buyer-company users. Round 2: the stored value (false) for normal buyers, ignored for a super admin. After the end: full data.
cases.oracle: `should_show_placed_bids_stats_only?` (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:297-305`), used at `trade_controller.rb:1099, 1462`. The digest omits the buyer-company condition in the second branch (`:301`).

cases.section: Quantities, line counts, attachments and price limits
cases.title: A vendor sees the requested quantity unless it is a Dutch auction closing on several vendors
cases.why: In a multi-vendor Dutch auction the quantity is hidden by design; elsewhere a vendor cannot quote without it.
cases.setup: Price round with no quantity-display setting; Dutch auction closing on multiple vendors with no setting; one with the setting explicitly true. Remaining quantity setting on and off.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor read each round.
cases.expected: Price round: quantity shown. Multi-vendor Dutch, no setting: hidden. Setting true: shown. Remaining quantity is shown only when that setting is exactly on.
cases.oracle: `show_quantity_requested?` (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:164-169`), `show_remaining_quantity_to_sellers?` (`:171-173`).

cases.section: Quantities, line counts, attachments and price limits
cases.title: A line needs a delivery location and a unit; missing either is a clear refusal
cases.why: A line without location or unit cannot be quoted; the buyer must be told which field is missing, not get a server error.
cases.setup: Draft event.
cases.steps: Add a line with no delivery location; then one with no unit.
cases.expected: Refused with a message naming the missing field ("must exist"); nothing saved. Never HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: `belongs_to :buyer_hub`, `:unit` required (`trade_product.rb:60-66`). How the event-flow controller reports the model error (status/code) is (unverified) — an untyped 500 here is a defect.

cases.section: Quantities, line counts, attachments and price limits
cases.title: The price ceiling is checked on the price unless the round names another column
cases.why: A ceiling checked on the wrong number (price vs landed) lets an over-budget bid through.
cases.setup: Price round with ceiling 500 and GST and freight widgets; second round whose validation settings name a net-price column.
cases.steps: A vendor bids price 480 with GST 18 % and freight 30 on each.
cases.expected: Round 1: accepted (480 ≤ 500). Round 2: checked on 480 + 86.4 + 30 = 596.4 → refused.
cases.oracle: `validation_widgets_configuration[key].target_column`, default "price"; net-price fallback formula (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:608-638`).

cases.title: Vendors are ranked on line price and on the lot gross total unless the round says otherwise
cases.why: Rank decides L1; a buyer-specific ranking setting must win over the generic one.
cases.setup: Round A: no ranking setting. Round B: generic ranking widget "landed cost" (a lot widget) only. Round C: buyer line widget set and generic ranking widget set.
cases.steps: Read each round's ranking widgets.
cases.expected: A: line "price", lot "gross_total". B: lot ranks on landed cost, line falls back to "price". C: the buyer setting is used. Rounds created on or before 8 May 2024 rank on "price" for both.
cases.oracle: Stage `ranking_widgets`; `get_ranking_widgets_line_and_lot` (`trade_request.rb:2587-2616`); legacy `ranking_widget_line` in settings (`:1891-1895`, serializer `:128`).

cases.title: Knockout and Dutch auctions refuse multi-product rounds without fast bidding
cases.why: These strategies work on one price per vendor; publishing a multi-line one without fast bidding would run an auction that cannot rank.
cases.setup: Company with projects; knockout auction with 2 lines, fast bidding off; second with fast bidding on; Dutch auction made as a plain price round type.
cases.steps: Publish each.
cases.expected: Round 1 and the wrong-mode round: refused "You are not allowed to perform this action". Round 2: published.
cases.oracle: HTTP 422 code 101 (`trade_controller_helper.rb:4552-4556`, `FAST_FILLING_VALID_RFX_MODES`).

cases.title: Fast-bidding bulk price: a formula missing an input is a clear refusal, not a crash
cases.why: The bulk price drives the knockout; a vendor who leaves one formula input empty should be told so.
cases.setup: Knockout auction with fast bidding and a template bulk-price formula `qty * rate`.
cases.steps: 1. Vendor submits rate and qty → bulk price computed. 2. Vendor submits only rate. 3. A round with no strategy settings stored is read.
cases.expected: 2: "Missing required formula variables: qty" is raised as an ArgumentError → untyped 500; 3: `.with_indifferent_access` on nil → 500.
cases.oracle: `trade_request.rb:739-763` (Dentaku, strings → float, raise at `:751-755`); readers `:1635-1669`.

cases.section: Counter offers and bid tags in reports
cases.title: Award and comparison reports pick each vendor's initial, negotiated and best-offer bids correctly
cases.why: "Initial vs final" and negotiation savings come from these tags; a wrong tag credits savings to the wrong step.
cases.setup: Price round, QA vendor: bid 1 (normal); buyer counter offer accepted; bid 2; buyer adds a surrogate bid; best-offer revision bid 3; a rejected bid 4.
cases.steps: Download the award proposal report and the Master QCS for the vendor.
cases.expected: Last sentence: a vendor with no normal bid left makes the comparison `>= nil` raise (unverified reachability: needs the normal bid rejected or revoked before a best-offer revision).
cases.oracle: `trade_request.rb:2731-2830` (tags; latest counter offer by created_at, id desc; rejected/revoked removed `:2769`; `:2787, 2791` compare with `final_normal_bid_id`); used by `awarding_proposal_report_data_model.rb:772`, `mqcs_diff_checker_service.rb:231`.

cases.title: A round without a currency setup shows the rupee symbol; a multi-currency round shows each vendor its own currency
cases.why: A vendor quoting in the wrong currency is a 80× error on USD.
cases.setup: Round 1 with no currency configuration. Round 2 multi-currency (base INR, allowed USD with precision 2, no label set); vendor A prefers USD, vendor B has no preference.
cases.steps: Read both rounds as the buyer and as each vendor.
cases.expected: Round 1: symbol from the round's default currency symbol, ₹ when unset. Round 2: currency mode "multiple currencies"; A sees USD with precision 2 and the label falling back to the symbol; B gets no preferred currency (base). A round whose currency setup lacks a base currency should be refused when saved, not break every later read (today: NoMethodError, unverified how it can be saved).
cases.oracle: Stage `currency_configuration`, `currency_preferences`, `default_currency_symbol`, `default_currency_label_type`; `currency_configuration.rb:9-94`; `trade_request.rb:1535-1537, 2638-2644`.

cases.title: Realised and unrealised custom savings use different reference amounts
cases.why: Realised savings are on the awarded quantity, unrealised on the full quantity; today the second overwrite makes both the same number, so one of them is always wrong.
cases.setup: `gate: show_custom_savings`. Price round, one line of 100 units; vendor A 10/unit, vendor B 9/unit; award 40 units to B.
cases.steps: Close the round; read the custom savings references (realised, unrealised).
cases.expected: Both references hold the same value — the value of whichever option was computed last.
cases.oracle: Stage `misc.custom_savings_configuration` / line meta `custom_savings_configuration`; `update_reference_price` overwrites every reference (`savings_configuration.rb:210-216`, the `reference_price unless …` line is a no-op); options `:73-76`, references `:341-356`.

cases.title: A forward auction's best possible amount should use the highest offers
cases.why: In a sale the buyer wants the highest price; filling the quantity from the lowest offers understates the achievable amount and the savings.
cases.setup: Forward (sell) round, one line of 100 units; offers: A 50 units at 10, B 100 units at 12.
cases.steps: Close; read the line's best possible amount in savings.
cases.expected: The result of `btps.reverse` is thrown away, so the walk takes A first: 50 × 10 + 50 × 12 = 1,100 (assuming the lines arrive in ascending price, as the code comment says).
cases.oracle: `get_possible_best_bid_amount` (`trade_product.rb:695-711`), used by `savings_configuration.rb:173, 184` and `event_indicators/lot_based.rb:107`. Selected amount = Σ price × quantity of selected lines (`:713-719`).

cases.title: An apostrophe in a line description should not stop savings from being saved
cases.why: Line meta data (which holds the buyer's product description) is written with hand-built SQL; "Men's gloves" ends the string early and the save fails, so custom savings or a PR amendment silently never lands.
cases.setup: `gate: show_custom_savings`. Price round whose line description is "Men's safety gloves"; a QA vendor bid.
cases.steps: Close the round; after 10 s read the line's custom savings.
cases.expected: The background job fails with a database syntax error and the line has no custom savings (the round-level part, written first, is present). Not reproduced live.
cases.oracle: Line `meta_data.custom_savings_configuration` missing while stage `misc.custom_savings_configuration` exists; `TradeProduct.update_meta_data` interpolates `'#{meta_data_hash.to_json}'` (`trade_product.rb:305-319`), called by `custom_savings_calculator_worker.rb:31`, `purchase_requests/amendment_service.rb:790, 852`, `lpo/refresh_data_service.rb:193`. Line meta data holds `product_description` (Procol DB SELECT on 198678).

cases.title: Invitation, go-live and reminder mails reach exactly the round's audience at the right times
cases.why: Vendors bid only if they are told; an invited-but-unregistered vendor that never gets the mail is lost competition, and a mail about a draft leaks a plan.
cases.setup: Needs vendor mailboxes the tester can read (not example.com). Round with `gate: send_web_bidding_mail`, `send_event_live_email_to_vendor` and `send_event_expiry_reminder_to_vendor` (reminder at 80 %), starting 1 h after creation, lasting 10 h. Audience "everyone" with one registered mapped vendor and one invited (not yet registered) vendor; a second round restricted to one vendor; a draft event; a technical round.
cases.steps: Publish; collect the mails each vendor receives and their times.
cases.expected: For "everyone" / "everyone except" audiences, invited vendors are filtered as if their invitation ids were company ids, so the invited vendor is likely missed (unverified live).
cases.oracle: Mailbox contents and timestamps. `send_web_bidding_mail` (`trade_request.rb:2332-2371`); recipients `:1413-1437, 1476-1480`; times `:843-864`, `company.rb:1075-1090`; creation notifications `:1935-1975`; WhatsApp `:2312-2320`; managers' alert `:2236`; approval-completion pushes `:1943-1951`; RFI/RFP evaluation reminder end − 1 day or end − duration/4 (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:982-988`).

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: A reversed window on a started round is refused by the "already started" rule first
cases.why: Shows the guard order: whatever the times are, a started round answers 258 — the reschedule path has no end-after-start check of its own (API-EVDTME-018).
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ, bidding started at publish, no bids.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{"bid_start_time": {{now+7200}}, "bid_end_time": {{now+3600}}}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!'.

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: Times sent as words on a started round are refused without a crash
cases.why: On an upcoming round the same words crash in the time conversion (API-EVDTME-023); on a started round the 258 guard must come first.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ, bidding started at publish, no bids.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}` with `{"bid_start_time": "QA_Platform_later_{{stamp}}", "bid_end_time": "QA_Platform_later_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: Refused cleanly, never a server error. HTTP 422, code 258 'You cannot re-schedule this event!'.

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: Rescheduling a round that does not exist
cases.why: Bogus ids must fail closed before any policy or schedule logic.
cases.setup: Signed-in QA buyer; no event needed.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==` with `{"bid_start_time": {{now+3600}}, "bid_end_time": {{now+7200}}}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found' (the id decodes to 999999999).

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: Rescheduling with a garbled round id
cases.why: A garbled id decodes to nothing; the lookup must not crash.
cases.setup: Signed-in QA buyer; no event needed.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/WrongUuid1=` with `{"bid_start_time": {{now+3600}}, "bid_end_time": {{now+7200}}}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.section: A round that has already started cannot be rescheduled
cases.title: A reschedule body that also carries configurations skips the started rule
cases.why: The reschedule branch is chosen only when `configurations` is blank; adding any configurations turns the request into a full settings edit that rebuilds the round's config, re-runs the RFP/RFQ time rule and can move the extra closing (evaluation) window of a live round.
cases.setup: A live RFQ with an extra closing time and no bids. Manual: the settings edit rewrites the round's config from the company defaults and cannot be bounded on a run's event.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/<round>` with `{"bid_start_time": <now+3600>, "bid_end_time": <now+7200>, "extra_closing_time": <now+9000>, "configurations": {"template_id": <the round's template id>}}`; read the round back.
cases.expected: No 258. The bidding window keeps its start/end (`edit_trade_schedules(…, true)` only re-types it) but the extra closing schedule is moved to the sent times and closed_at follows. Should be refused like any other reschedule of a started round.
cases.oracle: `extra_closing_time` in the read-back equals the sent value; `starting_from` unchanged.

cases.section: Rescheduling an upcoming round (manual — every recipe starts bidding at publish)
cases.title: A bad delivery schedule in a reschedule cancels the whole reschedule
cases.why: Unlike the live-edit path (API-XDAMD-047/052), the reschedule path scopes the delivery schedule to the round and refuses an unknown one; because the refusal leaves the transaction early, Rails 7.0 rolls the new times back too.
cases.setup: An upcoming RFQ as API-EVDTME-016.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/<round>` with `{"bid_start_time": <now+4h>, "bid_end_time": <now+5h>, "delivery_schedules": [{"uuid": "Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==", "delivery_by": <now+30d>}]}`. 2. Read the round back. 3. Repeat with a real delivery schedule and `"delivery_by": null`.
cases.expected: 1. HTTP 422, code 15 'Operation failed'; 2. the times are unchanged (rolled back); no reschedule notification. 3. Should be 422; today `Time.at(nil)` raises → HTTP 500.
cases.oracle: Read-back times = the old ones after step 1; status < 500 in step 3.

cases.section: Rescheduling an upcoming round (manual — every recipe starts bidding at publish)
cases.title: Rescheduling a knockout or Dutch auction rebuilds its rounds
cases.why: Knockout/Dutch auctions run in rounds; the old rounds must be voided and new ones built from the new start, or the auction runs on the old clock.
cases.setup: An upcoming knockout auction (QA vendors only).
cases.steps: Reschedule it; read its trade rounds back.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; previous active rounds are void, a new set starts at the new start with the same price/time difference; for Dutch with rfx projects, the round scheduler job is enqueued for the first round's end.
cases.oracle: trade_rounds rows: old status void, new version = previous max + 1.

cases.section: Rescheduling an upcoming round (manual — every recipe starts bidding at publish)
cases.title: Rescheduling an RFQ or a technical round tells vendors by push only
cases.why: The new reschedule emails are for auctions only (and RFI has its own mails); a vendor invited to an RFQ or RFP whose start moved gets no email.
cases.setup: An upcoming RFQ and an upcoming RFP round, QA vendor 1 invited to each.
cases.steps: Reschedule each; check QA vendor 1's mailbox and push/notification menu.
cases.expected: A push ("auction notification" when the audience is everyone, plus the 15-minutes-before push) and the manager push when `auction_create_notification_to_admins` is on; no email. Product to confirm whether RFQ/RFP vendors should be emailed.
cases.oracle: No email to QA vendor 1; notification-menu entry present.

cases.section: Auction reschedule and extension emails (commit c74ea64581, manual)
cases.title: Moving an auction earlier can lose the 80% expiry reminder
cases.why: A reschedule re-plans the start reminders but not the expiry reminders; the old 80% job only re-times itself forward, so if the new 80% point is before the old job, the reminder comes late — or not at all once the round has ended.
cases.setup: An upcoming auction (start S, 1 h long) with `send_event_expiry_reminder_to_vendor` true; QA vendors only.
cases.steps: Reschedule to start S − 3 h (same length); watch for the "expiry reminder" mail.
cases.expected: The reminder that was due at S+48 min fires after the new round has ended and is dropped (`bid_end_time < now`); vendors get no expiry reminder. Should be re-planned to new start + 80%.
cases.oracle: No `event_expiry_reminder_to_vendor` mail during the new window.

cases.section: Auction reschedule and extension emails (commit c74ea64581, manual)
cases.title: Which extensions do NOT send the new email
cases.why: The mail is gated on auction mode; testers must not expect it elsewhere, and the gaps should be a product decision.
cases.setup: Live rounds of each kind, QA vendors only: RFQ, knockout auction, Dutch auction, BOQ auction, staggered line-item auction.
cases.steps: Extend each by its normal path (staggered: the screen's per-line extension, API-EVDTME-045; also reopen lines, API-EVDTME-048); check mailboxes.
cases.expected: No "Submission time extended" mail for RFQ (not `is_auction?`), knockout/Dutch (excluded), BOQ (gets the older bidding-time-extension mail instead) and staggered per-line changes (no extension flag is set). Only `auction` / `rfq_then_auction` rounds get it.
cases.oracle: Mail present only for auction / rfq_then_auction.

cases.section: Auction reschedule and extension emails (commit c74ea64581, manual)
cases.title: An extension can start buyer expiry reminders an event never had
cases.why: At publish, buyer expiry reminders are planned only for single-round (dummy event group) events; the new extension code plans one for any auction unless `send_event_expiry_reminder_to_buyer` = "disable_for_buyer", so buyers of normal events start receiving a reminder only after a late extension.
cases.setup: A live auction inside a normal (non-dummy) event group; `send_event_expiry_reminder_to_buyer` absent; QA buyer is the only buyer-side user.
cases.steps: Past the 80% point, extend the auction by 60 min; check the buyer's mailbox. Repeat with `send_event_expiry_reminder_to_buyer` = "disable_for_buyer".
cases.expected: First run: the buyer gets an expiry reminder at the new 80% point (none existed before). Second run: none. Product to confirm whether the first is intended.
cases.oracle: `event_expiry_reminder_to_buyer` job present only in the first run.

cases.section: Auction reschedule and extension emails (commit c74ea64581, manual)
cases.title: A refused or rolled-back reschedule sends nothing
cases.why: The reschedule notifications moved from `after_save` to `after_save_commit` in #16149; a reschedule that fails after the save (bad delivery schedule, API-EVDTME-024) must not tell vendors their auction moved.
cases.setup: An upcoming auction, QA vendors only.
cases.steps: 1. Reschedule with an unknown delivery schedule id (code 15). 2. Try to reschedule after it has started (code 258).
cases.expected: No reschedule mail or push in either case; times unchanged.
cases.oracle: QA vendor mailboxes and notification menus empty for the round.

cases.title: Per-line times on a draft round are refused
cases.why: staggered_time has no permission check of its own; the lookup (active rounds only) and the staggered check are all that stand between a caller and the schedule.
cases.setup: A fresh draft event with an unpublished RFQ round.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{tradeId}}/staggered_time` with `{"trade_products_time": {"999999999": {"start_time": {{now+60}}, "end_time": {{now+600}}}}}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found' — a draft is not in the active lookup.

cases.title: Per-line times on a closed round are refused
cases.why: Re-timing lines after close would reopen bidding through the back door.
cases.setup: A fresh RFQ whose window and extra closing time are over; no bids.
cases.steps: As API-EVDTME-041 on this round.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found' (not active, or not staggered — both answer 4).

cases.title: Per-line times on a technical round are refused
cases.why: A technical round never has per-line closing.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFP+RFQ event.
cases.steps: As API-EVDTME-041 on `/trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/staggered_time`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.title: Per-line times on an awarded round are refused
cases.why: Nothing about an awarded round's clock may change.
cases.setup: A fresh RFQ with QA vendor 1's bid, closed, award proposal submitted.
cases.steps: As API-EVDTME-041 on this round.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.title: Per-line times sent as a list or as text crash the request
cases.why: The code iterates `trade_products_time` as a key→times map; a list element arrives as the "key" with nil times and text has no `each` — both unrescued.
cases.setup: A live staggered auction; buyer console.
cases.steps: 1. `PATCH /trade/<round>/staggered_time` with `{"trade_products_time": [{"start_time": <now>, "end_time": <now+600>}]}`. 2. Same with `{"trade_products_time": "QA_Platform_text"}`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 (code 2 or 507 'Invalid Time Input'). Today HTTP 500 (NoMethodError on nil / on String).
cases.oracle: Status < 500.

cases.title: Reopening a line that has not ended yet is refused with a misleading message
cases.why: The check is right, the message ('Operation failed') is not.
cases.setup: A live staggered auction where line 3 is still running.
cases.steps: Reopen line 3 for 10 min.
cases.expected: Refused: HTTP 422, code 15 'Operation failed'. Should say the line is still open.
cases.oracle: 422 + 15; line 3 times unchanged.

cases.title: Reopening with no lines, or a zero, negative or word extension, is refused on a staggered round
cases.why: The parameter checks behind the round check; on a staggered round they are what answers.
cases.setup: A live staggered auction with one expired line.
cases.steps: Send `{"reopen_time_extension": 600}`; then `{"trade_product_uuids": ["<line>"], "reopen_time_extension": 0}`; `-600`; `"ten"`.
cases.expected: Each: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (a word converts to 0).
cases.oracle: 422 + 2 four times; times unchanged.

cases.title: Any buyer of the company with create rights can reopen lines of someone else's auction
cases.why: reopen_line_items checks only "may create events" and "same company", not ownership or team (reschedule and extension use the full `update?` policy).
cases.setup: Buyer B of the same company, with create permission, not on the owner's team, not super admin; a live staggered auction owned by A with an expired line.
cases.steps: As B, reopen the expired line.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. Product to confirm; the reschedule/extension equivalent applies `update?`.
cases.oracle: Line reopened by B (paper trail whodunnit = B).

cases.title: Reopened lines are not announced to vendors
cases.why: Vendors who saw a line close have no reason to come back unless told; the reopen sets none of the extension notification flags.
cases.setup: As API-EVDTME-048, QA vendors 1 and 2.
cases.steps: Reopen two lines; check vendor push/notification menu and mailboxes.
cases.expected: No push or email about the reopen (the round's live view updates only when the vendor reloads). Product to confirm.
cases.oracle: No new notification for QA vendors.

cases.title: Reopening a line on a round that is not staggered
cases.why: Reopening exists only for staggered line-item auctions; on anything else the call must change nothing.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ (not staggered), QA vendor 1 invited, no bids. The buyer has create permission.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/{{tradeId}}/reopen_line_items` with `{"trade_product_uuids": ["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="], "reopen_time_extension": 600}`.
cases.expected: Refused. HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.title: Reopen without naming any line: the round check answers first
cases.why: Pins the guard order (permission → own active round → staggered → parameters); on a staggered round this body answers 2 (API-EVDTME-051).
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ (not staggered).
cases.steps: `POST /trade/{{tradeId}}/reopen_line_items` with `{"reopen_time_extension": 600}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.title: Reopen for zero seconds: the round check answers first
cases.why: Boundary of the extension check, behind the round check.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ (not staggered).
cases.steps: `POST /trade/{{tradeId}}/reopen_line_items` with `{"trade_product_uuids": ["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="], "reopen_time_extension": 0}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.title: Reopen with the extension written as a word: the round check answers first
cases.why: Hostile input must be refused cleanly, never reach the time arithmetic on a non-staggered round.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ (not staggered).
cases.steps: `POST /trade/{{tradeId}}/reopen_line_items` with `{"trade_product_uuids": ["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="], "reopen_time_extension": "QA_Platform_ten_minutes_{{stamp}}"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.title: Reopen on a round that does not exist
cases.why: Bogus ids fail closed.
cases.setup: Signed-in QA buyer; no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/reopen_line_items` with `{"trade_product_uuids": ["Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw=="], "reopen_time_extension": 600}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.title: Reopen with a garbled round id
cases.why: A garbled id decodes to nothing; the scoped lookup must not crash.
cases.setup: Signed-in QA buyer; no event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/WrongUuid1=/reopen_line_items` with the body of API-EVDTME-061.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.title: Reopen on a draft round
cases.why: Only active rounds of the buyer's own company are looked up.
cases.setup: A fresh draft event with an unpublished RFQ round.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/{{tradeId}}/reopen_line_items` with the body of API-EVDTME-061.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.title: Reopen on a fully closed round
cases.why: After the evaluation window the round is closed; reopening lines then must be impossible.
cases.setup: A fresh RFQ whose window and extra closing time are over; no bids.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/{{tradeId}}/reopen_line_items` with the body of API-EVDTME-061.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found' (not active, or not staggered).

cases.title: Reopen on a technical round
cases.why: A technical round has no lines to reopen.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFP+RFQ event.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/{{rfpTradeId}}/reopen_line_items` with the body of API-EVDTME-061.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 4 'Request not found'.

cases.section: The request shape and finding the round
cases.title: A blank "weight on" is refused
cases.why: Lot versus line decides where every weight row is stored; an empty value must not default silently.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Same as the happy path (API-EVDWGT-013) with `"weightage_on": ""`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2; no weight rows, round unweighted.

cases.section: The request shape and finding the round
cases.title: A round that does not exist answers "insufficient parameters", not "not found"
cases.why: The lookup uses `find_by_id`, so an unknown round falls into the parameter check. The screen shows "Insufficient parameters" for a deleted or mistyped round, which sends the buyer looking at the wrong thing.
cases.setup: Signed-in buyer only (recipe `none`).
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/edit_weight_parameters` with a valid lot weight body.
cases.expected: Refused before any policy check. HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (a 404 or code 4 'Request not found' would be clearer).
cases.oracle: 422 code 2, never 500.

cases.section: The request shape and finding the round
cases.title: A garbled round id is refused the same way
cases.why: `WrongUuid1=` decodes to nothing; `find_by_id(nil)` must stay a clean refusal.
cases.setup: Recipe `none`.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/WrongUuid1=/edit_weight_parameters` with a valid lot weight body.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: The request shape and finding the round
cases.title: A round waiting for creation approval cannot be weighted
cases.why: A round in "requested" status is not `active`; the buyer sees the weight button on the order page but every save answers "Insufficient parameters".
cases.setup: A company with create-trade approval (v1 or v2) so the published round sits in status requested. Needs an approval-flow company; manual.
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/:id/edit_weight_parameters` with a valid body.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. Product decision: either allow weights before approval or say why.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2; round status still requested.

cases.section: The request shape and finding the round
cases.title: The parameter check runs before authorization, so outsiders can probe which rounds exist
cases.why: For another company's live round a valid body answers 455, an empty body answers 2, and a non-existent or non-live id answers 2 — the difference tells an outsider that the id is a live round.
cases.setup: Buyer of company B (e.g. Demo Account 2) and the id of a live round of company A (the run's own round). Two companies' logins; manual.
cases.steps: As B: 1. valid body on A's round; 2. valid body on `Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==`.
cases.expected: Today: step 1 HTTP 422 code 455 'You are not authorized to perform this action', step 2 HTTP 422 code 2. Better: authorize (or answer one code) before revealing existence.
cases.oracle: Different codes for "exists" and "does not exist".

cases.section: First save, re-edits and what the round shows afterwards
cases.title: Weights cannot be cleared back to an unweighted round
cases.why: Sending an empty table is the natural "remove all weights"; it is refused, and no other action clears `misc.weightage`. Once weighted, a round stays weighted.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`; arrange: the happy-path save.
cases.steps: `PATCH …/edit_weight_parameters` with `{"weightages": {"weightage_on": "lot", "values": {}}}`; read the round.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'; the round is still weighted with qa_freight_adj. (Product gap: no way to remove all weights.)
cases.oracle: 422 code 2; `trade_config.is_weighted_bid_event` true; `weightages.key_attributes` contains "qa_freight_adj".

cases.section: First save, re-edits and what the round shows afterwards
cases.title: A vendor's unsubmitted draft bid does not lock the weights
cases.why: The lock counts only submitted (active / selected / requested / anomaly) bids; an opened but unsent draft must not freeze the buyer.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`; QA vendor 1 opens a draft bid but does not submit it.
cases.steps: Buyer saves the happy-path weight.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 'Weights added successfully!'.
cases.oracle: 200; round weighted.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: Each weight must be an object, not a bare number
cases.why: `{"qa_freight_adj": "100"}` has no label or type; it must not be guessed.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: `"values": {"qa_freight_adj": "100"}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A name made only of HTML tags is stripped to nothing and refused
cases.why: Every string parameter is HTML-stripped before the action runs; `` becomes empty and must hit the blank-name rule, not store an empty header.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with `"label": ""`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: The weight type is case-sensitive
cases.why: Integrations that send "Relative" get a generic error; documents the exact contract.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with `"input_type": "Relative"`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A weight with no vendor values is refused
cases.why: A named weight with nobody in it would add a column of blanks.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body without `"data"`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A missing (null) vendor value is refused
cases.why: A null must not be stored as 0.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with `"data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": null}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A relative weight of exactly -100% is refused
cases.why: Lower boundary of the same rule.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Relative, value `"-100"`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A relative weight just inside the range is accepted
cases.why: Confirms the boundary is exclusive, not off by one.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Relative, value `"99.99"`; read the round.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; QA vendor 1's value reads 99.99.
cases.oracle: `weightages.values.qa_freight_adj.data.<vendor 1>` "99.99".

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A negative absolute weight (a credit) is accepted
cases.why: Absolute weights have no range; a negative amount is how a buyer credits a preferred vendor. It must be stored with its sign.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Absolute, value `"-250"`; read the round.
cases.expected: HTTP 200; value reads -250.
cases.oracle: `weightages.values.qa_freight_adj.data.<vendor 1>` "-250.0".

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: A line value that is itself an object is refused
cases.why: Deeper nesting must be refused, not flattened.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Line mode, `"data": {"{{vendorUuid}}": {"Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==": {"v": 1}}}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: Relative weights do not have to add up to 100
cases.why: Weights are independent ± adjustments, not shares of a whole; buyers coming from scoring-matrix tools expect a sum rule. Documents that none exists.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Two relative weights for QA vendor 1: qa_freight_adj "60" and qa_quality_pen "70".
cases.expected: HTTP 200; both stored.
cases.oracle: 200; `weightages.key_attributes` has 3 entries.

cases.section: What the weight table must look like (ValidateService)
cases.title: Two weights with the same name are accepted
cases.why: The screen refuses duplicate names; the API does not, so two identical column headers and a repeated criterion in the vendor's terms are possible.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Two keys (qa_freight_adj, qa_quality_pen) both labelled "QA_Platform_Same_{{stamp}}".
cases.expected: HTTP 200. Should be refused like the screen does.
cases.oracle: No 5xx; `misc.weightage.weightage_names` lists the name twice.

cases.title: weightages sent as true is refused cleanly
cases.why: Contrast with 047/048: `true` has no `[]`, so `try` returns nil and the parameter check catches it.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: `{"weightages": true}`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: A weight key containing "uuid" is mangled by the id decoder
cases.why: Every parameter key containing "uuid" is renamed and its value decoded as an id — including a weight key the buyer named e.g. "qa_uuid_bonus". The weight object becomes a number and the save is refused with a generic message the buyer cannot act on.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with the key `qa_uuid_bonus` instead of `qa_freight_adj`.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. (The screen builds keys from the typed name, so a weight called "uuid bonus" can never be saved.)
cases.oracle: 422 code 2.

cases.title: HTML in a weight KEY is stored raw
cases.why: Values are HTML-stripped, keys are not. The key becomes a sheet column `key_attribute` and, on the edit screen, the displayed weight name (underscores → spaces). Raw markup in keys relies entirely on every renderer escaping.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with the key `qa_`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 and the key kept verbatim in `misc.weightage.key_attributes`. Should be refused (keys limited to letters, digits, underscore).
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: A 400-digit weight becomes Infinity and the round still reads
cases.why: `to_f` of a huge string is Infinity, which Postgres stores; reads and later rankings must not break on it.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Absolute value of 400 nines; read the round.
cases.expected: Should be refused as out of range. Today: HTTP 200 and the value reads "Infinity". The round read must stay 2xx.
cases.oracle: No 5xx on the save or the read.

cases.title: A weight named "weighted_total" collides with the synthetic total column
cases.why: The action appends `weighted_total` to every list; a buyer key with the same name gives two total columns and makes `handle_removed_weight_keys` ignore that key on removal.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with the key `weighted_total`.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 and `weighted_total` twice in the key list. Should be refused as a reserved key.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.title: A weight named like a bid column ("price") still leaves the schema readable
cases.why: Weight widgets are appended to the buyer's sheet with the weight key as `key_attribute`; "price" duplicates the real price column's key.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`.
cases.steps: Happy-path body with the key `price`; read the buyer schema.
cases.expected: Should be refused (reserved widget key). Today: HTTP 200; the schema read must not crash.
cases.oracle: No 5xx on save; `GET /v1/trade/{{tradeId}}/schema` 2xx.

cases.section: Bids already in, and the round's state
cases.title: A rejected or revoked bid no longer locks the weights
cases.why: The lock counts only bids in active / selected / requested / anomaly_detected. After the only bid is rejected the buyer may re-weight even though a vendor has already shown its price.
cases.setup: `rfq_with_bid`, setting off; buyer rejects the bid (with rebidding allowed). Manual (reject step).
cases.steps: Happy-path save after the rejection.
cases.expected: HTTP 200. Product decision whether a priced-then-rejected bid should still lock.
cases.oracle: 200 after the reject; 422 code 15 before it.

cases.section: Bids already in, and the round's state
cases.title: Two saves at the same moment can double a vendor's weight
cases.why: Rows are found-or-built with no unique index; two concurrent first saves both insert, and the score sums every active row.
cases.setup: `published_rfq`; two identical saves fired within milliseconds. Manual (concurrency).
cases.steps: Fire both; count Weightage rows for (round, vendor, key).
cases.expected: One row. Today (suspected): two rows, weight counted twice.
cases.oracle: DB row count; read shows "200.0" instead of "100.0" for a lot weight of 100.

cases.section: Bids already in, and the round's state
cases.title: Weights can still be added after the bidding window closed with no bids
cases.why: There is no time check, and a round with no bids stays `active` after expiry (it moves to closed only when every line is closed). Weights added after the deadline change the record of an expired event.
cases.setup: RFQ, QA vendor 1 invited, no bids, window and extra time over (recipe `closed_rfq`).
cases.steps: Happy-path save.
cases.expected: HTTP 200 'Weights added successfully!' (or 422 code 2 if the round has already been moved to closed). Should be refused after close.
cases.oracle: No 5xx.

cases.section: Bids already in, and the round's state
cases.title: A technical (RFP) round cannot be weighted
cases.why: Weights adjust prices; a technical round has no ranking mode (`auction_config` nil), so the first save is refused.
cases.setup: Live RFP + RFQ event (recipe `published_rfp_rfq`).
cases.steps: `PATCH /trade/{{technicalTradeUuid}}/edit_weight_parameters` with the happy-path body.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, code 15 'Operation failed'.
cases.oracle: 422 code 15.

cases.section: Ranking, comparison and who can see the weights
cases.title: Weight columns appear only in the buyer's web sheet
cases.why: Buyers see one read-only column per weight plus "Weighted Total" (line mode: "Weighted <ranking key>"); vendors and the mobile app do not get the columns.
cases.setup: A weighted round. Manual (sheet layer shape is not asserted by the runner).
cases.steps: Read `GET /v1/trade/:id/schema` as buyer (web), as vendor, and as buyer from the mobile app.
cases.expected: Buyer web: weight widgets present with `mode_type` read and the round currency prefix. Vendor / mobile: absent.
cases.oracle: Global (lot) or inline (line) widgets list.

cases.section: Weights set while creating the round (POST /trade/template_input) — catalog only
cases.title: Weights on a price-based auction at creation refuse the whole create
cases.why: The rank / traffic-light rule also applies at creation; the error is raised inside the create transaction, and Rails 7.0 rolls back on `return`, so no half-created round should remain.
cases.setup: Create a price-based auction with `weightages`. Manual.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/template_input`; list the event's stages afterwards.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 code 15 'Operation failed'; no new round.
cases.oracle: No trade_request row created.

cases.section: Weights set while creating the round (POST /trade/template_input) — catalog only
cases.title: An unknown weight identifier at creation crashes instead of being refused
cases.why: An identifier with no matching line maps to a nil key, which reaches the Sorbet-typed save as `item_id: nil`.
cases.setup: Create an RFQ with line weights keyed by an identifier no line carries. Manual.
cases.steps: `POST /trade/template_input`.
cases.expected: Should be 422 code 2. Today (suspected): TypeError → HTTP 500 (create rolled back).
cases.oracle: 5xx is the defect.

cases.section: Round numbers, names and status labels
cases.title: Every new round gets a reference number whose prefix tells its type
cases.why: Buyers quote these numbers to vendors and finance; a wrong prefix or a reused number sends people to the wrong round.
cases.setup: One event with a technical round (RFP), a price round (RFQ), and the price round later moved to a reverse auction. `gate: show_reference_id` on one stage, off on another.
cases.steps: 1. Publish the event. 2. Note each round's reference. 3. Move the price round to auction and note the new auction round's reference. 4. Create a second event and note its price round's reference.
cases.expected: Technical round "RFP-n", price round "RFQ-n", the auction made from it "RA-n" with a fresh number (not the RFQ's), a forward auction would be "FA-n". The number is the company's running count of rounds, so the next event's round has a higher number. With reference display on, the round title reads "Title [RFQ-n]"; with it off, the reference is not shown.
cases.oracle: Stage `ref_uuid` (only present when `config.show_reference_id` is true, `trade_template_serializer.rb:55-57`); otherwise Procol DB `trade_requests.ref_id` (SELECT). Prefix `get_ref_identifier` (`trade_request.rb:2527-2543`); number = `companies.trade_requests_count` at create (`:382-386`); rfq_then_auction always re-numbered (`:374-380`).

cases.section: Owner, open tender and a second auction
cases.title: A round is a closed tender open to everyone unless the company has open tenders switched on
cases.why: An open tender is listed publicly to vendors; a round becoming open by accident exposes the buyer's requirement.
cases.setup: Company without `gate: enable_open_tender_events`; a second company with it on, an event marked "show under open events", one price round and one auction in each.
cases.steps: Publish each and read the stored tender type and audience.
cases.expected: First company: closed tender, audience "everyone". Second company: the price round becomes an open tender; the auction stays closed (auctions are never open tenders); an event not marked "show under open events" stays closed.
cases.oracle: `before_save :set_tender_value` (`trade_request.rb:3152-3159`, `company.rb:215-217`); DB `trade_requests.tender` (0 open / 1 closed), `customised_audience` 0; stage read `customised_audience` false.

cases.section: Bidding window, extensions and evaluation windows
cases.title: On a round that closes line by line, an extension does not move the following window
cases.why: Line-by-line (staggered) closing has its own timetable; only the round's overall closing time follows the extension.
cases.setup: Auction with staggered line closing, followed by an evaluation window.
cases.steps: Extend the last line's end; read the round's closing time and the evaluation window.
cases.expected: The round closing time becomes the extended end; the evaluation window is not shifted.
cases.oracle: `trade_schedule.rb:151-152, 158` (staggered → only `closed_at` updated).

cases.section: Bidding window, extensions and evaluation windows
cases.title: Savings are recalculated after the extended end, not at the original end
cases.why: Savings computed at the original end miss the bids placed in the extension.
cases.setup: Live price round with a reference price; QA vendor bid; `gate: show_custom_savings` for the custom figures.
cases.steps: 1. Extend the round; the vendor improves its price in the extension. 2. After the new end, read the round's savings.
cases.expected: Savings use the improved price; custom savings appear about 2 s and standard savings about 5 s after the new end.
cases.oracle: `trade_schedule.rb:168-169` queues `SavingsCalculatorWorker` (end + 5 s) and `CustomSavingsCalculatorWorker` (end + 2 s); custom worker returns early while `closed_at > now` (`custom_savings_calculator_worker.rb:9`).

cases.section: Send to evaluation and evaluation status
cases.title: With "only the creator's scores" on, scoring after bidding ends only refreshes the buyer rank
cases.why: The setting freezes other evaluators' scores; if it still re-ran the full scoring, a late evaluator could change results.
cases.setup: `gate: update_only_creator_scores_in_evaluation`; technical round with two responses scored; bidding ended.
cases.steps: A second evaluator changes a score; read the responses' ranks and line best prices.
cases.expected: Only the buyer rank (and line best price) is recalculated; other stored scores are unchanged. Before the bidding end the full recalculation runs.
cases.oracle: `update_only_creator_scores?` (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:1362-1373`), branch at `trade_request.rb:1987-2004`.

cases.section: Send to evaluation and evaluation status
cases.title: The technical report with approvals should not fail for a round that was never sent to evaluation
cases.why: The report's approval section prints "Send for TR at" from the first evaluation window; a round evaluated without one makes the whole report fail.
cases.setup: Technical round with an approved technical award proposal, where the round has no evaluation (extra closing) window (e.g. scored straight after bidding).
cases.steps: Download the technical report.
cases.expected: The report job raises (no window → `.first` is nil) and the report never becomes ready (unverified whether an evaluated round can lack the window on this client).
cases.oracle: `rfi_comparison_report.rb:474` → `get_send_for_evaluation_start_time` (`trade_request.rb:774-776`, `.first.start_time` with no guard).

cases.section: Quantities, line counts, attachments and price limits
cases.title: The number of items on a round is counted the way the buyer sees them
cases.why: Event cards and reports show "n items"; a technical round counting its form instead of the event's lines, or variants counted as separate items, misleads the buyer.
cases.setup: Event with 3 lines; technical round; price round with the same 3 lines; an alternate-bidding round with 2 products × 2 variants at one location.
cases.steps: Read each round's item count.
cases.expected: Technical round 3 (the event's lines); price round 3 (its lines); alternate bidding: 2 items, 4 variants, and it counts as a multi-product round.
cases.oracle: `number_of_products` (`trade_request.rb:2243-2256`); `is_multi_product` (`:1174-1179`); `misc.number_of_variants`.

cases.section: Quantities, line counts, attachments and price limits
cases.title: More than 15 attachments on one line is refused on every way of creating a round
cases.why: The limit protects storage and the vendor's download; it is enforced on one create path only.
cases.setup: Draft event.
cases.steps: 1. Create a round through the classic create with a line carrying 16 attachments. 2. Add a round through the event flow (template input) with a line carrying 16 attachments.
cases.expected: Only the classic create checks it (`trade_controller.rb:136`); the event-flow path has no such check (unverified: whether it has its own limit elsewhere).
cases.oracle: HTTP 422 code 489; `maximum_attachments_limit_exceeded?` (`trade_controller_helper.rb:5376-5379`), `MAX_ATTACHMENT_COUNT = 15` (`trade_product.rb:55`).

cases.section: Quantities, line counts, attachments and price limits
cases.title: A minimum decrement below half a paisa should not silently become no minimum
cases.why: Rounding the tick to two decimals turns 0.004 into 0, so vendors can lower by any amount.
cases.setup: Auction line with tick size 0.004 (and a second line with no tick but a round-level price-change slab of 5).
cases.steps: A vendor lowers its price by 0.001 on each line.
cases.expected: Line 1 tick reads 0.0 and the change is accepted.
cases.oracle: `tick_size` = `to_f.round(2)` (`trade_product.rb:508-512`); fallback `config.price_change_slab` (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:193-196`).

cases.section: Quantities, line counts, attachments and price limits
cases.title: English auction: each vendor's step and floor are measured from the best price
cases.why: In an English auction a vendor must beat the best price by a tick; a wrong step lets a vendor "beat" the best by nothing.
cases.setup: English auction (`gate: is_english_auction_enabled`), line best 1,000, vendor A at 1,050, tick 10 (second line: tick 1 %).
cases.steps: Read A's required step and floor; A bids 990, then 995.
cases.expected: Step = |1,050 − 1,000| + 10 = 60 → A must reach 990 or lower; 990 accepted, a later 995 refused. Percentage line: + 1 % × best, rounded up to 2 decimals. A non-English percentage tick = previous target value × tick % / 100, rounded up.
cases.oracle: `trade_product.rb:187-197, 239-251`; `trade_template_helper.rb:5479-5513`. Default widget for English auction "price", allowed flag default false (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:884-897`).

cases.title: Each auction type shows its own default indicators to vendors
cases.why: Indicators tell a vendor how far it is from winning; a price-based auction must not show rank and a traffic-light auction must show its colour.
cases.setup: Four auctions: rank, rank with line-by-line closing, price, traffic light; plus a Dutch and a knockout.
cases.steps: Read each round's indicator settings.
cases.expected: Rank → rank; rank + line closing → rank and best price on gross total; price → best price on gross total and best price; traffic light → colour and best price on gross total (plus the best-ranking widget when the template has one). Optional indicators are the rest of rank / best price / gross total, each defaulting to off; Dutch and technical rounds offer none (Dutch with projects: rank); knockout offers rank. Traffic-light zones for best-price and rank indicators default to none.
cases.oracle: `trade_config.other_auction_indicators_config` (`trade_template_serializer.rb:98`); `default_auction_indicator` / `get_possible_other_auction_indicators` (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:698-726, 745-774`); traffic light rank vs price (`:227-233`). Twin EDGE-EVRMTR-038 reads the sandbox round, whose settings block carries the indicators.

cases.title: Knockout rounds run one at a time in order and remember who took part
cases.why: Only vendors who took part in earlier rounds may go on; two active rounds with the same number would let a vendor bid twice.
cases.setup: Knockout auction with 3 rounds; Dutch closing on multiple vendors; Dutch "on total amount" (not on base price).
cases.steps: Watch the running round at each boundary; vendor A bids in round 1 only; read round 2's eligible vendors.
cases.expected: Exactly one round is running at any moment (a round is running strictly between its start and end); the next round is the one numbered +1; A is listed as having taken part in round 1. A second active round with the same number is refused ("Round no has already been taken", wording unverified).
