Dutch closes on several vendors only when closing mode is "multiple"; "on total amount" only when base-price mode is explicitly off.
cases.oracle: `trade_round.rb:27-45`; next round `trade_request.rb:735-737`; Dutch flags `:1639-1645`.

cases.title: Savings strategies drop references with no value and compute the lot best amount by closing mode
cases.why: A strategy with no reference price would show 100 % savings; the lot best amount differs for lot-closing and line-closing rounds.
cases.setup: Lot-based savings with budget set and last purchase price empty; round A closes as a lot, round B line by line with 2 lines (best 10 × 5 and none on line 2).
cases.steps: Read the savings strategies and best amounts.
cases.expected: Last purchase price is not offered for lot-based savings; references without a value are not stored. A uses the lot best price; B uses Σ best line price × quantity = 50 (line 2 skipped). A reference is per unit when it is "on price", else an amount. Initial best amount takes each vendor's first bid line. In the auction reports the vendor savings column is "realised price drop" on a buy round and "realised price increase" on a sell round; the buyer performance report's awarded amount is the sum of the selected bids' landed amounts.
cases.oracle: `savings_configuration.rb:44-46, 55-63, 87-90, 124, 190-207`; `trade_product.rb:721-740`.

cases.section: Terms, default settings and reads that must not crash
cases.title: A new price round starts with the documented default settings
cases.why: Defaults decide whether vendors get mails, whether bids can be revoked and how numbers are rounded; a wrong default silently changes every new event.
cases.setup: New price round on a client with no overrides.
cases.steps: Read the round's settings.
cases.expected: Price-increase and price-decrease approvals off; user names hidden; revoke bid allowed (default on); reopen flags unset; new-bid mail, web-bidding mail and select-bid notification off; auto cash discount off; auto-award off; multiple POs per bid off; baseline cost adjustment off; T&A bids not hidden from QCS; unverified-vendor selection allowed (default on); widget precision 2; request layout "json template"; vendor activity type "onboarding"; fast bidding off; English auction off; partial closing: no participant approval, editable widget "participant quantity"; company profile shown only when the round has no settings at all.

cases.section: Terms, default settings and reads that must not crash
cases.title: Reading a round that has no lines, no schedule or no widgets is a clear answer, not a crash
cases.why: Half-built drafts exist (a round saved before its lines, an imported round without widgets); listing or opening them must not take the page down.
cases.setup: Draft price round saved with no line items; a round whose widget list for one line type is missing; a book-building line with no threshold.
cases.steps: Open each round, its summary and its line list; save a line on the round without widgets.
cases.expected: Product readers on a round with no lines, the summary with no schedule, widget readers and line save with a missing widget list, and the threshold quantity raise → untyped 500 (each path unverified live).

cases.section: Terms, default settings and reads that must not crash
cases.title: A line's unit symbol and formula columns are filled when the line is saved
cases.why: Vendors read the unit next to the quantity; buyer formula columns (e.g. budget = qty × rate) must be computed before vendors see the line.
cases.setup: Template with a buyer formula column `qty * target_rate`; line qty 10, target rate 25, unit "KG" with custom symbol.
cases.steps: Save the line; read it.
cases.expected: Formula column 250; unit shows the line's own symbol, else the unit's symbol. A formula that cannot be computed leaves the column blank (only logged).
cases.oracle: `save_formula_values` (`trade_product.rb:93, 828-835`) into `other_details`; `unit_value` (`:114-116`).

cases.section: Round numbers, names and status labels
cases.title: Changing a draft round's type keeps its number and changes only the prefix
cases.why: A buyer who switches a draft round from RFQ to auction should not get a new number that no longer matches what was shared internally.
cases.setup: Draft event with a price round numbered RFQ-n.
cases.steps: 1. Change the draft round's type to auction and save. 2. Read its reference.
cases.expected: The reference becomes RA-n with the same n.
cases.oracle: `trade_requests.ref_id` before/after; `before_update :update_ref_id` splits on "-" and re-prefixes (`trade_request.rb:278, 388-394`).

cases.section: Round numbers, names and status labels
cases.title: Round status in the auction report reads Open, Expired, Closed or Withdrawn
cases.why: The status column of the downloaded auction report is what auditors read; a raw internal word looks like a broken report.
cases.setup: Four auction rounds: one live, one past its end but not closed, one closed, one withdrawn.
cases.steps: Download the auction bidding report for each.
cases.expected: "Open", "Expired", "Closed", "Withdrawn". A round withdrawn through the path that stores status "withdrawn" (not "in_active") should also read "Withdrawn"; today it prints the raw lowercase "withdrawn".
cases.oracle: RFQ-status column = `display_status` (`auction_bidding_excel_report_data_model.rb:139`); mapping `trade_request.rb:1228-1238` maps only `in_active` to "Withdrawn".

cases.section: Round numbers, names and status labels
cases.title: Downloaded attachment folders are named after the round type
cases.why: The zip of a round's attachments is filed by its folder name; "Technical", "RFQ" and "Auction" must match the round.
cases.setup: Event with a technical round, a price round and an auction, each with one attachment.
cases.steps: Download the attachments zip of each round.
cases.expected: Folder "<event ref>_Technical_Attachments" for the technical round (RFP or RFI), "<event ref>_RFQ_Attachments" for the price round, "<event ref>_Auction_Attachments" for the auction (also for an auction made from an RFQ).
cases.oracle: `download_zip_task_controller.rb:55` uses `stage_name` (`trade_request.rb:1240-1251`).

cases.section: Terms, default settings and reads that must not crash
cases.title: Terms stored as old plain text are returned as text with stable ids
cases.why: Rounds copied from old events carry plain-text terms; the acceptance pop-up must still list them.
cases.setup: Round copied from an old event with plain-text terms; a new round with structured terms.
cases.steps: Read both rounds' terms (plain and structured).
cases.expected: Plain text in both; legacy items get ids "legacy_<round>_<n>".
cases.oracle: `terms_and_conditions_structurable.rb:18-59`; stage `terms_and_conditions`, `terms_and_conditions_structured`.

journeys.title: Award outcomes: split awards, approval notes and purchase orders
journeys.goal: Split an award across vendors and lines, get it approved with a note for approval, and turn it into purchase orders that carry exactly the awarded vendor, quantity and price.

cases.section: What the vendors see after the award (see also events-deep3-lek.md)
cases.title: The winning vendor sees "Awarded" with its awarded quantity, not its quoted quantity
cases.why: A vendor told it won 30 units when it was awarded 15 will ship the wrong quantity.
cases.setup: A split award (15 of the vendor's quoted 30) that is final.
cases.steps: 1. Sign in as the winning vendor and open the event and the purchase order.
cases.expected: The event shows the bid as awarded with 15 units; the order shows 15 units.
cases.oracle: Screen text; cross-check with API-EVDAPO-002 / 004.

cases.section: Orders created by a final award
cases.title: One order per awarded vendor, and none for a vendor that was not awarded
cases.why: A missing order means a supplier never receives the PO; an extra one means paying for goods nobody awarded.
cases.setup: An award that is final: S1 split between three vendors (198678), or S3 line-wise between two vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Approve the award to completion. 2. List the orders the event's round created.
cases.expected: Exactly one order for each awarded vendor; none for the vendors left out.
cases.oracle: `SELECT … FROM orders WHERE trade_request_id = <round>` — seller_company_id set = awarded vendors.

cases.section: Orders created by a final award
cases.title: Each order's lines carry the awarded quantity
cases.why: A vendor awarded 10 of its quoted 30 units must be ordered 10.
cases.setup: As API-EVDAPO-001.
cases.steps: 1. Read each order's lines.
cases.expected: The lines' quantities add up to exactly what that vendor was awarded, one line per awarded line item.
cases.oracle: `order_items.quantity` per order = awarded_quantity.

cases.section: Orders created by a final award
cases.title: Each order carries the vendor's own awarded unit price
cases.why: Two vendors on one split line have different prices; each order must carry its own.
cases.setup: As API-EVDAPO-001 (single-line awards).
cases.steps: 1. Read each order's price.
cases.expected: The order's unit price is the price of that vendor's awarded bid.
cases.oracle: `orders.price` = the vendor's submitted unit price.

cases.section: Orders created by a final award
cases.title: The order states the awarded quantity, not the quoted quantity
cases.why: The order header's quantity is what lists, reports and integrations read; if it shows the quoted 30 for an award of 10, the PO says 30.
cases.setup: As API-EVDAPO-001; at least one vendor awarded less than it quoted (S1 on 198678).
cases.steps: 1. Read each order's quantity.
cases.expected: The order's quantity equals the awarded quantity.
cases.oracle: `orders.quantity` = awarded quantity. Code reading: the header copies `bid.quantity` (the quoted quantity) — suspected to state the quoted quantity on every partial award.

cases.section: Orders created by a final award
cases.title: Line-wise award: each vendor's order holds only the line it won
cases.why: A vendor that won line 1 must not be ordered line 2 at its (losing) line-2 price.
cases.setup: S3: QA vendor 1 won line 1, QA vendor 2 won line 2; both had quoted both lines.
cases.steps: 1. Read each vendor's bid lines after the award.
cases.expected: The won line is "selected"; the vendor's other line is marked not awarded ("negotiated"); the order holds one line.
cases.oracle: `bid_trade_products.status` 2 for the won line, 10 for the other; `order_items` count 1.

cases.title: One line split between three vendors adds up to the line's quantity
cases.why: Splitting a line between suppliers is the everyday way to spread supply risk; if the split is refused or silently altered the buyer cannot award as decided.
cases.setup: gate: `is_partial_awarding_enabled`. A closed RFQ, one line of 30 units; QA vendors 1, 2 and 3 have live bids (vendors 1 and 2 tied at the best price, vendor 3 higher).
cases.steps: 1. Open an award. 2. Award 15 units to QA vendor 2, 10 to QA vendor 1 and 5 to QA vendor 3 in one change.
cases.expected: Accepted; the proposal holds the three vendors with exactly 15, 10 and 5 units.
cases.oracle: `POST /proposal`, then `POST /proposal/:id/add_response` 200; `proposals.responses_hash.data[<vendor>].egli_data[<line>].awarded_quantity` = 15 / 10 / 5.

cases.title: Each vendor's awarded amount is its awarded quantity times its own price
cases.why: The award amount per vendor is what the approver signs off and what the vendor is promised; if it counts the vendor's whole quote instead of the awarded share, the approval is for the wrong money.
cases.setup: As API-EVDAWD-001, after the split.
cases.steps: 1. Read the award back. 2. For each vendor compare the amount with awarded quantity × that vendor's unit price.
cases.expected: QA vendor 2: 15 × its price; QA vendor 1: 10 × its price; QA vendor 3: 5 × its price — to the paisa.
cases.oracle: `proposals.responses_hash.data[<vendor company id>].total_amount` equals Σ awarded_quantity × unit price. Code reading: without a master comparison "proposal value" formula or a round `proposal_value_source`, the per-line value is the bid line's full gross total, whatever quantity is awarded. Live 2026-10-03: correct at 198678 and 32461 on add (a value formula applies); the fallback bites on remove — see API-EVDAWD-005.

cases.title: The award's total value is the sum of what each vendor was awarded
cases.why: Approval routing uses the total (flows are chosen by rules such as "total value ≥ 1"); a wrong total sends the award to the wrong approvers and shows the wrong spend.
cases.setup: As API-EVDAWD-001.
cases.steps: 1. Open the award as the buyer and read its total value.
cases.expected: Total = (15 + 10) × the tied best price + 5 × QA vendor 3's price.
cases.oracle: `GET /proposal/:id` → `proposal_values.total_proposal_value` (formatted) equals the computed total; stored `meta_data.total_l1_proposal + total_non_l1_proposal` likewise.

cases.title: Awarding more than the line's quantity across vendors is refused when partial awarding is on
cases.why: Over-awarding commits the buyer to more goods than were sourced.
cases.setup: gate: `is_partial_awarding_enabled`. As API-EVDAWD-001 (25 units already awarded to vendors 1 and 2).
cases.steps: 1. Raise QA vendor 3's award to 10 units (25 + 10 = 35 > 30).
cases.expected: Refused: "You cannot select bid with more than requested quantity." Nothing changes.
cases.oracle: HTTP 422, code 561.

cases.title: Line-wise split: each line goes whole to its own best bidder, with exact amounts
cases.why: Multi-line events are usually awarded line by line to whoever is cheapest on each line; each vendor's award must carry only its line.
cases.setup: A closed RFQ with two lines (30 and 20 units) and three QA vendors; QA vendor 1 is cheapest on line 1 and QA vendor 2 on line 2.
cases.steps: 1. Award line 1 (30 units) to QA vendor 1 and line 2 (20 units) to QA vendor 2. 2. Read each vendor's amount, the total and the L1 part.
cases.expected: QA vendor 1 = 30 × its line-1 price; QA vendor 2 = 20 × its line-2 price; total = their sum; all of it is L1.
cases.oracle: add_response 200; `responses_hash.data[v].egli_ids` = only that vendor's line; amounts as computed; `total_l1_proposal` = total.

cases.title: Submitting the award puts it into approval, no longer a draft
cases.why: Once the buyer sends an award for approval, what the approver sees must be what was submitted.
cases.setup: A closed RFQ with a built award (S1 or S3); an applicable award approval flow.
cases.steps: 1. Submit the award, choosing an applicable approval flow. 2. Read the award's status.
cases.expected: Accepted; the award is "waiting for approval" (requested).
cases.oracle: `POST /proposal/:id/submit` 200; `proposals.status` = 4.

cases.title: No second award can be started while one is in approval
cases.why: Two awards for one event in parallel could both be approved and double the order.
cases.setup: As API-EVDNFA-001, award in approval.
cases.steps: 1. Start a new award on the same event.
cases.expected: Refused: "The proposal has already been submitted".
cases.oracle: `POST /proposal` → 422 code 573.

cases.title: The submitted award cannot be changed
cases.why: An approver must not approve one allocation and see another executed.
cases.setup: As API-EVDNFA-001.
cases.steps: 1. Try to change a vendor's awarded quantity on the submitted award.
cases.expected: Refused: only a draft can be changed ("Proposal does not exists").
cases.oracle: `POST /proposal/:id/add_response` → 422 code 721 (or 573).

cases.title: Approving every step makes the award final
cases.why: Only a fully approved award may close the bids and create purchase orders.
cases.setup: As API-EVDNFA-001; the signed-in buyer is the approver of every step of the chosen flow (198678).
cases.steps: 1. Approve step 1. 2. Approve step 2 (and any further step). 3. Read the award's status.
cases.expected: Each approval is accepted; after the last one the award is final (selected) — not before.
cases.oracle: `POST /approval_workflow/approval_requests/resolve_approval` 200 per step; `proposals.status` 4 → 2.

cases.section: Orders created by a final award
cases.title: The buyer's order page shows the same quantity and price as the award
cases.why: The buyer reviews and releases the PO from this page.
cases.setup: As API-EVDAPO-001 (S1).
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, open each order.
cases.expected: Quantity (and, for single-line orders, price) as awarded.
cases.oracle: `GET /orders/:id` → quantity / price.

cases.title: An award that goes through a contract creates no order
cases.why: With contract forms on the award, the contract replaces the PO; an order as well would double the commitment.
cases.setup: gate: `is_contract_creation_enabled`. An award that carries contract forms.
cases.steps: 1. Submit the award. 2. List the round's orders.
cases.expected: No order; a contract is created instead.
cases.oracle: `orders` empty for the round; `proposal_helper.rb:152` passes `skip_order_creation: true`.

cases.title: Without a vendor code, PO integration refuses the award instead of creating a broken order
cases.why: The ERP rejects a PO without a vendor code; the award must stop before that.
cases.setup: gate: `is_po_integration_enabled`. An event from a PR; the awarded vendor has no vendor code; the company does not allow orders without a vendor code.
cases.steps: 1. Award the vendor's bid.
cases.expected: Refused: "Unable to create order, Vendor Code is not present."

cases.title: Vendors tied at the best price count as best-price (L1) awards
cases.why: The L1 / non-L1 split is how a buyer justifies an award; two vendors quoting the same lowest price are both the lowest bidder, and showing their share as "not L1" invites an audit question that has no basis.
cases.setup: As API-EVDAWD-001 (QA vendors 1 and 2 tied at the best price). On 32461: the whole line to one of two tied vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Read the award's "awarded to L1" and "awarded to others" amounts.
cases.expected: The tied vendors' shares are counted as L1; only QA vendor 3's share is "others".
cases.oracle: `proposal_values.total_l1_proposal` = Σ shares of vendors holding the best price. Code reading: a vendor counts as L1 only when its line rank equals 1, and a tie at the best price shifts every rank by one (both tied leaders are rank 2) — so tied leaders are suspected to be counted as non-L1.

cases.title: Taking a vendor off the award removes exactly its amount, and putting it back restores it
cases.why: Buyers rework an award several times before submitting; totals that drift after a remove/add cycle make the final number untrustworthy.
cases.setup: As API-EVDAWD-001 (198678), or the whole line awarded to one vendor (32461).
cases.steps: 1. Take QA vendor 3 off the award. 2. Read the totals. 3. Put QA vendor 3 back with 5 units. 4. Read the totals again.
cases.expected: After step 1 the total is the other two vendors' amounts only and QA vendor 3 is no longer listed; after step 3 the totals are as in API-EVDAWD-003. On 32461, removing the only vendor leaves an empty award worth ₹0.
cases.oracle: add_response with `action: "remove"` 200; `responses_hash.data` loses the vendor; `meta_data` totals match the recomputed sums.

cases.title: Changing an awarded vendor's quantity changes its amount
cases.why: "Give vendor 3 three units instead of five" is a normal correction; if the quantity changes but the amount does not, the proposal shows a value nobody agreed to.
cases.setup: As API-EVDAWD-001, QA vendor 3 awarded 5 units.
cases.steps: 1. Award QA vendor 3 again, now with 3 units. 2. Read QA vendor 3's awarded quantity and amount.
cases.expected: Awarded quantity 3; amount 3 × QA vendor 3's price.
cases.oracle: `responses_hash.data[v3].egli_data[line].awarded_quantity` = 3 and `total_amount` = 3 × price. Code reading: re-adding a vendor already on the line skips the amount recalculation but merges the new quantity — suspected: quantity changes, amount stays.

cases.title: A vendor who never bid cannot be awarded
cases.why: Awarding an invited vendor with no quote would create a purchase with no agreed price.
cases.setup: A closed RFQ where QA vendor 4 was invited but never bid.
cases.steps: 1. Try to award QA vendor 4 one unit.
cases.expected: Refused: the vendor is not present in the latest round — or has no bid on the line.
cases.oracle: HTTP 422, code 826 (or 715).

cases.title: With partial awarding off, the whole line awarded to one vendor carries the exact amount
cases.why: The simplest award must be exactly right before the complex ones mean anything.
cases.setup: Demo Account 2 32461 (partial awarding off). A closed RFQ, one line of 30 units, two vendors tied at the best price.
cases.steps: 1. Award all 30 units to QA vendor 2. 2. Read its amount and the total.
cases.expected: Amount and total = 30 × QA vendor 2's price.
cases.oracle: `total_amount` and `proposal_values.total_proposal_value` = 30 × price.

cases.title: With partial awarding off, a second vendor cannot be added to a line already fully awarded
cases.why: With partial awarding off the line goes to one vendor; adding a second vendor's whole quote would double the quantity.
cases.setup: Demo Account 2 32461; QA vendor 2 already awarded the whole line.
cases.steps: 1. Also award QA vendor 1, without stating a quantity (its quoted 30 units).
cases.expected: Refused: the line's quantity is already awarded.
cases.oracle: HTTP 422, code 561. (Sending an explicit quantity skips this check entirely — already covered by API-XMAT bidding-matrix M2.)

cases.title: Once the award is final, every awarded vendor's bid is marked awarded
cases.why: The vendor's bid status drives what the supplier sees ("Awarded") and what reports count as won.
cases.setup: An award that has been submitted and fully approved (198678, where the buyer is the approver of an applicable flow).
cases.steps: 1. After approval, read each awarded vendor's bid.
cases.expected: Each awarded vendor's bid is "selected"; a vendor that was not awarded keeps an active, unawarded bid.
cases.oracle: `bids.status` = 2 (selected) for awarded vendors.

cases.section: Award changes the runner does not cover
cases.title: A bid revised after it was put on the award blocks the submit
cases.why: The approver must approve the price the vendor actually offers now.
cases.setup: Award open during bidding with QA vendor 1 on it; QA vendor 1 then revises.
cases.steps: 1. Submit the award.
cases.expected: Refused: "A few bids have been revised. Please re-award to continue.", or "Proposal cannot be empty" when the revision took the old bid off.
cases.oracle: HTTP 422 code 1126 / 683. Already run live in bidding-matrix M7 (both clients answered 683).

cases.title: The submitted award cannot be discarded as if it were a draft
cases.why: Discarding is for drafts; a submitted award is withdrawn through the approval, leaving a trail.
cases.setup: As API-EVDNFA-001.
cases.steps: 1. Discard the submitted award.
cases.expected: Refused: "Invalid Parameters".
cases.oracle: `POST /proposal/discard_draft_proposal` → 422 code 888.

cases.title: Approving an already-approved step again changes nothing
cases.why: A double click or a second tab must not approve twice or re-run the award.
cases.setup: As API-EVDNFA-005, after the award is final.
cases.steps: 1. Approve the first step again.
cases.expected: Refused: the step is no longer pending ("Request not found").
cases.oracle: 422 code 4 (code 491 "already approved" is also acceptable wording).

cases.title: A rejected award comes back as a new draft carrying the same allocation
cases.why: After a rejection the buyer reworks the award; losing the allocation would force a rebuild from scratch.
cases.setup: An award in approval; the approver rejects it.
cases.steps: 1. Reject. 2. Read the event's awards.
cases.expected: The rejected award is "rejected"; a new draft exists that points back to it and holds the same vendors and quantities.
cases.oracle: `proposals` rows; `meta_data.previous_proposal_id`.

cases.title: Submitting an award while bidding is still open stops the bidding
cases.why: Awarding mid-bidding is allowed by default; once an award is in approval no vendor may revise under it.
cases.setup: An RFQ still open; an award built and submitted into a flow.
cases.steps: 1. Submit. 2. As a vendor, try to bid.
cases.expected: The round's submission time is expired by the submit; the vendor's bid is refused.
cases.oracle: `proposal_helper.rb:252-268` expires the latest commercial round; vendor bid → 422 code 33.

cases.title: Several POs on one bid each carry only their own lines
cases.why: `allow_multiple_po_on_same_bid` splits one bid into several POs (up to 20); quantities must not repeat across them.
cases.setup: A round that allows several purchase orders on one bid (off at both demo clients today).
cases.steps: 1. Close the bid twice with different line selections.
cases.expected: Two orders whose lines do not overlap; the 21st is refused.
cases.oracle: `orders` / `order_items`; code 17.

cases.section: Award changes the runner does not cover
cases.title: A colleague can discard another buyer's draft award
cases.why: Discarding a draft has no creator check — any user of the company can throw away a colleague's half-built award.
cases.setup: Two buyers of the same company; buyer A has a draft award on an event.
cases.steps: 1. As buyer B, discard buyer A's draft.
cases.expected: Accepted (the draft becomes inactive). Should be refused unless B owns the draft or is a super admin.
cases.oracle: `POST /proposal/discard_draft_proposal` 200 for a non-creator; the proposal row status 0.

cases.section: Award changes the runner does not cover
cases.title: Scoring a technical response empties every draft award of the event
cases.why: A buyer's half-built award silently disappears when an evaluator's score goes live.
cases.setup: An RFP+RFQ event; the buyer has a draft award with two vendors; an evaluator then submits a score.
cases.steps: 1. Build the draft award. 2. Let the evaluator submit a score (no approval flow). 3. Re-open the draft award.
cases.expected: The draft award is empty (vendors and totals reset). Should at least warn the buyer.
cases.oracle: `proposals.responses_hash` empty and totals 0 after step 2.

cases.section: Award changes the runner does not cover
cases.title: A zero-quantity award does not add the vendor's full quote to the total
cases.why: "Awarded 0" is how a buyer parks a vendor; counting its whole quote inflates the award.
cases.setup: gate: `is_partial_awarding_enabled`. A closed RFQ, two vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Award QA vendor 1 the whole line and QA vendor 2 zero units. 2. Read the totals.
cases.expected: QA vendor 2 contributes ₹0.
cases.oracle: `responses_hash.data[v2].total_amount` = 0. Code reading: without a value formula the full bid gross is used (same root cause as API-EVDAWD-002).

cases.title: The buyer can approve its own award
cases.why: At PROCOL DEMO the buyer who submits the award is also the approver of both steps of several flows: the "four eyes" rule is configuration only, nothing in the code prevents self-approval.
cases.setup: A flow whose approvers include the requester (several exist at 198678, e.g. the recent requests 32607–32609 had the requester as approver of both steps).
cases.steps: 1. Submit an award into such a flow. 2. Approve it as the same user.
cases.expected: Accepted. Should a requester be barred from approving their own request? Product decision; record it.
cases.oracle: resolve_approval 200 with approver identifier = requested_by_user_id.

journeys.title: Several vendors competing on one event
journeys.goal: Three or four vendors bid against each other: ranks and L1 update after every bid, ties and rebids are handled, auctions extend when a late bid lands, and no vendor ever learns a competitor's price.

cases.title: The vendor's live screen and the downloaded quote show nothing of the competitors
cases.why: The API being clean does not prove the PDF/Excel export is.
cases.setup: A live RFQ with three vendors' bids.
cases.steps: 1. As one vendor, open the event, then download its own quote/summary.
cases.expected: Only its own data on screen and in the file.
cases.oracle: Search the screen text and file for the other vendors' names and prices.

cases.title: A late bid that changes the leader extends the auction by the configured minutes
cases.why: Without the extension the auction rewards sniping: a vendor bids in the last seconds and nobody can answer.
cases.setup: A fresh rank auction (about 4½ minutes) with dynamic closing (last 1 minute, +2 minutes, rank limit 1); QA vendors 1 and 2 tied, QA vendor 3 last.
cases.steps: 1. Confirm the auction carries the settings. 2. Inside the last minute, QA vendor 3 bids below everyone. 3. Read the auction's end time.
cases.expected: The settings are stored as sent; the end time moves out by exactly 2 minutes.
cases.oracle: `GET /v1/trade/:id/schema` trade_config; `GET /trade/:id` `ending_at` before vs after (±5 s).

cases.title: A second late lead change extends again
cases.why: Extensions must keep working round after round, as long as the lead keeps changing late.
cases.setup: As API-EVDAUX-001, after the first extension.
cases.steps: 1. Inside the last minute of the extended window, QA vendor 1 bids below QA vendor 3. 2. Read the end time.
cases.expected: The end time moves out by another 2 minutes.
cases.oracle: `ending_at` = previous + 120 s (±5 s).

cases.section: RFQ with four vendors — the buyer's view after every move
cases.title: After the first bid, that vendor leads and its price is the L1 price
cases.why: The comparison is the buyer's live scoreboard; it must be right from the first bid.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ, one line of 30 units, four QA vendors invited, no bids.
cases.steps: 1. QA vendor 1 bids. 2. As the buyer, open the comparison.
cases.expected: QA vendor 1 is marked best bidder; nobody else is; the L1 price is QA vendor 1's price.
cases.oracle: `GET /v1/trade/:id/event_indicators` → `auction_identifiers_data.<vendor>.inline.<line>.rank.best_bidder`; `GET /v1/trade/:id/schema?l1_prices=true` → `l1_prices.line_item_based.<line>.price`.

cases.section: RFQ with four vendors — the buyer's view after every move
cases.title: A higher bid the buyer places on a vendor's behalf does not take the lead
cases.why: A surrogate bid (typed in by the buyer from a vendor's email or phone quote) must compete exactly like an own bid — no better, no worse.
cases.setup: As API-EVDCMP-001 after QA vendor 1's bid.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, enter a higher price on QA vendor 3's behalf. 2. Open the comparison.
cases.expected: The surrogate bid is accepted; QA vendor 1 still leads; L1 unchanged.
cases.oracle: `POST /bids/template_input` 200; indicators and l1_prices as in API-EVDCMP-001.

cases.section: RFQ with four vendors — the buyer's view after every move
cases.title: A rebid below the leader takes the lead, and the old bid stops counting
cases.why: Rebidding is how competition works; the comparison must follow the newest bid of each vendor, not its old one.
cases.setup: As API-EVDCMP-003.
cases.steps: 1. QA vendor 2 rebids below QA vendor 1. 2. Open the comparison.
cases.expected: QA vendor 2 is now the only best bidder; L1 = its new price.
cases.oracle: As API-EVDCMP-001; QA vendor 2's earlier bid is "revised" and no longer ranked.

cases.section: RFQ with four vendors — the buyer's view after every move
cases.title: A tie at the best price on an RFQ: both vendors are shown as best
cases.why: Two equal lowest quotes are both L1; marking only one (or neither) misleads the award.
cases.setup: As API-EVDCMP-004.
cases.steps: 1. QA vendor 1 rebids exactly QA vendor 2's price. 2. Open the comparison.
cases.expected: Accepted (ties are allowed on RFQs); both QA vendors 1 and 2 are marked best bidder; L1 = the tied price.
cases.oracle: Both `best_bidder: true`; l1_prices = tied price. The tie rule (98) applies only to non-RFQ rounds with `is_tie_bid_allowed` false.

cases.section: RFQ with four vendors — the buyer's view after every move
cases.title: A vendor bids itself after the buyer bid on its behalf: one live bid, at the vendor's price
cases.why: The surrogate and the vendor's own portal are two doors to the same bid; two live bids for one vendor would double-count it in ranking and award.
cases.setup: As API-EVDCMP-003 (the buyer placed QA vendor 3's surrogate bid).
cases.steps: 1. QA vendor 3 signs in and bids a slightly lower price itself. 2. Count QA vendor 3's live bids.
cases.expected: Either the vendor's bid is accepted as a revision of the surrogate bid, or it is refused; in both cases QA vendor 3 has exactly one live bid, at its latest accepted price.
cases.oracle: `PATCH /v1/bids/:id` 200 or 422 96/99; `SELECT count(*) FROM bids … status IN (active, selected, requested)` = 1 for the vendor.

cases.section: Auction with three vendors — what each vendor sees of its own rank
cases.title: In a rank auction every vendor sees its own current rank after each move
cases.why: The rank is the only signal a vendor gets in a rank auction; a stale or wrong rank stops the price falling.
cases.setup: A fresh rank auction (best price not shown), one line, QA vendors 1–3.
cases.steps: 1. Vendors bid; read each vendor's own view. 2. After late rebids (see events-deep3-aux.md) read each view again.
cases.expected: Each vendor's rank matches the order of the latest prices (lowest = 1).
cases.oracle: The vendor's `GET /trade/:id` carries its rank; compared with the order of submitted prices.

cases.section: RFQ with four vendors — the buyer's view after every move
cases.title: Two lines: each line's best bidder and L1 price are worked out per line
cases.why: On multi-line events a vendor can be cheapest on one line and dearest on another; a per-event ranking would award the wrong lines.
cases.setup: A fresh RFQ with two lines; QA vendor 1 cheapest on line 1, QA vendor 2 cheapest on line 2, QA vendor 3 never cheapest.
cases.steps: 1. All three bid. 2. Open the comparison for each line.
cases.expected: Line 1: QA vendor 1 best, L1 = its line-1 price. Line 2: QA vendor 2 best, L1 = its line-2 price.
cases.oracle: indicators `inline.<line>` per line; `l1_prices.line_item_based.<line>.price` per line.

cases.title: While others bid, a vendor's views carry nothing of them
cases.why: If a vendor can read a competitor's price it can undercut by one rupee; the event is no longer competitive and the buyer is exposed.
cases.setup: A fresh live RFQ with four QA vendors. Checked twice: before QA vendor 2 has bid (QA vendor 1 has), and after QA vendor 2 took the lead (QA vendor 1 reads).
cases.steps: 1. As the reading vendor, open the round, its page data and the event. 2. Search every reply for the other vendors' names, company ids, prices and totals.
cases.expected: Nothing of any other vendor appears.
cases.oracle: Zero hits across the three replies; the run lists each hit's field path in Details.

cases.title: A vendor cannot open another vendor's quote by its id
cases.why: Bid ids travel in URLs and notifications; knowing one must not be enough to read it.
cases.setup: As API-EVDLEK-001 after QA vendor 2 has bid; checked from QA vendor 4 (never bid) and QA vendor 1 (bid).
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, ask for QA vendor 2's quote by QA vendor 2's bid id.
cases.expected: Refused: "Bid not found" — no price, no name.
cases.oracle: `GET /v1/trade/:id/quote_details/:other_bid` → HTTP 422 code 32.

cases.title: A bid the buyer placed on a vendor's behalf is as hidden as an own bid
cases.why: Surrogate bids are written by the buyer's staff; a different code path must not mean weaker hiding.
cases.setup: As API-EVDLEK-001; the buyer has just placed QA vendor 3's surrogate bid.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 1, open the round, its page data and the event and search for QA vendor 3.
cases.expected: Nothing of QA vendor 3 appears.
cases.oracle: Zero hits.

cases.title: In a rank auction vendors see their rank, never a competitor's price or name
cases.why: A rank auction shows position only; a price visible in the reply turns it into an open-book auction.
cases.setup: A fresh rank auction (English-auction mode off, best price not configured), QA vendors 1–3; checked during bidding (QA vendor 3) and after the late bids (QA vendor 2).
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, open the three views and search for the others.
cases.expected: Nothing of any other vendor; if the round shows the best price by configuration, only that one figure may appear.
cases.oracle: Zero hits (a best-price figure is tolerated only when the round's config says best price is shown).

cases.title: A vendor that lost (or won only a share) does not see who else won or at what price
cases.why: Award details are commercially confidential; leaking them sets the floor of the next negotiation.
cases.setup: The S1 award is final (split between QA vendors 1, 2 and 3); QA vendor 4 never bid.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 4, and as QA vendor 3, open the three views and search for the other vendors.
cases.expected: Nothing of the others.
cases.oracle: Zero hits.

cases.title: A winning vendor sees its own award, not its co-winners'
cases.why: Split awards put competitors side by side on one line; each must see only its own share.
cases.setup: As API-EVDLEK-005.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 2, and as QA vendor 3, open the three views and search for the other vendors.
cases.expected: Nothing of the other vendors.
cases.oracle: Zero hits.

cases.title: An invited vendor that has not bid sees nothing of the vendors that have
cases.why: A late joiner who could read the field would bid last with full knowledge.
cases.setup: As API-EVDLEK-001 after three vendors have bid; QA vendor 4 has not.
cases.steps: 1. As QA vendor 4, open the three views and search for the other three.
cases.expected: Nothing of the others.
cases.oracle: Zero hits.

cases.section: What a vendor receives about competitors
cases.title: A vendor must not receive other vendors' individual price limits
cases.why: Vendor-specific ceiling and floor prices are the buyer's negotiating position per supplier; each vendor seeing every other vendor's limit tells it exactly how far a competitor is allowed to go.
cases.setup: Price round with vendor-specific ceiling prices for two vendors (QA vendor: 120, vendor B: 105) on line 1.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor, open the price round (the bidding screen) and read the line details it receives.
cases.expected: The vendor's view carries its own ceiling (120) at most; vendor B's limit appears nowhere.
cases.oracle: In the vendor's stage payload, `trade_products[].validations` must not contain `vendor_validations` keyed by B's company id. Today the raw `validations` column is serialized to every caller.

cases.section: What a vendor receives about competitors
cases.title: A vendor asking the live page for "L1 prices" gets nothing
cases.why: The buyer console asks the live page for the lowest price per line; the same request from a vendor must not return the competitor's L1 price and total, whatever the sealed-bid, masking or best-price settings say.
cases.setup: Sealed-bid price round; vendor B has bid 95 on line 1; the QA vendor has bid 100.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor, open the live event the way the console does, asking for L1 prices.
cases.expected: No L1 prices in the vendor's view.
cases.oracle: Vendor `GET /v1/trade/:id/schema?l1_prices=1` → no `l1_prices` (or empty); today `get_l1_prices_for_event` runs for any caller when the param is present (`v1/trade_controller.rb:439`) and returns B's 95.

cases.section: What a vendor receives about competitors
cases.title: Who else bid and their bid status stay hidden from a vendor (known defect BUG-63, the bid-count angle)
cases.why: The live page's participant list is built from every bid; besides names it carries each competitor's status and revision count.
cases.setup: Price round, vendor B bid twice (one revision), the QA vendor bid once.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor, open the live event.
cases.expected: The participant list holds only the QA vendor's own bid.
cases.oracle: Vendor `schema` → `participants_data` has no layer for B (no B name, bid id, status or `bid_count`). Rank is set on layers only for the buyer company (`v1/trade_controller.rb:352-361`). Today all layers are returned (BUG-63).

cases.title: A vendor does not receive the dutch auction's stop price
cases.why: The end price is where the price ladder stops; a vendor knowing it simply waits for it.
cases.setup: Dutch auction on an eRFx project, start 1,000, end price 700, step 50; QA vendor invited.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor, open the auction during a round.
cases.expected: The current round price is shown; the end price (700) is not in the vendor's view.
cases.oracle: Vendor stage payload round block: `end_price` absent. Today `end_price` is sent to everyone (`trade_template_serializer.rb:474, 1035`).

cases.section: The vendor's event card and its own bid row
cases.title: On a price round a vendor never learns its own rank
cases.why: Price rounds (RFQs) never show ranks to vendors; the vendor's own bid row is gated only by sealed-bid, so a lot-closing RFQ bid row can carry the vendor's rank.
cases.setup: RFQ closed on lot (not sealed), vendor B 95, QA vendor 100.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor, open its bid on the price round.
cases.expected: No rank in the vendor's own bid row.
cases.oracle: Vendor bid row `data.rank` is nil; today `bid.get_rank` is filled whenever the stage closes on lot and is not sealed (`bid_template_serializer.rb:25-35`), while the card and NewBidSerializer check `should_show_rank?`.

cases.section: The vendor's event card and its own bid row
cases.title: The best price on a vendor card respects sealed bids, masking and the stage's best-price switch
cases.why: The card is a second place the best price appears; each switch that hides it on the live page must hide it here too.
cases.setup: Three auctions: sealed-bid; masked (closed-envelope); best-price indicator off. Vendor B bid 95, QA vendor 100 in each.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor read the card's best price on each.
cases.expected: No best price on any of the three.
cases.oracle: Card `best_price` nil on sealed (`card_serializer.rb:317-318`); `best_price_v1` nil when sealed, masked for the caller, or `other_auction_indicators_config.best_price` not true (`:477-480`).

cases.section: The project page a vendor opens
cases.title: A vendor opening the project page receives no award proposals
cases.why: Users without teams default to the "purchase" mode, and vendor users have no teams — so the project page hands vendors the award proposals with L1 / non-L1 totals and the note for approval.
cases.setup: Project with an award proposal submitted; the QA vendor invited (and bid).
cases.steps: As the QA vendor, open the project page.
cases.expected: No proposals in the vendor's view.
cases.oracle: Vendor `GET /event_groups/:id` → `proposals` = []; today `get_proposals_for_user` returns [] only when `!is_purchaser?`, and `authorized_modes` = ["purchase"] for a user with no teams (`user.rb:570-574`).

cases.section: The project page a vendor opens
cases.title: A vendor opening a technical round's live page receives no technical proposals or results
cases.why: The same "purchaser" default reaches the technical round, where proposals carry the evaluation outcome.
cases.setup: Technical round evaluated, recommendation submitted; the QA vendor responded.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor, open the technical round.
cases.expected: No proposals, no evaluation results.
cases.oracle: Vendor `schema` on the RFP: no `proposals`, `show_evaluation_results` false (`v1/trade_controller.rb:384-385`).

cases.title: Bids well before the last minute do not move the end time
cases.why: An auction that extends on every bid never ends.
cases.setup: As API-EVDAUX-001, at the start.
cases.steps: 1. Three vendors bid in the first minute. 2. Read the end time.
cases.expected: Unchanged.
cases.oracle: `ending_at` unchanged (±2 s).

cases.title: Every vendor's bid takes the extended end time
cases.why: Each bid stores its own end time; a vendor whose bid still carries the old end may be shut out early.
cases.setup: As API-EVDAUX-001, right after the first extension.
cases.steps: 1. Read each vendor's live bid's end time.
cases.expected: All equal the new end time.
cases.oracle: `bids.end_time` (SELECT, own QA records) = new `ending_at` (±5 s).

cases.title: A late bid that does not reach the top rank does not extend
cases.why: With a rank limit of 1, only a fight for first place should keep the auction open.
cases.setup: As API-EVDAUX-003, before QA vendor 1's late bid: QA vendor 2 is behind.
cases.steps: 1. Inside the last minute, QA vendor 2 improves its price but stays behind the leader. 2. Read the end time.
cases.expected: Unchanged.
cases.oracle: `ending_at` unchanged (±2 s).

cases.title: A revision smaller than the tick size is refused, in either direction
cases.why: The tick size stops "one-paisa" undercutting; the code checks only the absolute change, so a tiny price INCREASE is refused for the same reason.
cases.setup: A live auction whose line has a tick size of ₹10; QA vendor 1 has bid ₹5,000.
cases.expected: Steps 1 and 2 refused "Quoted price difference must be greater than the tick size"; step 3 accepted.

cases.title: Without dynamic closing, a last-minute new leader still adds 3 minutes when the round allows it
cases.why: The older extension path (`update_trade_end_time`) is the default for many auctions.
cases.setup: A rank auction without dynamic closing, whose round extends the end time on a last-minute new leader (rank limit 1).
cases.steps: 1. In the last minute a vendor takes rank 1. 2. Read the end time.
cases.expected: +3 minutes; never on an RFQ.
cases.oracle: `ending_at` + 180 s.

cases.title: Dynamic closing without an extension value does not break the bid
cases.why: Code reading: a blank `time_extension_value` makes the extension multiply nil — the late bid may fail or the extension silently not happen.
cases.setup: A rank auction with dynamic closing on and the extension minutes left blank.
cases.steps: 1. Bid in the last minute and take the lead. 2. Read the bid and the end time.
cases.expected: The bid is accepted and the auction extends by the documented default (3 minutes).
cases.oracle: Bid 200; `ending_at` + 180 s. A 500 or no extension is a defect.

cases.section: RFQ with four vendors — the buyer's view after every move
cases.title: A third, higher own bid leaves the leader unchanged
cases.why: Proves the ranking reads every bid, not only the latest one.
cases.setup: As API-EVDCMP-002.
cases.steps: 1. QA vendor 2 bids above both. 2. Open the comparison.
cases.expected: QA vendor 1 still the only best bidder; L1 unchanged.
cases.oracle: As API-EVDCMP-001.

cases.section: RFQ with four vendors — the buyer's view after every move
cases.title: A vendor that never bids is never shown as a bidder
cases.why: An invited vendor without a quote must not appear as best or ranked.
cases.setup: As API-EVDCMP-005; QA vendor 4 invited, no bid.
cases.steps: 1. Open the comparison.
cases.expected: QA vendor 4 is not marked best (absent or "not best").
cases.oracle: `auction_identifiers_data` has no best_bidder true for QA vendor 4.

cases.section: Auction with three vendors — what each vendor sees of its own rank
cases.title: Matching the best price in an auction is allowed unless the round forbids ties
cases.why: Whether ties are allowed decides whether a vendor may simply match the leader.
cases.setup: As API-EVDCMP-008, QA vendor 1 already bid.
cases.steps: 1. QA vendor 2 bids exactly QA vendor 1's price.
cases.expected: Accepted when ties are allowed (the default); refused "A bid at this price already exists" when the round forbids tie bids.
cases.oracle: `PATCH /v1/bids/:id` 200, or 422 code 98.

cases.section: Competition rules the runner does not cover
cases.title: In the last five minutes a vendor cannot raise its price on a single-line round
cases.why: Late price increases are a classic way to game the close.
cases.setup: A live single-line round within 5 minutes of its bid end; QA vendor 1 has bid.
cases.steps: 1. QA vendor 1 rebids higher.
cases.expected: Refused "You cannot increase the price"; a lower rebid is accepted.

cases.section: Competition rules the runner does not cover
cases.title: A rejected leader's bid stops counting and the next vendor becomes best
cases.why: After a rejection the comparison must promote the next best bid, or the buyer awards a rejected price.
cases.setup: Three vendors bid; the buyer rejects the leader's bid (round 2 owns the reject action itself).
cases.steps: 1. Reject the leader. 2. Open the comparison.
cases.expected: The second-lowest vendor is now best; L1 = its price.
cases.oracle: indicators/l1_prices; `app/models/concerns/bid_concern.rb format_tp_vs_latest_btps` uses the vendor's previous active bid when the latest is rejected.

cases.section: What a vendor receives about competitors
cases.title: Weightages and currency preferences do not name the other vendors
cases.why: In a weighted event the per-vendor weight (the buyer's loading on each supplier) and each supplier's chosen currency are keyed by company; sent to every viewer they reveal the field and the buyer's preferences.
cases.setup: Weighted RFQ with per-vendor weights for the QA vendor and vendor B; multi-currency with B quoting in USD.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor, open the price round.
cases.expected: The vendor's view has its own weight and currency only.
cases.oracle: Vendor stage payload `weightages` and `currency_preferences` contain only the QA vendor's company uuid; today every participant's uuid and value.

cases.section: What a vendor receives about competitors
cases.title: The stage configuration sent to a vendor does not list which other vendors were asked for a best offer
cases.why: The best-offer request names the invited companies inside the stage config; a vendor reading it learns who is still in contention.
cases.setup: Closed RFQ in evaluation; buyer requests a best offer from vendor B only.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor (not invited to the best offer), open the stage.
cases.expected: No list of invited companies; the request text (remarks) is empty for the QA vendor.
cases.oracle: Vendor stage payload `trade_config.allowed_participants_to_edit_in_bid_review_time.request_for_best_price` absent or without B's id; `remarks` = "" because the vendor is not listed (`can_show_remarks`).

cases.section: What a vendor receives about competitors
cases.title: Only the buyer receives the stage's internal "misc" data
cases.why: The stage's misc block holds precomputed bids, savings and the rebid block list; it is buyer-only on the stage serializer.
cases.setup: Price round with two bids and savings configured.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, read the stage. 2. As the QA vendor, read the same stage.
cases.expected: Buyer: misc present. Vendor: no misc.
cases.oracle: `misc` non-null for the buyer company, null for the vendor (`trade_serializer.rb:109-114`); on update-vendor stages the fallback must not hand the full misc to a non-buyer (`merge_vendor_update_misc`, gap).

cases.title: A vendor knocked out of a round does not keep receiving the current round
cases.why: The participation check intersects two id lists and treats the (always truthy) array as "yes", so knocked-out vendors keep seeing round times and prices.
cases.setup: Knockout auction, round 1 accepted by vendor B only; the QA vendor did not accept and is out.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor, open the auction during round 2.
cases.expected: No round-2 times or latest bulk price for the QA vendor.
cases.oracle: Vendor payload has no current-round block; today `round_participant_ids & participant_ids` (an Array) is truthy (`trade_template_serializer.rb:1072-1074`).

cases.title: Remaining quantity is hidden from vendors unless the stage allows it; the price trail is buyer-only
cases.why: Remaining quantity tells vendors how much is left to win; the bulk-price trail shows the buyer's whole ladder.
cases.setup: Knockout auction with "show remaining quantity to sellers" off.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, open the auction. 2. As the QA vendor, open it. 3. Turn the setting on and repeat step 2.
cases.expected: Buyer: remaining quantity and the full price trail. Vendor: no remaining quantity and no trail; after step 3 the vendor sees remaining quantity but still no trail.
cases.oracle: `remaining_quantity` nil for the vendor unless `show_remaining_quantity_to_sellers`; `event_bulk_price_trail` only in the buyer payload.

cases.section: The vendor's event card and its own bid row
cases.title: Vendor card rank and colour only while the auction runs, never on a sealed stage
cases.why: Ranks shown before the start or after the end, or on sealed stages, break the auction's rules.
cases.setup: Rank auction closed on lot, two vendors bid; a second auction with sealed bids.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor read its card rank before start, during, and after end on the open auction, and during the sealed one.
cases.expected: Rank only during the open auction (and only once the vendor has done the revisions the stage requires); nothing on the sealed one; traffic colour likewise.
cases.oracle: Card `rank` / `traffic_signal_color` nil outside auctioning and on sealed stages (`card_serializer.rb:636-675`).

cases.section: The vendor's event card and its own bid row
cases.title: The bid count shown to a vendor follows the stage setting and the "more than three" rule
cases.why: "4 vendors have bid" is competitive pressure the buyer may want off; with few bids it identifies competitors.
cases.setup: Price auction with "vendors may see the bid count" on, then off; first with 3 bids, then with 4 (the QA vendor among them). Also an RFQ with 5 bids.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor read the card's bid count in each state.
cases.expected: Setting on: hidden at 3, "4" at 4. Setting off: hidden. RFQ: hidden for a vendor. Knockout: hidden.
cases.oracle: Card `bid_count`: nil when `is_vendor_allowed_to_view_bid_count` false, RFQ + category seller, knockout + not buyer, or `bids_count <= 3`; shown above 3 only if the vendor has its own bid. Brokers on an RFQ are not blocked by the seller check (gap).

cases.section: The vendor's event card and its own bid row
cases.title: Until award notifications are on, a vendor sees "active" and "bid placed" instead of "closed" and "accepted"
cases.why: Telling the losing vendors early, or the winner before the PO, is the buyer's choice (gate: `select_bid_notification`).
cases.setup: RFQ, two vendors, stage closed and the QA vendor's bid awarded; setting off, then on.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor read the card status, the card stamp and its bid status.
cases.expected: Off: status "active", stamp "bid placed", bid status "active". On: "closed", "bid accepted", "selected".
cases.oracle: Card status (`card_serializer.rb:374-378`), stamp (`:446-458`), bid row status (`bid_template_serializer.rb:365`).

cases.section: The vendor's event card and its own bid row
cases.title: The buyer's award remark is not shown to the vendor
cases.why: The selection remark is written for the approvers ("cheapest after negotiation, B refused terms"); it is serialized into the awarded vendor's own bid row.
cases.setup: RFQ awarded to the QA vendor with a selection remark naming another vendor.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor open its bid.
cases.expected: No buyer selection remark in the vendor's view.
cases.oracle: Vendor bid row has no `selection_remark`; today it is set for any selected bid (`bid_template_serializer.rb:231, 380`).

cases.section: The project page a vendor opens
cases.title: The project page keeps the buyer's notes and history away from vendors
cases.why: Clara's summary, the ownership trail, last-purchase-order refresh data and amendment remarks are buyer working notes.
cases.setup: Project amended once with a remark, ownership transferred, last-PO data refreshed.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor open the project page.
cases.expected: None of those in the vendor's view; stage owner name only for the buyer.
cases.oracle: Vendor project show lacks `clara_summary`, `owner_trail`, `lpo_refresh_data`, `amendment_remarks` (today sent unconditionally, `show_serializer.rb:242-244, 290-331`); stage `owner` empty for the vendor (`:107-110`).

cases.section: The project page a vendor opens
cases.title: Line items: last purchase price is buyer-only; PR creator details and quantities are hidden from vendors and brokers when configured
cases.why: The last PO price is the buyer's benchmark; PR creator contacts let a vendor bypass procurement.
cases.setup: Project lines with last-PO data; gate: `mask_pr_creator_details_for_vendor` on and quantity widgets disabled.
cases.steps: Read the project's line items as the buyer, as the QA vendor, and (if available) as a broker user.
cases.expected: Buyer: all fields. Vendor and broker: no last-PO fields, no PR creator name/phone/email, no quantity.
cases.oracle: `get_line_items`: `last_po_*` only when `is_client_side`; creator and quantity masking today checks category "seller" only, so a broker still receives them (gap).

cases.title: With vendor masking, buyer users see aliases and no vendor contact details
cases.why: Masking lets a buyer team evaluate without knowing who quoted; the real name or the bidder's phone in any one field defeats it.
cases.setup: gate: vendor masking on; RFQ live, two vendors bid; a buyer user without the unmask right.
cases.steps: As that buyer read the bids list, the rejected bids, bidder remarks and a single bid.
cases.expected: Aliases everywhere; no bidder phone or email.
cases.oracle: Bid rows show `other_details.company_name` alias; `user.phone`/`email` absent (`bid_template_serializer.rb:211-213`). Surrogate/buyer-added remarks show the buyer company (`bidder_remarks_serializer.rb:11-15`).

cases.section: Bid details, suspicious bids and other buyer reads
cases.title: Reading one vendor's bid details: only the stage owner (or a super admin)
cases.why: The policy for this read always says yes; the only guard is "owner or super admin" in the action itself.
cases.setup: Live price round owned by buyer user A; a colleague B in the same company, not the owner.
cases.steps: As B, ask for the QA vendor's bid details on the round.
cases.expected: Refused: "You are not allowed to perform this action".
cases.oracle: `GET /bids/get_bid_details?…` → HTTP 422, code 101 (`bids_controller.rb:367-369`). A super admin of ANOTHER company passes this check (gap, `R-VIS-016-4`).

cases.section: Bid details, suspicious bids and other buyer reads
cases.title: Bid details for a vendor with no bid is a "bid not found", not a crash
cases.why: Opening a vendor's row before it bids is ordinary; the action dereferences the missing bid and fails with an untyped error.
cases.setup: Session: the BUYER (owner of the sandbox). The sandbox price round is live with no bids.
cases.steps: Ask for the QA vendor's bid details on the round.
cases.expected: Refused as "Bid not found".
cases.oracle: HTTP 422, code 32 'Bid not found'. Today `bid` is nil and `bid.errors` (line 385) or `bid.id` (line 378) raises → HTTP 500.

cases.section: Bid details, suspicious bids and other buyer reads
cases.title: Suspicious-bid details are refused unless the stage turns the indicator on, and never name masked vendors
cases.why: The list maps IP addresses to vendor names; it must exist only where the buyer enabled it and must respect masking.
cases.setup: Sandbox price round (indicator off by default); a second stage with the suspicious-bid indicator on (gate: `is_suspicious_bid_indicator_enabled`) and two vendors bidding from one IP.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer ask for the sandbox round's suspicious bids. 2. Ask for the second stage's. 3. Ask for a stage id that does not exist.
cases.expected: 1: refused "You are not allowed to perform this action". 2: one entry, the IP's location and both vendor names (aliases if masking applies). 3: "Trade Request not found".
cases.oracle: 1: HTTP 422 code 101 (`show_suspicious_bids?` false). 2: `[{ip, location, vendors:[…]}]`. 3: HTTP 422 code 95.

cases.section: Bid details, suspicious bids and other buyer reads
cases.title: Creating an event needs the create permission and sourcing access
cases.why: A vendor-management-only user (onboarding team) must not be able to start sourcing events.
cases.setup: A buyer user whose only team is vendor management (no create permission on trades).
cases.steps: As that user try to add a stage to a draft project.
cases.expected: Refused "not allowed".
cases.oracle: HTTP 422, code 455 from `TradeRequestPolicy#create?` (`trade_request_policy.rb:13-16`); `has_access_for_sourcing_events?` false only when vendor management is the user's only mode.

cases.section: Bid details, suspicious bids and other buyer reads
cases.title: A buyer working for several client companies sees only the company chosen at login
cases.why: Multi-company buyers pick a client company; everything they read must be boxed to it.
cases.setup: A buyer mapped to two client companies; logs in choosing company 1; an event exists in company 2.
cases.steps: Open company 2's event by its link.
cases.expected: Not visible.
cases.oracle: Read refused (455/536 per endpoint) because `allowed_companies` = [company 1] (`company.rb:466-468`).

cases.section: Bid details, suspicious bids and other buyer reads
cases.title: A vendor's list of auctions it took part in opens even when one of them is a sealed-bid lot auction
cases.why: The serializer for that list is given no "allowed companies", so on a sealed lot stage it fails and the vendor's whole history list breaks.
cases.setup: The QA vendor has bid in a sealed-bid auction closed on lot (any status).
cases.steps: As the QA vendor (mobile app version that uses the new list, or the website) open "participated auctions".
cases.expected: The list opens; that auction shows without rank.
cases.oracle: `GET /v1/trade/get_participated_auctions` → HTTP 200; today `nil.exclude?` in `BidTemplateSerializer#get_data` → HTTP 500 (`participated_events_serializer.rb:52`, `bid_template_serializer.rb:26`).

cases.title: After an extension the buyer can switch the auction to sealed bids
cases.why: Sealed bids end the sniping war; the switch is offered only once an extension happened.
cases.setup: As API-EVDAUX-001 after the first extension.
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, switch on sealed bids. 2. Read the auction.
cases.expected: Sealed bidding starts with its own extension time; dynamic closing switches off.
cases.oracle: `PATCH /trade/:id` with `other_auction_indicators_config.is_sealbid_enabled`; `sealbid_enabled` true.

cases.section: Auction with three vendors — what each vendor sees of its own rank
cases.title: A tie at the best price in an auction: both tied vendors are told rank 2
cases.why: Today a vendor sharing the lowest price is told it is second; it may cut its price for nothing, or stop bidding believing it cannot win.
cases.setup: As API-EVDCMP-008; QA vendors 1 and 2 bid the same price, QA vendor 3 higher.
cases.steps: 1. Read each vendor's own rank.
cases.expected: QA vendors 1 and 2 see rank 2, QA vendor 3 sees rank 3 — the dense ranking shifts every rank when the best is shared. Product decision needed: tied leaders arguably should see rank 1 ("joint first").
cases.oracle: Vendor views as in API-EVDCMP-008.

cases.title: Bidder remarks and rejected-bid lists are buyer-only
cases.why: Remarks often contain prices ("can do 4,700 if…").
cases.setup: Any live round with two vendors' remarks.
cases.steps: 1. Confirm that the vendor app is not allowed to call the bidder-remarks and rejected-bids reads.
cases.expected: Both are console-only in the app allow-list, so a vendor session cannot read them.
cases.oracle: `config/app_auth_config.yml` agribid_website has no `trade#bidder_remarks` / `rejected_bids`. Static check — never send these as a vendor (a 401 signs the vendor out).

cases.section: The vendor's event card and its own bid row
cases.title: "How far from best" on the vendor card is computed on the vendor's own total
cases.why: The percentage tells a vendor how much to drop; a wrong base misleads every revision.
cases.setup: Price auction with best price shown; best total 950, the QA vendor's total 1,000.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor read the card's difference from best.
cases.expected: 5.0 % (|950 − 1,000| × 100 ÷ 1,000, rounded to 2). When the vendor is best (difference 0) nothing is shown.
cases.oracle: Card `best_quote_difference` = "5.0%"; nil when 0, for knockout/dutch, and in brokerage workspaces.

cases.section: The vendor's event card and its own bid row
cases.title: A vendor's event card carries no buyer-internal fields
cases.why: The same card serializer serves vendors without an actor check; Clara's stuck reasons, the pending unregistered-bid count and scheduled-job status are internal.
cases.setup: Project with Clara auto-pilot stuck, one unregistered (email) bid pending, a scheduled publish job.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor list its events.
cases.expected: None of those fields in the vendor's card.
cases.oracle: Vendor project card lacks `clara_stuck_reasons`, `pending_unregistered_bids_count`, scheduled-job status (`event_group/card_serializer.rb:3-6, 26-44, 100-104`).

cases.title: "Bidding statistics only" hides the participant list from the buyer too
cases.why: The stats-only mode is meant to show counts, not who; an empty participant list is the observable promise.
cases.setup: gate: `show_bidding_stats_only`, on a live auction with two bids.
cases.steps: As the buyer open the stage and the live indicators.
cases.expected: Participants empty; live indicators empty.
cases.oracle: Stage payload `participants` = {} (`trade_template_serializer.rb:239-243`); `event_indicators` → {} (masked).

cases.section: Bid details, suspicious bids and other buyer reads
cases.title: Bid details without the vendor, or for a round that does not exist, are refused with a clear reason
cases.why: Positive control for the parameter checks before the owner check.
cases.setup: Session: the BUYER. The sandbox price round.
cases.steps: 1. Ask for bid details without the vendor's company. 2. Ask with a stage id that does not exist.
cases.expected: 1: "Insufficient parameters". 2: "Request not found".
cases.oracle: 1: HTTP 422 code 2. 2: HTTP 422 code 4 (`bids_controller.rb:362-366`).

cases.section: Bid details, suspicious bids and other buyer reads
cases.title: "Allowed to reopen" is not offered to vendors on a technical round
cases.why: The flag is true for every caller on an RFP; the screen may show vendors a reopen action the API should refuse.
cases.setup: Closed technical round; the QA vendor responded.
cases.steps: 1. As the QA vendor read the stage's reopen flag. 2. If the vendor app offers it, try to reopen.
cases.expected: Flag false for the vendor; any reopen attempt refused.
cases.oracle: Vendor stage `trade_config.is_allowed_to_reopen_event` false (today true, `trade_template_serializer.rb:808`); reopen as vendor → 401/422, never 200.

journeys.title: Every bid number is right
journeys.goal: Every figure Procol computes from bids — line totals, tax, charges, discounts, bid totals, ranks, L1, savings, precision, currency and the comparison report — matches an independent recalculation from what the vendors actually quoted, and no vendor ever sees another vendor's prices.

cases.title: A vendor who has not bid yet can open its card on a scored traffic-light auction
cases.why: The card's colour lookup reads the vendor's score without checking it exists; an invited vendor who has not bid yet would get an error page instead of the event.
cases.setup: Traffic-light auction on price (not on rank), ranges set; vendor A has bid, the QA vendor is invited but has NOT bid.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor, open the event list / the event card while it is live.
cases.expected: The card opens with no colour for the vendor.
cases.oracle: No 500 from the vendor's event list / card request. `LotBased#color` reads `participant_score['color']` on nil (`lot_based.rb:33-39`) — a 500 there is the defect.

cases.section: Loading factor in the different rank services
cases.title: With a loading factor, the vendor card rank and the buyer's live rank must agree
cases.why: The lot rank service applies the loading factor under a key that is not set yet, so it adds nothing; the live page applies it. A vendor can be told "you are L1" while the buyer's screen (and the award) ranks it second.
cases.setup: gate: `loading_factor_enabled`. Auction closed on lot, two lines, line 2 loading factor 15. Vendor A quotes 100 and regrets line 2 (loaded score 115); vendor B quotes 110 on both.
cases.steps: 1. Buyer: read the live ranks. 2. Vendor A: read the rank on its event card. 3. Vendor B: the same.
cases.expected: Everyone sees B rank 1 and A rank 2.
cases.oracle: Buyer `event_indicators` gives B "1"; today vendor A's card (`EventIndicators::LotBased#rank`) gives A 1 because `lot_based.rb:15` passes `ranking_key: @ranking_key` before `@ranking_key` is assigned on line 16. Any disagreement is the defect.

cases.section: Loading factor in the different rank services
cases.title: Auto award picks the vendor that is L1 on the buyer's screen (loading factor and buyer ranking included)
cases.why: Auto award ranks with the plain vendor score and the lot service without the loading factor; on an event with either, it can award the vendor the buyer's screen shows as second.
cases.setup: gate: `auto_award`. Lot-closed auction with auto award on and a loading factor as in API-EVRCAL-016 (or a buyer ranking widget as in API-EVRCAL-002). Let the stage close.
cases.steps: 1. Note L1 on the buyer's live page just before close. 2. After the auto award runs (a few seconds after close), read the award.
cases.expected: The vendor awarded is the one shown as L1 on the buyer's live page (B).
cases.oracle: Selected bid's company = B. Today `AutoAwardingService` uses `LotBased` with key `rank` (`auto_awarding_service.rb:32, 75`) — no loading factor, no buyer rank — and awards A.

cases.title: The default savings reference is the best FIRST quote, priced at the buyer's quantity
cases.why: The negotiation margin is "first best quote minus final"; if later revisions or the vendor's own quantity were used, the reported saving would be wrong.
cases.setup: RFQ, two lines: L1 buyer quantity 10, L2 buyer quantity 5; savings configuration with the default strategy, lot based. Vendor A first quotes L1 100 / L2 200 (total 2,000), then revises to 90 / 190 (1,850). Vendor B first quotes 95 / 210 (2,000), then revises to 92 / 205 (1,945). A quotes quantity 8 on L1 (the reference must still use 10).
cases.steps: Close the stage and read the stage savings.
cases.expected: Reference = min over vendors of (first bid Σ price × buyer quantity) = min(100×10+200×5, 95×10+210×5) = 2,000. Final best = 1,850. Saving = 150, i.e. 7.50 %.
cases.oracle: `GET /v1/trade/:id/aggregate_savings` (or the stage's `misc.savings_data`) default strategy: reference 2000, amount 150, percent 7.5. Only taxes-free base `price` is used.

cases.title: A vendor never receives savings data in its own quote or sheet
cases.why: Savings reveal the buyer's reference (budget, last price, the competitor's first quote); a vendor holding it knows how far it can move.
cases.setup: RFQ with savings configured (budget reference), the QA vendor has bid; stage closed and savings computed.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor, open its quote / the event page.
cases.expected: No savings figures anywhere in what the vendor receives.
cases.oracle: Vendor's quote/sheet payload has `show_savings_data: false` and no `savings_with_strategy` / `vendor_specific_savings` keys; the buyer's has them.

cases.title: On a sealed-bid stage the vendor gets no auction indicators, and the best price only after it has bid
cases.why: Sealed bidding exists so vendors bid blind; indicators or the best price before the vendor's own bid defeat it.
cases.setup: Sealed-bid auction; vendor A has bid; the QA vendor has not.
cases.steps: As the QA vendor open the live event before and after placing its bid.
cases.expected: Before and after: no ranks/colours (indicators hidden). The best price never appears before its own bid.
cases.oracle: Vendor payload `hide_auction_indicators: true` (sealbid); order-details best price absent until the vendor company has a bid.

cases.title: Freight on a single-product bid is per unit below 20 and a lump sum from 20
cases.why: The model guesses whether freight was typed per unit or as a total by its size; one paisa decides whether a bid's freight is 19.99 or 1,999 — enough to change L1.
cases.setup: Single-product price round (the one-line, non-sheet layout), buyer quantity 100. Vendor A quotes 50 per unit with freight 19.99; vendor B quotes 50 per unit with freight 20.
cases.steps: Submit both bids; read each bid's freight total and landed total on the comparison.
cases.expected: A: freight 19.99 × 100 = 1,999, landed 6,999. B: freight 20 (lump sum), landed 5,020 — B is L1 although it charges more freight per unit. The product should apply one documented rule (per unit or lump sum) whatever the amount.
cases.oracle: Bid `price_breakup_json.total_global_freight_charges` A = 1999.0, B = 20.0; `total_freight_charges` follows. Threshold `< 20.0` at `bid.rb:1026`.

cases.title: Award value per vendor = awarded quantity × that vendor's unit price
cases.why: The award proposal is what gets approved and ordered.
cases.setup: A split award (covered live by the round-3 deep-dig scenarios S1/S3).
cases.steps: Read the proposal values.
cases.expected: The calculator's `awardTotals()`.
cases.oracle: proposal_values vs awardTotals.

cases.title: A bid's total is the same in every place on a charges template
cases.why: The comparison, the quote view and the bid record must not disagree once charges are involved.
cases.setup: S2 bids.
cases.steps: Read the total from the stage, the quote details and the bid record (gross total, landed amount, rank price).
cases.expected: One figure everywhere.
cases.oracle: INV-SAME.

cases.title: A discount above 100 % cannot make a bid total negative
cases.why: A negative total would rank as the best bid. The percentage widget is free text on the vendor side.
cases.setup: S2 stage with a fourth QA vendor invited.
cases.steps: Vendor 4 submits a 150 % discount.
cases.expected: Refused; or, if accepted, the total is never negative and never ranks best.
cases.oracle: PROBE-NEG.

cases.title: A vendor's own views carry no competitor's prices or company ids
cases.why: On a sealed RFQ a vendor who sees rivals' prices can undercut by a rupee; this breaks the tender.
cases.setup: Three QA vendors bid on a fresh RFQ.
cases.steps: Each vendor reads the stage and its page data through its own app.
cases.expected: Nothing of another vendor: no name, company id, unit price, line total or bid total.
cases.oracle: INV-ISOLATION.

cases.title: Isolation holds on a charges template
cases.why: Same as EVI-ISO-001, with bid-level charges also private.
cases.steps: As EVI-ISO-001.
cases.expected: Nothing of another vendor.
cases.oracle: INV-ISOLATION.

cases.title: Isolation in a rank auction (only the vendor's own rank)
cases.why: Rank auctions may show rank, never prices.
cases.steps: As EVI-ISO-001.
cases.expected: Own rank only.
cases.oracle: INV-ISOLATION.

cases.section: Line figures — what each quoted line is worth
cases.title: A quote is stored exactly as the vendor entered it
cases.why: Every later figure is built on the stored price, quantity and tax rate. If one digit changes on the way in, every total, rank and saving after it is wrong.
cases.setup: A fresh RFQ on the default buy template with QA vendors invited; the vendor's quote has fractional quantities, a 4-place price and different GST rates per line.
cases.steps: 1. The vendor opens a bid, prices every line and submits. 2. The buyer opens the comparison.
cases.expected: Every unit price, quantity and GST rate on the comparison reads back exactly as entered (only formatting may differ, e.g. "18" vs "18.0").
cases.oracle: INV-ECHO: stored values equal the submitted ones as exact decimals.

cases.section: Line figures — what each quoted line is worth
cases.title: Line total = unit price × quantity, plus GST on it
cases.why: The line total is what the buyer compares and later pays; it must follow the template's formula to the paisa.
cases.setup: Default buy template: line total = price × quantity + price × quantity × GST / 100.
cases.steps: 1. A vendor quotes ₹123.4567/KG for 7.5 KG at 18 % GST. 2. Read the bid's line totals.
cases.expected: 123.4567 × 7.5 × 1.18 = ₹1,092.5918 (to the company's places), on the bid record and in the comparison.
cases.oracle: INV-LINE: `bid_products[].price_breakup.total_landed_amount` equals the calculator's value within one unit of the last place.

cases.section: Line figures — what each quoted line is worth
cases.title: Fractional and very large quantities do not lose precision
cases.why: Bulk buys (250,000 KG; 999,999.999 KG) and fractional ones (0.5 KG) are where float drift and rounding show up first.
cases.steps: Quote each line and read the line totals and the bid total.
cases.expected: Each total equals the exact product of price, quantity and (1 + GST) to the shown places; nothing is truncated or turned into scientific notation.
cases.oracle: INV-LINE, INV-BID.

cases.section: Line figures — what each quoted line is worth
cases.title: A ₹0 unit price is not a quote and never becomes L1
cases.why: A zero left in a cell must not make a vendor the cheapest bidder or create a free order line.
cases.setup: Two vendors; vendor 1 enters ₹0 on line 1.
cases.steps: 1. Vendor 1 submits with ₹0 on line 1. 2. Read L1 on line 1.
cases.expected: Either the bid is refused, or line 1 is left unquoted for vendor 1; L1 on line 1 is the other vendor's ₹50.
cases.oracle: PROBE-ZERO: no `l1_prices` entry with price 0.

cases.title: L1 price per line is the lowest unit price
cases.why: L1 drives award recommendations and savings.
cases.setup: Three vendors, five lines.
cases.steps: Read L1 prices per line.
cases.expected: The lowest unit price among live bids, with that bid's line total.
cases.oracle: INV-L1.

cases.title: Best bid total and ranks on a charges template use the full total
cases.why: With discounts and charges the cheapest goods value may not be the cheapest bid.
cases.setup: S2 bids.
cases.steps: Read the best bid total and ranks.
cases.expected: The lowest calculated total (after discount, charges and tax).
cases.oracle: INV-BEST, INV-RANK.

cases.title: Rank auction: overall ranks on the bid total
cases.why: In a rank auction the rank IS what vendors bid against.
cases.setup: A rank auction with three vendors at ₹101.25, ₹99.50, ₹100 per unit.
cases.steps: Read the buyer's ranks and best total.
cases.expected: 99.50 → 1, 100 → 2, 101.25 → 3; best total = vendor 2's total.
cases.oracle: INV-RANK, INV-BEST.

cases.title: Each vendor sees its own correct rank in a rank auction
cases.why: A vendor shown the wrong rank bids against a phantom.
cases.setup: As EVI-RANK-009.
cases.steps: Each vendor reads the stage.
cases.expected: Its own rank by the same rule.
cases.oracle: VENDOR-RANK.

cases.title: The comparison report (Excel) shows the same figures as the screen
cases.why: Buyers forward the Excel to approvers; it must match the screen.
cases.setup: S1 bids.
