cases.steps: Download the RFQ comparison report and read each vendor's block.
cases.expected: Each vendor's unit prices, line totals and bid total are present.
cases.oracle: INV-REPORT.

cases.title: Line savings = reference − best unit price
cases.why: Savings are reported to management; each line's must be exact.
cases.setup: PROCOL DEMO fills a last-purchase-price reference per line.
cases.steps: Read best line-wise savings and each quote's savings.
cases.expected: Reference − unit price per unit (shown truncated to 4 places), % = amount ÷ reference × 100 (2 places).
cases.oracle: INV-SAV-LINE.

cases.title: Total savings = Σ line savings × quantity over Σ reference × quantity
cases.why: The savings card is the headline number for the event.
cases.setup: As EVI-SAV-001.
cases.steps: Read aggregate savings.
cases.expected: The calculator's amount, reference and % (2 places).
cases.oracle: INV-SAV-AGG.

cases.title: Every GST slab (0, 5, 12, 18, 28 %) is applied to the right line
cases.why: Mixed-tax RFQs are normal; a slab applied to the wrong line or a 0 % read as blank changes the comparison.
cases.setup: Lines quoted at 0, 5, 12, 18 and 28 % across three vendors.
cases.steps: Read every line total.
cases.expected: Each line total = price × quantity × (1 + its own GST / 100).
cases.oracle: INV-LINE.

cases.title: Tax charged on the bid total after discount and charges
cases.why: Many templates tax the sub total (after discount, including freight); taxing the wrong base over- or under-states every bid.
cases.setup: A stage whose bid-level formulas are: discount = Σ lines × discount %; sub total = Σ lines − discount + freight + other charges; tax = sub total × tax %; total = sub total + tax.
cases.steps: Three vendors bid with different discount, freight, other charges and tax (12, 18, 28 %).
cases.expected: Discount, sub total, tax and total equal the calculator's values for each vendor.
cases.oracle: INV-BID on every bid-level formula.

cases.title: Bid total = the template's total formula over the lines
cases.why: The bid total is what the buyer ranks on (ranking widget "gross total").
cases.setup: Default template: total = Σ line totals.
cases.steps: Read each vendor's total on the comparison.
cases.expected: The calculator's total to the shown places.
cases.oracle: INV-BID.

cases.title: The bid total is the same on the comparison, the quote and the bid record
cases.why: A buyer who opens a quote must see the same total as on the comparison.
cases.setup: Any bids.
cases.steps: Read the total from six places.
cases.expected: One figure.
cases.oracle: INV-SAME.

cases.title: A vendor's app that sends wrong totals cannot change the figures
cases.why: The vendor's browser computes totals and sends them. If the server trusted them, a vendor could claim ₹1 and rank first.
cases.setup: A fresh RFQ; vendor 1's request carries ₹1 as every line total and as the bid total, with real prices and quantities.
cases.steps: 1. Vendor 1 submits. 2. The buyer reads the totals.
cases.expected: Every total is recomputed from price and quantity; ₹1 appears nowhere.
cases.oracle: INV-LINE, INV-BID, INV-SAME on the tampered bid.

cases.title: Wrong totals sent by a vendor cannot make it L1
cases.why: Follows EVI-TOT-006: the ranking must use the recomputed total.
cases.setup: As EVI-TOT-006; vendor 2 is cheaper.
cases.steps: Read best bidder, L1 and best total.
cases.expected: Vendor 2 is best; the best total is vendor 2's recomputed total.
cases.oracle: INV-BEST, INV-L1.

cases.section: Which bids and which score are ranked
cases.title: Only active, awarded or pending-approval bids are ranked; a rejected bid drops out and the others move up
cases.why: A rejected or revised bid that still held L1 would keep another vendor from being shown as best and could be auto-awarded.
cases.setup: Rank auction on a buy event, two QA vendors (or one vendor plus one surrogate bid). Vendor A bids 100, vendor B bids 110.
cases.steps: 1. Read the live ranks: A is 1, B is 2. 2. Reject A's bid. 3. Read the live ranks again.
cases.expected: After the rejection only B is ranked and B is rank 1; A has no rank and no best-price contribution.
cases.oracle: `GET /v1/trade/:id/event_indicators` → `auction_identifiers_data` has an entry only for bids in status active/selected/requested (`Bid::VALID_STATUSES_TO_RANK`); B's `global.rank.value` = "1" after the reject; A's bid id no longer appears.

cases.section: Which bids and which score are ranked
cases.title: A separate buyer ranking is used for the buyer's view only; vendors stay ranked on their own score
cases.why: With a buyer ranking widget (e.g. price plus a buyer-only adjustment) the buyer must see the adjusted order while vendors are ranked on what they quoted; mixing the two leaks the adjustment.
cases.setup: gate: `buyer_ranking_widget`. A rank auction with a buyer ranking widget configured, two vendors whose order differs between the vendor score and the buyer score (A: price 100, buyer score 130; B: price 110, buyer score 115).
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer, read the live ranks. 2. As vendor A, open the live event and read its rank.
cases.expected: The buyer sees B first (115 < 130). Vendor A sees itself as rank 1 (100 < 110).
cases.oracle: Buyer `event_indicators` `global.rank` follows `buyer_rank`; the vendor's own rank (vendor card / quote) follows `rank`. `get_ranking_key` returns buyer_rank only for a buyer with the widget configured.

cases.section: Which bids and which score are ranked
cases.title: On a sell (forward) event the highest score is rank 1
cases.why: Forward auctions (scrap sales) invert the order; an ascending sort there would award the lowest offer.
cases.setup: A forward (sell) rank auction, vendors offering 500, 450 and 520.
cases.steps: Read the live ranks.
cases.expected: 520 is rank 1, 500 rank 2, 450 rank 3; the best price shown to the buyer is 520.
cases.oracle: `event_indicators` ranks "1"/"2"/"3" for 520/500/450; `global.best_price.value` = "520".

cases.section: Best price shown on the live page
cases.title: The overall best price is one number, the same under every vendor, and is not rounded
cases.why: The best price is what vendors chase; if it were rounded (100.456 shown as 100.46) a vendor could bid "below" it and not be best.
cases.setup: Price auction, buy event, two vendors: A quotes 100.456, B quotes 101.50.
cases.steps: Read the live best price for each vendor's row.
cases.expected: Every row shows the same best price, 100.456, written without rounding; B's own 101.50 is shown elsewhere as 101.5 (trailing zero dropped).
cases.oracle: `global.best_price.value` = "100.456" in every bid entry; the value is produced by `get_converted_display_value` which only strips trailing zeros (no round/truncate).

cases.section: Best price shown on the live page
cases.title: With a loading factor the ranks include the penalty but the best price does not
cases.why: A vendor who regretted a loaded line can be L2 while its own price is shown as the "best price"; the buyer must understand the two numbers are on different bases.
cases.setup: gate: `loading_factor_enabled`. Auction, two lines; line 2 has loading factor 15. Vendor A quotes 100 in total and regrets line 2; vendor B quotes 110 on both lines.
cases.steps: Read the live ranks, best price and loading factor columns.
cases.expected: A's ranked score is 115, so B is rank 1 and A rank 2. The best price shown is 100 (A's unloaded price). A's loading factor column shows 15, B's 0.
cases.oracle: `global.rank` B "1", A "2"; `global.best_price.value` = "100"; `global.loading_factor.value` A = 15.0, B = 0.0.

cases.section: Best price shown on the live page
cases.title: With a technical round scored, a vendor marked "technically not acceptable" is left out of the line ranks
cases.why: A TNA vendor's low price must not be L1 on a line it is not allowed to win; but before any evaluation exists it still counts.
cases.setup: Technical + price round; vendor A scored TNA on line 1, vendor B acceptable. On line 1 A quotes 90, B 100.
cases.steps: 1. Before any evaluation, read the line-1 ranks and best price. 2. After the evaluation is submitted, read them again.
cases.expected: Before: A is rank 1, best price 90. After: A has no rank on line 1, B is rank 1 and the line best price is 100.
cases.oracle: `inline[company][line].rank` and `inline…best_price` change as stated; the exclusion applies only when the project has evaluations (`get_event_score_for_participants_excluding_tna`).

cases.title: Traffic light on a buy event: at or below the lower bound is green, up to the upper bound yellow, above it red
cases.why: The boundary values decide which vendors are told they are competitive; an off-by-one at the bound sends the wrong signal.
cases.setup: Traffic-light auction on price, buy event, lower bound 100, upper bound 120. Three vendors quote exactly 100, exactly 120 and 120.01.
cases.steps: Read each vendor's colour.
cases.expected: 100 → green, 120 → yellow, 120.01 → red.
cases.oracle: `global.traffic_light_color.value` = green / yellow / red; `BidsGroup.get_color_within_range` buy branch `value <= lower` green, `lower < value <= upper` yellow, else red.

cases.title: Traffic light on rank: the buyer's live page and the vendor's card must show the same colour
cases.why: The live page compares the vendor's raw score with the bounds while the vendor card compares its dense rank; with rank bounds 1–2 a vendor at rank 1 with score 100 is green on the card and red on the buyer's page.
cases.setup: Traffic-light auction on rank, bounds lower 1, upper 2. Vendors A 100 (rank 1), B 110 (rank 2), C 130 (rank 3).
cases.steps: 1. As the buyer read the live colours. 2. As vendor A open the event list and read the card colour.
cases.expected: Both views: A green, B yellow, C red.
cases.oracle: Today `event_indicators` `global.traffic_light_color` uses `score_hash['color'] || score_hash['rank']` (raw score 100 → red) while `EventIndicators::LotBased#color` uses the dense rank (1 → green). A mismatch is the defect.

cases.title: Line-level default reference is each line's lowest first quote; a line with only revised quotes has none
cases.why: On line-closed events the margin is per line; a line whose only quotes were superseded must not report a reference of 0 (100 % saving).
cases.setup: RFQ closed per line, savings default strategy on lines. L1: A first 100 then 90; B first 95. L2: only A, whose first quote was later revised.
cases.steps: Close the stage; read line-wise savings.
cases.expected: L1 reference 95 (lowest first quote), final 90, saving 5 per unit. L2 has no default reference and shows no saving.
cases.oracle: `GET /v1/trade/:id/best_line_wise_savings`: L1 reference 95; L2 has no default entry (not 0, not 100 %).

cases.title: A negative default saving is hidden, and the setting that hides it never switches back
cases.why: When the final best is worse than the first best, the default saving is negative; it is hidden and the stage is flagged "do not show default savings" for good, even if a later revision makes the saving positive.
cases.setup: RFQ with the default saving strategy. Vendor A first quotes 100, later only quotes above it (the lowest active bid becomes 105).
cases.steps: 1. Close the stage; read savings and the stage flag. 2. Reopen / extend, let a vendor revise to 90, close again; read savings.
cases.expected: Step 1: no default saving shown, flag off. Step 2: a positive default saving (10) should be shown again.
cases.oracle: Step 1: default entry absent, `config.show_default_savings` = false. Step 2 today: the flag stays false (the worker only ever sets it to false — `savings_calculator_worker.rb:34-41`); the saving stays hidden. That is the defect.

cases.title: Line savings totals use the buyer's quantity for the default strategy and the vendor's for others, rounded to the price precision
cases.why: Per-unit references are multiplied up to amounts; using the wrong quantity misstates the total saving.
cases.setup: RFQ, one line, buyer quantity 10; reference strategies: default (per unit) and budget 98 per unit. Best vendor quotes 95 for quantity 8. First best quote was 100.
cases.steps: Close; read the total line-wise savings.
cases.expected: Default: (100 − 95) × 10 = 50 on reference 1,000 → 5.00 %. Budget: (98 − 95) × 8 = 24 on reference 784 → 3.06 %. Values rounded to the price precision (2) with trailing zeros dropped.
cases.oracle: Aggregated line savings per strategy as listed; percent = total savings ÷ total reference × 100.

cases.title: A savings configuration whose references are all empty does not break the stage
cases.why: When every reference value is empty the configuration keeps a nil list, and reading savings loops over it — the savings card and the precomputed comparison would fail.
cases.setup: RFQ with a savings configuration saved with every reference value blank; one bid; close.
cases.steps: Open the stage, the savings card and the comparison.
cases.expected: All open; savings shows nothing.
cases.oracle: No 500 from `aggregate_savings`, `best_line_wise_savings` or the comparison; `SavingsConfiguration.read` sets `reference_prices` nil and `get_all_savings` iterates it (`savings_configuration.rb:241`).

cases.title: Realised savings exist only once a bid is awarded; unrealised only before
cases.why: "Realised" must mean money actually committed; showing realised savings before award (or unrealised after) misreports the procurement result.
cases.setup: gate: `show_custom_savings`. RFQ, one line quantity 10; vendors' first quotes 100 and 104; final best 95.
cases.steps: 1. Close without awarding; read custom savings. 2. Award the 95 bid for the full quantity; wait ~10 s; read again.
cases.expected: Step 1: only unrealised, reference 1,000 (best first quote × 10). Step 2: only realised, reference 1,000 for the selected quantity, final 950, saving 50.
cases.oracle: `misc.custom_savings_configuration` strategies: step 1 `unrealised` only; step 2 `realised` only (`valid?` rules) with the values listed.

cases.title: Vendor-specific savings percent is not cut to a whole number
cases.why: With whole-number references and final amounts, an integer division turns 10 % into 0 %, or a zero reference into a crash.
cases.setup: Lot-based vendor-specific savings with reference 1,000 for vendor A; A's last bid total 900 (whole numbers).
cases.steps: Read vendor A's vendor-specific savings.
cases.expected: Saving 100, 10 %. With a reference of 0 the saving shows no percentage, without an error.
cases.oracle: `vendor_specific_savings` for A: amount 100, percent 10 (not 0). Reference 0 must not return 500 (`reference.rb:61, 77-78`).

cases.title: "Awarded" columns recompute the bid on the awarded quantity
cases.why: Awarded totals must use what was awarded, not what was quoted; otherwise the PO value and the award summary disagree.
cases.setup: Template with awarded-quantity widgets; vendor quotes 10 units at 100 (gross 1,000 + 18 % GST); award 6 units.
cases.steps: Read the award comparison's "Awarded" columns for the vendor.
cases.expected: Awarded gross total = 6 × 100 × 1.18 = 708; with nothing awarded every awarded column is 0.
cases.oracle: Awarded widget values use `awarded_quantity` in place of `participant_quantity` in every formula when any line has an awarded quantity > 0.

cases.title: Mentioning someone who is not an active member of the workspace is refused
cases.why: A mention notifies by mail; mentioning an outsider (or a garbled id) must not send event details to them.
cases.setup: Session: the BUYER. The sandbox event's price round.
cases.steps: Post a message that mentions an id that is not a user of this workspace.
cases.expected: Refused: "You are not allowed to perform this action"; no message saved.
cases.oracle: HTTP 422, code 101; `GET /remarks?item_type=TradeRequest&item_uuid=…` does not list the message.

cases.section: Live data endpoints on a stage with no bids
cases.title: Live indicators, L1 data and savings on a live round with no bids answer empty, not with an error
cases.why: Every live page opens these before the first bid; a crash there blanks the buyer's screen at the most watched moment.
cases.setup: Session: the BUYER. The sandbox event: published, one open price round, no bids.
cases.steps: Read the round's live indicators, its L1 data and its line-wise savings.
cases.expected: All three answer successfully with empty data.
cases.oracle: HTTP 200 for each: `event_indicators` → `auction_identifiers_data` empty (or `{}` when masked); `l1_data_for_event` → `{}` (no scores); `best_line_wise_savings` → no entries.

cases.title: Line landed cost: price plus positive GST minus the line cash discount plus line freight
cases.why: The per-unit landed cost feeds the line rank on landed-cost stages; a negative GST or a missing discount changes who is L1.
cases.setup: Sheet price round, line with buyer quantity 10. Vendor quotes price 100, GST 18 %, line cash discount 2 %, line freight 5; a second line with GST entered as −5.
cases.steps: Submit; read the line breakup.
cases.expected: Line 1 landed cost = 100 + 18 − 2 + 5 = 121 per unit (1,210 total); without cash discount 123. Line 2: the negative GST adds nothing (landed = price + freight).
cases.oracle: Bid line `final_price` = 121.0; `landed cost without CD` = 123.0; line 2 `applicable_gst` = 0 (`gst > 0` guard).

cases.title: Bid-level GST and line GST do not double-count
cases.why: The bid keeps two GST figures: one from the bid's own GST field over the landed total, one summed from the lines; the lot GST adds both, so a vendor that fills both is taxed twice.
cases.setup: Charges template where both a bid-level GST field and line GST exist; vendor quotes two lines (1,000 at 18 % and 500 at 5 %) and also fills bid GST 18 %.
cases.steps: Read the bid's tax amounts and lot GST on the comparison.
cases.expected: One tax total for the bid (205 if lines carry the tax; the bid field should not add another 18 % of the landed total).
cases.oracle: `gst_tax_amount` (bid column) + `gst_tax_order_total` (lines) = `lot_gst`; today both are added (`bid.rb:1014-1017`). Also `Bid#gst` returns the FIRST line's GST while `gst_tax_amount` reads the column (`bid.rb:845-847`).

cases.title: A field the vendor leaves blank in a formula takes the buyer's value, then zero
cases.why: Totals silently built from the buyer's default (or 0) can make a bid look cheaper than what the vendor meant.
cases.setup: Template line formula total = (price + packing) × quantity; the buyer filled packing = 5 on line 1 and nothing on line 2. Vendor quotes price 100, quantity 10, and leaves packing blank on both.
cases.steps: Submit; read both lines' totals.
cases.expected: Line 1 = (100 + 5) × 10 = 1,050; line 2 = (100 + 0) × 10 = 1,000. The screen should show the vendor which values were filled for it.
cases.oracle: Line totals 1050.0 / 1000.0 (fallback to creator widget, then 0: `bid_trade_product.rb:421-430, 323-334`).

cases.title: A bid whose total formula cannot be computed is not saved with a missing total
cases.why: When a global formula fails, the error goes only to the error tracker and the bid is saved without that figure; the comparison then ranks a bid with no total.
cases.setup: Template whose global total formula refers to a field that does not exist on this stage (a template edit gone wrong).
cases.steps: Vendor submits a bid; buyer opens the comparison.
cases.expected: The submission is refused with a clear error, or the total is computed; a bid without its total must not be listed or ranked.
cases.oracle: Today the save continues with the key missing (`bid.rb:1200-1205`); the bid's `price_breakup_json` lacks the formula key.

cases.title: A multi-currency stage without a total widget still opens and ranks
cases.why: The multi-currency total reads the total widget's configuration without a guard; a template without it breaks every screen that needs a bid total.
cases.setup: Multi-currency price round on a template with no gross-total global widget; one vendor bids in USD.
cases.steps: Open the comparison and the vendor's bid.
cases.expected: Both open; the bid total is the sum of line totals in the base currency.
cases.oracle: No 500; today `Bid#gross_total` does `nil['configuration']` (`bid.rb:1272-1273`).

cases.title: With automatic cash discount, every line is priced on its effective price — and a line without the discount data does not crash
cases.why: Auto cash discount reduces each line by a notional amount; a line saved without that data makes the whole bid fail.
cases.setup: gate: `allow_auto_cd` on a buy stage; vendor quotes two lines, price 100 each, notional discount 3 on line 1; line 2 saved without auto-discount data (e.g. added after the setting changed).
cases.steps: Submit; read effective prices and the bid's rank score.
cases.expected: Line 1 effective price 97; line 2 effective price 100; the bid ranks on Σ effective amounts; no error.
cases.oracle: `effective_price` = price − `auto_cd_hash.notional_2`; today a line without `auto_cd_hash` raises in `effective_total_amount` (`bid_trade_product.rb:494-501`).

cases.section: What a rank is computed on
cases.title: Without a ranking setting, a line is ranked on the unit price, not on the landed cost
cases.why: Testers and buyers expect "L1" to be the cheapest landed cost; on a template with no ranking configuration the line rank uses the base price, so a high-tax quote can be L1.
cases.setup: Sheet price round closed per line, no ranking widget configured. Vendor A: price 100, GST 28 % (landed 128). Vendor B: price 105, GST 5 % (landed 110.25).
cases.steps: Read the line ranks.
cases.expected: A is line L1 (100 < 105) although B is cheaper landed. Record which basis the buyer's screen labels; if it says "landed" the rank contradicts it.
cases.oracle: Line rank key = `price` when no `ranking_widget_line`/`ranking_widget` (`trade_request_model_helper.rb:828-838`); bid (lot) rank on `gross_total`.

cases.section: What a rank is computed on
cases.title: Every vendor on a line is ranked on the same field
cases.why: When the ranking field is empty on one vendor's line, that vendor falls back to base price or landed cost while the others are ranked on the field — two units in one ranking.
cases.setup: Line ranking on a "total cost of ownership" field; vendor A fills it (950), vendor B leaves it blank with price 900 (landed 1,000).
cases.steps: Read the line ranks.
cases.expected: B is either ranked on the same field (treated as missing → unranked/last) or the bid is refused for the missing field; never compared 900 against 950.
cases.oracle: Today B's score = its landed/base price (`bid_trade_product_rank_helper.rb:147-158`) → B rank 1.

cases.section: What a rank is computed on
cases.title: Ranks round to the field's precision — including a precision of 0
cases.why: Two quotes that display the same must tie; with precision 0 no rounding happens, so 100.4 beats 100.6 though both show "100".
cases.setup: Single-currency auction whose ranking field has 0 decimals; vendor A 100.4, vendor B 100.6. Repeat with 2 decimals and 100.004 / 100.006.
cases.steps: Read the ranks.
cases.expected: Precision 0: A and B tie (both shown 100, the tie rule applies). Precision 2: 100.004 and 100.006 round to 100.00 and 100.01 — A rank 1.
cases.oracle: Today precision 0 skips rounding (`bid_rank_helper.rb:172`: `precision > 0`) → A rank 1, B rank 2 while both display 100.

cases.section: What a rank is computed on
cases.title: Weighted ranking adds each vendor's weight to its line score
cases.why: Weights encode the buyer's preference (quality, payment terms); the rank must move by exactly the weight.
cases.setup: Weighted RFQ/auction; vendor A weight 10, vendor B weight 0; line prices A 95, B 100.
cases.steps: Read the line ranks and scores.
cases.expected: A's score 105, B's 100 → B is rank 1.
cases.oracle: Line score = price score + `weighted_total` (`bid_trade_product.rb:1240-1252`); the best price stored is still the line price (A 95).

cases.title: When a vendor's own revision drops it down the ranking, the vendors who moved up are told
cases.why: "Your rank has changed" brings vendors back into a live auction. It is sent to the vendors holding the ranks between the reviser's new and old rank, and that range is empty when the reviser got worse, so nobody hears that they moved up.
cases.setup: Live rank auction, price increase allowed, rank-change notifications on. Vendor A 100 (L1), vendor B 110 (L2), the QA vendor 120 (L3).
cases.steps: 1. Vendor B revises to 90: B becomes L1, A L2 — control. 2. Vendor A then revises to 130: B stays L1, the QA vendor moves to L2, A drops to L3. 3. Read A's, B's and the QA vendor's notifications after each step.
cases.expected: Step 1: A is told its rank changed. Step 2: the QA vendor (moved up) and A (moved down) are told.
cases.oracle: `rank_change` notifications. Step 1 passes today (range 1..2). Step 2 today: range `3..2` is empty (`bid.rb:310`), so no notification — the defect.

cases.title: Rejecting the L1 bid in the last three minutes extends the auction as documented
cases.why: The code means to extend the auction when the leading bid is rejected or revoked near the end (so others can react), but compares the wrong record and never does.
cases.setup: Live auction with "update end time on late bid" on, not dynamic closing; vendor A is L1; 2 minutes left.
cases.steps: The buyer rejects A's bid (or A revokes it). Read the end time.
cases.expected: End time extended by the configured minutes (default 3).
cases.oracle: Today no extension: `.index(self)` looks for the BidTrade in a list of Bids → always nil (`bid_trade.rb:151-153`).

cases.title: A vendor's draft bid is visible only to the user who started it
cases.why: Drafts are a vendor's work in progress; neither the buyer nor the vendor's colleagues should see them.
cases.setup: Vendor user 1 saves a draft (not submitted) on a live round.
cases.steps: Read the bid lists as the buyer, as vendor user 2 (same company), and as vendor user 1.
cases.expected: Only user 1 sees the draft.
cases.oracle: Draft listed only when `show_draft_bid` and `bids.user_id = current user` (`bids_group.rb:27-32`).

cases.title: A rejected award approval puts the bid where the approval setting says
cases.why: After a rejected award the bid must return to a known state: back to active (default), rejected, or back to the previous approver.
cases.setup: gate: `handle_approval_rejection_as`. An award approval flow; three runs with the rejection handling set to "make active again", "reject the bid" and "send back to the previous approver".
cases.steps: Award a bid; the approver rejects; read the bid and line statuses.
cases.expected: Make active again → the bid and its lines are active; reject → rejected; send back → waiting for approval again, with the previous approver to act.

cases.title: An award approval that expires or is withdrawn releases the bid and forgets the awarded quantities
cases.why: A stale "awarded 60 of 100" kept on a released bid would be reused by the next award.
cases.setup: Standalone RFQ, partial award (60 units) sent for approval.
cases.steps: Withdraw the approval (or let it expire); read the bid.
cases.expected: Bid and lines active again; no awarded quantities stored.
cases.oracle: Bid `meta_data.awarded_quantities` removed (`bid.rb:2043-2055`); the withdraw response must not hide an error from the afterflow (`approval_requests_controller.rb:187-189`).

cases.title: Partial award at approval: zero, negative or more than what is left is refused with an accurate message
cases.why: On standalone events the awarded quantity is checked at approval; the refusal says "more than requested" even for 0 or −5.
cases.setup: Standalone RFQ, line quantity 100, 40 already awarded.
cases.steps: Send for approval awards of 0, −5, 61 and 60.
cases.expected: 0, −5 and 61 refused (60 accepted). The message for 0/−5 should say the quantity must be positive.
cases.oracle: HTTP 422 code 561 'You cannot select bid with more than requested quantity.' for all three (`bids_controller_helper.rb:2183-2197`); Σ awarded rounded to 6 dp compared with remaining; a line with remaining nil is not checked.

cases.title: A vendor awarded zero is not an awarded vendor
cases.why: A zero quantity left on a vendor's line (after un-awarding) still makes it "awarded" for the letter of award, so the vendor can receive an LOA for nothing.
cases.setup: Award proposal: vendor A 100 units, vendor B set to 0 (selected then reduced to 0).
cases.steps: Submit with "send letter of award"; read who gets an LOA.
cases.expected: Only A.
cases.oracle: Today `awarded_vendor_company_ids` includes B (`awarded_quantity.present?` is true for 0, `proposal.rb:527-535`).

cases.title: A tied L1 vendor's award counts as L1
cases.why: The rank shift on ties makes every tied vendor "not L1", moving their award into "non-L1".
cases.setup: Two vendors tied at the best price; award one of them.
cases.steps: Read total_l1_proposal / total_non_l1_proposal.
cases.expected: The awarded line counts as L1.
cases.oracle: proposal_values.

cases.title: Bid-level charges and discount are stored as entered
cases.why: Freight, other charges and discount are typed once per bid; they must not be lost when the lines are saved.
cases.setup: S2 stage (charges, discount, tax on the total).
cases.steps: A vendor submits freight ₹500, other charges 0, discount 0 %, tax 18 %.
cases.expected: The comparison shows exactly those inputs for that vendor.
cases.oracle: INV-ECHO on the bid-level inputs.

cases.title: Line totals without line tax on a charges template
cases.why: When tax is charged on the total, the line must not also carry tax.
cases.setup: S2 stage, line total = price × quantity.
cases.steps: Read each line total.
cases.expected: Line total = price × quantity exactly.
cases.oracle: INV-LINE.

cases.title: The discount amount is taken from the line sum
cases.why: A 7.5 % discount must be 7.5 % of the goods value, not of the taxed or freighted value.
cases.setup: S2; vendor 2 offers 7.5 %.
cases.steps: Read the discount figure.
cases.oracle: INV-BID on the discount formula.

cases.title: The sub total = lines − discount + freight + other charges
cases.why: The sub total is the taxable base; every charge and the discount must land in it once.
cases.setup: S2; vendor 3 has a 2.25 % discount, ₹1,250.40 freight and ₹99.99 other charges.
cases.steps: Read the sub total.
cases.expected: The calculator's sub total to the shown places.
cases.oracle: INV-BID.

cases.title: No NaN, Infinity or negative totals with charges and discounts
cases.why: Impossible numbers on a comparison sheet destroy trust and can sort first.
cases.setup: S2 bids.
cases.steps: Scan every figure the buyer reads.
cases.expected: None.
cases.oracle: INV-SANE.

cases.title: A foreign-currency bid is converted to base at the stage's rate
cases.why: Comparing a USD bid with an INR bid needs the rate the buyer set; base = amount × rate.
cases.setup: A client with multi-currency enabled; stage rates INR 1, USD 83.25; one vendor bids in USD.
cases.steps: Read the comparison in base currency.
cases.expected: Every USD figure × 83.25, rounded only for display.
cases.oracle: `toBase()` of the calculator vs the comparison.

cases.title: Exchange rates cannot change once bids are in
cases.why: Changing the rate after bidding re-ranks bids silently.
cases.setup: Multi-currency stage with a bid.
cases.steps: Try to change the rate.
cases.expected: Refused.

cases.section: Line figures — what each quoted line is worth
cases.title: Prices with many decimals and tiny prices total correctly
cases.why: Unit prices like ₹0.3333/KG over thousands of KG produce long decimals; rounding each step would move the total.
cases.setup: A line at ₹0.3333 × 1234.567 KG at 5 % GST.
cases.steps: Quote and read the line total.
cases.oracle: INV-LINE.

cases.section: Line figures — what each quoted line is worth
cases.title: The smallest price the screen allows is a real quote
cases.why: ₹0.0001 (or ₹0.01 at 2 places) is legal; it must total, rank and save correctly, not be dropped as zero.
cases.setup: Vendor 1 quotes the smallest price at the company's places on line 2.
cases.steps: Read the line total, L1 and line savings for line 2.
cases.expected: Line total = price × quantity × 1.18; vendor 1 is L1 on line 2; savings against the reference are computed from that price.
cases.oracle: INV-LINE, INV-L1, INV-BEST, INV-SAV-LINE.

cases.title: Money columns use the company's decimal places
cases.why: PROCOL DEMO shows 4 places, Demo Account 2 shows 2; the same template must follow each company.
cases.setup: A fresh stage on each client.
cases.steps: Read the stage's widget precision and the company's setting.
cases.expected: Price, GST and line total at the company's places.
cases.oracle: PRECISION.

cases.title: The L1 data names the lowest-price quote and its quantity
cases.why: L1 data is used to pre-fill counter offers and awards.
cases.setup: As EVI-RANK-001.
cases.steps: Read L1 data per line.
cases.expected: The lowest unit price and that quote's quantity.
cases.oracle: INV-L1DATA.

cases.title: A tie at the lowest price: L1 shows that price, whichever vendor
cases.why: Tied prices are common in RFQs; the shown price must be the tie price.
cases.setup: Lines where two or three vendors quote the same unit price.
cases.steps: Read L1 per line.
cases.expected: The tie price, with one of the tied vendors' line totals.
cases.oracle: INV-L1.

cases.title: Every tied vendor is marked best bidder
cases.why: Marking only one tied vendor best hides an equal offer.
cases.setup: As EVI-RANK-003.
cases.steps: Read best-bidder flags per line.
cases.expected: All tied vendors best; nobody else.
cases.oracle: INV-BEST.

cases.title: Ranks follow the dense-rank rule, a tie at the best moving everyone down
cases.why: Procol shows tied leaders as rank 2 (nobody rank 1); the shown ranks must follow that rule consistently.
cases.setup: Ranks visible on the stage.
cases.steps: Read shown ranks.
cases.expected: Dense rank over the ranking figure; with a tie at the best, every rank +1.
cases.oracle: INV-RANK.

cases.title: A lower price with a higher tax: screen L1 and report "best net price" may differ
cases.why: Procol has three L1 definitions: lowest unit price (screen L1), lowest ranking score, and lowest net price after tax (Excel). A buyer must know which one each shows.
cases.setup: Line 2: vendor A ₹100 at 28 % (₹128 after tax), vendor B ₹105 at 5 % (₹110.25), vendor C ₹104 at 18 %.
cases.steps: Read screen L1 for line 2 and the report's best net price.
cases.expected: Screen L1 = ₹100 (vendor A, unit price basis); report best net price = ₹110.25 (vendor B).
cases.oracle: INV-L1 + REPORT-L1.

cases.title: The report after the close matches the screen after the close
cases.why: Reports read the stored savings copy; it must equal the live one.
cases.setup: S1 after the close.
cases.steps: As EVI-REP-001.
cases.expected: Same.
cases.oracle: AFTER-CLOSE + INV-REPORT.

cases.title: The report on a charges template carries the bid totals
cases.why: Charges and tax on the total must reach the Excel.
cases.steps: As EVI-REP-001.
cases.expected: Same totals.
cases.oracle: INV-REPORT.

cases.title: The report's best net price is the cheapest price after tax
cases.why: See EVI-RANK-008.
cases.steps: Read "Best Net Price" for line 2.
cases.oracle: REPORT-L1.

cases.title: Each vendor's own line savings in the quote view
cases.why: The quote view shows savings per vendor; it must use that vendor's price.
cases.setup: As EVI-SAV-001.
cases.steps: Open each vendor's quote.
cases.expected: Reference − that vendor's unit price.
cases.oracle: INV-SAV-LINE (quote details).

cases.title: Savings and every figure stay the same after the close
cases.why: The savings worker recomputes and stores savings 5 s after the close; the stored copy feeds reports.
cases.setup: S1 with a 6-minute window.
cases.steps: Re-run every check after the close.
cases.expected: All agree.
cases.oracle: AFTER-CLOSE.

cases.title: Savings with a tiny best price do not overflow or show NaN
cases.why: A near-zero price makes savings ≈ 100 %; it must stay a number.
cases.setup: S5 (smallest price on line 2).
cases.steps: Read line and total savings.
cases.expected: Exact amounts; % below or equal to 100; no NaN / Infinity.
cases.oracle: INV-SAV-LINE, INV-SAV-AGG, INV-SANE.

cases.title: A zero savings reference shows no percentage, not "Infinity %"
cases.why: amount ÷ 0 in Ruby floats is Infinity, rounded and sent as text.
cases.setup: A budget reference of 0 on a line (needs the savings configuration edited on the stage).
cases.steps: Read savings.
cases.expected: No percentage (blank), never "Infinity" / "NaN".
cases.oracle: INV-SANE.

cases.title: GST per unit and landed cost per unit in the price breakup
cases.why: The per-unit landed cost feeds the comparison report's "net price" and the orders' final price.
cases.setup: Any line with a GST rate and no freight or discount.
cases.steps: Read the bid's price breakup.
cases.expected: GST per unit = price × GST / 100; landed cost per unit = price + that GST.
cases.oracle: INV-BREAKUP on `bid_products[].price_breakup.gst_tax_amount` and `.landed_cost`.

cases.title: No impossible numbers on the comparison
cases.why: NaN / Infinity / negative totals must never reach a buyer.
cases.setup: Any bids.
cases.steps: Scan the stage, comparison, indicators, savings and L1 reads.
cases.expected: None.
cases.oracle: INV-SANE.

cases.title: A draft bid's total is not used for any decision
cases.why: Draft bids skip recomputation and keep the client's total; the price-change approval check reads it.
cases.setup: A non-RFQ stage with price-change approval required; a vendor saves a draft with a wrong total, then submits a revision.
cases.steps: Observe whether approval is triggered by the real or the claimed change.
cases.expected: The approval decision uses the recomputed total.
cases.oracle: Approval raised (or not) matches the recomputed price change.

cases.section: Which bids and which score are ranked
cases.title: The "vendor rank" column always ranks on the vendor's own score, even with a buyer ranking
cases.why: The buyer console shows both "rank" (buyer order) and "vendor rank" (what the vendor is told); if vendor rank followed the buyer score the buyer would misread what each vendor sees.
cases.setup: gate: `display_vendor_rank_in_auction_qcs`. Same event as API-EVRCAL-002.
cases.steps: Read the live ranks as the buyer.
cases.expected: "Rank" puts B first; "Vendor rank" puts A first. With the stage's rank display off, vendor rank is blank.
cases.oracle: `global.vendor_rank.value` = dense rank on key `rank` (A "1", B "2"); `global.rank.value` on `buyer_rank`. Vendor rank is nil when `should_show_rank?` is false.

cases.title: When rank display is off, line ranks are blank — but the "best bidder" flag still marks the leader
cases.why: A price auction with ranks hidden is meant to show no position; a true/false "best bidder" flag next to a blank rank tells the reader who is L1 anyway.
cases.setup: Price-based auction, buy event, rank indicator off in the stage's optional indicators; vendors A 100 and B 110.
cases.steps: Read the live line indicators for both vendors.
cases.expected: The rank is empty for both, but A's line carries "best bidder: yes" and B's "best bidder: no". It should carry no best-bidder flag when ranks are hidden.
cases.oracle: `inline[A][line].rank` = `{"value": "", "best_bidder": true}`, B's `best_bidder: false`; `should_show_rank?` is false (`auction_config` price and `other_auction_indicators_config.rank` not true).

cases.title: Alternate bidding shows line ranks even when rank display is off
cases.why: The normal path hides ranks when the stage says so; the alternate-bidding path skips that check, so the same setting behaves differently by layout.
cases.setup: Alternate-bidding auction (vendors may quote alternates per line), rank indicator off, two vendors.
cases.steps: Read the live line indicators.
cases.expected: Ranks should be blank like on a normal stage. Today they are filled in.
cases.oracle: `inline[company][line].rank.value` is a number although `should_show_rank?` is false; compare `auction_indicators_service.rb:189-193` (no check) with `:145` (checked).

cases.title: Traffic light on a forward (sell) price auction uses the opposite bands
cases.why: For a sale, a higher offer is better; the bands must flip or the best buyer is shown red.
cases.setup: Forward traffic-light auction on price, lower bound 500, upper bound 450 (sell: green at or above 500, yellow from 450 up to below 500). Offers 500, 450 and 449.99.
cases.steps: Read each colour.
cases.expected: 500 → green, 450 → yellow, 449.99 → red.
cases.oracle: Forward branch `value >= lower` green, `upper <= value < lower` yellow, else red; used only when the event is a forward auction AND the traffic light is not on rank.

cases.title: No colour at all when the bounds are not set
cases.why: A traffic-light event saved without ranges must not paint everyone red (or crash); it should show no colour.
cases.setup: Traffic-light auction whose traffic-light ranges are empty; one vendor bid.
cases.steps: Read the live indicators and the vendor's event card.
cases.expected: No colour is shown anywhere and nothing fails.
cases.oracle: `traffic_light_color` absent from `global` (guard `misc["traffic_light_ranges"].present?`); card colour nil; no 500.

cases.section: Loading factor in the different rank services
cases.title: Auto award with no ranked bid at all is a clean "no bid to award", not an error
cases.why: On a lot stage with no scores the service computes company 0 and looks for its bid; the outcome must be a recorded "nothing to award", not a stuck job.
cases.setup: gate: `auto_award`. Lot-closed auction with auto award on and no bids; let it close.
cases.steps: After close, read the stage and its award state.
cases.expected: The stage is closed, nothing is awarded, and the auto-award history says there was no bid to award.
cases.oracle: No selected bid; the auto-award log/history entry "No bid found to Auto Award"; no failed job retried in a loop.

cases.title: Savings appear a few seconds after the stage closes, and not at all without a ranked bid
cases.why: Savings are computed by a job 5 seconds after close; a tester reading too early sees nothing and files a false bug, while a stage with only rejected bids must show none.
cases.setup: Two RFQs with a savings configuration: one with an active bid, one whose only bid was rejected.
cases.steps: Close both; read savings at once, then again after 20 seconds (bounded wait).
cases.expected: First stage: empty at once, filled after ~5–10 s. Second stage: never filled.
cases.oracle: `misc.savings_data` / aggregate savings present only for the first stage after the job (`closed_at + 5 s`); `SavingsCalculatorWorker` skips stages with no ranked bid.

cases.title: A savings strategy other than default, with no best quote on a line, must not zero the reference
cases.why: For budget/historical references the quantity comes from the best quote; with no quote the quantity is 0 and the reference itself is reported as 0, hiding the budget.
cases.setup: RFQ, two lines, budget reference on both; vendors quote only line 1.
cases.steps: Close; read line-wise savings for line 2.
cases.expected: Line 2 shows its budget reference and no saving (or "no quote"), not a reference of 0.
cases.oracle: Today line 2 budget `reference_price` = 0 (quantity nil.to_f) — `savings_calculator.rb:113, 117-119`.

cases.title: Realised price drop keeps the savings of every strategy even when one strategy has no awarded bid
cases.why: The loop returns an empty list as soon as one strategy finds no selected bid, throwing away the strategies already computed.
cases.setup: Two vendor-specific line strategies; the vendor's selected bid exists for the line of strategy 1 only.
cases.steps: Award; read the vendor's realised price drop.
cases.expected: Strategy 1's saving is shown.
cases.oracle: Today the list is `[]` (`return [] if selected_bid.blank?` inside the loop, `vendor_specific_savings_calculator.rb:19`).

cases.title: Smart lot L1 amount is price × quantity, not a rounded price × quantity
cases.why: Rounding the unit price before multiplying turns 10.005 × 1,000 into 10,010 instead of 10,005 — the lot split value is off by the rounding times the quantity.
cases.setup: RFQ eligible for smart lots, one line quantity 1,000, L1 vendor price 10.005 (precision 2).
cases.steps: Run smart lot classification; read the line's L1 amount.
cases.expected: 10,005 (or 10,005.00); the bid's own line amount is 10,005.
cases.oracle: Today `best_price.round(precision) * quantity` = 10,010 (`event_group_controller_helper.rb:826-833`). Difference = defect.

cases.title: The partial-award share is quantity-and-price weighted
cases.why: Charges and global amounts are split by the share of value awarded; a quantity-only share misallocates freight or discounts.
cases.setup: Two lines: L1 quoted 10 × 100, L2 quoted 5 × 400. Award 5 units of L1 and nothing of L2.
cases.steps: Read the award's global (bid-level) amounts, e.g. freight 300.
cases.oracle: `percent_distribution` = 0.1667; global percent-and-amount fields scaled by it.

cases.title: Mentioning the same colleague twice in one message is accepted
cases.why: The check counts mentions with duplicates but looks users up without, so writing "@Priya … @Priya" is refused as "not allowed" — a confusing refusal for an ordinary message.
cases.setup: Session: the BUYER. The sandbox event's open price round; an active colleague in the workspace.
cases.steps: Post a message on the round that mentions the same colleague twice.
cases.expected: The message is saved and the colleague is notified once.
cases.oracle: Today HTTP 422, code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action' (`user_ids` has 2 entries, `@users` 1). A 101 is the defect.

cases.title: A plain message without mentions is saved
cases.why: The positive control for the two cases above: the chat itself works on a live round.
cases.setup: Session: the BUYER. The sandbox event's price round.
cases.steps: Post a plain message (no mentions, no attachments).
cases.expected: Saved.
cases.oracle: HTTP 200; the message is returned by the remarks list.

cases.title: A message with more than ten attachments is refused
cases.why: The attachment cap is the only limit on chat uploads; above it the message must be refused with its own message.
cases.setup: Session: the BUYER. The sandbox price round.
cases.steps: Post a message with eleven attachment links (links on this company's storage).
cases.expected: Refused with the attachment-limit message.
cases.oracle: HTTP 422, code 864. Links that are not the company's storage are refused earlier with 101 (`validate_company_urls`), so the runnable twin asserts only "refused, no crash".

cases.title: The freight shown on a single bid follows the same rule as the stored freight
cases.why: The single-bid view divides freight above 20 by the quantity and leaves smaller values as they are — the inverse of how it was stored — so the vendor and buyer read a different freight than the one totalled.
cases.setup: Same bids as API-EVRMBP-001.
cases.steps: Open each bid's detail.
cases.expected: The freight per unit and total shown agree with the stored breakup (A 19.99/unit = 1,999; B 20 total = 0.20/unit).
cases.oracle: NewBidSerializer `freight_charges`: multi-product as stored; else value > 20 divided by quantity; else as stored (`new_bid_serializer.rb:196-203`) — compare with `price_breakup_json`.

cases.section: What a rank is computed on
cases.title: The rank sent to approval rules on a line-closing stage is the worst line rank
cases.why: Approval rules like "awarding a non-L1 bid needs the CFO" read one rank per bid; on per-line stages that is the worst line, so a bid that is L1 on nine lines and L2 on one needs the CFO.
cases.setup: Price round closed per line, approval flow with a condition "bid rank > 1"; vendor A is L1 on line 1 and L2 on line 2.
cases.steps: Award A on both lines; read which approval flow applies.
cases.expected: The "rank > 1" flow applies (rank sent = 2). Record this as the documented behaviour.
cases.oracle: Approval data `bid_rank` = max of line ranks (`bid.rb:1624-1630`).

cases.title: A revision counts as a rank change against the vendor's own previous bid, whoever placed it
cases.why: The previous rank is looked up by user, not company; when a colleague placed the earlier bid every revision counts as "changed", which feeds approvals and notifications.
cases.setup: Vendor company with two users; user 1 bids 100 (L1); user 2 revises to 99 (still L1).
cases.steps: Read the bid's change timeline / rank-change flag.
cases.expected: Not a rank change (L1 → L1).
cases.oracle: Today old rank = 500000 because no revised bid of user 2 exists (`bid_rank_helper.rb:259-271`) → `is_rank_changed?` true; `meta_data.change_timeline` shows a change.

cases.title: The stage's bid count matches the bids the buyer can see
cases.why: The count includes bids hidden from the list (another user's draft, a surrogate bid awaiting its creation approval); "3 bids" over a list of 2 makes buyers distrust the screen.
cases.setup: Live RFQ: two vendor bids, plus one surrogate bid pending creation approval.
cases.steps: As the buyer read the bid count and the bids list.
cases.expected: Count 2 = bids listed (or the pending one is listed and labelled).
cases.oracle: Today `increment_active_bids_count` runs for every bid that is not revised/revoke/rejected (`bids_group.rb:127-128`), after the visibility filter decided not to list it (`:119-123`).

cases.title: The event page shows the top four live bids; quote details show the full history
cases.why: Two lists with different rules; a tester comparing them must know which statuses each holds.
cases.setup: Live RFQ with six vendors bidding (one revised, one rejected).
cases.steps: Open the event page bid block and one vendor's quote details.
cases.expected: Event page: four bids, only active/awarded/pending-approval, best first. Quote details: active, revised, awarded, pending-approval and approval-requested bids; rejected not shown.

cases.title: With company profiles hidden, vendor names appear only on the awarded bid and the viewer's own
cases.why: "Show company profile" off is a lighter masking; it must hold everywhere except where the name is needed.
cases.setup: gate: `show_company_profile` off, and vendor communication off; three vendors bid; one is awarded.
cases.steps: As the buyer read the bids list.
cases.expected: Names and the message button only on the awarded bid.
cases.oracle: `show_company_name` false except selected/own bid; `is_communication_allowed` false except selected (`bids_group.rb:480-492`). The bid-level profile switch is hard-coded on (`bid.rb:810-830`), so only the stage switch hides names.

cases.title: Quick revise is offered only to the bid's own side, on a running stage that is not knockout or dutch
cases.why: Quick revise changes a bid in one click; offered to the wrong person (another vendor, or on a knockout round) it lets someone alter a price that is not theirs.
cases.setup: Running RFQ with the QA vendor's normal bid and a surrogate bid placed for vendor B; a running knockout auction; a closed RFQ.
cases.steps: Read the quick-revise flag on each bid as the QA vendor, as a colleague of the QA vendor, and as the buyer.
cases.expected: Normal bid: offered to the bid's owner and colleagues of the same company only. Surrogate bid: only to a viewer whose companies include vendor B. Never on knockout/dutch or a closed stage.
cases.oracle: Quick-revise flag per `bids_group.rb:503-511`.

cases.title: On a lot event, the award quantities of one lot never come from another lot's proposal
cases.why: A lookup with no lot number matches every proposal, so a bid can pick up awarded quantities from a different lot.
cases.setup: Event split into lots 1 and 2; proposal for lot 1 selected (vendor A 50 units); vendor A also bid in lot 2.
cases.steps: Read vendor A's awarded quantities on lot 2.
cases.expected: None on lot 2.
cases.oracle: `Bid#get_egli_vs_awarded_quantity_hash` with nil lot uses the `lot_no` scope that matches all (`proposal.rb:44`, `bid.rb:727-728`).

cases.title: Sending an award for approval gives the process validators view access; approvers added later get edit access
cases.why: Who can open the event after award is decided by these side effects, not by the team setup.
cases.setup: Company with a process-validator team; award proposal with an approval flow; an approver step added after submission.
cases.steps: Submit the proposal; add an approver; open every stage as a process validator and as the added approver; withdraw the proposal and repeat.
cases.expected: While active/requested/selected: validators can view every stage, the added approver can edit. After withdrawal the validators' access is removed.
cases.oracle: Stage access lists: validator viewer access on active/requested/selected, removed on other non-draft statuses (`proposal.rb:93-114`); approver editor access on added steps, notification only for additions (`proposal.rb:783-820`).

cases.title: Awarding the same bid twice within three seconds is refused once, not done twice
cases.why: A double click on Award creates two POs unless the short lock holds.
cases.setup: RFQ with multiple PO per bid on; one active bid.
cases.steps: Send the award twice within one second.
cases.expected: One award; the second refused "Transaction in Progress".
cases.oracle: Second call HTTP 422 code 516; one PO entry (`bid_multiple_po_helper.rb:36-46`). If the first call fails mid-way the lock is not released for 3 s (gap) — a retry inside 3 s is refused.

cases.title: "Amount" is the goods value before tax and charges
cases.why: The bid record's amount is used as the pre-tax value in reports; it must exclude tax, freight and discount.
cases.setup: S2 bids.
cases.steps: Read the bid record's amount.
cases.expected: Σ unit price × quantity.
cases.oracle: INV-AMOUNT.

cases.title: Multi-currency line totals are rounded per line before the sum
cases.why: The single-currency path does not round; the two paths can disagree by a few paise on many-line bids.
cases.setup: As EVI-CUR-001 with 60 lines.
cases.steps: Compare Σ rounded line totals with the bid total.
cases.expected: The bid total equals the exact sum (to the shown places).
cases.oracle: INV-BID.

cases.section: Line figures — what each quoted line is worth
cases.title: Many lines in one bid all total correctly
cases.why: Large RFQs (50+ lines) are where a per-line rounding habit adds up to a visible error in the bid total.
cases.setup: An RFQ with 60 lines, mixed quantities and GST slabs, two vendors.
cases.steps: Both vendors quote every line; read the bid totals.
cases.expected: Each bid total equals the sum of the exact line totals (not the sum of rounded line totals) to the shown places.
cases.oracle: INV-BID, INV-LINE on every line.

cases.title: Line L1 on a charges template is still the lowest unit price
cases.why: Line L1 is per unit; bid-level charges must not leak into it.
cases.setup: S2 bids.
cases.steps: Read L1 per line.
cases.expected: The lowest unit price per line.
cases.oracle: INV-L1, INV-L1DATA.

cases.title: PDF reports
cases.why: Event detailed / summary PDFs carry the same figures.
cases.setup: Any closed stage.
cases.steps: Download the PDF.
cases.expected: Same figures as the screen.
cases.oracle: Not automated: no reliable PDF text extraction in the repo.

cases.title: The stage page and the savings card show the same saving
cases.why: Two screens, one number.
cases.setup: As EVI-SAV-001.
cases.steps: Compare the stage's aggregate savings with the savings card.
cases.expected: Same amount and %, allowing for the places each shows (today the stage shows 4 places, the card 2).
cases.oracle: INV-SAV-AGG (two places).

cases.title: The pre-tax amount equals Σ price × quantity
cases.why: See EVI-CHG-006; on the default template it is the base of the GST total.
cases.setup: Any bids.
cases.steps: Read the bid record's amount.
cases.expected: Σ unit price × quantity.
cases.oracle: INV-AMOUNT.

cases.title: The bid count matches the bids listed
cases.why: "3 bids" on the card must mean three live bids on the sheet.
cases.setup: Any stage with bids (vendor and surrogate).
cases.steps: Compare the stage's bid count with the bids listed.
cases.expected: Equal.
cases.oracle: INV-COUNT.

cases.title: Alternate bidding ranks every vendor-line together and the "best price" is the best ranking score
cases.why: With alternates, the ranks are pooled across all lines; testers expecting per-line ranks will misjudge a correct screen as wrong (or the other way round).
cases.setup: Alternate-bidding auction, lines L1 and L2; vendor A quotes 100 on L1 and 50 on L2, vendor B 80 on L1 and 60 on L2.
cases.steps: Read the line ranks and best price.
cases.expected: Scores 100, 50, 80, 60 are ranked together: A-L2 (50) is 1, B-L2 (60) 2, B-L1 (80) 3, A-L1 (100) 4; the best price on every line is 50.
cases.oracle: `inline[..][..].rank.value` as listed; `inline…best_price.value` = "50" everywhere.

cases.title: Cost reduction and MRP discount with a zero base are shown as "not applicable", not 0 %
cases.why: A 0 initial price or 0 MRP makes the percentage undefined; reporting 0 % reads as "no reduction" and hides bad data.
cases.setup: Template with a cost-reduction mapping and an MRP field; one vendor whose initial price (or MRP) is 0 and final 50.
cases.steps: Read the comparison (master QCS) for that vendor.
cases.expected: Cost reduction / decremental discount blank or "n/a".
cases.oracle: Today 0 (Dentaku division by zero → nil → 0.0; unverified gem behaviour). With initial 100 and final 90 the cost reduction is 10 %.

cases.title: The cash-discount text reads "X% for N days." only when both are given
cases.why: A discount without its credit days (or days without a rate) must not print a half sentence on the comparison and the PO.
cases.setup: Two vendors: A gives discount 2 with 30 days; B gives discount 2 and no days.
cases.steps: Read the cash-discount column for both.
cases.expected: A: "2.0% for 30 days." B: blank.
cases.oracle: `display_cash_discount` (`bid.rb:1371-1375`).

cases.title: A bid placed more than three minutes after the end is marked as negotiated offline
cases.why: Bids the buyer enters after close (offline negotiation) are labelled so reports keep them apart from live bidding.
cases.setup: Closed RFQ in evaluation; the buyer adds a surrogate bid 5 minutes after the end, another 2 minutes after.
cases.steps: Read both bids' labels on the comparison/report.
cases.expected: The 5-minute one is "offline negotiated", the 2-minute one is not.
cases.oracle: `is_offline_negotiated?` = created_at > bid_end_time + 3 min (`bid.rb:631-633`).

cases.title: An unknown report type is refused, not a server crash
cases.why: An untyped 500 is always a defect.
cases.setup: A stage with bids.
cases.steps: Ask for the comparison report with report type "excel_report".
cases.expected: HTTP 422 with a message, never 500.
cases.oracle: Status.
